“只要把所有要求的货物按时送到小红那里就可以了，对吧？是的。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]我明白，在那种情况下，那样的行为确实非常糟糕。鸟居但在这些殖民地，我们关心的是结果，而不是表面的体面。” 看到了吗？尽管她自己面临着种种困难，但她丝毫没有放松对他人应尽的责任。这就是她以前的样子。萤把耳朵侧过来。“……会吗？” 她以前总是直言不讳地表示自己会一时冲动就做出一些事情。最近她有没有再这样做过呢？ “嗯……至少，不是其他人，也不是这栋房子。” 如果这样的话，那么确实，她变得柔软了。不过，这听起来也不是一件坏事。 热灯笼托着下巴，叹了口气，她的目光渐渐变得遥远。 "[pc.ra kitsune |我由衷地感谢你，真的。 [pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] |谢谢。 [pc.name] ]我知道，一旦开始为别人负责而不再只关心自己，我就必须安定下来生活。但是，当我翻阅过去几个月来一直保存的日记时，我自己的故事……才意识到，这种变化其实是悄无声息地发生在我的生活中的，而我却完全没有察觉到。 当初我产生这个想法的时候，就已经接受了这样一个事实：我们所有人终有一天都不得不长大，即便是像我这样有天赋的人也不例外。我本来也可以接受自己妈妈是个有点傻气的人，但绝对不能接受她永远像个孩子一样，整天追逐天上的星星。然而，即使我已经下定了这样的决心……当小红问你是否已经安定下来时，还是会让人感到一阵怅然。” 萤低头看着自己隆起的腹部，将手放在上面轻轻抚摸，同时摇动着尾巴；你接受了她的邀请，与她十指相扣，感受到那紧实而温暖的力量——即使隔着厚厚的布料，也能清晰地感受到它的存在。 这并不是件坏事。 [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] |[pc.name] ]但我又陷入这种情绪状态了……” 就连这些情绪也发生了变化，变得与那种压抑、充满忍耐的情绪氛围更加一致了——这种情绪似乎笼罩着整个殖民地里的每一个人。 “不是吗？也许等这个孩子出生后，我的好心情就会恢复过来。在给孩子们讲故事的时候，我还能装得挺像样的，但累人。" ] ]
rows.raw: " [hotaru.isMILF |[rand |"I'll confess, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], ]I quite like the attention that comes with being this massive. The double-takes. The pointing. The whispering. The disbelief. The eyes constantly on me when I so much as waddle down to Kohaku to get my allotment for the week." Hotaru rubs her palms and looks very pleased with herself. "It reminds me of when Kohaku and I were little, although the stares were more angry back then." All right, there's no need to oversell herself on this; her cheeks are all red. There'll be time for being smug after the child's safely out of her. "I know, I know. It just... well... this was always worthwhile, but it hasn't been so fun for a while now. And... you're going to show me more favor for being so diligent with your issue, aren't you?" What? A laugh. "I'm just kidding[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. But I hope you do drop by lots in the coming weeks. I'm so overdue, it absolutely can't be long now before my body decides it's time. You want to enjoy me like this as much as you can, while you can, right? I'm surprised that someone as round as I am still has appeal, but it takes all kinds to make a world." |[kohaku.wellFed |"Kohaku dropped by the other day to pick up the silk and gloat at me." Gloat? Whatever for? "Oh, you know. Silly things, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |that's all ]." Hotaru rolls her eyes and snaps her fingers, sending a small shower of bluish sparks fizzling to the floor. "If she was going to be fat, I was going to be fat too. Little gremlin was absolutely determined that we were going to be plump colonial ladies together, and that the only regret she had was that my three sizes didn't get even more ridiculous than they already are." You look Hotaru up and down, and sigh. Seamstress was already more curvaceous than merchant to begin with, and now the balance has been restored. Is this, then, the story of their lives? Just messing with each other until it's come to this? "Yes." None of this would've happened if she didn't happily feed Kohaku enormous amounts of food while she was with child and saddle the little golden fox with all that baby fat that's never, ever coming off. "All I did was to put those delicious meals in front of her; she was the one who ate it all without thinking." And she was the one who kept drinking wyldsap for her discomforts despite knowing what it was doing to her. "Just whose side are you on, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |[pc.name] ]?" You? You're on no one's side — or maybe you're on the side of whatever makes this little spat interesting. After all, you were more than happy to act as go-between for the both of them, plying Kohaku with food and Hotaru with sap. Now then, it's not all so bad; Hotaru might deflate a little once she's popped her way overdue kit. "Or I could end up like Kohaku and not lose a single inch," Hotaru harrumphs. "Now that I'm starting to look properly cow-shaped, I might as well adopt the look — if Miko can pull off the look, so can I. At least my clothes fit me throughout all these months, which is more than I can say for that gremlin." |"Kohaku apologized for the prank when she dropped by the other day to pick up the silk." Kohaku. Apologize. Now that's an interesting combination of words. "You don't say. To be honest, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], ]I can count the number of times she's apologized to me for anything. Other people? That's her customer face. Me, though..." Familiarity breeds contempt, but anyway, you can see why Kohaku would do such a thing. This prank has clearly spiraled out of control. Although to hear talk around the den about things in Hotaru spiraling out of control, this isn't the worst of it. "I..." Hotaru looks like she's about to argue the point, then hugs her enormous pregnant belly and allows you to soothe her with a kiss and several pats. "I guess it isn't all bad. The cowish proportions have a charm of their own." Come now, she's hardly comparable to Miko even now. But you daresay she's improved considerably over the course of her pregnancy — maybe this prank did more good than harm. Hotaru purses her lips and studies you, winnowing your words for the slightest shred of insincerity, then sighs in resignation and pinches her cheeks. "You really do think I look better filling out my clothes, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |huh ]? It's still sobering — even without the wyldsap, I would've still plumped a little, that's natural and expected. This, though, being pregnant for so much longer aside... well, when you put it that way, I won't burn her to a crisp when I can finally run again. ] "Little creature didn't get away cleanly, though. I tripped her on the way out. Even she didn't expect that from someone as pregnant as me." You look Hotaru up and down — her massive middle, her lush tails that counterbalance her weight out front, the way she has to waddle around under her own weight. No, you wouldn't have seen it coming, either. Well, was that small revenge at least satisfying? "No[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. I felt bad about tripping her and started crying, then got mad at myself for feeling sorry for that little creature who got me into this in the first place. By the time the mood had passed, she'd made her escape." |"I'll be honest[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ] — I'm going to miss being this pregnant when it's finally over." And you're glad she's able to see the good that came out of Kohaku's little prank. "Little prank. Well, I guess I'm partly to blame, too." Hotaru sniffs. "Don't get me wrong, it's not something that I'll want to do again for some time, if ever. But an excuse to be even more of a homebody, eat what I want when I want, and the only people I ever have to see are Mai, Kohaku, you and the kits who come for story time? I'll miss it, just a little." Instead, she'll have a little kit making all kinds of demands on her time. How the tables have turned. "About that? For all that she's overstayed her time in me, our daughter's been really obliging and well-behaved. I mean, being burdened is unavoidable, but I'm aware that these past months could have been very, very much more draining than they already were if our daughter were so minded." Hotaru chuckles nervously and strokes her taut middle with her fingertips. "[pc.ra kitsune |Your Eminence |[pc.name] ]... at least I've dealt with moods all my life, even if having a kit inside me's made my gift flare up more intensely. But I'll take something I know over all the other things that could've happened. You hear stories." Hopefully she'll be just as well-behaved outside the womb as she is in. "Too well-behaved, if you ask me." Hotaru sighs and pats her swollen middle. "I'd be worried if Mai didn't give the both of us a clean bill of health[kohaku.anyKids |; I still remember Kohaku being miserable about sleepless nights thanks to her brat ]. I'm not asking to be driven to my wits' end, but kits should have some playful energy to them. I know I'm reaching pretty far when our daughter isn't even born yet, but I guess you can call it a mother's worry." ] |[rand |So, how did her little game turn out? With her huge tummy sticking out ahead of her so far that her skirts are but drapes for that shelf, surely everyone in the den's caught on by now, right? Hotaru chuckles and hugs her big pregnant belly to herself, drumming its taut surface with her fingers. "[pc.ra kitsune |Now that you're one of us, you truly do understand the value of a good scheme for its sake, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. ]It was fun while it lasted, making up all those excuses, gaslighting as many people as I could. While I'm no Miko, it did help that I had a respectable three sizes to begin with." You'd argue that her loose, heavy clothes had far more to do with concealing her pregnancy as long as she did, but eh. She had fun doing it, that's what matters in the end. Who was the last one to finally notice? "To be perfectly honest, I think just about everyone did months ago, but were simply too polite to say anything about it. But as for the last person... well, it's Takahiro, but that doesn't mean anything. Man's half-drunk most of the time, after all. Second last beat that drunk by a couple months — the artificer — but honestly, it's no fault of his. If it weren't for his adoptive daughter pestering him, he wouldn't care for most social obligations. "Honestly? The most fun I had happened early on — leaving Kohaku guessing, teasing Rindo. I think Tetsuya was kind of mad that I didn't care for his lectures on parental responsibility and being ready for kits — I don't care to hear what I already know and very deliberately set aside. Doubly so, when I have you helping to keep me straight." Hey, when did she become your responsibility? A laugh. "I know what you're thinking, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ], and no, it's long before you put a child in me. I've been your burden to bear the moment you let me get close to you." You never noticed... "Exactly." ...And by the time you did? You knew that Hotaru was bad news, but kept her around anyway. "That's how it is." Hotaru cozies in and gives your shoulder a light nibble. "I know I don't have the capability, class or even stability to be anyone's first pick... so having as much as I've been given in spite of being gifted [pc.ra kitsune |, especially from the divine champion [pc.himHer]self, ]is more than I ever expected to begin with. Thank you for that, [pc.name]." |"I will confess, now that it can't be that long before I pop, I'm starting to worry if I'll actually do right by this kit." Hotaru gives you a small grin and shrug. "Yes, yes, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |I know ]. It's far too late to second-guess myself, but it's hardly the worst of the troublesome thoughts I've had in my moods." If nothing else, she's committed herself to be here for her kit, which is more than her mother did for her. Letters full of well-meaning words pale in comparison to being there to begin with. "There is that, I guess. Still, I shouldn't be patting myself on the back for doing what's expected of me." Hotaru lowers her gaze and folds her ears forward as she lays her hands on her protruding belly. "This child's been extremely well-behaved even before being born — if anything turns out wrong, it'll have been my fault, not hers." That's also getting ahead of herself before her daughter's even out of the womb. You know that Hotaru frets about you while you're away — now, with someone just as important due to arrive any day, she's got someone else to divide her attentions between. "Why, I didn't know having my favor weighed so heavily on you, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |[pc.name] ]. While you're right, I'll be sure to devote a little while every day to thinking about you, and no one else." There's the Hotaru you know. |"Actually, I want to ask you a question, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |[pc.name] ]. Have I gotten soft?" Soft? Well, while it isn't obvious thanks to how she dresses, it's undeniable that Hotaru's tummy isn't the only part of her that's expanded from being with child. That, addition of feminine grace does include baby fat, so yeah, she's gotten softer. Hotaru blows you a raspberry. "I don't mean soft soft. I mean soft as in, well, settling down. Kohaku mentioned the last time we were at the baths that I haven't gotten up to as much mischief as I used to, and not just because I've got a child in me weighing me down. I'm aware that my gift has been driving me in different directions these last several months, and Kohaku's not wrong in claiming I'm being more responsible these days." Does being more responsible include staying in bed the entire morning because she was moody and crying into her pillow? "So long as all the requested goods are delivered to Kohaku on time? Yes[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. I understand that'd be terrible behavior on the other side of the Torii, but here in the colonies we're interested in results, not keeping up appearances." See? Despite her own personal difficulties, she hasn't faltered in her duties to others in the slightest. The Hotaru she was before... Hotaru turns her ears down. "...Would have?" She's been quite upfront about setting things alight on a whim. Has she done any of that lately? "Well... not other people or this house, at least." If that's getting soft, then yes, she's gotten soft. Doesn't sound like a bad thing, though. Hotaru cups her chin and sighs, her gaze growing distant. "[pc.ra kitsune |You have my gratitude, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |Thanks, [pc.name] ]. I knew I'd have to settle down once I started being responsible for someone other than myself, but reading the diary I've been keeping these last several months, my own story... it's quite sobering how it's crept up on me without me realizing it. "When I first had this idea, I'd accepted that we all have to grow up someday, even someone as gifted as me. I would've been fine with a ditz for a mom, but not a perpetual child chasing the stars in the sky. But even having resolved myself to this... it's still sobering when Kohaku asks if you've settled down." Looking down at her large baby bump, Hotaru hugs it to herself and swishes her tails; you accept the invitation and lace your fingers with hers, caressing the tight, intensely warm weight palpable even through the heavy fabric. "It's not a bad thing, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |[pc.name] ]. But I'm just having one of my moods again." Even those have changed to be more in line with the depressing, long-suffering thread that winds its way through everyone in the colony. "Isn't that right? Maybe my good humor will return once this child's out of me. I can fake it well enough during storytime for the kits, but that's tiring." ] ] "

rows.original: [hotaru.anyKids |Now that you've met Hotaru's parents, they seem pretty normal, all things considered. Hotaru clicks her tongue. "You do remember that my mother tried to set you on fire, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |right ]?" Well yes, but it was an accident, and she apologized quite profusely after. She's a bit of a ditz, isn't she? Gods know how Hotaru's father's stayed with her all these years. "You've tolerated my gift all this while, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |you know ]. I think you already know the answer to that." You'd like to think you've done more than tolerate Hotaru's presence, but — well, yes. Keeping her around isn't healthy, but you persist in doing it anyway, and it's worked out in the end. Besides, her moods can be, uh, exciting, especially while she was with child. "Same thing with my parents." Personally, you find all this rather interesting. Ditz would be a kind way of describing Hotaru's mother and her gift — one has to wonder how she's survived that much danger these last twenty-odd years. "Luck. Luck and occasional flashes of insane brilliance born from the depths of oblivious airheadedness. I know I'm hardly objective when speaking of my mother, but that's the only explanation that makes sense to me." A sigh. "She knows her luck's running out, which is why they've finally come home to stay and fuss over their new granddaughter[pc.ra kitsune |, especially one [pc.mf |fathered |sired ] by the newly anointed divine champion ]. With the way things are going, it won't be two years before she starts demanding I have more." She's not going to give in to this pestering, is she? "[pc.ra kitsune |Don't worry about it. If I can hold my own against the divine champion, how much more when it comes to my parents |Who knows ]? It depends on how raising Kaori goes — our daughter's hardly any trouble at all, hasn't a bad bone in her body to the point where it's actually tiring. While I wish that my mother had been here these last two decades, I'll settle for her taking an interest in her grandchild, if only because she can foist Kaori back onto me when she tires of her granddaughter. "Look, I'm not going to say there isn't any lingering resentment. But at least Mom and Dad have figured out that they're not going to buy their way into the good graces of the homeland — we're colonials for five generations now, if you count Kaori. They've had some good finds these last years, but it was never enough, because it could never be enough; people like us will never be worth an imperial commendation. At least I'm taking this better than Kohaku is. Little gremlin may never get used to her folks being around." |"You're asking about my parents[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]?" She's an only child, then? "If they had any kits on the road, they haven't been sent back here to join me. I was born before they got together with Kohaku's folks to adventure across the continent, looking for the riches that would buy us standing back across the ocean — I guess they've been too busy to mate these last twenty years or so. While I do wonder how growing up with a brother or sister would have been different, I'm sure Kohaku has been a decent stand-in." They're adventurers? That's the first time you've heard of kitsune going off for the thrill of it. "No, not adventurers. Prospectors. They've been with Kohaku's folks for the last twenty years, digging around, seeking some mythical motherlode that may or may not exist. Decent quality metal of any kind is really rare on the other side of the Torii gate, Kohaku tells me it's one of our chief exports and there's always demand. "These last twenty years, our parents have been enamored of the idea that if only they can amass the wealth, they can buy the standing to move back home[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." Hotaru sighs. "Become respectable people instead of colonials. I don't know about that, this is my home, not some place neither I nor them have really seen. I personally think it's just an excuse they use to go out and adventure, but that's neither here nor there. "And when you're out in the wilds and placing yourself in danger, you can't have kits tugging at your tails, and especially not one who's particularly gifted. Hence, Kohaku and I were left here to be raised by Kom— I mean, the den matron. She's done that before, take in kits who've lost their parents for one reason or the other. Gives her something to do to while away her unending punishment." She sounds just a little bitter about it. The black-furred vixen shows you her teeth. "Why, what gave it away? [pc.ra kitsune |No offense, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], but for all their hopes that they could eventually buy their way back into the Old Country, my parents didn't care very much for their so-called duties to the gods, lords, or clan |Chasing a dream? It's about the journey, not the destination? At their age, they could really stop searching for something that probably exists in just their imaginations ]. Their adventures haven't killed them, but to be raised by the den matron like an orphan, I think a little bitterness is warranted. Kohaku may hide it well, but that feeling of abandonment stings her just as badly." ... "I'm sorry." Hotaru deflates. "You didn't deserve that[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Or maybe you did, poking around sore spots like that." Do they ever come back? "Once or twice a year. There're also letters, when they can find another fox to deliver them. At the end of the day, when I'm being brutally honest with myself... I wouldn't want to live with me, either. Maybe that's why they've been out seeking the motherlode for twenty years now. Reputedly, my mother's gifted too, and I'm sure if we'd to live together our combined moods would've burned the house down. Maybe it's better this way." Try as she might, Hotaru can't keep her voice from cracking as she says those last words. You reach out for her, but she waves off the gesture. "I don't want pity or anything[pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ] — it's just how things are now. While I'd have liked my parents to be around when I was young, it's all water under the bridge. Now, I'm happy being a homebody, and if I want company there're always children willing to hear a story. And you, of course." ]

[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] |你知道的 ]我想你已经知道这个问题的答案了。” 你总觉得自己所做的不仅仅是容忍萤的存在，但事实上——嗯，确实如此。让她留在身边并不符合任何好的结果，但你还是坚持这么做了，而最终，事情也还算顺利地解决了。此外，她的情绪变化有时会相当激烈，尤其是在她怀孕期间。 “我父母也是这样。” 运气。运气，以及偶尔从那些愚蠢至极的行为中迸发出来的惊人智慧。我知道，当谈到我的母亲时，我很难保持客观，但这是唯一能让我觉得合理的解释。”他叹了口气。她知道自己的好运即将耗尽，正因为如此，他们终于决定回家，好好照顾他们的新孙女了。[pc.ra kitsune |尤其是某一个。 [pc.mf |由……创立 |生下了…… ]由这位新被册封的神圣冠军所领导 ]照目前这个势头，用不了两年她就会开始要求我再给她更多了。” 她应该不会屈服于这种纠缠吧？[pc.ra kitsune |别担心这个。如果我都能与那位神一般的强者抗衡，那么对付我的父母就更不在话下了。 |谁知道呢 rows.raw: " [hotaru.anyKids |Now that you've met Hotaru's parents, they seem pretty normal, all things considered. Hotaru clicks her tongue. "You do remember that my mother tried to set you on fire, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |right ]?" Well yes, but it was an accident, and she apologized quite profusely after. She's a bit of a ditz, isn't she? Gods know how Hotaru's father's stayed with her all these years. "You've tolerated my gift all this while, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |you know ]. I think you already know the answer to that." You'd like to think you've done more than tolerate Hotaru's presence, but — well, yes. Keeping her around isn't healthy, but you persist in doing it anyway, and it's worked out in the end. Besides, her moods can be, uh, exciting, especially while she was with child. "Same thing with my parents." Personally, you find all this rather interesting. Ditz would be a kind way of describing Hotaru's mother and her gift — one has to wonder how she's survived that much danger these last twenty-odd years. "Luck. Luck and occasional flashes of insane brilliance born from the depths of oblivious airheadedness. I know I'm hardly objective when speaking of my mother, but that's the only explanation that makes sense to me." A sigh. "She knows her luck's running out, which is why they've finally come home to stay and fuss over their new granddaughter[pc.ra kitsune |, especially one [pc.mf |fathered |sired ] by the newly anointed divine champion ]. With the way things are going, it won't be two years before she starts demanding I have more." She's not going to give in to this pestering, is she? "[pc.ra kitsune |Don't worry about it. If I can hold my own against the divine champion, how much more when it comes to my parents |Who knows ]? It depends on how raising Kaori goes — our daughter's hardly any trouble at all, hasn't a bad bone in her body to the point where it's actually tiring. While I wish that my mother had been here these last two decades, I'll settle for her taking an interest in her grandchild, if only because she can foist Kaori back onto me when she tires of her granddaughter. "Look, I'm not going to say there isn't any lingering resentment. But at least Mom and Dad have figured out that they're not going to buy their way into the good graces of the homeland — we're colonials for five generations now, if you count Kaori. They've had some good finds these last years, but it was never enough, because it could never be enough; people like us will never be worth an imperial commendation. At least I'm taking this better than Kohaku is. Little gremlin may never get used to her folks being around." |"You're asking about my parents[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]?" She's an only child, then? "If they had any kits on the road, they haven't been sent back here to join me. I was born before they got together with Kohaku's folks to adventure across the continent, looking for the riches that would buy us standing back across the ocean — I guess they've been too busy to mate these last twenty years or so. While I do wonder how growing up with a brother or sister would have been different, I'm sure Kohaku has been a decent stand-in." They're adventurers? That's the first time you've heard of kitsune going off for the thrill of it. "No, not adventurers. Prospectors. They've been with Kohaku's folks for the last twenty years, digging around, seeking some mythical motherlode that may or may not exist. Decent quality metal of any kind is really rare on the other side of the Torii gate, Kohaku tells me it's one of our chief exports and there's always demand. "These last twenty years, our parents have been enamored of the idea that if only they can amass the wealth, they can buy the standing to move back home[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." Hotaru sighs. "Become respectable people instead of colonials. I don't know about that, this is my home, not some place neither I nor them have really seen. "And when you're out in the wilds and placing yourself in danger, you can't have kits tugging at your tails, and especially not one who's particularly gifted. [pc.ra kitsune |No offense, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], but for all their hopes that they could eventually buy their way back into the Old Country, my parents didn't care very much for their so-called duties to the gods, lords, or clan |Chasing a dream? rows.original:
"Many around the den would call me a seamstress, [pc.ra kitsune
        |your Eminence, 
    ]and that's not wrong. It's the most prominent part of my job to be sure, since its end products are what they see... however, I feel that it fails to properly encapsulate the whole of my duties. Explaining it all will take a while — I hope you don't mind?"
    
    No, of course not. If you didn't want to know, you wouldn't have asked. You've come to expect long-winded answers when dealing with [pc.ra kitsune
        |your fellow 
    ]kitsune, so she can just let you have it.
    
    Hotaru [pc.ra kitsune
        |gives you a respectful nod. "But of course, your Eminence. Allow me to explain in detail."
        |beams at you, a mischievous smile playing on her lips. "Why, are you trying to learn our mysterious and inscrutable ways?"
        
        Maybe? This is more about her than any kind of cultural exchange, though.
        
        "From what Kohaku tells me, we don't really live that different lives from the locals, although she's more of a broad-picture woman and often misses the details that aren't pertinent to her job."
    ]
    
    You motion for her to go on, but instead Hotaru gets to her feet and motions for you to follow her. "If you don't mind[pc.ra kitsune
        |, my [pc.mf
            |lord
            |lady
        ]
    ]? A little tour, if you would."
    
    It can't hurt — seeing things for yourself is better than just sitting down and hearing her talk. Hotaru leads you over to several racks consisting of large, shallow baskets in which fresh leaves have been laid out. The leaves come from several potted shrubs growing by the windows, their dense foliage drinking in the sun.
    
    "It begins here, with the mulberries. Like the silkworms they feed, the plants have been domesticated for centuries, if not millennia — carefully selected for quick growth, resilience, a long growing season, and most importantly, production of many leaves. Along with some other supplements to their diet, I take the mulberry leaves to be fed to the silkworms. Often, there is much excess; the leaves have to be regularly picked to ensure good, continuous production, and when they get too old to be fed to the silkworms I send them to be processed into mulberry paper."
    
    Hotaru leads you within arm's reach of the basket racks, and within are writhing masses of white silkworms; she beams with obvious pride as she presents them to you with a grandiose wave of her hand.
    
    "I'm afraid there aren't any moths cocooning at the moment, [pc.ra kitsune
        |your Eminence, 
    ]but when they do I separate out those with superlative qualities — like resistance to diseases — from those less so. They form the basis of the next generation of silkworms, while the rest are harvested by steeping in boiling water. The cocoons of moths that make it to adulthood are not useless, either — I still use them for stuffing in quilts, coats, pillows and the like. Nevertheless, their value as thread and fabric is significantly diminished."
    
    ...You see. Fascinating, so far. A few questions, though?
    
    [pc.ra kitsune
        |Hotaru does a little bow from the middle of her chest. "I would be honored to answer any questions your Eminence has."
        |"I was going to ask you to wait until I was done..." Hotaru waggles a finger, and her smile broadens. "But I like hearing the sound of your voice. Go on."
    ]
    
    You notice that there aren't any cages, hives or the like in Hotaru's working space. Aren't the moths just going to fly away?
    
    "They are, by and large, incapable of flight. The moths have been thoroughly domesticated even before arriving on the shores of Kitsuhon an eternity ago[pc.ra kitsune
        |, my [pc.mf
            |lord
            |lady
        ]ship
    ]. A few are perhaps still capable, but the desire to breed and be with their kind has them returning to their enclosures before long."
    
    And the bugs in the cocoons, what happens to them after they've been... harvested?
    
    Hotaru shows you her teeth. "[pc.ra kitsune
        |They're perfectly edible, your Eminence
        |Why, we eat them
    ]. Waste not, want not — even staggering them as much as I can in accordance with the mulberries' growing season, each harvest of cocoons means I have plenty to give to others. I usually boil the pupating silkworms in sweet-sour sauce for myself and the neighbors, and if there is yet more, I season and preserve them with salt and spices in Macahn fashion and deliver them to Kohaku as snacks for distribution. Taste pretty good, if I say so myself."
    
    ...
    
    [pc.ra kitsune
        |Hotaru is obviously struggling not to look smug at your discomfiture, but is failing, if not obviously so. "Shall we continue, my [pc.mf
            |lord
            |lady
        ]?"
        |A giggle. A snort. And then, unwilling to contain herself, Hotaru points and starts laughing so hard that tears start leaking from the corners of her eyes. "Oh dear. Oh dear. You should see your expression right now, [pc.name]. But it's true — we do eat them. Disease can be a major problem for silkworms, so I keep their habitat sanitary, and they're prepared like any other meal. I don't see why you're so squeamish given that people in this part of the world eat treasure bugs...
        
        "Anyway, shall we continue?"
    ]
    
    If she doesn't mind...
rows.translation:
洞穴里的很多人都叫我裁缝[pc.ra kitsune
        |阁下， 
    ]没错，这确实是我的工作中最重要的一部分，因为最终呈现给他们的成果就是我的工作成果……不过，我觉得这样并不能完全反映我的全部职责。如果要详细解释的话，可能需要花一些时间——希望你不会介意。”

不，当然不会。你若不想知道，就不会问了。你早已习惯[pc.ra kitsune
        |同为你族人的 
    ]狐妖总是长篇大论地回答问题，尽管让她说就是了。

萤[pc.ra kitsune
        |恭敬地点了点头。“但当然，阁下。请允许我详细说明一下。
        |她朝你投来目光，唇边挂着调皮的笑容：“哦，难道你是想了解我们这些神秘莫测的行事方式吗？”

也许吧？不过，这其实更多是与她个人有关的事情，而不是什么文化交流。

“据红叶告诉我，我们的生活方式其实和当地人并没有太大区别。不过她总是更关注整体情况，往往忽略了那些与她工作无关的细节。
    ]
    
    你示意她继续说下去，但萤却站了起来，示意你跟她一起走。“如果你不介意的话[pc.ra kitsune
        |我的[pc.mf
            |领主
            |女士
        ]
    ]如果你愿意的话，让我带你稍微参观一下吧。”

这总不会有什么坏处——亲自动手看看总比只是坐着听她描述要好。萤带你来到了几排架子前，那些架子上摆着一些大的、浅口的篮子，里面整齐地摆放着新鲜的树叶。这些叶子来自窗边几盆灌木，它们茂密的枝叶尽情吸收着阳光。

“一切都是从这些桑树开始的。就像它们所喂养的蚕一样，这些植物也被人类驯化了几个世纪，甚至几千年——人们精心挑选那些生长迅速、抗逆性强、生长季节长，尤其是能够产生大量叶子的品种来进行培育。除了在他们的饮食中添加一些其他补充品外，我还会采集桑叶来喂养蚕。通常，这些桑叶会剩余很多；为了保证蚕能持续获得足够的饲料，我们必须定期采摘新的桑叶。而当那些桑叶变得太老、不再适合喂养蚕时，我就会把它们送去加工成桑纸。热田将你带到离篮架只有几步之遥的地方，那里密密麻麻地爬满了白色的蚕；她自豪地笑着，一边挥手将它们展示给你看。

“恐怕现在还没有蛾子正在结茧呢[pc.ra kitsune
        |阁下， 
    ]但当它们出现时，我会把那些具有优异特性的蚕——比如具有抗病能力的蚕——区分出来，而把那些特性较差的蚕分开。前者会成为下一代蚕的基础，而后者则通过浸泡在沸水中被提取出来利用。那些成功长成成虫的蛾子的茧也并非毫无用处——我仍然会用它们来填充被子、外套、枕头等等。不过，相比之下，这些茧作为纱线或织物的价值确实要低得多。

……你瞧，到目前为止，这一切确实非常有趣。不过，我还是有几个问题想问。
    
    [pc.ra kitsune
        |萤从胸前微微鞠了一躬，说道：“能回答阁下的任何问题，我感到无比荣幸。
        |我本来想让你等我忙完再说话的……”萤摇了摇手指，笑容更加灿烂了。“不过，我喜欢听你的声音。继续说吧。
    ]
    
    你注意到，萤的工作空间里没有任何笼子、蜂箱之类的东西。这些蛾子不会飞走吗？

“其实，它们基本上已经失去了飞行的能力了。早在很久以前，这些蛾子就被彻底驯化了，所以在来到基苏洪的海岸之前，它们就已经不能飞行了。[pc.ra kitsune
        |我的[pc.mf
            |领主
            |女士
        ]运输
    ]其中有些或许仍然具备这种能力，但它们渴望繁衍后代、与同类在一起，因此不久之后就会回到自己的栖息地。”

那么，那些被‘收获’后的茧中的虫子们，会发生什么呢？

萤露出了她的牙齿，仿佛在警告你一样。[pc.ra kitsune
        |它们完全可以食用，阁下。
        |为什么？我们就是把它们吃掉啊。
    ]不浪费，就不会缺乏——即使我要根据桑树的生长季节来合理安排采收时间，但每次收获到足够的茧后，我就有足够的物资可以分送给别人。我通常会用甜酸酱把正在化蛹的蚕煮熟，留着自己和邻居们吃；如果还有剩余，就会按照玛卡恩式，用盐和香料将它们腌制保存起来，然后送到红鹤那里，让它们分发给其他人作为零食。说实话，味道相当不错。
    
    [pc.ra kitsune
        |萤显然在努力忍住不露出嘲笑你的表情，但显然她并没有成功。“我们继续吧，我的[pc.mf
            |领主
            |女士
        ]？"
        |一阵轻笑，一声嗤笑，然后，萤再也控制不住自己，指了指某个方向，笑得如此厉害，以至于眼泪都从眼角流了出来。“天哪，天哪，你现在看看自己的表情吧[pc.name]但事实就是——我们确实会吃它们。疾病对蚕来说是一个很大的威胁，所以我一直保持它们生活环境的清洁，而且这些蚕也会像其他食物一样被加工处理。我不明白你为什么会有这样的抵触情绪，毕竟在这个地区，人们早就习惯吃这种虫子了……

“不管怎样，我们继续吧？
    ]
    
    如果她不介意的话……

Like the silkworms they feed, the plants have been domesticated for centuries, if not millennia — carefully selected for quick growth, resilience, a long growing season, and most importantly, production of many leaves. Along with some other supplements to their diet, I take the mulberry leaves to be fed to the silkworms. Often, there is much excess; the leaves have to be regularly picked to ensure good, continuous production, and when they get too old to be fed to the silkworms I send them to be processed into mulberry paper."
    
    Hotaru leads you within arm's reach of the basket racks, and within are writhing masses of white silkworms; she beams with obvious pride as she presents them to you with a grandiose wave of her hand.
    
    "I'm afraid there aren't any moths cocooning at the moment, [pc.ra kitsune
        |your Eminence, 
    ]but when they do I separate out those with superlative qualities — like resistance to diseases — from those less so. They form the basis of the next generation of silkworms, while the rest are harvested by steeping in boiling water. The cocoons of moths that make it to adulthood are not useless, either — I still use them for stuffing in quilts, coats, pillows and the like. Nevertheless, their value as thread and fabric is significantly diminished."
    
    ...You see. Fascinating, so far. A few questions, though?
    
    [pc.ra kitsune
        |Hotaru does a little bow from the middle of her chest. "I would be honored to answer any questions your Eminence has."
        |"I was going to ask you to wait until I was done..." Hotaru waggles a finger, and her smile broadens. "But I like hearing the sound of your voice. Go on."
    ]
    
    You notice that there aren't any cages, hives or the like in Hotaru's working space. Aren't the moths just going to fly away?
    
    "They are, by and large, incapable of flight. The moths have been thoroughly domesticated even before arriving on the shores of Kitsuhon an eternity ago[pc.ra kitsune
        |, my [pc.mf
            |lord
            |lady
        ]ship
    ]. A few are perhaps still capable, but the desire to breed and be with their kind has them returning to their enclosures before long."
    
    And the bugs in the cocoons, what happens to them after they've been... harvested?
    
    Hotaru shows you her teeth. "[pc.ra kitsune
        |They're perfectly edible, your Eminence
        |Why, we eat them
    ]. Waste not, want not — even staggering them as much as I can in accordance with the mulberries' growing season, each harvest of cocoons means I have plenty to give to others. I usually boil the pupating silkworms in sweet-sour sauce for myself and the neighbors, and if there is yet more, I season and preserve them with salt and spices in Macahn fashion and deliver them to Kohaku as snacks for distribution. Taste pretty good, if I say so myself."
    
    ...
    
    [pc.ra kitsune
        |Hotaru is obviously struggling not to look smug at your discomfiture, but is failing, if not obviously so. "Shall we continue, my [pc.mf
            |lord
            |lady
        ]?"
        |A giggle. A snort. And then, unwilling to contain herself, Hotaru points and starts laughing so hard that tears start leaking from the corners of her eyes. "Oh dear. Oh dear. You should see your expression right now, [pc.name]. But it's true — we do eat them. Disease can be a major problem for silkworms, so I keep their habitat sanitary, and they're prepared like any other meal. I don't see why you're so squeamish given that people in this part of the world eat treasure bugs...
        
        "Anyway, shall we continue?"
    ]
    
    If she doesn't mind...
    '

rows.original: Leading you away from the mulberries and silkworms, Hotaru brings you to another corner of her workspace where two wooden devices rest. "Kazuo was kind enough to build these for me[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. This one — " she taps the nearest device — "unravels the cocoons and joins several strands into usable thread, all I have to do is to find the leading edges and feed them into the machine. Much faster than doing it by hand. The other is but a loom, but both devices are each powered through a pedal down by the bottom. I don't fully understand his design — they're certainly unorthodox — but I comprehend enough to operate them and not need to go to him every time something gets stuck. The governor has him on more important tasks, I'm told." And from the loom, fabrics, and from there, clothes? Hotaru nods [pc.ra kitsune |and bows. "Just so, your Eminence. |and smiles. " ]There's more to it, like bleaching, dyes and patterning, but I'd rather not take you in there because of the alchemical stink. But yes, I could theoretically take silk fresh off the loom and make something of it, even if it would pain my aesthetical sense to do so." You see. Thanks for the tour, then — even if you suspect it was just so she could get an amusing reaction out of you. That being said, a few questions. "[pc.ra kitsune |My [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |Yes ]?" Does she work with fabrics other than silk? "If people bring them to me, yes." Hotaru reaches down and brings up her pleated skirts in a hand. "For example, these are flaxen. Not a fan of leather or furs... but I can do something with them, yes; colonial life necessitates it sometimes. I do like cotton, but that would mean taking time away from silk..." Right, you'll keep that in mind if it comes to it. And does she get much work here in the tree? You'd imagine just about everyone knows some needlework — stitching, patching and mending. "But not cutting wholesale from cloth, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |I don't imagine ]. And most certainly not from silkworm silk," Hotaru sighs. "To be perfectly frank, I don't bother myself with mercantile matters — such things are best left to Kohaku, who handles them more adroitly than I ever could. She just tells me what is required of me for the fortnight, I deliver what is asked of me, and pick up the goods necessary for my work. Sure, people ask me for a favor every now and then, but I see those as chances to procure materiel the little golden fox can't." All right, you're getting a more complete picture of Hotaru's role in the den now. She has your thanks for humoring you. "It's a chance to talk without needing to work at the same time, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence. Besides, I can hardly deny a request from such an important personage as you |isn't it? Besides, I can hardly pass up the opportunity to introduce a local — " she lowers her voice to a husky drawl — "barbarian to a small but fine aspect of our culture ]." Somehow, you get the feeling that Hotaru's being less than completely serious about this. She winks at you slyly. "[pc.ra kitsune |Oh, I would never dare, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. Tease the very champion of the August Master at the Centre of Heaven? Me |Why, whatever would lead you to such a conclusion ]? "But I do hope that I've given you a sufficient overview of the other aspects of my duties about the den[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. While 'seamstress' is sufficient, I suppose, it really doesn't get it all, don't you agree?"
rows.translation: 萤将你从那些桑树和蚕茧旁带走，带你来到她工作区的另一个角落，在那里摆放着两个木制装置。 “一夫好心地为这些装置做了设计并帮我制作了出来。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]这个——”她指着最近的那个设备继续说道，“能够将茧拆开，然后将几根丝线合并成可使用的线材。我只需要找到这些线材的起始端，然后将它们放入机器中即可。这样比手工操作快多了。另一个设备其实只是一种织布机，但这两个装置都是通过下装的踏板来控制运行的。我并不完全理解他的设计理念——这些装置确实有些非传统——但我已经掌握了足够的操作方法，因此在使用过程中遇到问题时，也不需要每次都去找他求助。我听说，州长让他去处理一些更重要的任务了。” 那么，从织布机里出来的布料，最终会变成衣服吗？ 热亚鲁点了点头。 [pc.ra kitsune |正是如此，阁下。 |然后微笑着说道。 ]其实还有更多的步骤，比如漂白、染色和印花等等，但由于那些过程中会散发出难闻的气味，我不太想带你去了解这些过程。不过，理论上来说，我完全可以利用刚从织布机里取下来的丝绸来制作一些东西，尽管这样做会违背我的审美观念。 嗯，谢谢你的讲解——虽然我怀疑你这么做只是想引起我的兴趣罢了。话虽如此，我还是有几个问题想问。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] |是的。 ]她还会使用除了丝绸以外的其他面料吗？” “如果人们把那些面料带来给我的话，当然会使用。”萤伸手拿起了自己那条百褶裙，“比如这些亚麻面料。我不太喜欢皮革或毛皮。……不过我确实可以用它们做一些事情，没错；在殖民地生活中，有时候确实需要这样做。我确实很喜欢棉花，但那就意味着要减少用来制作丝绸的时间了……” “对了，如果真到了那一步，你一定要记住这一点。那么，她在树上干活的时候，会遇到很多麻烦吗？你可能会认为，几乎每个人都会一些针线活——比如缝补、修补衣物之类的。 “但是，从布料上直接剪下整块布来制作衣物，这个技能就没人会了吧。 [pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |我想不通。 ]而且，肯定不是用蚕丝制成的，”萤叹道，“说实话，我根本不关心这些商业事务——这类事情最好交给琥珀，她处理起来比我熟练多了。她只会告诉我这两周需要我做些什么，我按照要求去完成任务，然后取回完成工作所需的材料而已。当然，人们偶尔会向我求助，但我把这些机会看作是获取那些小金狐无法得到的物资的途径。 好了，现在你应该对萤在这个团队中的角色有了更全面的了解了。这正是一个可以边聊天边不用工作的机会。 [pc.ra kitsune |阁下，更何况，对于像您这样位高权重的人物提出的请求，我实在难以拒绝。 |不是吗？而且，我绝对不能错过这个机会来介绍一位本地人——她压低声音，用一种低沉的口音说道——野蛮人我们文化中一个虽小却十分重要的方面 ]不知为何，你会觉得萤对此并不是那么认真。 她狡黠地朝你眨了眨眼。[pc.ra kitsune |哦，我可从来不敢，我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]敢戏弄位于天中心的天中尊主的守护者？我吗？ |究竟是什么让你得出了这样的结论呢？ ]但我确实希望，我已经向你们充分介绍了我在管理这个巢穴方面所承担的其他职责。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]虽然“缝纫师”这个称呼已经足够了，但我认为它其实并不能完全表达这个职业的含义，您不觉得吗？

rows.original: Hotaru's eyes twinkle. "There is a saying in Macah[pc.ra kitsune|, your Eminence] — 'great minds speak of ideas, middling minds speak of events, small minds speak of other people.' Well, I for one say that it's much more fun to deal with each other, aren't I right?" You wouldn't have asked to gossip if that weren't the case. "Ask away, then."
rows.translation: 萤眼中闪着光，说道：“在玛卡恩[pc.ra kitsune|，阁下]伟大的头脑谈论思想，平庸的头脑谈论事件，狭隘的头脑谈论他人。”嗯，就我而言，我认为其实还有更多有趣我们都是为了更好地相处而交流的，对吧？” 如果不是这样，你也不会主动去闲聊吧。 “那就尽管问吧。

rows.original: [rand |"My name means 'firefly' in my mother tongue[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ] — it's a little funny that I wound up raising silkworms, is it not? Alas, there's little value in fireflies, as pretty as they may be; they may be pretty to admire, but quickly die with the cold. "On the other hand, I suppose my name is fitting after a sense, since I mostly use my natural inclinations to put on light shows for the amusement of others. Perhaps some might say that this is an inadequate or inappropriate use of one's natural gifts and that one should aim higher in life. [pc.ra kitsune |I can't say I think very highly of those sentiments in that context |Yeah, screw them ]. What's the point if you can't have fun?" |It seems like a good number of kitsune around the den have come from the Old Country at some point or another in their lives. What's Hotaru's story that led her to the other side of the world? "None[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. I was born and bred here." Huh, really? Miko and Mai aside, it feels like every resident of the tree has some terrible past they're running from. And even the sisters are plagued by their ancestor's past, even if they didn't do anything themselves. "Well, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]do understand that those who remain by the seat of the governor tend to be those who require constant care or supervision for one reason or another and stand out for that reason. Those of us who were born in this land are more adventurous in ranging out into the wilderness, so you see less of us here. There are many who visit the tree and yet do not reside here." And yet she does. "It's as close to living in luxury as one can get, I'm told, so I consider myself very lucky. The colonial governor has made efforts over the centuries to cultivate a sense of beauty and refinement in her surroundings, if nothing else. "Buuuuut... if you find it more interesting, I could be someone else for you[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Someone who chafed against the unspoken social restrictions on large families and came here to escape them? Or perhaps you'd be more enamored of a disgrace who repeatedly failed the imperial civil service examinations and self-exiled to save her family's face? Maybe a wanted ninja on the run masquerading as a seamstress with her secret art of assassination via needles through the nose and into the brain — how thrilling!" The way she handles a needle, you could believe that last one. That kind of precision... "...Only comes with many, many pricked fingers[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]." |"When I was younger, people liked to say that I might have a drop or two of divinity in me because of my red eyes; I was apparently considered very cute as a child. While the lineage of the main families of the twelve divine clans has been shown to be impossible to water down, I suppose that doesn't apply to the branches that fan out from the main body, does it? And me, I am but a simple leaf if that were to be true[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]... "Maybe it is better that I am colonial-born, is it not? That way I can reap the rewards of being pretty without having to worry about all the troubles that one such as Rindo is beset by. That striking shade of bright red... to dress and do myself up around my eyes as a theme, it really makes me feel all pretty and self-satisfied. That warm, good feeling... ah, it is too intoxicating[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. I strongly recommend it." |Did she learn her trade herself? The silkworm-raising part is something you wouldn't have expected to be taking place in the Marches, even if it's amongst foxes. "Is there any particular reason for that[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" Well... the way you see it, when people around here want similar fabrics, they're content to work something out with a drider or two, even if it might take some effort. "Well, of course I learnt it from someone," Hotaru replies with a sly smile. "A mysterious sage appeared to me in a dream and told me to visit him in a cave to the west of here[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. When I followed the vision and met with said sage, he presented me with a legacy of these native silkworms and mulberries, secretly raised by the elves away from society in their deepest temples. They considered me a foreigner, but recognized my talent and were desperate for someone to pass their knowledge and treasures on to." Really? "No. I just wanted to see your face while I spun that yarn." Oh... "There aren't that many ways in which one falls into their trade around these parts, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |to be sure ]. It was what my mother did and her mother before her, so it's what I do now and in all likelihood, what at least one of my future daughters will do. I have to ask Kohaku to send for new silkworms every so often, as getting fresh blood is good to prevent inbreeding; usually a trade of worms for worms is sufficient. But otherwise... it's a simple existence that while not exciting proves to be content." |You've noticed that while Hotaru primarily deals in silk, her clothes aren't of the same material. Is there a reason for that? "[pc.ra kitsune |"Of course, your Eminence. I feel that it's not done for someone of my station to overdress — someone like me is more suited to simple and modest dress |Hmph. If you're implying that it's because I've no confidence in my goods to use them myself, perish the thought. My skirts may be flaxen and my overcoat woolen, but I made them both from scratch. I just think that dressing down to earth suits me more, that's all ]." In that case, all this silk... does it flow across the ocean, or is it in demand with the colonials? "There is some market, I'm told." Hotaru tucks her ears in and shrugs. "But that's Kohaku's job, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |so I really don't care ]. She tells me what's expected of me when she comes to drop off my allotment every two weeks, and picks up the completed pieces to be brought to the storehouse. The worms and dyes keep my mind and body occupied well enough, so to have her shoulder that burden for me is welcome." |"My name means 'firefly' — pretty enough, yet also unassuming enough. Much suited for one such as me, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |I'd say ]. My foxfire was — " she searches for the right words in Belharan — "possessed of superlative qualities, or so my parents told me. When I was younger, I wondered if it would be possible for me to be sent back over the ocean, to study the art of being able to harness the innate talents I supposedly possessed and... maybe be a performer of sorts, put on lovely foxfire displays. Or failing that, have a go at the imperial civil service examinations like the stories used to tell, ahaha." Clearly it didn't pan out, or else she wouldn't be here cutting clothes from fabric. "When you're no longer a child, the paths open to your future become clearer, and you have to set aside such flights of fancy," Hotaru sighs, raising a hand to her cheek. "Would my entire clan, let alone my family, have the money needed to send me over to study under the clergy of the serpent goddess for years? Would I have the ability to compete against those far more talented than I am and who had been studying since young for the examinations? I have committed no crime, and yet everyone who knows the military provost's situation understands how colonials are viewed. When you understand all this, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ], you realize that maybe raising silkworms isn't such a bad life after all, and one that grants me more freedom and happiness on this side of the ocean. "Still, a firefly must put on her display for others, knowingly or not... it's fun helping with the summer festivals." ]
rows.translation: [rand |在我的母语中，我的名字意味着‘萤火虫’。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]说来也挺讽刺的，我最后竟然开始养蚕了，不是吗？唉，萤火虫虽然很漂亮，但它们的价值其实很低；它们或许很值得观赏，但一遇到寒冷就会立刻死去。” “不过，从某种意义上来说，我的名字倒也挺贴切的，因为我的主要工作就是利用自己的天性为别人带来欢乐，让他们看到美丽的灯光表演。也许有些人会认为，这样利用自己的天赋未免太肤浅、太不恰当了，认为一个人应该追求更高层次的目标。 [pc.ra kitsune |我必须说，在那种情况下，我对这种观点并不抱有很高的评价。 |去他们的吧。 ]如果不能找点乐子，那这一切还有什么意义呢？” |看起来，洞穴里的这些狐妖们，在他们的一生中，都有过来到这个国家的经历。那么，萤的故事又是怎样的，才让她走到了世界的另一端呢？ “没有什么特别的故事。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]我在这里出生并长大。” “嗯，真的吗？除了米可与舞，感觉这个村子里的每个居民都背负着一些可怕的过去，一直在逃避它们。就连那对姐妹，也深受她们祖先那些往事的影响，尽管她们自己并没有做过什么错事。” “嗯， [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输工具。 ]我明白，那些选择留在原地的人，往往是因为某些原因而需要持续的照顾或监督，因此他们才会如此选择。而我们这些出生在这片土地上的人，更喜欢去荒野中探险，因此在这里看到我们的身影就会比较少。有很多人只是来参观这棵树，并没有真正在这里居住。 然而，她却住了下来。 “据人们所说，这里已经算是接近奢华生活的地方了，因此我觉得自己非常幸运。几个世纪以来，这位殖民地总督一直在努力营造一种美丽而高雅的环境，至少在这一点上，他是成功的。 但是……如果你觉得这样更有趣的话，我也可以扮演成别的角色哦。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]是一个那些对那些针对大家庭存在的无形社会束缚感到不满，因此来到这里试图摆脱它们的人呢？还是说，你可能会对那位屡次未能通过科举考试，为了维护家族颜面而选择自我流放的女性更感兴趣呢？也许是一个被通缉的忍者正在逃亡，她伪装成一名缝纫女工，运用她那隐秘的刺杀技巧——用针刺穿鼻孔直达大脑，想想多刺激啊！” 看她使用针线的方式，你真的会相信她真的会使用那种技巧。那种精准度…… “……只有那些手指被多次刺伤的人才能拥有。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输 ]。" |在我小时候，人们总说因为我的红眼睛，我身上或许流淌着一丝神灵的血脉；显然，在人们眼中，我是个非常可爱的孩子。虽然十二个神族的主要家族的血统显然是不可能被稀释的，但我猜，对于那些从这些主要家族分支出来的小家族来说，这一点应该并不适用吧？而对我来说，如果真是这样的话，我只不过是其中一片普通的叶子罢了。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]也许我出生在殖民地反而更好，不是吗？这样我就可以享受美丽带来的种种好处，而不必像林多那样陷入各种麻烦之中。那种鲜艳的红色……以它作为我的装扮主题，真的让我感到自己非常漂亮，也让我感到非常满足。那种温暖、愉悦的感觉……啊，真是太令人陶醉了。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输 ]我强烈推荐它。 |她是自己学习这门手艺的吗？养蚕这种事情，你绝对想不到会在边境地区发生，哪怕是在那些以狐妖闻名的地方。 “有没有什么特别的理由导致这种情况发生呢？[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]嗯……在你看来，当这里的人们需要类似的布料时，他们愿意花些功夫去和一两个织布工商量解决，即使这可能需要一些努力。” “当然了，我也是从别人那里学会这个手艺的，”萤狡黠地笑着回答，“有个神秘的贤者在我梦中出现，告诉我要去这里西边的一座洞穴里找他。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输 ]当我追寻那道愿景，与那位贤者会面时，他将这些由精灵们在最隐秘的庙宇中秘密饲养的本土蚕和桑树传给了我。他们虽然将我视为外人，但却认可我的才能，迫切希望有人能够继承他们的知识与珍宝。真的吗？” “不，我只是想在你讲故事的时候看看你的表情。” 哦…… “在这个地方，想要选择某一行当，其实并没有太多途径。 [pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |可以肯定的是 ]这是我母亲做的，她的母亲之前也是这么做的，所以我现在也在这么做，而且很有可能，我的某个女儿将来也会这么做。我需要定期让琥珀去采购新的蚕，因为保持新鲜的蚕种有助于避免近亲繁殖；通常情况下，用旧的蚕去换取新的蚕就足够了。不过除此之外……这种生活虽然并不令人兴奋，但却让人感到满足。 |你可能已经注意到，虽然萤主要经营丝绸生意，但她自己的衣服却并不是用丝绸制成的。这是为什么呢？[pc.ra kitsune |当然，阁下。我认为，像我这样的身份的人，不应该穿着过于华丽。像我这样的人，更适合穿着简单、朴素的服装。 |哼，如果你是想说因为我对自己的手艺没有信心，所以才不亲自使用这些作品，那你就大错特错了。虽然我的裙子是用亚麻制成的，外套也是羊毛做的，但这两件衣服都是我亲手制作的。我只是觉得，穿着朴素些更适合我而已，仅此而已。 ]在那种情况下，所有这些丝绸……它们是会漂洋过海被运到那里，还是说殖民地的人们对这些丝绸有需求呢？ “据我所知，还是有一定市场的，”萤把耳朵凑过来，耸了耸肩说，“但这是琥珀的工作范围吧。 [pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |所以我真的毫不在意。 ]每两周她来取我分到的那份工作量时，都会告诉我应该完成哪些任务，然后还会把我已经完成的部分收走，带到仓库去。养蚯蚓和制作染料这些工作确实让我忙得不可开交，所以有她来帮我分担这些负担，我真的很感激。 |我的名字意味着‘萤火虫’——这个名字既漂亮又低调，非常适合像我这样的人。 [pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |我想说的是…… ]我的狐火——她努力在贝尔哈兰语中寻找合适的词语来表达——“拥有着卓越的品质，至少我的父母是这么告诉我的。小时候，我常常想，是否有可能被送到遥远的海外去，去学习如何运用那些据说我与生俱来的天赋……或许可以成为一名表演者，展现出那些美丽的狐火表演。要是那样不行，那就像故事里说的那样，去参加科举考试吧，哈哈。” 显然，这些想法都没有实现，否则她现在就不会在这里裁剪布料了。 当你不再是个孩子的时候，通往你未来的道路就会变得更加清晰，那时你就必须放下这些不切实际的幻想了，”萤叹息着，将手放在脸颊上。“我的整个家族，更不用说我的家人了，他们哪有足够的钱让我去蛇女神的神职人员那里学习多年呢？我是否有能力与那些天赋远胜于我、并且从小就开始为这些考试而学习的人竞争呢？我并没有犯任何罪，然而，任何了解军事院长处境的人都知道，殖民地居民在人们眼中的地位是怎样的。当你理解了这一切之后， [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输 ]你渐渐意识到，养蚕或许并不是一种糟糕的生活方式，反而能让我在海洋的这一边获得更多的自由与幸福。 “不过，萤火虫终究还是要为他人展示自己的光芒，无论它是自觉地还是无意识地……参与这些夏日庆典确实是一件很有趣的事情。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"My name means 'firefly' in my mother tongue[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ] — it's a little funny that I wound up raising silkworms, is it not? Alas, there's little value in fireflies, as pretty as they may be; they may be pretty to admire, but quickly die with the cold. "On the other hand, I suppose my name is fitting after a sense, since I mostly use my natural inclinations to put on light shows for the amusement of others. Perhaps some might say that this is an inadequate or inappropriate use of one's natural gifts and that one should aim higher in life. [pc.ra kitsune |I can't say I think very highly of those sentiments in that context |Yeah, screw them ]. What's the point if you can't have fun?" |It seems like a good number of kitsune around the den have come from the Old Country at some point or another in their lives. What's Hotaru's story that led her to the other side of the world? "None[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. I was born and bred here." Huh, really? Miko and Mai aside, it feels like every resident of the tree has some terrible past they're running from. And even the sisters are plagued by their ancestor's past, even if they didn't do anything themselves. "Well, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]do understand that those who remain by the seat of the governor tend to be those who require constant care or supervision for one reason or another and stand out for that reason. Those of us who were born in this land are more adventurous in ranging out into the wilderness, so you see less of us here. There are many who visit the tree and yet do not reside here." And yet she does. "It's as close to living in luxury as one can get, I'm told, so I consider myself very lucky. The colonial governor has made efforts over the centuries to cultivate a sense of beauty and refinement in her surroundings, if nothing else. "Buuuuut... if you find it more interesting, I could be someone else for you[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Someone who chafed against the unspoken social restrictions on large families and came here to escape them? Or perhaps you'd be more enamored of a disgrace who repeatedly failed the imperial civil service examinations and self-exiled to save her family's face? Maybe a wanted ninja on the run masquerading as a seamstress with her secret art of assassination via needles through the nose and into the brain — how thrilling!" The way she handles a needle, you could believe that last one. That kind of precision... "...Only comes with many, many pricked fingers[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]." |"When I was younger, people liked to say that I might have a drop or two of divinity in me because of my red eyes; I was apparently considered very cute as a child. While the lineage of the main families of the twelve divine clans has been shown to be impossible to water down, I suppose that doesn't apply to the branches that fan out from the main body, does it? And me, I am but a simple leaf if that were to be true[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]... "Maybe it is better that I am colonial-born, is it not? That way I can reap the rewards of being pretty without having to worry about all the troubles that one such as Rindo is beset by. That striking shade of bright red... to dress and do myself up around my eyes as a theme, it really makes me feel all pretty and self-satisfied. That warm, good feeling... ah, it is too intoxicating[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. I strongly recommend it." |Did she learn her trade herself? The silkworm-raising part is something you wouldn't have expected to be taking place in the Marches, even if it's amongst foxes. "Is there any particular reason for that[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" Well... the way you see it, when people around here want similar fabrics, they're content to work something out with a drider or two, even if it might take some effort. "Well, of course I learnt it from someone," Hotaru replies with a sly smile. "A mysterious sage appeared to me in a dream and told me to visit him in a cave to the west of here[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. When I followed the vision and met with said sage, he presented me with a legacy of these native silkworms and mulberries, secretly raised by the elves away from society in their deepest temples. They considered me a foreigner, but recognized my talent and were desperate for someone to pass their knowledge and treasures on to." Really? "No. I just wanted to see your face while I spun that yarn." Oh... "There aren't that many ways in which one falls into their trade around these parts, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |to be sure ]. It was what my mother did and her mother before her, so it's what I do now and in all likelihood, what at least one of my future daughters will do. I have to ask Kohaku to send for new silkworms every so often, as getting fresh blood is good to prevent inbreeding; usually a trade of worms for worms is sufficient. But otherwise... it's a simple existence that while not exciting proves to be content." |You've noticed that while Hotaru primarily deals in silk, her clothes aren't of the same material. Is there a reason for that? "[pc.ra kitsune |"Of course, your Eminence. I feel that it's not done for someone of my station to overdress — someone like me is more suited to simple and modest dress |Hmph. If you're implying that it's because I've no confidence in my goods to use them myself, perish the thought. My skirts may be flaxen and my overcoat woolen, but I made them both from scratch. I just think that dressing down to earth suits me more, that's all ]." In that case, all this silk... does it flow across the ocean, or is it in demand with the colonials? "There is some market, I'm told." Hotaru tucks her ears in and shrugs. "But that's Kohaku's job, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |so I really don't care ]. She tells me what's expected of me when she comes to drop off my allotment every two weeks, and picks up the completed pieces to be brought to the storehouse. The worms and dyes keep my mind and body occupied well enough, so to have her shoulder that burden for me is welcome." |"My name means 'firefly' — pretty enough, yet also unassuming enough. Much suited for one such as me, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |I'd say ]. My foxfire was — " she searches for the right words in Belharan — "possessed of superlative qualities, or so my parents told me. When I was younger, I wondered if it would be possible for me to be sent back over the ocean, to study the art of being able to harness the innate talents I supposedly possessed and... maybe be a performer of sorts, put on lovely foxfire displays. Or failing that, have a go at the imperial civil service examinations like the stories used to tell, ahaha." Clearly it didn't pan out, or else she wouldn't be here cutting clothes from fabric. "When you're no longer a child, the paths open to your future become clearer, and you have to set aside such flights of fancy," Hotaru sighs, raising a hand to her cheek. "Would my entire clan, let alone my family, have the money needed to send me over to study under the clergy of the serpent goddess for years? Would I have the ability to compete against those far more talented than I am and who had been studying since young for the examinations? I have committed no crime, and yet everyone who knows the military provost's situation understands how colonials are viewed. When you understand all this, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ], you realize that maybe raising silkworms isn't such a bad life after all, and one that grants me more freedom and happiness on this side of the ocean. "Still, a firefly must put on her display for others, knowingly or not... it's fun helping with the summer festivals." ] "

rows.original: [var0 |"There was a period of some decades between the end of the Godswar and the colonial governor receiving her current post," Hotaru says. "While the best-known stories of her are from the ten years she spent walking the land with the August Master at the Center of Heaven, there are also many other tales of things that she's supposedly done that I find immensely interesting[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Most of those tales are the kind that are used to scare misbehaving kits into being mindful of their futures and the price of failure, but the proportion of truth in all of that is a notion that sparks my imagination." For someone like her, to not just be able to live in the same time as a legend, but also have the chance to see and perhaps even speak with one... you take it that she's quite enamored of Komari. "I'd be more fascinated if she were willing to answer questions about her youth, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |to be sure ]. The den matron is one of the few still-living people from that era — inasmuch as she can still be considered such — and is no doubt a trove of knowledge of what life was like back then. Her refusal to speak much about the past... I personally think that she believes those years are better left buried, for her to be so reticent." Or maybe because Hotaru's been pestering her? "Gods forbid[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]! I know my station and do not overstep my bounds." Does knowing her station involve making gossip about the den matron and colonial governor? "Oh, oh, [pc.ra kitsune |but I could not hope to refuse inquiries from your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, especially from someone of your station. Everyone is uncertain of exactly where you stand, your Eminence, but they're all pretty sure it's above the colonial governor |but you're not one of us and hence don't count." A thin smile plays across Hotaru's face. "Hence, I can gossip and make up stories with you as much as I please ]." You haven't been around these people for too long, all things considered, but you're pretty sure this isn't how their etiquette and mannerisms work... |Does she know about Komari's line being cursed? "Of course I do, [pc.ra kitsune | my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. Though few would bring it up as plainly as I'm now doing, the fact is rather inescapable when the sisters are in public caring for the shrine every day. After all, stories about her lineage are told to children to keep them mindful of their future, and the fact that the consequences of one's failures are not necessarily confined to the self, but others as well, and in particular one's descendants." Hotaru's a connoisseur of stories — she should know that of how Komari got into her current position, right? "Yes[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." Does she think it's equitable that Komari's descendants bear the brunt of her mistake? Their only crime was being born to the wrong clan line. "[pc.ra kitsune |With all due respect, your Eminence, e |E ]quitable has nothing to do with it." Hotaru sighs. "Our actions simply have consequences that stretch beyond us, inasmuch as one kitsune who is branded faceless ruins our image amongst other peoples." She's... that's not exactly... you know what, it's probably a lost cause to try and get these people to see around that blind spot... |You've oft heard that Komari's used as some kind of bogeyman to scare young foxes into falling in line, but everyone's too polite to discuss the details with [pc.ra kitsune |someone of your station |a so-called outsider like you ]. But Hotaru's fond of talking and a great storyteller — perhaps she could fill you in on the details. [pc.ra kitsune |Hotaru clearly makes to sigh, but catches herself and stifles it. "Most certainly, your Eminence |Hotaru sighs. "They're not pretty stories, but you already knew that ]. Most use the colonial governor as a caution against shirking one's duties, others tell of the price that one pays for failure — many people are deathly afraid of failing, I hear, and hence never try to begin with — or the perils of not holding the divine in high enough regard. There are many lessons to be drawn from the colonial governor's life, to be sure; of such bricks is the innocence of childhood constructed[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Always a tengu lurking around to kidnap naughty children to their cold and miserable island. The den matron is a living legend, if you don't mind the saying — it's just that the legends are not ones that paint her in a good light." And what's her personal take on all this? Hotaru looks confused for a moment — [pc.ra kitsune |you can only guess that someone of your station asking for her opinion of her stories isn't something that happens every day |this is certainly a question that she's not used to being asked, at least when it comes to her stories ].Clearly contemplative, she taps her chin, then [pc.ra kitsune |bows her head and begins. "I... I do not believe that this is all, your Eminence |clears her throat and begins uncertainly. "I... I don't think the stories make up the whole of the puzzle, that there must be some pieces lost to time, or the narrative has been altered in the retelling ]. The ostensible reason that the den matron is the way she is today is because she allowed the heir apparent of one of the divine clans to perish under her watch, but at the same time by all the tales I've collected there were mitigating circumstances... not that such are excuses when dealing with a life so important. "The proper penalty would have been death, and yet it was a fate harsher than death[pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. There must be more to the story, and yet there is no way to find out. The colonial governor herself certainly isn't telling." |"The den matron has lived — no, existed for so long, she's a walking historical archive," Hotaru says wistfully. "Oh, the stories that they tell of her when she was supposedly younger...they're mostly of the period that immediately followed the Godswar. But what about during those terrible times? And of before them? She lived through them... doesn't it set your heart aflutter, thinking of the stories that she has to tell[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]?" You'll say. Knowledge about the world before the Godswar is painfully lacking. Well, accurate accounts; there's no lack of legends, folklore and the like.[pc.bg acolyte scholar |Both academic and religious texts pertaining to that period are notably missing: not a surprise given the cataclysmic effect of the Godswar, but still. ] Having someone who actually lived through those events recount her experiences would constitute an excellent primary source, if nothing else. "And yet the den matron will not speak about it. I understand that it's painful for her, since it pertains to her current condition, but..." Hotaru sighs, raising a hand to her cheek. "I just want the stories, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |that's all ]. I don't even care if they're true or not, so long as they're interesting." |"The den matron has occupied the post of colonial governor since the effort was founded around two centuries ago[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Neither does she show any signs of slowing down — she's had a heir each generation, but ah, they never got to succeed her. She's responsible for the prosperity of the colonies as a whole, and it's thanks to her guidance that we have what we have today on this side of the ocean. I wouldn't exist if not for her, so I have to express my gratitude. Is this not the case?" |[pc.ra kitsune |As you ask for Hotaru’s thoughts on Komari, she instantly freezes. Staring at you like an animal frozen in the torchlight, the [silly |dubious creature |seamstress ] stammers, trying to find her words. Eventually, she succeeds, composing herself and answering you. "Ah... what of the den matron, your Eminence? If you wish to know her personal history, I’m hardly the right girl to ask, you know. In fact, I—" You clarify that you didn’t mean anything like that; you simply wanted to know whether she’s heard anything interesting lately. [pc.isDK |You can’t hide your evil grin |There's an awkward silence ] as Hotaru shifts uncomfortably, put on the spot by your authority. Before long, however, she gets a grip on herself. Stiffening her back, the seamstress stands ramrod straight, and looks you directly in the eyes. "I haven’t the slightest idea what you’re referring to, your Eminence," Hotaru replies, a little too quickly. "The humdrum of the den has been the same as always; I can’t recall anything of particular import standing out." ...She’s lying through her teeth, but you’re not about to let her know you can see it. Opting to toy with her a bit more, you ask what she has heard; spare you no detail, no matter how nominal. Immediately, Hotaru’s eye contact wavers, and [silly |sweat begins beading above her brow. For a pyromaniac, she sure can’t stand being in the hot seat... |she shifts once more. ] Clearing her throat, the seamstress gives an awkward, stilted laugh, as she idly toys with a loose lock of her black hair. "Ah, a-actually, there was one thing that I’d heard. J-just a rumor, I assure you, and so patently absurd that I could scarcely entertain the notion, but someone — whose name escapes me at the moment — had implied that yourself and the governor, had, ah—" [pc.isDK |Spit it out already, you’re tired of her dancing around things. |The point, if she would? ] Hotaru blanches, staring directly at you as she resumes. "Th-that the two of you had sex, your Eminence." Immediately backpedaling, Hotaru continues to stammer out a correction. "B-b-but I can assure you, such a rumor isn’t something that I would even consider taking with a grain of truth, your Eminence! After all, s-such a thing would be absolutely absurd, right? It was probably a mere jest I misconstrued, I wager." Hotaru’s usually-cool demeanor is little more than tattered scraps; instead of her typical smirk, her face bears an awkward, queasy grin as she shoots you a pleading glance, profoundly uncomfortable. You suppose that’s the best you’ll get out of her; waving your hand, you echo her limp attempt at humor with a forced laugh of your own, the atmosphere between you thick enough to cut. |Asking Hotaru about her thoughts on the den’s matron, you’re caught off guard has her cheeky smirk grows into a full-blown smile, mischief in her eyes. As she gives you a teasing laugh, she idly strokes a cheek, smiling right at you. "Oh? You want to hear my thoughts on the governor? I’m hardly knowledgeable on the subject; if anything, you should be lecturing me, on account of how close you two have gotten." How’d she find out about that? Komari did her best to— Hotaru gives you a judgmental look, interjecting as you attempt to reason. "You do realize the den matron’s office is rather close to my own dwelling, yes? The walls here are far from thick, [pc.name]. If she were doing her best, she would have at least soundproofed the affair, you know." That’s... a fair point. What’s she doing eavesdropping, though? Hotaru sighs, pinching the bridge of her nose as she rubs her eyes. Not even looking at you, she continues speaking. "To call it 'eavesdropping' would imply intent, [pc.name]. I confess that at first, it was quite amusing; I was doing my best to listen in, at least initially." Hotaru returns her gaze to you, exhaustion in those crimson eyes as she regards you. "And yet, I find myself striving to cover my ears in an endeavor to hear less, by the end of it. I don’t even want to imagine what the two of you have been getting up to, but unfortunately, I have rather a good idea of it. So yes, I am painfully aware of your escapades, against my best wishes." You... don’t really have a response to that. Instead, the two of you sit in silence for a bit, awkwardly staring at each other in a sort of social paralysis. ] Eventually, Hotaru breaks the silence by clearing her throat, clearly wishing to change the subject. The den matron is one of the few still-living people from that era — inasmuch as she can still be considered such — and is no doubt a trove of knowledge of what life was like back then. "Gods forbid[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]! I know my station and do not overstep my bounds." Does knowing her station involve making gossip about the den matron and colonial governor? "Oh, oh, [pc.ra kitsune |but I could not hope to refuse inquiries from your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, especially from someone of your station.
