"Ah, a-actually, there was one thing that I’d heard. J-just a rumor, I assure you, and so patently absurd that I could scarcely entertain the notion, but someone — whose name escapes me at the moment — had implied that yourself and the governor, had, ah—" [pc.isDK |Spit it out already, you’re tired of her dancing around things. |The point, if she would? ] Hotaru blanches, staring directly at you as she resumes. "Th-that the two of you had sex, your Eminence." Immediately backpedaling, Hotaru continues to stammer out a correction. "B-b-but I can assure you, such a rumor isn’t something that I would even consider taking with a grain of truth, your Eminence! After all, s-such a thing would be absolutely absurd, right? It was probably a mere jest I misconstrued, I wager." Hotaru’s usually-cool demeanor is little more than tattered scraps; instead of her typical smirk, her face bears an awkward, queasy grin as she shoots you a pleading glance, profoundly uncomfortable. You suppose that’s the best you’ll get out of her; waving your hand, you echo her limp attempt at humor with a forced laugh of your own, the atmosphere between you thick enough to cut. |Asking Hotaru about her thoughts on the den’s matron, you’re caught off guard has her cheeky smirk grows into a full-blown smile, mischief in her eyes. As she gives you a teasing laugh, she idly strokes a cheek, smiling right at you. "Oh? You want to hear my thoughts on the governor? I’m hardly knowledgeable on the subject; if anything, you should be lecturing me, on account of how close you two have gotten." How’d she find out about that? Komari did her best to— Hotaru gives you a judgmental look, interjecting as you attempt to reason. "You do realize the den matron’s office is rather close to my own dwelling, yes? The walls here are far from thick, [pc.name]. If she were doing her best, she would have at least soundproofed the affair, you know." That’s... a fair point. What’s she doing eavesdropping, though? Hotaru sighs, pinching the bridge of her nose as she rubs her eyes. Not even looking at you, she continues speaking. "To call it 'eavesdropping' would imply intent, [pc.name]. I confess that at first, it was quite amusing; I was doing my best to listen in, at least initially." Hotaru returns her gaze to you, exhaustion in those crimson eyes as she regards you. "And yet, I find myself striving to cover my ears in an endeavor to hear less, by the end of it. I don’t even want to imagine what the two of you have been getting up to, but unfortunately, I have rather a good idea of it. So yes, I am painfully aware of your escapades, against my best wishes." You... don’t really have a response to that. Instead, the two of you sit in silence for a bit, awkwardly staring at each other in a sort of social paralysis. ] Eventually, Hotaru breaks the silence by clearing her throat, clearly wishing to change the subject. "At any rate, was there something else you wished to ask me about, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]?" ] '

rows.original: [party.has kiyoko |Hotaru opens her mouth to speak, and then her vivid red eyes catch sight of Kiyoko standing a little off by your side. Her gaze slides back and forth between the both of you several times, and then she bows her head and speaks. "I have nothing but the utmost respect for the Myobu[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Like the den matron, she is a wealth of knowledge on historical matters and beloved by her subjects. To have the high lady Otomo around helping the den matron with matters of state has made life better for everyone in the colonies, and it is our pride that we feel represented in having a den mother, regardless of what happens. Divine blood cannot be watered down or relinquished." Very diplomatic. Very tactful. And very much wanting to talk about something else, anything else rather than this. |[rand |"I don't get why everyone is taking High Lady Otomo's return so nonchalantly, I really don't. Is everyone else so ground-down by life in the colonies that one simply cannot feel excited any more?" Hotaru looses a huge, dramatic sigh. "This is something that has never happened before in known history — now there are thirteen den mothers. The Myobu is one, there is no doubt: the divine blood of kings cannot be signed away. "Then there's the matter of her return two centuries after her supposed death, and by the actions of [pc.ra kitsune |the newly-minted champion of his divine lordship |an outsider ], no less. How is this not amazing? And yet people are acting disinterested...I just can't take it any more!" [pc.ra kitsune |It's several moments after her outburst that Hotaru's mind catches up with her heart and she remembers who she's speaking to. "O-oh, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. I, uh, forgot myself — " She just about to get on the floor and kowtow to you when you catch her by the scruff of her neck and pull her back up onto her chair. No, no, that's not necessary. You asked for an opinion, and got a honest one. Now, you know you'll probably get some kind of shame in this silly convoluted webway of etiquette if you don't appropriately admonish her for her directness or something, but that's a blow you think you can take. "T-thank you. I just..." Hotaru mops the cold sweat from her brow. So long as she meant what she said and it wasn't just another yarn of hers she's spinning, you're fine. ] |"High Lady Otomo is so graceful," Hotaru says with a wistful sigh. "I'd love to have the chance to take her measurements and put some clothes on her. Every single movement of hers is unsullied and perfect... you are immensely fortunate to have the privilege of being the Myobu's [var0 |husband |consort ], [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name], and don't you forget it ]." Well... that isn't completely right, but it isn't completely wrong, either. It's certainly the image that Kiyoko would like to project upon others, and... maybe you should get back to the point here. It's unlikely that Hotaru will ever get her wish, because Kiyoko makes her own clothes. At least, you've never seen her wear anything that wasn't of her own design, and she only has that one... "Ah! Ah! Even so, there's nothing's stopping her from modeling for me, is there?" The melodrama is oozing off Hotaru at this point, the seamstress nearly outright jabbing her needle into her fingers several times before she catches herself and sets it down in her agitation. "Oh, but I don't dare to ask... if she did agree, I'd faint, and then the opportunity would be wasted." She does realize that she's talking to... wait no, of course she does. She said as much just now. Although you can understand why she'd be reluctant to ask you to pass along the message... how about getting Kinu to do it in her stead? "Oh, the young lady Otomo... I'd love to put some clothes on her, too. She is far more approachable... yes, yes, I'll ask both her and her mother at once. Maybe have them model together and ask someone to capture the divine scene on paper... they would do it for them, right?" |"Ah[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]... as forbidden as it may be, I do sincerely wish that someday I'd be able to hear High Lady Otomo speak about her time living on the astral plane. No doubt it'd be painful for her — that and the vast chasm between our stations makes it a vanishingly small hope — but it's still something I'd like to do if ever given the opportunity." Perhaps that could be arranged in the future, but you're curious as to why, exactly. "The Myobu has had an experience of the sort which is truly unique. To reside within the dream of a god for so long, to have everything provided for and yet be alone, to endure such — that kind of firsthand account of suffering is something that needs to be understood, no matter how painful it is[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. Even if it's only to permit others to comprehend in some small fashion what she went through before meeting you... bitter as it is, it ought not to be forgotten. Bitterness has a place and purpose in a story, and we ought not to forget that." Very poetic, but you're not sure that Kiyoko's experiences in the Astral Plane makes a story. "But are they not[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? We are all the protagonists of our own stories; from a selfish perspective, the way we see the world is about each and every one of us. We make narratives of the events about us to tie them together with meaning, and the one the Myobu has woven is fascinatingly stellar, with the potential to become just as timeless as the legend of the crane wife. Mmm... now that's a tale to capture the imagination." |"Surprisingly — or unsurprisingly for those who know how these things work — High Lady Otomo has not supplanted the den matron in her administrative or leadership positions, even though she technically has every right to. That[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence, ] tells me — and anyone else who has the eyes to see — much about her, and paints her in a positive light." That makes sense. If anything, Kiyoko's been busy managing her own home to deal with Komari's as well. Her faithful retainer's been doing so good a job in the couple centuries of her absence; why change what's working quite well for all parties involved? "Indeed. If anything, the den matron is molding the young lady Otomo for the role, to the point of an engagement with her great-great-grandson and directing Miko and Mai to act as her aides... well, there's that continuity, if nothing else. I really what she has in mind, but the young lady Otomo seems happy enough jumping through the hoops that her elders have set before her, so it can't be bad. It'll be interesting to see what the future has in store for us. Could make for a gripping tale, and one with a happy ending to boot." Wouldn't the people across the ocean have something to say about Komari giving up her appointment of colonial governor to someone else? You get the impression that as infamous as Komari is, she doesn't have that kind of authority to grant her title to someone else. "To be completely honest, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]I fully suspect that the people in the capital wouldn't care so long as the market for goods remains open and materiel and local goods flow back," Hotaru replies with a sigh. "There are other ways of getting around it, too — the den matron might hold onto the title while the young lady Otomo de facto assumes her responsibilities, for one, all the way to her bringing up the matter to the ministries of the left and right to be dealt with. Although I don't think she will do that last one; the high lady has certainly been content to keep a low profile and doesn't want to rock the boat." Hmm... "It is your family's future too, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]but my estimation is that they know what they're doing and it's best to leave them to it. There is reason. There is precedent. What is important is to have legitimacy and continuity, while not presenting oneself as a threat." How does she know all — wait, she's a storyteller, of course she'd know.[pc.bg minstrel | You yourself ought to know, but it's been a while since you actually properly plied your trade as a minstrel, so it slipped your mind. ] "To say that period dramas enjoy a courtly setting is an understatement[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. And while such tales are often embellished as they must be, there's still nevertheless enough truth in them for that requisite verisimilitude. The exact workings may change from generation to generation, but the spirit remains the same." |"As someone close to her, do you think the high lady Otomo has an interest in stories[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" Well, Kiyoko endeavors to be cultured, and folktales happen to fall under that umbrella, so you'd expect her to know something of them, yes. "If only I could request an audience with her sometime and discuss the topic," Hotaru says with a wistful sigh. "Not only seeking tales that might have been lost with the Godswar, but also comparing those that came before with those that came after. Stories themselves change along with the peoples that tell them, and that also goes for which folktales come in and fall out of favor." This really means a lot to her, doesn't it? "My mind needs something to do when my fingers are at work, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]. Once I'm done with the design, the rest is just busywork... but back to the point, do you think the Myobu would deign to see me? I do have red eyes, so surely there must be at least a drop or two of divine blood in my body... would that be enough to request an audience for such a mundane matter, I wonder?" ] ]
rows.translation: [party.has kiyoko |萤张开嘴想要说话，这时她那双鲜艳的红眼睛看到了站在你身旁的清子。她的目光在你们两人之间来回扫了几次，然后低下头说道： “我对Myobu家族只有深深的敬意。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]就像那个族群的女领袖一样，她也在历史事务方面拥有丰富的知识，深受族人的爱戴。有大友这位高位女士协助那位族群女领袖处理国家事务，确实让殖民地里的每个人都过上了更好的生活。我们感到非常自豪，因为有一位这样的领袖来代表我们，无论发生什么情况，这一地位都是不可动摇的。神圣的血统是无法被稀释或放弃的。 真是非常外交辞令，也非常委婉。而且，她显然非常希望转移话题，任何话题都好，就是不想继续讨论这个事情。 |[rand |我真的不明白为什么大家都对高阶女武士大友的回归如此漠不关心，真的不明白。难道在殖民地的生活让大家都变得如此麻木，以至于再也无法感到兴奋了吗？”萤叹了口气，那声叹息充满了戏剧性。“这种事在已知的历史上从未发生过——现在，情况已经变得如此不同了十三那些“母亲般的人物”。毫无疑问，Myobu就是其中之一：王室的血脉是不能被随意转让的。 “还有她在被认为已经死亡两百年之后突然出现这件事，以及她的种种行为[pc.ra kitsune |这位新晋被封为神之仆从的英雄 |一个外人 ]毫不夸张。这难道不令人惊叹吗？然而人们却表现得无动于衷……我真的再也无法忍受了！ [pc.ra kitsune |在她情绪失控地喊叫了几秒钟之后，萤的理智终于赶上了她的情绪，她这才想起自己正在和谁说话。“哦，天啊[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]船……我，呃，有点忘乎所以了——” 她差点就跪倒在地向你磕头了，这时你抓住她的脖子，把她拉回了椅子上。不，不，其实没必要这样。你征求了我的意见，而我给了你一个坦诚的回答。现在你知道了，如果不对她的直率行为进行适当的批评或告诫，那么在这个繁琐复杂的礼仪体系中，你很可能会感到一些羞愧……但你也认为这种后果自己是可以承受的。 谢谢你。我只是……”萤用毛巾擦去额头上的冷汗。 只要她是真心的，而不是又在编造一些故事，那就没什么问题。 ] |大友大人真是优雅至极，”萤叹息着说道，“我真希望能有机会为她量尺寸，然后为她制作一些衣服。她的每一个动作都那么得体、那么完美……能够有幸成为宫本家的成员，你真是太幸运了。 [var0 |丈夫 |配偶 ]， [pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |[pc.name]，而且，你可千万不能忘记这一点。 ]嗯……那可不行。完全地没错，但这也并非完全错误。这确实是纪代子希望别人看到的自己的形象，而且……也许你应该回到正题上来。热奈子很可能永远无法实现她的愿望，因为纪代子都是自己缝制衣服的。至少，你从来没见过她穿过不是自己设计的衣服，而她也只有那一件…… “啊！啊！不过，这总不会妨碍她为我当模特吧？”此时，萤身上散发着一种夸张的戏剧性氛围，那位裁缝几次差点把针扎到她的手指上，直到她回过神来，才慌忙把针放下来。哦，但我不敢问……如果她真的同意了，我肯定会晕过去的，那样的话机会就浪费了。” 她其实很清楚自己在和谁说话……等等，当然她知道。她刚才不就是这么说的吗？虽然你能理解她为什么不愿意让你转达这个消息……但让小娟代她去做这件事怎么样呢？ “哦，那个大友小姐……我也很想给她准备一些衣服穿啊。她是要容易接近得多……是的，我会去问的。两者都她和她妈妈一起吧。或许可以让她们一起进行模特表演，然后请别人把这一幕美妙的场景记录下来……她们肯定会愿意帮忙的，对吧？ |啊[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输 ]尽管这可能被视为一件禁忌之事，但我真心希望有朝一日能够听到高阶女士大友讲述她在星界生活中的一段经历。毫无疑问，这对她来说必定是一段痛苦的回忆——再加上我们彼此所处的立场之间存在巨大的差距，使得这种希望几乎渺茫不可及——但只要有机会，我依然非常渴望能够做到这一点。或许将来可以安排这样的机会，但你确实很好奇，究竟为什么会有这样的安排。 “宫布有着一段真正独一无二的经历。在神的梦境中生活了如此漫长的时间，一切都有人安排，但却始终处于孤独之中，忍受着那样的痛苦——这种亲身经历带来的苦难，无论有多么令人难以忍受，都必须要被人们理解。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输 ]即使这只是为了让别人能够稍微理解她在遇见你之前所经历的一切……尽管那些经历充满痛苦，但我们不应该忘记它们。痛苦在故事中也有其存在的意义和作用，我们千万不能忘记这一点。” 这段话确实很富有诗意，但你是否确定清子的那些在星界中的经历真的能够构成一个完整的故事呢？ “但是，这些经历难道不正是故事的重要组成部分吗？[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]我们每个人都是自己故事中的主角；从自私的角度来看，我们看待世界的方式其实反映了我们每一个人。我们会为发生在自己身边的事情编造故事，以此赋予它们意义。而Myobu所编织的这个故事，实在精彩绝伦，它有可能像“鹤妻”的传说一样，成为永恒的经典。嗯……这真是一个能够激发人们想象力的故事啊。 |令人惊讶的是——对于那些了解这些运作机制的人来说，这其实并不奇怪——高阶女士大友并没有在行政或领导职位上取代那位女头目，尽管从理论上来说，她完全有这个权利。[pc.ra kitsune |阁下， ]这确实说明了很多关于她的事情，也让任何人都能清楚地看到她的真实形象——她被描绘成了一个积极正面的人物。 确实如此。事实上，基约子一直忙于打理自己的家庭，同时还要照顾麻里。在她离开的这两百年里，她那忠实的仆从们表现得非常出色；既然目前的安排对所有相关方来说都十分有效，为什么还要做出改变呢？ “的确如此。事实上，那位女首领正在培养年轻的奥托摩小姐，让她逐渐适应这一角色，甚至已经安排她与自己的玄孙订婚，并指派米可与真希来协助她的工作。嗯，有……至少，这种连贯性是值得肯定的。我真的很想知道她到底在想什么，但大友小姐似乎很乐意按照长辈们为她设定的规则来行事，所以应该没什么不好的结果吧。看看未来会给我们带来什么，一定会很有趣。这完全可以成为一个引人入胜的故事，而且还是一个有着幸福结局的故事。 那么，大洋彼岸的人们，对于麻里放弃自己担任殖民地总督的职位、将其让给别人这件事，难道不会有什么看法吗？你会觉得，尽管小毬声名狼藉，但她并没有那样的权力可以将自己的头衔授予别人。 “说实话， [pc.ra kitsune |阁下， ]我完全怀疑，只要商品市场依然开放，物资和本地产品能够正常流通，京城里的人们根本不会在意这些事情，”萤叹息着回答道。“其实也有其他解决办法——比如女头目可以继续保留这个头衔，而大友家的那位年轻小姐则实际承担起所有的职责，直到她将这个问题提交给左翼政府部门为止。以及人们都有权得到公平对待。不过我觉得她应该不会做出最后那件事来；那位高位女士一直以来都很低调，她肯定也不想惹麻烦。” “嗯……” “这毕竟也是你家庭的未来啊。 [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输工具。 ]但我认为，他们知道自己在做什么，最好让他们自己去处理。这是有原因的，也有先例可循。重要的是要确保行为的合法性与连贯性，同时不要让自己显得像是一种威胁。 她怎么会知道这么多呢——等等，她毕竟是个讲故事的人，她当然会知道这些。[pc.bg minstrel | 你自己应该很清楚，不过已经有一段时间没有真正认真地从事吟游诗人的工作了，所以这件事被你忘掉了。 ] 说古装剧总是以宫廷为背景，这种说法其实还是轻描淡写了。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输 ]虽然这样的故事往往会被添油加醋，但其中确实包含着足够的真实成分，从而使得这些故事具有必要的可信度。具体的实现方式可能会随着世代的更迭而发生变化，但其核心精神却始终如一。 |作为她身边的人，你认为那位高贵的大友大人会对故事感兴趣吗？[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]嗯，清子一直努力让自己显得有文化，而民间故事显然也属于这种‘有文化’的范畴，所以你当然可以预料到她会对这些故事有所了解。” “要是我能找个机会跟她单独聊聊这个话题就好了，”萤叹了口气说道。我们不仅在寻找那些可能随着《神战》的结束而遗失的故事，还在将这些古老的故事与后来的版本进行对比。故事本身会随着讲述它们的人们而发生变化，同样，哪些民间传说会流行起来，哪些又会逐渐被遗忘，也都会受到这些变化的影响。这对她来说真的意义重大，不是吗？ “当我的手指在忙碌的时候，我的大脑也需要一些事情来做[pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |[pc.name] ]等我把设计工作完成，剩下的就只是些琐事了……不过回到正题，你觉得Myobu会愿意见我吗？我的眼睛确实是红色的，所以我的体内肯定至少有一两滴神之血液吧……这样的条件，应该足以让我有资格为这么一件琐事请求会面吧？ ] ]

"Then there's the matter of her return two centuries after her supposed death, and by the actions of [pc.ra kitsune |the newly-minted champion of his divine lordship |an outsider ], no less. How is this not amazing? And yet people are acting disinterested...I just can't take it any more!" [pc.ra kitsune |It's several moments after her outburst that Hotaru's mind catches up with her heart and she remembers who she's speaking to. "O-oh, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. I, uh, forgot myself — " She just about to get on the floor and kowtow to you when you catch her by the scruff of her neck and pull her back up onto her chair. No, no, that's not necessary. You asked for an opinion, and got a honest one. Now, you know you'll probably get some kind of shame in this silly convoluted webway of etiquette if you don't appropriately admonish her for her directness or something, but that's a blow you think you can take. "T-thank you. I just..." Hotaru mops the cold sweat from her brow. So long as she meant what she said and it wasn't just another yarn of hers she's spinning, you're fine. ] |"High Lady Otomo is so graceful," Hotaru says with a wistful sigh. "I'd love to have the chance to take her measurements and put some clothes on her. Every single movement of hers is unsullied and perfect... you are immensely fortunate to have the privilege of being the Myobu's [var0 |husband |consort ], [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name], and don't you forget it ]." Well... that isn't completely right, but it isn't completely wrong, either. It's certainly the image that Kiyoko would like to project upon others, and... maybe you should get back to the point here. It's unlikely that Hotaru will ever get her wish, because Kiyoko makes her own clothes. At least, you've never seen her wear anything that wasn't of her own design, and she only has that one... "Ah! Ah! Even so, there's nothing's stopping her from modeling for me, is there?" The melodrama is oozing off Hotaru at this point, the seamstress nearly outright jabbing her needle into her fingers several times before she catches herself and sets it down in her agitation. "Oh, but I don't dare to ask... if she did agree, I'd faint, and then the opportunity would be wasted." She does realize that she's talking to... wait no, of course she does. She said as much just now. Although you can understand why she'd be reluctant to ask you to pass along the message... how about getting Kinu to do it in her stead? "Oh, the young lady Otomo... I'd love to put some clothes on her, too. She is far more approachable... yes, yes, I'll ask both her and her mother at once. Maybe have them model together and ask someone to capture the divine scene on paper... they would do it for them, right?" |"Ah[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]... as forbidden as it may be, I do sincerely wish that someday I'd be able to hear High Lady Otomo speak about her time living on the astral plane. No doubt it'd be painful for her — that and the vast chasm between our stations makes it a vanishingly small hope — but it's still something I'd like to do if ever given the opportunity." Perhaps that could be arranged in the future, but you're curious as to why, exactly. "The Myobu has had an experience of the sort which is truly unique. To reside within the dream of a god for so long, to have everything provided for and yet be alone, to endure such — that kind of firsthand account of suffering is something that needs to be understood, no matter how painful it is[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. Even if it's only to permit others to comprehend in some small fashion what she went through before meeting you... bitter as it is, it ought not to be forgotten. Bitterness has a place and purpose in a story, and we ought not to forget that." Very poetic, but you're not sure that Kiyoko's experiences in the Astral Plane makes a story. "But are they not[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? We are all the protagonists of our own stories; from a selfish perspective, the way we see the world is about each and every one of us. We make narratives of the events about us to tie them together with meaning, and the one the Myobu has woven is fascinatingly stellar, with the potential to become just as timeless as the legend of the crane wife. Mmm... now that's a tale to capture the imagination." |"Surprisingly — or unsurprisingly for those who know how these things work — High Lady Otomo has not supplanted the den matron in her administrative or leadership positions, even though she technically has every right to. That[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence, ] tells me — and anyone else who has the eyes to see — much about her, and paints her in a positive light." That makes sense. If anything, Kiyoko's been busy managing her own home to deal with Komari's as well. Her faithful retainer's been doing so good a job in the couple centuries of her absence; why change what's working quite well for all parties involved? "Indeed. If anything, the den matron is molding the young lady Otomo for the role, to the point of an engagement with her great-great-grandson and directing Miko and Mai to act as her aides... well, there's that continuity, if nothing else. I really what she has in mind, but the young lady Otomo seems happy enough jumping through the hoops that her elders have set before her, so it can't be bad. It'll be interesting to see what the future has in store for us. Could make for a gripping tale, and one with a happy ending to boot." Wouldn't the people across the ocean have something to say about Komari giving up her appointment of colonial governor to someone else? You get the impression that as infamous as Komari is, she doesn't have that kind of authority to grant her title to someone else. "To be completely honest, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]I fully suspect that the people in the capital wouldn't care so long as the market for goods remains open and materiel and local goods flow back," Hotaru replies with a sigh. "There are other ways of getting around it, too — the den matron might hold onto the title while the young lady Otomo de facto assumes her responsibilities, for one, all the way to her bringing up the matter to the ministries of the left and right to be dealt with. Although I don't think she will do that last one; the high lady has certainly been content to keep a low profile and doesn't want to rock the boat." Hmm... "It is your family's future too, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]but my estimation is that they know what they're doing and it's best to leave them to it. There is reason. There is precedent. What is important is to have legitimacy and continuity, while not presenting oneself as a threat." How does she know all — wait, she's a storyteller, of course she'd know.[pc.bg minstrel | You yourself ought to know, but it's been a while since you actually properly plied your trade as a minstrel, so it slipped your mind. ] "To say that period dramas enjoy a courtly setting is an understatement[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. And while such tales are often embellished as they must be, there's still nevertheless enough truth in them for that requisite verisimilitude. The exact workings may change from generation to generation, but the spirit remains the same." |"As someone close to her, do you think the high lady Otomo has an interest in stories[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" Well, Kiyoko endeavors to be cultured, and folktales happen to fall under that umbrella, so you'd expect her to know something of them, yes. "If only I could request an audience with her sometime and discuss the topic," Hotaru says with a wistful sigh. "Not only seeking tales that might have been lost with the Godswar, but also comparing those that came before with those that came after. Stories themselves change along with the peoples that tell them, and that also goes for which folktales come in and fall out of favor." This really means a lot to her, doesn't it? "My mind needs something to do when my fingers are at work, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]. Once I'm done with the design, the rest is just busywork... but back to the point, do you think the Myobu would deign to see me? I do have red eyes, so surely there must be at least a drop or two of divine blood in my body... would that be enough to request an audience for such a mundane matter, I wonder?" ] ] "

rows.original: [kinu.isInari |[rand |"You have to admire the clothes that the young lady Otomo wears[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Cotton really suits her — she manages to pull off the pastoral look, and yet her garments are suited for hard manual labor without getting in the way or tearing. There's only one question, though..." Yes? "How does she wear all that in the fields without getting it all absolutely filthy? For example, those sleeves — even when I see her going home through the fields at the end of the day she's as pristine as when she wandered in. I can't wrap my head about how she manages to do it it, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]and it's tearing me apart inside. If only I could do that for myself, I could come up with much fancier designs that wouldn't need to be washed with even slight use. Ah... as her [pc.mf |father |parent ], you wouldn't know how she does it, do you?" No, actually. You just took her look for granted. "I won't let this stand. I'll figure out her secret somehow!" |"I've been keeping an eye on the young lady Otomo's efforts for some time now[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Everything she grows is so much more rich and vibrant." You didn't figure her for a vegetable person. "Some vegetables are an interesting if unorthodox source of various dyes, fabric softeners and the like which are useful to my profession[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. The ones that the young lady Otomo are able to bring forth from the earth are absolutely amazing, and if nothing else, someone like me can always use a bit of starch." |Actually, you had a question for her. [pc.ra kitsune |Hotaru bows her head and lowers her gaze. "I will endeavor to aid you in any way I can, your Eminence." |Hotaru tilts her head and wiggles her ears. "Yes?" ] Do... do kitsune use their own fur in clothing? Stuffing, or maybe fur into yarn and then fabric, or just outright fox-fur? "That's an interesting question, but the short answer is yes, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence. I |i ]t does happen." And the long answer? A sigh. "It varies between people, but kitsune fur can be possessed of quite fetching qualities when used in clothing[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. At the same time, people also consider it highly unsanitary to wear clothes made of your own sheddings — or someone else's, for that matter. But it can happen if someone's fur is simply too good, or if one is really destitute. Or you might give such a garment to your lover as a token, and accepting it means the strength of one's feelings is strong enough that one is willing to defy social convention. A bold statement[pc.ra kitsune | to be sure, your Eminence |, isn't it ]? "Either way, if shed fur is to be used in clothing... it needs to be thoroughly sanitized first; salt and bleach stone are good. Otherwise, that's just disgusting. May I [pc.ra kitsune |humbly inquire as to the reason for your interest, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |ask why you're so interested, [pc.name] ]?" Oh, it's because you've seen Kinu's clothes, and — "With that lustre, they almost certainly are. I would imagine that her attitude towards despising waste would tie into that decision." Ah... |You're taking an interest in helping Kinu get to know more people her age. Maybe it's just you seeing things, but the only young folks that she hangs around with in a social context is Mai. Not even Miko, just Mai. Anything else, she just prefers to be with her plants, and it's kind of worrying — you understand that she had less social contact than most other people growing up due to the extraordinary nature of the situation she was in. Hotaru is about her age, isn't she? "I would likely have a few summers on young lady Otomo, but that isn't wrong[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. There's no way to get across my whole meaning without being a little blunt — you're asking me to be her friend, or at least interact with her more?" That's right. She had no one but her family for a long time, and you're worried that it's a trend that she isn't going to outgrow. She's going to succeed her mother someday, and as much as people joke about eccentric nobility she's not going to be able to do her job well while preferring the company of radishes to most people. [pc.ra kitsune |Something flickers behind Hotaru's vivid red eyes for a fraction of a moment, and then it's gone, hiding behind the mask of the seamstress' public persona. "Of course I will do what I can for the young lady Otomo, your Eminence. All of us in the colonies are here to wholeheartedly serve she who her future subjects have named the colonial princess." The colonial princess, huh. Has a nice ring to it. Well, you're grateful that she's willing to help. |Hotaru tucks her ears back against her head and scowls. "Permission to be honest?" ...Yes? "I think it's better for the young lady Otomo that people keep some distance from her and leave her to her business, which she is very good at. Talking to people is not her business. That way, her future subjects will be able to construct an image of her based on her clan's reputation and the stories surrounding her person, instead of actually talking to the girl herself and having said image shattered in quite a horrible way." Harsh, but you feel like Hotaru has some personal experience with this. "I couldn't help myself but seek out such a stellar personage when I heard of her, you know? But the young lady Otomo is not a person with the kind of temperament suited to being social. Talking to people is an art when communication doesn't come naturally, and she lacks the motivation to dumb her words and ideas down so that other people can comprehend them. Hence, she only speaks with Mai and I think it's better that way. As I said, the people love the image they've made of the young lady Otomo, not the girl herself. If they were to hold an extended conversation with her, their opinion might very well change." She's put a lot of thought into this, you see.[pc.bg minstrel | You've had similar experiences in your past as a minstrel working an audience, before all this happened... ] Hotaru shrugs. "I tell stories for my own amusement, [pc.name]. Of course I'd look into how exactly the tools of that trade work. There's more to speaking than just moving your mouth, you know — you've got to be heard.[pc.bg minstrel | You should know. ]" ] |"I will say, whether she consciously does it or not, the young lady Otomo's choice of clothing is magnificent[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." You don't think that she does it deliberately — you've never seen Kinu actually plan an outfit for herself, let alone care how she presents herself to strangers. For her to actually stop and consider the impact she's having on others feels... alien in a sense. It's just not her. "Then you should be glad that her instincts are filling in for her where her conscious mind isn't[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." Could she elaborate a little on that? You're getting the gist of what she's trying to say, but you'd like her to go a little deeper. Hotaru sighs. "[pc.ra kitsune |Of course, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |Sure ]. As someone who designs clothes for a living, one has to be mindful of the statements they make. The young lady Otomo is seen wearing practical, tear-resistant work clothes while in the fields, and those around her see her actions and appearance and feel a kinship with her, regardless of the truth of her actual approachability. They see her long sleeves and modest dress laid over the figure beneath and build an image of well-mannered young woman in their minds. Yet the fact that the dirt, dust and damp of the fields refuse to cling to her person — I have no idea how she manages that — lends an otherworldly quality to her appearance that dissuades people from actually interacting with her despite the kinship they feel. "The end result is, I loosely translate a term from [pc.ra kitsune |our |my ] mother tongue, a goddess of the grain. They admire her from afar with wonder, believe that she is close to their lives, and yet none dare approach the goddess when she walks through their fields turning the earth fruitful." And she got all of that just by studying your daughter's clothes? You think that's just a bit of a stretch, isn't it? "Not all of the effect comes from her fashion sense, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |to be sure ], but it is as much an essential piece of the puzzle as the outward marker of her divine heritage is. It would not work if she dressed herself differently." ] |[rand |"Ah, it is a pleasure to hear the young lady Otomo speak. If only I had a voice like that, I'd be able to captivate an audience like she does[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ] — be it speaking personally or publicly, to hear her words makes you really believe in whatever she's saying without you realizing it — even I, who ought to know better, still required several moments before catching myself and understanding what's going on." This is sounding quite like flattery of your daughter, but do go on. "Oh, it's no flattery, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |to be sure ]. You and I know that the young lady Otomo is above my caliber — talking to people is an art when communication doesn't come naturally, as you need to phrase your message and ideas in a way to get them across. "So many conversations are wasted with people simply talking over each other while waiting to steer the conversation to what they really want to talk about. The young lady Otomo has clearly put the effort into avoiding such messes, and as someone who understands how much of an effort it can be, I approve of her endeavors." |Actually, you had a question for her. [pc.ra kitsune |Hotaru bows her head and lowers her gaze. "I will endeavor to aid you in any way I can, your Eminence." |Hotaru tilts her head and wiggles her ears. "Yes?" ] Do... do kitsune use their own fur in clothing? Stuffing, or maybe fur into yarn and then fabric, or just outright fox-fur? "That's an interesting question, but the short answer is yes, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence. I |i ]t does happen." And the long answer? A sigh. "It varies between people, but kitsune fur can be possessed of quite fetching qualities when used in clothing[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. At the same time, people also consider it highly unsanitary to wear clothes made of your own sheddings — or someone else's, for that matter. But it can happen if someone's fur is simply too good, or if one is really destitute. Or you might give such a garment to your lover as a token, and accepting it means the strength of one's feelings is strong enough that one is willing to defy social convention. A bold statement[pc.ra kitsune | to be sure, your Eminence |, isn't it ]? "Either way, if shed fur is to be used in clothing... it needs to be thoroughly sanitized first; salt and bleach stone are good. Otherwise, that's just disgusting. May I [pc.ra kitsune |humbly inquire as to the reason for your interest, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |ask why you're so interested, [pc.name] ]?" Oh, it's because you've seen Kinu's clothes, and — "With that lustre, they almost certainly are. Her fur is absolutely divine; I would imagine many would judge the weight of the cleanliness taboo to be far outweighed by the glamor of wearing garments spun from your daughter's shed fur[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." Ah... |"[pc.ra kitsune |Oh, your Eminence. ]Do you think the young lady Otomo would model for me, if someone of sufficient standing were to approach and ask?" Is she prodding you to ask Kinu for her? Because that's what it feels like. "Well... in not so many words, yes[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. The young lady Otomo has a very particular kind of body that you don't often see amongst our people, even the colonial-born. She is extremely petite, but also just as curvaceous — I'd love to be able to take on the challenge of making her look even better than she does already." Oh? Why doesn't she ask Kinu herself, instead of going through you? "She is the colonial princess, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |after all ]..." And that makes her less approachable than [pc.ra kitsune |the divine champion? Hotaru lowers her gaze. "With all due respect, are you teasing me, your Eminence?" Yes. Yes, you are. You know perfectly why you're more approachable than Kinu is — it's your stunning good looks, isn't it? There's a moment where Hotaru's clearly weighing whether you're being serious or not, and then she takes the bait and decides to double down. Wrapping a tail about your ankle, the seamstress lowers her voice to a husky purr. "Yes, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, it is indeed your sheer attractiveness that inspires people to overcome the social barriers that would normally separate them from you, and not, say, the absence of such established social barriers which come with being the only champion to be declared within living memory if not longer." |you? Hotaru lowers her gaze. "With all due respect, are you teasing me?" Yes. Yes, you are. You know perfectly why you're more approachable than Kinu is — it's your stunning good looks, isn't it? There's a moment where Horatu's clearly weighing whether you're being serious or not, and then she takes the bait and decides to double down. Wrapping a tail about your ankle, the seamstress lowers her voice to a husky purr. "Yes, it's your stunning good looks, which the young lady Otomo has no doubt inherited from you, given the blatant difference in her figure from her mother and indeed, most of her people." ] Tch. Well, whatever she thinks, you imagine that Kinu needs to get more in contact with her future subjects, and someone like Hotaru will do just fine. Your daughter dearest is a novelty in and of herself, and girl like that doesn't follow fashion, she sets it. "You're telling me to go and approach her myself[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" You're telling her that she should adore her future liege up front. |"Have you seen how the young lady Otomo dresses[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" Given that she's your daughter and you see her on the regular, you'd hope that you've seen her dressed before. [pc.ra kitsune |Hotaru swallows hard and doesn't say anything, but you get the impression that she was biting her tongue hard |"Ha ha, very funny. But there's the point." Hotaru pauses her needlework and frowns ]. "I'm quite envious of her, to be honest." Oh? "She just seems to do everything so effortlessly. For example, I spent so long learning what colors go well together and with what fabrics, and looking at her handcrafted clothes, she just does it all by instinct and gets amazing results that're better than mine." Well, speaking as someone who was there as much as you could be during her formative years, you can say with certainty that while Kinu makes it look easy and while she did have aptitude for just about everything under the sun, it'd have been worthless without any effort going into it. That, and you know that Kiyoko would have driven her with an intensity that would make even a boulder quail. But that's part of her projected image, isn't it? The divine find mundane tasks trivial, performing them with grace, poise and ease. The perfect princess who through her love and competency inspires unwavering loyalty in her subjects. The stuff of stories. "Stories which unfortunately depart just a little from reality too often." Hotaru sighs, and then forces a smile. "But they also have to come from somewhere, and the young lady Otomo appears to be as genuine an article as they come. You and the Myobu are truly blessed[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]." |"The young lady Otomo is well-known to everyone — I daresay that she has far more public appearances than her mother. Maybe it's just me, but it does look like the colonial governor is heavily pushing her into being some kind of symbol or icon... not that it's a bad thing, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |of course ]." Hmm, can she tell you more? You'd do it yourself, but circumstances don't really allow you to keep as close an eye on Kinu's life as you'd like. "[pc.ra kitsune |Most certainly, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. |Sure! ] The most public highlight is that the young lady Otomo will make a public performance every week in the gardens — it truly feels impromptu and not something that's staged, and it's never exactly the same time every week. And while few have the time to pause and listen for the rest of the day, even passing by and hearing her on the zither, or whatever instrument she's chosen to play that day is enough to put a spring in one's step until dusk. But it's mostly the zither..." ...Hmm. You'd think that this organic nature is quite vital to the effort — the effect it has sounds different than what a formal appearance would have. Though you're sure that your daughter has considered it deeply and thought it over up and down no less than thrice, the fact that by Hotaru's account, she manages to make these regular appearance nevertheless feel spontaneous and inspired in nature is saying something. Hotaru's a storyteller — she should know the importance of not being too heavy-handed with a message, and not letting the audience peek behind the curtain... "There is that, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |sure ]. But even for someone like me who understands something of the fundamentals behind what she's doing, the illusion is nevertheless intact, if weaker. That's how much the young lady Otomo is able to exert her presence, and I find it interesting. Is it something that can be learned, or is it intrinsic to divine lineage as her mother's heir?" ] ]
rows.translation: [kinu.isInari |[rand |你真的不得不佩服大友小姐所穿的那些衣服。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]棉质衣物真的很适合她——她能够将那种田园风格的造型演绎得恰到好处，而且这些衣服也适合进行繁重的体力劳动，既不会妨碍她的行动，也不会被弄破。不过，还是有一个问题…… 嗯？ 她怎么能在田里穿着那些衣服活动，却一点都不会弄脏呢？比如那些袖子——即使我看到她每天晚上下班时穿过田地回家，她的衣服也依然干干净净的，一点污渍都没有。我实在想不通她究竟是怎么做到的。 [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输工具。 ]这真的让我内心备受煎熬。要是我也能为自己做到这一点，那我就能设计出一些更加精致的产品了，这些产品即使稍微使用一下也不需要清洗。啊……要是她也能这样该多好[pc.mf |父亲 |家长 ]你根本不知道她是怎么做到的，对吧？” “不，其实并不是这样。你只是把她的那种眼神当作理所当然的事情来看待罢了。” “我绝不会让这种事情就这样过去。我一定要想办法弄清楚她的秘密！ |我已经有段时间一直在关注这位名叫奥托摩的年轻女子的努力了。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]她种植的所有蔬菜都显得更加丰富、更有生机。” 你真没想到她竟然对蔬菜这么感兴趣。 “有些蔬菜其实是各种染料、织物柔软剂等物质的有趣但并不常见的来源，而这些东西对我的工作来说非常有用。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]那位名叫Otomo的年轻女子从大地中挖掘出来的那些东西，确实令人惊叹不已；至少像我这样的人，总是会需要用到一些这样的东西的。 |其实，你本来有话要问她的。 [pc.ra kitsune |萤低下头，目光柔和地说：“殿下，我会尽我所能来帮助您的。 |萤歪着头，抖了抖耳朵。“怎么了？” ] 狐妖们会用自己的毛皮来制作衣服吗？是用来当填充物，还是把毛皮纺成线再制成布料，又或者直接使用狐妖毛皮呢？ Hotaru lowers her gaze. "With all due respect, are you teasing me?" Yes. Yes, you are. You know perfectly why you're more approachable than Kinu is — it's your stunning good looks, isn't it? "[pc.ra kitsune |Most certainly, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. |Sure! ] The most public highlight is that the young lady Otomo will make a public performance every week in the gardens — it truly feels impromptu and not something that's staged, and it's never exactly the same time every week. rows.original: [var0 | "Want to hear a secret, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |or at least something that's not so well-known ]? The military provost likes to head back across the ocean every so often. They're ostensibly for business, since the den matron approves them to begin with, but he obviously takes more pleasure from the chance to stretch his legs than ought to be warranted. "I know this because Kohaku aside, he's the only one around these parts to have money from our homeland on hand, and it's a little more spending money than what's strictly necessary. I've never seen it for myself, but the major roads all have a network of rest stops conveniently spaced a day's travel on foot apart; as an imperial official, the provost has the right to a night's room and board at any honjin for free. I don't mind, though — while he may be uptight in some cases, hearing him speak of his business trips makes for good stories and fuels the imagination." Would she ever want to go there, assuming that her work permitted as such? "Oh, by the gods, no! Today's colonial-born is yesterday's bumpkin from the backwater mountain provinces, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]someone who comes from a place where people are sent as humiliation. Even the military provost's station doesn't exclude him from quiet scorn...well, if I went, I wouldn't make that fact public, but it's hard to hide all your mannerisms. "...I can understand his enthusiasm, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ], I really do. Have you ever experienced a sense of nostalgia for a place that you've never been to before? I think the ancient Belharans had a word for it that escapes my mind right now, but that's the feeling I get when I hear him talk about it when he returns." A sense of nostalgia for a place that you've never been to before, huh? "It's not easy, being born in one place and yet feeling like you rightfully belong somewhere else[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]; take my word for it. This goes doubly so when you don't feel wholly welcome in that somewhere else, either... the military provost may be aggravating from time to time, but I do ask for your leniency in these matters." |"Since the military provost was born into a priestly clan, it was expected when he was young that he would enter some form of religious service eventually," Hotaru says with a small smile. "I remember when I was young and seeing him run around carefree as a kit, then he went on a trip back across the ocean with the den matron and never was the same again. Oh, it was such a waste[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]... it was as if every last iota of whimsy had been boiled right out of him. We must all pass out of childhood sometime, but it's a gradual process; for it to happen all at once for him was sobering, to make an understatement." It's hard to not imagine him as having a huge stick up his butt... or as a kid, for that matter. But she says that he entered a profession that wasn't expected of him? From what you understand, doing that sort of thing is incredibly difficult in this rigid society of theirs... [pc.ra kitsune |and yours, now. ] "If you watched him growing up, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]of course you'd know it wasn't easy. But fewer expectations are placed upon us who don't even rise to the level of provincials, and the colonial governor has money and pull. Filling all relevant governmental positions with her descendants is obviously to her benefit. "There are few ways to actually make meaningful upwards or even sideways moves amongst us[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]; it's one of the reasons why so many turn up for the imperial civil service examinations every five years. Our dear military provost left us for that number of years, and when he returned, I no longer called him by his first name. Not just because of his position, but because there was nothing left about him that I recognized." Hotaru sighs, distracted enough that she nearly jabs herself with her needle. You shake your head at all this — still, he managed to achieve what he wanted in spite of the forces arrayed against him, right? "But at what cost[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? At what cost? Few will speak of it openly, but it's well-known that he's desperately beholden to people who loathe him and want to see him fail. That, and the only reason he has that sword of his is because ceremonial weapons were excluded from the laws on blade lengths some centuries back..." Well, isn't he a downright mess. "The stereotypical ending of a Belharan tale is to send everyone off into the sunset to have a happy life. For us, the stereotype is that the protagonist commits suicide. A bit of an exaggeration, perhaps, but there's a drop of truth to our penchant for beautiful tragedy." |"You know, when I was younger, I fancied myself a match for the military provost," Hotaru says with a wistful sigh, raising a hand to her cheek. "Call me a romantic[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ], but I have a thing for the tragic and melodramatic. Sure, I knew it probably wasn't going to happen, but a girl can dream... now, I'm just counting myself lucky to have dodged an arrow at the last moment. Can you imagine being with such a humorless scold for the rest of your life? I'd be driven to an early grave well before my time, ahaha." Her fancying him... no, you don't want to think about it. "No, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]you don't. But he used to be such the cute kid... I was younger then, too, and feeling certain things for the first time. Just about everyone who was halfway decent-looking and wasn't made of wood or stone were just about on my fantasy list. I teased him for a whole summer, can you believe that? He's the perfect straight man for just about any joke." |You've been wondering about Nakano... "Yes[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" Is his situation common, or is it special? The whole being set an impossible task that he's expected to fail at — that sounds like something anyone with half a brain on either side would refrain from. "Such matters are rather pronounced with us, but certainly not restricted to one people or culture; there are plenty of examples in what folktales of pre-Godswar times remain, and in more recent history, word coming out of the Belharan Heartlands and Jassira. Everyone needs someone to look down upon, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]knowingly or unknowingly — another group to point at and say 'thank the gods that we aren't like them.' "It's long been a pastime of the urban courtiers to needle the provincial governors and warrior class as rubes and hicks — something that I also note was supposedly prevalent in the old Belharan empire[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. With the establishment of the colonies, now even the provincials have someone to look down upon. ]他们才订婚不久，她就已经把他完全掌控在手里了。未来肯定会有很多有趣的事情发生，尤其是对那些喜欢散布谣言的人来说，比如小红这种人。 说句公道话，对于那个可怜的男孩来说，金子几乎在见到别人的瞬间就让他们完全臣服于她的掌控之下。你最亲爱的女儿继承了她母亲的那一套本事——总能让别人按照她的意愿行事，同时让对方误以为这些其实是自己的主意；毫无疑问，她很快就会找到一个像中野这样直率且容易被操控的人，让自己完全掌控局面。至于这是好事还是坏事……嗯，时间会给出答案。 “就像我说的，这是段有趣的时光。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]嗯……在我们的一些圈子里，大友这位年轻女士会被视为女性美德的典范。 [silly |这就是所谓的最佳表现状态，你知道的。 ]仅仅因为这一点，她所散发出的那种魅力就已经相当惊人了。而当人们考虑到这位名叫大友的年轻女士一直在努力将自己的这种天赋发挥到极致时…… “我本身也是一名故事讲述者，因此了解她用来吸引听众的一些技巧；即便掌握了这些知识，我还是会不由自主地被她吸引。那位军事长官……啊，面对这样的力量，他根本没有任何胜算。余生他都将全心全意地执行她的命令，而她却永远不会公开露面。 ]
rows.raw: " [var0 | "Want to hear a secret, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |or at least something that's not so well-known ]? The military provost likes to head back across the ocean every so often. They're ostensibly for business, since the den matron approves them to begin with, but he obviously takes more pleasure from the chance to stretch his legs than ought to be warranted. "I know this because Kohaku aside, he's the only one around these parts to have money from our homeland on hand, and it's a little more spending money than what's strictly necessary. I've never seen it for myself, but the major roads all have a network of rest stops conveniently spaced a day's travel on foot apart; as an imperial official, the provost has the right to a night's room and board at any honjin for free. I don't mind, though — while he may be uptight in some cases, hearing him speak of his business trips makes for good stories and fuels the imagination." Would she ever want to go there, assuming that her work permitted as such? "Oh, by the gods, no! Today's colonial-born is yesterday's bumpkin from the backwater mountain provinces, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]someone who comes from a place where people are sent as humiliation. Even the military provost's station doesn't exclude him from quiet scorn...well, if I went, I wouldn't make that fact public, but it's hard to hide all your mannerisms. "...I can understand his enthusiasm, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ], I really do. Have you ever experienced a sense of nostalgia for a place that you've never been to before? I think the ancient Belharans had a word for it that escapes my mind right now, but that's the feeling I get when I hear him talk about it when he returns." A sense of nostalgia for a place that you've never been to before, huh? "It's not easy, being born in one place and yet feeling like you rightfully belong somewhere else[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]; take my word for it. This goes doubly so when you don't feel wholly welcome in that somewhere else, either... the military provost may be aggravating from time to time, but I do ask for your leniency in these matters." |"Since the military provost was born into a priestly clan, it was expected when he was young that he would enter some form of religious service eventually," Hotaru says with a small smile. "I remember when I was young and seeing him run around carefree as a kit, then he went on a trip back across the ocean with the den matron and never was the same again. Oh, it was such a waste[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]... it was as if every last iota of whimsy had been boiled right out of him. We must all pass out of childhood sometime, but it's a gradual process; for it to happen all at once for him was sobering, to make an understatement." It's hard to not imagine him as having a huge stick up his butt... or as a kid, for that matter. But she says that he entered a profession that wasn't expected of him? From what you understand, doing that sort of thing is incredibly difficult in this rigid society of theirs... [pc.ra kitsune |and yours, now. ] "If you watched him growing up, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]of course you'd know it wasn't easy. But fewer expectations are placed upon us who don't even rise to the level of provincials, and the colonial governor has money and pull. Filling all relevant governmental positions with her descendants is obviously to her benefit. "There are few ways to actually make meaningful upwards or even sideways moves amongst us[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]; it's one of the reasons why so many turn up for the imperial civil service examinations every five years. Our dear military provost left us for that number of years, and when he returned, I no longer called him by his first name. Not just because of his position, but because there was nothing left about him that I recognized." Hotaru sighs, distracted enough that she nearly jabs herself with her needle. You shake your head at all this — still, he managed to achieve what he wanted in spite of the forces arrayed against him, right? "But at what cost[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? At what cost? Few will speak of it openly, but it's well-known that he's desperately beholden to people who loathe him and want to see him fail. That, and the only reason he has that sword of his is because ceremonial weapons were excluded from the laws on blade lengths some centuries back..." Well, isn't he a downright mess. "The stereotypical ending of a Belharan tale is to send everyone off into the sunset to have a happy life. For us, the stereotype is that the protagonist commits suicide. A bit of an exaggeration, perhaps, but there's a drop of truth to our penchant for beautiful tragedy." |"You know, when I was younger, I fancied myself a match for the military provost," Hotaru says with a wistful sigh, raising a hand to her cheek. "Call me a romantic[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ], but I have a thing for the tragic and melodramatic. Sure, I knew it probably wasn't going to happen, but a girl can dream... now, I'm just counting myself lucky to have dodged an arrow at the last moment. Can you imagine being with such a humorless scold for the rest of your life? I'd be driven to an early grave well before my time, ahaha." Her fancying him... no, you don't want to think about it. "No, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]you don't. But he used to be such the cute kid... I was younger then, too, and feeling certain things for the first time. Just about everyone who was halfway decent-looking and wasn't made of wood or stone were just about on my fantasy list. I teased him for a whole summer, can you believe that? He's the perfect straight man for just about any joke." |You've been wondering about Nakano... "Yes[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" Is his situation common, or is it special? The whole being set an impossible task that he's expected to fail at — that sounds like something anyone with half a brain on either side would refrain from. "Such matters are rather pronounced with us, but certainly not restricted to one people or culture; there are plenty of examples in what folktales of pre-Godswar times remain, and in more recent history, word coming out of the Belharan Heartlands and Jassira. Everyone needs someone to look down upon, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]knowingly or unknowingly — another group to point at and say 'thank the gods that we aren't like them.' "It's long been a pastime of the urban courtiers to needle the provincial governors and warrior class as rubes and hicks — something that I also note was supposedly prevalent in the old Belharan empire[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. With the establishment of the colonies, now even the provincials have someone to look down upon. That's simply the case of not just our dear military provost, but just about anyone who holds any title here... his circumstances may be bad, but at least he's not a monster used to frighten children into obedience and industriousness." |Hotaru chuckles and shakes her head. "Can you believe how absolutely oblivious our dear military provost is[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? To spend all those years without being aware of all the burning stares directly planted on the back of his neck. I don't think it's any fundamental failure of sensitivity — even if he doesn't express it well in one medium, his scroll painting is good enough to demonstrate he's not stunted in that regard. "Seriously, now. If not for the den matron stepping in and outright arranging their marriage, we'd never have had this happy ending. One too steeped in inaction to do any more than yearn from a distance, and the other too much of a brick to realize that yearning for that it is. [pc.ra kitsune |My [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship... ]I'm not saying that it's always necessary or even appropriate, but sometimes a little nudging from the right parties is required for everyone's benefit and sanity." %"Nudging" in this case being setting up relationships between people by an old lady with nothing better to do? "Quite so, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence ]." |You've heard a lot about how Rindo's a lot happier now that she's got her fairy-tale marriage with someone she's been pining after for so long. What does Nakano think about it, though? Hotaru smiles. "You're asking me[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? Shouldn't you be asking Kohaku for the latest, juiciest gossip around these parts?" Yes, but she's the storyteller around these parts. "Ah. Well...on the grounds of suitability, there certainly is no question, so he is appeased. Rindo is divine, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]and —" You know full well about how suitable the match is. What you want to know is how he feels about the matchup. "I have it on good authority that he's extremely proud of his wife[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. The man treats her well, and not because he's obligated to — what family she still has is estranged from her at this point. Their personalities are... well, compatible. I would not say that they're guaranteed a happily ever after, but they have a better chance than most." That's good to hear. You didn't make the wrong decision in letting her go... if Rindo will have a safer and happier life this way, you're content. Even if her husband has a stick up his rear when it comes to most people. |"Ahaha. Have you noticed[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? The military provost has been trying to draw his new wife — he keeps on asking for more mulberry paper from me on the side, and each time I have to politely but firmly tell him to go through the proper channels like the den matron requested. Poor man — I've seen some of the scroll paintings he's done, and they manage to capture Rindo pretty well. Nevertheless, the point of a portrait isn't to accurately capture a person's likeness, hmm?" You have to admit, Rindo presents a unique challenge for anyone who wants to make her appear fetching. "Maybe he'd have better luck trying to draw her if she hadn't had such misfortune. Then again, if nothing ill had befallen her, neither of them would be in the positions they're today[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]..." |"It's quite a situation that our dear military provost has found himself caught in, isn't it[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" Hotaru says, eyes twinkling and ears twitching with mischief. "The young lady Otomo is the warrior's three traditional allegiances to the clan, liege, and divine compressed into one person. On one hand, he's much less likely to run into one of those traditional loyalty dilemmas; on the other hand, having all of them neatly wrapped in one package is absolutely terrifying for the poor dear. I don't know what it'll be like in the future from them as a couple, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]but it should be exceedingly interesting." |"There's a rumor going around that the den matron is not so pleased about the match that the Myobu has suggested between her great-great-grandson and the young lady Otomo[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]," Hotaru says with a slight inclination of her head. "Of course, the matron herself would never dare to contradict her liege in such a fashion, but as with any event concerning notable people, there will be talk." Oh? Assuming there was any truth to said rumor — which there is none, of course — what reason could Komari have to oppose an engagement between Kinu and Nakano? Hotaru says nothing at first, her gaze darting from side to side to make sure no one else is around. Then, [pc.ra kitsune | |leaning in close and ]lowering her voice to a conspiratorial stage whisper, she begins: "it's this way, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |you see ]... the military provost has always been quite an ambitious young man. The suitability of such aspirations from one of the — well, he's technically not even from the warrior caste — from one of his station aside, his zeal has gotten him into trouble before. The den matron had been hoping for a match to settle him down somewhat, but the young lady Otomo no doubt has her own ideas, and she worries that he may be driven by his future wife to do something drastic. "Not that such a thing would ever happen, of course, or that the den matron would be contentious enough to dispute the Myobu's assessment of the situation. Foolish rumors abound these days[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]; I would pay little heed to them." And Kinu would no doubt be more discerning than to drive a volatile young man like her fiance to do anything stupid. To be honest, she's never said anything about her long-term plans for the future, being content to simply do as her elders say. Or maybe it just seems that way... |"The military provost and the young lady Otomo make for an excellent couple, don't they[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? They haven't been engaged that long, and she's already got him eating out of her hand. These are going to be interesting times ahead of us, and especially for rumor-mongers like little Kohaku." To be fair to the poor boy, Kinu has just about everyone eating out of her hand within moments of meeting them. Your daughter dearest has her mother's way of making someone go along with what she wants while making the poor sop imagine it was his or her idea all along; there's little doubt that she'll have someone as direct and easily manipulable as Nakano wrapped around her little finger in no time at all. As to whether that's a good or bad thing... well, time will tell. "Like I said, interesting times[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Mmm... in some of our circles, the young lady Otomo would be considered a living ideal of femininity. [silly |This is what peak performance looks like, you know. ]The amount of sheer charisma she exudes from that fact alone is considerable, and when one considers that the young lady Otomo has been schooled in developing that talent to its fullest... "I'm a storyteller and know some of the tricks that she uses to keep an audience enthralled; even with that knowledge behind me, I still fall for them. The military provost... ah, he has no hope against such a force. He'll be wholeheartedly doing her bidding for the rest of his life without her hand ever being revealed." ] "

rows.original: [kohaku.anyKids |[rand |You're curious. Could she make Kohaku's old clothes fit again? While Kohaku wearing the clothing of her people is pretty great, there's something to be said for her old outdoors outfit, as it were. You wouldn't mind seeing her back in her previous clothes, if letting them out or something is a possibility. "Let's be frank, my [pc.swornGod keros |[pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |dear ]: there's absolutely no 'letting out' of those clothes. Kohaku isn't so small now, even if it isn't in the upward direction —" Hotaru makes some stretching gestures — "and there's no possible way anyone's stretching the original material to cover her body ripening like that." So... she can't do it? "Not as I am right now, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |no ]. I suppose if I got my hands on enough of the correct fabrics and such, had a little bit to study the clothes themselves and had some materials to waste on learning I could eventually fashion something similar but in a larger size." Well, now that she has a kit to care for, Kohaku's only taking day trips. No overnight ones, unfortunately, which limits her activities somewhat. Bringing back that sort of stuff for Hotaru to experiment on — "[pc.ra kitsune |Perhaps if I may humbly suggest an alternative way of looking at the situation, your Eminence?" Hotaru dips her head respectfully. "A different perspective, as it were." Oh? Do tell. "I entreat you to imagine our dear quartermaster some years in the future, your Eminence |But you know what? Even if I could, I wouldn't do it." What? Why? "Imagine a Kohaku several years down the road, my friend ]. She goes to her clothes trunk, opens it up, and stares down at the tiny little skirt and figure-hugging leggings that she used to be able to squeeze herself into, bottom-heavy or not. Every year she does this, perhaps hoping that something will have changed, and it has — with every year, the fleeting hope that she'll be able to fit back into them grows more and more distant." Hotaru wiggles her ears and grins; she's clearly enjoying spinning this yarn a bit too much. "It's not going to happen. It will never happen. And I want to see how this story ends — whether it be with her either throwing them out or handing them down to her daughter, or keeping them until her dying day. Whether it's a tragedy or a comedy... well, that's really up to her to decide, isn't it?" She's absolutely vicious when she wants to be, that's all you're going to say. "A good storyteller must be able to evoke a medley of emotions[pc.swornGod keros |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. I do want to see how this plays out." |Does she mind that Kohaku's leaving your kit with her when she goes out on a trading run? "Mmmh. I don't mind in the least, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |no ]," Hotaru purrs as she dips her head and folds her ears. "The child and I... from the first moment I laid eyes upon her, even with one so young, I was quick to recognize a kindred spirit when I saw one. [pc.swornGod keros |An energetic young spirit... certainly I can see much of myself in that. When two personalities are so close, why would I ever mind being her occasional caretaker? It simply means I can pass the kit back to her mother at the best of times, your Eminence — there is no room for complaints, none at all |Not the kind of kit I'd want to be a mother to, you understand, but someone to care for a little while and spoil thoroughly before handing her back to her mother. Kohaku's the one who has to do all the troublesome parts, I just have to be myself, that's all ]." There's just something in the way that Hotaru says it that sends sends a chill down your spine. You wouldn't want to be Kohaku in a dozen years' time... |"Oh, there's something about Kohaku's kit that makes me really ache for one of my own, your Eminence. It's not like I haven't seen my fair share of the young before, but this one..." the seamstress sighs wistfully. "Even so young, this one is truly a child after my own heart. Maybe after I'm done babysitting this little gremlin I'll go and rethink my life, get over this hump that's been keeping me in place all this while and make one of my own." Hey, if she's enthusiastic about it, why bother waiting? The road ahead is long, so there's no reason to stall any further — by the time things have fallen in place for her, Kohaku's kit should be old enough to be toted around with her mother. The more nomadic lupine tribes used to do something like that all the time, walking around with puppies on backs; that's where the term %"puppy pack" comes from, after all. "Mmmmh. Maaaybe. It would still be a conscious decision instead of a happy accident like Kohaku's has been." She laughs at that, although there's little humor in it. "Not that we colonials have any expectations placed upon us, what with being the lowest of the low. But still... as passionate as losing control over oneself in the heat of the moment may be, there's something to be said for the torrid tension in performing the act with the full lustful intention of conceiving a child, and that's the poison which I wish to drink deeply from when the time comes." It sounds like she's all got it planned out... "Far from it, [pc.swornGod keros |your Eminence. F |f ]ar from it. But there's so much infectious energy spilling about these days, I might wind up motivated to take action myself. I'm not going to be young forever, after all, and won't have the kind of lifespan that say, Rindo has to be able to drag my feet as much as I want." |Is it that common for kitsune to not want to name their kits for the few handful of months of their lives? "Depends, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |really ]." Hotaru taps her fingers together as she considers the question. "There's no real set period, from what I hear — some do three months, others do six, I think the mountain province where Kohaku's kind comes from has it up to a year. Then there're the snobs who loudly proclaim it a silly superstition and grab it as an excuse to posture about how enlightened they are. Really, now." Hmm... "If you want to know how long it'll be with Kohaku, why don't you go ask her yourself[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? Oh wait, you can't, because asking how long it'll be before a baby is out of danger of crib death isn't something [pc.swornGod keros |a divine champion is expected to do, begging your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship's pardon |people do, oh no ]." You sigh. She really has a way with words, doesn't she? "I'm a storyteller on the side[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. That means I've got a flair for the dramatic, even the somewhat depressing dramatic." Hotaru shifts her eyes. "I'm just going to say that all the people sneering down at the unwashed masses who believe in superstitious nonsense tend to have the money and means to make things better when disaster strikes, as opposed to those who don't. Just saying." ] |[kohaku.pregStage 1 2 4 |[rand |"Oh, I was absolutely thrilled to hear that dear Kohaku's caught a kit in her belly," Hotaru purrs. "Truth be told, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]I still am. It's going to be so, so amazing all around." Because she'll have to come here for new clothes? "No, she already has all the maternity wear she needs. But... finally! An excuse for me to prod her into ditching that garish outfit — what do those skirts even do, anyway? Besides, she looks so much better when fully in black." There's always a chance that Kohaku might be able to fit back into her old clothes once she's given birth... Hotaru stares at you[pc.swornGod keros |. You can tell she's desperately trying to stifle her laughter, but it's a foregone conclusion: despite being in the presence of authority, despite all etiquette that's been instilled in her since birth, Hotaru simply can't hold it in. Whatever force of dreary melancholy that's instilled in all kitsune from birth must've passed over the seamstress, for she eventually bursts into a giggling fit, wringing her hands as she struggles unsuccessfully to keep it in. "Oh. Oh dear, oh dear. P-please forgive me for the display, your Eminence, but — oh, oh, I just can't —" |, then bursts out into ringing peals of laughter. She doesn't try to contain herself in the least, instead doubling over and leaning against the nearest wall to prevent herself from falling to the floor altogether. Whatever force of dreary melancholy that's instilled in all kitsune from birth must've passed over the seamstress, for she laughs so hard that she doubles over and gets all wheezy, wisps of foxfire rising from her skin and dancing in the air. "Fit back into her old clothes," Hotaru gasps. "That's a good one, that's a good one. Oh dear, oh dear." ] Given her profession, she really does have a front row seat to kitsune women outgrowing their clothes over the course of bearing kits, huh? No one knows better than a seamstress, it's true... "Well, it's an old wives' tale that one of the reasons we wear our sashes so high up is to give our tummies ample room to grow over the year we're with child. That, and everything is all folds and knots so an increasingly maternal body can be accounted for. The changes are different between each woman and each pregnancy, but a general improvement is expected all around." Hotaru grins and rubs her hands together. "Of course, whether you choose to believe such silly tales from an equally whimsical storyteller is completely up to you[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Ahem." So, that does mean that there's still a chance that Kohaku will still be able to fit her clothes after she's borne the child? [pc.ra kitsune |"Chance? Well, maybe, your Eminence. Given how tiny that walking fashion disaster is, though, I wouldn't wager my month's allotment from the storehouse on it, that's all I'm saying. This is going to be quite interesting to watch." |"Chance? Whoever said anything about leaving it to chance? Oh no, by the time she squeezes that kit out of her, she'll never be able to wear that walking fashion disaster ever again." Hotaru has a small, nasty smile on her lips as she puts her hands together. "All it takes is a fruit-filled sweet dessert here, some deep-fried cabbage cakes there, some lovely grilled pond smelt with firm flesh and a wonderful taste... the delights of home-cooked food for someone who works so hard, haha. "I'm sure you've noticed it by now, the way her appetite has doubled, tripled, quadrupled. What's an extra meal a day to a little thing like her with a baby growing in her belly? Just eat eat eat eat, and it's going not just into her tummy, but her tits and thighs too. [kohaku.wellFed |You've been feeding her too, haven't you? Just watching a little creature like her pack away a mind-boggling amount of food for the sheer amusement of it? Ehehehe, great job, great job ]. Save for the obvious baby bump, it's pretty well-hidden under her clothes, but I can tell when it's happening. There's going to be no way that Kohaku's fitting into that eyesore by the time I'm through with her." She's not worried about Kohaku finding out? "Oh, given how much gossip the little chatterbox goes through, I'm sure she already knows. And that's the best thing about making sure she becomes nice and curvy while with child — she won't be able to help herself one bit. And when those garish clothes are finally gone... she'll have to wear those that I put together for her, instead of just on festivals. Ah..." You look Hotaru up and down and shake your head. If this is how she treats her friends, you really, really wouldn't want to be her enemy. ] |"Ever since she was given the responsibility of being the storehouse quartermaster, I've urged Kohaku to train one of her underlings to be able to lead a trade caravan should she become indisposed," Hotaru says with a sigh. "Every time I've brought it up, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]she kept on putting it off... well, now look at what's happened. She's in no shape to go anywhere, and that's just going to be moreso the case in the coming months. If my finished clothes start piling up in the storehouse... well, I know who to blame." But Hotaru still can function at some basic level, right? "[pc.ra kitsune |I thank you for you concern, your Eminence. ]Yes, I'm mostly self-sufficient, and the same could be said of the entire colony; the mulberry paper will still keep flowing, if nothing else," Hotaru sighs. "The perfumed prince has an unending need of it. Oh well, someone will rise to the challenge, I'm sure. The den matron can be ruthlessly efficient when she puts her mind to it — I pity the poor rag who ends up being the one to lead the caravans." |"You know, [pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence, ]Kohaku's always had her happy smiling customer-pleasing face on since she was given dominion over the storehouse. Even I who grew up with her was having trouble picturing her as having anything but that people-pleaser smile... the important thing here is, was." To be fair, it's not really her fault. Every time you go and see her in the storehouse, she makes an effort to be energetic and upbeat like she was before. "And sometimes she even manages it,[pc.ra kitsune | your Eminence, ]" Hotaru purrs. She tries to cover up her smug little smile, but not quickly enough. "Oh, for her to bear the suffering of irate people, of those looking to take advantage of a tiny golden creature, of trying to do business with cheats, liars, and people too stupid to bundle sticks together. All she has suffered in good time with an unwavering smile, dedicated to the task of gathering goods for the den at the best deals. Nothing has ever soured her upbeat nature that she's donned like a mantle... up until the little thing has a big baby in her belly. Ah, surprises are coming from every direction these days, are they not? To think that this would be the thing that cracked the mask and brought her down. rows.original: [var0 |Since she says she was born here... how long have Miko and Mai been shrine maidens? But a me of fifteen or sixteen summers certainly had an outsized influence on how the uniforms eventually turned out, given that they came to me for advice quite often."
