rows.original:
Now this is an interesting missive you see laid out on the table amongst the others. While you knew the kitsune were interested in metals in the region, you didn't know they cared about gemstones too.
            
            Nakano's eyes dart over to the scrip in particular, and he [pc.ra kitsune
                |gives you a little dip of his head. "Your Eminence, one of the commissions of this colony is to study the lay of the land in all its respects and deepen our understanding of it; my cousins have inherited this endeavor from their predecessors, who did the same for those who came before them. While I mostly understand geomancy from the perspective of its usage in war and other conflict, Miyuki prefers to take a broad approach to these matters and likes to have as many pieces in hand as possible before attempting to put them together."
                
                And this results in requests for rocks and gems.
                
                "Since she cannot go to the locations for obvious reasons, your Eminence, the reasonable alternative is to bring bits of these locations to her. It is nice to have goals that are well-defined and theoretically achievable every now and then, even if the practicality of doing so is in question."
                
                Odd of him to call that last bit into question.
                
                Nakano stiffens, but doesn't pursue that particular thread of thought; you can envision his mind simply snipping it altogether before it has any chance of troubling him. 
                |clears his throat. "Oh. That. My cousin Miyuki would like to have some of the local gems for geomantic purposes — studying the lay of the land and all that. While it isn't directly related to the security of the den as a whole, she still considers it important enough to involve me and mine."
                
                So Mai sees fit to use him as her errand boy.
                
                Contrary to expectations, Nakano doesn't take offense at the not-so-subtle jibe and deflates a little. "That is an accurate, if blunt, assessment of that facet of our relationship, yes. That is not to say that studying the lay of the land in all its forms is not part of the colonial commission, but there are proper ways in which to request something that is out of another's official purview.
                
                "But happily, since we have a willing local eager to help us with the matter, that will not be a problem, would it?"
                
                Hey now, you didn't give your word as to whether you'd take the job or not — you haven't even heard the details.
                
                "Oh, do come now. It is well-known that the natives of this land are direct, honest and boisterous, a people who value straight talk and wear their hearts on their sleeves. You would never ask about something if you were not interested in it, were you?" Nakano tries to clap you on the shoulder, a motion that makes it painfully clear that he's not used to doing such. "I am absolutely sure you will be using your knowledge and acumen to ingratiate yourself with my cousin and be of service to us all."
            ]
            
            The details, if he doesn't mind. He thinks the items Mai has requested will be too difficult to obtain?
            
            "I am no prospector, but the territorial claims of the known location makes travel to said location difficult, and the other is not clear to us altogether. [pc.ra kitsune
                |As you understand, your Eminence, in this particular case I am but a messenger, someone to apportion responsibility for tasks, or in your esteemed case, spread the word of an opportunity
                |Frankly, with the way my cousin penned the missive, I suspect she was deliberately vague in her wording in order to infuriate me. Of course, I have no concrete proof of such, but that is exactly what makes that brand of teasing insufferable
            ]. Either way, it would be best if you consulted with Miyuki yourself, in order to prevent errors from being introduced into the message as it is passed along."
            
            Is this matter urgent?
            
            "It is not[pc.ra kitsune
                |, your Eminence
            ]. However, as my cousin put it, she would like it done within the year, if at all." [pc.ra kitsune
                |Standing, Nakano gives you a bow from the waist. "Best of fortune to you, divine champion; I am sure you will return to us victorious posthaste. Pardon me for breaking off this conversation, but I need to inform my cousin that the task has been taken. She will no doubt be expecting you shortly and be ready to receive you with all the honors that are due your station."
                |Nakano waves you off. "Well then, run along now. I have to write to Miyuki and let her know you're on your way to her."
                
                She's just downstairs, yes? 
                
                "Correct, but doing so creates a paper trail of accountability and responsibility that isn't there in a verbal message. It's all right, I wouldn't expect you to understand anyway. Now, if you don't mind."
            ]

你看，桌子上摆放着这些信件，其中有一封确实挺有意思的。虽然你早就知道那些狐族对这一地区的金属很感兴趣，但没想到他们也对宝石感兴趣。

中野的目光特别落在了那封信上，他[pc.ra kitsune
                |他微微点了点头，说道：“阁下，这个殖民地的任务之一就是全面了解当地的地形地貌，加深我们对这些地区的认识；我的几位堂兄弟也是继承了前人的这一职责，他们的前辈们也为他们的前人做过同样的工作。虽然我主要是从风水在战争与其他冲突中的应用角度来理解它的，但美雪更倾向于采用一种更为全面的角度来探讨这些问题，并且喜欢在尝试将各种因素结合起来之前，尽可能收集到更多的信息。这就导致了人们对岩石和宝石的需求。

“由于她出于显而易见的原因无法前往那些地方，阁下，一个合理的解决办法就是将这些地方的样本带给她。偶尔设定一些定义明确、理论上也能够实现的目标，确实是一件好事——即便这些目标的可行性在实际操作中还存在疑问。

rows.raw:
'
            Now this is an interesting missive you see laid out on the table amongst the others. While you knew the kitsune were interested in metals in the region, you didn't know they cared about gemstones too.
            
            Nakano's eyes dart over to the scrip in particular, and he [pc.ra kitsune
                |gives you a little dip of his head. "Your Eminence, one of the commissions of this colony is to study the lay of the land in all its respects and deepen our understanding of it; my cousins have inherited this endeavor from their predecessors, who did the same for those who came before them. While I mostly understand geomancy from the perspective of its usage in war and other conflict, Miyuki prefers to take a broad approach to these matters and likes to have as many pieces in hand as possible before attempting to put them together."
                
                And this results in requests for rocks and gems.
                
                "Since she cannot go to the locations for obvious reasons, your Eminence, the reasonable alternative is to bring bits of these locations to her. It is nice to have goals that are well-defined and theoretically achievable every now and then, even if the practicality of doing so is in question."
                
                Odd of him to call that last bit into question.
                
                Nakano stiffens, but doesn't pursue that particular thread of thought; you can envision his mind simply snipping it altogether before it has any chance of troubling him. 
                |clears his throat. "Oh. That. My cousin Miyuki would like to have some of the local gems for geomantic purposes — studying the lay of the land and all that. While it isn't directly related to the security of the den as a whole, she still considers it important enough to involve me and mine."
                
                So Mai sees fit to use him as her errand boy.
                
                Contrary to expectations, Nakano doesn't take offense at the not-so-subtle jibe and deflates a little. "That is an accurate, if blunt, assessment of that facet of our relationship, yes. That is not to say that studying the lay of the land in all its forms is not part of the colonial commission, but there are proper ways in which to request something that is out of another's official purview.
                
                "But happily, since we have a willing local eager to help us with the matter, that will not be a problem, would it?"
                
                Hey now, you didn't give your word as to whether you'd take the job or not — you haven't even heard the details.
                
                "Oh, do come now. It is well-known that the natives of this land are direct, honest and boisterous, a people who value straight talk and wear their hearts on their sleeves. You would never ask about something if you were not interested in it, were you?" Nakano tries to clap you on the shoulder, a motion that makes it painfully clear that he's not used to doing such. "I am absolutely sure you will be using your knowledge and acumen to ingratiate yourself with my cousin and be of service to us all."
            ]
            
            The details, if he doesn't mind. He thinks the items Mai has requested will be too difficult to obtain?
            
            "I am no prospector, but the territorial claims of the known location makes travel to said location difficult, and the other is not clear to us altogether. [pc.ra kitsune
                |As you understand, your Eminence, in this particular case I am but a messenger, someone to apportion responsibility for tasks, or in your esteemed case, spread the word of an opportunity
                |Frankly, with the way my cousin penned the missive, I suspect she was deliberately vague in her wording in order to infuriate me. Of course, I have no concrete proof of such, but that is exactly what makes that brand of teasing insufferable
            ]. Either way, it would be best if you consulted with Miyuki yourself, in order to prevent errors from being introduced into the message as it is passed along."
            
            Is this matter urgent?
            
            "It is not[pc.ra kitsune
                |, your Eminence
            ]. However, as my cousin put it, she would like it done within the year, if at all." [pc.ra kitsune
                |Standing, Nakano gives you a bow from the waist. "Best of fortune to you, divine champion; I am sure you will return to us victorious posthaste. Pardon me for breaking off this conversation, but I need to inform my cousin that the task has been taken. She will no doubt be expecting you shortly and be ready to receive you with all the honors that are due your station."
                |Nakano waves you off. "Well then, run along now. I have to write to Miyuki and let her know you're on your way to her."
                
                She's just downstairs, yes? 
                
                "Correct, but doing so creates a paper trail of accountability and responsibility that isn't there in a verbal message. It's all right, I wouldn't expect you to understand anyway. Now, if you don't mind."
            ]
            
            '

rows.original: After hearing Nakano give his brief summary, you shake your head and state there's nothing on the table that you're inclined to pick up at the moment. "As you wish[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]." Nakano's expression is perfectly and politely emotionless in that blank mask you've seen a number of kitsune wear in public. Wonder which is stronger beneath that carefully constructed facade — disappointment or frustration? Nevertheless, he puts away the missives on the shelf, stacking them neatly, then seats himself once more and regards you. "Anything else you might wish to inquire of me?"
rows.translation: 在听完中野的简要总结后，你摇了摇头，表示目前没有任何方案让你感兴趣，愿意考虑采纳。 “如你所愿[pc.ra kitsune|，我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]。”中野的表情毫无情绪，那副你曾在许多狐妖在公共场合戴过的空洞面具，将他的情感完美地隐藏了起来。不知道在这层精心构筑的外表之下，究竟是失望更强烈，还是沮丧更甚呢？不过，他还是把那些信件放回架子上，整齐地叠好，然后再次坐下，注视着你。“还有其他什么你想向我咨询的吗？”

Kinu is your daughter, after all, and [pc.ra kitsune|you think he would agree that she has quite the pedigree on both sides of her family. More than a suitable match, given the circumstances|despite you being a filthy, barbaric outsider and all, you are concerned for her well-being]. Certainly there is no problem with asking about her, is there? "No, of course not. You are her [pc.mf|father|parent], after all." The chink in his armor vanishes as quickly as it'd appeared. He looks a little worried at perhaps being contentious when speaking of his ancestor and liege, yet goes on anyway. Poor bastard must feel pretty strongly about this... "She already thinks me too much of a romantic and too ambitious, even if said ambition is not wholly for myself; were I to marry into high nobility, those tendencies and passions would be inflamed even further. I am not entirely sure she would rather not have me settle with some provincial maid, but she is entirely within her power to order me to stop seeing the young lady Ōtomo if she had the mind to do so." Well, you're not going to question the den matron's wisdom, but maybe Komari understands that her own personal misgivings don't outweigh the benefits of tying her house with that of her own liege. That, and it makes it all the better that he and Kinu actually like each other to begin with; it makes such matters go over far more smoothly. Nakano looks even more troubled at that, but nods hesitantly. "Great-great-grandmother is possessed of the wisdom and foresight to set aside her own misgivings for the good of others. It is something that I am attempting to learn myself in steps, especially given the nature of my station and commission." You're sure that having Kinu by his side in his endeavors will make them all the more successful, and prevent him from going overboard where Komari has misgivings. "Yes. Yes, that is right." The tone with which Nakano's saying it suggest he's trying to convince himself more than he is you, but hey, if it'll bring them closer together... "That is an angle that I should seek to extend further. Perhaps it will deepen our relationship in a positive manner." ] [party.has kiyoko |[rand |Hearing all this, Kiyoko makes a little purring noise in the back of her throat and smiles, leaning forward on Nakano's desk. "I am very pleased to hear from others that my daughter has grown into such an enthralling yet refined young vixen. You seem like an adequately capable young man with drive and passion in serving both Komari and the empire's interests across the ocean." Those words, neatly driven by the careful weight of Kiyoko's authority, shatter the iron mask of Nakano's facade of careful composure. Ears folding forward atop his head, the military provost openly winces, his gaze respectfully avoiding Kiyoko's. "I — um, ah, am greatly honored by your praise, [silly|Myobu-sama|Lady Ōtomo], even if I do not deserve it..." "Well, if there is something you did do to be unworthy of my praise, [silly|Taisa-san|Provost], it would be to be overambitious. Zealously advocating for the position of your liege and clan's fortunes is one thing; aspiring to greater rank, power or wealth for oneself is another, and sometimes it can be hard to tell between the two. Oftentimes unfortunate warriors justify the latter with the former; I am not accusing you of such, but you would do well to remember your great-great-grandmother's concerns. Serve the empire well and do right by the Kurokawa name, but beware of allowing desire for recognition and glory lead you astray. Colonials are already disparaged in the homeland; do not give them further reason to look down upon all who reside here, my daughter included." I — I will remember that." "Kinu will help you stay on the right path. She has, after all, had an education." |Upon hearing this account, your kitsune wife turns her gaze skyward and contrives to look thoughtful. "I, too, am pleased that you are getting on so well with my daughter, Provost. Such a nice and eager young man you are — you remind me of some of the boys whom would flit around me back in the day, hoping to draw me away from my studies. Oh well, my daughter and you make for quite the adorable couple, don't you? Girls as elegant and well-educated as her are hard to find out here on the frontier. You do deserve each other, no more, no less." The words emerge from Kiyoko's mouth dripping sincerity so thick you could slice it with a knife. You glance between your kitsune wife and the man who might possibly be your future son-in-law, wondering at the sudden tension in the air, and then the carefully applied weight of Kiyoko's words crumbles Nakano's steely facade like a heap of bricks. "T-thank you, [silly|Myobu-sama|Lady Ōtomo]. Forgive me, I... I am not used to being praised like this from those outside of my family." "Oh! Just like Kinu, then. She has had an education, but not an experience — there is still much that is left for her to learn which is impossible for me to teach." "Do not belittle your efforts, [silly|Myobu-sama|Lady Ōtomo] — Kinu is every bit the match for any of the younger ladies at the imperial court." "Oh, so truly lacking in experience in anything and everything outside of their little political and status games, if they are anything like those of my time were. I hope you will be of assistance to my daughter, Provost — she has so many needs that even she herself may not be aware of." "I... of course." |Hearing all this come from Nakano, your fox-wife smiles and gives him a gentle dip of her head. "My, aren't you two the busy duo. I approve of all this quite wholeheartedly." "I... [silly|Myobu-sama|Lady Ōtomo]?" "However Komari may feel about the two of you being together, I do imagine that the both of you do indeed make for quite the charming couple. I certainly have no issue with you being with my daughter, Provost." "Such praise coming from one of your station, [silly|Myobu-sama|Lady Ōtomo] —" Your fox-wife waves off Nakano's protests dismissively. "I know something of the situation you've found yourself in, and how you are bravely facing down a task others would have considered perilous if not outright impossible. That's quite brave and admirable in itself — I'm sure that with my daughter's help, you'll make it through. Couldn't have made a better choice myself, to be honest." "I — thank you." ] Well, that was something all right. Praise coming down from high office, especially from someone so close to Kinu, has thrown poor Nakano for a loop. Looking extremely smug and pleased with herself, your fox wife leans in you kiss you on the cheek and whisper into your ear. "Those like him are so fun to tease; he will make for an excellent son-in-law. Nonetheless, I meant every word of what I said to him. There are worse choices our daughter could have made in selecting a potential consort; I'm just glad that she took her lessons to heart." ] That looks to be the end of this particular thread of conversation for now; you don't think Nakano [party.has kiyoko|is in much shape to even approach the subject of Kinu after your fox-wife's thrown him that much off-kilter|is going to be volunteering any more details for now]. Perhaps you should move onto other business for a bit? '

rows.original: [flags.NAKANO_TRAIN |"It is my honor to be able to instruct you, your Eminence. You are a quick and perspicacious learner — exceedingly to, to the extent that would astound most people." Oh, such flattery. "It remains the fact that you are able to acquire and understand techniques and matters in days and weeks that would take others months or years of practice and learning to even begin to familiarise themselves with. That expedites these efforts considerably." Even though Nakano is as calm and peaceable as a still lake, you can tell that he's really not happy about this. To him, martial art and prowess is a matter of philosophy and a way of life in itself, and having to do this seriously upsets him deeply — and yet he cannot disobey his great-great-grandmother and liege, let alone his god. [pc.isDK |Well, sucks to be him. You need every scrap of power, every option you can make use in your quest before you and you're not going to stop just because an insufferable brat feels bad about it. |It feels a little bad to do this to him, but you don't really have years to sit about doing... whatever it was he did. Part of the reason you agreed to all of this was that you needed every scrap of power you could get to deal with this crisis, and you need to come into yourself now. If you really must, there'll be plenty of time to sit down and study once Kasyrra and everything else has been dealt with. ] "If you will let me know what you intend, the lesson can begin forthwith." |Nakano's expression remains peaceably calm as you broach the topic, but something flickers behind his gaze as you broach the subject. "That is correct, your Eminence. In fact, his divine lordship personally dropped by some time ago to let me know that I should make myself available about this time today, because you would ask me this question." Ah, Keros getting up to his usual tricks as always; two coppers says he did it just to watch the man squirm. The distaste for the thing that he has to do and yet must hide, juxtaposed against a direct order from — well, it doesn't get much higher in the foxen hierarchy than Keros himself. [pc.isDK |And you have to admit — watching the bastard squirm like that, caught in the trap of his own beliefs so blatant it's a played-out theme in Old Country classics, is hilarious. Maybe it's because you're his champion now, but you're starting to see how Keros can find humor in this |It feels a little bad to see a man squirm like that, caught in the trap of his own beliefs so blatant it's a played-out theme in Old Country classics, but at the same time this outcome couldn't have been avoided. It's too much to hope that Nakano will actually rethink his fundamental perspectives, but at least watching him carefully avoid the blind spots in his beliefs is amusing in a way. This is certainly what Keros was going for, at any rate ]. Well, will he do it? "Of course, your Eminence. It is to our eternal shame and regret that the situation is such that even the seat of the imperial governor does not warrant a proper dojo for the practise of skill at arms, but I will make alternative arrangements such that you may be instructed in the usage of foxfire and other faculties in engagement." That's good.[flags.FLOOF_HAUS_NAKANO_RESOLUTION 1 2 3 |Even though you managed to defeat him during your first encounter, this is a field in which he undoubtedly surpasses you — you'll be happy to take instruction from him in that regard. What's the thing these foxes say at a time like this? Please be kind to me? Nakano winces at that; reminding him of that shame certainly had the intended effect. He's just got so many big and obvious buttons, it's hard not to want to press them. |It will greatly please you to have such a capable teacher at hand. After all, he managed to defeat you when you first met — that should suffice to prove his strength, shouldn't it? Nakano stiffens; you can see the gears turning in his head as he quickly runs through his internal book of etiquette and figures out the appropriate response. "Your compliment is quite gracious, your Eminence." You're just stating the facts — after all, you can't learn until you've admitted your own shortcomings and failings. Now then, perhaps you should look to starting? |You've never actually seen him in action, but his martial prowess is certainly well-known amongst the other denizens of the fox den. Even though this is training, you're sure you'll be able to see some of that for yourself. Nakano stiffens; you can see the gears turning in his head as he quickly runs through his internal book of etiquette and figures out the appropriate response. "Your compliment is quite gracious, your Eminence." Really, you're looking forward to it. ] "If your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship will select something you wish to learn, we can begin forthwith." ]
rows.translation: [flags.NAKANO_TRAIN |“能为您指导，是我的荣幸，阁下。您学起来既迅速又敏锐——程度之深，足以令大多数人惊叹。” 哦，真是太会拍马屁了。 “事实依然是，您能在短短几天或几周内掌握并领会那些别人要花数月甚至数年练习与学习才能开始熟悉的技术与知识。这大大加快了这些功课的进度。” 尽管中野像一潭静水般平和安详，但你能看出他其实对此很不痛快。对他来说，武术与武艺本身就是一门哲学、一种生活方式，而不得不认真做这件事让他深感苦恼——然而他既不能违抗自己的高祖母兼君主，更不能违抗自己的神。 [pc.isDK |唉，他可真倒霉。你需要抓住每一丝力量、每一个在冒险中能为你所用的选择，而你不会仅仅因为某个让人受不了的小鬼心里不痛快就停下脚步。 |对他这样做确实有点不公平，但你确实没有太多时间可以浪费在……他之前所做的那些事情上。你当初同意接受这一切，部分原因就是你需要利用一切可用的资源来应对这场危机，现在你必须集中精力解决问题。如果真的有必要的话，等卡希拉以及所有其他问题都得到解决之后，你会有足够的时间坐下来仔细研究这些事情的。 ] “如果您愿意告诉我您的打算，课程便可以立即开始。” |你提起这个话题时，中野的表情依然平和如水，但你越往下说，他目光深处似乎有什么东西闪了一下。“没错，阁下。事实上，他的神圣陛下不久前亲自来过，让我在今天这个时候空出时间来，因为您会问我这个问题。” 啊，凯罗斯又在耍他那些老把戏了；我赌两枚铜币，他这么做就是为了看那家伙坐立不安。他厌恶自己不得不做却又必须隐瞒这件事，而这种厌恶又与来自——嗯，在狐妖的等级体系里，没有比凯罗斯本人更高的存在了——的直接命令形成了对比。 [pc.isDK |你不得不承认——看着那混蛋那样坐立不安，被困在自己那些信念的陷阱里，而那些信念昭然若揭，简直成了旧国经典里用滥了的桥段，真是非常搞笑。也许是因为你现在成了他的冠军，所以你开始明白凯罗斯为什么能从中找到乐趣 |看着一个人那样坐立不安，被困在自己那些昭然若揭、简直成了旧国经典里用滥了的桥段的信念陷阱里，心里确实有点过意不去，但与此同时，这样的结果也无可避免。指望中野真正重新审视自己的根本观点实在太过奢望，不过，至少看着他小心翼翼地避开自己信念中的盲点，倒也挺有意思的。无论如何，这肯定正是凯罗斯想要达到的效果 ]。 那么，他会去做吗？ “当然，阁下。令我们永感羞愧与遗憾的是，如今就连帝国总督的官邸都配不上一座用来练习武艺的正式道场；不过我会另作安排，让您能够学习如何运用狐火及其他能力投入战斗。” 那很好。[flags.FLOOF_HAUS_NAKANO_RESOLUTION 1 2 3 |尽管你在第一次交锋中成功击败了他，但在这个领域，他无疑比你更出色——在这方面，你很乐意向他学习。在这种时候，这些狐妖们通常会说什么呢？“请对我好一点吧？” 中野听到这里不禁皱起了眉头；提醒他那段羞耻的经历，确实达到了预期的效果。他身上有太多那么明显、容易触发的“按钮”了，让人实在忍不住想要去按它们。 |有这样一位能力出众的老师在身边，一定会让你感到非常欣慰。毕竟，在你们初次见面时，他就已经成功地击败了你——这一点应该足以证明他的实力了吧？ 中野的身体一僵；你能看见他脑子里的齿轮在转动，他飞速翻检着心中那本礼仪手册，琢磨出得体的回应。 “您的赞美真是太客气了，阁下。” 你只是在陈述事实而已——毕竟，只有承认自己的缺点和不足，才能真正学到东西。那么，或许你应该从现在开始行动了吧？ |你其实从未见过他实战的表现，但他的武艺在狐狸洞的其他居民中无疑是出了名的。虽然这次只是训练，但你肯定有机会亲眼看到他的实力。 中野的身体一僵；你能看见他脑子里的齿轮在转动，他飞速翻检着心中那本礼仪手册，琢磨出得体的回应。 “您的赞美真是太客气了，阁下。” 说真的，你真的很期待这件事。 ] “如果[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]您想选择要学习的内容，我们便可以立即开始。” ]

rows.original: There are no powers Nakano can teach you right now.
rows.translation: 目前，中野并没有什么能力可以教给你。
rows.raw: "There are no powers Nakano can teach you right now."

rows.original: [flags.NAKANO_TRAIN_CHOICE |"Allow us to begin, then, your Eminence." A bow. "Everything is so informal and improper, but such is the reality of life in the Colonies — one must make do with what one must. Great-great-grandmother says we are to do without so that those who follow after us may have." ... Without another word, Nakano sets aside his things, gathers up the wooden training swords and guides you all the way down through the fields and gardens to the little spot behind the shrine where you can have some privacy. He tries to guide you through some of the appropriate social graces before the lesson starts, but it's really just awkward considering how much higher you are now in the kitsune hierarchy than he is, yet technically still are his student... Either way, given your [pc.bgMulti soldier noblescion |martial past as a soldier |noble lineage and the expectations thereof |decent grounding in weapons handling from your adventures and more ], you're able to handle the wooden sword with reasonable proficiency. You're here to learn what only a kitsune can teach, and Nakano focuses his effort in directing you in the blending of foxfire with your strikes and blows, doing what he can to adjust his teachings to your techniques that are no doubt foreign to him — superficially, if not in essence. "A perfectly balanced spirit is also a perfectly balanced physical presence, and neither creates weakness nor reveals it to your enemy. The most direct manifestation of chi and ki working in concert, of the seen and unseen, are the martial applications of foxfire. Being lacking in one or the other means the whole fails — it is more than the sum of the parts." You see. The hours pass by. Nakano is always ineffably polite, as is expected of him, but the quiet sense of — no, it isn't disapproval, but more begrudging acceptance, maybe tinged with a little disappointment — lingers. Given such a people as the kitsune, you're not really surprised that they've perfected the art of passive-aggression, but still. Maybe it's all in your own mind and you just don't like him, and you're projecting that onto the boy... [rand |[kiyoko.isFree |[kinu.isInari |Huh. You wonder — since you're here, if there's any chance Kinu might see the two of you going at it. If she does, you do want to make her proud of you. "We are sequestered away from prying eyes here, your Eminence. You need not worry about embarrassing yourself by accident — Mikoto and Miyuki do not let just anyone back in here behind the shrine. I feel the sting of shame in having to come to such arrangements myself... but nothing can be done about it, or at least in the time frame that we have." Oh no, you were just wondering if there's a chance — from all the talk about the den, she's shaping up to be quite the devout girl, and visits the shrine almost daily after work. You know so little of kitsune and Old Country culture in general that it's kind of embarrassing to ask Kinu directly. "Hm... far from it being my place to speak ill of the young lady Otomo, but if your Eminence commands me to be direct then I will say that there are a few who think that someone of her birth should not be doing work that is beneath her. The prevailing attitude, though, is that her willingness to work hard and get her hands dirty is an example for all in the colonies, and since one of the aspect of the August Master at the Center of Heaven is that of agriculture, there is no holier and more divine calling than that of working the land, especially since she does it so well. "Frankly, I do not know much, as that is out of my purview and I care little for idle gossip. My simpleton cousin Hitoshi should be able to inform you on the matter, your Eminence; he is much closer to the young lady Otomo than I am." |So, Kinu really exhibits the same qualities that you do when learning new things? You have to admit, the circumstances of her childhood meant that you couldn't have spent as much time as you wanted with her, and both your and her mother's perceptions of her abilities are bound to be slanted as her parents. It'd be nice to have someone else who was close to her voice their opinion. "Ah... the young lady Otomo is nothing short of a genius, I would say. I must admit to my shame that I am somewhat envious — for more than five years I have been attempting to grasp the art and forms of traditional long-form poetry, yet she instinctively understands them all at a first glance. It is quite admirable." If she got it from you, you can only wonder if such a trait is truly heritable. It would be quite the boon to Kiyoko's family line were it to be passed down from generation to generation. You're already not bad at this yourself, but given time, Kinu might — no, will outdo you at everything. "Your Eminence is truly blessed. Everyone has their own pace they are comfortable with, but you are able to pick up much in the blink of an eye and not forget anything you have learned. Such unprecedented ability — it is becoming evident why the August Master at the Center of Heaven made you his champion, your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. Choosing someone who was already strong would have been one thing, but choosing someone who has the ability to grow stronger rapidly is even better. The legends about his divine lordship always have him choosing the one with greater potential over the one who is great but static in their power. Such is an affectation of his — like us, his efforts towards an end can span many, many generations. It is not our place to try and comprehend what schemes the August Master at the Center of Heaven concocts, unless he deigns to explain them to us of his own accord." Does that happen often? "All the time. It is part of being who we are, your Eminence; it is not something that can be explained. Only time can reveal this unto you." ] |Look, you understand that he doesn't really like the Marches or its local people — you got that well enough before you became a kitsune and Keros' personal champion. But what does he think life might have been like if, say, for the want of a nail, he hadn't been born in the colonies?" "Speculation on what might or might not have been is —"Nakano begins, then remembers who he's talking to and shuts up, bowing his head. "Please forgive my contentiousness, your Eminence." Forgiven. Please, continue. "I am not entirely sure myself. Certainly, if I had been a provincial like Mikoto or Miyuki and not a colony-child, it might have been a more honorable situation — at least, the chance at earning honor and praise on the battlefield with an eye on a place serving the Cherry Blossom Throne in the capital would not be completely closed to me. It is shameful on a generational level and is reflected in everything that is done. "Yet it has been remarked to me that I am quite fortunate in having my duties to my liege, family and religion all wrapped up neatly in the person of my great-great-grandmother. Thus, I am able to avoid many of the dilemmas that those who follow the way of the warrior often face — conflicts between the demands of liege and family, or liege and the laws of his divine lordship. Great-great-grandmother says that it is some small compensation for the injustices that have been dealt to me for her failings, although I refuse to see it that way." So what does he see it as? "An opportunity. There is much potential in this land." So what's the plan? For them to sweep across and subjugate this land like Belhar once threatened to do to them, until the Godswar kicked in? Nakano stiffens and twitches, then clearly remembers who you are now. "No, your Eminence. Certainly, that is what the natives are used to, swarming the land with bodies in a show of arms... I understand it is the way of many who make war here to do so. Certainly if the Cherry Blossom Throne had the mind to do that, the immigrants would be tanuki, not kitsune. Raccoon dogs breed quickly, efficiently, and voraciously, expanding to fill the land in a few generations. It is a strategy that has historically proven effective, and then once again when the foreigners from the field Belharan fleet needed to be absorbed." You don't say anything, but think back to Evergreen and her many, many daughters — and that's just one tanuki. "Great-great-grandmother's designs are more subtle, and hence I do not understand them all, but I am content to trust in her lead and obey her unquestioningly." That's a line of thought you've been seeing in most foxes, but him most of all. The level of in-trust in their society that you've seen is unprecedented, but maintaining that requires extreme rejection of out-groups. "There is a proverb that is roughly translated as, 'Who is the better warrior? Is it the one who fights his evil lord, or the one who serves the evil lord unto death?' The answer is, of course, is 'the one who serves without question.' And of course, in all societies, those under seek to emulate those at the top." You just shake your head and continue with the lesson. To Nakano, surely this is all plain and obvious, but from your perspective it's just madness. Maybe that's part of why Keros chose you... to watch both you and Nakano squirm when forced to go through these motions. ] | |"Your ability to learn quickly is truly astounding, your Eminence. We will be done before too long, now." You've been meaning to ask — is this trait of yours really that rare? Certainly there've been others, right? "Everyone has their own pace they are comfortable with, but you are able to pick up much in the blink of an eye and not forget anything you have learned. Such unprecedented ability — it is becoming evident why the August Master at the Center of Heaven made you his champion, your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. Choosing someone who was already strong would have been one thing, but choosing someone who has the ability to grow stronger rapidly is even better." He was quite enamored of your soul, but you don't think this quirk of yours has anything to do with that, otherwise it'd have left you when he divested you of it to join the great kitsune collective. "Over the ocean in the Old Country, there are legends of people who are able to rapidly gain power. They are... chosen, in a way." Chosen by who? By the gods? "No... not by any of the lesser or even greater kami. They are chosen, made pawns by creatures beyond this reality, the void between the spheres, as you might call it. They reach out and touch the lives of people, give them the capability to gain power from..." From? "...From victory and overcoming obstacles, if the circumstances are merciful. Others mandate that the power can only be gained from the death of others, or by the acquisition of material wealth, or other more sinister actions that place the souls of these chosen ones in peril. These creatures play games with the lives of those such as us for their amusement, and in exchange they give power. Mastery at arms that might take one a decade of study, meditation and practise in order to strengthen one's body and deepen one's spirit — for these pawns, they would surpass such careful cultivation of one's self if one proved amusing enough to these creatures, shed enough blood." You just shake your head at that. That situation's sounding awfully familiar... "Oh, your Eminence is certainly not one who is so touched," Nakano adds hurriedly. How can he tell? "Such powers always come at a price. The same legends also state that those who accept the offer... terrible things happened to those whom they loved and cared about, be it their families, their lieges, or even entire clans, and these events almost always occurred when these pawns were very young. Nothing of the sort has happened to your Eminence, as far as we know, and you are blessed [a] [kiyoko.isFree| loving family| people] who care deeply for you. Hence, while the end result is similar, you cannot be one who is touched by these outsiders." A sobering notion, indeed. Well! Back to the lesson at hand — you've gotten derailed enough from your endeavors. |Where did he learn his trade, if you may ask? "It is deeply touching that your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship would concern [pc.himHer]self with my matters and personal well-being." The question, please. "After my coming-of-age ceremony at fifteen, great-great-grandmother sent me back to my homeland to be trained in the way of the warrior. She said it was about time the colonies needed more than a militia after two and a half centuries of existence, and it was better that someone local do it rather than someone assigned from the capital. I would have —" he searches for a suitable translation for the concept — "skin in the game, as it were. She also wanted to keep governance of the colonies' functions in our family as much as possible. I was able and willing." How was it like, being able to cross the ocean to the land he considers his own? "Two years in the capital, three years on my clan's provincial holdings to put what I learned into practice. The provinces are as full of demons and malcontents as they are ever — when the nekomata are not outright rebelling every century or two, they are resorting to banditry." he spits. "In some ways, the provincial situation is worse than the colonial one." You sigh inwardly, noting that Nakano delicately danced around the question of his personal feelings. Now, you could directly order him to be frank, but no doubt that would violate several dozen invisible and unspoken rules of fox etiquette expected of someone of your station. So instead, you nod and concentrate on the lesson. ] The rest of the lesson proceeds as before, and as always, Nakano declares that you're done by the time the sun begins to set. While there's more practice that you can do on your own time, you've managed to grasp the basics of the technique he's tried to impart — the strategy and timing of how to use the technique is up for you to figure out on your own, given the limited time you have for learning. Certainly, the new awakening within you and the realization that you perhaps were always able to do these things with foxfire that you were never aware of only leaves questions as to where your limits truly lie. "Inquire again should there be something new you wish to learn, your Eminence. As we all gain experience and come to new realizations and enlightenments, as our spirits deepen and we become more comfortable with our forms, so do our options broaden. And for one as gifted as you, I have little doubt that time will come soon once again." With that, he bows deeply from the waist, waits for you to present him with your slightly signed wooden sword, then retreats in the direction of the shrine. |"That is something I can impart to you, your Eminence. Allow me to gather the lesson materials and we may depart for a more suitable venue forthwith." Not too long later, the two of you find yourselves at the back of the shrine gardens behind the shrine itself, sequestered away from prying eyes save for [var0|Miko and Mai's|Mai's|Miko's]. Nakano's gathered a pair of simple wooden training blades and has presented you with one of them while keeping the other for himself.[party.has kiyoko | While the two of you busy yourselves with the preparations, Kiyoko makes herself comfortable atop the stone table Mai uses for her physician practice, curling her tails about her person and watching the proceedings. ] "I hear you are well-versed in the welding of many kinds of weapons, your Eminence." That's true, but truth be told, it isn't through any effort of your own[pc.bgMulti soldier noblescion |, even though it might be expected of someone with a military background like yours |, even though as a noble scion you were expected to have acquired some skill at arms as part of your upbringing ]. You've always been able to have some kind of instinctual proficiency with any kind of weapon you pick up, be it the bow, polearm or blade and so forth. Mastery may take a little while, but picking up something you unearthed in an old ruin and at least achieving satisfactory results with it's nothing new to you. It's not just weapons, either — pretty much anything you set your mind to, you can master pretty quickly given the right instruction and material. That's why you're confident you can get this lesson down by the end of today. Nakano takes that in, looking thoughtful as he scratches his chin. "[kiyoko.isFree |So that is where the young lady Otomo has inherited that particular trait of hers from. I confess, it is an excellent one to have |I begin to see why the August Master at the Center of Heaven has seen fit to elevate you to this position. There were of course rumours about your abilities, but to have them personally confirmed is another thing ]. One should be versed in many weaponry skills; you should not overuse one weapon. This is as bad as using the weapon poorly since it becomes easy for an enemy to find a weakness in your style after countless uses of the same weapon. Pattern recognition is something even the lowliest conscript, rebel or bandit can manage and turn to their advantage against you." That makes sense. "Flexibility is important — the ability to change in accordance with one's own situation to easily shift between disciplines, methods, and options when presented with new information, conforming to your situation to seek the most efficient and productive path. A person should master many aspects of life allowing them to possess both balance and flexibility. But of course, you are already appraised of that, your Eminence. Let us begin, then." Since you're already reasonably well-versed in all kinds of weaponry, Nakano's able to skip the basics and get right down to the part that's truly novel to you; the combination of martial prowess and your newfound metaphysical nature. Still, even though you try to keep to the technical, it soon becomes apparent that the martial and the spiritual are inseparable from the kitsune perspective. "Timing is important in dancing and pipe or string music, for they are in rhythm only if timing is good; timing and rhythm are also involved in the military arts, shooting bows, and riding horses. In all skills and abilities there is timing.... there is timing in the whole life of the warrior, in his thriving and declining, in his harmony and discord. All things entail rising and falling timing. You must be able to discern this — down to the natural timing and rhythms of your body." Hm. "Your breathing, the beating of your heart, those are the physical aspects of your timing, your chi. Through the seen, you manipulate the unseen — your ki. That rhythm and timing is what joins us all kitsune together through our connection to —" he says something in his mother tongue that presumably has no translation in Belharan — "and hence effectively we all gain strength through joining our souls together. And then, by knowing what timings are applicable and which are not, through the seen to the unseen, and the unseen manipulates the seen —" The blade of the wooden sword he's holding ignites, wreathed in ghostly blue foxfire. Searing heat wafts off the weapon, making the air waver, yet Nakano's holding the grip quite calmly. "Now you try it, your Eminence, and should you have any doubts, allow me to walk you through the process." The art of managing foxfire in combat is less straightforward than it appears at first glance, even to someone with your talents. What seems to come effortlessly to Nakano — and frankly every other kitsune you've ever known — takes conscious, determined effort on your part, a reminder of how new you are still to not just this body, but this reality. The problem is compounded by the fact that there are several words and concepts that aren't really translatable into Belharan by simple virtue of the fact that there are no real equivalents that capture the entire nuance of such; the both of you have to make do with half-measures and approximations, and that needlessly complicates matters. But as you said, you were confident of getting this done before the day is out, and hold true to that. By the time the sun's begun to set, you've experienced an awakening of sorts both inside and out, using Nakano's instruction to better control the natural instincts and faculties that've been gifted to you as a kitsune. He nods in satisfaction at your movements, acknowledging that whatever misgivings he may have over your lack of spiritual and philosophical grounding in his art, at least you've got the technique down. "That will be sufficient for a day's work. There is so much more I wish I could impart to you, your Eminence, but you seem sufficiently familiar with that I have tried to teach and our time today runs short." That's sufficient — you learned something today, indeed. "As I was taught myself: 'Know the smallest things and the biggest things, the shallowest things and the deepest things. As if they were a straight road mapped out on the ground — these things cannot be explained in detail and must be experienced for oneself. From one thing, know ten thousand things.' "When you attain the Way of strategy there will not be one thing you cannot see.. Upon mastery of the Way, you will be able to defeat ten as easily as you defeated one. When you attain such prowess, will it mean you are not invincible?" Being invincible would be nice, yes. "Inquire at any time if you need further instruction, your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. Both the August Master at the Center of Heaven and the Imperial Governor have directed me to make myself available at your leisure. There are still more things to learn if that is your wish, especially as you grow in your own power and are able to exert greater mastery over both chi and ki." Will do. You hand Nakano back the wooden sword and note that while yours is slightly singed from foxfire, his is as pristine as when he'd brought it in. Ah well, important divine champions like you can't be expected to do everything while taking instruction. He bows to you all the way from the waist, to which you return with the nod that you're pretty sure's expected of you, then turn to leave. [party.has kiyoko |As you make your way away, Kiyoko slinks off the stone table and falls in step with you at your side, beaming. "[kinu.isInari |You looked like you were having fun back there." Did you? You suppose you must have gotten engrossed in the spirit of things back there. "Oh yes. You were very dashing, crossing blades with the military provost. Quite the show, really." Mm, you do serve to entertain. Maybe it's Keros rubbing off on you with you being his champion and all, but there's never a boring moment these days. |Quite the ambitious young man, isn't he?" Straight-laced... and properly respectful of his superiors as is befitting. You must admit that you're enjoying this maybe a little too much. Kiyoko clucks her tongue at that. "Hmmm. Someone of your station should be both dignified and magnanimous. I wouldn't mind it if the two of you managed to make peace with each other — and this is a good step forward, as well as joining our fold. Our daughter has taken a liking to him, after all, and being able to get along is something that is valued in our society, in a sense." So long as he remains cordial and courteous, you'll see what you can do about it. Kiyoko raises a finger to her lips. "Given your situation, I don't see that changing." ] |As you pass through the shrine gardens, your body's filled with a strange heat, your footsteps light despite the regimen Nakano's just put you through for the last handful of hours. It's not quite right to say something's awakened within you — that was Keros' doing — but you feel like you're more in control of yourself now. This is something you can get used to. ] ]
rows.translation: [flags.NAKANO_TRAIN_CHOICE |那么，容我们开始吧，阁下。一支弓。一切都显得如此随意、不规范，但这就是殖民地生活的现实——人们只能勉强接受现状，利用手头的一切资源。曾曾祖母说过，我们必须现在节俭，这样后来的子孙才能有更好的生活。 …… 中野二话不说，收拾好自己的东西，拿上那些木制训练剑，然后带着你们穿过田野和花园，来到神社后面的那个小地方——那里可以让人保持一些隐私。在课程开始之前，他试图教你一些基本的社交礼仪，但考虑到你在狐族等级体系中现在所处的位置远高于他，而从技术上讲你仍然算是他的学生，这些努力其实显得有些尴尬。无论如何，考虑到你的情况[pc.bgMulti soldier noblescion |作为军人的战斗经历 |高贵的血统以及由此带来的种种期望 |通过各种冒险经历，你已经掌握了相当扎实的武器使用技巧。 ]你的木剑运用技巧已经相当娴熟了。你来这里，就是为了学习只有狐妖才能传授的知识。中野倾尽全力指导你如何将狐火的力量融入你的攻击之中，他尽其所能调整自己的教学方法，以适应你的技巧——尽管这些技巧在本质上可能与他所熟知的方法有所不同，但在表面上看，却并无太大差异。 一个精神状态与身体状况都达到完美平衡的人，既不会表现出虚弱，也不会让敌人察觉到自己的弱点。这种平衡的最直接体现就是气以及ki狐火的各种实战应用，正是有形与无形因素相互配合的结果。缺少其中任何一方，整个体系就会失效——它的效果绝不是各部分简单相加所能得到的。 你瞧， 时间一点点流逝。中野一如既往地彬彬有礼，这也在意料之中，但那种隐约的感觉——不，不是不满，更像是一种勉强接受的态度，或许还带着一丝失望——依然萦绕在心头。对于像狐族这样的种族来说，他们将消极抵抗这种手段运用得如此娴熟，其实也不足为奇。不过，也许这一切都只是你的主观臆断，只是你不喜欢他，才会把这种情绪投射到这个男孩身上罢了…… [rand |[kiyoko.isFree |[kinu.isInari |哈，你在想——既然你已经来了，会不会有机会让小娟看到你们两个在一起呢？如果她看到了，你肯定希望她能为你感到骄傲吧。 在这里，我们远离了旁人的窥视，阁下。您不必担心会不小心出丑——美琴和美雪不会让随便什么人进入这个神社后面的区域。我自己也不得不采取这样的措施，实在觉得有些难为情……但在这个时间范围内，我们也无能为力。 "All the time. It is part of being who we are, your Eminence; it is not something that can be explained. Only time can reveal this unto you." ] |Look, you understand that he doesn't really like the Marches or its local people — you got that well enough before you became a kitsune and Keros' personal champion. But what does he think life might have been like if, say, for the want of a nail, he hadn't been born in the colonies?" "Speculation on what might or might not have been is —"Nakano begins, then remembers who he's talking to and shuts up, bowing his head. "Please forgive my contentiousness, your Eminence." Forgiven. Please, continue. "I am not entirely sure myself. Certainly, if I had been a provincial like Mikoto or Miyuki and not a colony-child, it might have been a more honorable situation — at least, the chance at earning honor and praise on the battlefield with an eye on a place serving the Cherry Blossom Throne in the capital would not be completely closed to me. It is shameful on a generational level and is reflected in everything that is done. "Yet it has been remarked to me that I am quite fortunate in having my duties to my liege, family and religion all wrapped up neatly in the person of my great-great-grandmother. Thus, I am able to avoid many of the dilemmas that those who follow the way of the warrior often face — conflicts between the demands of liege and family, or liege and the laws of his divine lordship. Great-great-grandmother says that it is some small compensation for the injustices that have been dealt to me for her failings, although I refuse to see it that way." So what does he see it as? "An opportunity. There is much potential in this land." So what's the plan? For them to sweep across and subjugate this land like Belhar once threatened to do to them, until the Godswar kicked in? Nakano stiffens and twitches, then clearly remembers who you are now. "No, your Eminence. Certainly, that is what the natives are used to, swarming the land with bodies in a show of arms... I understand it is the way of many who make war here to do so. Certainly if the Cherry Blossom Throne had the mind to do that, the immigrants would be tanuki, not kitsune. Raccoon dogs breed quickly, efficiently, and voraciously, expanding to fill the land in a few generations. It is a strategy that has historically proven effective, and then once again when the foreigners from the field Belharan fleet needed to be absorbed." You don't say anything, but think back to Evergreen and her many, many daughters — and that's just one tanuki. "Great-great-grandmother's designs are more subtle, and hence I do not understand them all, but I am content to trust in her lead and obey her unquestioningly." That's a line of thought you've been seeing in most foxes, but him most of all. The level of in-trust in their society that you've seen is unprecedented, but maintaining that requires extreme rejection of out-groups. "There is a proverb that is roughly translated as, 'Who is the better warrior? Is it the one who fights his evil lord, or the one who serves the evil lord unto death?' The answer is, of course, is 'the one who serves without question.' And of course, in all societies, those under seek to emulate those at the top." You just shake your head and continue with the lesson. To Nakano, surely this is all plain and obvious, but from your perspective it's just madness. Maybe that's part of why Keros chose you... to watch both you and Nakano squirm when forced to go through these motions. ] | |"Your ability to learn quickly is truly astounding, your Eminence. We will be done before too long, now." You've been meaning to ask — is this trait of yours really that rare? Certainly there've been others, right? "Everyone has their own pace they are comfortable with, but you are able to pick up much in the blink of an eye and not forget anything you have learned. Such unprecedented ability — it is becoming evident why the August Master at the Center of Heaven made you his champion, your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. Choosing someone who was already strong would have been one thing, but choosing someone who has the ability to grow stronger rapidly is even better." He was quite enamored of your soul, but you don't think this quirk of yours has anything to do with that, otherwise it'd have left you when he divested you of it to join the great kitsune collective. "Over the ocean in the Old Country, there are legends of people who are able to rapidly gain power. They are... chosen, in a way." Chosen by who? By the gods? "No... not by any of the lesser or even greater kami. They are chosen, made pawns by creatures beyond this reality, the void between the spheres, as you might call it. They reach out and touch the lives of people, give them the capability to gain power from..." From? "...From victory and overcoming obstacles, if the circumstances are merciful. Others mandate that the power can only be gained from the death of others, or by the acquisition of material wealth, or other more sinister actions that place the souls of these chosen ones in peril. These creatures play games with the lives of those such as us for their amusement, and in exchange they give power. Mastery at arms that might take one a decade of study, meditation and practise in order to strengthen one's body and deepen one's spirit — for these pawns, they would surpass such careful cultivation of one's self if one proved amusing enough to these creatures, shed enough blood." You just shake your head at that. That situation's sounding awfully familiar... "Oh, your Eminence is certainly not one who is so touched," Nakano adds hurriedly. How can he tell? "Such powers always come at a price. The same legends also state that those who accept the offer... terrible things happened to those whom they loved and cared about, be it their families, their lieges, or even entire clans, and these events almost always occurred when these pawns were very young. Nothing of the sort has happened to your Eminence, as far as we know, and you are blessed [a] [kiyoko.isFree| loving family| people] who care deeply for you. Hence, while the end result is similar, you cannot be one who is touched by these outsiders." A sobering notion, indeed. Well! Back to the lesson at hand — you've gotten derailed enough from your endeavors. |Where did he learn his trade, if you may ask? "It is deeply touching that your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship would concern [pc.himHer]self with my matters and personal well-being." The question, please. "After my coming-of-age ceremony at fifteen, great-great-grandmother sent me back to my homeland to be trained in the way of the warrior. She said it was about time the colonies needed more than a militia after two and a half centuries of existence, and it was better that someone local do it rather than someone assigned from the capital. I would have —" he searches for a suitable translation for the concept — "skin in the game, as it were. She also wanted to keep governance of the colonies' functions in our family as much as possible. I was able and willing." How was it like, being able to cross the ocean to the land he considers his own? "Two years in the capital, three years on my clan's provincial holdings to put what I learned into practice. The provinces are as full of demons and malcontents as they are ever — when the nekomata are not outright rebelling every century or two, they are resorting to banditry." he spits. "In some ways, the provincial situation is worse than the colonial one." You sigh inwardly, noting that Nakano delicately danced around the question of his personal feelings. Now, you could directly order him to be frank, but no doubt that would violate several dozen invisible and unspoken rules of fox etiquette expected of someone of your station. So instead, you nod and concentrate on the lesson. ] The rest of the lesson proceeds as before, and as always, Nakano declares that you're done by the time the sun begins to set. While there's more practice that you can do on your own time, you've managed to grasp the basics of the technique he's tried to impart — the strategy and timing of how to use the technique is up for you to figure out on your own, given the limited time you have for learning. Certainly, the new awakening within you and the realization that you perhaps were always able to do these things with foxfire that you were never aware of only leaves questions as to where your limits truly lie. "Inquire again should there be something new you wish to learn, your Eminence. As we all gain experience and come to new realizations and enlightenments, as our spirits deepen and we become more comfortable with our forms, so do our options broaden. And for one as gifted as you, I have little doubt that time will come soon once again." With that, he bows deeply from the waist, waits for you to present him with your slightly signed wooden sword, then retreats in the direction of the shrine. |"That is something I can impart to you, your Eminence. Allow me to gather the lesson materials and we may depart for a more suitable venue forthwith." Not too long later, the two of you find yourselves at the back of the shrine gardens behind the shrine itself, sequestered away from prying eyes save for [var0|Miko and Mai's|Mai's|Miko's]. Nakano's gathered a pair of simple wooden training blades and has presented you with one of them while keeping the other for himself.[party.has kiyoko | While the two of you busy yourselves with the preparations, Kiyoko makes herself comfortable atop the stone table Mai uses for her physician practice, curling her tails about her person and watching the proceedings. ] "I hear you are well-versed in the welding of many kinds of weapons, your Eminence." That's true, but truth be told, it isn't through any effort of your own[pc.bgMulti soldier noblescion |, even though it might be expected of someone with a military background like yours |, even though as a noble scion you were expected to have acquired some skill at arms as part of your upbringing ]. You've always been able to have some kind of instinctual proficiency with any kind of weapon you pick up, be it the bow, polearm or blade and so forth. Mastery may take a little while, but picking up something you unearthed in an old ruin and at least achieving satisfactory results with it's nothing new to you. It's not just weapons, either — pretty much anything you set your mind to, you can master pretty quickly given the right instruction and material. That's why you're confident you can get this lesson down by the end of today. Nakano takes that in, looking thoughtful as he scratches his chin. "[kiyoko.isFree |So that is where the young lady Otomo has inherited that particular trait of hers from. I confess, it is an excellent one to have |I begin to see why the August Master at the Center of Heaven has seen fit to elevate you to this position. There were of course rumours about your abilities, but to have them personally confirmed is another thing ]. One should be versed in many weaponry skills; you should not overuse one weapon. This is as bad as using the weapon poorly since it becomes easy for an enemy to find a weakness in your style after countless uses of the same weapon. Pattern recognition is something even the lowliest conscript, rebel or bandit can manage and turn to their advantage against you." That makes sense. "Flexibility is important — the ability to change in accordance with one's own situation to easily shift between disciplines, methods, and options when presented with new information, conforming to your situation to seek the most efficient and productive path. A person should master many aspects of life allowing them to possess both balance and flexibility. But of course, you are already appraised of that, your Eminence. Let us begin, then." Since you're already reasonably well-versed in all kinds of weaponry, Nakano's able to skip the basics and get right down to the part that's truly novel to you; the combination of martial prowess and your newfound metaphysical nature. Still, even though you try to keep to the technical, it soon becomes apparent that the martial and the spiritual are inseparable from the kitsune perspective. "Timing is important in dancing and pipe or string music, for they are in rhythm only if timing is good; timing and rhythm are also involved in the military arts, shooting bows, and riding horses. In all skills and abilities there is timing.... there is timing in the whole life of the warrior, in his thriving and declining, in his harmony and discord. All things entail rising and falling timing. You must be able to discern this — down to the natural timing and rhythms of your body." Hm. "Your breathing, the beating of your heart, those are the physical aspects of your timing, your chi. Through the seen, you manipulate the unseen — your ki. That rhythm and timing is what joins us all kitsune together through our connection to —" he says something in his mother tongue that presumably has no translation in Belharan — "and hence effectively we all gain strength through joining our souls together. And then, by knowing what timings are applicable and which are not, through the seen to the unseen, and the unseen manipulates the seen —" The blade of the wooden sword he's holding ignites, wreathed in ghostly blue foxfire. Searing heat wafts off the weapon, making the air waver, yet Nakano's holding the grip quite calmly. "Now you try it, your Eminence, and should you have any doubts, allow me to walk you through the process." The art of managing foxfire in combat is less straightforward than it appears at first glance, even to someone with your talents. What seems to come effortlessly to Nakano — and frankly every other kitsune you've ever known — takes conscious, determined effort on your part, a reminder of how new you are still to not just this body, but this reality. The problem is compounded by the fact that there are several words and concepts that aren't really translatable into Belharan by simple virtue of the fact that there are no real equivalents that capture the entire nuance of such; the both of you have to make do with half-measures and approximations, and that needlessly complicates matters. But as you said, you were confident of getting this done before the day is out, and hold true to that. By the time the sun's begun to set, you've experienced an awakening of sorts both inside and out, using Nakano's instruction to better control the natural instincts and faculties that've been gifted to you as a kitsune. He nods in satisfaction at your movements, acknowledging that whatever misgivings he may have over your lack of spiritual and philosophical grounding in his art, at least you've got the technique down. "That will be sufficient for a day's work. There is so much more I wish I could impart to you, your Eminence, but you seem sufficiently familiar with that I have tried to teach and our time today runs short." That's sufficient — you learned something today, indeed. "As I was taught myself: 'Know the smallest things and the biggest things, the shallowest things and the deepest things. As if they were a straight road mapped out on the ground — these things cannot be explained in detail and must be experienced for oneself. From one thing, know ten thousand things.' "When you attain the Way of strategy there will not be one thing you cannot see.. Upon mastery of the Way, you will be able to defeat ten as easily as you defeated one. When you attain such prowess, will it mean you are not invincible?" Being invincible would be nice, yes. "Inquire at any time if you need further instruction, your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. Both the August Master at the Center of Heaven and the Imperial Governor have directed me to make myself available at your leisure. There are still more things to learn if that is your wish, especially as you grow in your own power and are able to exert greater mastery over both chi and ki." Will do. You hand Nakano back the wooden sword and note that while yours is slightly singed from foxfire, his is as pristine as when he'd brought it in. Ah well, important divine champions like you can't be expected to do everything while taking instruction. He bows to you all the way from the waist, to which you return with the nod that you're pretty sure's expected of you, then turn to leave. [party.has kiyoko |As you make your way away, Kiyoko slinks off the stone table and falls in step with you at your side, beaming. "[kinu.isInari |You looked like you were having fun back there." Did you? You suppose you must have gotten engrossed in the spirit of things back there. "Oh yes. You were very dashing, crossing blades with the military provost. Quite the show, really." Mm, you do serve to entertain. Maybe it's Keros rubbing off on you with you being his champion and all, but there's never a boring moment these days. |Quite the ambitious young man, isn't he?" Straight-laced... and properly respectful of his superiors as is befitting. You must admit that you're enjoying this maybe a little too much. Kiyoko clucks her tongue at that. "Hmmm. Someone of your station should be both dignified and magnanimous. I wouldn't mind it if the two of you managed to make peace with each other — and this is a good step forward, as well as joining our fold. Our daughter has taken a liking to him, after all, and being able to get along is something that is valued in our society, in a sense." So long as he remains cordial and courteous, you'll see what you can do about it. Kiyoko raises a finger to her lips. "Given your situation, I don't see that changing." ] |As you pass through the shrine gardens, your body's filled with a strange heat, your footsteps light despite the regimen Nakano's just put you through for the last handful of hours. It's not quite right to say something's awakened within you — that was Keros' doing — but you feel like you're more in control of yourself now. This is something you can get used to. ] ] "

rows.original: [flags.NAKANO_TRAIN_BACKOUT |On second thought, maybe not today. There's something else you have to take care of right now that you just remembered. "I am available at your pleasure, your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. Please, handle your business first and return when it is convenient for you." You will. Nakano waits for you to dismiss him and you do, allowing the military provost to return to his more mundane tasks. |On second thought, maybe not today. You just remembered that there's something important you need to take care of and you need to postpone the matter — but at least he's not aware of your intentions for certain. You'll come back another time and pick this back up when it's more fitting. Nakano is as calm as ever, but despite his expression carefully unchanging you can feel the relief oozing from him as he bows deeply from the waist. "I will be awaiting your return, your Eminence. Please, feel free to return any time you are able; it will be my honor to be able to instruct one such as you." That ends the conversation quickly enough, and you step away from the military provost as he turns back to his work. ]

rows.original: As the edges of the fields fall away and the stone path rises to take place of packed dirt, you find yourself entering the broad expanse of the gardens that surround the little shrine tucked away at the back of the tree. Stone lanterns line the path, [dayNight |although at this time of day they're doused in favor of natural light that filters in from between the cherry blossom tree's gigantic roots |flickering away with the signature eerie azure glow of foxfire ]. The air's silent save for a calm breeze through the open flowerbeds, and for a moment a sense of disarming tranquility takes you up until you hear the voice: "Good [dayNight |day |evening ]. How may I assist you [dayNight |today |at this hour ]?" It's warm, pleasant and feminine, if the Belharan is faltering and slightly broken. As you turn, you come face-to-face with a specimen of wispy, foxy beauty, possessed of radiant white hair and fur and dressed in the traditional style of the kitsune. A little thin and slight in stature, the three-tailed kitsune has set aside [dayNight |her delicate gardening tools and clasped gloved hands before her |the stick and lantern she was using to light the stone lamps with, clasping her hands before her ] to give you a bow. But that's about where it ends. The entire left half of her body — your right, that is — is a mess of reddish-brown scars in direct contrast to her otherwise pale complexion, the eye on that side glassy, unfocused and dead. It's a horrible, ghoulish countenance in direct contrast to the allure the other side of her has, but it doesn't seem to trouble the white-furred fox any as the entirety of her expression pulls into a small smile. "I'd heard that the governor had given permission to someone to visit the colony. You would be [pc.himHer], right? Are you lost? The arcology can be confusing if you're not familiar with its ins and outs." [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona etheryn berwyn quin |"Gods," Cait breathes, leaning in and trying to whisper despite her clear shock. "She can't be older than I am, and yet... oh, the poor thing. I want to hug her and tell her it'll be all right." You have similar sentiments, but perhaps it wouldn't be best to give such an overt display of affection as a first impression. |"We-ll," Brint whispers to you, trying to disguise his sigh as a snort and be as uncharacteristically discreet as a big, lumbering minotaur can. "Now if that isn't a pretty sight. I've seen veterans who were honorably discharged from service for less." |"We-ll," Brienne whispers to you, trying to disguise her sigh as a snort and be as uncharacteristically discreet as a big, lumbering cowgirl can. "Now if that isn't a pretty sight. I've seen veterans who were honorably discharged from service for less." |Arona sucks in a sharp breath at the sight. "Wow. I wouldn't even take that one as a slave — fucking something that pathetic would just make me sad." You throw her a sharp glance, and she folds her arms and stares you down. "What? Did I say something wrong?" |"O-oh, that's terrible," Ryn says, swallowing hard at the sight. "The poor girl." |"O-oh. I — I — " Berwyn fumbles about for something to say, then gives up and turns off to the side, clearly not wanting to put his foot deeper inside of his mouth at a time like this. |Quintillus winces at the sight of the disfigured kitsune, lowering his voice to a whisper. "Ouch. Now that had to be painful, whatever happened to her. I've seen a number of things in my time, both before and after the cult... and this is pretty high up." Uh, that is — ] The white-furred kitsune says nothing but bows even further, folding her ears forward as she awaits your reply; you note that her left ear is slightly shorter than the right, no doubt a product of the same thing that caused her scarring. Uh, yes, that's you. "My name is Rindo Igarashi. Might I ask for yours?" It's [pc.name]. [pc.name], [pc.title]. And no, you're not lost. You were just looking around, that's all. The inside of this tree is very different in every aspect from anywhere else in the Marches; you'd just like to stand around for a bit and soak in the atmosphere. "I'm pleased to make your acquaintance, [pc.name]. There are occasionally new arrivals here in the governor's holdings, but most of them arrive by way of the torii gate and not the front door. And, well, you are the first in living memory to have done so, I believe. But if you're here for the atmosphere and aesthetics, please feel free to enjoy yourself as much as you wish. This is a public space, after all." Is she the garden's caretaker? A nod. "It is not my primary duty, and Miko and Mai are obliged to assist me from time to time, but it is correct to say that because of my talents and what limited education I have, the responsibility of its upkeep falls upon my shoulders." The more that dead, sightless eye looks straight at you, the more the queasy sensation in the pit of your stomach grows. The uniform pinkness of it, as if the red of her pupil had exploded and bled out the entirety of its contents into the white — you just, you just, it's —
rows.translation: 当田野的边缘逐渐消失，石砌的小路取代了那被压实的泥土，你便走进了那片广阔的花园。这些花园环绕着隐藏在树林深处的小神龛。小路两旁排列着石灯。 [dayNight |尽管在这个时间段，室内光线已经被从樱花树巨大的树根间隙中透进来的自然光所取代了。 |在那种特有的、诡异的蔚蓝色光芒中逐渐熄灭…… ]空气中一片寂静，只有微风轻轻吹过开阔的花坛，这一刻，一种令人放松的宁静感油然而生——直到你听到了那个声音： “好了。 [dayNight |天 |晚上 ]。 我能为您做些什么呢？ [dayNight |今天 |此刻 ]这里温暖、舒适，充满了女性特有的柔美气息。不过，贝尔哈兰的气息似乎有些微弱，甚至有些不稳。当你转身时，你会看到一个拥有纤细、狐魅般美貌的生物——它拥有闪亮的白色毛发和皮毛，穿着典型的狐妖服饰。这个三尾狐妖身材娇小纤细，似乎[dayNight |她那精致的花艺工具，以及戴着手套的双手，就摆在她面前。 |她手中拿着那根用来点燃石灯的棍子和灯笼，双手交叠在身前。 ]向您鞠躬。 但也就仅此而已了。她身体的左侧——也就是您的右侧——布满了红棕色的疤痕，这些疤痕与她原本苍白的肤色形成了鲜明的对比；而那一侧的眼睛也变得呆滞无神，无法聚焦。那是一张可怕而阴森的面孔，与她另一面的魅力形成了鲜明的对比，但似乎并没有让这只白毛狐妖感到困扰，因为她的整个表情最终都化作了一丝微笑。 “我听说总督已经允许某人访问这个殖民地了。你将会[pc.himHer]对吧？你是不是迷路了？如果你不熟悉这个建筑群的构造，确实会感到有些困惑。 [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona etheryn berwyn quin |天啊，”凯特轻声说道，她凑近身体，尽管内心充满震惊，仍试图低声安慰对方。“她不可能比我年纪大吧，然而……哦，那个可怜的孩子。我真想抱抱她，告诉她一切都会好起来的。” 你也有同样的感受，但或许在初次见面时，最好不要表现得如此过于亲密。 |我们……”布林特轻声对你说，试图将自己的叹息伪装成哼声，同时尽可能地保持低调——毕竟对于一个体型庞大、行动笨拙的弥诺陶洛斯来说，这已经算是非常谨慎的表现了。“真是难得的一幕啊……我见过一些因表现优异而光荣退役的退伍军人，他们的待遇还不如这个呢。 |我们……”布蕾妮轻声对你说，试图将自己的叹息伪装成哼声，同时尽可能地保持低调——毕竟，对于一个身材高大、行动笨拙的牛仔女孩来说，这已经算是非常谨慎的表现了。“看吧，这一幕真是美极了。我见过一些因表现优异而光荣退役的军人，他们的待遇还不如这个呢。 |阿罗娜看到这一幕，猛地吸了一口冷气。“哇，就算把它当作奴隶我也不要——这么可怜的东西，让我看了只会觉得难过。” 你狠狠地瞪了她一眼，而她则双臂交叉，直视着你的眼睛。 “怎么了？我说什么错了吗？ |哦，那糟糕透了天哪，”小琳看着这一幕，艰难地咽了口唾沫，“那个可怜的女孩…… |哦……我……”贝尔温支支吾吾地想找话来说，但最终放弃了，转身走开了——显然，在这种时候，他实在不想再说更多让自己陷入更尴尬的境地了。 |昆蒂卢斯看到那只面目全非的狐妖时，不禁皱起了眉头，然后将声音压低成耳语般轻柔的语气说道：哎哟！不管她遭遇了什么，那肯定非常痛苦。这些年来，我在邪教活动之前和之后都见过很多事情……而这件事的严重程度确实相当高。 呃，也就是说…… ] 那只白色毛发的狐妖什么也没说，只是将身体弯得更低了，耳朵也向前耷拉着，等待着你的回答。你注意到，它的左耳比右耳稍微短一些，这无疑也是导致它身上出现那些疤痕的原因。 “嗯，没错，就是你。” “我叫五十岚凛朵，请问您叫什么名字呢？ [pc.name]。 [pc.name]， [pc.title]不，你并没有迷路。你只是在四处看看而已。这棵树的内部在各个方面都与其他地方的“边境地区”截然不同；你只是想站在这里，好好感受一下这种氛围罢了。 “很高兴认识你。 [pc.name]在总督的领地里，偶尔也会有新来的人出现，但他们大多数都是通过其他途径来到这里的。鸟居从侧门进入，而不是前门。嗯，我相信，在我们有记忆以来，你是第一个这样做的人。但如果你是冲着这里的氛围和美学而来的，那么请随时尽情享受吧。毕竟，这里是一个公共空间。她是这个花园的管理员吗？” 她点了点头：“虽然这不是我的主要职责，米可与舞也会偶尔帮忙，但可以说，由于我的能力和所受的教育有限，维护这个花园的责任确实落在了我的肩上。那颗已经失去光泽、无法看见东西的眼睛越是直直地盯着你，你胃里的那种不适感就会越加强烈。它那均匀的粉红色，仿佛她的瞳孔中的红色已经完全破裂，所有的颜色都渗入了白色之中——真的，就是这种感觉——
rows.raw: ' As the edges of the fields fall away and the stone path rises to take place of packed dirt, you find yourself entering the broad expanse of the gardens that surround the little shrine tucked away at the back of the tree. Stone lanterns line the path, [dayNight |although at this time of day they're doused in favor of natural light that filters in from between the cherry blossom tree's gigantic roots |flickering away with the signature eerie azure glow of foxfire ]. The air's silent save for a calm breeze through the open flowerbeds, and for a moment a sense of disarming tranquility takes you up until you hear the voice: "Good [dayNight |day |evening ]. How may I assist you [dayNight |today |at this hour ]?" It's warm, pleasant and feminine, if the Belharan is faltering and slightly broken. As you turn, you come face-to-face with a specimen of wispy, foxy beauty, possessed of radiant white hair and fur and dressed in the traditional style of the kitsune. A little thin and slight in stature, the three-tailed kitsune has set aside [dayNight |her delicate gardening tools and clasped gloved hands before her |the stick and lantern she was using to light the stone lamps with, clasping her hands before her ] to give you a bow. But that's about where it ends. The entire left half of her body — your right, that is — is a mess of reddish-brown scars in direct contrast to her otherwise pale complexion, the eye on that side glassy, unfocused and dead. It's a horrible, ghoulish countenance in direct contrast to the allure the other side of her has, but it doesn't seem to trouble the white-furred fox any as the entirety of her expression pulls into a small smile. "I'd heard that the governor had given permission to someone to visit the colony. You would be [pc.himHer], right? Are you lost? The arcology can be confusing if you're not familiar with its ins and outs." [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona etheryn berwyn quin |"Gods," Cait breathes, leaning in and trying to whisper despite her clear shock. "She can't be older than I am, and yet... oh, the poor thing. I want to hug her and tell her it'll be all right." You have similar sentiments, but perhaps it wouldn't be best to give such an overt display of affection as a first impression. |"We-ll," Brint whispers to you, trying to disguise his sigh as a snort and be as uncharacteristically discreet as a big, lumbering minotaur can.
