And is she feeling it? "I... it would not be as bad if they had not decided to try and bar the young lady Otomo in her chambers and set it alight. Several more moments, and she would have suffered my fate, or worse. The way these outsiders attempted to murder her... it strikes a little too close to home for me. "But please forgive me. This conversation should be about the young lady Otomo, and not my own insecurities." She doesn't need to apologize, you're the one who asked her. [pc.ra kitsune |"Your Eminence, I am sure you will do an excellent job in your appointement. Perhaps this is what his divine lordship was considering when he decided he needed a champion, and in the colonies. |Rindo simply turns her head, refusing to look you in the eye. " ]People are uncertain about the immediate future, even if they may not show it. Please watch over us." |"The heavens be praised that no lasting harm came to the young lady Otomo. She is our princess, regardless of whether her mother has abdicated her position or not; neither blood nor arahitogami can be wiped out with a piece of paper. If it were not for the alien appearances and behaviors of the assailants, I might have suspected foul play by any number of peoples on the other side of the ocean. Politics by other means, as the saying goes." What would have happened if it'd been foul play by anyone who might resent the existence of your family? Rindo thinks a moment, then shakes her head. "I don't know[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]; that web is too complex for someone as simple as me to navigate. But another of the reasons that in retrospect, I'm glad that the marriage that was arranged for me never came to pass. Even in a branch family, I would've been caught up in such plots whether I liked it or not. Here in the colonies, things are simpler... even the enemies one faces are more direct. "But I should not be talking about myself. Even in the comparatively short time she has been with us, the young lady Otomo has played true to her clan name and captured the hearts of the colonials. While it's been truly great for morale, the inverse would happen if tragedy were to befall her. Hence, do be assured that everyone will be watching out for her from here on out[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." And as her parent, you'll be keeping an eye out, too. This whole business may demand that you leave your daughter unattended for extended periods of time, but if you don't deal with the matter of Kasyrra, there won't be much of a world for Kinu to inherit. Kinu may be a grown woman, but even so you're glad the other foxes are looking out for her. "I have but one eye, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]but I'll do my part. The young lady Otomo is fun to talk to." |Ever since your home was invaded, everyone's been on edge. You really liked the calming atmosphere the fox den had before all this happened, and now it's soured even though people are trying to get on with their lives as normally as they can. Even the gardens about the shrine have lost some of their tranquil atmosphere; you miss the way things were. "We are one people, of one mind, and possessed of one soul[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Especially here in the colonies... an attack against one of us from outside is an attack against all of us. Everyone feels the trepidation and unease — we have no illusions about what is at stake here. Life must continue, but to pretend that nothing has happened is not possible, either. Now that others have attempted to harm one of our own, everyone is vigilant. Not necessarily afraid — although there is some of that, too — but vigilant." There is that. You've noticed how quickly moods spread throughout the kitsune den and the foxes who live within, as quickly as a school of fish decides to turn itself around. Sure, similar things can happen in a close-knit community like Hawkethorne, but this is uncanny. "Everyone is hoping for the full recovery of the young lady Otomo posthaste, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ]. Not just in body, but in spirit as well." You don't think you'll be able to rest easy after everything that's happened, but at least you'll feel better knowing that Kinu has so many people backing her up. She's your daughter and ultimately your responsibility here, but the help is appreciated. A small bow. "Even though her mother may have abdicated, we are still eager and willing to serve." |"The governor has requested that I prepare several seedlings for the purpose of restoring the High Lady Otomo's home[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. [kiyoko.married |Since it is also your home, you will be pleased to know that I've shaped but the best for this purpose. ]While a fair few have already been put into the earth, more will be needed for the long-term effort; even though the raiders razed much of the structure, we will build it anew and better. We will see to it that some good will come out of this tragedy." What are the seedlings intended for, if you may ask? "Vines for binding materials together, roots to fix burnt earth, and other sundry construction purposes. Your home will look exactly the same, but emerge stronger, more fireproof, and easier to defend. Now that we know there's a threat and some of the forms it can take, that makes it easier to design countermeasures. Everyone is coming together in this time of need, as we always have for one of our own." Still, you have to thank her. "There's no need to thank me[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]; it's understood that everyone is bound by reciprocity. There's no doubt that the young lady Otomo will come to us, too, when the situation calls for it. Such is our way." ] |[rand |"Ah, to be the attempt of not just one, but two targeted assassinations and survive... it must be terrible on one's peace of mind." Rindo keeps her small, placid smile, but her voice perceptibly softens. "While my brother asked me to come to the colonies for the sake of my health and a more suitable environment for me recovery, I also know what he was trying to say by omission. For the young lady Otomo to continue leading a normal life despite what she must be feeling right now must be no small feat; I will admit to being a little envious at such immense resolve." Ah, Kinu [kinu.isInari |is as stolid and solid as a rock; her head is hard, her skull thick and her will indomitable. She wouldn't let something as trivial as her own safety or concern for her life tear her from the fields she loves so much; if she were to cease surrounding herself with green growing things, it would be death in a sense, wouldn't it? |is every bit like her lady mother, silk hiding iron despite grace and soft-spokenness. She wouldn't let something as trivial as her own safety or concern for her life tear her from her duties to those around her; she wouldn't be your darling daughter if that weren't the case, would it? ] "[pc.ra kitsune |Your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |Ah ]... even when you put it that way, someone like me would not be able to withstand the thought, let alone do so unflinchingly. That the young lady Otomo is able to do so makes her a cut above us all where I would be sorely tempted to hide in my quarters and not come out like I did when I first arrived in the colonies." Rindo dips her head at you in a respectful nod. "Please, admiration is due where it is. I would find it immensely difficult to live as I do constantly watching over my shoulder, reminded of the stark nature of my mortality any more than I already am." |"The colonial governor has instructed me to shift several beds of nadeshiko flowers off to the east, as well as plant several new paulownia saplings by the water. Not exactly aesthetic, to be sure, but the geomantic purpose in doing so is crystal clear. Not only does the new arrangement repel hexes with greater efficiency, but it also casts a cloak of obscurity over us such that alternative means of spying upon our location are harder. It is subtle, but the increased focus on our security betrays her worry." Mm, that's not surprising. It is Komari's duty to ensure the security of everyone living in the colonies, after all, and she is a practical enough woman to know where her priorities lie, even if it means making her gardens a little less pleasing to the eye. What is that compared to the lives of the people under her charge, after all? "Just so[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." Anything else she's been doing to step up security about these parts? While everything looks as it always has been, you've also been around the foxes long enough to know that they're good at subtle touches and hidden surprises concealed in plain sight. "The den matron has asked both Kazuo[silly |-san ] and I to focus on the development of more intricate and better skilled blade puppets to make up for the lack of numbers which the military provost has under his command. They are not very intelligent and are only able to take simplistic commands, but they are also disposable and fight well enough, given that they are fashioned with a single task in mind." Rindo pauses a moment and sighs. "I think my colleague is a little too excited to be able to work on something that has genuinely captured his interest of late. After that business with analysing that control rod from the first time, he really needed a project he could feel passionate about as opposed to that which he performed as a matter of duty." The man does love his puppetry, doesn't he? "Automation has always been an interest of Kazuo[silly |-san ]'s, and what little remnants of the Belharan empire's old constructs that have been unearthed in this region have captured his attention. I'm sure he truly desires to have genuine targets to test his creations against in earnest..." Rindo looks pensive a moment, then shudders. "Please, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]perhaps we can speak of something else?" |Rindo puts her fingers together and turns her gaze from you. "Well, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]I am not entirely sure if it's proper to voice this particular of mine..." It's all right for her to speak her mind; you won't get mad or anything. What's up? "It's extremely foolish of me, but I find my more emotional side wishing that I were in the young lady Otomo's shoes, if only because it meant the provost would be showering me with so much attention. [kinu.isInari |It's not as if she appreciates having him try to put a security detail on her, even if keeping her safe is part of his job, so why not let someone who would appreciate it have as much? It's not fair... I would certainly enjoy the attention far more than she does. |Seeing her being taken care of like that as his fiancee and walking side by side with him... ah, I know it is about your daughter and you should take offense, and all it does is remind me of my failings. I had a whole five years and never even moved to express myself even subtly ] "But here I am, foolishly speaking ill of my betters... and even so! Even so! Ah, I should [kinu.isInari |do something about it, take this as an impetus to let the provost know of my feelings for him before it's too late; I have had five years in the colonies since I was a girl and never said anything, and yet it is only a matter of time before the colonial governor arranges for him to be married. That I have not said anything is my own fault, but to see the young lady Otomo get all that attention from him even if it is unrequited and will never go anywhere makes me so upset. Given that she is already engaged to Hitoshi, I should not worry, that is true |give up already, they are already engaged under the auspices of [silly |Myobu-sama |the high-lady ]; I should not even dream of settling for being a second wife or even a concubine ]. And yet, my body is aching deep inside with resentment and, um, something else... it is foolish, is it not?" Given that she's talking about wanting to put her own life in danger in order to catch the eye of the man she's infatuated with, yes, it's foolish to the highest degree. And yet, you did promise that you wouldn't get mad with her... even if she did take a jab or two at Kinu, if unavoidably given the nature of the discussion. Rindo bows her head and folds her ears down and to the side. "You said you would not get angry if I were forthright[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." And you aren't. [kinu.isInari |Maybe this should serve as a wake-up call for her — she had five years to make a move, and dithered out of her own indecision and insecurity. She can't control what she looks like, not with scars like these, but she can control how she behaves and it's made worse because she's already overcome so much and knows that for herself. If she's infatuated with Nakano, she'd better start moving forward on things; neither of them are getting any younger |She had five years to make a move, and didn't. When it comes down to it, even she admits it was her own indecision that led to this point — since she's not willing to be a second wife or concubine, something that's rare even if permissible in Old Country society, she should start looking forward and seeing about being more proactive the next time she gets infatuated with someone ]. "...The wrenching sensation has not gotten any better; if anything, it has gotten worse..." Then perhaps it will provoke her to action. |"I am very glad that the young lady Otomo did not suffer any permanent injuries to her person even after two attempts on her life. The gods must be watching over her, as expected of someone who is of direct matrilineal descent from them." Given that Rindo herself has white fur, they don't seem to have done much for her... "Ah, but I do not have — forgive me, but it is complicated[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Maybe we can sit down another time and discuss the intricacies of divine favor, but for now let me just say that it would be a terrible pity if a flower as fine as the young lady Otomo were to be blemished or marred in any way. Consider my fate — " she touches the uneven scars of her burned cheek — "and think if she had awoken minutes later on the first night. It is nothing that should happen to anyone, and so we should thank the gods for their providence, should we not?" Well, you're certainly thankful that Kinu is whole and unhurt. "Mm." Rindo lowers her gaze. "Everyone in the colonies is concerned for her well-being[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." |"Even though the colonial governor has ordered a lockdown of the torii gate, my life has not changed much[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. But thank you for being concerned about my well-being." You're just [pc.ra kitsune |doing the job that you signed up for as their patron deity's champion |doing your part to prove to the kitsune that you're capable of caring for other people as people, that's all ]. "My life is simple and my work fulfilling; I suppose I will miss soybeans as they do not grow easily in this climate and soil, but that is a small matter. Furthermore, I have confidence in the colonial governor and the sacred tree in their ability to keep us safe. Unless further developments happen — which the young lady Otomo seems to be keeping from us by drawing them to herself in an act of noble self-sacrifice — I think I will be fine. Save for the occasional departure every ninety days or so to feed, I do not leave the den much..." She doesn't desire more, then. Rindo shakes her head. "Once, I was slated for more, much more than most people will have in their lifetimes. All that was taken from me in an instant; I was taught in the harshest of manners how transient such worldly attachments can be. Now that we are under threat, I am still content with the little I have, because I have always intentionally made do with as much when I could have Kohaku bring me more. "Y[pc.ra kitsune |our Eminence, you |ou ] will find that us colonials are not unaccustomed to making do with little, even though we have come so far in the time we have been here under the governor's guidance. Please, do not worry about us and see to your family first; they are the ones to be bearing the brunt of this ordeal, especially the young lady Otomo. We will be as we have always been." ] ] '

rows.original: [rand |"It's tiring but necessary work," Rindo replies with a smile. "The shrine to the August Master at the Center of Heaven must be beautified, after all, and with no expense spared. I get to study and observe the specimens I have within the self-contained beds while I'm on the job, too, and being in such a vibrant environment with fresh air every day has done wonders for my health. "When I first arrived in the colonies, my left limbs were still weak from the burns, the skin tight and itchy all the time. While it hasn't gone away and never will, I feel a lot better and stronger in that half of my body now — it's certainly better than studying all day, and easier on my nerves, too. The colonial governor insisted that I work hard like everyone else during my first days here, and though I resented her for it at the time, I'm now quite thankful for her insistence on such." She seems a lot happier than she would otherwise have been cooped up in a room nursing her wounds. "Seeing people on their way through the gardens to petition his divine lordship at his shrine gives me joy. I feel like what I do has meaning, and that may be the most important thing about it all. Before, what I did was under the expectation of being married off, and I performed my studies because I was expected to... but this is different." |"There are several established aesthetic principles that I have to adhere to when designing and tending to the gardens, or at least the part meant for public viewing," Rindo explains. "For example, I should strive to have everything appear as natural as possible, untouched by artifice. Of course, for that to happen, a lot of work has to go into keeping it in shape. Quite paradoxical, given that the most so-called natural thing to do would be to let everything run rampant, but I fully understand what they meant." To be honest, while you're ignorant of these principles, you wouldn't even know, really. "That is the best outcome, yes. Ideally, you would feel the effects of my work without even knowing that the gardens had been shaped by my hand. You honor me with such praise, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]." Oh, now she's laying it on pretty thick. "It is true." |"While I do most of the fine work by myself, I have to borrow one of [silly |Fukuizumi-san |the artificer ]'s puppets when it comes to heavy lifting or gruelling labor. Sometimes trees have to be felled, dead branches pruned and cleared, stumps and roots dug up, and earth moved; I am not strong enough to handle such on my own, and others have their own tasks to handle. Simple, dumb labor is what the puppets are built for; they should be put to their purpose." They're not dangerous, are they? "They work well enough within the parameters they're given, and as a shaper myself, I have some knowledge of how they function, even if it is nowhere as extensive as their creator's." Rindo sighs. "Work is important for the spirit, and we should endeavor to do as much of our own work as possible. But even though I know I cannot go to such lengths of physical labor myself, I cannot help but feel at least a little guilty for asking for assistance from that man, and it doesn't help that he is... eccentric." |"The gardens do much more than beautify his divine lordship's shrine," Rindo explains with a smile. "For example, the arrangement of the shrubs, flowerbeds and trees form several geomantic patterns that direct the natural spiritual emanations and essences of the plants to form powerful wards against evil spirits and spells. Such arrangements are common sights in fortifications back in the Old Country, where blocking a hex may be just as vital as blocking an arbalest bolt." You had no idea. "Every major adjustment to the gardens' arrangement must go through the colonial governor for review and approval before it may be enacted. It is also why walking on the grass is discouraged." Given the little chuckle back there, you're not sure if the latter statement was completely serious... still, that's quite impressive. "Of course, there are other purposes. The water iris, lilies and lotuses serve to purify streams flowing into the arcology by means of their stems and roots; these cultivars have been carefully shaped to absorb toxins from the inflow and break them down. The outflow back to nature uses reeds, which absorb large quantities of water as well and are easily gathered and burned to destroy toxins and corruption if need be, or turned into building materials otherwise." That's quite impressive; everything works together to give rise to more than one purpose. If nothing else, the design and planning that went into all of this must have been astronomical. "As the old tanuki saying goes, 'no plant wasted.' Though it may not look like it, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]space is at a premium here in the den, and thus efficiency is key." |"The shrine gardens are open to the public at all times of day. So long as you are mindful of others and conduct yourself with propriety, you are welcome to stay as long as you like. Of course, should you behave otherwise, Miko, Mai and I are within our rights to request that you leave; this place is not ours, but we merely hold it in stewardship for the August Master at the Center of Heaven." Has she had to evict anyone from the premises before? Rindo chews on her lip as she thinks, folding her ears forward. "Not... not often, I don't think. I cannot speak for Miko and Mai, but personally I've only had to chase off Takahiro for being drunk and disorderly. Most people are conscientious enough to be pleasant, be it on their way to the shrine or simply to take in the atmosphere for a while. It makes me happy when people come to appreciate my work and share in the peace it has brought me, so come all you want[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ][party.has kiyoko |, [silly |High Lady |Myobu-sama ] ]." ]
rows.translation: [rand |这是一项虽然辛苦但必不可少的工作，”林多微笑着回答道，“毕竟，位于天中心的天之中央尊主神社必须得到修缮，而且必须不惜任何代价。在工作期间，我还可以研究那些被放置在专门培育箱中的样本，而且每天都能生活在这样一个空气清新、充满活力的环境中，对我的健康确实大有裨益。 当我第一次来到这些殖民地时，我的左半身仍然因为烧伤而显得虚弱，皮肤总是紧绷且发痒。虽然这种状况至今仍未消失，也不会消失，但我现在感觉自己左半身的状况已经好多了，也强壮了许多——这总比整天学习要好得多，也对我的神经来说更加轻松。殖民地的总督要求我在初来这里的几天里像其他人一样努力工作。虽然当时我对此感到不满，但现在我真的很感激她的这一要求。 如果她一直被关在房间里疗伤，她现在的样子肯定会比现在快乐得多。 看到人们穿过花园，前往他的神殿向他的神圣陛下请愿，这让我感到非常高兴。我觉得自己所做的一切都是有意义的，而这或许才是最重要的。以前，我学习只是因为别人期望我这么做，将来也会被嫁出去；我学习，也只是因为别人有这样的期望罢了。……但这次不一样。 |在设计和打理这些花园时，至少是那些供公众观赏的部分，我必须遵循一些既定的美学原则，”林多解释道。“例如，我应该努力让一切看起来尽可能自然，不带有任何人为造作的痕迹。当然，要想实现这一目标，就必须投入大量的精力来确保一切井然有序。这其实有点矛盾——因为最“自然”的做法应该是让一切顺其自然、失去控制，但我完全理解他们的意图。说实话，既然你对这些原则一无所知，那你其实也根本不会察觉到这些。 “没错，那样的结果才是最好的。理想情况下，你应该能感受到我的努力所带来的影响，却丝毫不知道这些花园其实是经过我精心设计才变成现在的样子的。您能给予我这样的赞美，真是让我感到无比荣幸。 [pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |[pc.name] ]哦，现在她可真是说得太过分了。” “这是事实。 |虽然大部分细致的工作都是我独自完成的，但我还是需要借用到某一样工具或资源。 [silly |福岛先生 |工匠 ]在需要重体力劳动或艰苦的工作时，它们就是我的得力帮手。有时候，我们需要砍伐树木、修剪并清理枯枝、挖出树桩和根系，还要搬运泥土——我一个人根本没有足够的力气来完成这些工作，而其他人也有自己要处理的任务。简单、重复性的劳动正是这些傀儡被创造出来的目的——它们就应该被用来完成这样的工作。” “它们应该不会构成危险吧？” “在给定的使用范围内，它们的表现已经足够好了。作为制造者，我对它们的工作原理也有一些了解，虽然这些知识远不如它们的创造者那么深入。琳多叹了口气。工作对精神状态确实很重要，我们应该尽自己最大的努力去完成工作。但尽管我知道自己无法从事那么繁重的体力劳动，我还是会因为向那个男人求助而感到内疚，更何况他本身…………有点古怪。 |这些花园的作用可不仅仅是美化他这位神圣君主的居所，”林多微笑着解释道，“比如，灌木丛、花坛和树木的布局形成了几种风水格局，这些格局能够引导植物自然散发出的灵性能量，从而形成强大的屏障，抵御邪恶精灵和法术的侵袭。在旧国时期的防御工事中，这样的布局十分常见——因为阻挡邪术与阻挡弩箭同样重要。 你根本不知道。 “对于花园布局的任何重大调整，都必须先经过殖民地总督的审核和批准才能实施。这也是为什么不建议在草地上行走的原因。” 听到那边传来的轻笑声，你不确定后半句话是否完全是认真的……不过，这也确实令人印象深刻。 当然，这些植物还有其他用途。水鸢尾、百合和莲藕通过它们的茎和根来净化流入弧形建筑群的溪流；这些植物品种经过精心培育，能够吸收流入水中的毒素并将其分解。而流回自然的水体则利用芦苇来净化——芦苇不仅能吸收大量水分，而且在需要时还可以被收集起来燃烧，从而销毁其中的毒素和污染物；当然，它们也可以被用作建筑材料。 这确实令人印象深刻；所有这些元素相互配合，共同实现了多种功能。单是设计和规划工作所投入的成本，想必也是巨大的。 正如那句古老的狸猫谚语所说：“没有哪种植物是被白白浪费的。”虽然看起来可能并非如此，但实际上[pc.ra kitsune |阁下， ]在这个巢穴里，空间是非常宝贵的，因此效率才是关键。 |这些神社花园全天都对公众开放。只要您注意不影响他人，行为得体，就可以在这里待多久都行。当然，如果您有不恰当的行为，我和米可、真子也有权要求您离开——这个地方并不属于我们，我们只是受天中宫的天之中央尊主委托来管理它而已。她之前有没有不得不把别人赶出过这个地方？ 林多咬着嘴唇思考着，把耳朵向前搭着。“没有……应该没有吧。我无法代表米可和舞，但就我个人而言，只有过一次因为贵弘喝醉后闹事，才不得不把他赶走。大多数人都很有自觉性，会表现得彬彬有礼，无论他们是在前往神社的路上，还是只是想暂时感受一下那里的氛围。当人们前来欣赏我的作品，并感受到它带给我的宁静时，我会感到非常开心，所以，请随时前来吧。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ][party.has kiyoko |， [silly |高阶女士 |宫部大人 ] ]。" ]
rows.raw: ' [rand |"It's tiring but necessary work," Rindo replies with a smile. "The shrine to the August Master at the Center of Heaven must be beautified, after all, and with no expense spared. I get to study and observe the specimens I have within the self-contained beds while I'm on the job, too, and being in such a vibrant environment with fresh air every day has done wonders for my health. "When I first arrived in the colonies, my left limbs were still weak from the burns, the skin tight and itchy all the time. While it hasn't gone away and never will, I feel a lot better and stronger in that half of my body now — it's certainly better than studying all day, and easier on my nerves, too. The colonial governor insisted that I work hard like everyone else during my first days here, and though I resented her for it at the time, I'm now quite thankful for her insistence on such." She seems a lot happier than she would otherwise have been cooped up in a room nursing her wounds. "Seeing people on their way through the gardens to petition his divine lordship at his shrine gives me joy. I feel like what I do has meaning, and that may be the most important thing about it all. Before, what I did was under the expectation of being married off, and I performed my studies because I was expected to... but this is different." |"There are several established aesthetic principles that I have to adhere to when designing and tending to the gardens, or at least the part meant for public viewing," Rindo explains. "For example, I should strive to have everything appear as natural as possible, untouched by artifice. Of course, for that to happen, a lot of work has to go into keeping it in shape. Quite paradoxical, given that the most so-called natural thing to do would be to let everything run rampant, but I fully understand what they meant." To be honest, while you're ignorant of these principles, you wouldn't even know, really. "That is the best outcome, yes. Ideally, you would feel the effects of my work without even knowing that the gardens had been shaped by my hand. You honor me with such praise, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]." Oh, now she's laying it on pretty thick. "It is true." |"While I do most of the fine work by myself, I have to borrow one of [silly |Fukuizumi-san |the artificer ]'s puppets when it comes to heavy lifting or gruelling labor. Sometimes trees have to be felled, dead branches pruned and cleared, stumps and roots dug up, and earth moved; I am not strong enough to handle such on my own, and others have their own tasks to handle. Simple, dumb labor is what the puppets are built for; they should be put to their purpose." They're not dangerous, are they? "They work well enough within the parameters they're given, and as a shaper myself, I have some knowledge of how they function, even if it is nowhere as extensive as their creator's." Rindo sighs. "Work is important for the spirit, and we should endeavor to do as much of our own work as possible. But even though I know I cannot go to such lengths of physical labor myself, I cannot help but feel at least a little guilty for asking for assistance from that man, and it doesn't help that he is... eccentric." |"The gardens do much more than beautify his divine lordship's shrine," Rindo explains with a smile. "For example, the arrangement of the shrubs, flowerbeds and trees form several geomantic patterns that direct the natural spiritual emanations and essences of the plants to form powerful wards against evil spirits and spells. Such arrangements are common sights in fortifications back in the Old Country, where blocking a hex may be just as vital as blocking an arbalest bolt." You had no idea. "Every major adjustment to the gardens' arrangement must go through the colonial governor for review and approval before it may be enacted. It is also why walking on the grass is discouraged." Given the little chuckle back there, you're not sure if the latter statement was completely serious... still, that's quite impressive. "Of course, there are other purposes. The water iris, lilies and lotuses serve to purify streams flowing into the arcology by means of their stems and roots; these cultivars have been carefully shaped to absorb toxins from the inflow and break them down. The outflow back to nature uses reeds, which absorb large quantities of water as well and are easily gathered and burned to destroy toxins and corruption if need be, or turned into building materials otherwise." That's quite impressive; everything works together to give rise to more than one purpose. If nothing else, the design and planning that went into all of this must have been astronomical. "As the old tanuki saying goes, 'no plant wasted.' Though it may not look like it, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]space is at a premium here in the den, and thus efficiency is key." |"The shrine gardens are open to the public at all times of day. So long as you are mindful of others and conduct yourself with propriety, you are welcome to stay as long as you like. Of course, should you behave otherwise, Miko, Mai and I are within our rights to request that you leave; this place is not ours, but we merely hold it in stewardship for the August Master at the Center of Heaven." Has she had to evict anyone from the premises before? Rindo chews on her lip as she thinks, folding her ears forward. "Not... not often, I don't think. I cannot speak for Miko and Mai, but personally I've only had to chase off Takahiro for being drunk and disorderly. Most people are conscientious enough to be pleasant, be it on their way to the shrine or simply to take in the atmosphere for a while. It makes me happy when people come to appreciate my work and share in the peace it has brought me, so come all you want[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ][party.has kiyoko |, [silly |High Lady |Myobu-sama ] ]." ] '

rows.original: [var0 |[rand |"It's a little embarrassing going out with others to find benefactors," Rindo admits with a slight blush. "Because of my appearance, I cannot quite offer up the opportunity to copulate in exchange for feeding; many find my appearance disturbing, and the natives are no exception. Many are repulsed and do not wish to receive pleasure from my body in exchange for their beneficence... therefore, I have had to come up with some other things in trade." Such as? Looking away, the white-furred kitsune looks shocked for a moment as she clearly realizes or remembers something, then puts her fingers together and twiddles them. "[pc.ra kitsune |Forgive me, your Eminence, but... I would rather not say, if you please. It is somewhat personal |I would rather not say ]. I know I was the one who brought this up, but I just recalled — " Well, if it makes her uncomfortable, you won't press. How about something else? "Yes, let's." |She still has family across the ocean, right? Does she still keep in touch with them? "That's correct. I... I do not correspond with them. Looking back upon things, my existence only made their lives more complicated and brought undue attention upon them. My mother had hoped, through the marriage that I was slated for, to rise somewhat in social esteem; no, things are better this way. Like a child given a fortune, they would not have known what to do with anything I'd brought them. "Is it hard to leave and break ties, to be considered all but dead? Yes, it is, very much indeed. But it is for the best. As the saying goes, nothing can be done about it." |"That night when the fire broke out in my chambers, a wanderer came in off the street to help my brother clear the wreckage of the timbers and drag me out half-alive; if not for their help, my brother wouldn't have gotten to me in time and I would've been burnt up. It was a strange figure, bundled up in clothes so loose that none of us could tell if it was a man or a woman inside all of that... the magistrate's office put out a call for the stranger to step forward during the investigations into the cause of the fire, but no one ever came." A wandering do-gooder appearing in the nick of time to set things right; it sounds like something out of a legend. "I don't think it was even a person under all of that. My memories are unclear, but by all accounts the wanderer had only one tail. That's not possible — even the youngest kit fresh out of the womb has two, yet everyone's recollections align on that single point." If she doesn't think it was someone underneath all of that, what was it? Rindo looks askance. "I don't know, and I wouldn't dare to speculate[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. Something cursed, certainly." |"It's surprising how quickly one's fortunes can change in the blink of an eye, and completely out of the blue. When I laid myself out to sleep, I was going to be married into a distant branch family of a divine clan, was studying in preparation for the next imperial examinations in hopes of landing a minor appointment in the civil service as befitted my station, was going to improve my family's standing through my future and pretty face. "And within the space of an hour or two, all of that went up in smoke." ... "Back then, it felt like some kind of cruel joke, that everything I'd worked for and come to expect since I was a kit was taken from me in an instant; why work for anything if all your efforts could be made pointless at the whims of the gods? It would have been easy for me to slip into despair; it was easy for me to slip into despair at the carefully planned life that'd been laid out before me to be destroyed in an instant and me myself thrust into an uncertain future. "But that is not our way[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. It was a long and strange road to get from there to here, but now I stand before you with a smile on my face." |"My name stems from a particular kind of flower — I believe it is called the gentian in the Belharan language. There're local variants of the plant native to these lands, too, but they have sharper leaves, shallower roots and violet flowers instead of the deep blue that they take in my homeland. Those that I brought along with me from across the ocean changed the color of their petals over successive generations, but not their roots or leaves... being able to make these observations first-hand makes me all the happier to be a student of natural history." |"I think the most difficult part of adjusting to my new existence was seeing the world through one eye. Even after healing, my scars still itched and felt tight, but I could live with that, take salve to ease the hurts. The loss of my ability to truly judge distance and depth, though... I didn't know how much I relied on it until it was taken from me. At the time, I grew frustrated... but years on from the fact, I think I've learned to have a greater appreciation for everything and everyone around me and not take them for granted, with the knowledge that it can be gone the very next day without any warning whatsoever. As one might put it, it's a change of perspective." |"I arrived in the colonies when I was fourteen summers of age, barely months after the fire. The burns on my body weren't completely healed yet, but the physician determined that I was well enough to make the trip through the torii gate, and my brother confessed to me that he feared for my life if I continued to stay with them. Living in the colonies would be beneficial for my health in more ways than one, and a position had already been secured for me. "I... there was nothing left, save my family, and I had to agree with my brother that this was for the best. My fiancee's clan had called off the betrothal, and with it my education and access to their finances. Even so, I was a loose end... a loose end who needed to be tied up. Better that I tie myself up than let someone else do it for me, in a fashion that might be far more uncomfortable than I would like. "And so here I am, five years on. Life has not been perfect, but it's been better than I otherwise would have had, and it's a virtue to be grateful for what you have.." ] |[rand |"It's still a little embarrassing going out to seek benefactors," Rindo admits with a slight blush. "While I've gotten better about it ever since meeting you, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ], the natives still find my appearance disturbing, which is perfectly understandable; while I understand that scars can be considered quite attractive amongst the locals, mine aren't the sort that are earned in battle and valor. "But even though many are repulsed and do not wish to receive pleasure from my body, leading me to resort to other trades in exchange for their beneficence... I no longer feel as self-conscious about it as I used to do. I am your concubine, am I not[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" That she is. Not to worry — so long as Rindo remains in service to you as your concubine, you'll take good care of her. Well, even beyond that, given that should she ever choose to leave when this passes you won't drop her like a hot potato, but she knows what you mean. Rindo's lip twitches, and she puts her fingers together and twiddles them; you can't tell if she's trying to work up the courage for something, or consciously hold herself back. Then at last, she surges forward and wraps her arms about you in a wide hug, rolling her body from side to side against yours, as if she were an animal trying to get her scent all over you; her burnt, leathery scars press against your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] as she rolls all over you in that hug of hers, but you've gotten used to their feel at this point. When it's finally time for the both of you to be parted, Rindo pulls back with an exhilarated sigh and glances around to make sure no one was spying on the both of you; it's all you need to do to reassure her of such with a pat to the head. "Ohh..." her one good eye is disoriented and vacuous until a second patting snaps it back to attention. "I hope I was not too familiar, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ], but... I needed that." |She still has family across the ocean, doesn't she? Has she received any further news on how they're doing? Rindo gets a faraway, half-lidded look in her good eye and half-turns to regard you. "Admittedly, no, and I have asked the den matron to not forward me any news of the matter under it is conclusively resolved one way or the other. Before, I already neglected to correspond with them; my existence only made the lives of my kin more complicated and brought undue attention upon my house, especially since all this has started up once more. Since the matter is being handled by those with far greater ability than I could ever hope to bring to bear, what would be the point of such news that I can take no practical action upon? "Learning to discern what I could practically change and what I could not was an important step forward, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ]. After that, the way forward became clear. Some call it mental sanitation, I simply consider it practical." |How is being your concubine holding out for her? You take it that her social standing has changed, for the better or for worse? "All in all, I would say that it's increased, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ]. Kohaku is a perfect little chatterbox... within two days of her being given the news, just about everyone in the den knew about it. No doubt whoever is causing trouble across the ocean for me and mine is already in the know about this change in the state of affairs, so all that truly remains is to wait and see what happens." That's all? No curious or judgemental looks from her fellow foxes? Not even envious ones? Given the rigid nature of kitsune social structure, you'd have imagined that someone becoming [pc.ra kitsune |the divinely appointed champion |a native ]'s concubine would have made more of a splash than that. "Oh, don't get me wrong, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]there's plenty of talk going on around me; it's just that none of it is centered about whether it was right or not. After all, if this relationship was supported by the den matron, everyone trusts that there's got to be a good reason behind it all, so even those who might have had reservations or be outright opposed to my concubinage aren't going to say anything.[pc.ra kitsune | Besides, who would be so audacious as to question the choice of someone as esteemed as you? ]" You chuckle dryly and ruffle Rindo's thick hair. All right, she's made her point. All's well that ends well, and hopefully it stays that way. "There is something to being united in purpose, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ], even if one may not be fully cognizant of it. Like a school of fish turning, as it were. Everyone trusts the den matron to do right by them, and that trust has yet to been betrayed; as a result, someone like me is able to reap the benefits thereof." |"Don't worry about me," Rindo says as you hold her close. "You have important business out in the world to attend to, being [pc.ra kitsune |his divine lordship's champion and all |a native noble of no small import ]; you can leave me in the care of everyone here and I'll be fine. When you need my comforts, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]I'll be here waiting for you, as is my duty and desire alike." You know she's right, but the way she puts it is... well... She giggles at that, shaking her head. "It is true that there are no more mysterious one-tailed strangers around to pull me out of even more suspicious fires, but now I am surrounded by people much better than that. Do not worry that you're shirking on your promise to care for my safety while you are absent — remember that said protection is more in our association with each other, rather than any physical presence." No, you didn't quite mean that. There are other things you feel she ought to expect from you as your concubine. Rindo looks confused for a moment, then raises a hand to her mouth and giggles. "Oh, oh. Do not worry about that in the least, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence. |okay? ] Even if it does not involve copulation, I was perfectly able to keep myself fed before you arrived, and now I would not trouble you with such obligations. I am an adult after all, and capable of providing for myself. "And as for the more emotional needs... that has not changed from before, so once again, there is no need for worry. You should not feel obliged to share your love with me, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ] — while I'll accept it all the same, I would rather you take comfort in me because you truly wish to, and not because you feel like it is your duty to me because I am your concubine. It is more... enriching that way." Even so... "Concubinage as we practice it originated not in Kitsuhon, but in Macah, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ]. Near the end of one of their dynasties, there were simply so many in his silly little palace that if they were lucky, said ape of an emperor would visit them one night a year, if not two. There were hundreds. "Happily, the practice has changed quite considerably in accordance with our culture, but even so! I am certainly not starved for attention, and if I were that desperate I'd have other measures to sate myself. Don't concern yourself overly with my welfare, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]. I'm an adult and capable of seeing to my basic needs; remember that I pulled myself out of my hole before you came along. I won't break just because you don't see me for a few days." With a final giggle, Rindo pulls herself close and kisses you on the cheek. "Worry not about me. If you remember nothing else from all that I've said, remember that." |"It's odd. Despite the situation that my family now finds itself in, I feel a lot less pressured than I did when I first found myself in the colonies. "Maybe it's just because I'm not who I was before, that's all. The den matron is doing her best on my behalf, and I've come to accept that after becoming your concubine, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]there's nothing more I can reasonably do about the situation." You don't have very much to say, but there's plenty you can do. Like, for example, pulling Rindo against you in a warm hug and feeling her thick hair and tails shift and press against your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] while she sighs softly. "It feels like a weight's been lifted off me. Was I always worrying that this would happen, even if I didn't know it, and now that it has I'm simply glad that it has finally come to a head? That everything I was unknowingly preparing for was to steel me for this? Or simply that I'm ready to fatalistically accept anything that might happen next? "Or maybe it's just because I'm your concubine now, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ]?" ] |[rand |"It's still a little embarrassing going out to seek benefactors," Rindo admits with a slight blush. "I hope I was not too familiar, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ], but... that felt good." You can only hope it was. Locally, then, since the latter by her own admission has limited relevance. "Less than it would have rightfully warranted, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |then ]." This is very interesting. "I, uh, she said that I needed bigger hips. Wider, that is, for easy births." Rindo gestures with her hands in the unmistakable roundness of a rounded curve, clearly completely flustered by the entire recounting of the process[pc.ra kitsune | and dropping all formality to boot ]. Yes... you've probably heard enough. Huh. That's something you didn't consider, but makes sense in context — that being said, Kinu's still just a young woman, or at least as the Marches count these things. The thought of her having a retainer waiting on her is... well, she needs to be fully responsible for herself first before taking on others, and that's a skill she's still learning. Who will take care of the sacred gardens in her stead? "Well, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]that is also part of it. Certainly I will not be forbidden from gardening on occasion in the future — it is a pastime befitting someone of my standing — but the actual bulk of the care will have to fall to someone else. In these years before I assume full responsibility in the service of the young lady Ōtomo, I will have to select and train a protege in its care. This, too, is part of my training — the ability to find, retain, and train talent for the young lady Ōtomo's future needs." Even though she just said her education would be largely identical to Kinu's, you nevertheless have to thank her for going through with all this for your daughter's sake. It should have been obvious, but her marrying into Komari's clan has brought along with it so much extra work she needs to shoulder... Certainly I will not be forbidden from gardening on occasion in the future — it is a pastime befitting someone of my standing — but the actual bulk of the care will have to fall to someone else. In these years before I assume full responsibility in the service of the young lady Ōtomo, I will have to select and train a protege in its care. This, too, is part of my training — the ability to find, retain, and train talent for the young lady Ōtomo's future needs." Even though she just said her education would be largely identical to Kinu's, you nevertheless have to thank her for going through with all this for your daughter's sake. It should have been obvious, but her marrying into Komari's clan has brought along with it so much extra work she needs to shoulder... "I cannot remain a flower girl forever, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]. That much was certain — even though the reality was constantly comfortably off in the distance, it was also much closer than my perception would allow me. The high lady Ōtomo has been very kind in giving me a gradual road forward in order to ease me out of my current role and into a better one, without making too many adjustments to my life all at once. "That, and I cannot deny that my current situation has its privileges..." |"The high lady Ōtomo has given me permission to be more familiar with her both in speech and action," Rindo admits, rubbing her forehead. Maybe it's just a matter of getting over that initial trepidation — you can see where Rindo's coming from. Kiyoko is the person with the most authority in the colonies, and it can be hard for some to get over that instinct to bow and scrape; this is certainly doubly so for a kitsune. But as the saying goes, familiarity breeds contempt... if Kiyoko demands it, then no doubt she'll fall into the appropriate bracket of speech, or however the kitsune make measure of these things. "I certainly hope that you're right about this,[pc.ra kitsune | my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]" Rindo admits with a small sigh. rows.original: [var0 |[kinu.isInari |[rand |"The young lady Otomo puts so much work and effort into our fields, even though she has her own to take care of. You don't think her mother would have formally trained her in the art of shaping as it pertains to agriculture — Kiyoko was always disapproving of Kinu's agricultural pursuits since she was very young. It's probably as Rindo says — that it was either self-taught, or it's just something your daughter does without even realizing it herself. "I've asked her for some of her techniques," Rindo admits with a wistful sigh. "I thought that perhaps I could learn something with which I could improve the gardens. "On one hand, it must be gratifying to be so blessed with abundance. On the other hand, such effortless success means there is a lack of impetus to improve." Oh, she doesn't need to worry about the latter in the least — you'll talk to Kinu about it. To imagine what your daughter could do if she truly applied herself... oh, the possibilities. |"The young lady Otomo is fun to talk to. "That is true; kitsune noblewomen are classically trained in feminine weaponry to defend the home when the others are out. But even so, such hidden depths of ferocity! Your household would be more harmonious if she were a little more yielding, but then she wouldn't be the daughter you know anymore, would she? |"Even though Mai teases the young lady Otomo a lot, it's all good-natured. Even you can't beat her on a regular basis, so having Mai instil some humility in your dear Kinu is for the best. Sometimes, the talented need to be brought down to earth by the experienced. "I learn so much just by watching them that I don't mind losing when it comes to my turn to play[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." |Rindo sighs wistfully. "The young lady Otomo is possessed of such a robust and voluptuous body that I can't help but feel a little envious, to my eternal shame. "That's why I worry a little... but what good would worrying do, over something that I can't control and cannot influence?" ] |[rand |"The young lady Otomo comes through the gardens on the way to the shrine every afternoon, and never fails to greet me by name. Wanting to help Kinu is fine, but she really shouldn't go to such lengths until she's setting herself back to do so — gods know you've had problems yourself spoiling your daughter during her childhood. Well, you're not going to push her to do something that she doesn't want to do, but when she does gather herself she ought to know that your daughter's always welcoming, and as her parent you think it'd be good for her to have more friends on a personal level, rather than just her looking down on everyone from up top, if she gets what you mean. "..." |"The young lady Otomo is always very kind to everyone she meets. Well, you know from personal experience that Kinu is anything but blind to the nature of people[kiyoko.numKits 2 | — it comes with her job of big sister, after all ]. "I shouldn't worry, since I know there's someone else watching out for her, but I still do. I just... it's just... I suppose my own bad memories are coloring my perception of the issue. Please forgive me[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." ] ] |[kinu.isInari |[rand |"The young lady Ōtomo has been very kind to me ever since our concubinage has been formalized[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. Word has been getting around lately that she needs to put on a bit of weight — you're not sure if it's Kiyoko or Komari who put Kinu up to it, but anything your daughter grows and cooks is delicious. "I expect that she feels some responsibility for me now, even if our households are still technically separate. The young lady Ōtomo may not speak very much, but it is actions like these which have led me to believe that we have always been friends, even if she does not say it outright." |"I think the young lady Ōtomo has warmed up to me ever since I became your concubine,[pc.ra kitsune | my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]" Rindo begins. "Our tasks still keep us away from each other in different spheres of life, but I feel that because of our shared relation through you, we've grown closer. Silk covering metal, as it were. Rindo puts her hands to her cheeks and shakes her head vigorously. "I know I shouldn't speak ill of the young lady Ōtomo, and especially not when she's now technically my liege, but — the instinct's eating me up inside, and I think it's only going to get worse before it gets better." Look... has she ever just considered talking to Kinu about it? Rindo stares at you wide-eyed. "T-that would be complaining[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. Not just complaining, but complaining to one's face. It's just-" Not done? She swallows hard, and that's all the answer you need. Now then. Kinu has spent her entire childhood growing up in the ways of manners, etiquette and being a good listener, or so her mother has been so kind to inform you. Your darling daughter has made a lot of effort to appear approachable to the people whom she will eventually rule over, and you'd like Rindo here to appreciate said effort and humor her, okay? "I..." A direct command backed by divine authority should be sufficient to get around all those instinctive inhibitions in her head? 一方面，能够拥有如此丰富的资源，肯定是一件令人欣慰的事情。另一方面，这种毫不费力的成功反而会让人缺乏提升自己的动力。” 哦，她完全不必担心后一点——你可以和小娟谈谈这个问题。想象一下，如果你的女儿真正全力以赴，她能够取得多大的成就……哦，可能性真是无穷无尽啊。 rows.original: [var0 |"The colonial governor has been very kind to me for the five years that I've been here — at first, I resented it, thinking that it was merely cheap sympathy of the sort that was thrown at me in the first months of my convalescence. Then, I thought it was because I bore white fur and the brandings of divinity, and that she was trying to curry favor with me... "What a fool I was. We're all broken here in the colonies[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]; one way or the other, we're all broken. Since no one usually speaks of it in polite company, it took me a little while to learn of the governor's unique circumstances, but when I did — oh, the shame." She couldn't have known. "Even then, I shouldn't have behaved as petulantly as I did. It's true that I was hurting, not just from the loss of my future or my body but also because of the fact that I'd been torn away from my family and everything I'd known. Given the way I lashed out at her whenever she tried to help me, resenting that she put me to work under Miko and Mai... I'm trying to make it up to her every day for the grief that I must have given her, for the infinite patience she must have had with me. To treat someone like that who was only trying to help yet another one who had landed in her demesne — my behavior was absolutely unforgivable." |"When I was younger, I had the chance to personally meet a few provincial governors who were making visits to my betrothed's family, usually begging his mother for some political favor or the other. Maybe it's just the few I encountered, but they all viewed their positions as shameful banishments, and were constantly scheming to try and return to the capital with the luxuries and opportunities that being so close to the Cherry Blossom Throne brought. "The colonial governor is something else altogether. Maybe it's because she built this entire place with her own two hands, maybe it's because she knows the capital is forever closed to the likes of her, maybe it's because she is no longer truly kitsune because of her curse. Whatever the case... she didn't have the same air about her that I sensed on all those other officials when I met her, and I think that's what eventually led me to coming around on her words. "Because of the nature of what we are, our society is by necessity rigid to instil discipline in managing one's hunger; there is little room for those who even stay slightly from the Way, even the repentant or victims of misfortune. The colonial governor has created a place where those broken like me can find a second chance and be put to productive work in service of the Cherry Blossom Throne, and that is something to be thankful for; do-overs are hard to come by in the Old Country where shame can stain your line for generations. The fact is unavoidable that we are failures or descendants of failures; we're the ones often rightfully rejected by culture and society and left to live in a strange land and away from familiar things. And a place for us to belong and still be useful to the Cherry Blossom Throne is a good thing, even though we're seen as even lower than the backwater provinces." |"Prior to arriving through the torii gate, I wasn't sure what I was going to be doing in the colonies, or what I was even capable of doing; I had the vague idea that I would be performing tasks related to my education in natural history and shaping, and that would be the end of it. After all, the true reason I was being sent across the ocean was to get rid of me in the same way that inconvenient people used to be sent to the backwater provinces in the past. "The colonial governor was very kind in taking a personal interest in my case — she assigned me productive work that I could do despite my still-healing burns, put me in a position where I could see the positive impact of the tasks I was assigned to, and through her insistence that no pair of hands be idle, gave structure to my life instead of allowing me to spiral into despair. I think that was important — the ability to see the good that one is doing and the meaningfulness of one's work is something that's far more evident here in the colonies, freezing backwater as it might be. Whenever I was tempted to feel useless and pity myself, I was faced with the very tangible and undeniable proof of the gardens I was assigned to tend to. "Sometimes, nothing can be done about matters. It's not unknown for people to come through the gate, wander off into the forest and vanish for good; for many, being torn away from one's old reality can be a fate worse than death, which is why exile to the colonies is so terrible. But at least the governor tries to save them, and I truly believe that her conscience is clear on every point that she did her utmost to draw them away from the brink of despair — only the gods know how many people she's seen pass through that gate over the centuries she's lived." |"They tell cautionary stories of the colonial governor back in the Old Country across the ocean. At this point, she's a legend... and not in a good way[silly | — 忌み狐 is the term they use when they don't want to say her name, which is always ]. The retainer who failed her liege and was not just banished from the land, but also directly cursed by the patron deity of her people for her failings in letting his descendant perish on her watch; a curse passed down in the blood which continues to afflict all her descendants with madness and shame, even those who have moved back to the Old Country. "[silly |外道, the term is... s |S ]omeone who has fallen beyond the Way — no longer truly a kitsune, made to perform penance in perpetuity until his divine lordship is satisfied, and who knows when that will be. They say that this is what happens to you if you're lazy, if you're lax in your duties, if you don't pay attention to detail and serve with your utmost strength. "I don't know what I was truly expecting, given all the stories I'd heard of the colonial governor, the most cursed of all the unclean and banished foxes removed from polite society. Some sort of abomination, maybe, with sharp teeth, baggy eyes and unkempt fur, halfway to losing a hold upon her hunger. I certainly did not expect someone who could have been my own grandmother... appearances can be deceiving, of course, but even so. In these last five years I've labored in the seat of her governance, that appearance has been anything but false." |"Have you ever wondered why the colonial governor favors youkan so much? If I were in her place, undying and not needing to eat at all, I'd soon find everything turning to ash in my mouth, no matter how tantalising the sweetmeat. That she still stubbornly finds joy in something as simple and base as eating... that says something about her." ... Rindo closes her eyes, folds her ears forward and clenches her fists. "Would it be that I had such strength of will; for the past five generations, the governor's existence has been one endless loop of death and loss without release, if one's inclined to be pessimistic. But she's not. That dessert was reputedly her deceased consort's favorite, too, back in the day. If she put that out of her mind, if she forgot it, the governor wouldn't be herself any more; she'd be something in the shape of her, perhaps, but not the person herself. And... I wonder if it helps her remember; our minds are not made to contain more than a lifetime's worth of memories. "Equivalent exchange — the price of love is inevitable loss, but we shouldn't let that prevent ourselves from loving anyway. Life isn't about avoiding loss and suffering; if it were, suicide is the best way to avoid suffering, isn't it? But it's not — and seeing the colonial governor move forward regardless of the price to be paid, I came to realize how much simpler my situation was in comparison and that my contentious nature was in the wrong. Everything fell in place after that." |Rindo softly clears her throat as you ask her about Komari; turning around a bit, her good eye scans your surroundings, before appearing satisfied with your current privacy. Nonetheless, her voice is a hushed whisper as she leans close to you. "[pc.ra kitsune |Your Eminence |[pc.name] ], I was recently, ah... made aware of a certain rumor, involving yourself and Matron Komari... I was hoping to ask you about it, if I may." [pc.dcb |Oh boy, guess this was inevitable. What has she heard? |Uh-oh. You think you know what this is about. What's she heard? |Ooh, gossip! What's she heard, huh? You hope it's something cool! ] Rindo looks around once more, before whispering into your ear. "Well... the talk of the town is, you and the matron have been... entertaining one another. Whether or not such rumors are true is another matter, but—" You're about to interject, but Rindo shushes you before you can speak. Continuing, her good eye remains fixed onto you. "Before you elaborate, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ], I'd like to clarify that I'd rather not know if it's true. That's... not something I'd like to visualize. If it is, however, I do have a humble request." Oh? What would that be? "Do be gentle with Matron Komari, please. It's been a long, long time since she had anyone; while his divine lordship's curse may help to preserve her body, she is still old. I'm sure you understand my concerns." ...[silly |Bruh |Ah ]. It's all you can do not to snicker at the oddity of the situation. Covering your mouth with a hand, you tell Rindo that you'll keep it in mind; she hasn't got anything to be worried about. Rindo nods gently, giving you a thin smile as she steps back. "Thank you, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]; that's all I ask. Now then, had you wished to discuss anything else?" ]

]无论如何，我们所有人都有着自己的伤痛。因为在这种正式的场合里，通常没有人会谈论这个话题，所以我花了一些时间才了解到那位州长所面临的特殊处境。但当我了解到真相后——哦，真是太令人难过了。 她根本不可能知道这些的。 即便如此，我也不应该表现得如此任性。的确，我当时非常痛苦——不仅因为失去了自己的未来和身体，更因为被从家人和熟悉的一切中夺走。每当我试图帮助她时，我都会对她发脾气，甚至怨恨她让我在米可和舞的领导下工作……现在，我每天都在努力弥补给她带来的痛苦，感谢她对我所表现出的无限耐心。对于这样一个只是试图帮助另一个陷入困境的人，我竟然用那样的方式对待她——我的行为确实不可原谅。 |在我年轻的时候，我有幸亲自见过几位前来我未婚夫家拜访的省级官员。他们通常都是去求他母亲帮忙谋取一些政治上的好处。也许只是我遇到的那些人如此，但他们都认为自己的职位是一种耻辱，因此一直在密谋如何能够回到京城，从而享受靠近皇权所带来的种种优渥条件与机会。 这位殖民地总督确实与众不同。也许是因为她完全是靠自己的双手建立了这个地方，也许是因为她知道首都永远不会向她这样的人敞开大门，又或许是因为那场诅咒让她不再真正属于狐族。无论原因是什么……当我见到她的时候，她身上并没有那些其他官员所具有的那种气质，而我想，正是这一点最终让我开始相信她的话了。 由于我们的本质决定了，我们的社会在培养人们控制饥饿感的自律能力方面，必然会采取严格的态度；对于那些稍微偏离这种规范的人，无论是那些幡然醒悟的人，还是那些遭遇不幸的人，社会几乎不会给予任何宽容的空间。这位殖民地总督创造了一个这样的地方：对于那些像我这样遭遇不幸的人来说，这里提供了重新开始的机会，让他们能够从事有益的工作，为“樱花王座”服务。这一点确实值得感激；在那个古老的国家，重新获得机会实在是一件难得的事情，因为耻辱往往会让一个家族的声誉受损数代人。事实上，我们注定是失败者，或是失败者的后裔；我们常常被文化与社会理所当然地排斥，被迫生活在陌生的环境中，远离熟悉的一切。然而，如果有一个地方能够让我们找到归属感，同时还能为“樱花王座”发挥作用，那无疑是一件好事——即便在我们眼中，这个地方甚至比那些偏远省份还要低微。" |在通过……之前鸟居当时我并不确定在那些殖民地会做些什么，甚至也不清楚自己究竟有什么能力；我只有一个模糊的想法：可能会从事与我在自然历史和雕塑方面的所学相关的任务，仅此而已。毕竟，把我派往大洋彼岸的真正原因，其实就是想把我扔到某个偏远的地方去，就像过去人们会把那些惹人厌烦的人送到边远省份一样。 那位殖民地总督非常关心我的处境，她亲自为我安排了一些工作，这些工作即使在我烧伤尚未痊愈的情况下，我也能够完成。她让我能够看到自己所承担的任务所带来的积极效果，同时也坚持不让任何一个人闲置下来，这样我的生活才重新有了秩序，而不是陷入绝望之中。我认为这一点非常重要——能够看到自己所做的一切带来的积极影响，以及自己的工作所具有的意义，在这些偏远、封闭的殖民地中，这种感受尤为明显。每当我想要觉得自己一无是处、自怨自艾时，那些由我负责照料的花园，就会为我提供那些实实在在、无可辩驳的证据，让我明白自己的价值所在。 有时候，对于某些事情，人们确实无能为力。有人会穿过大门，走进森林，然后永远消失不见，这种事并不少见；对许多人来说，被从自己熟悉的现实世界中夺走，这种遭遇甚至比死亡还要可怕，因此被流放到殖民地，实在是一种极其残酷的惩罚。但至少这位州长在努力拯救他们，我真心相信，对于自己所做的一切，她的良心是清白的。她已经竭尽全力将他们从绝望的边缘拉了回来——只有神明才知道，在她漫长的生命中，有多少人走过了那道门槛。" |人们会讲述关于大洋彼岸旧大陆上那位殖民地总督的警示故事。如今，她已经成了一个传说……只不过，这个传说是负面的。[silly | 忌み狐”是他们用来指代她的那个名字时的说法，因为他们实在不想直接说出那个名字。 ]那个背叛了自己的主君、不仅被逐出这片土地，还因为自己的失职——让主君的后代在她看管期间丧生——而遭到族群守护神的直接诅咒的女性；这个诅咒通过血脉传承下来，至今仍在折磨着她所有的后代，让他们陷入疯狂与耻辱之中，即便是那些已经回到了旧国的人也不例外。 "[silly |外道”，这个词……嗯，怎么说呢…… |S ]那些已经背离了正道的人——不再算是真正的狐妖，他们必须永远接受惩罚，直到他们的神明主宰感到满意，而谁也不知道这一刻究竟会到来。人们说，如果一个人懈怠、不履行自己的职责、不注重细节，也不全力以赴地侍奉神明，那么就会落到这样的地步。 说实话，我根本不知道自己究竟期待着什么。毕竟我听到了太多关于那位殖民地总督的故事——人们称她为所有被驱逐、被社会摒弃的‘不洁之狐’中最可恶的一个。或许她就是某种令人作呕的生物，长着锋利的牙齿、凸出的眼睛和杂乱无章的毛发，几乎已经失去了控制饥饿感的能力…… 我确实没有想到，一个人竟然会看起来像我的祖母……当然，外表有时候会具有欺骗性，但即便如此，过去这五年里，我一直担任着她所担任的职务，而她的那副模样，确实一点也没有虚假之处。" |你有没有想过，为什么那位殖民地总督会偏袒幽玄这么多吗？如果我处在她的位置，既不会死亡也不需要进食，那我很快就会发现，无论那些美味的食物有多诱人，它们在我口中都会立刻化为灰烬。而她却依然能够从如此简单、平凡的事情——进食中找到快乐……这一点，确实说明了她的性格。 等价交换——爱的代价往往是失去，但我们不应该因此而放弃去爱。人生本来就不是为了逃避失去与痛苦；如果真是这样，那么自杀不就是避免痛苦的最佳方式吗？但实际上并非如此。看到那位殖民地总督不惜付出任何代价也要坚持自己的道路，我突然意识到，与他的处境相比，我的问题其实简单得多，而我之前那些争执与抱怨，其实都是无谓的。从那以后，一切似乎都变得井然有序了。
