Life isn't about avoiding loss and suffering; if it were, suicide is the best way to avoid suffering, isn't it? But it's not — and seeing the colonial governor move forward regardless of the price to be paid, I came to realize how much simpler my situation was in comparison and that my contentious nature was in the wrong. Everything fell in place after that." |Rindo softly clears her throat as you ask her about Komari; turning around a bit, her good eye scans your surroundings, before appearing satisfied with your current privacy. Nonetheless, her voice is a hushed whisper as she leans close to you. "[pc.ra kitsune |Your Eminence |[pc.name] ], I was recently, ah... made aware of a certain rumor, involving yourself and Matron Komari... I was hoping to ask you about it, if I may." [pc.dcb |Oh boy, guess this was inevitable. What has she heard? |Uh-oh. You think you know what this is about. What's she heard? |Ooh, gossip! What's she heard, huh? You hope it's something cool! ] Rindo looks around once more, before whispering into your ear. "Well... the talk of the town is, you and the matron have been... entertaining one another. Whether or not such rumors are true is another matter, but—" You're about to interject, but Rindo shushes you before you can speak. Continuing, her good eye remains fixed onto you. "Before you elaborate, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ], I'd like to clarify that I'd rather not know if it's true. That's... not something I'd like to visualize. If it is, however, I do have a humble request." Oh? What would that be? "Do be gentle with Matron Komari, please. It's been a long, long time since she had anyone; while his divine lordship's curse may help to preserve her body, she is still old. I'm sure you understand my concerns." ...[silly |Bruh |Ah ]. It's all you can do not to snicker at the oddity of the situation. Covering your mouth with a hand, you tell Rindo that you'll keep it in mind; she hasn't got anything to be worried about. Rindo nods gently, giving you a thin smile as she steps back. "Thank you, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]; that's all I ask. Now then, had you wished to discuss anything else?" ] "

rows.original: [kohaku.anyKids |[rand |"Hmm... I'm not sure if I should say this, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |really ]. It feels wrong to badmouth someone..." You asked, so she's welcome to answer. Besides, you're not Kohaku, so it's not as if the entire den will be knowing about whatever it is by the next morning. "I know it's irrational, especially when one considers that the child is but a newborn, but I simply don't have a good feeling about Kohaku's daughter. [rindo.anyKids|Even if my own kit is about the same age|[rindo.pregStage 1|Even after my kit's popped from my tummy and grown up a little|If I were to have a child of my own]], I wouldn't let them play together." All right, you understand why she'd feel guilty about that — it is a pretty strong stance for someone as unassuming as Rindo to take. That being said... why, though? Rindo folds her arms and puts her hands in her sleeves. "It's just... a feeling. Nothing more[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. I don't have any proof or insight or divine revelation, nothing like that. It makes me feel terrible, but every time I see that child I get the impression that she's a dubious creature filled with terrible mischief. The kind who would defraud others without a single regret, as it were. There's absolutely no logical reason for my mind to reach for that... and yet it happens anyway. I'm sorry. Please don't tell Kohaku this — it would upset her to no end, even if it were just me who has these thoughts." |"Kohaku certainly has gotten a lot more popular now that she's a mother," Rindo remarks. "Everyone loves her daughter, and seeing the both of them together makes it even cuter than if they were both separate." How did the saying go? That the whole is more than the sum of the parts? Well, it's certainly true in her case — from what you've seen during your visits to the storehouse, people can't keep their hands off mother and daughter, both of them equally golden. "It's very, very endearing indeed, and fits the kind of energetic person that Kohaku is. I wonder if the novelty will pass, or they'll continue being this popular for some time to come. Seeing them like that, you can't help but wish the best for them." |"I'm seeing Kohaku more and more in the gardens these days. Usually it's on her way to the shrine to petition his divine lordship or get up to mischief with Miko, but I've managed to convince her to linger a little longer every now and then[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. Whatever the reason, it's good for her to be out and about at home — I think the only reason that she ever left the storehouse was to go on caravan, or for festivals where attendance was a social obligation. The decision to be more involved locally was a conscious one, although I do question why, of all people, she glommed onto Miko." It can't have been an easy decision for Kohaku to make. "On the contrary, the mater came up in our conversation the other day and she said there'd never been an easier decision. Everything in her life, all her experiences had led up to preparation for this point, and now that she was engaged in dealing with said matter it was time to put said preparation into practice instead of getting more of it. I'm not entirely sure what she meant by that — no doubt there are several implications that are obscure to me — but the main thrust of her reasoning sounds solid enough." |"In order to acknowledge her daughter's arrival, the den matron has decided to expand her quarters,[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence, ]" Rindo tells you with a respectful dip of her head. "Her sleeping chambers were originally a side closet attached to the storehouse — she insisted on it because living in the place meant she could be first in every morning and last to leave, which is what she felt was expected of her. But the place is small, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |you see ], and certainly wholly inadequate to the task of accommodating even a single child, hence the decision." Oh, that certainly is interesting. You've never actually heard of major renovations being made to the tree before — isn't it a living being, even if the foxes live in it? How does that work out? You think back to the first time you entered this place and how the inside of the tree felt bigger than the outside, plus the way the corridors and passageways seemed to change at a whim — an effect that, to be sure, feels a lot more muted now that its inhabitants have come to accept you being here, if it's present at all. Rindo thins her lips just a little. "I do not know[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Nevertheless, as someone who has some skill in shaping, the den matron has summoned me along with the artificer to work with her on the matter in the time to come. It is certainly not something that can be accomplished overnight, and before we even begin we must examine the situation and be sure that the proposed changes will not cause problems that will have to be fixed later. I'm quite excited to be able to work on something of more import than shrubs, flowerbeds and miniature trees, to be sure. [pc.ra kitsune |That feeling of fulfilment, of the realization of what you have been working towards... I'm sure you empathize, your Eminence. ] "But when we are done, however long that may take, Kohaku will have improved accommodations for herself and her get; that tiny place is no way for an energetic kit to live. There has not been much call for renovations in my generation, given the surfeit of accommodations amongst the branches; that the den matron has chosen to grant Kohaku this boon instead of requesting that she move to existing accommodations is a show of confidence in her future. I hope she understands this well[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." ] |[kohaku.pregStage 1 |[rand |"I must admit that it's a little shocking to see how much Kohaku's appetite has expanded while she's with child[rindo.anyKids | — even when I was a week or two away from my fullest I wasn't that hungry |[rindo.pregStage 1 | — I'm carrying myself, and while there's the urge to eat a bit more at meals I thank the gods that it hasn't gotten to that point. I wouldn't be able to do anything like that ] ]. I went into the storehouse the other day to get some of the decorations I'd ordered for the gardens, and Hotaru was there, steadily passing Kohaku a steady supply of snacks while she devoured them. It seemed absolutely never-ending..." Why was she tempted to join in? "You tease[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. But... I was, which is why I turned around and resolved to come back later in the day. If I'd tried to stay until the both of them were finished, I might've done something I would've regretted later." |"There's a rumor going around that Kohaku's been blessed by the August Master at the Center of Heaven himself, and that touching her tummy while she's with child will bring you good luck," Rindo tells you. "Have you tried it[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" You don't need any special reason to pet Kohaku's belly a lot — she deserves it just for being herself, and if that means some of this supposed good luck rubbing off onto you, you're all for it. Has she tried it? Rindo blushes a little. "I... I have[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." And did that bring her good fortune? "It felt like it, and perhaps the belief is enough to make at least some small part of it true." A warm smile. "[rindo.anyKids |But I think I'm the one who has been more thoroughly blessed by the August Master at this point. I did it anyway, let her share in my good fortune so that she can join me in motherhood swiftly and smoothly. That[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence, ]is what it's all about. She's the one who needs good fortune, not me. |[rindo.pregStage 1 |It was somewhat awkward for me to reach her over my own roundness, with how large it is, so Kohaku suggested that we rub our tummies together. That way we could share each others' good luck, and I wouldn't have to stretch all the way over." Oh, that would've been a sight to see. "It was a little embarrassing, but everyone seemed to like the moment of girlish playfulness, so I'm content with how it turned out[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Good fortune or no, it was worth it and made Kohaku happy, so I'm okay with that. |Kohaku had good fur before, but now that she's with child it's positively glowing with richness and vitality[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ] — it's so heart-warming to think that her child is giving back to her even in this small manner, isn't it? I may not have fully believed in the whole good fortune thing, but I just couldn't help but run my fingers through that fur. If only I had fur with that kind of gloss and texture... ] ]" Well, if Rindo isn't the kindly soul. That being said, one does wonder where that rumor came from, though. "Miko or Kohaku herself[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]," Rindo answers without hesitation. "Or perhaps the both of them working together, that's also possible. They have it in their mischievous natures to do something like this, and the fact that neither of the Kurokawa sisters have come forward to confirm or deny said rumors suggests Miko's hand in it. "In either case, it doesn't really matter. It keeps Kohaku in a good mood, and an expecting mother should be upset as little as possible, the rigors of her body notwithstanding." |"I particularly enjoy the fact that Kohaku's around more these days instead of being out and about on her business; it gives me more time to speak with her and understand her better. Well, maybe not so much speaking with her as opposed to hearing her speak, but it's still the same. Maybe it's just my imagination, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]but she has a lot more to say these days than before." Or maybe it's that she's around more to hear her speak. Kohaku is the kind of person who can hold a one-sided conversation and there really aren't that many other fonts of entertainment that're familiar to her. Perhaps Rindo could take the chance to help a little golden fox find a way to constructively spend a lot more free time? Rindo dips her head and titters. "I already have some ideas, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]so don't worry about it. All of her free time will be vanishing in the space of several months, so perhaps one shouldn't get too involved... but I do have some ideas. Please, leave it to me." |"Kohaku's gotten a lot more cuter than she was before," Rindo says with a giggle. "Do you know what I think she resembles[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? One of those adorable fortune cat statuettes I remember from my youth, all chubby, welcoming, and considerably heavier on the bottom. Even better, proprietors would place them in storefronts to bring in good fortune, so she fits! Although with how large she's going to be getting, being on her feet all day is going to be tiring, isn't it?" It would be. That being said, being with child really does tend to improve foxen women, doesn't it? "Mmm... [rindo.anyKids |having gone through it, I can't say that I'm impartial[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." |[rindo.pregStage 1 |I can't say that I'm impartial[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." Rindo drums her fingers on her ripe, round belly. |it does appear to be a trend at first glance, yes." She gives you a small dip of the head. ] ] "But I would submit that it helps bring out the best in us and amplify our most fetching qualities. For example, I would never be able to achieve the degree of adorable cuteness that Kohaku exudes, and has only intensified while she's been with child; it simply would not be in me. Similarly, I do not believe Kohaku would be anyone but herself, not would her condition exaggerate anything that wasn't already in her to begin with[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. We are simply who we are, and becoming mothers simply deepens our nature or forces us to confront our true selves. Is it not said that one truly discovers who oneself is when placed under strain?" ] |[rand |"Kohaku keeps on teasing me about getting married. I always say that she's liable to be scooped up first, given that she's small, cute and doesn't have burn scars over half her body, but she keeps on saying that I have a winning personality and that scars are actually attractive to a good number of people. I'm not sure if she's trying to tease me, it's really hard to tell given how good she is at mimicking emotions she doesn't really feel as part of her job. "Either way, it's not as if the colonies are awash with eligible bachelors, so the question really isn't one I should give great consideration to, anyway. Hmph, what a tease!" |"Kohaku really tries to please everyone, but while others think that it's an adorable affectation I'm not so sure about that myself." That's an interesting point of view. Could she explain? "If you end up trying to be like other people so they'll like you and do it too much, you'll lose sight of who you really are. Constantly trying to change yourself to be like other people to be accepted — maybe you didn't have a good grounding on your perception of yourself to begin with, or maybe you're trying to be someone you aren't. Either way, I don't think either is very healthy, but the nature of her tasks means that she has to do it in order to fit in with the natives when she's around them. Maybe that's why one of the reasons why people who do merchanting aren't really that well-liked, despite everything..." |"That little golden fox is really quite a gossip, I tell you. When I first arrived in the colonies, I thought I'd keep my head down and leave my past behind since nobody knew who I was or why I'd come over the ocean. I don't know how she managed it, but within a week Kohaku had managed to ferret out every single detail about my past and spread it all over the den." Is she sure it was Kohaku? That sounds quite tactless, digging into someone's past like that. Rindo folds her arms into her sleeves and pouts. "Well, I couldn't prove anything — who can, with a situation like that? Even so, I know she did it, and she's a notorious gossip to boot. It had to be her. "Even if it ultimately was for the best in forcing me to confront it and learn that everyone was fine with me being who I was, the whole episode nevertheless still left a pretty bad taste in my mouth. You just don't do that to people, digging up their personal secrets and spreading them all over, even if you think it's for their own good. As you said, it's tactless and rude. I supposed I might have been someone of particular interest given my face and fur, but even so!" |"I was told not to bring money when I came across from the Old Country, that there wouldn't be any use for it in the colonies. It was a strange feeling but a freeing one as well, even if it was more symbolic than anything; after my fiance's family called off the betrothal, it wasn't as if I had much to my name any more. Going up to Kohaku, collecting my first requisition from her... I think it was then that it truly sank in that I was going to have to live a much more humble and ascetic life than what I'd gotten used to in a large city. "She offered me taiyaki. I think being able to taste something sweet softened the blow somewhat... that, and she didn't openly stare at my face and even offered to trade in any of my possessions I found extraneous for things that I'd be needing for my new life in the colonies. And as the days dragged into months, the only news of the Old Country I'd get was from her lips, whenever I came in to claim my weekly allotment of necessities and make requisitions for particulars... I think the necessity of talking to someone as perpetually cheerful as that helped. She was just starting in her role as storehouse manager and quartermaster, just like I was in mine... "...Has it only been five years? It truly feels like a lot longer." |"Have you ever noticed that Kohaku's verbal tic of 'nojya' sometimes seems to be slightly off? Strictly speaking, if she were to be conversing in our mother tongue, she'd be using that sentence-ender of hers wrongly about a third of the time or so. Sure, she does come from the region of our homeland where it's common to do that sort of thing, but she also arrived here when she was very young. "What I'm getting at, I suppose, is that I'm not really sure if the verbal tic is genuine, or if it's just something that she adopted in an effort to be even more cutesy and charming than she already is. I guess it doesn't really matter in the end, but it's still something that bothers me in the back of my mind." ] ] ]
rows.translation: [kohaku.anyKids |[rand |嗯……我不确定是否应该说出来[pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |真的 ]说别人的坏话总觉得不太对……” 既然你问了，那她当然可以回答。而且，你又不是小花，所以就算她说了什么，第二天早上整个团队也不会都知道的。 “我知道这种感觉很不合理，尤其是考虑到那个孩子还只是个新生儿，但我就是对小花的女儿没有好感。 [rindo.anyKids|即使我自己的装备也差不多是那个年代的产物……|[rindo.pregStage 1|即使我的装备已经从我的肚子里“长”出来，并且稍微长大了一些……|如果我也有自己的孩子的话……]]我不会让他们一起玩的。” 好吧，你现在应该明白她为什么会为此感到内疚了吧—— 是对于像林多这样低调的人来说，这样的立场确实相当强硬。不过……为什么呢？ 林多双臂交叉，将手插进袖子里，说道：“只是……有一种感觉而已。没有别的原因。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]我没有任何证据、直觉或神灵的启示，没有任何这样的东西。这让我感到非常难受，但每次看到那个孩子，我都会觉得她是一个满口坏话、喜欢搞恶作剧的家伙——那种会毫无愧疚地欺骗别人的人。我的想法完全没有任何逻辑依据，但就是会这样。对不起，请不要告诉小花，如果只有我有这样的想法，也会让她非常难过的。 |自从成为母亲之后，小白确实变得受欢迎多了，”凛堂评论道，“大家都很喜欢她的女儿，而看到她们母女在一起，场面会更加可爱，比分开来看要有趣得多。 有句俗话说得好：整体往往大于部分之和。在她的案例中，这句话确实成立——从你参观仓库时的所见所闻来看，那些人简直对这对母女俩爱不释手部，她们俩确实都美得令人无法抗拒。 确实非常非常可爱，也完全符合红叶那种充满活力的人设。不知道这种新鲜感会不会很快消失，还是会在未来一段时间内一直这么受欢迎。看到他们这样的表现，真的会不由自主地为他们感到高兴和祝福。" |这些天，我在花园里越来越经常看到小红。她通常是在去神社向她的神明大人祈愿，或者是在和米可一起调皮捣蛋，不过我偶尔也能说服她多留一会儿。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输 ]无论出于什么原因，她能在家里四处走动、参与各种活动，这对她来说肯定是好事——我认为她唯一会离开仓库的时候，就是去参加商队活动，或者是一些参加这些活动被视为社交义务的节日。她决定更多地参与当地的活动，这是一个经过深思熟虑的决定。不过，我确实很好奇，为什么在所有人当中，她偏偏选择了与米科在一起。对小花来说，做出这样的决定肯定不是一件容易的事。 “相反，前几天我们在聊天时她提到，这个决定其实再简单不过了。她生命中的每一件事、每一次经历，都在为这一刻做准备。如今，当她真正开始处理这些事情时，是时候将这些准备付诸实践了，而不是继续进行更多的准备工作。我不太清楚她那句话的具体含义——毫无疑问，其中包含了一些我不太明白的隐含意义——但她的推理逻辑本身听起来还是相当合理的。 |为了庆祝自己女儿的出生，洞穴的女首领决定扩建她的居住空间。[pc.ra kitsune |阁下， ]琳多恭敬地低下头说道：‘她的卧室原本是储藏室旁边的一个小隔间——她坚持要住在那里，因为这样她就可以每天早上第一个到达那里，最后一个离开，她觉得这才是别人对她的期望。’不过那个地方实在太小了[pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |你懂的 ]显然，这样的设施完全无法满足甚至是一个孩子的需求，因此才做出了这样的决定。” “哦，这确实很有趣。你以前肯定从未听说过这棵树曾经进行过大规模的翻修吧——尽管狐妖们住在里面，但它不也是一种生物吗？这是怎么运作的呢？你回想一下自己第一次来到这个地方的时候，那时候树的内部给你的感觉比外部还要宽敞，而且那些走廊和通道似乎会随时发生变化——当然，现在这里的居民已经接受了你的存在，这种效果可能已经减弱了很多，甚至可能已经完全消失了。 琳多微微抿了抿嘴唇，说道：“我不知道。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]尽管如此，由于我在造型方面具备一定的能力，巢穴的女首领还是邀请我和那位工匠一起，在未来的一段时间内共同处理这个问题。这显然不是一蹴而就的事情，在开始行动之前，我们必须先仔细分析现状，确保所提出的修改方案不会引发后续需要解决的麻烦。能够参与处理比灌木、花坛和微型树木更重要的事情，我确实感到非常兴奋。 [pc.ra kitsune |那种成就感，那种看到自己为之努力的一切终于得以实现的感觉……我相信您一定能感同身受，阁下。 ] 不过，无论需要多长时间，等我们完成这些工作后，琥珀就能拥有更舒适的居住环境了——那个狭小的地方根本不适合一个充满活力的小家伙居住。在我们这一代人中，由于各个分部之间有大量的住所可供选择，因此几乎没有人要求对现有住房进行翻修。而巢穴的女主管选择给予琥珀这样的优惠，而不是要求她搬到现有的住处去，这其实是对她未来的信任的一种体现。我希望她能够充分理解这一点。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]。" ] |[kohaku.pregStage 1 |[rand |我必须承认，看到小红在怀孕期间食欲变得如此旺盛，确实让人感到有些惊讶。[rindo.anyKids | — 即便在我距离达到最胖状态还有一两周的时间时，我其实也不觉得特别饿。 |[rindo.pregStage 1 | — 我现在还能控制自己的食欲，虽然在吃饭时确实会想多吃一点，但还好情况还没有发展到那种地步。要真是那样，我就真的无能为力了。 ] ]前几天我去了仓库，去取一些为花园准备的装饰品，结果看到萤也在那里，她一直在不断地给琥珀提供零食，而琥珀则津津有味地吃着那些零食，似乎永远也吃不完…… 为什么我会想要加入她们呢？ “你真是太会逗人了[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]运输 rows.original: [rand |"Do you know of the artificer's prosthetic arm?" You've seen it, yes. Anyone who's encountered the man can't help but notice the wooden arm joined at his shoulder where a real one should be — still green and sprouting, and every bit as nimble and dexterous as a real one would be. Maybe even better. "The official report was that there was an accident in one of the buildings he and several other shapers had designed. It was under construction, he was overseeing it as the on-site engineer, and suddenly one of the roots gave way and crushed his arm under a pallet of roofing tiles. It had to be amputated, as it was beyond saving." That's quite gruesome. Is that why he ended up on this side of the ocean? "They say... they say he engineered the accident deliberately, to have an excuse to test out his newly invented prosthetic on himself. Do you believe it?" If that's the case, why didn't he just cut off his arm and do it that way? Why need a pretext? "Ah... you see, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], ]our society has, uh, unspoken rules about how things are done. And cutting off your own arm to sate your thirst for scientific curiosity is not something that is done in the Old Country... nor anywhere, for that matter. The accident was too timely and convenient, the crush too clean, the replacement such a perfect success. Or at least, that's how the story goes... it's not out of the question that he could have done it, right?" No, thinking about it, you could definitely see Komari's pet madman doing just that. Others might be off-limits, but experimenting on himself... yes, you can see why such rumours could take root, they're certainly plausible. |"The artificer is far more adept at the art of shaping than I am — for example, I could never hope to fashion a puppet as detailed and open to command like he is easily able to do. However, our expression of the art and associated duties are almost completely divergent, so we tend to see each other more as equal colleagues than one above the other. He is more senior, of course, but that is only to be expected. I'll leave the measurements of the water treatment pool to him, and he'll leave the upkeep of the reeds and checking of miasma levels to me. It all works out in the end when we make the twice-monthly report to the colonial governor." |"Kazuo always instinctively gives me the creeps when I look at him," Rindo admits, biting her lip nervously as if expecting the artificer to appear out of nowhere. "Sure, he's made himself useful and improved uncountable things about the den since his arrival, given that he used to be a civil engineer. Sure, his puppets save me so much heavy lifting and hard labor which I couldn't hope to do myself with my scarred left half. Sure, he's always been professional and polite with me... maybe too polite. "But... he's a madman. A useful madman, that's true, but a madman nevertheless. His knowledge of shaping is only surpassed by the imperial governor, and that's because she's had more than five lifetimes over to learn what she has. I just find myself instinctively wanting to be as far away from him and his living prosthetic of an arm as i can, and the worst part of it all is that I can't justify any reason for me to do so. It's the exact same thing people would do when they saw me and my burnt-off face coming down the street — they would not so discreetly give a wide berth and avoid looking at my disfigurement too closely. I... I just feel terrible about treating him with such prejudice, and yet I can't help myself." |"I'm sure Kazuo doesn't mean to leave his workshop such a mess, he just forgets to clean up when his mind's off chasing his next great idea. All the junk is a danger to him and Mai when she comes in to bring him his tea — sometimes, when I come in to return the puppets I borrow and he's not around, I'll tell the construct to pick up the mess before returning itself to its alcove." She giggles. "When I come in, the man'll tell me just his puppets cleaned up his workshop without him telling them to, and asks if I think his constructs are starting to exhibit behaviors he didn't put there when he made them. "Sometimes, it takes a very intelligent man to believe a very silly thing." |"Kazuo really loves tea, all forms of the stuff prepared in all manner of styles. Mai also loves the stuff — better that than smoking — and so she's always willing to oblige. "And with everything else the man does, it's an obsession. He really doesn't care for tea etiquette, but his knowledge of blends, aromas and flavors is encyclopedic, surpassing even Mai's. That ferocity and intensity of purpose, directed at something so seemingly trivial... it can get scary at times." ]
rows.translation: [rand |你知道那位工匠制作的假肢手臂吗？” 你肯定见过，对吧。任何见过那个人的人，都会注意到他肩膀上那只木制手臂——在正常应该有真手臂的地方。那木臂还是绿色的，上面还长着新枝，它的灵活性和灵巧性，丝毫不亚于真正的手臂。也许甚至更糟。 “官方报告称，他在设计的其中一栋建筑发生了事故。那栋建筑当时正在建设中，他作为现场工程师负责监督施工过程，突然之间，其中一根支撑结构发生了坍塌，导致一块屋顶瓦片压在他的手臂上，造成了严重伤害。那部分组织必须被切除，因为已经无法挽救了。” “听起来真是太可怕了。难道这就是他来到大洋这边的原因吗？” “人们说……人们说他是故意制造了那场事故，这样就能有借口在自己身上测试他新发明的假肢了。你相信吗？” 如果真是这样，那他为什么不直接砍掉自己的手臂来达到目的呢？为什么非得找个借口呢？ “啊……你明白的， [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]， ]我们的社会有一些不成文的规定，规定了事情应该如何进行。而为了满足自己对科学的好奇心而割掉自己的手臂，这种行为在老挝是绝不会发生的……事实上，在任何地方都不会有人这么做。这次事故发生得实在太及时、太凑巧了，事故造成的后果也处理得过于“干净”，而替代品的使用也取得了堪称完美的效果。或者至少，故事是这么讲的……也不能排除他真的这么做过的可能性，对吧？ 不，仔细想想，完全有可能想象到小毬那个疯狂的宠物会做出这种事。别人或许不在他的攻击范围内，但对自己进行实验的话……完全有可能。…是的，你可以理解为什么这样的谣言会流传开来，它们确实听起来很可信。 |那位工匠在塑造艺术方面比我熟练得多——比如说，我永远不可能像他那样轻松地制作出如此精致、且能够响应指令的木偶。然而，我们在表达这种艺术以及履行相关职责的方式上几乎完全不同，因此我们更倾向于将彼此视为平等的同事，而不是上下级关系。他的资历当然更深厚，这也是意料之中的事。我会把水处理池的测量工作交给他，而芦苇的维护以及瘴气浓度的检测则由我来负责。每两个月向殖民地总督汇报一次情况时，这些分工安排最终都会得到妥善的协调。" |每当我看到一夫的时候，我总会不由自主地感到一阵不安，”凛堂承认道，她紧张地咬着嘴唇，仿佛随时都期待着那个工匠会突然出现在面前。“当然，他确实为我们的藏身处做出了很多贡献，也改进了许多方面——毕竟他以前是一名土木工程师。当然，他的木偶也让我免去了许多繁重的体力劳动，毕竟我的左半身带着伤，根本无法完成那些工作。当然，他对待我总是非常专业且礼貌……也许吧。太有礼貌。 但是……他是个疯子。没错，是个有用的疯子，但终究还是个疯子。他在塑形方面的造诣，只有那位帝国总督能比得上，而那也是因为总督拥有超过五世的时间来钻研这些知识。我发现自己本能地想要尽可能远离他和他那具“人造肢体”。最糟糕的是，我找不到任何理由来解释自己的这种行为。就像人们看到我那张被烧毁的脸走在街上时，也会本能地避开我，避免仔细看我的伤痕一样。我……我对自己因为他而产生这样的偏见感到非常内疚，但却控制不住自己。 |我敢肯定，一夫并不是故意把他的工作间弄得这么乱糟糟的，只是当他全神贯注地思考下一个伟大的创意时，就会忘记打扫卫生。所有这些杂物对他和舞来说都是安全隐患——有时候，当我去还他借来的木偶，而他又不在场时，我就会让那个自动装置在把木偶放回原处之前把垃圾清理干净。她轻声笑了起来：“当我进去的时候，那个男人会告诉我，他的那些木偶竟然在没人吩咐的情况下自己把他的工作间收拾得干干净净，然后还会问我，是否觉得这些木偶开始表现出一些他在制作它们时根本没有设定过的行为。而我总是答应，因为那就是事实，不是吗？” 而他从来都不会停下来思考一下：也许是她自己让他们这么做的吧？ 林多微笑着说道：“有时候，只有非常聪明的人才愿意相信一些非常愚蠢的事情。" |一夫真的很喜欢茶，各种种类、各种制作方式的茶他都喜欢。这是他向殖民地总督唯一提出的要求——希望能进口来自旧国不同地区的茶叶。他总是问我是否考虑在殖民地种植茶叶，舞也一样，总是让我给她准备一些好茶。舞也很喜欢茶，比起抽烟，她更喜欢喝茶，所以她总是很乐意帮忙准备这些茶。 再加上这个人做的其他所有事情，这种对茶的执着简直已经成了一种病态。他其实并不在意饮茶时的礼仪规范，但他对各种茶叶的搭配、香气以及味道的了解简直博大如百科全书，甚至超过了舞。这种强烈的专注力，被投入到这样一件看似微不足道的事情上……有时候真的会让人感到害怕。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"Do you know of the artificer's prosthetic arm?" You've seen it, yes. Anyone who's encountered the man can't help but notice the wooden arm joined at his shoulder where a real one should be — still green and sprouting, and every bit as nimble and dexterous as a real one would be. Maybe even better. "The official report was that there was an accident in one of the buildings he and several other shapers had designed. It was under construction, he was overseeing it as the on-site engineer, and suddenly one of the roots gave way and crushed his arm under a pallet of roofing tiles. It had to be amputated, as it was beyond saving." That's quite gruesome. Is that why he ended up on this side of the ocean? "They say... they say he engineered the accident deliberately, to have an excuse to test out his newly invented prosthetic on himself. Do you believe it?" If that's the case, why didn't he just cut off his arm and do it that way? Why need a pretext? "Ah... you see, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], ]our society has, uh, unspoken rules about how things are done. And cutting off your own arm to sate your thirst for scientific curiosity is not something that is done in the Old Country... nor anywhere, for that matter. The accident was too timely and convenient, the crush too clean, the replacement such a perfect success. Or at least, that's how the story goes... it's not out of the question that he could have done it, right?" No, thinking about it, you could definitely see Komari's pet madman doing just that. Others might be off-limits, but experimenting on himself... yes, you can see why such rumours could take root, they're certainly plausible. |"The artificer is far more adept at the art of shaping than I am — for example, I could never hope to fashion a puppet as detailed and open to command like he is easily able to do. However, our expression of the art and associated duties are almost completely divergent, so we tend to see each other more as equal colleagues than one above the other. He is more senior, of course, but that is only to be expected. I'll leave the measurements of the water treatment pool to him, and he'll leave the upkeep of the reeds and checking of miasma levels to me. It all works out in the end when we make the twice-monthly report to the colonial governor." |"Kazuo always instinctively gives me the creeps when I look at him," Rindo admits, biting her lip nervously as if expecting the artificer to appear out of nowhere. "Sure, he's made himself useful and improved uncountable things about the den since his arrival, given that he used to be a civil engineer. Sure, his puppets save me so much heavy lifting and hard labor which I couldn't hope to do myself with my scarred left half. Sure, he's always been professional and polite with me... maybe too polite. "But... he's a madman. A useful madman, that's true, but a madman nevertheless. His knowledge of shaping is only surpassed by the imperial governor, and that's because she's had more than five lifetimes over to learn what she has. I just find myself instinctively wanting to be as far away from him and his living prosthetic of an arm as i can, and the worst part of it all is that I can't justify any reason for me to do so. It's the exact same thing people would do when they saw me and my burnt-off face coming down the street — they would not so discreetly give a wide berth and avoid looking at my disfigurement too closely. I... I just feel terrible about treating him with such prejudice, and yet I can't help myself." |"I'm sure Kazuo doesn't mean to leave his workshop such a mess, he just forgets to clean up when his mind's off chasing his next great idea. All the junk is a danger to him and Mai when she comes in to bring him his tea — sometimes, when I come in to return the puppets I borrow and he's not around, I'll tell the construct to pick up the mess before returning itself to its alcove." She giggles. "When I come in, the man'll tell me just his puppets cleaned up his workshop without him telling them to, and asks if I think his constructs are starting to exhibit behaviors he didn't put there when he made them. And I always say yes, because it's the truth, isn't it?" And he never stops to consider that she might have told them to do it? Rindo smiles. "Sometimes, it takes a very intelligent man to believe a very silly thing." |"Kazuo really loves tea, all forms of the stuff prepared in all manner of styles. It's the only luxury he's requested of the colonial governor — tea imported from different regions of the Old Country. He's always asking me if I'll ever turn my attention to the possibility of tea cultivation in the colonies, and the same goes for Mai in asking her to brew up a nice pot. Mai also loves the stuff — better that than smoking — and so she's always willing to oblige. "And with everything else the man does, it's an obsession. He really doesn't care for tea etiquette, but his knowledge of blends, aromas and flavors is encyclopedic, surpassing even Mai's. That ferocity and intensity of purpose, directed at something so seemingly trivial... it can get scary at times." ] "

rows.original: [hotaru.anyKids |[rand |"Oh, the seamstress? I've been hearing more about her, now that she has a child. Not as much as I'd have expected to were I back on the other side of the torii[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ], but I've had many years to accept the eccentricities of the colonies." Perhaps it's for the best that the other half of the den's gossip circle actually take a dose of her own medicine and experience what it's like to be gossiped about. You take it that having a kit out of wedlock is frowned upon in the Old Country? Rindo gives you a small nod. "Not exactly out of wedlock[pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. There is the matter of society, which helps us discipline our appetites and dissuade us from turning outright predatory on those who live with us, especially the tanuki. More importantly... children need to be fed, and it can be hard for one parent to gather sufficient essence for everyone. Customs vary, but in the particular province I came from, anyone facing hardship would receive help from others." And you expect that in turn, people were expected to not unnecessarily impose on others' generosity and civic-mindedness. "Just so[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. The longer you wear this form, the more in line with our thinking you become." Um, thanks? "Form and function are wedded to each other, and so it is the same for child-raising |. The more you enmesh yourselves with us, the more you're coming around to our way of thinking. As far as I know, you may be the only local who has ever tried in earnest." Um, thanks? Although you're seriously surprised at being the first, really. "As with Hotaru's case, it's to do with the reason behind the intent rather than the intent itself ]. Therefore, it is not strictly a matter of wedlock: for example, there is no shame in having a child with a concubine. Indeed, at various times it was even encouraged amongst those who could afford it, in direct opposition to common mores." But back to the point of Hotaru — she's perfectly fine with Kaori. "Yes. So long as there's no trouble, I expect the seamstress will receive none. All of us are in the colonies for our own reasons[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]." [hotaru.isMILF |With how curvaceous Hotaru's become, you don't doubt that she won't have any problems finding enough benefactors |Despite her eccentricities, Hotaru has always been the careful kind when it comes to these things. You're not worried that she won't be able to feed both Kaori and herself ]. And well, you'll chip in when you can. "I don't doubt that you'll take good care of her[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. She deserves it." |"I hear that the seamstress' new kit is even more gifted than she is." Rindo pauses, takes in your expression, then hurriedly shakes her head. "Oh, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]I didn't mean it that way. It's not a euphemism for... well, that. But if Mikoto is right, the infant has taken her mother's spiritual power, and concentrated it even further. We can only hope that the gift and affliction are not one and the same." You'd hope so, too. You're aware of all those old legends that claim that great gifts also come with great burdens, but stories are just that. Besides, you're just that special[pc.ra kitsune | — enough to be a god's champion, at any rate. If that isn't enough for free boons for your children, what is? |. ] Rindo laughs at that. "Well, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], ]Hotaru was only too eager to show off little Kaori when I came to deliver the dyes she needed. Unlike the mother, the daughter is calm even as an infant. Hardly fussed when Hotaru let me hold her — [rindo.anyKids |even if my son is well-behaved, this is something else altogether |well-behaved is one thing, but kits should have energy ]. Perhaps it's too early to pass judgement, but that child was born old. "Mikoto says she'll be keeping an eye on that one, but I get the feeling Kaori will exasperate her thoroughly in the years to come. Not because of any mischief, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]but a complete lack of it — which in its own way is just as infuriating, especially to someone like Mikoto." |"Such a coincidence that you should bring up Hotaru[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. I was speaking with the den matron the other day about the next generation of colonials, [rindo.anyKids |my son included, ]and how they're shaping up to be different from those fresh through the torii gate. I'm not that much different, but some family lines have been here since they sailed over with the den matron, and she's had a long time to observe the gradual changes in the generations." That's interesting, but how does Hotaru come into all of this? Rindo pauses, perhaps realizing that she's treading into gossip territory, then resigns herself to entering the pit she's dug. "Of course, you're aware that Hotaru is gifted, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |no doubt ]. Her own mother was somewhat touched as well, but not as deeply as Hotaru is, and now her own daughter — "— It's just such a great change from one generation to the next. To someone who is in a position to observe these things like Matron Komari is, the more generations a certain family line has been in the colonies, the more pronounced the change between generations. Generally speaking, that is — exceptions exist, as always." And Hotaru's line has been here since the beginning? "Or close to it[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. Certainly longer than I have." Rindo wrings her hands and sighs. "This isn't so strange when you consider how the provinces back across the ocean have their own local stereotypes and customs, right down to individual prefectures. For example, the mountain stock that Kohaku's derived from. "Compared to those, the colonies have only existed for a short time, and to be blunt, we are a collection of those who are not explicitly criminal, but simply do not fit well in society. And eventually, a mixture of things becomes something in its own right, something which little Kaori embodies ever more than her mother. But here and now, I'm able to observe myself the same process which created all the little colorful provincial cultures and attitudes. Isn't it exciting[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]?" |"Mmmmh." Rindo wrings her hands, hesitating. "The seamstress[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" Is something the matter, for her to clam up at the sound of Hotaru's name? "Well, Mikoto asked me to pick up several mulberry cultivars from her the other day, and it took an hour longer than it should have because Hotaru insisted on showing off her daughter." And she's bothered by the delay? A laugh. "No, not at all. We don't do things like the mainland, not in the colonies — being a little late with a delivery because you met a friend and had a talk is understandable. I was somewhat troubled by that attitude when I first arrived, but I've gotten used to it as the years have passed. "No, it's about little Kaori. Hotaru let me hold her for a little while, and I got the feeling that she'll be a handful for her mother in the years to come." Hmm, how so? The time you've spent with Kaori has only given you the impression of a rather calm child, disinclined to fuss. "Exactly what I mean. Hotaru isn't just a storyteller, she's a well-known gossip, friends with Kohaku, and overall catalyst for all kinds of trouble. Even if motherhood has imposed some kind of responsibility on her, Hotaru remains who she is at heart despite settling down a little out of necessity. "But the kit? It's strong enough I could feel it while simply holding her in my arms[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. There won't be any concerns about her foxfire getting out of control, despite her gift being stronger than her mother's. But two personalities so disparate having to live under the same roof... she might just drive her mother to exasperation without even intending to." With all respect, while you can feel it too, Kaori's just a little swaddled kit who does little more than eat and sleep. "[rindo.anyKids |Trust me[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ], my son did more than just eat and sleep when he was Kaori's age |That's exactly what I mean[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Kits that age do more than just feed and nap ]. It's... being surprisingly well-behaved, and for one so young. "[pc.ra kitsune |My [pc.mf |lord |lady ]... ]I'm not going to say that the future is set in stone, or that people don't change. But it's what I sense in little Kaori's aura [rindo.anyKids |in much the same way I felt out my son's nature |that gives me pause ], let alone the spiritual scent that hangs around her. The fact that it's intense enough for even you to feel it should be proof enough; Hotaru should prepare herself for the years to come. If it's possible for a child to be too well-behaved, it's that one." ] |"Oh, the seamstress? She... she does her job, I suppose. There really isn't much to say about her, and given where we are that could be considered a good thing[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. When everyone has a colorful past, the one with a mundane upbringing is a saint." Rindo smiles ruefully. "I should know." It's hard to understand what was lost if one never had it to begin with. Hotaru was born here and presumably never experienced the whole of what it is all these melancholy foxes shipped over an ocean have lost. Presumably her kind are more common away from Komari's seat of power, but... "Oh, don't take me wrong[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. There's nothing wrong with being so-called mediocre — she lives an industrious, content life, and Hotaru is always polite when I come to deliver the materials for her dyes at Kohaku's request. But... I'm the kind of person who prefers to put together her own clothing, for obvious reasons. We just don't have that many chances to have meaningful interaction. I do wonder sometimes what it must be like to be born here and only know of our homeland through hearsay, but that's something I could conceivably ask a lot more people..." ]
rows.translation: [hotaru.anyKids |[rand |哦，那位裁缝？自从她生了孩子之后，我就经常听到关于她的事情。不过，比起如果我还住在另一边的话，听到的次数还是少了一些。鸟居[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]不过，这些年来我已经学会了接受殖民地人们的那些古怪行为。” 或许，对于那个八卦圈里的其他人来说，让他们自己也尝到被别人闲聊的滋味，反而是件好事。你明白，在旧国，未婚生子是被人看不起的吧？ 林多轻轻点了点头：“也不完全是未婚生子[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]社会这一因素有助于我们约束自己的欲望，防止我们对与自己共同生活的人，尤其是那些狸猫，产生过度的掠夺行为。更重要的是……孩子们需要食物，而单靠一位父母往往难以收集到足够的资源来养活所有人。各地的风俗习惯有所不同，但在我所在的那个省份，任何遇到困难的人都会得到他人的帮助。 而人们也期望，反过来，别人不会不必要地占用他人的慷慨与热心。 只是为了这个原因而已。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]你越是长时间穿着这种服装，就会越符合我们的思维方式。” “嗯，谢谢？” “形式与功能是密不可分的，养育孩子也是如此。 |你们与我们越是紧密地合作，就越会逐渐接受我们的思维方式。据我所知，你可能是唯一一个真正尝试过这样做的人。” “嗯，谢谢？不过你们居然觉得自己是第一个这样做的人，真是让我感到很惊讶。” “就像萤的情况一样，关键在于做这件事的动机，而不是动机本身。 ]因此，这严格来说并不属于婚姻关系的问题：例如，与妾室生下孩子并不会被视作可耻的事情。事实上，在某些时期，对于那些有能力承担这种费用的人来说，这种行为甚至还会被鼓励，这与当时的普遍道德观念截然相反。 不过，回到萤的话题上来——她对香织并没有任何意见。 “是的。只要不会惹上麻烦，我想那位裁缝应该也不会遇到什么问题。我们所有人来到这些殖民地，都是出于各自不同的原因。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]。" [hotaru.isMILF |像萤现在这样身材曲线如此优美，毫无疑问，她肯定能轻松找到很多愿意支持她的人。 |尽管萤有些古怪，但在这些事情上，她一直都是非常谨慎的。你应该不会担心她无法同时照顾香织和自己吧？ ]我相信你一定会好好照顾她的。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]她值得这样的待遇。 |我听说那位裁缝的新工具套装，甚至比她本人还要厉害呢。”琳多停顿了一下，观察你的反应，然后急忙摇了摇头：“哦，不[pc.ra kitsune |阁下， ]我并不是那个意思。这并不是什么委婉的说法……嗯，其实并不是。那个但如果美琴说的是对的，那么那个婴儿确实吸收了她母亲的精神力量，并将其进一步凝聚了起来。我们只能希望，这份天赋与带来的苦难并非同一回事。” 你当然也希望能如此。你应该也知道那些古老的传说——那些声称伟大的天赋总会伴随着沉重的负担的传说吧？但传说终究只是传说而已。更何况，你本身就已经足够特别了。[pc.ra kitsune | ——至少足以成为神的使者。如果这还不够让你为孩子们获得免费的恩赐，那还有什么才够呢？ |。 ] 林多听了之后笑了起来。“嗯，”她说。 [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]， ]当我去送萤所需要的染料时，她可是一刻也不愿意错过向大家展示小香织的机会。与她的母亲不同，这个女儿即使在婴儿时期也显得非常安静乖巧。当萤让我抱她的时候，她甚至一点都没有哭闹或不安。 [rindo.anyKids |即使我的儿子表现得很乖，但这件事还是另当别论。 |守规矩是一回事，但角色们确实应该充满活力才对。 ]或许现在下结论还为时过早，但那个孩子似乎生来就带着某种“成熟”的特质。 “美琴说她会照看那个孩子，但我感觉在未来的几年里，香织肯定会把她逼得抓狂……并不是因为她会做出什么调皮捣蛋的事，而是因为她的行为方式[pc.ra kitsune |阁下， ]以及它们将会如何与那些全新的、未经改变的事物有所不同。托里门……我其实也没什么不同，但有些家族血脉是从那些与族长一起迁徙过来的时候就存在了。那位族长有足够的时间来观察这些血脉代代相传过程中所发生的变化。” “这确实很有趣，但萤与这一切又有什么关系呢？” 林多停顿了一下，或许意识到自己正在谈论一些八卦话题，但最终还是决定继续说下去：“当然，你们都知道萤是个有天赋的人[pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |毫无疑问 ]她的亲生母亲也感到有些触动，但并没有萤那么深刻。而现在，她自己的女儿—— “——从一代人到另一代人，这种变化实在是太大了。对于像麻里夫人这样有机会观察这些现象的人来说，一个家族在殖民地生活了多少代，代与代之间的变化就会越明显。一般来说，就是——当然，例外情况总是存在的。 那么，萤的这条台词从一开始就存在了吗？ “或者差不多是从一开始就有的。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]肯定比我的时间要长得多。”林多双手绞在一起，叹了口气，“这简直所以想想看，那些远在大洋彼岸的省份，甚至每个具体的县，都存在着自己独特的当地刻板印象和习俗，这确实挺奇怪的，对吧？比如，琥珀所继承的那种山区血统，就是这样的例子。 与那些人相比，我们的这个群体存在的时间其实很短。坦白说，我们只是一群那些并没有犯下严重罪行，但却不太适应社会的人。而最终，这些人的聚集形成了一种独特的存在——这种存在在香织身上得到了淋漓尽致的体现，她比她的母亲更完美地代表了这一群体的特征。但就在此刻，我能够观察到自己正在经历同样的过程——这个过程造就了那些丰富多彩的地域文化与人们特有的态度。这难道不令人兴奋吗？[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]？" |嗯……”琳多绞着双手，犹豫着说道，“那位裁缝[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]她听到萤的名字就突然变得沉默不语，这是怎么回事呢？” “嗯，前几天美琴让我去取她那里的一些桑树品种，结果因为萤非要展示她的女儿，所以花费的时间比预期的要长了一个小时。 她是因为交货延迟而感到困扰吗？ ]尽管她的天赋比她母亲更强，因此根本不用担心她的“狐火”会失控。但是，两个如此截然不同的性格被迫生活在同一个屋檐下……她或许无意中就会让她的母亲感到恼火不堪。 恕我直言，虽然你也可能有这种感觉，但薰其实只是一个什么都不做的孩子，整天除了吃就是睡而已。[rindo.anyKids |相信我。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]在我儿子像薰这个年纪的时候，他可不只是吃喝玩睡而已 |这就是我想要表达的意思。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]那些会随时间老去的道具，可不仅仅是用来提供食物和让角色小憩的 ]。 它的表现出奇地好，对于这么年幼的生物来说，实在是不寻常。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]…… ]我并不是说未来就已经注定不可改变，也不是说人们不会发生变化。但从小薰身上散发出来的气息，让我感受到了这一点。 [rindo.anyKids |我正是以同样的方式来了解我儿子的性格特点的。 |这让我有些犹豫。 ]更不用说她身上散发出的那种精神气息了。这种气息如此强烈，连你都能感受到，这一点就应该足以证明一切了；萤应该为未来的岁月做好准备了。如果一个孩子能够太就是那个表现最好的。 ] |哦，那位裁缝吗？她……她应该把工作做得很不错吧。关于她，实在没什么太多可说的，而考虑到我们现在的处境，这也算是一件好事吧。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]当每个人都有丰富多彩的过去时，那个成长经历平淡无奇的人反而成了圣人。”林多无奈地笑了笑，“我应该明白这个道理的。” 如果一个人从一开始就从未拥有过某些东西，那就很难理解究竟失去了什么。萤出生在这里，想必她从未经历过那些远渡重洋而来的忧郁狐妖们所失去的一切。大概在麻里的势力范围之外，她这样的家伙应该更为常见吧……不过…… “哦，别误会我的意思。[pc.ra kitsune |，阁下 ]所谓平庸并没有什么不好——她过着勤劳而满足的生活，而且每当我应琥珀的请求去给她送染料材料时，萤总是表现得非常有礼貌。但是……出于一些显而易见的原因，我更喜欢自己动手制作衣服。我们其实并没有太多机会进行有意义的交流。有时候我会想，如果一个人出生在这里，却只能通过道听途说来了解自己的旧国，那会是一种怎样的体验……不过，这个问题我应该可以问更多的人……" ]
rows.raw: " [hotaru.anyKids |[rand |"Oh, the seamstress? I've been hearing more about her, now that she has a child. Not as much as I'd have expected to were I back on the other side of the torii[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ], but I've had many years to accept the eccentricities of the colonies." Perhaps it's for the best that the other half of the den's gossip circle actually take a dose of her own medicine and experience what it's like to be gossiped about. You take it that having a kit out of wedlock is frowned upon in the Old Country? Rindo gives you a small nod. "Not exactly out of wedlock[pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. There is the matter of society, which helps us discipline our appetites and dissuade us from turning outright predatory on those who live with us, especially the tanuki. More importantly... children need to be fed, and it can be hard for one parent to gather sufficient essence for everyone. Customs vary, but in the particular province I came from, anyone facing hardship would receive help from others." And you expect that in turn, people were expected to not unnecessarily impose on others' generosity and civic-mindedness. "Just so[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. The longer you wear this form, the more in line with our thinking you become." Um, thanks? "Form and function are wedded to each other, and so it is the same for child-raising |. The more you enmesh yourselves with us, the more you're coming around to our way of thinking. As far as I know, you may be the only local who has ever tried in earnest." Um, thanks? Although you're seriously surprised at being the first, really. "As with Hotaru's case, it's to do with the reason behind the intent rather than the intent itself ]. Therefore, it is not strictly a matter of wedlock: for example, there is no shame in having a child with a concubine. Indeed, at various times it was even encouraged amongst those who could afford it, in direct opposition to common mores." But back to the point of Hotaru — she's perfectly fine with Kaori. "Yes. So long as there's no trouble, I expect the seamstress will receive none. All of us are in the colonies for our own reasons[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]." [hotaru.isMILF |With how curvaceous Hotaru's become, you don't doubt that she won't have any problems finding enough benefactors |Despite her eccentricities, Hotaru has always been the careful kind when it comes to these things. You're not worried that she won't be able to feed both Kaori and herself ]. And well, you'll chip in when you can. "I don't doubt that you'll take good care of her[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. She deserves it." |"I hear that the seamstress' new kit is even more gifted than she is." Rindo pauses, takes in your expression, then hurriedly shakes her head. "Oh, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]I didn't mean it that way. It's not a euphemism for... well, that. But if Mikoto is right, the infant has taken her mother's spiritual power, and concentrated it even further. We can only hope that the gift and affliction are not one and the same." You'd hope so, too. You're aware of all those old legends that claim that great gifts also come with great burdens, but stories are just that. Besides, you're just that special[pc.ra kitsune | — enough to be a god's champion, at any rate. If that isn't enough for free boons for your children, what is? |. ] Rindo laughs at that. "Well, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], ]Hotaru was only too eager to show off little Kaori when I came to deliver the dyes she needed. Unlike the mother, the daughter is calm even as an infant. Hardly fussed when Hotaru let me hold her — [rindo.anyKids |even if my son is well-behaved, this is something else altogether |well-behaved is one thing, but kits should have energy ]. Perhaps it's too early to pass judgement, but that child was born old. "Mikoto says she'll be keeping an eye on that one, but I get the feeling Kaori will exasperate her thoroughly in the years to come. Not because of any mischief, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]but a complete lack of it — which in its own way is just as infuriating, especially to someone like Mikoto." |"Such a coincidence that you should bring up Hotaru[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. I was speaking with the den matron the other day about the next generation of colonials, [rindo.anyKids |my son included, ]and how they're shaping up to be different from those fresh through the torii gate. I'm not that much different, but some family lines have been here since they sailed over with the den matron, and she's had a long time to observe the gradual changes in the generations." That's interesting, but how does Hotaru come into all of this? Rindo pauses, perhaps realizing that she's treading into gossip territory, then resigns herself to entering the pit she's dug. "Of course, you're aware that Hotaru is gifted, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |no doubt ]. Her own mother was somewhat touched as well, but not as deeply as Hotaru is, and now her own daughter — "— It's just such a great change from one generation to the next. To someone who is in a position to observe these things like Matron Komari is, the more generations a certain family line has been in the colonies, the more pronounced the change between generations. Generally speaking, that is — exceptions exist, as always." And Hotaru's line has been here since the beginning? "Or close to it[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. Certainly longer than I have." Rindo wrings her hands and sighs. "This isn't so strange when you consider how the provinces back across the ocean have their own local stereotypes and customs, right down to individual prefectures. For example, the mountain stock that Kohaku's derived from. "Compared to those, the colonies have only existed for a short time, and to be blunt, we are a collection of those who are not explicitly criminal, but simply do not fit well in society. And eventually, a mixture of things becomes something in its own right, something which little Kaori embodies ever more than her mother. But here and now, I'm able to observe myself the same process which created all the little colorful provincial cultures and attitudes. Isn't it exciting[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]?" |"Mmmmh." Rindo wrings her hands, hesitating. "The seamstress[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]?" Is something the matter, for her to clam up at the sound of Hotaru's name? "Well, Mikoto asked me to pick up several mulberry cultivars from her the other day, and it took an hour longer than it should have because Hotaru insisted on showing off her daughter." And she's bothered by the delay? A laugh. "No, not at all. We don't do things like the mainland, not in the colonies — being a little late with a delivery because you met a friend and had a talk is understandable. I was somewhat troubled by that attitude when I first arrived, but I've gotten used to it as the years have passed. "No, it's about little Kaori. Hotaru let me hold her for a little while, and I got the feeling that she'll be a handful for her mother in the years to come." Hmm, how so? The time you've spent with Kaori has only given you the impression of a rather calm child, disinclined to fuss. "Exactly what I mean. Hotaru isn't just a storyteller, she's a well-known gossip, friends with Kohaku, and overall catalyst for all kinds of trouble. Even if motherhood has imposed some kind of responsibility on her, Hotaru remains who she is at heart despite settling down a little out of necessity. "But the kit? It's strong enough I could feel it while simply holding her in my arms[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. There won't be any concerns about her foxfire getting out of control, despite her gift being stronger than her mother's. But two personalities so disparate having to live under the same roof... she might just drive her mother to exasperation without even intending to." With all respect, while you can feel it too, Kaori's just a little swaddled kit who does little more than eat and sleep. "[rindo.anyKids |Trust me[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ], my son did more than just eat and sleep when he was Kaori's age |That's exactly what I mean[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Kits that age do more than just feed and nap ]. It's... being surprisingly well-behaved, and for one so young. "[pc.ra kitsune |My [pc.mf |lord |lady ]... ]I'm not going to say that the future is set in stone, or that people don't change. But it's what I sense in little Kaori's aura [rindo.anyKids |in much the same way I felt out my son's nature |that gives me pause ], let alone the spiritual scent that hangs around her. The fact that it's intense enough for even you to feel it should be proof enough; Hotaru should prepare herself for the years to come. If it's possible for a child to be too well-behaved, it's that one." ] |"Oh, the seamstress? She... she does her job, I suppose. There really isn't much to say about her, and given where we are that could be considered a good thing[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. When everyone has a colorful past, the one with a mundane upbringing is a saint." Rindo smiles ruefully. "I should know." It's hard to understand what was lost if one never had it to begin with. Hotaru was born here and presumably never experienced the whole of what it is all these melancholy foxes shipped over an ocean have lost. Presumably her kind are more common away from Komari's seat of power, but... "Oh, don't take me wrong[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. There's nothing wrong with being so-called mediocre — she lives an industrious, content life, and Hotaru is always polite when I come to deliver the materials for her dyes at Kohaku's request. But... I'm the kind of person who prefers to put together her own clothing, for obvious reasons. We just don't have that many chances to have meaningful interaction. I do wonder sometimes what it must be like to be born here and only know of our homeland through hearsay, but that's something I could conceivably ask a lot more people..." ] "

rows.original:
"I believe that she is the one who saved my life[pc.ra kitsune
        |, [rindo.married
            |my [pc.mf
                |lord
                |lady
            ]
            |your Eminence
        ]
    ]. Unfortunately, I don't have anything but gratitude with which to repay her."
    
    "That's fine," you reassure her. "Hana knowing that you at least managed to survive with your life and thriving after a fashion would be repayment enough, I think. Someone who would be so motivated to pull you from the flames wouldn't even think twice about needing more than that."
    
    "It's not the future that was originally laid out for me, that I envisioned... but it's more than adequate considering my circumstances, and she gave me that chance. Truth be told, it's better that all these years passed before I had news of her again[pc.ra kitsune
        |, [rindo.married
            |my [pc.mf
                |lord
                |lady
            ]
            |your Eminence
        ]
    ]. If we had met when I first arrived in the colonies, it is likely I would have cursed Hana to her face for forcing me to live against my will. A clean death in the flames would have prevented me from burdening others and solved no small number of problems."
    
    ...
    
    Rindo turns her good eye upon you. "But that is in the past, and with time and age comes a new perspective. I cannot leave the safety of the tree, but please, send her my regards."
rows.translation:
“我相信，正是她救了我的命。[pc.ra kitsune
        |， [rindo.married
            |我的[pc.mf
                |领主
                |女士
            ]
            |阁下
        ]
    ]。不幸的是，我所能给予她的只有感激之情。”
    
    “没关系，”你安慰她，“我想，对于哈娜来说，知道你至少活了下来，并且还在某种程度上过得不错，这就已经是一种足够的回报了。那种会毫不犹豫地把你从火中救出来的人，根本不会考虑是否还需要更多的付出。”
    
    “这虽然不是我原本想象中的未来，但考虑到我的处境，这已经足够了，而她给了我这样的机会。说实话，这些年过去了，我终于再次得到了关于她的消息，这样反而更好。[pc.ra kitsune
        |， [rindo.married
            |我的[pc.mf
                |领主
                |女士
            ]
            |阁下
        ]
    ]。如果我在初到这些殖民地时就遇到了她，恐怕我会当面诅咒哈娜，因为她强迫我违背自己的意愿活着。在火焰中干净利落地死去，反而能让我不再拖累别人，也能解决不少麻烦。”
    
    ……
    
    林多用她那只完好的眼睛看着你：“但那些都已经过去了，随着时间的流逝，人们的观点也会发生变化。我无法离开这棵树的安全环境，但请代我向她问好。”

rows.original: [rindo.isConcubine |[rindo.pregStage 1 2 3 |[rand |"Ah[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]..." Rindo's breath catches in her throat, and she lowers her gaze. "Even though I know it is already too late to have second thoughts on the matter, there is always that thread of doubt as to whether I should have gone this far in trying to protect myself. To have a child for this purpose..." You notice that her hands have unconsciously gone to the slight, barely perceptible swell of her lower belly, and waste no time in taking them in your own and squeezing her fingers comfortingly. The sides of her hands press against the firmness of her bump, and you see her features freeze and lips tremble as the sensation strikes home. As early as she is into her child-bearing, poor Rindo is exceptionally sensitive about her womb, and doubly so on her scarred side. Now, she needs to embrace the healing power of the word %"and." Can she do that? "I don't exactly follow, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]..." It's true that one of the reasons she conceived this child was to help with her troubles, her past that's recently awoken to haunt her once more. But there are also plenty of other reasons for her having chosen to get pregnant, and one of them is that she does in fact feel affection for you and desires to bear your child. And that's not to mention the aching need she had to have her womb filled... There are completely good, whole, and unselfish reasons for her to have embarked on this course of action, and you don't want to hear her have doubts in the least about how right it was for her to do this. This swell in her belly wasn't created because of her selfishness, but because the both of you wanted it to be, and you don't want her to have any self-doubts as to her own motives. Is that clear? Rindo doesn't meet your gaze, and turns her eyes away to the side. Ah... the longer she's walked this path, the more sure she will be that it was the right choice. All she has to do is keep on it, and she'll be seeing through her initial uncertainty soon enough. You lace your fingers with Rindo's, tips pushing lightly into her lightly swollen womb, and feel very satisfied as her muscles shiver with sensitive pleasure. That being said, how's Hitoshi taking to having a high noblewoman under his roof on a regular basis? "We-ll... I'm not too sure[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Hitoshi intimidated, huh? You haven't had much reason to personally interact with the man, but everything you've heard about him would imply the contrary. "Look at it from our point of view, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |[pc.name] ]. A divinity has descended upon our home and is doing the housework while helping your wife care for you infant son. On one hand, you are deeply honored that someone so illustrious would care for your family, and yet on the other hand it feels sacrilegious in a sense. His divine lordship's behavior aside, it is a little awkward because you are not deserving of such, and yet you are receiving it anyway..." You don't know about all this; you'd get tired out just from thinking about Kinu that way. "It is admittedly very draining, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |indeed ], but we would never deny the young lady Ōtomo's help, especially when she does everything so perfectly. For the insignificant price of allowing her to help care for my son, my husband receives a home with a new beauty to its simplicity, and I receive much-needed instruction in how I ought to be a wife and mother..." You can only shake your head at that — surely there's a little irony there in Rindo picking up these things from Kinu, who is neither wife nor mother yet. Not that you don't doubt Kiyoko hasn't schooled your daughter in her expectations in both roles, but even so...! "My son is quiet and never complains, but I am sure he is very glad to receive the young lady Ōtomo's divine care." |"Now that I am a mother, it feels relieving to be able to live my life for others again," Rindo tells you with a smile as she fusses over her son. After I arrived in the colonies, so much of my life turned to me being the focus — while the den matron and everyone else has been exceedingly kind and patient towards my situation, the fact remains that I was extremely needy and even petulant for the first year or so after my arrival, that the situation was reversed and now people were caring for me instead of the other way around. "Since I've come to terms with what happened and moved on with my life, I've tried to give back to the people who so graciously put up with my moodiness and helped me every step of the way — an attitude that would not have existed very much across the ocean. But even so, I've never managed to recapture the feeling of being able to live my life for others, or at least not until I finally found myself wedded off and had a child." Is it that important for her? Does that sensation of indebtedness, not particularly to the people who helped her come this far, but to the cosmos and existence at large, really weigh so heavily on her conscience?[pc.ra kitsune | You search your feelings for a moment, but fail to discover any long-buried compulsions to be rid of any indebtedness to others, or desire for servitude. Is that not enough? Technically, I am head of my household, but I am bound to the den matron... Hitoshi does not say much, but I can tell that he is appreciative of the sound of my voice and that of the house settling as I tend to it. And now that we have a son, there is yet another who needs me, inasmuch as I found myself needing others when I first arrived in this place." Well, if it makes her happy, who are you to complain? Hopefully your worries are unfounded — it's not just Hitoshi out there in the fields, after all. "Ah, but it will be him who is first to the rescue should something indeed happen. But most importantly, though, is that the both of them get to spend time with each other out under the sun. I do not quite understand it myself, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]but I do not need to understand to know that something has transpired for the better, and so I am content. Perceptions on fidelity and the line do not translate perfectly from one to the other, but suffice to say that you do not necessarily imagine that each and every single one of the foxes roaming the woods for benefactors are single and unattached, do you? "We all have needs that are to be sated, and seeking benefactors is one of the oldest ways in which we take care of these needs. There is a proper way in which things are done, and everyone knows what is allowed and not allowed..." Except you, evidently. "[pc.ra kitsune |You have a long time to learn such, your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, and a loving family with which to help you along with the process |The more time you spend with us, the sooner you'll pick up these nuances, [pc.name]. So, long story short, Nakano won't come up hopping mad and demanding to behead you if you decide to play benefactor to her. "The same way I am not to attempt to toast him or come up weeping and wailing for infidelity if he is to sate himself on some pale elf outrider. Like I said, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]there are proper ways for things to be done and we simply do not see things the way even a number of peoples in my homeland do, out of sheer necessity." You're just... well, you'd assumed that it would be that way because everything about kitsune society feels so hidebound. It's a little surprising to discover... [kiyoko.married|well, Kiyoko has never really been bothered by you going around and doing whatever you please despite the both of you being married. Maybe you should've considered that, huh.] "Was there not a similar situation amongst the upper classes of Belharan society[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]? That they would wed for a myriad of reasons but seek romantic dalliances elsewhere, so long as it was kept discreet and no bastards were born of such trysts? What more should it be for us that we do not do this for entertainment, but to sate needs; we are able to keep the platonic and the romantic separate. But do not worry about it; feel free to play benefactor to me any time you desire[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. I now not only have myself to look out for, but a family as well; certainly squeamishness does not befit the head of a household." |"I am still getting used to having mealtimes with many people,[pc.ra kitsune | your Eminence, ]" Rindo says with a little dip of her head. "It is an intensity of emotion all the way from having someone else to prepare the food with to the actual act of eating with everyone, and while I'm sure that time and familiarity will dull some of that sensation the memory of this suddenness will stay with me. People take so much for granted." While you understand that Rindo might have prepared her own meals while living alone, did she not have the opportunity to eat with her own kin before she arrived in the colonies? "Oh, I did not always prepare my own meals — Mikoto and several others were kind enough to occasionally send food over every so often. That, and when I was younger... dining with my family was a rarity. Even my own mother considered it above her station to have me at the same table as her, so blessed and divine I was, destined to join their humble house with that of a great divine clan... but that is all over and in the past, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]scattered like ashes in the wind." Oh, you see. Rindo bobs her head slightly at you. "It is an experience one easily takes for granted, but I am still a newlywed... it is hard to change from thinking of Mikoto as my superior to my in-law. A man of his standing deserves better." The entire family gets together to eat their meals, then? "That is correct[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. We have two meals a day — one in the morning between Mikoto waking up and Miyuki turning in, and another in the evening before the reverse happens. No one is allowed to miss it, although I suppose Hitoshi will no longer turn up in the future when he marries the young lady Ōtomo and joins her household. "But the simple act of being able to sit at a table and have a meal that you did not all cook by yourself — that is a pleasure that one takes for granted until one loses it, or never had that joy to begin with. Such is the case for many of life's small blessings, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]. The den matron understands that, too, which is why she dines with us, although she strictly speaking has no need to eat any more." Mm. A distant expression grows in Rindo's good eye as her smile widens just a fraction. "I had my apprehensions about being married, and they were not all completely unfounded[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. On the other hand, the small, unexpected joys that I have discovered after being wedded ensure that I never feel regret in having made this choice, even if it was arguably under duress. "It is a vastly new experience, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |I'll say ]. Something as simple as having someone to curl up against at night and wake up to in the morning can be amazingly profound. You can't just live life for yourself, and have to get used to living with someone in a way that is intimate in a way that I've never quite experienced before.
