rows.original: You take a deep breath, eye the procession that's now almost upon the shrine, then slip away into the crowd. [pc.ra kitsune |No one obviously pays you any mind, but the kitsune about you always flow such that there's a little circle of space about you in the direction you're heading in, an unconscious thing, maybe. All the better for you — the fewer people that remember you were ever here, the better... |No one says anything or even so much throws you an odd glance to acknowledge your presence, but you nevertheless feel like you stick out like a sore thumb in the midst of the festivities. ] You're not running away, you know that. But this is Rindo's day, and she doesn't need to be reminded of your rejection here and now; she needs to be happy and you're going to let her have what she deserves. Given her determination and realization that she still needs to move further forward despite all that she's achieved already, you don't doubt that the girl herself had a hand in hastening events to this point. With all of the foxes attending the wedding and offering their congratulations from the side of the path, the rest of the sacred gardens, let alone the tree itself, is deserted, and you spend a little time resting your legs on a bench and watching the proceedings from afar and in private. The wedding procession winds its way to the shrine and disappears inside — bride and groom first, followed by Komari and her great-great-granddaughters, and then Kiyoko and Kinu. [kiyoko.married|Your thoughts wander back to the day of your marriage to Kiyoko, and then a small smile crosses your face as the good memories resurface|The way the kitsune get married, according to their traditions... shaking your head, you stifle a sigh]. Yes... it's better this way. This is what Rindo deserves, instead of being caught as your concubine for only the gods know how long. Even with the shadow of her situation looming over her and the circumstances that no doubt led to this wedding, she looked so happy. This is the right choice, and given how much has been taken from the poor girl it's only right that someone else give of themselves for her to have just that bit of happiness... Lost in your thoughts, you're brought back out of your contemplative state by both bride and groom emerging from the shrine to a fresh bout of music and well-wishes from the massed foxes. None of the kitsune crowding about Rindo and her new husband show any contrition over her half-burned state in her traditional foxen wedding garb, and the girl is smiling widely and genuinely as she accepts the congratulations from her fellow kitsune. Slowly, the procession winds its way back down the hill as the bride and groom retreat to further celebrations elsewhere, and the tide of fluffy foxes pulls up in their wake, following them like the tide going out to sea. Eventually, though, you feel a pair of arms wrap themselves about your collarbone, followed by [kiyoko.numKits 8 |ample |small ] breasts pressing against the back of your neck and light breathing on your [pc.hair]. The soft scent of fox fur and floral herb oil washes over you, and you're reminded of the fact that Kiyoko can move very silently when she has the mind to[kiyoko.pregStage 3 |, despite being hugely pregnant ]. "Feeling melancholy, beloved?"[kiyoko.pregStage 3 | Your fox-wife nuzzles the heavy, firm swell of her kit-filled belly into your back, and you feel marginally better for it. ] Melancholy's one way to put it. You're happy for Rindo and all, that she's finally found the courage to act on her desires instead of stewing in inaction; you know that this is best for her. But you just need to get over the lingering emotions that're getting in the way of rational knowledge, that's all. "I fully believe that you did the right thing, beloved; the girl looked genuinely happy. [kinu.isInari |She had been pining for years over Komari's overzealous great-great-grandson, hoping that he'd somehow notice her. Not daring to take a step forward, and yet not able to retreat, either... and after she was jolted into action, it was surprisingly easy |She had been pining for years over Komari's overzealous great-great-grandson, hoping that he'd somehow notice her. Not daring to take a step forward, and yet not able to retreat, either... and then came along our sweet, sweet daughter and scooped him up. Sometimes, it takes a little pain to get one moving... but when she did take action, at least she did it swiftly ]." Her arms tighten about you a little, her slight body leaning into you a little more, sharing her warmth with you. "So many of our fears that paralyze us from meaningful action are completely made up in our own minds; there's a lesson to be learned there." You know, you know. Sighing, you stand from the bench and give Kiyoko a little kiss on the lips, then sigh as you draw away. Is everyone gone? "In a small den like this, a marriage is everyone's business, so yes. That, and people love an excuse to lay down their work and have a bit of fun. It'll be some hours yet before the festivities die down... but on the other hand, someone needs attending to, don't they?" You'll be fine, but... you just need a little time [party.has kiyoko |with her. Just the two of you, as it were. You'd feel guilty taking her from her official place, though... |alone. She has other business to attend to, doesn't she? Being an important personage and all... you just need a little while to yourself before you're on the road again. ] "The ceremonies which strictly necessitate my presence are already done with, beloved. As for the rest... our firstborn will suffice in my place. Responsibility or not, I want to tend to you, and no one will question me for doing it. Am I not such a selfish creature?" Ah, she may be, but you love her for it. "Just a while, then?" Just a while, and then the both of you have to be on your way. Look, dusk is already upon you, and before someone notices that she's missing... A soft kiss. "Just a while, then."
rows.translation: 你深吸一口气，注视着那支队伍——他们已经快要到达神龛了——然后悄悄地混入了人群之中。 [pc.ra kitsune |显然，没有人会在意你，但围绕在你身边的那些狐狸们总会形成一种无形的气场，在你前进的方向上形成一个小范围的空间。或许这是一种无意识的反应吧。不过这对你来说反而是件好事——记住你曾经在这里的人越少，就越好…… |没有人说些什么，甚至也没有人向你投来异样的目光来确认你的存在，但你依然觉得，在这欢乐的场合中，自己就像是个碍事的人一样，显得格格不入。 ] 你知道，你并不是在逃避什么。但今天是林多的生日，她现在不需要再被提醒你曾经拒绝了她；她需要的是快乐，而你也会让她得到应得的东西。考虑到她的决心，以及她意识到尽管已经取得了很多成就，自己仍然需要继续前进，你肯定不会怀疑，这个女孩本身也在一定程度上加速了事情的发展，使事情发展到了今天这一步。 你正沉浸在思绪之中，突然，新郎和新娘从神龛中走出来，新鲜的音乐声响起，周围聚集的狐妖们也纷纷送上祝福，将你从沉思中拉了回来。那些围在凛朵和她新婚丈夫周围的狐妖们，没有一个因为她穿着传统的狐妖婚服而被烧伤而表现出丝毫歉意；而这个女孩在接受同伴们的祝贺时，脸上也洋溢着真诚而快乐的笑容。渐渐地，队伍开始沿着山坡向下返回，新郎和新娘则前往其他地方继续庆祝。那些毛茸茸的狐妖们也跟随着他们，就像退潮时的海水一样，一路追随他们的足迹。 rows.raw: " You take a deep breath, eye the procession that's now almost upon the shrine, then slip away into the crowd. [pc.ra kitsune |No one obviously pays you any mind, but the kitsune about you always flow such that there's a little circle of space about you in the direction you're heading in, an unconscious thing, maybe. All the better for you — the fewer people that remember you were ever here, the better... |No one says anything or even so much throws you an odd glance to acknowledge your presence, but you nevertheless feel like you stick out like a sore thumb in the midst of the festivities. ] You're not running away, you know that. But this is Rindo's day, and she doesn't need to be reminded of your rejection here and now; she needs to be happy and you're going to let her have what she deserves. Given her determination and realization that she still needs to move further forward despite all that she's achieved already, you don't doubt that the girl herself had a hand in hastening events to this point. With all of the foxes attending the wedding and offering their congratulations from the side of the path, the rest of the sacred gardens, let alone the tree itself, is deserted, and you spend a little time resting your legs on a bench and watching the proceedings from afar and in private. The wedding procession winds its way to the shrine and disappears inside — bride and groom first, followed by Komari and her great-great-granddaughters, and then Kiyoko and Kinu. [kiyoko.married|Your thoughts wander back to the day of your marriage to Kiyoko, and then a small smile crosses your face as the good memories resurface|The way the kitsune get married, according to their traditions... shaking your head, you stifle a sigh]. Yes... it's better this way. This is what Rindo deserves, instead of being caught as your concubine for only the gods know how long. Even with the shadow of her situation looming over her and the circumstances that no doubt led to this wedding, she looked so happy. This is the right choice, and given how much has been taken from the poor girl it's only right that someone else give of themselves for her to have just that bit of happiness... Lost in your thoughts, you're brought back out of your contemplative state by both bride and groom emerging from the shrine to a fresh bout of music and well-wishes from the massed foxes. None of the kitsune crowding about Rindo and her new husband show any contrition over her half-burned state in her traditional foxen wedding garb, and the girl is smiling widely and genuinely as she accepts the congratulations from her fellow kitsune. Slowly, the procession winds its way back down the hill as the bride and groom retreat to further celebrations elsewhere, and the tide of fluffy foxes pulls up in their wake, following them like the tide going out to sea. Eventually, though, you feel a pair of arms wrap themselves about your collarbone, followed by [kiyoko.numKits 8 |ample |small ] breasts pressing against the back of your neck and light breathing on your [pc.hair]. The soft scent of fox fur and floral herb oil washes over you, and you're reminded of the fact that Kiyoko can move very silently when she has the mind to[kiyoko.pregStage 3 |, despite being hugely pregnant ]. "Feeling melancholy, beloved?"[kiyoko.pregStage 3 | Your fox-wife nuzzles the heavy, firm swell of her kit-filled belly into your back, and you feel marginally better for it. ] Melancholy's one way to put it. You're happy for Rindo and all, that she's finally found the courage to act on her desires instead of stewing in inaction; you know that this is best for her. But you just need to get over the lingering emotions that're getting in the way of rational knowledge, that's all. "I fully believe that you did the right thing, beloved; the girl looked genuinely happy. [kinu.isInari |She had been pining for years over Komari's overzealous great-great-grandson, hoping that he'd somehow notice her. Not daring to take a step forward, and yet not able to retreat, either... and after she was jolted into action, it was surprisingly easy |She had been pining for years over Komari's overzealous great-great-grandson, hoping that he'd somehow notice her. Not daring to take a step forward, and yet not able to retreat, either... and then came along our sweet, sweet daughter and scooped him up. Sometimes, it takes a little pain to get one moving... but when she did take action, at least she did it swiftly ]." Her arms tighten about you a little, her slight body leaning into you a little more, sharing her warmth with you. "So many of our fears that paralyze us from meaningful action are completely made up in our own minds; there's a lesson to be learned there." You know, you know. Sighing, you stand from the bench and give Kiyoko a little kiss on the lips, then sigh as you draw away. Is everyone gone? "In a small den like this, a marriage is everyone's business, so yes. That, and people love an excuse to lay down their work and have a bit of fun. It'll be some hours yet before the festivities die down... but on the other hand, someone needs attending to, don't they?" You'll be fine, but... you just need a little time [party.has kiyoko |with her. Just the two of you, as it were. You'd feel guilty taking her from her official place, though... |alone. She has other business to attend to, doesn't she? Being an important personage and all... you just need a little while to yourself before you're on the road again. ] "The ceremonies which strictly necessitate my presence are already done with, beloved. As for the rest... our firstborn will suffice in my place. Responsibility or not, I want to tend to you, and no one will question me for doing it. Am I not such a selfish creature?" Ah, she may be, but you love her for it. "Just a while, then?" Just a while, and then the both of you have to be on your way. Look, dusk is already upon you, and before someone notices that she's missing... A soft kiss. "Just a while, then." "

rows.original: Yes. Rindo realized that one can't keep on running away from the reality of the situation, and the least you can do is learn from her example. As you watch the procession come up the hill, you square your shoulders and steel your jaw. Miko shades the couple with a large umbrella as they accept well-wishes from just about the entire population of the den, and bit by bit, step by step, they come up to you... "[pc.ra kitsune |Your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ]," Rindo says as she stands before you, hand in hand with [kinu.isInari |Nakano |Hitoshi ]. You have to give it to Miko and Mai — the entire burnt half of her body doesn't merely not detract from, but in a strange way, accentuates the soft white of her wedding garb and its ceremonial hood. Maybe there's something to the whole 'imperfections make someone or something all that more beautiful' school of thought that these foxes have, given that Rindo herself is personifying it at the moment... There are so many more things that you could say to the both of them here and now — that you're sorry for having pushed things to a head like this, that you know that this is the best course of action for her, that she'll be happier tied to someone who isn't absent all the time, that she deserves this instead of a mere concubinage. But all of these words would not just be ashes on your tongue, they would completely spoil the mood of the event and be awkward and creepy to boot. This day isn't about you, it's about her. Of course. Your congratulations to the both of them, and you hope that they're happy together. [kinu.isInari |All it really took was for both Nakano and Rindo to finally learn that they cared for each other all this while; you can only hope that the rest of their lives is smooth sailing now that they know. |As Komari said, what Rindo needs in her life is reliability and stability, and you couldn't think of a better person suited to give those to her. ] There's a bit of silence, as if they were expecting more, but none's forthcoming as you don't want to put your foot in your mouth. Rindo looks to her husband-to-be, and then the both of them give you a small nod; the both of them tighten their fingers about each other and then continue down the path to the shrine, Miko bringing up their rear with the umbrella as they accept the well-wishes of those further ahead. Something tightens in your chest as you watch the procession move away from you, but it passes in the blink of an eye. A passing fit of melancholy, little more... The wedding procession winds its way to the shrine and disappears inside — bride and groom first, followed by Komari and her great-great-granddaughters, and then Kiyoko and Kinu. [kiyoko.married |Your thoughts wander back to the day of your marriage to Kiyoko, and then a small smile crosses your face as the good memories resurface |The way the kitsune get married, according to their traditions... shaking your head, you stifle a sigh ]. Yes... it's better this way. This is what Rindo deserves, instead of being caught as your concubine for only the gods know how long. Even with the shadow of her situation looming over her and the circumstances that no doubt led to this wedding, she looked so happy. This is the right choice, and given how much has been taken from the poor girl it's only right that someone else give of themselves for her to have just that bit of happiness... With the passing of the bride and groom, the sea of fox ears and fluffy tails about you thins somewhat, and you're about to leave when both bride and groom emerge from the shrine to a fresh bout of music and well-wishes from the massed foxes. Slowly, the procession passes by you once more and winds its way back down the hill as the bride and groom retreat to further celebrations elsewhere, and the tide of fluffy foxes pulls up in their wake, following them like the tide going out to sea. No one actually forbids you from following and joining in the remainder of the revelry — [pc.ra kitsune |if anything, you know that it'd be expected of someone in your position as a social obligation |and you know that the foxes wouldn't mind in the least ] — but your feet suddenly feel leaden, and your heart heavy up to the point when you feel a pair of arms wrap themselves about your collarbone, followed by [kiyoko.numKits 8 |ample |small ] breasts pressing against the back of your neck and light breathing on your [pc.hair]. The soft scent of fox fur and floral herb oil washes over you, and you're reminded of the fact that Kiyoko can move very silently when she has the mind to[kiyoko.pregStage 3 |, despite being hugely pregnant ]. "Feeling melancholy, beloved?"[kiyoko.pregStage 3 | Your fox-wife nuzzles the heavy, firm swell of her kit-filled belly into your back, and you feel marginally better for it. ] Melancholy's one way to put it. You're happy for Rindo and all — that she's finally found the courage to act on her desires instead of stewing in inaction — you know that this is best for her. But you just need to get over the lingering emotions that're getting in the way of rational knowledge, that's all. Turning, you give Kiyoko a slight kiss on the lips, then pull away with a sigh. "Shall we walk a little?" You look at the last of the fluffy tide departing from the gardens. Doesn't she have to be in attendance at the remainder of the wedding celebrations? "Our firstborn daughter will deal with that, beloved; it'll be a good learning experience for her and a simple practical exercise in preparation for her future duties as my heir. A wedding's as easy as it comes. No, I'm perfectly within my privileges to want to deal with you first. Am I not such a selfish creature?" Sighing, you stand from the bench and give Kiyoko a little kiss on the lips, then sigh as you draw away. Is everyone gone? "In a small den like this, a marriage is everyone's business, so yes. That, and people love an excuse to lay down their work and have a bit of fun. It'll be some hours yet before the festivities die down... but on the other hand, someone needs attending to, don't they?" You'll be fine, but... you just need a little time [party.has kiyoko |with her. Just the two of you, as it were. You'd feel guilty taking her from her official place, though... |alone. She has other business to attend to, doesn't she? Being an important personage and all... you just need a little while to yourself before you're on the road again. ] "Mm, don't you try to push me away, beloved. I fully believe that you did the right thing, beloved; the girl looked genuinely happy. [kinu.isInari |She had been pining for years over Komari's overzealous great-great-grandson, hoping that he'd somehow notice her. Not daring to take a step forward, and yet not able to retreat, either... and after she was jolted into action, it was surprisingly easy |She had been pining for years over Komari's overzealous great-great-grandson, hoping that he'd somehow notice her. Not daring to take a step forward, and yet not able to retreat, either... and then came along our sweet, sweet daughter and scooped him up. Sometimes, it takes a little pain to get one moving... but when she did take action, at least she did it swiftly ]." Her arms tighten about you a little, her slight body leaning into you a little more, sharing her warmth with you. "So many of our fears that paralyze us from meaningful action are completely made up in our own minds; there's a lesson to be learned there." There is. "I'm glad that you found the courage to wish her well. The fact that the marriage had other purposes attached to it doesn't detract from the fact that it should be the happiest day of her life." She's right, and you know it. [kinu.isInari |Rindo's had a crush on Nakano for years now, and it's not all the time that this kind of situation works out as well as it did |Rindo might have had a crush on Nakano for years until your daughter scooped him up, but for her not everyone gets to emerge from that kind of situation with a better outlook on the future than she did ]. But for now... you'd like to have a moment to let the melancholia pass. "Just a while, then?" Just a while, and then the both of you have to be on your way. Look, dusk is already upon you, and before someone notices that she's missing... A soft kiss. "Just a while, then. I don't want you moping too long, beloved, it's not good for you." Ah, you won't...

[dayNight|Miko|Mai] is good to her word; you're not exactly sure what she does, but there's a distinct surge of power in the air as the [dayNight|orange|gray]-furred shrine maiden touches one of the gate's posts and a shimmering portal of light appears in the empty air beneath the arch. "Safe travels, [pc.ra kitsune|yer Eminence," [dayNight|Miko|Mai] says as you pass by her and through the gate, bowing deeply|ya hear?" [dayNight|Miko|Mai] says as you pass by her and through the gate, bowing]. "Y'all come back here anytime — don't be a stranger, now!" [dayNight|Miko|Mai]'s words ring in your ears as the light envelopes you, and once more you find yourself in the Ways Between, familiar yet alien at the same time. "

rows.original: As you take a leisurely stroll through the rice fields, the cloudless, root-ridden sky above you helps calm your mind. Pondering whether you should make a habit of this, you lose track of your steps, venturing deeper and deeper into the cultivated land. Realizing that you've strayed a little too far from the path, you look around and notice that you ended up in a fallow section of the paddies. It doesn’t take you long to discover what's off: there are pieces of minced straw and scraps of metal all around you. A battlefield? Probably not. A training ground? Perhaps. There’s a single training dummy left standing amidst the chaos, donning a sturdy plate and a wide hat. As you approach to check it out, a booming clash of metal breaks the silence. The dummy’s armor, stripped away by a perfectly placed arrow, crashes to the ground. Startled by the sound, you step backwards and instinctively ready your [pc.weapon]. The wind whistles in your ears, followed by the blur of a wheel of silken fox tails. The sound of slicing and dicing replaces the whistle as you realize that something is hacking at the defenseless training dummy, overwhelming it. Every slash chips away at its material, relentless as wildfire but precise as a surgeon. The attacker crouches near the dummy, swinging the blade so fast that it appears to be immobile in its scabbard. With a final slash and the blade now unsheathed, the warrior appears behind the dummy as its head is hacked clean off its body, rolling to the ground until it hits your foot. You focus your gaze on the unfortunate target, or what little remains of it — nothing more than a pile of minced straw. The warrior vixen slowly stands up, back turned towards you. "You can imagine my surprise when I was told that not only was the den attacked... but also that the intruder [pc.isKitsune |has been appointed Champion of Keros. Can't blame my sister Azami if she let you through... |[var0 |had bested my little sister, Azami, in combat... |bested almost everyone in combat. My sister, Azami, has lost out on a pretty good fight, because ] ] I can feel it in my blood; you're interesting!" As the kitsune turns around, unsheathing a second, shorter blade, you immediately note the strip of black cloth covering her right eye. Her left gleams with confidence as she assumes her fighting stance, oozing fearlessness and impatience. The grin on her face is a telltale sign of her excitement, but there's no malice or ill-intent in her demeanor; it's like she genuinely wants to face you in battle just for fun. Who is this wild-looking kitsune? As you ready your weapon for this new fight, the feisty fox's single eye widens in shock as realization dawns. "Dammit, that's right..." she mutters to herself, sheathing both of her weapons as her fierce expression shifts to one of resignation. Wow, that was... sudden. Is everything all right? What was that all about? "Urgh, I'm sure Governor Komari would shave my tails from tip to base if I did something like this to [pc.isKitsune |Keros' champion... and she would have every reason in this world to do so. My name's Sayumi Ishida, taskmaster of the wildlings. I've heard that you fought your way into this place and obtained Lord Keros' favor... I'm very impressed, I do like a new face! Tell me: can we skip the formalities in private, your Eminence?" |our honored guest... and she would have every reason in this world to do so. My name's Sayumi Ishida, taskmaster of the wildlings. So, you fought your way in here, huh?" ] Sayumi scratches her head as she recognizes the fact that she almost challenged you to a fight, then breaks into a sheepish, perhaps even apologetic smile. Well, that much makes sense; you're pretty sure it isn't customary for the kitsune to cross blades as a greeting. You nod, [pc.isKitsune |allowing her to drop the honorific |confirming that your first meeting with the den hasn't exactly been peaceful ]. Perhaps you can walk back to the den together? It would be the perfect opportunity to properly introduce yourselves.
rows.translation: 你悠闲地漫步在稻田之间，头顶万里无云、盘根错节的天空让你的心绪平静下来。你琢磨着是否该把这件事变成习惯，不知不觉便忘了数着脚步，越走越深入这片耕作之地。意识到自己偏离小径太远，你环顾四周，发现自己走进了一片休耕的水田。没过多久你就察觉到哪里不对劲：四周散落着切碎的稻草和金属碎片。战场？大概不是。训练场？也许吧。 一片狼藉之中只剩下一个还立着的训练假人，身上披着结实的板甲，戴着一顶宽檐帽。你走上前想查看究竟，一声轰然的金属撞击打破了寂静。假人身上的护甲被一箭精准地射落，哐当砸在地上。你被这声响惊得后退一步，本能地握紧了[pc.weapon]。 风在耳边尖啸，随之而来的是一团丝缎般狐尾旋成的残影。 呼啸声被切割劈砍的声响取代，你这才意识到有什么东西正在猛砍那个毫无防备的训练假人，将其彻底压制。每一刀都在削去它的材质，如野火般猛烈，又如外科医生般精准。 袭击者蹲伏在假人身旁，挥刀快得仿佛刀刃始终静卧在刀鞘里。最后一记劈砍，刀锋出鞘，那名战士现身于假人身后，假人的头颅被干脆地砍离身体，滚落在地，一直滚到你脚边。你凝神看向这个倒霉的靶子，或者说它残存的那点东西——不过是一堆切碎的稻草。 那位女战士缓缓站起身，背对着你。 “你能想象我听说巢穴不仅遭到袭击……而且那名闯入者[pc.isKitsune |还被任命为凯罗斯的冠军时，有多惊讶了吧。要是我妹妹阿兹米放你进来，那也怪不得她……” |[var0 |在战斗中胜过了我的小妹阿兹米…… |在战斗中胜过了几乎所有人。我妹妹阿兹米因此错过了一场相当精彩的较量，因为 ] ]我的血液能感觉到；你很有意思！“ 狐妖转过身来，同时抽出第二把较短的刀，你立刻注意到她右眼上蒙着一条黑布。她左眼闪着自信的光，摆出战斗架势，浑身散发着无所畏惧与迫不及待的气息。她脸上的笑容明白无误地昭示着她的兴奋，但神态中并无恶意或歹念；她似乎真的只是觉得和你交手好玩。这只模样野性的狐妖究竟是谁？ 你举起武器准备迎接这场新的战斗，这只火辣的狐狸独眼却骤然瞪大，仿佛忽然想起了什么。 ”该死，差点忘了……“她自言自语地嘟囔着，把两把武器收回鞘中，凶悍的神情转为无奈。 哇，这……也太突然了。你没事吧？刚才那是怎么回事？ ”呃，要是我对[pc.isKitsune |凯罗斯的冠军做出这种事……那麻里总督肯定会把我的尾巴从尖到尾全剃光，而且她完全有理由这么做。我叫石田沙由美，野狐众的教头。听说你是一路打进来的，还得到了凯罗斯大人的青睐……我很佩服，我确实喜欢新面孔！告诉我：咱们能不能私下免了这些客套，大人？“ |我们这位贵客做出这种事……那麻里总督肯定会把我的尾巴从尖到尾全剃光，而且她完全有理由这么做。我叫石田沙由美，野狐众的教头。这么说，你是一路打进来的，嗯？” ] 沙由美意识到自己差点就向你发起挑战，挠了挠头，随即露出一个局促、甚至有些歉意的笑容。嗯，这倒也说得通；你相当确定，狐妖并不时兴用刀剑相交来打招呼。 你点点头，[pc.isKitsune |允许她省去敬称 |承认你与这座巢穴的初次见面并不算和平 ]。也许你们可以一起走回巢穴？那正是正式互相介绍的好机会。

rows.original:
"I guess I must apologize for my sudden challenge, [pc.isKitsune
        |[pc.mf
            |Lord
            |Lady
        ]ship
        |[pc.name]
    ]..." she admits with a laugh. " I do have a tendency to act first, ask questions second..." 
    
    As you walk together, Sayumi scratches her cheek with her index finger and smiles, trying her best to face the awkwardness of the situation. You assure her that no offense has been taken, you were just startled by how fast everything happened.
    
    She breathes a sigh of relief. "Thank Keros," she begins, "But still, apologizing isn't enough for me. If there's anything you want to know, I'm ready to answer." 
    
    Actually, you do have a few questions. Was the place you ended up in her training ground?
    
    "Exactly. It's a rather abandoned patch of land that my sister and I use to practice the techniques we're less familiar with. As you can imagine, having an audience when you're more prone to fall on your ass is not ideal."
    
    She chuckles, brushing her hair to the sides of her forehead. She and her sister, huh? She did mention that Azami, the concierge, was her sister; can she tell you more?
    
    "The one and only," she smiles, placing her left hand on the handle of her longer sword. "I'm the eldest, even if our personalities might suggest otherwise. I serve directly under her as the field overseer for the wildlings. Despite this, we aren't much different from most siblings when we're off duty. While she is the strict, no-nonsense type, I prefer to keep things relaxed and direct, even if some people say I deviate too much from established protocols."
    
    You give her a quizzical look.
    
    "But what can I do?" she chuckles. "I like to take things spontaneously and I have a knack for improvisation."
    
    With how straightforward she's showing herself to be, those statements aren't entirely unfounded. You don't dislike it, though, as it's an opportunity to get a more direct perspective on kitsune customs. 
    
    Continuing your conversation, you ask why you’re only meeting her now — she wasn't present during your... [pc.isDK
        |conquest of
        |loud approach with
    ] the den.
    
    "Oh, believe me; had I been here, I would have been your first opponent," Sayumi smiles, turning to face you. "To answer your question, yes. My duties keep me in the forest for long periods of time. I might have missed out on the fun, but one of the scouts was stranded after a skirmish with those red, winged pests. We are wildlings, we do not leave any of our own behind."
    
    Sayumi nods and, for the first time, you see a stern glimmer in her emerald green eye.
    
    "But what about you?" she asks, her laidback behavior restored. "How did you end up here knocking at our door?"
    
    As you are about to tell her about Evergreen, the wild vixen widens her good eye again.
    
    "Keros' tails, I need to cut our meeting short. My break ended some time ago and I lost track of time. I'm sorry, [pc.isKitsune
        |[pc.mf
            |Lord
            |Lady
        ]ship
        |[pc.name]
    ]! You can come to my private rooms later! I'm sure we have a lot to share!"
    
    You watch Sayumi run off into the fields just as swiftly as she arrived. You'll do your best to find her quarters. They must be on the top floor, where all the other apartments are.
rows.translation:
我猜我得为刚才突然向你挑战道个歉，[pc.isKitsune
        |[pc.mf
            |大人
            |女士
        ]您
        |[pc.name]
    ]……“她笑着承认。”我这人一向是先动手、后问话……“ 
    
    你们并肩同行，沙由美用食指挠了挠脸颊，微笑着，尽力面对这份尴尬。你向她保证自己并没有动怒，只是被事情发展得这么快吓到了。
    
    她松了口气。”感谢凯罗斯，“她开口道，”不过光是道歉对我不够。你要是有什么想知道的，我随时愿意回答。“ 
    
    其实你确实有几个问题。你刚才闯进的地方，是她的训练场吗？
    
    ”没错。那是一片挺荒废的地，我和妹妹用来练习我们不太熟悉的技术。你可以想象，在你自己更容易摔个屁股蹲的时候，有观众在旁边可不太理想。“
    
    她轻笑着，把头发拨到额头两侧。她和她妹妹啊？她确实提过，那位负责接待的阿兹米是她妹妹；能不能请她多讲一些？
    
    ”独一无二的那一个，“她微笑着，左手按在较长的武士刀刀柄上。”我是长女，尽管我俩的性子可能让人以为是反过来的。我直接听命于她，担任野狐众的战地督导。话虽如此，下了差我们和大多数姐妹没什么两样。她是那种严厉、不讲情面的类型，而我更喜欢轻松直接的处事方式，哪怕有人说我太不守既定规矩。“
    
    你疑惑地看了她一眼。
    
    ”可我又能怎么办呢？“她轻笑道。”我喜欢随性行事，而且我天生擅长临场发挥。“
    
    看她表现得如此直率，这些话倒也不是全无根据。不过你并不讨厌这样，因为这正好是个更直接地了解狐妖习俗的机会。 
    
    你继续着谈话，问她为什么直到现在才见到她——你[pc.isDK
        |征服
        |大张旗鼓地闯入
    ]这座巢穴的时候，她并不在场。
    
    ”哦，相信我；要是我当时在这儿，我会是你第一个对手，“沙由美笑着转过身面对你。”回答你的问题：是的。我的职责让我长时间待在森林里。我可能错过了不少乐子，但有一名斥候在和那些红色带翅膀的害虫交手后被困住了。我们是野狐众，绝不丢下任何一个自己人。“
    
    沙由美点点头，你第一次在她翠绿色的眼睛里看到一丝严厉的光。
    
    ”那你呢？“她问道，懒散随意的态度又回来了。”你是怎么跑到这儿来敲我们大门的？“
    
    你正要跟她讲起常青的事，这只野性十足的母狐狸仅剩的那只眼睛又瞪大了。
    
    ”凯罗斯的尾巴啊，我得把咱们的会面提前结束了。我的休息时间早就过了，我给忘了。抱歉，[pc.isKitsune
        |[pc.mf
            |大人
            |女士
        ]您
        |[pc.name]
    ]！你回头可以来我的私人房间！我相信我们有很多可聊的！“
    
    你看着沙由美像来时一样迅捷地奔回田野。你得尽力找到她的住处。那一定在顶层，所有其他公寓都在那儿。

My duties keep me in the forest for long periods of time. I might have missed out on the fun, but one of the scouts was stranded after a skirmish with those red, winged pests. We are wildlings, we do not leave any of our own behind."

rows.original: You're interested in knowing more about this wild, carefree kitsune. Despite her appearance, it's clear that she's garnered a good amount of respect in the den if, as the taskmaster of the wildlings, she serves as Azami's field overseer. Judging by your first encounter, she's an expert swordswoman. What else can she do? She lets out a small laugh, crossing her arms under her bosom. "There's nothing I love more than a good sword fight, but archery is pretty high up there as well. People say many things about me, but I consider myself to be much less of a showoff than what you might have heard. Let's see, what else can I say about myself? I'm a simple woman: I like to cross blades with people capable of giving me a challenge and to explore the wilderness. Oh! I guess there is something most people don't know." Sayumi grabs a pouch hanging from her waist, opens it up, and hands you a wooden statue of a fox. You take it into your hands and carefully study it. It's actually a very nicely done carving. The design is not new to your eyes, you're pretty sure you've seen similar ones around the den, but the level of detail is exquisite. "Carving wood is one of my favorite pastimes. It's such a good way to let your mind wander while your hands do the rest. Takes some time to improve on it, but once you do it's one of the best feelings in the world. Seeing someone's face brighten like yours makes me very happy." It is a beautiful little figurine. Smiling, you return it to Sayumi before asking if there's more to her exploits. Surely a woman like her has many other songs to sing. "You mean apart from all the times I've snuck outside the forest for the thrill of adventure? Heh, I could start and go on for hours. Some say I've done it too much, but the freedom to make my own mistakes is all I've ever wanted." Surely there must be something she wished it didn't happen. "There are some things I wish I realized sooner..." she admits, appearing lost in thought for the slightest moment. "Maybe one day I'll tell you those tales, but for now, let me tell you that I've only ever known one way to live and act: my way." she concludes with a cheeky smile. You pause for a second, then you nod and smile, surprised. You'll be ready to hear those tales, when the time comes. "I'm much better at living cool stories rather than telling them, but I'll do my best," she chuckles, gently scratching the side of her neck. What about her childhood? Has she always been such a free spirit? "Ever since I was a kit! If I had a pebble for every time Governor Komari scolded me, gave me a detention or chewed me out, I'd have enough to pave a path from here all the way to Keros' shrine." Wow... [pc.isCunning |and what about paving the way back? She needs to up her game if she wants to give Komari a run for her money |that's a lot of pebbles ]. "There was that time when I glued old Jūshirō's katana in its scabbard, I think I was eight at the time. Poor guy spent over ten minutes trying to force it out until the handguard came flying! You should have seen his face!" She bursts out laughing. "Governor Komari banned me from training with a sword for a week after that. Let me tell you, there's nothing worse than being forced to watch something you absolutely love doing without being able to do it." Tough, but just. "And it wouldn't be the last time, either!" Sayumi laughs. "There was this other time when I categorically refused to try yakisoba. I was a willful kit, to say the very least... I didn't even know how it tasted, but I hated it nonetheless. One day, Governor Komari just looked at me, mouthed 'Okay', and then took the dish away. When dinnertime came, she gave me yakisoba again and told me that I wasn't going to have anything else until I gave it a taste. After a long night of waiting, I finally cracked and took a bite. The funniest part? Yakisoba is one of my favorite foods to this day." You laugh, finding the whole thing to be pretty amusing, but also very effective at schooling stubborn children. "From that moment on, I've always given everything a chance, no matter how bad the first impression was. I will never forget how good yakisoba tasted that day, and I'm not losing out on an opportunity to enjoy something just as much." You agree, adding that Komari must have been like a second mother for her. "In a way, yes. She could be as scary as any mother, like that time when I broke a tea kettle back when I was eleven. Keros forbid, it felt like a punch to the gut when she said: 'I’m not mad, I’m just disappointed.'." You know the stories of how frightening the Imperial Governor can be[flags.KOMARI_FUCKED |, and seeing her naked possibly made her even more frightening, but the only thing you tell is that she sure knows how to keep people in line ]. "No doubt about that... I feel the chills to this day, but thanks to that incident, I learned about the beauty of kintsugi." Kintsugi? [pc.bg scholar |You recall seeing an illustrated manuscript from your academic studies. It involves highlighting and revealing damage, rather than concealing it, right? She nods. ] "It's a Kitsuhon art where broken pottery is repaired through the use of a special golden lacquer," Sayumi answers. "The process highlights the shattering, almost as if the ceramic is wearing its hardships like a badge of honor. If a metal is shining and untarnished, it means that it has never been truly tested. It might sound over the top, but it's what I believe." You smile, understanding where she's coming from. Some people prefer to throw away and replace instead of repairing, and Sayumi's a supporter of the latter.
rows.translation: 你想更多地了解这只野性又无忧无虑的狐妖。尽管她外表如此，但她在巢穴里显然颇受敬重——毕竟身为野狐众的教头，她还担任阿兹米的战地督导。从你们的初次相遇来看，她是个用刀的高手。她还有别的本事吗？ 她轻笑一声，双臂交叉抱在胸下。 “我最爱的就是痛痛快快比一场剑，不过射箭也排得挺靠前。关于我的说法有很多，可我觉得自己远没有你听说的那么爱显摆。让我想想，还能说自己点什么？我是个简单的女人：喜欢和能给我带来挑战的人刀剑相交，喜欢去荒野里闯荡。哦！我想起一件大多数人不知道的事。” 沙由美从腰间摘下一只小袋，打开，递给你一尊木雕的狐狸像。你接过来仔细端详。这其实雕得相当漂亮。这个造型对你来说并不新鲜，你相当确定在巢穴里见过类似的，但这尊的细节精致得令人惊叹。 “雕木头是我最喜欢的消遣之一。让脑子随意游荡、双手去做剩下的事，这法子再好不过了。想进步得花些时间，可一旦练成，那是世上最棒的感觉之一。看到别人的脸像你这样亮起来，我特别开心。” 这确实是一尊美丽的小雕像。你微笑着把它还给沙由美，然后问她是否还有别的壮举。像她这样的女人，肯定还有许多别的歌可以唱。 “你是说除了那些为了追求冒险刺激而溜出森林的经历？嘿，我要是讲起来能讲上好几个钟头。有人说我做得太过火了，可我想要的一直就是犯错也能由我自己做主的自由。” 总该有些事是她希望不曾发生过的吧。 “有些事，我希望自己能早些明白……”她承认道，有那么一瞬似乎陷入了沉思。“也许哪天我会把那些故事讲给你听，但现在先告诉你：我活着、做事，从来只认一条路——我自己的路。”她带着调皮的笑容总结道。 你顿了顿，然后有些意外地点点头、笑了笑。等时机到了，你随时愿意听那些故事。 “比起讲精彩的故事，我还是更擅长活出精彩的故事，不过我会尽力的，”她轻笑着，轻轻挠了挠脖子侧面。 那她的童年呢？她一直就是这么个自由自在的性子吗？ “从小就是！要是麻里总督每次骂我、罚我禁闭或者训我一顿，我就能得到一颗石子，那攒下的石子足够我从这儿一路铺到凯罗斯的神社。” 哇……[pc.isCunning |那铺回来的路呢？她要是想跟麻里一较高下，可得再加把劲 |那可真是一大堆石子 ]。 “有一回，我把老十次郎的武士刀粘在了刀鞘里，那年我大概八岁。可怜的家伙花了十多分钟使劲往外拔，最后连护手都飞了出去！你真该看看他当时的脸色！”她放声大笑。“那之后，麻里总督禁止我练刀一个星期。跟你说，被迫看着自己最爱做的事却不能动手，没有比这更难受的了。” 严厉，但公正。 “而且这也不是最后一次！”沙由美笑道。“还有一次，我死活不肯尝炒面。至少可以说，我是只很犟的小狐狸……我连它什么味道都不知道，却照样讨厌它。有一天，麻里总督只是看了我一眼，无声地说了句‘好吧’，就把盘子收走了。到了晚饭时间，她又给我端来炒面，告诉我除非尝一口，否则什么都别想吃。熬过了漫长的一夜，我终于撑不住，咬了一口。最搞笑的是什么呢？直到今天，炒面都是我最爱的食物之一。” 你笑了起来，觉得这事相当有趣，而且对管教犟孩子确实非常有效。 “从那一刻起，无论第一印象多糟，我都会给任何东西一个机会。我永远忘不了那天炒面有多好吃，也绝不会再错过同样能让我享受的机会。” 你表示赞同，并补充说，麻里对她来说一定就像第二个母亲。 “某种意义上，是的。她可以像任何一位母亲那样吓人，比如我十一岁那年打碎一只茶壶的时候。凯罗斯作证，当她说出‘我不生气，我只是失望’时，那感觉就像肚子上挨了一拳。” 你听说过帝国总督有多可怕[flags.KOMARI_FUCKED |，而见过她裸体的样子，说不定还让她变得更加吓人了，但你只说出口的是：她确实很懂得怎么让人服服帖帖 ]。 “那还用说……我到现在想起来还会发冷，不过多亏了那件事，我才懂得了金缮之美。” 金缮？[pc.bg scholar |你想起求学时见过的一份配图手稿。它的做法是凸显并展露损伤，而不是将其遮掩，对吧？ 她点了点头。 ] “那是狐本的一门技艺，用特制的金色漆料修补破损的陶器，”沙由美答道。“这个过程会凸显那些裂痕，仿佛瓷器把自己的苦难当作荣誉勋章佩戴着。金属若始终光亮无瑕，就意味着它从未真正经受过考验。这话听起来也许太夸张，但我就是这么相信的。” 你微笑着，明白她的意思。有人更愿意丢掉换新，而不是修补，沙由美则属于后者的拥护者。
rows.raw: " You're interested in knowing more about this wild, carefree kitsune. Despite her appearance, it's clear that she's garnered a good amount of respect in the den if, as the taskmaster of the wildlings, she serves as Azami's field overseer. Judging by your first encounter, she's an expert swordswoman. What else can she do? She lets out a small laugh, crossing her arms under her bosom. "There's nothing I love more than a good sword fight, but archery is pretty high up there as well. People say many things about me, but I consider myself to be much less of a showoff than what you might have heard. Let's see, what else can I say about myself? I'm a simple woman: I like to cross blades with people capable of giving me a challenge and to explore the wilderness. Oh! I guess there is something most people don't know." Sayumi grabs a pouch hanging from her waist, opens it up, and hands you a wooden statue of a fox. You take it into your hands and carefully study it. It's actually a very nicely done carving. The design is not new to your eyes, you're pretty sure you've seen similar ones around the den, but the level of detail is exquisite. "Carving wood is one of my favorite pastimes. It's such a good way to let your mind wander while your hands do the rest. Takes some time to improve on it, but once you do it's one of the best feelings in the world. Seeing someone's face brighten like yours makes me very happy." It is a beautiful little figurine. Smiling, you return it to Sayumi before asking if there's more to her exploits. Surely a woman like her has many other songs to sing. "You mean apart from all the times I've snuck outside the forest for the thrill of adventure? Heh, I could start and go on for hours. Some say I've done it too much, but the freedom to make my own mistakes is all I've ever wanted." Surely there must be something she wished it didn't happen. "There are some things I wish I realized sooner..." she admits, appearing lost in thought for the slightest moment. "Maybe one day I'll tell you those tales, but for now, let me tell you that I've only ever known one way to live and act: my way." she concludes with a cheeky smile. You pause for a second, then you nod and smile, surprised. You'll be ready to hear those tales, when the time comes. "I'm much better at living cool stories rather than telling them, but I'll do my best," she chuckles, gently scratching the side of her neck. What about her childhood? Has she always been such a free spirit? "Ever since I was a kit! If I had a pebble for every time Governor Komari scolded me, gave me a detention or chewed me out, I'd have enough to pave a path from here all the way to Keros' shrine." Wow... [pc.isCunning |and what about paving the way back? She needs to up her game if she wants to give Komari a run for her money |that's a lot of pebbles ]. "There was that time when I glued old Jūshirō's katana in its scabbard, I think I was eight at the time. Poor guy spent over ten minutes trying to force it out until the handguard came flying! You should have seen his face!" She bursts out laughing. "Governor Komari banned me from training with a sword for a week after that. Let me tell you, there's nothing worse than being forced to watch something you absolutely love doing without being able to do it." Tough, but just. "And it wouldn't be the last time, either!" Sayumi laughs. "There was this other time when I categorically refused to try yakisoba. I was a willful kit, to say the very least... I didn't even know how it tasted, but I hated it nonetheless. One day, Governor Komari just looked at me, mouthed 'Okay', and then took the dish away. When dinnertime came, she gave me yakisoba again and told me that I wasn't going to have anything else until I gave it a taste. After a long night of waiting, I finally cracked and took a bite. The funniest part? Yakisoba is one of my favorite foods to this day." You laugh, finding the whole thing to be pretty amusing, but also very effective at schooling stubborn children. "From that moment on, I've always given everything a chance, no matter how bad the first impression was. I will never forget how good yakisoba tasted that day, and I'm not losing out on an opportunity to enjoy something just as much." You agree, adding that Komari must have been like a second mother for her. "In a way, yes. She could be as scary as any mother, like that time when I broke a tea kettle back when I was eleven. Keros forbid, it felt like a punch to the gut when she said: 'I’m not mad, I’m just disappointed.'." You know the stories of how frightening the Imperial Governor can be[flags.KOMARI_FUCKED |, and seeing her naked possibly made her even more frightening, but the only thing you tell is that she sure knows how to keep people in line ]. "No doubt about that... I feel the chills to this day, but thanks to that incident, I learned about the beauty of kintsugi." Kintsugi? [pc.bg scholar |You recall seeing an illustrated manuscript from your academic studies. It involves highlighting and revealing damage, rather than concealing it, right? She nods. ] "It's a Kitsuhon art where broken pottery is repaired through the use of a special golden lacquer," Sayumi answers. "The process highlights the shattering, almost as if the ceramic is wearing its hardships like a badge of honor. If a metal is shining and untarnished, it means that it has never been truly tested. It might sound over the top, but it's what I believe." You smile, understanding where she's coming from. Some people prefer to throw away and replace instead of repairing, and Sayumi's a supporter of the latter. "

rows.original:
Sayumi’s personal quarters look cozy, even though they’re not the tidiest. On the right side of the room stands a bookcase, haphazardly stuffed with various books and scrolls, but what catches your eye the most is located on the wall on the opposite side of the entrance: the portrait of a fox standing in a snowy forest.
    	
	"A suggestive piece, isn't it? The fox is seemingly relaxed, but if you pay attention to its eyes, you can see that it's still wary of its surroundings." 
	
	You hear Sayumi's voice and your cheeks flush red. Apologizing, you admit that the painting just caught your fancy for longer than you expected.
	
	"Don't think too much about it! It's a topic like any other," she assures after breaking into a laugh.
	
	"Kohaku brought it in, mentioning how 'It looks just like you! Laidback, but with an ear to the ground!'" she says, doing her best impression of Kohaku. "She wanted my best wooden carving, but it was worth it; it does represent me nicely."
	
	You can't help but echo Kohaku's sentiment, as it perfectly encapsulates Sayumi's nature: passionate and relaxed, while keen and perceptive.
	
	"Hahaha! Thanks, [pc.isKitsune
	|[pc.mf
		|Lord
		|Lady
	]ship
        |[pc.name]
    ]. Some would say that's too straightforward, but it's how I like it."
    	
	Taking the opportunity to ask more about the things she keeps in her room, your gaze wanders across her collection. What's Sayumi's choice of reading material?
    	
	"Most of them are tomes with battle maneuvers and sword techniques. I've been writing some myself, but it's hard to explain the nuances between each of the stances. The way you move your wrist while handling a nodachi is not the same you would for, let's say, a nagamaki."
    	
	[pc.bgcl soldier warrior
        |You know your way around battlefield weapons and the forms that make them effective, so you completely understand the difficulty in conveying the exact movements when you can't show them visually.
        |You know that describing something is not the same as showing, which can definitely impact how a technique is performed, especially when it comes to the finer details.
        	
    ]
    	
	As you reflect on the matter, your eyes notice the weapon rack in front of the bookcase. There are several Kitsuhon weapons of varying sizes — is she a collector?
	
	"Oh, those? Nothing too special," she starts, scratching one of her ears. "When I was old enough to walk, I started taking an interest in martial arts, so I trained with several weapons: the yari, masakari axe, rokushakubō, naginata, yumi, kanabō... even the double-edged swords outsiders tend to use. The ones you see over there are mostly keepsakes from my time as a trainee. Good weapons, all of them, but nothing like a daishō."
	
	Daishō? Is she referring to the pair of swords she always carries at her waist?
	
	"That's right," she confirms, moving her hand to the pommel of her longer blade.
	
	"The katana and the wakizashi move at a different pace, forcing the opponent to split their attention between the two. While the enemy is at the mercy of the wakizashi, the katana swoops in for the final blow. Flexibility, erraticness and speed; that's the name of the game."
	
	The grin on Sayumi's face during the entire explanation reminds you how passionate she is for sword fighting. You chuckle: it's wholesome, in a way. 
	
	"It has its drawbacks though: you're moving around a lot and very fast, so you better develop something to fall back on when you're running low on juice. I switch to iaidō when that happens."
    	
	[pc.bgcl soldier warrior
        |You're familiar with the concept, as any battle master worth their weight should know how to adapt to the shifting tides of war. Nevertheless, you let her continue.
        |Can she elaborate further?
    ]
    	
	"Sheathe your blades, keep your katana ready at all times and stay low on your legs. It's a sword style entirely based on precision, all about controlling your breath and waiting for the perfect moment to strike. Exactly what you need when you're trying to rest, since you'll be standing still rather than moving."
    	
	[flags.SAYUMI_SPAR
        |That's exactly what you've observed when you sparred; her fighting style's every bit as adaptable as she claims.
        |You nod once, intrigued by her words. One day, you would like to see her fight.
    ]
    	
	[flags.SAYUMI_SPAR
        |"Hey, speaking of which, now that we've finally sparred once, I can tell you all about my battle mentality. You know what I just said? Well, when I'm in combat, I forget everything."
        	
		Huh? [pc.isBimbo
            |That happens to you a lot too when you start thinking about sex. Which is always...
            	...
            	What was she saying?
            |Is it some kind of intense focus at the point that everything else around it disappears? A 'live in the moment' kind of deal?
        ]
        	
		"Old Jūshirō would probably hate me for this, but if I had to try putting it into words, it would be: 'don't think, go with your gut.'
        	
		Why is that? The displeasing from her teacher, you mean.
        	
		"He's a firm believer that it's something that cannot be described, but only applied. If I were to put it in my own terms, I'd be that your mind is clear from everything, to the point that your body acts without you controlling it. Old Jūshirō would say: 'The body knows how to act, while the mind ignores every tactic or strategy, otherwise it would be defeated. It's like imitating a scarecrow: while immobile, it fulfills the duty to its job. Like a statue, it prevents the fields from being devastated by crows.' "
        	
		So it could be assimilated to doing something without knowing you're doing it? Kinda like walking or chewing?
        	
		"Well... sort of. As I've said, simplifying the 'zen' practices old Jūshirō taught us would have made him hit us with a stick. You've seen me, though: my body goes on its own while my mind is just loving every moment of it," she laughs. "I guess it's my very personal zen."
        	
		You smile back. How could you forget how the ecstasy flowered on her face during your sparring session? It seemed that it was the moment where she found her center. [flags.SAYUMI_FUCKED
            |That and when you two are fucking.
        ]
    ]
rows.translation:
沙由美的私人房间看起来颇为温馨，虽说算不上最整洁。房间右侧立着一个书架，上面胡乱塞满了各式书籍和卷轴，但最吸引你目光的东西挂在入口对面那面墙上：一幅狐狸伫立在雪林中的画像。
    	
	“一幅很引人遐想的画，对吧？画里的狐狸看似放松，可只要你留意它的眼睛，就会发现它仍在警惕着四周。”
	
	听到沙由美的声音，你的脸颊涨得通红。你向她道歉，承认自己只是被那幅画吸引，盯着看的时间比预想的要久。
	
	“别想太多啦！这不过是个再普通不过的话题，”她笑出声后这样宽慰你。
	
	“是琥珀把它带回来的，还说‘它跟你简直一模一样！随性，但耳朵始终贴着地面！’”她说这话时，尽力模仿着琥珀的语气。“她想要我最好的木雕，不过这很值得；它确实把我的样子表现得很贴切。”
	
	你忍不住附和琥珀的看法，因为它完美地概括了沙由美的本性：热情而放松，同时敏锐又洞彻。
	
	“哈哈哈！谢谢你，[pc.isKitsune
	|[pc.mf
		|Lord
		|Lady
	]ship
        |[pc.name]
    ]。有人会说这样太直来直去了，可我就喜欢这样。”
    	
	趁着这个机会，你想多问问她房间里收藏的东西，目光便在她的藏品间游走。沙由美平时都读些什么书？
    	
	“大多是讲战术招式和剑术技巧的书。我自己也写过一些，可要解释清楚各种架势之间的微妙差别实在太难了。你握薙刀时转动手腕的方式，跟——比如说——握长卷刀时是不一样的。”
    	
	[pc.bgcl soldier warrior
        |你熟悉战场上的各种武器以及让它们发挥威力的招式，所以你完全理解，在没法亲身示范的情况下，要把动作精确描述出来有多难。
        |你知道描述某件事和把它演示出来完全是两回事，这绝对会影响一门技艺的施展效果，尤其是在细节上。
        	
    ]
    	
	你一边琢磨着这件事，目光一边注意到书架前的那排武器架。上面摆着好几件大小不一的狐本武器——她是个收藏家吗？
	
	“哦，那些啊？没什么特别的，”她开口道，挠了挠自己的一只耳朵。“我到了能走路的年纪就开始对武术感兴趣，于是练过好几种武器：长枪、钺斧、六尺棒、薙刀、长弓、金砕棒……连外来人爱用的双刃剑也练过。你看到的那些，大多是我当学徒时留下的纪念品。都是好武器，可哪件都比不上大小。”
	
	大小？她指的是她总挂在腰间的那对刀吗？
	
	“没错，”她确认道，手移向那把较长刀剑的刀柄。
	
	“太刀和胁差的行进节奏不同，逼得对手不得不把注意力分散在两者之间。当敌人被胁差逼得左支右绌时，太刀便从旁掠入，给出致命一击。灵活、无常、迅捷；这才是这套刀法的精髓所在。”
	
	整个讲解过程中，沙由美脸上的笑意都在提醒你：她对剑术有多么痴迷。你轻笑起来：从某种角度说，这挺可爱的。
	
	“不过它也有缺点：你要不停地大幅度快速移动，所以最好练出一套能在果汁耗尽时依靠的东西。遇到那种情况，我就会切换成居合道。”
    	
	[pc.bgcl soldier warrior
        |你对这个概念很熟悉，毕竟任何有真本事的战斗大师都该懂得如何适应战场上风云变幻的局势。话虽如此，你还是让她继续讲下去。
        |她能再详细说说吗？
    ]
    	
	“收刀入鞘，让太刀随时待命，双腿压低。这是一种完全建立在精准之上的剑术，讲究控制呼吸，等待那一击必杀的最佳时机。这正是你需要的休息方式，因为你会站着不动，而不是四处奔走。”
    	
	[flags.SAYUMI_SPAR
        |这正是你和她切磋时观察到的；她的战斗风格确实如她所说那般随机应变。
        |你点了点头，对她的话很感兴趣。总有一天，你想亲眼看看她战斗的样子。
    ]
    	
	[flags.SAYUMI_SPAR
        |“嘿，说到这个，既然我们终于切磋过一次了，我可以好好跟你讲讲我的战斗理念。你还记得我刚才说的吗？嗯，当我身处战斗之中时，我会忘掉一切。”
        	
		咦？[pc.isBimbo
            |你一开始想着性事也会经常这样。而那你随时都在想……
            	……
            	她刚才在说什么来着？
            |这是不是某种极度专注，专注到周围的一切都消失了？一种‘活在当下’的状态？
        ]
        	
		“老师十次郎大概会为这话揍我一顿，可如果要我试着用语言说出来，那就是：‘别去想，跟着直觉走。’”
        	
		那是为什么？你是指，她的师父对此很不满。
        	
		“他坚信这种东西无法言传，只能身体力行。如果要用我自己的话来表达，那就是你的心一片空明，空到身体在你没有操控的情况下自行行动。老师十次郎会说：‘身体知道该如何行动，而心则无视一切战术与策略，否则它就会落败。这就像模仿稻草人：虽静止不动，却履行了自己的职责。又如雕像，它让田地免遭乌鸦的蹂躏。’”
        	
		所以这可以理解为在不自知的情况下做某件事？有点像走路或咀嚼？
        	
		“嗯……差不多吧。我说过了，要是把老师十次郎教我们的那些‘禅’的修行简单化，他准会拿棍子敲我们。不过你也看到了，我的身体自行其是，而我的心只是在享受每一刻，”她笑道。“我猜，这就是我个人的禅吧。”
        	
		你也回以微笑。你怎么可能忘记切磋时她脸上绽放出的那份极乐？那一刻，仿佛她找到了自己的中心。[flags.SAYUMI_FUCKED
            |还有你俩做爱的时候。
        ]
    ]
rows.raw:
"
    Sayumi’s personal quarters look cozy, even though they’re not the tidiest. On the right side of the room stands a bookcase, haphazardly stuffed with various books and scrolls, but what catches your eye the most is located on the wall on the opposite side of the entrance: the portrait of a fox standing in a snowy forest.
    	
	"A suggestive piece, isn't it? The fox is seemingly relaxed, but if you pay attention to its eyes, you can see that it's still wary of its surroundings." 
	
	You hear Sayumi's voice and your cheeks flush red. Apologizing, you admit that the painting just caught your fancy for longer than you expected.
	
	"Don't think too much about it! It's a topic like any other," she assures after breaking into a laugh.
	
	"Kohaku brought it in, mentioning how 'It looks just like you! Laidback, but with an ear to the ground!'" she says, doing her best impression of Kohaku. "She wanted my best wooden carving, but it was worth it; it does represent me nicely."
	
	You can't help but echo Kohaku's sentiment, as it perfectly encapsulates Sayumi's nature: passionate and relaxed, while keen and perceptive.
	
	"Hahaha! Thanks, [pc.isKitsune
	|[pc.mf
		|Lord
		|Lady
	]ship
        |[pc.name]
    ]. Some would say that's too straightforward, but it's how I like it."
    	
	Taking the opportunity to ask more about the things she keeps in her room, your gaze wanders across her collection. What's Sayumi's choice of reading material?
    	
	"Most of them are tomes with battle maneuvers and sword techniques. I've been writing some myself, but it's hard to explain the nuances between each of the stances. The way you move your wrist while handling a nodachi is not the same you would for, let's say, a nagamaki."
    	
	[pc.bgcl soldier warrior
        |You know your way around battlefield weapons and the forms that make them effective, so you completely understand the difficulty in conveying the exact movements when you can't show them visually.
        |You know that describing something is not the same as showing, which can definitely impact how a technique is performed, especially when it comes to the finer details.
        	
    ]
    	
	As you reflect on the matter, your eyes notice the weapon rack in front of the bookcase. There are several Kitsuhon weapons of varying sizes — is she a collector?
	
	"Oh, those? Nothing too special," she starts, scratching one of her ears. "When I was old enough to walk, I started taking an interest in martial arts, so I trained with several weapons: the yari, masakari axe, rokushakubō, naginata, yumi, kanabō... even the double-edged swords outsiders tend to use. The ones you see over there are mostly keepsakes from my time as a trainee. Good weapons, all of them, but nothing like a daishō."
	
	Daishō? Is she referring to the pair of swords she always carries at her waist?
	
	"That's right," she confirms, moving her hand to the pommel of her longer blade.
	
	"The katana and the wakizashi move at a different pace, forcing the opponent to split their attention between the two. While the enemy is at the mercy of the wakizashi, the katana swoops in for the final blow. Flexibility, erraticness and speed; that's the name of the game."
	
	The grin on Sayumi's face during the entire explanation reminds you how passionate she is for sword fighting. You chuckle: it's wholesome, in a way. 
	
	"It has its drawbacks though: you're moving around a lot and very fast, so you better develop something to fall back on when you're running low on juice. I switch to iaidō when that happens."
    	
	[pc.bgcl soldier warrior
        |You're familiar with the concept, as any battle master worth their weight should know how to adapt to the shifting tides of war. Nevertheless, you let her continue.
        |Can she elaborate further?
    ]
    	
	"Sheathe your blades, keep your katana ready at all times and stay low on your legs. It's a sword style entirely based on precision, all about controlling your breath and waiting for the perfect moment to strike. Exactly what you need when you're trying to rest, since you'll be standing still rather than moving."
    	
	[flags.SAYUMI_SPAR
        |That's exactly what you've observed when you sparred; her fighting style's every bit as adaptable as she claims.
        |You nod once, intrigued by her words. One day, you would like to see her fight.
    ]
    	
	[flags.SAYUMI_SPAR
        |"Hey, speaking of which, now that we've finally sparred once, I can tell you all about my battle mentality. You know what I just said? Well, when I'm in combat, I forget everything."
        	
		Huh? [pc.isBimbo
            |That happens to you a lot too when you start thinking about sex. Which is always...
            	...
            	What was she saying?
            |Is it some kind of intense focus at the point that everything else around it disappears? A 'live in the moment' kind of deal?
        ]
        	
		"Old Jūshirō would probably hate me for this, but if I had to try putting it into words, it would be: 'don't think, go with your gut.'
        	
		Why is that? The displeasing from her teacher, you mean.
        	
		"He's a firm believer that it's something that cannot be described, but only applied. If I were to put it in my own terms, I'd be that your mind is clear from everything, to the point that your body acts without you controlling it. Old Jūshirō would say: 'The body knows how to act, while the mind ignores every tactic or strategy, otherwise it would be defeated. It's like imitating a scarecrow: while immobile, it fulfills the duty to its job. Like a statue, it prevents the fields from being devastated by crows.' "
        	
		So it could be assimilated to doing something without knowing you're doing it? Kinda like walking or chewing?
        	
		"Well... sort of. As I've said, simplifying the 'zen' practices old Jūshirō taught us would have made him hit us with a stick. You've seen me, though: my body goes on its own while my mind is just loving every moment of it," she laughs. "I guess it's my very personal zen."
        	
		You smile back. How could you forget how the ecstasy flowered on her face during your sparring session? It seemed that it was the moment where she found her center. [flags.SAYUMI_FUCKED
            |That and when you two are fucking.
        ]
    ]
    "

rows.original: [flags.KOMARI_TLK_SAYUMI |You've heard that Sayumi's family has been connected to Imperial Governor Komari since before her departure. Would she be willing to tell you more about it? |She isn't the only person whose family name is Ishida, and you're very curious about the story of her clan. Would she be willing to tell you more about it? ] Sayumi relaxes her tails, letting out a soft sigh. "My clan... the Ishida clan has an unusual story. But around here, can any story really be called ordinary?" You see a faint smile on her lips as her single eye meets yours. "My great-grandfather, Takeru Ishida, was a childhood friend of Governor Komari’s. Originally, the Ishidas came from the mountains of the Old Country, where they dedicated their lives to ascetic martial practices. We weren’t of notable skill, not until Lord Takeru came along. He quickly gained fame as an archer and a scholar, making himself renowned enough that his clan became one of the ruling ones. When Governor Komari was sent into exile, Lord Takeru willingly decided to follow her. He didn’t have to, yet he did anyway... something I too would have done. Sticking by your friends during their darkest hour is the greatest thing to do." Sounds like he was indeed a great man. "With him, he brought in exile his greatest accomplishment, the Ishida clan's secret technique. The Lightning of Takeru." The Lightning of Takeru? That sounds ominous, but impressive at the same time. "'Takeru no Kaminari' in Kitsuhon language... a technique as powerful as it is dangerous. The practitioner uses their own body to channel the wrath of the heavens, manipulating it however they see fit to strike down their enemies. In a sense, the user becomes one with lightning." Is it really as dangerous as she says? [flags.SAYUMI_DOUBTS_TS |"I've already told you what the technique has done to my father... what I haven't is that I've felt it on my own skin too." [pc.dcb |You feel like you're expected to care about her problems, so you attempt to feign concern. |You start to worry. |Oh, no! The poor cuddly fox-cutie! ] What did she do? "I've watched my father perform the technique hundreds of times; the footwork, the breathing frequency, the way the magic was channeled around the body... If you know me, you know." A bitter smile follows her words as you narrow your eyes. She has attempted to master the technique, after all. "I thought I had everything figured out... heh, I told you that I was an even bigger moron back then. I retreated back at my usual spot, conjured the powers of the Lightning of Takeru, and lost control of it." She clenches her fist, trying to hide her frustration at the thought. "I didn't realize at the time, but what happened was nothing short of a miracle: I woke up mostly unscathed. I don't know what happened, but it must have been sheer dumb luck with how the energy escaped my body. I thought I just needed more practice, but the day after, father almost lost his life." She lowers her gaze. "There are many reasons why I haven't tried the technique again ever since, but the danger of it isn't one of them, I assure you, as I've studied several countermeasures. The real reason is... I was told: 'Do not reach for the heavens unless you're ready'," Sayumi intones. "Until I understand what my father meant by this, I don't feel worthy of mastering such power. "It might sound stupid to say..." she admits, taking a breath and trying to calm herself. "...but this is my way to do it," she concludes, her confidence renewed like a weight was taken off her chest. You smile back, assuring her that you have her back. Better yet, if she wants a sparring partner to look out for her when attempting the Lightning of Takeru again, you will be there. "Thank you, [pc.isKitsune |[pc.mf |Lord |Lady ]ship |[pc.name] ]" She puts her hands on your shoulder as her eye gleams with relief. "You'll be the first one to know, trust me." |"There’s a girl who lives here in the den, Rindo Igarashi is her name. Several years ago, she suffered a tragic accident that left her with permanent burns on her body. My father, Hiroyuki Ishida, suffered even worse injuries." Her eye narrows the very moment she mentions her father, and silence immediately follows. Grievously injured because of one wrong move? Most of the scars on her body have been inflicted by bladed weapons. Does this mean that she has successfully mastered the Lightning of Takeru? She slowly looks away, appearing uncharacteristically solemn. "A long time ago, I made a promise to never attempt the technique until I grasped what he wanted to say. Let's just leave it at that." Her stoic mask slowly changes, leaving an air of melancholy about her. You can see her conflict, so you decide to offer her your support whenever she might need it. [pc.isKitsune |Sayumi's ears twitch in surprise for a moment, then she turns her head away from you, her one eye filling with regret she hopes to hide beneath a smug smile. "G-governor Komari would chew me out if she knew I dragged Keros’ champion into unimportant matters! Or hit me on the head with her cane, or worst of all, just look disapprovingly with those eyes of hers..." Oh, yeah, kitsune customs. Right now, you aren’t Keros’ champion, but just [silly |a bumbling fox-sworn that is still new to Floofland and its floofers. Right? Riiiight? |a friend trying to offer support; is this enough for her? ] Sayumi's ears lower, then they relax once again: she's taken your words to heart. "I uh... thank you. I wasn't expecting to hear that." For a moment, you could have sworn you had seen a blush. |Her ears twitch in surprise for a moment, then Sayumi smiles radiantly. "This is why I like an outsider's mentality: you don't shy away from asking." For a moment, you could have sworn you had seen a blush. ] ]
rows.translation: [flags.KOMARI_TLK_SAYUMI |你听说过沙由美的家族在她离开之前就与太守麻里有所往来。她愿意多告诉你一些吗？ |她并不是唯一一个姓石田的人，而你对她的氏族故事非常好奇。她愿意多告诉你一些吗？ ] 沙由美放松了尾巴，轻轻叹了口气。 “我的氏族……石田一族有一段不寻常的故事。不过在这地方，哪段故事又真称得上寻常呢？” 你看见她唇边浮起一丝浅笑，她那只独眼与你对视。 “我的曾祖父，石田武，是太守麻里小时候的朋友。石田家原本来自旧国的群山之中，在那里世代潜心于苦修式的武道。我们的武艺并不出众，直到武大人出现。他很快便以弓手和学者的身份声名远扬，名声大到让他的氏族跻身统治氏族之列。太守麻里被流放时，武大人心甘情愿地决定追随她。他本没有必要这么做，可他还是这么做了……换成是我，我也会这么做。在朋友最黑暗的时刻守在朋友身边，是最了不起的事。” 听起来他确实是个了不起的人。 “他流放时随身带去了他最伟大的成就，石田一族的秘术。武之雷。” 武之雷？听起来很不祥，可同时又令人震撼。 “在狐本语里叫‘武之雷’……一门既强大又危险的技艺。修习者以自己的肉体为媒介引导天罚之力，再随心所欲地操控它击倒敌人。某种意义上，使用者会与雷电融为一体。” 真有她说的那么危险吗？ [flags.SAYUMI_DOUBTS_TS |“这门秘术对我父亲做过什么，我已经告诉过你了……我没说的是，我自己也亲身体会过。” [pc.dcb |你觉得这种场合应该表现出关心，于是试着装出一副担忧的样子。 |你开始担心起来。 |哦，不！可怜又软乎乎的狐娘小可爱！ ]她做了什么？ “我看过我父亲施展那门秘术上百次；步法、呼吸的频率、魔力在周身循环的方式……你要是了解我，就该知道。” 你眯起眼睛，她的话音之后跟着一抹苦笑。她终究还是尝试过掌握那门秘术。 “我以为自己已经全弄明白了……嘿，我跟你说过，那时候的我比现在还要蠢得多。我回到平时练习的地方，召唤出武之雷的力量，然后失去了对它的控制。” 她攥紧拳头，试图掩饰一想到这事就涌上来的懊恼。 “当时我没意识到，可发生的事简直堪称奇迹：我醒来时几乎毫发无伤。我不知道究竟发生了什么，但能量那样从我的身体里逃逸出去，只能说是走了天大的狗屎运。我以为自己只是需要多加练习，可第二天，父亲差点丢了性命。” 她垂下目光。 “从那以后我再没尝试过那门秘术，原因有很多，但我向你保证，危险并不在其中，因为我已经研究过好几种应对手段。真正的原因是……有人对我说过：‘除非你已经准备好，否则不要伸手去够天。’”沙由美一字一句地说。“在我明白父亲这句话是什么意思之前，我不觉得自己配掌握这样的力量。 “这话说出来也许很傻……”她承认道，深吸一口气，试着让自己平静下来。“……可这是我自己选择的路，”她做出结论，自信重新涌起，仿佛胸口卸下了一块大石。 你回以微笑，向她保证你会站在她这一边。更进一步说，如果她想要一个陪练搭档，在她再次尝试武之雷时替她守望，你一定会到场。 “谢谢你，[pc.isKitsune |[pc.mf |Lord |Lady ]ship |[pc.name] ]”她把手搭在你的肩上，独眼里闪着如释重负的光。“你会是第一个知道的人，相信我。” |“这处巢穴里住着一个女孩，名叫林多·五十岚。几年前，她遭遇了一场悲惨的事故，身上留下了永久的烧伤。我的父亲石田博之受的伤还要更重。” 她一提到父亲，独眼便眯了起来，紧接着是沉默。因为一步走错就身受重伤？可她身上大部分的伤疤都是刀剑之类的利器留下的。这是不是意味着，她已经成功掌握了武之雷？ 她缓缓移开视线，神情肃穆得不像她平时的样子。 “很久以前，我许下过一个承诺：在我弄明白他想说的是什么之前，绝不再尝试那门秘术。这事就到此为止吧。” 她那张坚忍的面具缓缓变化，整个人笼罩上一层忧郁的气息。你能看出她内心的挣扎，于是决定无论她何时需要，都愿意给予她支持。 [pc.isKitsune |沙由美的耳朵惊讶地抖了一下，随后她把头别开，那只独眼里满是悔意，她希望能用一抹得意的笑把它藏起来。 “要——要是让太守麻里知道我把凯罗斯的冠军扯进这些无关紧要的事里，她非把我骂得狗血淋头不可！要么拿手杖敲我的脑袋，要么最惨的是，就用她那双眼睛不满地盯着我看……” 哦，对了，狐族的规矩。 现在的你并不是凯罗斯的冠军，而只是一个[silly |刚来到毛茸茸乐园、对这里的毛团们还很陌生的笨手笨脚的狐誓者。对吧？对吧——？ |想给予支持的朋友；这对她来说够吗？ ] 沙由美的耳朵垂了下去，随后又放松开来：她把你的话听进去了。 “我，呃……谢谢你。我没想到会听到这样的话。” 有那么一瞬间，你发誓自己看到她脸红了。 |她的耳朵惊讶地抖了一下，随后沙由美绽开灿烂的笑容。 “这就是我喜欢外来者心态的地方：你们从不羞于开口问。” 有那么一瞬间，你发誓自己看到她脸红了。 ] ]

rows.original: "My sister? She's a workaholic in the purest sense of the word. She never takes a rest and buries herself into her duties for way longer than she should. Sometimes I try to help her by shouldering some of the burden, but it's often useless as she just ends up replacing it with even more chores. She always hated idleness, that much I understand... but after you work hard, you need to rest even harder. Believe it or not, she used to be much more rambunctious, but as time went on she became so stern and serious that you wouldn't believe they were the same person. We still argue from time to time like all siblings do, but she is family, and I'll love her no matter what, despite our differences."
rows.translation: “我姐姐？她是那种最纯粹的拼命三郎。她从不休息，把自己埋进公务里的时间长得远超应有的限度。有时我想帮她分担一些担子，可往往没什么用，因为她转头就会用更多的杂务把它替换掉。她一直讨厌无所事事，这点我能理解……可你拼命干完活之后，就该更拼命地休息。信不信由你，她以前可比现在闹腾多了，可随着日子过去，她变得那么严厉、那么一本正经，你根本不会相信她们是同一个人。我们偶尔还是会像所有兄弟姐妹那样吵架，但她是我的家人，不管我们之间有多少分歧，我都会永远爱她。”

Sometimes I try to help her by shouldering some of the burden, but it's often useless as she just ends up replacing it with even more chores. She always hated idleness, that much I understand... but after you work hard, you need to rest even harder. Believe it or not, she used to be much more rambunctious, but as time went on she became so stern and serious that you wouldn't believe they were the same person. We still argue from time to time like all siblings do, but she is family, and I'll love her no matter what, despite our differences.\"\n    "

rows.original:
"I like that guy. We're similar at heart, we both pursue our interests no matter what others might think. A couple of months ago, he decided to start experimenting on ways to create a new functioning eye for me. Hahaha! It was an interesting proposal, so I agreed after he pitched the idea to me. 
    
    "In fact, he's still working on it, but I don't know if he's made any progress at all. I told him there's no rush and that he should prioritize helping people who need it more than I do. I've lived with only one eye for over ten years, a couple more won't be a problem. Only thing I'd like for him to do is learn when to pull the brakes. It's one thing to be clever, and another to be wise. Sometimes, the two don't come together."
rows.translation:
“我喜欢那家伙。我们骨子里挺像的，都是不管别人怎么想，也照样去追求自己感兴趣的东西。几个月前，他决定开始试验，想给我造出一只能用的新眼睛。哈哈哈！这提议挺有意思，所以他把想法讲给我听之后我就答应了。
    
    “其实他到现在还在忙那件事，但我不知道他到底有没有取得什么进展。我跟他说过不用急，他应该优先去帮那些比我更需要帮助的人。我只有一只眼睛已经过了十多年，再多几年也不成问题。我唯一希望他学会的，就是知道什么时候该踩刹车。聪明是一回事，有智慧是另一回事。有时候，这两样东西并不会同时出现。”

It's one thing to be clever, and another to be wise. Sometimes, the two don't come together."
    "

rows.original: "One of the smartest people I know, even if he doesn't fully understand why that's the case. All he wants to do is wake up, work the fields, tend to plants, and go to sleep. He doesn't let the rumors about his supposed lack of ambition bother him, and has no other desire than to engage in what he loves. If we all were like him, the world would be a much better place. Like me and my sis, he lets his actions speak rather than his mouth, which is one of the many reasons why I hope he gets everything he wants from life."
rows.translation: “他是我认识的最聪明的人之一，尽管他自己并不完全明白为什么会这样。他想要的只是醒来、下地干活、照料植物，然后睡觉。他不会让那些说他胸无大志的流言困扰自己，除了投入自己热爱的事之外别无他求。如果我们人人都像他那样，这世界会好得多。他和我跟我姐一样，都是让行动说话，而不是靠一张嘴，这也是我希望他的人生能得到自己想要的一切的众多原因之一。”

Like me and my sis, he lets his actions speak rather than his mouth, which is one of the many reasons why I hope he gets everything he wants from life.\"\n    "

rows.original: "A woman of action. She reminds me of myself back when I was still fresh in the wildlings, just as willful, just as headstrong. She doesn't get along well with my sister, but when the situation calls for it, they manage to put their differences aside. You don't always have to be friends with your colleagues or bosses to be effective on the job, and Kurako is the finest example I can think of. She can improve on her... 'cravings,' though; everyone knows how much I love combat, you've seen it yourself from our first encounter, but not knowing when to stop has its consequences — consequences that she tends to ignore. Striking a balance between actions and words is what makes it all the better, if you ask me, and I'm sure she will agree soon enough."
rows.translation: “一个行动派的女人。她让我想起自己还在野狐里初出茅庐的时候，一样固执，一样倔强。她跟我姐姐相处得不算好，可到了需要的时候，她们还是能把分歧搁到一边。你不必非得跟同事或上司做朋友才能把工作干好，而仓子就是我能想到的最好的例子。不过她那些……‘癖好’还有改进的余地；人人都知道我有多热爱战斗，我们第一次交手时你也亲眼看到了，可不知道什么时候该收手是有代价的——而这些代价，她往往视而不见。要我说，在行动和言语之间找到平衡才会让一切更好，我相信她很快就会认同这一点。”
rows.raw: "\n    \"A woman of action. She reminds me of myself back when I was still fresh in the wildlings, just as willful, just as headstrong. 'cravings,' though; everyone knows how much I love combat, you've seen it yourself from our first encounter, but not knowing when to stop has its consequences — consequences that she tends to ignore. Striking a balance between actions and words is what makes it all the better, if you ask me, and I'm sure she will agree soon enough.\"\n    "

rows.original: "We have fought side by side many times, and she's surprisingly quick at thinking on her feet. It balances her lack of patience perfectly, because I can't describe with words how impulsive that girl is. Azami mentioned that lately she has been acknowledging that, which is good; it will help her to not get herself killed. She values her comrades higher than herself, and would be willing to take an arrow to the chest if it means dragging an injured friend to safety. I know a lot about getting injured, so I understand why she isn’t afraid of pain, but she shouldn’t downright ignore it."
rows.translation: “我们并肩作战过很多次，她临机应变的速度快得惊人。这恰好弥补了她缺乏耐心的毛病，因为我实在没法用言语形容那姑娘有多冲动。阿兹米提过，她最近开始承认这一点了，这是好事；这会帮她别把自己害死。她把同伴看得比自己更重，只要能拖着受伤的朋友脱离险境，她愿意用胸口去挡一支箭。我对受伤这种事了解得很深，所以我明白她为什么不惧怕痛苦，可她不该干脆把它无视掉。”
rows.raw: "\n    \"We have fought side by side many times, and she's surprisingly quick at thinking on her feet. rows.original:
"Hahah, that man has entire books worth of knowledge in his head; why would anyone need a library when you can just ask him?
    
    "'A sharp mind grows dull without practice as much as a sword does without a whetstone', as old Jushiro used to say, hence why he is the main strategist of the wildlings as well as my sister's second in command. Expected, knowing how mature and serious he is, perhaps even too much. Sometimes, I wish he was less strict, but if he was, he wouldn’t be as meticulous in his tasks, probably."
rows.translation:
“哈哈哈，那男人脑子里装着能写满整座图书馆的知识；当你可以直接问他时，谁还需要图书馆呢？
    
    “老十次郎以前常说：‘脑子不练会变钝，就像剑不磨会变钝一样’，正因如此，他既是野狐的首席军师，也是我姐姐的副手。这也在意料之中，毕竟他那么成熟、那么认真，也许认真得过头了。有时候我希望他别那么严格，可要是他不严格，大概也就不会对自己的差事那么一丝不苟了。”

rows.original: "Some people say it's difficult to get her attention, considering how she comes across as a bit of an airhead. The faster she can finish her job, the more satisfied she usually is, but this doesn’t mean that she’s superficial, quite the contrary, actually — she often finds the best and most creative solution with the least effort. I have great respect for people who can think outside the box, and Yuzu definitely checks that. She's the first that comes to mind when I think of 'don't judge a book by its cover'."
rows.translation: “有些人说很难引起她的注意，因为她给人的感觉有点迷糊。她越早干完活，通常就越满意，但这并不意味着她肤浅，恰恰相反——她常常能用最少的力气找到最好、最有创意的解决办法。我非常敬重能跳出框架思考的人，而柚子绝对算一个。一想到‘不能以貌取人’，我第一个想到的就是她。”

The faster she can finish her job, the more satisfied she usually is, but this doesn’t mean that she’s superficial, quite the contrary, actually — she often finds the best and most creative solution with the least effort. rows.original: "The situation is"—Sayumi grimaces—"more complicated than it looks. A lot has happened and a lot is still happening to all parties involved, and nobody’s completely right nor completely wrong. What started the chain of events happened many years ago, but know this: Azami’s the only one who can end it."
rows.translation: “这情况”——沙由美皱起脸——“比看起来要复杂得多。各方身上都发生过很多事，而且还有很多事正在发生，没有谁是绝对正确的，也没有谁是绝对错误的。引发这一连串事件的源头发生在很多年前，但你只要记住这一点：只有阿兹米能终结它。”
rows.raw: '\n    "The situation is"—Sayumi grimaces—"more complicated than it looks. A lot has happened and a lot is still happening to all parties involved, and nobody’s completely right nor completely wrong. What started the chain of events happened many years ago, but know this: Azami’s the only one who can end it."\n    '

rows.original: "She is a strange figure, almost mythical in a sense. Governor Komari told us of her political maneuvers that created this place, but usually that was it. Now I can see why... It would have awakened painful memories. Governor Komari is very important to me and my sister, so I am happy that she seems to feel lighter after High Lady Otomo’s arrival. To sum her up in a few words, High Lady Otomo is the picture you would see if someone were to ask you to imagine 'nobility.' She radiates high class with every action she takes, even the smallest. Hard to say if she was born with that talent or if it was something she learned over the years... perhaps a bit of both, which is why I have so much respect for her."
rows.translation: “她是个奇特的人物，某种意义上近乎神话。太守麻里跟我们讲过她那些缔造了此地的政治手腕，但通常也就只讲到那儿。现在我能明白为什么了……那大概会唤醒痛苦的回忆。太守麻里对我和姐姐来说非常重要，所以她似乎在乙女大君到来之后轻松了一些，我很高兴。要用几句话来概括乙女大君，她就是那种如果有人让你想象‘高贵’二字，你眼前会浮现出的画面。她的一举一动都散发着上流气质，哪怕是最细微的动作也不例外。很难说她这份才能是生来就有，还是多年学来的……也许两者都有，正因如此我才如此敬重她。”
rows.raw: "\n    \"She is a strange figure, almost mythical in a sense. Governor Komari told us of her political maneuvers that created this place, but usually that was it. Now I can see why... It would have awakened painful memories. Governor Komari is very important to me and my sister, so I am happy that she seems to feel lighter after High Lady Otomo’s arrival. To sum her up in a few words, High Lady Otomo is the picture you would see if someone were to ask you to imagine 'nobility.' She radiates high class with every action she takes, even the smallest. Hard to say if she was born with that talent or if it was something she learned over the years... perhaps a bit of both, which is why I have so much respect for her.\"\n    "

rows.original: "Aaah, her!" she snaps her fingers, smiling. "She is a bit of a special case here in the den, because even if her duties are similar to a wildling’s, she directly answers to Nakano. Her family is nobility back in the Old Country, but it didn't stop some people from firmly believing that she is cursed in some way because of her single tail. I hung out with her a couple of times, and I really couldn’t understand why they say she’s cursed, or the reasons why Lord Keros might have cursed her in the first place. She’s a perfectly normal girl like any other; pretty good at handling her naginata and a pretty fine cook."
rows.translation: “啊，她呀！”她打了个响指，笑起来。“在这处巢穴里，她算是个特例，因为即使她的职责和野狐差不多，她也是直接听命于中野的。她的家族在旧国是贵族，可这并没有阻止某些人坚信她因为只有一条尾巴而受到了某种诅咒。我跟她一起出去过几次，实在不明白他们为什么说她被诅咒了，也不明白凯罗斯大人究竟为什么会诅咒她。她就是和别的女孩一样普普通通的姑娘；薙刀使得相当不错，厨艺也相当好。”
