rows.original: [rand |"The seamstress has a new daughter, does she? I'm aware." Tetsuya quirks a wry smile at you — oh, he knows of your involvement in all this, no doubt. "One of the things I've noticed after arriving in the colonies is the particularly relaxed attitude people have about having children. [tetsuya.anyKids |I didn't expect to get caught up in it myself, but you happened, and here we are. ]It's true, word has it that some willingly come to the colonies because social attitudes about family sizes are considerably more relaxed, but hearing about a phenomenon and experiencing it for myself are two different things." What Hotaru did would have been looked down upon in the Old Country? Tetsuya scratches his chin at that. "Hmm... certainly disapproved of as irresponsible breeding, perhaps even going so far as to have her behavior described as feckless. You must understand, [pc.name] — the proportion of kitsune and our benefactor peoples have remained steady for a long, long time. The former should not be outsized compared to the latter, because beneficence should be an uncommon yet pleasant experience." To put it bluntly, the foxes don't want to outgrow their food supply. A wince. "Yes. Which is why indiscriminately having kits is frowned upon, to say the least. Things are different here in the colonies since benefactors are plentiful, but eventually a similar agreement will have to be reached in the generations to come, if we are to remain in these lands. Hopefully, enough of the old habits and attitudes will remain that it is not too painful. "But that is a problem for future generations. As for Hotaru, she can do as she pleases with considerably less consequence than she would face on the other side of the torii. She seems content with the one for now, so I don't think you've ignited something that'll prove difficult to put out. Hopefully." |"Truth be told, when news of what Hotaru had done reached my ears through the — ahem — usual sources, I was worried that she'd made a mistake." Huh. Interesting that a prince like him would deign to be concerned with the be concerned with a seamstress' personal affairs. Tetsuya waves off the concern. "You give me too much standing, [pc.name]. Here in the colonies, I have little authority. Besides, it's only natural to be concerned for one's neighbors; the tree is not exactly a bustling city. "But back to the point. When Kohaku told me about it, my first thought was that she should have reconsidered the situation from her perspective. Did she want a child, or did she just want the approval of parents she rarely saw? Parents who placed their thirst for adventure over her?" You've noticed Hotaru's determination to be there for Kaori, yes. "This shouldn't need to be said, but having kits is important and that kind of decision should be made when everyone involved is ready," Tetsuya continues. "There's 'continuing your familial lineage', and then there's 'sabotaging yourself and your kits' future by jumping blindly into parenthood'. "I understand things are more lax in the colonies, but even so, those who have many children are not that common even amongst the colonial lineages. All the more reason to make the few chances one has count — not that I'm saying neglect is justified under any circumstances, of course." And does he still worry about Hotaru making a mistake, now that things have settled down? "Hmm." He idly gathers up one of his tails and runs his fingers through the fine fur. "There are still worries, especially considering that Hotaru is gifted, but such is the case when it comes to being responsible for another life. The situation is better now that her parents have returned and look to be staying for the foreseeable future, and you..." You do what you can, but you have duties elsewhere. A wry chuckle. "Don't we all. Perhaps the true test will come when the novelty of the new arrival fades, and Hotaru settles in for years of child-raising with Kaori. I wonder if she'll start demanding another child at that point, ostensibly for both her and Kaori's sakes. Give that kind of vixen what she wants, and she'll quickly learn to keep demanding it from you." |You note that Hotaru wasn't shy about naming Kaori right out of the womb. She'd obviously been thinking of the name for a long time, but for a collector of old tales she was pretty quick to ignore the custom. "She just has confidence in her daughter, that's all. Despite what you said, [pc.name], that kind of unyielding belief is quite characteristic of our seamstress." Hmm?[tetsuya.anyKids | Actually, come to think of it, Setsuna was named pretty quickly, too. Not that you would've expected a nobleman to put any weight in peasant superstitions, but... ] Tetsuya's expression falls as he frowns, then rubs his temples and sighs. "Permission to speak bluntly? I fear there's no other way to speak of this custom without having to resort to euphemisms that confuse the point." He may. "It's about infant mortality." Oh. "The custom of not naming your child too soon after birth, that it was bad luck or that it would attract the attention of malign spirits — it originated in ancient times when a newborn surviving was not a sure thing. Whether it was a month, half a year, or even a full year after birth — depending on the province, it was advisable for parents to not get too attached, lest misfortune happen. "It's not surprising that the superstition recommends a whole year on the northern islands where the tengu have their autonomous province — mountainous terrain, harsh climates, poor soil, bleak skies and rough seas. Living in those places is hard, and while they produce hard people, the young are most vulnerable." So Hotaru immediately naming Kaori, despite certainly being aware of such customs and their origins, means she's thumbing her nose at them? A smile. "I prefer to believe it means she has utmost confidence in her daughter's ability to survive. [tetsuya.anyKids |It's the reason I was unafraid to name Setsuna as soon as possible. ] That, and she was already attached to the kit well before birth — it's a little too late for her to keep her distance." Hotaru, keeping her distance. No, such a thing would be impossible of her and her mercurial, burning passions. "As with many customs, though the reasons for such may have faded with time, people still follow them out of a sense of sentiment. The children of this den are well-provided for and Miyuki is adept at seifukujutsu, so there's not much chance of misfortune, but some still cling to their superstitions. Perhaps it's a reminder that while life is comfortable right now, it could take a turn for the worse very, very easily." Kaori[tetsuya.anyKids |, Setsuna ]... you understand now. "[tetsuya.anyKids |We believe in the strength of our children and their |Hotaru believes in the strength of her daughter and her ] will to live, [pc.name]. We refuse to entertain the possibility of misfortune, and hence have no need of customs intended to shield us from loss. I had no opinion on the seamstress prior to this, but her decision to immediately name her child has elevated her in my eyes considerably." ]
rows.translation: [rand |那位裁缝又添了一个女儿，是吧？我早就知道了。”铁也对你露出了一丝苦笑——毫无疑问，他知道你与这件事有关。“自从来到这些殖民地之后，我注意到的一点就是，人们对生孩子这件事的态度显得格外放松。 [tetsuya.anyKids |我本来没料到自己也会卷入其中，但你就出现了，于是我们就这样陷入了这种局面。 ]确实，有传言称，有些人之所以自愿来到这些殖民地，是因为那里对于家庭规模的社会观念要宽松得多。但是，仅仅听说这种现象与亲身体验它是两回事。 在旧国，萤的这种行为肯定会受到人们的鄙视吧？ 听到这里，哲也挠了挠下巴，说道：“嗯……这种行为肯定会被认为是一种不负责任的生育方式，甚至可能会被形容为愚蠢至极。你必须明白[pc.name] ——长期以来，狐族与我们这些受到恩惠的族群之间的比例一直保持稳定。前者的人数不应超过后者，因为恩惠本就应该是一种罕见而令人愉悦的经历。坦白说，这些狐妖并不希望自己的食物资源变得过于充足。 有人不禁皱起了眉头：“没错。正因为如此，无节制地生育幼崽才会受到批评，至少可以说是如此。在殖民地这里情况有所不同，因为这里有大量的施主，但无论如何，如果我们想继续留在这些土地上，未来的几代人也必须达成类似的共识。希望那些旧的习惯和观念还能保留足够多，这样改变过程就不会太痛苦。 “但那其实是未来几代人需要面对的问题。至于萤，她可以随心所欲地做自己想做的事，而且她所承担的后果也会比在另一种情况下轻得多。鸟居她目前似乎对现有的那个很满意，所以我觉得你并没有引发什么难以解决的问题。希望如此。 |说实话，当通过那些——嗯——常规渠道听到萤做了那些事之后，我真的很担心她犯了错。” 哈，有趣的是，像他这样的王子竟然会关心一个裁缝的私事。 哲也摆了摆手，表示不必担心：“你太高看我了。 [pc.name]在殖民地这里，我的权力其实很小。而且，关心自己的邻居也是人之常情——毕竟这里根本不是一个繁华的城市。” “不过，回到正题。当琥珀告诉我这件事的时候，我的第一反应是，她应该从自己的角度重新考虑一下这个情况。她是真的想要一个孩子，还是只是想要那些很少见面的父母的认可？那些将自己对冒险的渴望置于她之前的父母？ 你确实注意到了萤为支持香织所表现出的决心。 “这一点其实不必多说，但准备必要的条件确实很重要，而且这样的决定应该是在所有相关人士都准备妥当之后才做出的，”哲也继续说道，“一方面是要‘延续家族血脉’，另一方面则是如果贸然选择成为父母，就会‘毁掉自己以及自己的后代未来的发展’。 我知道在殖民地，规矩可能会宽松一些，但即便如此，在殖民地的家族中，那些生了很多孩子的家庭也并不多见。因此，就更应该珍惜自己所拥有的那为数不多的机会了——当然，我并不是说在任何情况下忽视这些机会都是可以接受的。 那么，现在情况已经稳定下来，他还会担心萤会犯错吗？ “嗯。”他闲闲地抓起自己的一条尾巴，用手指轻轻抚摸着那柔软的毛发，“还是会有些担心的，尤其是考虑到萤天赋异禀。但当一个人需要肩负另一个生命的命运时，这种情况就是不可避免的。现在她的父母回来了，而且看起来会在未来一段时间内留在这里，你…… 你尽力而为吧，但你在其他地方也有责任要履行。 他苦笑着说道：“我们不都是这样吗？也许真正的考验会出现在当这个新成员带来的新鲜感消退之后，当萤开始和香织一起多年抚养孩子的时候。我想知道，到那时她会不会开始要求再要一个孩子，表面上说是为了她和香织好。但如果你满足了这种女人的要求，她很快就会习惯一直向你提出这样的要求。 |你注意到，萤从女儿出生起就毫不犹豫地给她取名为香织。显然，她早就为这个名字考虑好了，但对于一个热衷于收集古老故事的人来说，她却很快忽略了这个传统。 “她只是对自己的女儿充满信心，而已。不管你说了什么[pc.name]，那种坚定不移的信念，正是我们这位裁缝的典型特点。” 嗯？[tetsuya.anyKids | 其实仔细想想，刹那这个名字也是很快就定下来的。虽然你大概不会认为一个贵族会重视那些农民的迷信，但是…… ] 哲也的脸色顿时阴沉下来，他皱起眉头，揉了揉太阳穴，然后叹了口气。“恕我直言吧……恐怕如果不使用一些会让人误解意思的委婉说法，就无法正确描述这个习俗了。” “确实如此。” “这个习俗与婴儿死亡率有关。 哦。 在孩子出生后不急于给他们取名的这一习俗，人们认为这样做会带来厄运，或者会招致恶灵的注意——这一习俗起源于古代，因为在那个时候，新生儿能否存活下来其实并不是确定的。无论是在孩子出生后一个月、半年，还是整整一年之后，根据不同的地区习俗，父母们都被建议不要过早地对孩子产生深厚的感情，以免招致不幸。 在这种迷信观念的影响下，人们建议在那些属于天狗自治区域的北方岛屿上生活一整年，这也并不奇怪。那些地方地势多山，气候恶劣，土壤贫瘠，天空阴沉，海浪汹涌。生活在这样的环境中非常艰难，虽然这样的环境能造就坚韧的人，但年轻人却最为脆弱。所以，尽管萤肯定了解这些习俗及其起源，但她还是直接叫出了香织的名字，这是否意味着她在蔑视这些习俗呢？ 我选择相信，这其实意味着她对女儿的生存能力充满了信心。 [tetsuya.anyKids |这就是为什么我毫不犹豫地决定尽快为“刹那”这个角色命名。 ]而且，在她出生之前，她就已经与这套装备产生了深厚的感情——现在想要保持距离，已经太晚了。” 萤，保持距离？不，对于她来说，这种事情根本不可能做到，因为她那多变而炽热的感情根本不允许她这样做。 “就像许多习俗一样，虽然这些习俗背后的原因可能已经随着时间的流逝而被人遗忘，但人们仍然出于情感的缘故而遵守它们。这个群体的孩子们得到了很好的照顾，而美雪也非常擅长处理这些事务。秘传武术所以，发生不幸的事情概率其实很小，但仍然有人固执地坚持着他们的迷信。或许，这只是在提醒我们：虽然现在的生活很舒适，但情况也很可能很快变得糟糕起来。[tetsuya.anyKids |，月海 ]……你现在明白了吧。[tetsuya.anyKids |我们相信我们的孩子拥有无穷的力量，他们一定能够…… |萤坚信自己女儿的力量以及她的潜力。 ]生存的意志， [pc.name]我们拒绝接受不幸可能发生这一事实，因此也无需那些旨在保护我们免受损失的风俗习惯。在此之前，我对那位裁缝并没有什么特别的看法，但她决定立即为自己的孩子取名，这一举动让她在我的眼中地位大大提升了。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"The seamstress has a new daughter, does she? I'm aware." Tetsuya quirks a wry smile at you — oh, he knows of your involvement in all this, no doubt. "One of the things I've noticed after arriving in the colonies is the particularly relaxed attitude people have about having children. [tetsuya.anyKids |I didn't expect to get caught up in it myself, but you happened, and here we are. ]It's true, word has it that some willingly come to the colonies because social attitudes about family sizes are considerably more relaxed, but hearing about a phenomenon and experiencing it for myself are two different things." What Hotaru did would have been looked down upon in the Old Country? Tetsuya scratches his chin at that. "Hmm... certainly disapproved of as irresponsible breeding, perhaps even going so far as to have her behavior described as feckless. You must understand, [pc.name] — the proportion of kitsune and our benefactor peoples have remained steady for a long, long time. The former should not be outsized compared to the latter, because beneficence should be an uncommon yet pleasant experience." To put it bluntly, the foxes don't want to outgrow their food supply. A wince. "Yes. Which is why indiscriminately having kits is frowned upon, to say the least. Things are different here in the colonies since benefactors are plentiful, but eventually a similar agreement will have to be reached in the generations to come, if we are to remain in these lands. Hopefully, enough of the old habits and attitudes will remain that it is not too painful. "But that is a problem for future generations. As for Hotaru, she can do as she pleases with considerably less consequence than she would face on the other side of the torii. She seems content with the one for now, so I don't think you've ignited something that'll prove difficult to put out. Hopefully." |"Truth be told, when news of what Hotaru had done reached my ears through the — ahem — usual sources, I was worried that she'd made a mistake." Huh. Interesting that a prince like him would deign to be concerned with the be concerned with a seamstress' personal affairs. Tetsuya waves off the concern. "You give me too much standing, [pc.name]. Here in the colonies, I have little authority. Besides, it's only natural to be concerned for one's neighbors; the tree is not exactly a bustling city. "But back to the point. When Kohaku told me about it, my first thought was that she should have reconsidered the situation from her perspective. Did she want a child, or did she just want the approval of parents she rarely saw? Parents who placed their thirst for adventure over her?" You've noticed Hotaru's determination to be there for Kaori, yes. "This shouldn't need to be said, but having kits is important and that kind of decision should be made when everyone involved is ready," Tetsuya continues. "There's 'continuing your familial lineage', and then there's 'sabotaging yourself and your kits' future by jumping blindly into parenthood'. "I understand things are more lax in the colonies, but even so, those who have many children are not that common even amongst the colonial lineages. All the more reason to make the few chances one has count — not that I'm saying neglect is justified under any circumstances, of course." And does he still worry about Hotaru making a mistake, now that things have settled down? "Hmm." He idly gathers up one of his tails and runs his fingers through the fine fur. "There are still worries, especially considering that Hotaru is gifted, but such is the case when it comes to being responsible for another life. The situation is better now that her parents have returned and look to be staying for the foreseeable future, and you..." You do what you can, but you have duties elsewhere. A wry chuckle. "Don't we all. Perhaps the true test will come when the novelty of the new arrival fades, and Hotaru settles in for years of child-raising with Kaori. I wonder if she'll start demanding another child at that point, ostensibly for both her and Kaori's sakes. Give that kind of vixen what she wants, and she'll quickly learn to keep demanding it from you." |You note that Hotaru wasn't shy about naming Kaori right out of the womb. She'd obviously been thinking of the name for a long time, but for a collector of old tales she was pretty quick to ignore the custom. "She just has confidence in her daughter, that's all. Despite what you said, [pc.name], that kind of unyielding belief is quite characteristic of our seamstress." Hmm?[tetsuya.anyKids | Actually, come to think of it, Setsuna was named pretty quickly, too. Not that you would've expected a nobleman to put any weight in peasant superstitions, but... ] Tetsuya's expression falls as he frowns, then rubs his temples and sighs. "Permission to speak bluntly? I fear there's no other way to speak of this custom without having to resort to euphemisms that confuse the point." He may. "It's about infant mortality." Oh. "The custom of not naming your child too soon after birth, that it was bad luck or that it would attract the attention of malign spirits — it originated in ancient times when a newborn surviving was not a sure thing. Whether it was a month, half a year, or even a full year after birth — depending on the province, it was advisable for parents to not get too attached, lest misfortune happen. "It's not surprising that the superstition recommends a whole year on the northern islands where the tengu have their autonomous province — mountainous terrain, harsh climates, poor soil, bleak skies and rough seas. Living in those places is hard, and while they produce hard people, the young are most vulnerable." So Hotaru immediately naming Kaori, despite certainly being aware of such customs and their origins, means she's thumbing her nose at them? A smile. "I prefer to believe it means she has utmost confidence in her daughter's ability to survive. [tetsuya.anyKids |It's the reason I was unafraid to name Setsuna as soon as possible. ] That, and she was already attached to the kit well before birth — it's a little too late for her to keep her distance." Hotaru, keeping her distance. No, such a thing would be impossible of her and her mercurial, burning passions. "As with many customs, though the reasons for such may have faded with time, people still follow them out of a sense of sentiment. The children of this den are well-provided for and Miyuki is adept at seifukujutsu, so there's not much chance of misfortune, but some still cling to their superstitions. Perhaps it's a reminder that while life is comfortable right now, it could take a turn for the worse very, very easily." Kaori[tetsuya.anyKids |, Setsuna ]... you understand now. "[tetsuya.anyKids |We believe in the strength of our children and their |Hotaru believes in the strength of her daughter and her ] will to live, [pc.name]. We refuse to entertain the possibility of misfortune, and hence have no need of customs intended to shield us from loss. I had no opinion on the seamstress prior to this, but her decision to immediately name her child has elevated her in my eyes considerably." ] "

rows.original: [tetsuya.isLover |"The local seamstress, is it? Fortuitous that you should bring her up — we ought to talk, [pc.name]." Oh, Tetsuya's using his important business voice, heh. And given the subject, you have a good guess of what's got him so worked up. Maybe it was a bit mean to sic Hotaru on him while you're lovers and he can be a bit of a stick in the mud about these things... but you wouldn't have him any other way. It's about Hotaru, isn't it? He raises an eyebrow. "You know?" The den isn't exactly a large place when it comes to its more permanent residents. Word gets around when one has two dedicated gossips on the job, and one of them is actually involved in the matter herself.. "Then that saves a lot of uncomfortable explanation." As cute as it would've been to watch him [pc.isDK |squirm |get all self-conscious ] while trying to broach the subject, there's no need to retread what you're already aware of. "I... was a little worried at how you might take the news. Everything was rather strong and sudden, and I feel like I've been swept up — not entirely against my will, but enough to be caught up in it. Hotaru's passion is very... genuine." Look, you haven't [pc.ra kitsune |been a kitsune |been around the kitsune ] for that long, but you're pretty sure someone of Tetsuya's station should be familiar with the idea of concubines. [rindo.isConcubine |For the sake of all the Seven, Rindo is your concubine, for crying out loud. ] "I am. I just wanted to be sure that you don't disapprove of any such liaison, [pc.name]. You may have different expectations, feel differently; I don't presume to —" You wave off Tetsuya's words. Come now, what does he think the Marches is full of, prudes? No doubt he's sampled the local benefactors from time to time. Still... you're glad that he thought to ask. No, knowing the kitsune, you're not going to guard him that jealously. If he thinks there's something genuine between him and Hotaru, he's welcome to take the seamstress as a concubine, if it comes to that. Of course, there's the fact that you set up this whole situation to begin with... but you're not about to let Tetsuya in on that secret. Tetsuya heaves a sigh of relief. "Thank you, [pc.name]. Hotaru's very... earnest. There's no doubt that she's very genuine in her affection, but I couldn't help but worry that I was doing wrong by you somehow." [rindo.isConcubine |When you took Rindo as your concubine, you were obliged to quickly learn how concubinage works amongst the kitsune. If you were to object to a similar situation arising between Tetsuya and Hotaru, that'd make you a terrible hypocrite, wouldn't it? |Look, while you're glad that Tetsuya's been keeping you and your feelings in mind, you'd be silly to get mad. ] The kitsune have pretty well-established rules around concubinage and its various situations; since you're [pc.ra kitsune |one now |amongst them ], you might as well follow customs meant to ease and avoid frictions. To put it simply, he needn't worry. You know how foxes are at speaking in roundabout ways, so you'll be as explicit as possible in hopes of driving home the point. "Then that puts that matter at rest, then. Don't worry, [pc.name] — I'll make sure that any side dalliances don't intrude on what we have together, as eager as Hotaru may be. That is, unless you wish to extend any invitations... but that's a matter for another time." |"The local seamstress, is it? I suppose you heard about it — the colonies are relatively small, and hearsay travels fast." Yes, you did. And yes, hearsay travels fast, especially when one of the gossipmongers is personally involved in the matter and wants to show off her achievements. "Achievements." Tetsuya quirks a smile. "I suppose that's one way to put it. A common seamstress catching the eye of an unattached prince with her passions — I knew Hotaru was a storyteller, but not her intentions of making such tales real." On a more serious note, congratulations. "It's a little too soon for that, [pc.name]. Nevertheless, the thought is appreciated. Hotaru has a directness that few of our kind have. Everything was rather strong and sudden, and I feel like I've been swept up — not entirely against my will, but enough to be caught up in it. Hotaru's passion is very... genuine." ]
rows.translation: [tetsuya.isLover |是那位当地的裁缝吧？你提到她真是太巧了——我们确实需要谈谈。 [pc.name]哦，哲也又在用他那严肃的商务语气说话了，呵呵。考虑到讨论的主题，你应该能猜到是什么让他这么激动吧。也许在你们还是恋人的时候让萤去针对他，确实有点过分了，而他在这种事情上确实会比较固执己见…… 但除此之外，你也不会得到他的帮助。 这件事和萤有关，对吧？ 他挑了挑眉毛：“你都知道了？” 对于那些长期居住在这里的人来说，这个巢穴其实并不是一个很大的地方。当一个人在工作中有两位热衷于传播八卦的人，而其中一位实际上还与这件事有关时，消息很快就会传开…… “这样就省去了许多尴尬的解释了。” 虽然看着他那样做肯定很有趣[pc.isDK |扭动身体 |变得非常不自在 ]在尝试谈论这个话题时，没有必要再重复那些你已经知道的事情。 “我……有点担心你会如何接受这个消息。这一切发生得太突然、太激烈了，我感觉自己被卷入了其中——虽然不是完全违背我的意愿，但确实被牵扯了进去。萤的热情是真的很……真挚。” 听着，你并没有[pc.ra kitsune |变成了一只狐狸 |见多识广 ]为了那个虽然过程有些漫长，但你应该可以确定，铁也所在部门里肯定有人了解妾室这种制度。 [rindo.isConcubine |为了所有七位的存在，林多你的妾室啊，真是的。 ] 我是这样的。我只是想确认你不会反对这样的联系罢了。 [pc.name]你的期望可能各不相同，感受也可能不一样；我不敢妄加揣测……” 你摆了摆手，表示不打算理会哲也的话。说真的，他到底以为这些边境地区都是些什么地方啊，难道都是些古板守旧的人吗？毫无疑问，他肯定也偶尔和那些当地的富商们有过来往吧。不过……你还是为他想到了要问这个问题而感到高兴吧。其实，以你的了解，他也不会那么吃醋地保护她的。如果他真的认为自己和萤之间有着某种真挚的感情，那么就算要娶那位缝纫女为妾，你也不会反对的。 当然，你从一开始就策划了这一切……但你肯定不会把这个秘密告诉哲也。 哲也松了一口气：“谢谢你。 [pc.name]萤真的……非常认真。毫无疑问，她的感情是真挚的，但我还是忍不住担心，自己会不会在某种程度上伤害了你。 [rindo.isConcubine |当你将凛堂收为妾室时，你就必须尽快了解狐族中妾室制度的运作方式。如果你反对哲也和萤之间出现类似的情况，那你就是个十足的伪君子，不是吗？ |你看，虽然你很高兴哲也一直在关心你和你的感受，但生气的话就太傻了。 ]狐妖一族对于纳妾以及与之相关的各种情况有着相当明确的规定；既然你[pc.ra kitsune |马上就好 |其中 ]你不妨遵守那些旨在减少摩擦、避免矛盾的习俗。 简单来说，他不必担心。你知道狐妖们总是喜欢拐弯抹角地说话，所以我会尽量直截了当地表达，以便把意思讲清楚。 “那么，这件事就解决了。别担心了。 [pc.name]我会确保任何旁枝末节都不会影响到我们之间的关系，无论萤有多么渴望参与其中。当然，除非你愿意邀请她加入……不过这个话题可以留到以后再讨论。 |是那位当地的裁缝吧？我想你们应该已经听说了——这些殖民地规模都比较小，所以流言传得也很快。” 是的，我们确实听说了。而且，流言确实传得很快，尤其是当那些爱传闲话的人本身就与这件事有关的时候。以及她想炫耀自己的成就。 “成就啊……”铁也苦笑着说道，“这么说倒也确实。一个普通的缝纫女，凭借自己的热情吸引了单身王子的注意——我早就知道萤是个喜欢讲故事的人，但没想到她真的会把这些故事变成现实。” 说正经的，恭喜你。 “现在这么说还有点早吧[pc.name]尽管如此，我还是很感激这个想法。萤拥有我们这类人中少有的直率。一切都发生得如此突然且激烈，让我感到自己被卷了进去——虽然并非完全违背我的意愿，但确实让我无法置身事外。萤的热情是如此……真挚。 ]

rows.original:
There is one thing, though. He doesn't think that Hotaru came on a bit too strongly? You know Tetsuya dislikes arranged relationships, prefers to sail his own ship, that sort of thing. Hotaru doesn't have any ulterior motive here, does she?
        
        "Do you suspect she does?"
        
        Her actions... well, coming from anyone else, they would be suspicious. But Hotaru...
        
        "...Is the mercurial kind," Tetsuya finishes. "You're right, [pc.name]. Coming from anyone else, I would've suspected something more and declined her advances. But coming from her... it's fast and impulsive, but I don't sense any duplicity — and trust me, my senses for such are quite keenly honed. And it's not as fast as you might think — I'm aware of how Hotaru's been looking at me for some time, and the resulting moods she's had. Honestly, I think [tetsuya.isLover
            |me being with you caused her to consider me 'taken'
            |the difference in our stations stayed her hand a while
        ], although I see she's finally gotten over herself and decided to make a move.
        
        "Now, I'm urging her to slow down and consider her next steps before escalating further — and to my surprise, it's working."
        
        That's great — Tetsuya doesn't suspect your hand in siccing Hotaru on him. Or if he does — which is perfectly possible, cheeky inscrutable ruffian that he is — he's not letting it slip. Which suits you just fine either way.
rows.translation:
不过有件事……他觉得萤的行为有点太急切了，不是吗？你知道，哲也并不喜欢包办婚姻，他更喜欢自己掌控自己的生活，就是这种性格。萤这次应该没有别的目的吧？
        
        “你怀疑她有别的目的吗？”
        
        她的行为……嗯，如果换作别人，肯定会让人起疑。但萤……
        
        “……她就是那种情绪多变的人，”哲也接着说道，“你说得对。 [pc.name]如果这是别人提出的，我可能会多想一些，然后拒绝她的追求。但如果是她……虽然她的行动很迅速、很冲动，但我没有感觉到任何虚伪之处——相信我，我在这类事情上可是有着相当敏锐的直觉的。而且，她的行动并没有你想象中那么快；我早就注意到萤一直都在注视着我，也知道这让她产生了什么样的情绪。说实话，我觉得[tetsuya.isLover
            |我和你在一起，让她觉得我“已经有对象了”。
            |我们立场上的差异让她暂时保持了沉默。
        ]虽然我看她终于不再那么固执己见了，决定采取行动了。
        
        “现在，我正在劝她放慢脚步，在进一步行动之前仔细考虑下一步该怎么做——令我惊讶的是，这种方法居然有效。”
        
        那太好了——哲也根本没怀疑是你指使萤针对他的。或者说，就算他怀疑了——毕竟他是个狡猾又难以捉摸的家伙——他也没有表现出来。不管怎样，这对你来说都是好事。
rows.raw:
"
        There is one thing, though. He doesn't think that Hotaru came on a bit too strongly? You know Tetsuya dislikes arranged relationships, prefers to sail his own ship, that sort of thing. Hotaru doesn't have any ulterior motive here, does she?
        
        "Do you suspect she does?"
        
        Her actions... well, coming from anyone else, they would be suspicious. But Hotaru...
        
        "...Is the mercurial kind," Tetsuya finishes. "You're right, [pc.name]. Coming from anyone else, I would've suspected something more and declined her advances. But coming from her... it's fast and impulsive, but I don't sense any duplicity — and trust me, my senses for such are quite keenly honed. And it's not as fast as you might think — I'm aware of how Hotaru's been looking at me for some time, and the resulting moods she's had. Honestly, I think [tetsuya.isLover
            |me being with you caused her to consider me 'taken'
            |the difference in our stations stayed her hand a while
        ], although I see she's finally gotten over herself and decided to make a move.
        
        "Now, I'm urging her to slow down and consider her next steps before escalating further — and to my surprise, it's working."
        
        That's great — Tetsuya doesn't suspect your hand in siccing Hotaru on him. Or if he does — which is perfectly possible, cheeky inscrutable ruffian that he is — he's not letting it slip. Which suits you just fine either way.
        "

rows.original: [rand |You know, now that you think about it, Tetsuya looks [flags.KEROS_MET |a lot like |vaguely similar to the general depiction of ] Keros. Not just his long, white hair, but his lean physique as well! Of course, while the man in front of you doesn't have the other things, like the Trickster's iconic number of tails or his red eyes, the similarities are there. With this in mind, does [tetsuya.isLover |your beloved |he ] get mistaken for Keros? [tetsuya.anyKids |Your silver fox |Tetsuya ] presses his index finger knuckle against his lips and smirks. "[tetsuya.isAcquaintance |It depends on whom you speak to, does it not? Back home, amidst my fellow kindred and peers, such assumptions were not oft-made, but I would be lying if I said the parallel was ne'er mentioned |It's happened. Not as much in the Old Country, but it happens — perhaps even more so, now that I'm far from my ancestral home ]. I can understand where the confusion comes from. Out of all the divine spirits, the August Master meddles the most in our mortal affairs, so the notion is not an unfounded one. [tetsuya.isAcquaintance |Verily, I share a passing resemblance to [pc.ra kitsune |our divine master |the trickster god ] and I am well versed in this fact |But yes, I know I look like [silly |that goofy fucker |our buddy, Keros ] ]." At least he admits it. That just leaves the question of why. "[tetsuya.isAcquaintance |The reason is because he and I are related. Distantly related |It's because he's a relative — distant relative ]." Tetsuya taps his pipe before idly inspecting it. "Matriarch Arisu Oja, otherwise known as the Lady of Jewels, was the fourth concubine of the August Master. As a descendent of this vaunted union, it[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | is |'s ] only fair to assume I[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | would bear a passing resemblance to him |'d look like them to some extent ]. Of course, [silly |every day, we stray further from god |as we go from generation to generation, we stray further from our divine ancestry. Furthermore, such features [tetsuya.isAcquaintance |are ne'er certain to |could simply never ] appear; conversely, they could manifest on a kit whose royal family showed no signs for entire generations ]." Interesting. So that's why he has gold eyes, instead of red, then. To which, he agrees back with an affirmative hum. |It's odd to see someone like him so far from home. If you took Tetsuya and put him beside a good majority of the den, he'd stand out like a sore thumb. So, the question on your mind is: why'd he become a runaway prince? "The decision to leave my homeland was mine to make; the inciting incident which led to my decision, however, was not. I travel because, deep down, [tetsuya.truth |I sought some cathartic liberation |there[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | is an appetency |'s a fascination ] to witness the world's scenic vistas firsthand. Experiencing everything life has to offer is why I walk[tetsuya.isLover |ed ] the horizons ]. Why do you ask?" If anything — curiosity and the desire to learn more about him. He's a genuine article, Old Country dignitary and he's here with farmers. With that in mind, perhaps he could offer his perspective as a prince of [pc.ra kitsune |a divine clan |one of their divine clans ] for a matter regarding the colonies. "I see no harm in that. Ask away." Despite some of the colonists' [pc.swornGod keros |reservations toward you, most of the people here generally venerate you [pc.isDK |with the respect that you deserve. This isn't some outlandish or conceited claim either; you're literally the chosen servant of your patron deity and you've been actively making sure that this tree doesn't burn down to the ground, but you digress |as the chosen servant of Keros ]. Along the way, you've come to understand |cautious xenophobia toward outsiders, you've come to see ] their way of life and acquainted yourself with the many eccentric figures of the den. However, therein lies a commonality amongst this eclectic community: everyone here is a colonial. [tetsuya.isAcquaintance |Tetsuya gives you an affirmative hum, but wordlessly |"Which itself bears an odious preconception to one's character in the eyes of the Old Country," Tetsuya adds. He then gestures and ] lets you continue. While most of the denizens here are just descendants of the original diasporas, there's still individuals like Kazuo, Rindo, or even the shrine sisters who stand out due to some social stigma which ultimately led to them finding their way here. There's more about this; point is, there's the connotations that come with being a colonial and you're curious as to what kind of sentiment or bias Tetsuya holds — if he holds a personal preference between his homeland or the colony. "I love my home and I love my people, but I doubt I could form a bias over one or the other. While it [tetsuya.isAcquaintance | is |'s ] good to have an sturdy mind, a wall is only good if you[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | are |'re ] trying to defend something. [tetsuya.isLover |Staying here with you, however, is my sacrosanct hill to die upon. As for my impression of the colony |All I know is ], when I passed [tetsuya.isAcquaintance |the threshold of the torii gate |through that gate ], I was enthralled by the pastoral beauty before me[tetsuya.isLover |. This was a brave new world filled with wondrous vistas to be seen and tales to be made. But, in forging my own destiny in this strange land, I beheld the greatest and most beautiful sight of all — you |, but if there ever comes a time when my heart yearns to see its ancestral home once again, I can return at my own convenience ]." ]

rows.original: "M[silly |oi |e ]?" Tetsuya presses the tips of his fingers against his chest. "[tetsuya.isLover |I'm charmed! |I would be glad to. ] What would you like to know?" That's the thing, you don't know much about him as a person. Perhaps he could [pc.isCunning |elucidate who he is to you |tell you a little about himself ]. "Well," he rubs his chin, "starting from the beginning, my sister and I were born as twins to a noble family in the Old Country. Between the two of us, I[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | am |'m ] the eldest sibling, but only by the technicality of a five minute difference. My fair sister was always a stubborn lady; it[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | is |'s ] something I enjoyed holding over her. That said, Natsumi was the firstborn daughter, so it presupposes her to inherit the position of Den Mother over the Oja clan and its constituent prefectures." You inquire if it's within the realm of possibility to eventually meet his twin sister. Tetsuya crosses his arms and shrugs nonchalantly. "There[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | is |'s ] always the possibility that Natsumi visits me; is it likely? No." Bummer. "She[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | is |'s ] a busy woman with a lot on her plate back home, but I know she cares about my well-being. Regardless, let us get back to the topic at hand." He continues. "In my younger years, loath am I to admit it, I was quite the obstinate child." Him — a brat?! [pc.isCunning |Extraordinary claims demand extraordinary proof[silly |, fuccboi ] |You can't see it ]. "[tetsuya.isAcquaintance |There are stranger truths out there. |It's true! ] I was a free-spirited child; mayhaps it was sibling influence or defiance in light of the expectations placed upon me. But over the years, I finally settled down and devoted myself to the many political and cultural studies befitting my station. Granted, in comparison to my sister, my obligations were much more lax; thus, I had the free time to explore my options. This is how I got into the arts of calligraphy and sightseeing. However, while I was good with a brush and given a keen eye for details, I cannot paint a picture for the life of me, even though it[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | is something I would like to become proficient |'s something I'd like to get good ] at in the foreseeable future." It can't be that bad, right? "Oh, I assure you, it is." He sounds so confident in that fact. You'd think his skills with a brush would carry over. Guess that isn't always the case. That said, he must surely have some saucy tales to tell of his failures. Tetsuya clicks his tongue. "Yes. More than just artistic pursuits, too. I can [tetsuya.isAcquaintance |recount some examples if you so wish |tell you some of them if you'd like ]." You'd like that. Lay it all out, [tetsuya.isLover |dear |pal ]. You have time to spare. [tetsuya.isAcquaintance |"I suppose it cannot be helped," the white kitsune says, taking a drink from his tea cup. The man then sets his drink down, reshifts his seated position, and clasps his hands together on his lap. |Tetsuya lowers his head, shrugs with his palms up, and laughs. "Guess I'm monologuing now." ] You and he go over his many misadventures in all their humorous and humiliating light.
rows.translation: M[silly |喂 |e ]？”哲也用指尖轻按着自己的胸口。[tetsuya.isLover |我被迷住了！ |我很乐意帮忙。 ]你想知道些什么呢？” 问题就在于，你对他的为人了解得并不多。也许他能够[pc.isCunning |向你说明他到底是谁。 |让我简单介绍一下他本人吧。 ]嗯，”他摸了摸下巴，“从头说起吧。我和我的妹妹是老国一个贵族家庭的双胞胎。我们两个[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | 是 |m ]我是家中的长子，只不过仅仅因为出生时间相差五分钟而已。我那位温柔的妹妹，一直以来都是个固执的人[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | 是 |的 ]这是我特别喜欢的一点。不过，夏美其实是家中的长女。女儿因此，这意味着她将继承Den Mother的地位，领导Oja氏族及其所属的各个领地。 你询问是否有可能最终见到他的双胞胎妹妹。 哲也双臂交叉，漫不经心地耸了耸肩：“那谁知道呢[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | 是 |的 ]总是有可能 Natsumi 会来看我吧？不过这种可能性有多大呢？应该不大吧。” 真可惜。 “她[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | 是 |的 ]在家里，她是个忙于各种事务的女性，责任重重，但我知道她很关心我的状况。无论如何，让我们回到正题上来。”他继续说道，“在我年轻的时候，虽然很不愿意承认，但我确实是个相当固执的孩子。” 他——一个任性的孩子？！ [pc.isCunning |非凡的主张需要非凡的证据来支撑。[silly |， 讨厌鬼 ] |你看不见它 ]。 "[tetsuya.isAcquaintance |这个世界上确实存在一些令人难以置信的真相。 |确实如此！ ]我曾经是一个性格自由奔放的孩子；或许这是受到兄弟姐妹的影响，又或许是因为我想反抗人们对我的种种期望。但随着时间的推移，我最终还是安定下来，开始致力于那些与我的身份地位相称的政治和文化研究。诚然，与我的姐姐相比，我的责任要宽松得多；因此，我有足够的时间去探索自己的兴趣所在。正是这样，我开始接触书法和观轻型旅行这些活动。不过，虽然我使用毛笔的技术还算不错，也对细节有着敏锐的观察力，但我却无论如何也画不出一幅像样的画来[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | 这是我希望能够掌握的技能。 |这是我想掌握的一项技能。 ]在可预见的未来，这是不可能的。那个糟糕，对吧？” “哦，我向你保证，确实如此。” 他说这话时显得非常自信。你可能会觉得，他在绘画方面的技巧应该也能应用到其他方面吧。不过，事实似乎并不总是如此。不过，他肯定有一些关于自己失败经历的有趣故事可以讲吧。 哲也咂了咂舌头：“没错。而且不仅仅是艺术方面的经历，还有很多其他的事情呢。 [tetsuya.isAcquaintance |如果你愿意，可以举一些例子来说明。 |如果你愿意的话，我可以告诉你其中的一些。 ]你肯定想要这样的。把一切都摊开来说吧。 [tetsuya.isLover |亲爱的 |朋友 ]你有空闲的时间。 [tetsuya.isAcquaintance |我想也没办法了，”那只白色的狐妖一边说，一边从茶杯中喝了一口茶。然后，那个男人把茶杯放下，调整了一下坐姿，双手交叠放在膝盖上。 |哲也低下头，双手一摊耸了耸肩，然后笑了起来：“看来现在我是在自说自话了。 ] 你们一起回顾了他那些充满幽默与尴尬的种种冒险经历。

[miko.anyKids |Perhaps even more so lately, on account for her having two extra mouths to feed. ]Her over-developed form is a clear reflection of this ceaseless consumption. [mai.sober |Miyuki, on the other hand," Tetsuya stops, puts on a wry smile, and lets out an audible chuff, "right." Holding his expression, [tetsuya.married |your fox-husband |the fox-man ] clicks his tongue and says, "Guess 'calm' is no longer applicable here, now is it?" There's many words you could use to describe Mai, but yes, calm is certainly not one of them. In comparison to how utterly impassive she once was, Mai feels like a completely different woman now. Without the dulling succor of her winterstem, which Mai heavily relied upon to subdue her hyperactive senses, it's like a shell has been cracked open, unleashing everything that was trapped underneath. Having the front row seat, you've seen the full, unfiltered range of her emotions and how intense they can get if they're left unchecked. In the long run, however, kicking the habit might be ultimately best for Mai's health; also, seeing her react in new and interesting ways has been fun. Still, for her to g[silly |o cold turkey |et cut off ] like that, while she[mai.pregStage 0 1 | was carrying your child, it must've been |'s carrying your child, it has to be ] rough on her. "I couldn't put it better myself," Tetsuya remarks, "and lo, I knew this possibility would come about sooner or later. Though, perhaps it's not as unwelcome as I initially thought. I won't opine on Miyuki's behalf, as I'm just an observer with no personal experience to draw upon; I will, however, declare both my sympathy and my envy for the shrine maiden. This is clearly a troubling time for Miyuki and such things are meant to be handled over a period of time. For her to endure in the face of the conditions posed against her is a true testament to her willpower and training. I trust she'll be a good mother." Tetsuya rests his chin against his palm and sighs. "What I wouldn't give to see the world through her eyes." Considering Mai's current predicament, you're inclined to believe she'd take that proposal in stride if it means she can dump her hyperactive senses onto him. While that'd be great for her, what about him? If that happend, you'd never get him to shut up! He gives you a rakish grin and says, "Me not shutting up is part of my charm[tetsuya.isLover |, dear ]. [kohaku.anyKids
        |[rand
            |Hmm, you've been meaning to ask, since he's a fellow traveler and all: does Tetsuya feel sad that Kohaku's looking to wind down her caravaning away from the den and pass the proverbial torch to someone else?
            
            "Oh, of course not. I've spoken with her on the matter and found that we have much in agreement. I did not travel for its own sake, but towards a purpose; it was a means to an end, not an end in itself.[tetsuya.isLover
                | Now that I've achieved that end, while I am not averse to the prospect of some more traveling, neither am I discontent without it.
            ]
            
            "It does pose the wider question: why do we do what we do? Are they an ends in themselves, or merely a means to an end? Will our actions ultimately be something meaningful to ourselves and others, or will we regret chasing something that was ultimately empty despite the transient pleasures the pursuit offered? Kohaku has thought about it and made that decision; I certainly do not find fault with her reasoning and if I am unhappy, it is from a place of reactionary emotionalism."
            
            She is quite young, though...
            
            Tetsuya slowly shakes his head. "I understand that is is customary for [pc.ra kitsune
                |leaders in this part of the world
                |your leaders
            ] to hold their positions until death or violent displacement, and peaceful abdications are rare and newsworthy events. However, consider this: in my homeland, the emperor is expected to abdicate perhaps in his mid-forties and ascend to the mountains to live a life of spiritual solitude away from worldly matters and be close to his divine ancestors. For someone who might live in extreme cases to be a venerable two hundred, that is a very early retirement."
            
            Yes, but Kohaku isn't the fox emperor.
            
            Tetsuya holds up a hand. "Please, allow me to continue. While the practice was attributed to the shoguns not wanting an emperor who could rival them and pose a political threat, it in truth began long before the shogunate came into being; they merely encouraged the practice. Is it better to abdicate early while your position is secure and you are at the height of your power, to help your successor and lend your assistance and connections, or hold on grimly to your title until the last and leave your successor bereft of the advantages?
            
            "Our historians generally agree that the early retirements of the emperors allowed for the smooth transition of power from one generation to the next, which in turn was a contributing factor to why our monarchial line is the longest unbroken one in the entire world. It helps when you have three to four retired emperors backing you up."
            |About the whole not-naming-your-newborn thing...
            
            "Yes?"
            
            It feels a little sad. Kohaku obviously loves her newborn daughter very much, but doesn't have the confidence to give her a name yet. You wish you could do something about it, but this feels like one of the things which she has to ultimately work out on her own; all you can do is to be close and distract her mind with other matters while the situation resolves itself.
            
            Tetsuya reaches [pc.heightRange 72
                |up
                |over
            ] and gives you a gentle pat on the back. "Sometimes it is the best thing we can do; sometimes it is the only thing we can do. The custom is actually more prevalent amongst the tanuki, who because of their sheer propensity to multiply tend to encounter such unfortunate incidents more often than the other peoples of my homeland. If you have more children, the numbers simply work out that you will see more infant mortality."
            
            [tetsuya.anyKids
                |He named Setsuna immediately, though.
                
                "Yes. Again, remember why the custom exists — those of my social class have had the benefit of the best care for our newborns that is available, so infant mortality is not prevalent to the point where we need to distance ourselves from our sons and daughters lest they leave us early and we must dull the pain. But not everyone has such fortune, despite efforts by servants of the gods to bring easier care to more people... and even in some places where the problem has been alleviated to some degree, ancestral memories linger, especially painful ones. Understandably, people are reluctant to be hurt.
                |It's just a bitter pill to swallow.[pc.raMulti barbarian slumrat
                    | Your tribe may have been scattered to the winds when you were young, but for it to happen enough that people have come up with a way to cope with it...
                    | Sure, you may have had a tough existence on the streets while you were younger, but this is something else altogether.
                ]
            ]
            
            "The world is filled with multiple little tragedies that would overwhelm us with grief if we dwelled on them, [pc.name]." Tetsuya's voice is calm and reassuring. "Kohaku remains warm and cheerful, even as she unthinkingly guards herself against pain... there is much to be learned there."
            |"Given that she has been running this imperial colony for five generations now, the den matron has had to keep a keen eye on the local demographics. She tells me she's come to expect a cycle of expansion from organic growth and those banished here, stabilization, and occasional contraction because of various reasons." Tetsuya looks thoughtful. "I'm simply glad that I don't need to worry myself with such matters, and can simply enjoy the fruits of other peoples' labor."
            
            Like Kohaku's?
            
            [tetsuya.anyKids
                |"And yours, of course
                |"Yes
            ]. And speaking of Kohaku, she is a useful indicator of the general social trends of this community. The den matron is expecting a general if gradual increase in the local population over the next decade or so before the inevitable stabilization phase, and has planned accordingly."
            
            But... surely he doesn't think that Kohaku had a daughter for the sake of fitting in, right?
            
            "Not solely, no. As with everything we do, I have little doubt that there were multiple causative factors... but given what I know of the situation from speaking with Mikoto, it would account for a hefty chunk of her motivations, yes." Shrugging, Tetsuya gives you a good-natured smile. "I don't think it's a problem in and of itself, so long as it turns out well in the end. Both Miko and I end up being able to play with and spoil a dubious little creature whose indiscretions we can safely leave her mother to deal with later, so I count this as a win."
            |What does he think of Kohaku's proposal to Komari to have the position of storehouse quartermaster to be heritable by her daughter?
            
            Tetsuya thins his lips and shakes his head at that. "Dangerous. I understand that Kohaku doesn't have any ill intentions behind the proposal, but intentions count for little when the dangers are very real."
            
            Dangerous? How so? You can understand that it might be unwise given that the child doesn't even have a name yet, so her claims of being able to infer aptitude are far-fetched at best, but dangerous?
            
            "Back across the ocean, low to middling-status positions in the civil service are open to any kitsune or tanuki who can outpace the competition in the placement examinations. The concept should not be alien to you — my cursory investigation into local political structures has revealed a plethora of minor functionary and dignitary titles a ruling authority may bestow upon an individual that are indeed not hereditary.
            
            "Of course, there are no civil service examinations in the colonies, but the den matron assigns positions as her judgement befits; there is an implicit trust that she will be wise and fair in this decision-making. There's some degree of hope that if one is diligent and faithful, one may also rise to the permitted degree in the local hierarchy, an effort which has borne fruit according to the colony records."
            
            You see where this is going. Allowing Kohaku's daughter to inherit the position directly as if it were some kind of family business would jeopardize not just the trust in the system, but also people's morale. You imagine that some of Kohaku's subordinates have their hearts set on being storehouse manager someday, and being told that they would be bench-warmers at best while her daughter came of age would be terribly dispiriting.
            
            "Much of how our society works is based on a lot of implicit trust. Deviating from the way things have been done to appease an individual's desires by holding down others unsurprisingly causes discontent. Kohaku is an excellent functionary, but she is not so vital as to be able to request that so many others sacrifice for her... on my part, I am sure that it will be a struggle to peaceably talk her out of this dangerous foolishness. How did the saying go? That the evil may rest, but the well-intentioned are relentless in their do-gooding? She may want to secure a better life for her daughter than what she had for herself, but in that case her daughter needs to prove her aptitude against all other candidates."
        ]
        |[kohaku.pregStage 1
            |[rand
                |"I frankly feel that concern over how Kohaku's indisposed nature might affect current supply is quite overblown; there's absolutely no need to worry about it." Tetsuya acknowledges the question with a nod. "That there's concern is good, but worries need to be rooted in reality or they can easily spin out of control. I have reviewed the matter with my own eyes, and there are multiple fallbacks and redundancies should something go awry: the self-sufficiency of the den, Kohaku's subordinates being able to caravan in her stead, the fact that most imports are luxuries, and more. If it comes to it, I could even use what influence I have to change things for the better, since I am still considered in good standing..."
                
                So, he's saying that she should relax and just enjoy the ride instead of being worried about her job?
                
                "Indeed. One of the harder lessons I've had to learn in my time is that few people are truly irreplaceable; even a prince like me appears to be scarcely missed in his homeland these days. Blunt as it may be, Kohaku is not the only one who is capable of performing her tasks; if she were, that would be a problem for the future even if the issue were not pressed now. Her inability to caravan at the moment should be seen as an opportunity, not a liability; perhaps it is my optimistic nature speaking here."
                |"I suppose this end was inevitable, was it not? From what I understand, there has been a surge of popularity in the local womenfolk desiring to bear kits in recent years — Komari informs me that the trend has lasted about seven years or so at this point. For someone as keenly attuned to the social mood as Kohaku is, coupled with her desire to fit in, this was in a way unavoidable."
                
                Was it? You feel like that's oversimplifying it a little.
                
                Tetsuya gives you an enigmatic smile. "Is it?"
                
                It feels like there should be more, that's all...
                
                "Sometimes the simplest answers are those which hold the most truth, [pc.name]. Komari tells me that a good number of those who came with her in the first generation consisted of foxes who were unhappy enough with the strict, if understandable social customs on family size. I suppose they were misfits in this sense... but it only stands to reason that the sentiment would have prevailed in some fashion, especially in a sense most of my peers would consider extreme and unreasonable. The imperial colony's population goes through swells and ebbs over time, I'm told — constant increase is a fool's errand, according to the den matron, and only a tumor grows for its own sake.
                
                "But it does feel like we're in the midst of another rising trend — one which the den matron has attempted to account for, and which poor little Kohaku has found herself swept up by. I am not entirely sure her decision was a conscious one, but just as a school of fish swim with one mind despite being comprised of many individuals, so does she respond to those around her. It seems to have worked out well for her, so I'm not surprised that she persists."
                |"I will admit, there's a certain amusement to be found in teasing poor Kohaku while she's moody," Tetsuya says with a chuckle. "I don't even have to do anything."
                
                Oh? How does he go about it?
                
                "Like I said: I simply don't do anything. It's obvious when she's trying to get emotional reactions out of people around her, so I just answer all her queries politely, calmly and directly. The failure to provoke an emotional response infuriates her all the more, and she tries harder; it's in this fashion that the cycle escalates until she can't hold it in any more and the fireworks begin. Consider it akin to holding up a mirror in front of an animal and watching it grow more and more irate at its own reflection — hence, the humor to be found in the situation."
                
                That seems a little cruel.
                
                "I would call it a self-inflicted wound; being unhappy is no excuse for you spreading it to others. Perhaps sufficient correction will suffice to straighten out this behavior instead of allowing her to infect others with her moodiness. Harsh, but in some cases it is the only thing that works. In the meantime, I can find some small amusement in watching Kohaku being driven to tears by her own actions — perhaps I would tell her to stop hitting herself, but that might be pushing the envelope a little too far."
                |"Kohaku approached me a little while ago and asked if I could use my arts to send her parents a message," Tetsuya tells you with a thoughtful expression on his face. "She wished to inform them of their incipient grandchild. I had to regret to inform her that such a thing was not possible."
                
                Ouch. That couldn't have been easy on her.
                
                A nod. "More than one would immediately think. In order for the crane to find its intended recipient, the sender must share some degree of mutual sympathy, familiarity, whatever you wish to call it. Not that it is well-quantified, partly because of the symbolic nature of this requirement, but it exists nonetheless. To press home the point, I attempted it twice for Kohaku, and after that she was forced to admit that it would not work."
                
                Yes... you can easily see how that would have been hard.
                
                Tetsuya's smile is carefully apologetic. "I've heard the story as it goes in the local gossip. I'm sure they did love their daughter very much, but at the same time loved the thrill of the search even more to give it up. Given their behavior towards Kohaku in the last decade and change, I don't think that receiving news of a grandchild would change the situation to any noticeable degree."

[kohaku.anyKids
        |[rand
            |嗯，你其实一直想问这个吧——既然他们都是同行者，那么哲也会不会因为小白打算结束自己的游牧生活，把这份责任传给别人而感到难过呢？

“哦，当然不会。我就这个话题和她谈过，发现我们的想法很一致。我旅行并不是为了旅行本身，而是为了某个目标；旅行只是达到那个目标的手段，而不是目的本身。[tetsuya.isLover
                | 既然我已经实现了这个目标，虽然我并不排斥继续旅行的可能性，但也没有因为没有旅行而感到不满。
            ]
            
            这确实引出了一个更广泛的问题：我们为什么要做我们现在正在做的事情？这些行为本身是目的，还是仅仅达到某种目的的手段？我们的行动最终是否会对自己和他人都有意义，还是我们会后悔追求那些虽然能带来短暂的快乐，但最终却毫无意义的东西？小白经过深思熟虑后做出了那个决定；我确实认为她的理由没有任何问题，如果我感到不满，那也只是出于一种消极的情绪反应罢了。

不过，她毕竟还很年轻。哲也缓缓摇了摇头。“我明白，这样做确实是惯例[pc.ra kitsune
                |这个地区的领导者们
                |你们的领导者
            ]他们会坚守自己的职位，直到死亡或被迫离开；而和平地退位则是一种罕见且值得报道的事件。不过，请考虑这样一点：在我的故乡，皇帝通常会在四十多岁的年纪退位，然后前往山区过上与世俗隔绝的隐居生活，以此接近自己的神灵祖先。对于那些在极端情况下能够活到两百岁的人来说，这样的退位其实算是非常早的退休了。
            
            是的，但琥珀并不是那只狐妖皇帝。”

铁也举起手来说：“请允许我继续讲。虽然这种做法被归因于幕府将军们不希望出现一个能够与他们竞争并构成政治威胁的皇帝，但实际上，这种做法在幕府成立之前就已经存在了；他们只不过是进一步推动了这一趋势而已。是在自己的地位稳固、权力达到顶峰的时候早早退位，帮助继任者并提供自己的帮助与人脉支持，还是顽强地坚守自己的头衔直到最后，从而导致继任者失去这些优势呢？
            
            我们的历史学家们普遍认为，皇帝们提前退位这一制度使得权力能够顺利地从一代传到下一代，而这正是我们的君主统治体系成为全世界延续时间最长的原因之一。当有三到四位已经退位的皇帝为你提供支持时，这种制度确实会起到很大的作用。
            |关于不给新生儿取名字这件事……

“嗯？”

这感觉有点让人难过。小花显然非常爱她刚出生的女儿，但暂时还没有信心给她取名字。你很想帮上忙，但这件事似乎最终还是需要她自己来解决；在情况得到解决之前，你所能做的就是陪伴在她身边，用其他事情来转移她的注意力吧。

铁也想了想[pc.heightRange 72
                |向上
                |超过
            ]然后轻轻拍了拍你的背，说道：“有时候，这是我们能做的最好的事情；有时候，这也是我们唯一能做的事情。这种习俗在狸猫中间其实更为普遍，因为它们天生就具有很强的繁殖能力，所以相比我故乡的其他民族，它们更容易遇到这种不幸的事情。如果你生了更多的孩子，那么婴儿死亡率的数字就会自然而然地升高。

I have reviewed the matter with my own eyes, and there are multiple fallbacks and redundancies should something go awry: the self-sufficiency of the den, Kohaku's subordinates being able to caravan in her stead, the fact that most imports are luxuries, and more. If it comes to it, I could even use what influence I have to change things for the better, since I am still considered in good standing..."
                
                So, he's saying that she should relax and just enjoy the ride instead of being worried about her job?
                
                "Indeed. One of the harder lessons I've had to learn in my time is that few people are truly irreplaceable; even a prince like me appears to be scarcely missed in his homeland these days. Blunt as it may be, Kohaku is not the only one who is capable of performing her tasks; if she were, that would be a problem for the future even if the issue were not pressed now. Her inability to caravan at the moment should be seen as an opportunity, not a liability; perhaps it is my optimistic nature speaking here."
                |"I suppose this end was inevitable, was it not? From what I understand, there has been a surge of popularity in the local womenfolk desiring to bear kits in recent years — Komari informs me that the trend has lasted about seven years or so at this point. For someone as keenly attuned to the social mood as Kohaku is, coupled with her desire to fit in, this was in a way unavoidable."
                
                Was it? You feel like that's oversimplifying it a little.
                
                Tetsuya gives you an enigmatic smile. "Is it?"
                
                It feels like there should be more, that's all...
                
                "Sometimes the simplest answers are those which hold the most truth, [pc.name]. Komari tells me that a good number of those who came with her in the first generation consisted of foxes who were unhappy enough with the strict, if understandable social customs on family size. I suppose they were misfits in this sense... but it only stands to reason that the sentiment would have prevailed in some fashion, especially in a sense most of my peers would consider extreme and unreasonable. The imperial colony's population goes through swells and ebbs over time, I'm told — constant increase is a fool's errand, according to the den matron, and only a tumor grows for its own sake.
                
                "But it does feel like we're in the midst of another rising trend — one which the den matron has attempted to account for, and which poor little Kohaku has found herself swept up by. I am not entirely sure her decision was a conscious one, but just as a school of fish swim with one mind despite being comprised of many individuals, so does she respond to those around her. It seems to have worked out well for her, so I'm not surprised that she persists."
                |"I will admit, there's a certain amusement to be found in teasing poor Kohaku while she's moody," Tetsuya says with a chuckle. "I don't even have to do anything."
                
                Oh? How does he go about it?
                
                "Like I said: I simply don't do anything. It's obvious when she's trying to get emotional reactions out of people around her, so I just answer all her queries politely, calmly and directly. The failure to provoke an emotional response infuriates her all the more, and she tries harder; it's in this fashion that the cycle escalates until she can't hold it in any more and the fireworks begin. Consider it akin to holding up a mirror in front of an animal and watching it grow more and more irate at its own reflection — hence, the humor to be found in the situation."
                
                That seems a little cruel.
                
                "I would call it a self-inflicted wound; being unhappy is no excuse for you spreading it to others. Perhaps sufficient correction will suffice to straighten out this behavior instead of allowing her to infect others with her moodiness. Harsh, but in some cases it is the only thing that works. In the meantime, I can find some small amusement in watching Kohaku being driven to tears by her own actions — perhaps I would tell her to stop hitting herself, but that might be pushing the envelope a little too far."
                |"Kohaku approached me a little while ago and asked if I could use my arts to send her parents a message," Tetsuya tells you with a thoughtful expression on his face. "She wished to inform them of their incipient grandchild. I had to regret to inform her that such a thing was not possible."
                
                Ouch. That couldn't have been easy on her.
                
                A nod. "More than one would immediately think. In order for the crane to find its intended recipient, the sender must share some degree of mutual sympathy, familiarity, whatever you wish to call it. Not that it is well-quantified, partly because of the symbolic nature of this requirement, but it exists nonetheless. To press home the point, I attempted it twice for Kohaku, and after that she was forced to admit that it would not work."
                
                Yes... you can easily see how that would have been hard.
                
                Tetsuya's smile is carefully apologetic. "I've heard the story as it goes in the local gossip. I'm sure they did love their daughter very much, but at the same time loved the thrill of the search even more to give it up. Given their behavior towards Kohaku in the last decade and change, I don't think that receiving news of a grandchild would change the situation to any noticeable degree."
            ]

[tetsuya.isLover |Let it be known, though, that I'm not going to hold back... even [tetsuya.married |if you're my wife |for you ] |[tetsuya.isFriend |Don't think I'll go easy on you, though, [pc.name] |I must warn you, though: I am an expert when it comes to these kinds of games, and I will not hold back ] ]." Of course not! If you're going to come out on top, it's going to be in spite of him doing his best, and you absolutely forbid him from throwing the game out of any sense of pity. He's got to be serious and give it his all, got it? Tetsuya's smile broadens. "Of course. Far be it from me to tarnish victory with a disingenuous performance. This is a challenge of wits, after all." With that, Tetsuya rises from his seat and motions for you to wait out in the living area while he ducks into another room to get the board and pieces. Soon enough, he's back, carrying the board under an arm and pulling up two cushions by the low table for the two of you. "Please make yourself comfortable, [pc.name]. I[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | will |'ll ] serve refreshments shortly — more tea and rice crackers for both of us. I look forward to [first |seeing what you can do |having another captivating game with you ]." You set up the board while Tetsuya gets more crackers and refills both cups with hot tea. So it comes to pass that you and [tetsuya.isLover |your beloved |Tetsuya ] wind up facing each other down over a game of [rand |shogi |go ], with drinks and snacks at your side. [rand |"Go and Shogi are the standard selection of games for someone in my position and heritage to dabble in. And, more often than not, the [silly |usual suspects |opponents I faced back home ] have been other scholars and patricians; while their skills and strategies varied from person to person, their reason for playing tended to be similar. The three most common motives I[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | have |'ve ] seen are as follows: a desire to pass the time, an excuse to socialize, and as an aim to flaunt one's experience." Which one does he fall under? "I play these games out of a love for the activity. I enjoy teaching, but I also enjoy learning. She[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | has |'s ] been a fine test of my skills." About that. How has his little rivalry with her been going? Mai's certainly no slouch when it comes to these kinds of games. "We go back and forth," Tetsuya says with a shrug. "Some days she wins, and some days I[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | am |'m ] the victor. But that is neither here nor there. You are my adversary this [dayNight |day |night ], and it[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | is |'s ] time to begin." ] [var0 |[silly |For the next half-hour to a full hour or so, the room is silent, punctuated only by the snap of rice crackers. The state of the battlefield that's the wooden game board shifts from moment to moment, the tides of war turning at seemingly a whim; it's hard to discern who exactly has the upper hand until seemingly out of nowhere, Tetsuya pulls off a series of moves that has you completely outmaneuvered in moments. This doesn't look good. If this continues any further you're going to lose! Fortunately, you've got a solution. Pointing past Tetsuya, you tell him to look at the wall over there. "What?" Tentatively, Tetsuya looks over his shoulder. Seizing the opportunity to act, you grab one of Tetsuya's pieces on the board and eat it. Once he turns back around, you repeat the process, eating another one of his pieces. You do this over and over again, and before long, the only pieces that remain on the board are yours. "Yes. That's a wall. I really don't know what you're expecting me to find over there," Tetsuya says as he turns back around. He then goes to move one of his pieces, but with all of them now gone, the only thing that happens is his fingernails clacking against the board. "What? Wait. What?! Where'd they all go?! I could've sworn I had you dead to rights. Do you know where my pieces went, [pc.name]?" You shake your head. Tetsuya rubs the back of his head and stares dumbfoundedly at the board. Since he's got no more pieces on the board, you ask if that means you win by default. "I mean" — Tetsuya looks underneath the table and then back at the board — "I guess so. I swear, this better not be one of Keros' tricks. Don't mind me, [pc.name]. Enjoy the rest of the crackers and tea — I'll look for the missing pieces." You chuckle at a job well done. It's not like he's going to find his missing pieces any time soon. This is what victory tastes like. |The picture of peaceful serenity doesn't last long, though. Within a handful of moves, Tetsuya completely outmaneuvers you, gaining free rein of the board. It's not long after that you're forced to admit defeat, perhaps a little relieved that this wasn't dragged out any longer than it needed to be. On his part, Tetsuya looks a little disappointed at the easy victory, pressing a knuckle to his lips as he looks over the remaining pieces on the board. Eventually, his shoulders go slack and he lets out a sigh. "I said I would[tetsuya.isFriend |[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | no |n' ]t go easy |n't hold back ]," Tetsuya mutters to himself. Well, considering that you don't play these sorts of games much, it's understandable that you'd lose to someone with far more experience. Sure, it sucks to lose, but there's no hard feelings between you and him. If anything, you're glad he didn't throw the game or drag it out for your benefit. It's as you've said: if you're going to beat him, it's going to be in spite of him doing his best. At the end of the day, though, what's important is that everyone has fun; it's not like there's money or reputation on the line. He did have fun, right? "The game was disappointing... but not without its own merits. I enjoy your company, [pc.name]. If you do end up applying yourself further, who knows how you might improve? If you[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | are |'re ] looking for a mentor, my door is always open." "Hmm..." Despite the intense gravitas about him, you get the impression that he's enjoying the challenge — or at least, more of a challenge than his usual opponents put up. The state of the game board shifts from moment to moment, the tides of war turning at seemingly a whim; it's hard to discern who exactly has the upper hand until seemingly out of nowhere, Tetsuya pulls off a series of moves that has you completely outmaneuvered in moments. "Good game, [pc.name], but it appears that I have won." Why yes... yes he has. Thinking back on it, there were a couple of points back there where making a slightly different move would have radically changed the game's outcome. Perhaps you should've capitalized on those opportunities and taken more risks, but you didn't, and this is where you are now. As the saying goes: hindsight's twenty-twenty. Nevertheless, you gave it your all. Tetsuya finishes the last of his tea and analyzes the board once more, raising a finger to his chin. "You put up a good fight, [pc.name] — not many are capable of doing that. Either way, this was a very pleasant game. I have learned a few things I want to try out next time." Of course. You've learned some things and enjoyed your time with him, too. |For the next half-hour to a full hour or so, the room is silent, punctuated only by the snap of rice crackers. Tetsuya starts off with a strong opening and bold play, but quickly [silly |realizes that you're [pc.himHer] when you stymie his opening gambit, causing him to take the game seriously and lock in |falls into a far more conservative strategy when you stymie his opening gambit. [tetsuya.hlfa |Your husband |Your beloved |Your friend |The foxen prince ]'s brows knit and furrow as he considers each move deeply, realizing that he's gotten in ahead of himself, perhaps due to simple overconfidence ]. Still, he gives as good as he takes. The tides of war shift back and forth on the battlefield of the game board, each move by either party slow and deliberate. Untouched, the tea grows cold and the rice crackers lie forlornly on their plate, but neither of you have time for such trivialities. By this point, Tetsuya's lips are a thin, straight line as he pinches his chin, those golden eyes of his darting back and forth across the board. When it happens, it surprises you almost as much as it does him; with a final, resounding clack, you set the piece in your hand down on the board and claim victory over Tetsuya. You then [pc.isBimbo |pump a fist in the air and cheer in celebration |sit back and regard him with a proud smile ]. "I[tetsuya.isAcquaintance | am |'m ] impressed, [pc.name]. But, through your sharp wit and skill, you've managed to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat. Tetsuya finishes the last of his tea and analyzes the board once more, raising a finger to his chin. "I wonder... if I caught onto your counterplay earlier and made this play here" — he jabs at the board with a finger — "and shored up my defenses here, would I have emerged victorious? rows.translation: 你问哲也是否愿意给你上几堂魔法课。 [var0 |哲也点了点头。“当然！那么……我们从哪里开始呢？” [pc.isMage |[var0 |你告诉哲也，你已经掌握了基础知识，并建议他讲一些更进阶的内容。 哲也开始为你讲解魔法的精微之处，你专注地听着。 |你说你对魔法的运作原理有相当深入的了解，所以希望他能直接从更复杂的理论讲起。 哲也若有所思地摸着下巴。“原来如此。那样的话，我们可以直接进入高级理论。你准备好开始了吗？” 你点了点头，哲也开始向你讲解魔法的精微之处。 |其实，你问哲也是否愿意听听你自己关于魔法的理论；最近你对这个课题思考了很多。 “哦？”哲也看着你，眼中闪烁着对你接下来所说之事的兴趣。“请说说你的想法吧。” ] |你告诉哲也，其实你对魔法整体上还相当陌生，也许他可以教你一些基础知识？ “当然。没有什么自然现象比魔法更包罗万象、更引人入胜了。要理解魔法的根基，任何有志成为奥术师的人都必须掌握一个基本事实：我们所谓的魔法，不过是凭借自身意志的力量，将以太能量有意识地、受控地引导成一种可重复、可预测的形态。要成为一名成功的奥术师，需要专注的冥想，以及一个常被忽视的方面——对自我的认知。了解自己最深层的欲望、抱负与动机，对精通魔法而言至关重要。我们这片土地上到处都是奥术师，他们出于某种被压抑的无意识需求，给自己和他人招来悲剧与毁灭。” 你留意着哲也说的每一个字，把比较重要的内容默默记在心里。 “引导法术时，建议借助法器来施放。法器就是你的法杖、权杖或水晶球。没有它们，一旦出了差错，施法者就可能成为那股灾难性能量的目标。那么，闲话少说，”哲也将手伸进长袍，取出一颗手掌大小的宝石，推到你面前，“让我们来看看你的魔法天赋吧。” ] |哲也举起手，让你停在了原地。“我很感谢你的热情，[pc.name]，但你现在必须休息，让今天所学的知识慢慢沉淀下来。我向你保证，将来还会有更多可以讨论的机会。”哲也对你微笑着。 也许他是对的。今天这堂课已经让你精疲力竭，最好明天再来。 ]

rows.original:
Smiling warmly, you stand from your seat and walk over to Tetsuya. He looks up at you questioningly and starts to rise, but you put a firm hand between his ears and tousle his white hair vigorously. That stops Tetsuya in his tracks, causing him to instantly soften under your touch, his large, pointed ears turning to either side of his head, as if trying to get away from you.
    
    Let them try all they want. Nothing's getting away from the sheer determination of your petting!
    
    Tetsuya bobs his head in time with your movements, completely enthralled by the sheer delight of being petted. His eyes are fully closed now as he mumbles and murmurs. Nevertheless, you pet harder, turning his carefully groomed hair into an utterly and incorrigibly disheveled wreck. After a few seconds, you manage to pin down one of [tetsuya.hlfa
        |your husband
        |your lover
        |your friend
        |the kitsune
    ]'s elusive ears between thumb and forefinger.
    
    Now that you've got him right where you want him, it's perfectly fine to stop and savor the moment. You've got time, after all. With Tetsuya's right ear firmly in your grasp, you take your time rubbing the outside with its glossy white fur, reveling in the warm softness. At the same time, your thumb commences exploring the fine, sensitive hairs of Tetsuya's inner ear, teasing the soft tufts that sprout from within. Since Tetsuya's ears have been rendered immobile, the rest of his body is more than happy to pick up the slack, playfully wiggling side-to-side. Furthermore, [tetsuya.hlfa
        |your husband
        |your lover
        |the kitsune
        |the kitsune
    ]'s fluffy tails twitch and curl with a life of their own.
    
    Running your hands down [tetsuya.hlfa
        |your husband
        |your lover
        |your friend
        |the kitsune
    ]'s hair, effortlessly gliding your [pc.nails] through his long, silken locks, you ask if he's enjoying himself.
    
    He lets out a throaty groan of delight which, in turn, elicits a soft chuckle from you. [tetsuya.isLover
        |It fills you with joy to see the effect you're having on your beloved.
    ]
    
    You slow down a little now, planting the heel of your palm on his forehead and moving your hand in a back-and-forth motion. Before long, your wrist and fingers get tired and you have to stop despite the kitsune's urgings for more. You finish up with a little shake of your fingers to ruffle the fringes of his hair, and then you withdraw.
    
    "That was nice," Tetsuya says with a satisfied sigh. "Normally this kind of thing is reserved for fealty-swearing ceremonies, but it does[tetsuya.isAcquaintance
        | not
        |n't
    ] hurt to just enjoy the simple things every now and again. Thank you."
rows.translation:
你微笑着从座位上站起来，走向哲也。他疑惑地抬头看着你，正准备起身，你却一把抓住他的耳朵，用力地拨弄着他那白色的头发。这一下让哲也愣住了，在你的触碰下，他立刻变得温顺起来，那双大大的、尖尖的耳朵也朝着身体的两侧歪了过去，仿佛想要躲开你一样。
    
    让他们想怎么试都试吧。没有什么能够抵挡你抚摸它的坚定决心！
    
    铁也随着你的动作轻轻点头，完全沉浸在被抚摸带来的愉悦之中。此刻他的眼睛已经紧紧闭上了，嘴里还不停地发出呢喃声。然而，你还是用力地抚摸着他，结果把他那精心打理过的头发弄得乱七八糟、再也无法整理整齐。几秒钟后，你终于抓住了他的一缕头发[tetsuya.hlfa
        |你的丈夫
        |你的爱人
        |你的朋友
        |那只狐狸
    ]被拇指和食指牢牢夹住的、那只难以捉摸的耳朵……
    
    现在你已经把他控制在了自己想要的位置，完全有时间停下来好好享受这一刻。毕竟，你还有足够的时间。当你紧紧握住哲也的右耳时，你会仔细地抚摸它那光滑的白毛，尽情享受那种温暖而柔软的触感。与此同时，你的拇指开始轻轻探索哲也内耳中那些细密而敏感的毛发，逗弄着从内部生长出来的柔软绒毛。由于哲也的耳朵已经无法动弹，他身体的其他部位便欣然接过了这个任务，开心地左右摇晃着。此外， [tetsuya.hlfa
        |你的丈夫
        |你的爱人
        |狐狸精
        |那只狐狸妖精
    ]那些蓬松的尾巴会自主地抽动、卷曲。
    
    当你用手轻轻抚摸它们时[tetsuya.hlfa
        |你的丈夫
        |你的爱人
        |你的朋友
        |那只狐狸精
    ]你的手指轻松地滑过她的头发[pc.nails]透过他那一头长长的丝发，你会忍不住问他是否玩得开心。
    
    他发出一声愉悦的呻吟，而这声呻吟反而让你忍不住轻声笑了出来。 [tetsuya.isLover
        |看到自己对所爱的人产生了积极的影响，你会感到无比开心。
    ]
    
    你现在稍微放慢动作，将手掌根部放在他的额头上，然后来回移动手掌。不久之后，你的手腕和手指就会感到疲劳，尽管那只狐妖不断催促你继续，你还是不得不停下来。最后，你轻轻摇晃手指，让他的发梢有些许晃动，然后才把手抽回来。
    
    “真是太舒服了……”铁也满意地叹了口气说道，“通常这种举动都是在进行效忠仪式时才会做的，不过这次也挺不错的。[tetsuya.isAcquaintance
        | 不是
        |不
    ]能够偶尔享受这些简单的事情，就已经很幸福了。谢谢。

At the same time, your thumb commences exploring the fine, sensitive hairs of Tetsuya's inner ear, teasing the soft tufts that sprout from within. Since Tetsuya's ears have been rendered immobile, the rest of his body is more than happy to pick up the slack, playfully wiggling side-to-side. Furthermore, [tetsuya.hlfa
        |your husband
        |your lover
        |the kitsune
        |the kitsune

        |your husband
        |your lover
        |your friend
        |the kitsune
