It's a sight to see as her body stiffens and the expression of ennui at routine calculations is quickly replaced by a beaming, dazzling countenance. "Welcome, welcome! It's certainly an honor to have you here, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] — is there something that I can arrange for your Eminence to receive, nojya?" |Upon seeing you draw close, Kohaku drops what she was doing and approaches you with small, delicate steps before bowing, her four tails wagging like an overexcited dog's. "Welcome, welcome! My [pc.mf |lord |lady ], it is with great pleasure that I'm able to receive your eminence in a simple storehouse like mine, nojya. Is there anything I can get for you today?" Perhaps. Business, pleasure... no reason one can't have both in the same trip. "Well, if you see anything you like or need a recommendation, don't hesitate to inquire, nojya! So long as it's something the den can spare, I would be glad to see to your needs, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. Simply ask!" ] |[rand |As you approach, Kohaku looks up from her bookkeeping and gives you a big smile. "Oh hey, it's you, [pc.name]! Could smell you from the door — we don't really get many people in here who aren't kitsune, nojya. You here for business, or pleasure?" Who says it can't be both? Business can be a pleasure — she certainly takes joy in what she does. A chuckle. "Eh. Lists and numbers may be what I'm good at, but talking to people is what I like, nojya. If I'm here, that means I'm not out there... which is why it's so nice of you to drop in. Now, can I get you anything? Crumbs land on the ground as Kohaku wipes her face off with the back of her hand. "I-uh, wasn't expecting anyone to show up today, nojya!" That's uh, well, you won't say it's fine, but it's cute enough for you to overlook the indiscretion. What's more concerning is that she'll get fat if she keeps on eating so many sweet things... "Eeeeh, it doesn't really matter. I work it off walking all around the Marches, nojya." Kohaku gives you a cheery, fanged smile. "Even the old warpstone network doesn't bring you everywhere. rows.original: Properly examine this foxy merchant's goods.
rows.translation: 仔细检查这个狡猾商人的商品吧。

rows.original: See what Kohaku has on offer today.
rows.translation: 来看看今天琥珀有哪些优惠活动吧。
rows.raw: "See what Kohaku has on offer today."

rows.original: For the low price of three metal bits, you can %"convince" Kohaku to see to instantly refreshing her shop's stock.
rows.translation: 只需支付三枚金属币这样低廉的代价，你就能“说服”琥珀立刻去补充她商店的商品库存。
rows.raw: 'For the low price of three metal bits, you can %"convince" Kohaku to see to instantly refreshing her shop\'s stock.'

rows.translation: 这些狐妖族使用铁而不是青铜。不知道为什么——或许仓库管理员能够解释这个现象。

rows.original: Engage this tiny merchant with some lovely conversation.
rows.translation: 与这位小商贩进行一些愉快的交谈吧。
rows.raw: "Engage this tiny merchant with some lovely conversation."

rows.original: Proposition this tiny, adorable merchant for a romp in the hay.
rows.translation: 向这位小巧可爱的商人求欢，一起在干草堆里快活一场吧。
rows.raw: "Proposition this tiny, adorable merchant for a romp in the hay."

rows.original: Kohaku is a conscientious little fox. Try asking her later towards the end of her shift.
rows.translation: 琥珀是一只非常尽责的小狐狸。你可以试着在她的值班时间快结束的时候去问她。
rows.raw: "Kohaku is a conscientious little fox. Try asking her later towards the end of her shift."

rows.original: Inquire about getting your own set of kunoichi attire.
rows.translation: 询问一下如何获得一套属于自己的女忍装束。
rows.raw: "Inquire about getting your own set of kunoichi attire."

rows.original: Kohaku should have your outfit in by now.
rows.translation: 琥珀应该已经把你的服装准备好了。
rows.raw: "Kohaku should have your outfit in by now."

rows.translation: 你的那套服装已经到货了，不过你得先腾出空间来放新东西。要是拿到了服装却带不回去，那就有点傻了。
rows.raw: "Your outfit is in but you need to make room for your new stuff. It'd be a bit silly to get the outfit and be unable to carry it back with you."

rows.original: Kohaku's reaction to you pulling out the broken off hilt from your possessions is amusing — the little golden kitsune's entire body perks up from head to tail, seized by a sudden surge of energy. Her ears perk up, her eyes brighten, and though it's hard to believe her tails and posture alike turn even more energetic to the point where she's but one sweet treat away from vibrating on the spot. Reaching out both hands to receive your gift, Kohaku sets it down on the table and looks it up and down in the cutest, most exaggerated fashion. "[pc.ra kitsune |Ah! Ah! My [pc.mf |lord |lady ], you came through! Of course I had no doubts that you would be successful, but still! Returning to us with such a prize is absolutely glorious, nojya — I hope it was not a lot of trouble for you, your Eminence!" If it were coming out of anyone else's mouth, the words would have sounded like she was laying it on far too thickly, but little Kohaku is the perfect picture of genuine enthusiasm and energy. No, it wasn't any trouble for you at all — given the other things you've done and plan to do in the Trickster's service, tracking down a caravan was a trivial task by comparison. From there, it was just a matter of working out a deal. "Oh! Oh! But working out a deal can involve a lot of effort; I should know, nojya! For you to make such an undertaking on our behalf, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], especially when the entirety of this matter was all caused by my failure to recognize its value when I first came across it — oh, for someone like your Eminence to cover for my mistakes! Where can I put my face, nojya?" For a moment, Kohaku looks like she's going to explode from embarrassment and prostrate herself on the ground before you, but she eventually settles for a deep bown from the waist. "Ah, um, while no real reward has been authorised by the den matron for this deed, I'm sure I can find something suitable for your efforts, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]!" Aha. Looking at that cheery smile on that little round face is good enough reward for you. Seriously, though, you didn't think it was that much trouble. "It is something that I was having trouble with, so credit goes to you, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. Merchants like that, they have ways and means of getting around, and they're only found when they want to be found. If they'd wanted to avoid you, you'd never have bumped into them no matter how hard you searched, nojya. I would know, I'm one of those people." You grin. So, she's calling herself a merchant? "No, but I still do some of the same things that they do, nojya. But thank you again, your Eminence! Not all of us can move as freely as you do, so believe me when I say everything you do is appreciated amongst us little people! I'll get one of Kazuo's puppets to take it up to him at the end of the day, I'm sure the artificer will be very pleased to receive it, nojya!" |You got it! Was it a lot of trouble for you, nojya?" Not that much. You wander around the Marches a lot, so it was only a matter of time before you ran into the caravan. From there, it was just a matter of working out a deal. "Oh! Oh! But working out a deal can involve a lot of effort; I should know, nojya! For you to make such an undertaking on our behalf, especially when the entirety of this matter was all caused by my failure to recognize its value when I first came across it — I can't quite thank you enough!" Aha. Looking at that cheery smile on that little round face is good enough reward for you — almost, that is. "Merchants like that, they have ways and means of getting around, and they're only found when they want to be found. If they'd wanted to avoid you, you'd never have bumped into them no matter how hard you searched, nojya. I would know, I'm one of those people." You grin. So, she's calling herself a merchant? "No, but I still do some of the same things that they do, nojya. Anyway, thank you again — there's a reason why you're our favorite outsider, and this is one of them! I'll get one of Kazuo's puppets to take it up to him at the end of the day, I'm sure the artificer will be very pleased to receive it!" ] What exactly is it about this stuff that's gotten that man so excited, anyway? Kohaku scratches the back of her head and wiggles her ears. "Well, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], ]he thinks that given the composition of some of the other goods I brought back from the caravan, the alloy used in their making could be used to contain powerful enchantments. There were only traces of it in what I brought back, but then I remembered the native telling me about that antique, nojya!" You see... "Since we've never really had much in the way of metal in the Old Country, we've traditionally used wood and stone to hold such magics." Kohaku points at one of the puppets in the storehouse busy doing all kinds of heavy lifting. "It's been a century or two, but that aspect of metallurgy is still pretty new to us, and we're making discoveries all the time! And what better way to innovate than to rediscover the past works of other peoples, instead of putting in the blood and sweat to do it all by yourself from scratch, nojya! It will take some time, but if it all bears fruit it will be a significant discovery, perhaps even worthy of an imperial commendation!" Right, it's all clear now. At least you've a clearer understanding why Kazuo is interested in the broken remnants of a weapon. Well, good luck to him reverse-engineering that crystal-metal alloy. Although you must ask... "[pc.ra kitsune |My [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |Yes ]?" Nakano also seemed quite interested in the matter when you picked up the task from him, even if he tried to not let it show. Given his line of work, you can see how he might be interested in better equipment for him and his. Is that it? "Eeeeeh? Oh no, no, no, that's not the case at all[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]! That man's nodachi is an ancestral heirloom that once sat in a shrine to the gods! He would die before admitting that it's anything less than perfect as it is, nojya!" Well, she's the local gossip and font of news — what does she think is the reason behind the local military provost's interest in such a matter? "Um, uh..." Kohaku's big red eyes dart this way and that, the little kitsune clearly trying to find a diplomatic answer that [pc.ra kitsune |won't turn one of two powerful local figures against her |will satisfy her innate need to be a tattle-tale without incurring Nakano's annoyance, if not wrath]. She squirms a bit on the spot, tails curling about herself as she desperately tries to hold it in, then the words come spilling out like water from a broken dam. "It's — it's not telling if everyone knows it already, even if they won't say it out loud! Ever since he came back from the capital, Nakano's been trying to entice a trained metalworker to the colonies; he and his do what they can, but eventually they have to be sent back through the gate to be touched up, reforged, that kind of thing! He's been trying for years, and if there's a major discovery —" Right, you see where this is going, and it makes complete sense. However, does it really take that much to lure an artisan metalworker all the way here? "Yes, nojya! Many big artisan families go back, like, way back, and they enjoy good standing and have the backing of many long-standing traditions behind them! You'd need something serious for one of them to come all the way out here — this is more of a backwater than the provinces, after all! No one in sound mind and good standing would willingly come to the colonies for a pittance!" And he thinks a major metallurgical discovery would do the trick. Right. All right, you've asked enough questions of her, so you'll be taking your leave. Best of luck with the hilt and everything. Still out of breath from her earlier outburst, Kohaku slumps forward onto her desk, then remembers [pc.ra kitsune |who she's facing |where she is ] and snaps back to attention, giving you a low bow. "Once again, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], ]please allow me to thank you for covering for my shortcomings, nojya! I cannot thank you enough[pc.ra kitsune | for deigning to lower yourself to deal with our troubles ]!" Oh, she should think nothing of it.

]！" 啊哈，看到那个圆圆的小脸上洋溢着的开心笑容，就已经是对你付出努力的最好回报了。说真的，你根本没想到这会这么麻烦吧。 这是某件非常重要的事情我之前在这方面遇到了麻烦，所以真的要感谢你，我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]那种商人，他们总有自己的办法躲躲藏藏，只有当他们想被找到的时候，才会现身。如果他们想避开你，无论你怎么寻找，都永远找不到他们，诺雅。我懂的，因为我就是那种人之一。 你笑了。所以，她自称是商人吗？ 不，但我还是会做一些和他们一样的事情，诺贾。不过还是要再次感谢您，尊贵的阁下！我们并不是所有人都能像您那样自由行动，所以请相信我，您所做的一切在我们这些普通人心中都是非常值得感激的！今天晚些时候，我会让和雄的一个木偶把这份礼物带给他，我相信那位工匠收到这份礼物一定会非常高兴的，诺贾！ |干得漂亮！这对你来说是不是挺麻烦的啊，诺雅？ 不行。那个很有可能。你经常在边境地区游荡，所以遇到那支商队只是时间问题。从那以后，剩下的就是商定好交易细节而已。 哦！哦！不过，要想达成一项协议确实需要付出很多努力；我太清楚这一点了，nojya！你能够为我们做出这样的努力，尤其是考虑到整个事情的起因其实都是因为我当初没有意识到它的价值——我真的不知道该如何感谢你才好！ 啊哈，看到那张圆圆的小脸上洋溢着的开心笑容，就已经是对你最大的奖励了——差不多算是吧。 那种商人，他们总有自己的办法躲躲藏藏，只有当他们想被找到的时候，才会现身。如果他们想避开你，无论你怎么寻找，也都永远找不到他们，诺雅。我懂的，因为我就是那种人之一。 你笑了。所以，她自称是商人吗？ 不，但我还是会做一些和他们一样的事情，诺雅。总之，还是要再次感谢你——你们之所以成为我们最喜欢的‘外人’，肯定是有原因的，而这一点就是其中之一！今天晚些时候，我会让和雄的一个木偶把这份礼物带给他，我相信那位工匠收到这份礼物一定会非常高兴的！ ] 究竟是这些东西的什么地方让那个男人如此兴奋呢？ 小花挠了挠后脑勺，还摇动着耳朵。嗯， [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]， ]他认为，考虑到我从商队带回的那些物品的成分，用来制造这些物品的合金应该能够用来承载强大的魔法效果。虽然我从商队带回的那些物品中只含有微量的这种合金，但后来我想起了那位当地人跟我讲过的那件古董——诺贾！ 你瞧…… 因为在古老的土地上，我们向来缺乏金属资源，所以传统上都是用木材和石头来承载这类魔法力量。琥珀指了指仓库里那些正在从事各种重体力劳动的木偶之一。虽然已经过去了一两个世纪，但冶金学的这一领域对我们来说仍然算是全新的领域，我们仍在不断取得新的发现！而有什么比重新研究古人留下的成果更好的创新方式呢？毕竟，自己从头开始付出所有的努力去探索，未免太辛苦了，不是吗？虽然需要一些时间，但如果这些努力能够取得成果，那将会是重大的发现，甚至有可能获得皇家的表彰！ 好吧，现在一切都清楚了。至少你更明白为什么和雄会对那种破损的武器残骸感兴趣了。嗯，祝他能在逆向工程那种晶体金属合金的过程中取得成功吧。不过……你还是得问问看才行。 "[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] |是的 ]？" |领主 |女士 ]， ]请允许我感谢你弥补了我的不足，诺雅！我真的感激不尽。[pc.ra kitsune | 因为您愿意屈尊来帮助我们解决这些麻烦 ]！" 哦，她不应该把这件事放在心上。
rows.raw: " Kohaku's reaction to you pulling out the broken off hilt from your possessions is amusing — the little golden kitsune's entire body perks up from head to tail, seized by a sudden surge of energy. Her ears perk up, her eyes brighten, and though it's hard to believe her tails and posture alike turn even more energetic to the point where she's but one sweet treat away from vibrating on the spot. Reaching out both hands to receive your gift, Kohaku sets it down on the table and looks it up and down in the cutest, most exaggerated fashion. "[pc.ra kitsune |Ah! Ah! My [pc.mf |lord |lady ], you came through! Of course I had no doubts that you would be successful, but still! Returning to us with such a prize is absolutely glorious, nojya — I hope it was not a lot of trouble for you, your Eminence!" If it were coming out of anyone else's mouth, the words would have sounded like she was laying it on far too thickly, but little Kohaku is the perfect picture of genuine enthusiasm and energy. No, it wasn't any trouble for you at all — given the other things you've done and plan to do in the Trickster's service, tracking down a caravan was a trivial task by comparison. From there, it was just a matter of working out a deal. "Oh! Oh! But working out a deal can involve a lot of effort; I should know, nojya! For you to make such an undertaking on our behalf, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], especially when the entirety of this matter was all caused by my failure to recognize its value when I first came across it — oh, for someone like your Eminence to cover for my mistakes! Where can I put my face, nojya?" For a moment, Kohaku looks like she's going to explode from embarrassment and prostrate herself on the ground before you, but she eventually settles for a deep bown from the waist. "Ah, um, while no real reward has been authorised by the den matron for this deed, I'm sure I can find something suitable for your efforts, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]!" Aha. Looking at that cheery smile on that little round face is good enough reward for you. Seriously, though, you didn't think it was that much trouble. "It is something that I was having trouble with, so credit goes to you, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. Merchants like that, they have ways and means of getting around, and they're only found when they want to be found. If they'd wanted to avoid you, you'd never have bumped into them no matter how hard you searched, nojya. I would know, I'm one of those people." You grin. So, she's calling herself a merchant? "No, but I still do some of the same things that they do, nojya. But thank you again, your Eminence! Not all of us can move as freely as you do, so believe me when I say everything you do is appreciated amongst us little people! I'll get one of Kazuo's puppets to take it up to him at the end of the day, I'm sure the artificer will be very pleased to receive it, nojya!" |You got it! Was it a lot of trouble for you, nojya?" Not that much. You wander around the Marches a lot, so it was only a matter of time before you ran into the caravan. From there, it was just a matter of working out a deal. "Oh! Oh! But working out a deal can involve a lot of effort; I should know, nojya! For you to make such an undertaking on our behalf, especially when the entirety of this matter was all caused by my failure to recognize its value when I first came across it — I can't quite thank you enough!" Aha. Looking at that cheery smile on that little round face is good enough reward for you — almost, that is. "Merchants like that, they have ways and means of getting around, and they're only found when they want to be found. If they'd wanted to avoid you, you'd never have bumped into them no matter how hard you searched, nojya. I would know, I'm one of those people." You grin. So, she's calling herself a merchant? "No, but I still do some of the same things that they do, nojya. Anyway, thank you again — there's a reason why you're our favorite outsider, and this is one of them! I'll get one of Kazuo's puppets to take it up to him at the end of the day, I'm sure the artificer will be very pleased to receive it!" ] What exactly is it about this stuff that's gotten that man so excited, anyway? Kohaku scratches the back of her head and wiggles her ears. "Well, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], ]he thinks that given the composition of some of the other goods I brought back from the caravan, the alloy used in their making could be used to contain powerful enchantments. There were only traces of it in what I brought back, but then I remembered the native telling me about that antique, nojya!" You see... "Since we've never really had much in the way of metal in the Old Country, we've traditionally used wood and stone to hold such magics." Kohaku points at one of the puppets in the storehouse busy doing all kinds of heavy lifting. "It's been a century or two, but that aspect of metallurgy is still pretty new to us, and we're making discoveries all the time! And what better way to innovate than to rediscover the past works of other peoples, instead of putting in the blood and sweat to do it all by yourself from scratch, nojya! It will take some time, but if it all bears fruit it will be a significant discovery, perhaps even worthy of an imperial commendation!" Right, it's all clear now. At least you've a clearer understanding why Kazuo is interested in the broken remnants of a weapon. Well, good luck to him reverse-engineering that crystal-metal alloy. Although you must ask... "[pc.ra kitsune |My [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |Yes ]?" Nakano also seemed quite interested in the matter when you picked up the task from him, even if he tried to not let it show. Given his line of work, you can see how he might be interested in better equipment for him and his. Is that it? "Eeeeeh? Oh no, no, no, that's not the case at all[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]! That man's nodachi is an ancestral heirloom that once sat in a shrine to the gods! He would die before admitting that it's anything less than perfect as it is, nojya!" Well, she's the local gossip and font of news — what does she think is the reason behind the local military provost's interest in such a matter? "Um, uh..." Kohaku's big red eyes dart this way and that, the little kitsune clearly trying to find a diplomatic answer that [pc.ra kitsune |won't turn one of two powerful local figures against her |will satisfy her innate need to be a tattle-tale without incurring Nakano's annoyance, if not wrath]. She squirms a bit on the spot, tails curling about herself as she desperately tries to hold it in, then the words come spilling out like water from a broken dam. "It's — it's not telling if everyone knows it already, even if they won't say it out loud! Ever since he came back from the capital, Nakano's been trying to entice a trained metalworker to the colonies; he and his do what they can, but eventually they have to be sent back through the gate to be touched up, reforged, that kind of thing! He's been trying for years, and if there's a major discovery —" Right, you see where this is going, and it makes complete sense. However, does it really take that much to lure an artisan metalworker all the way here? "Yes, nojya! Many big artisan families go back, like, way back, and they enjoy good standing and have the backing of many long-standing traditions behind them! You'd need something serious for one of them to come all the way out here — this is more of a backwater than the provinces, after all! No one in sound mind and good standing would willingly come to the colonies for a pittance!" And he thinks a major metallurgical discovery would do the trick. Right. All right, you've asked enough questions of her, so you'll be taking your leave. Best of luck with the hilt and everything. Still out of breath from her earlier outburst, Kohaku slumps forward onto her desk, then remembers [pc.ra kitsune |who she's facing |where she is ] and snaps back to attention, giving you a low bow. "Once again, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ], ]please allow me to thank you for covering for my shortcomings, nojya! I cannot thank you enough[pc.ra kitsune | for deigning to lower yourself to deal with our troubles ]!" Oh, she should think nothing of it. "

没错，你应该能理解这其中的逻辑，而且这一切确实都合情合理。不过，真的需要用这么多东西来吸引一位技艺高超的金属工匠来到这里吗？ 是的，诺贾！很多著名的工匠家族都会回去，就像方式他们根基深厚，享有良好的社会地位，背后还有许多悠久的传统作为支撑！要想让他们中的某个人专程来到这里，肯定得有非常重要的理由才行——毕竟这里可比那些省份还要偏远落后！任何一个神志清醒、地位稳固的人，都不会愿意为了微薄的报酬而来到这些殖民地来的！ 他认为，一项重大的冶金学发现就能解决这个问题。对吧。好吧，你们已经问了她足够多的问题了，现在可以离开了。 由于刚才的激烈情绪还没有平复下来，小花瘫软地坐在桌前，然后突然想了起来[pc.ra kitsune|她将面对的是谁|在她所在的地方]然后立刻恢复注意力，向你鞠了一个躬。再一次， [pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]， ]请允许我感谢你弥补了我的不足，诺雅！我真的感激不尽。[pc.ra kitsune| 因为您愿意屈尊来帮助我们解决这些麻烦]！" 天啊，她难道忘掉你之前说过的话了吗？那些话是告诉她不要因为自己认为犯下的错误而自责的。 对不起，诺雅！
rows.raw: " "[pc.ra kitsune |Oh, uh, you've come about that, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]?" Kohaku looks more than a little flustered about the whole affair when you bring up the matter of the request. "I thought that someone like Takahiro would be put on the job, not someone as illustrious as you, nojya! Truly, you are magnanimous to take the burdens of the little people upon yourself when you no doubt have more pressing concerns in his divine lordship's service!" |Oh! You've come about that request, nojya?" Kohaku looks more than a little flustered about the whole affair when you bring up the matter. "Well, I was expecting someone like Takahiro to be put on the job, but then he's worthless and drunk half of the time, nojya. Thanks for doing the den a service even when you really didn't need to..." ] Oh, she should think nothing of it. You're more than willing to help [pc.ra kitsune|your adopted people|out around here], and besides, you weren't using this anyway. Kohaku's reaction to you pulling out the weapon is amusing — confusion at first, with her head tilting and ears swivelling off to the sides, but her demeanour changes as comprehension dawns. The little golden kitsune's entire body perks up from head to tail, seized by a sudden surge of energy. Her ears perk up, her eyes brighten, and though it's hard to believe her tails and posture alike turn even more energetic to the point where she's but one sweet treat away from vibrating on the spot. Reaching out both hands to receive your gift, Kohaku sets it down on the table and looks it up and down in the cutest, most exaggerated fashion. "Oh! Uh... [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady], ]this is not quite I was expecting..." From your talk with Nakano, you understood that everyone was so interested in the relic despite its degraded state because it might have been fashioned from a ley-crystal alloy. Well, you'll do even better than that — during your travels, you came across a sorceress looking into the matter herself, and wrested from her a functional weapon. Since you're not using it, you might as well hand it over to the kitsune — it's either going to lie around collecting dust amongst your other things or wind up being sold off, so you're not particularly concerned about it all. "Ah! Ah!" If she was excited before, Kohaku looks like she's fit to explode on the spot, or at least start running around in circles until she collapses of exhaustion. "[pc.ra kitsune |My [pc.mf|lord|lady]! My [pc.mf|lord|lady]! You have truly gone well and above the requirements of duty in this matter — the artificer will be soooo excited to receive this, and frankly, I am too |This is so far beyond expectations, nojya! Kazuo had been expecting to work with a broken-down relic; he will be so excited to receive something fresh and new! And frankly, so am I! Will you just look at this thing — I am only good at appraising the mundane myself, but even I am getting excited just looking at it ]! Thank you, thank you so much for not just covering for a problem that arose because of my own ineptitude, but doing so in such a spectacular fashion, nojya!" She's more than welcome, but if she's really thankful to you, then the first thing you'd like is for her to stop thinking of all this as her own fault. Could things have been resolved instantly if she'd realized the value of what she was looking for the first time around? Yes, but then you'd never have heard of this to be able to present her with something better. Was it a mistake? Perhaps, but there's no reason it can't be turned into an opportunity. "My head's spinning, nojya..." Oh, never mind. She should breathe deeply a few times before she passes out. Anyways... "Can I help? Just say it, [pc.ra kitsune| your Eminence, ]and it will be done!" Well, you'd like to know more about why everyone's so interested in this ley-crystal alloy. You can guess that it's important, but for it to be blown up to this degree... "Uh, um, let me try to explain, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|nojya]. Since we've never really had much in the way of metal in the Old Country, we've traditionally used wood and stone to hold such magics." Kohaku points at one of the puppets in the storehouse busy doing all kinds of heavy lifting. "It's been a century or two, but that aspect of metallurgy is still pretty new to us, and we're making discoveries all the time! And what better way to innovate than to rediscover the past works of other peoples, instead of putting in the blood and sweat to do it all by yourself from scratch, nojya! It will take some time, but if it all bears fruit it will be a significant discovery, perhaps even worthy of an imperial commendation!" Right, it's all clear now. At least you've a clearer understanding why Kazuo was interested in the broken remnants of a weapon. Well, good luck to him reverse-engineering that crystal-metal alloy. Although you must ask... "[pc.ra kitsune |My [pc.mf|lord|lady] |Yes ]?" Nakano also seemed quite interested in the matter when you picked up the task from him, even if he tried to not let it show. Given his line of work, you can see how he might be interested in better equipment for him and his. Is that it? "Eeeeeh? Oh no, no, no, that's not the case at all[pc.ra kitsune|, your Eminence]! That man's nodachi is an ancestral heirloom that once sat in a shrine to the gods! He would die before admitting that it's anything less than perfect as it is, nojya!" Well, she's the local gossip and font of news — what does she think is the reason behind the local military provost's interest in such a matter? "Um, uh..." Kohaku's big red eyes dart this way and that, the little kitsune clearly trying to find a diplomatic answer that [pc.ra kitsune|won't turn one of two powerful local figures against her|will satisfy her innate need to be a tattle-tale without incurring Nakano's annoyance, if not wrath]. She squirms a bit on the spot, tails curling about herself as she desperately tries to hold it in, then the words come spilling out like water from a broken dam. "It's — it's not telling if everyone knows it already, even if they won't say it out loud! Ever since he came back from the capital, Nakano's been trying to entice a trained metalworker to the colonies; he and his do what they can, but eventually they have to be sent back through the gate to be touched up, reforged, that kind of thing! He's been trying for years, and if there's a major discovery —" Right, you see where this is going, and it makes complete sense. However, does it really take that much to lure an artisan metalworker all the way here? "Yes, nojya! Many big artisan families go back, like, way back, and they enjoy good standing and have the backing of many long-standing traditions behind them! You'd need something serious for one of them to come all the way out here — this is more of a backwater than the provinces, after all! No one in sound mind and good standing would willingly come to the colonies for a pittance!" And he thinks a major metallurgical discovery would do the trick. Right. All right, you've asked enough questions of her, so you'll be taking your leave. Still out of breath from her earlier outburst, Kohaku slumps forward onto her desk, then remembers [pc.ra kitsune|who she's facing|where she is] and snaps back to attention, giving you a low bow. "Once again, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady], ]please allow me to thank you for covering for my shortcomings, nojya! I cannot thank you enough[pc.ra kitsune| for deigning to lower yourself to deal with our troubles]!" Sheesh, did she just forget what you said about not beating herself up over her perceived mistakes? "Sorry, nojya!" "

rows.original: The first thing that strikes you about Kohaku is that she's short, even by kitsune standards. Most Marchers would consider the average foxen a little runty, but Kohaku is absolutely tiny at a mere four feet seven inches. Naturally, your eyes first come to a rest atop her head and the large fox ears that sit there — ever perky, expressive and alert to the slightest sound in her domain, they swivel to and fro with a life of their own, complementing their owner's extroverted demeanor. Their insides are a pale cream instead of the deep, rich gold of her hair and fur, the cottony, balled tufts of dense fur sticking out from each ear just begging to be tweaked and tickled. [kohaku.anyKids |After having had her kit, Kohaku's started paying a little more attention to her hair once more — it's still a mess, but not completely frazzled like it was recently. If anything, it reminds you of how it was before she became with child, but the little golden fox seems to like its new mid-thigh length and how it flows over the shape of her expansive hips and rear. Despite it still being messy even by Marcher standards, she manages to make mess look good, and one can only wonder if this isn't deliberate.[kohaku.wellFed | There's also the matter of the whole bearing a child thing making her hair and fur glossier and richer, something that's persisted even after the kit's out of her belly; while it may not be as obvious a change as that to the rest of her body, motherhood and all the nutrition her body's demanded as a result has really helped touch up her look with luscious threads of resilient spun gold. ] |[kohaku.pregStage 1 2 4 |With an incipient child growing in her belly and her spending more time at home these days, Kohaku's tried a new hairdo to match her more traditional clothing; she's put the threads of spun gold up into a crown braid to keep it all more manageable. It's a different look from before with an equally distinct sense of beauty, and it's truly remarkable that the little golden fox can change the air about her just by the way she does up her hair. It does make sense — now that she's not traveling nor running the risk of it all coming loose while outside, Kohaku can spend more time and effort in the mornings doing up her hair instead of preparing for trading excursions in other locales. |As Kohaku's belly has grown bigger, she's given up on the crown braid — with the growing burdens that kit-bearing is placing on her body, it's understandable why she doesn't want to go to the trouble of a complicated hairdo every morning. A pity that it was so short-lived, but even now as she is, the rich, golden waterfall is very much different when placed against her traditional clothing, as opposed to her old outfit. Before, it made her look pretty and cute; now, it makes her look graceful and maternal.[kohaku.wellFed | Pregnancy really suits her — whatever changes the child in her belly is making to the rest of her body, her gleaming, golden hair is a marked improvement from the already rich wonder that it was before as she settles into her new role. ] |With how encumbered she is these days, Kohaku doesn't have time — or more likely, the willpower — to do her hair. To say it's scraggly would be wrong, though: it's more wild, framing her face and spilling all the way down her back, over her derriere, and finally stopping somewhere mid-thigh. Golden strands glimmer in the light as they fan out from the main body of her hair, reminiscent of a thick-furred wildcat. Even in mild neglect, Kohaku's hair simply assumes the most appealing form for its circumstances, much like the rest of her. [kohaku.wellFed | Besides, there's no denying it: whatever else being with child has done to Kohaku's body, it's been absolutely fabulous for her hair. All the nutrition she's consumed during this time hasn't just gone towards ripening her baby and body, but also all her amazing lustrous floof that by all appearances are threads of spun gold. If the poor girl were any less frazzled, she'd be clipping her own fur to make clothes out of... ] |While there's clearly been some effort to try and get it in shape, Kohaku's hair simply won't obey her. It falls from her head in a glorious mess, framing her face almost all the way to her pointed chin and parting at her red, slitted eyes; behind her, it extends all the way to the curves of her pert, squeezable butt, threads of spun gold gleaming in the light. Even with how fastidious most kitsune are, you can see why Kohaku simply refuses to pin it up or get it into shape: it's wild and fabulous. ] ] [kohaku.anyKids |Her face was made for the job, and then further improved on: wide eyes, a small nose, and little vulpine fangs hidden behind thin lips. Over the course of her pregnancy, little Kohaku's gained what can only be called a bouncy radiance to her demeanor, and it's stuck with her despite the kit already being out of her belly. To say that it's extremely adorable is an understatement, and there's no way she isn't leveraging that expression for all it's worth in the course of her duties.[kohaku.wellFed | That, and the newfound rosiness of her cheeks — perhaps some of it might be attributable to her still being hormonal, but whatever the cause you're struck by the impulse to pinch them and dote on the little new mother like a squeaky toy. Putting all that energy in her while she was pregnant truly paid dividends. ] |[kohaku.pregStage 1 2 |Her face is what some would call made for the job: a pretty face is an asset in a merchant, and she's got the looks — wide eyes, a small nose, and little vulpine fangs. It's harder for Kohaku to summon up one of her trademark open-mouthed smiles these days with how being with child is playing havoc on her mood, but even her pouts are cute, so it's all good in the end.[kohaku.wellFed | It's a good thing that you've been regularly bringing her food, then — the easiest way to turn that frown of hers upside down is to distract her with eating. ] |Her face is what some would call made for the job: a pretty face is an asset in a merchant, and she's got the looks — wide eyes, a small nose, and little vulpine fangs. With her belly growing bigger and making her feel good, Kohaku's also smiling more these days than pouting. [kohaku.wellFed |The fact that you'd been feeding her extremely well while gravid has only exacerbated the situation — while the little golden fox's appetite and waistline have subsided to their original forms, her tits, hips and thighs have stubbornly remained as plump and sumptuous as they were in her final days of being pregnant. Ye gods. Would she be as full and blatant as she is right now if you didn't shovel all that food into her mouth? So full, yet not leaking... that's a petite but strong body she's got there. And as for what's below the waist... what it is now is a far cry from what it was. Having tasted the heady, addictive pleasures of child-bearing, Kohaku's pear shape remains luridly blatant — although the weight's off her and she no longer has to walk with a waddle, plenty of wiggle still remains. If this kit was an easy birth, the next is going to require no effort at all; even considering the loose and relatively modest cut of her clothes, all that mass makes its presence well-known, fabric hanging loosely off her derriere. There's no going back for the little golden fox's body — it's going to continually tempt you for the rest of your days into making another kit on that enormous ass which gave birth to your child. It's absolutely perverse, and like her belly when she was pregnant, Kohaku's petite body only makes her assets look bigger than they ought to be. ] |[kohaku.pregStage 0 1 2 3 4 |The rest of Kohaku's attire is strangely out of the norm for the rest of her kind. While there're definite cultural influences from the Old Country, her clothes would fit in more on the streets of Tychris or even the Winter City than here in a kitsune den. A simple cloth top holds back perky Bs, joined to a figure-hugging leather piece for her midriff, followed up by short skirts that wouldn't look out of place on Cait at all. Not that there's any naked thigh visible — black silken leggings hug her legs all the way to her high boots, and one gets the impression that the amount of thigh between the hem of her skirts and her boots has been very carefully calculated for maximum effect on anyone brave or lecherous enough to ogle. |Given how figure-hugging Kohaku's everyday clothes were, even [kohaku.wellFed |the slight ripening of her body and the gentle swell of her baby bump has made them uncomfortably tight all over. And speaking of maturation, even Kohaku's petite bosom has filled out somewhat, becoming somewhere about average by Marcher standards — a large DD, bordering on Es, capped by deep brown teats and risen areolae that blatantly outline themselves on her clothing. As with the rest of her, their relatively smaller size belies the sheer density of energy contained within them; weighty enough to rest comfortably atop the massively protruding heft of her overstuffed womb, Kohaku's milk-swollen tits spill slightly to the sides of the curve of her tummy, oversensitive beyond belief. Teardrop shapes aren't her style, but there's nothing preventing the little golden fox from sporting all kinds of turgid, tender roundness on her figure; her poor clothes are so tight that every heaving breath she draws has her bosom shivering with muted delight from friction with the fabric. But below the waist is where poor little Kohaku has absolutely expanded, perhaps even more than her tummy. You're what you eat, as the saying goes, and all the nutrition the little golden fox's devoured while being with child has all flown into her lower half, exacerbating her natural pear shape into something ridiculous. It's not just meat that she's put on, but you're pretty sure that her hormonal hips have widened to the point where as hefty as her child is in proportion to the rest of her, the birth won't be a difficult one. In the meantime, the distinct wiggle in Kohaku's waddle provides plenty of entertainment regardless of how it's viewed, and the thick yet taut globes of the little golden fox's rear form a blatant shelf for her hair to pool atop and spill over before ending at the middle of her ripened thighs. |Her natural inclinations and pregnancy hormones have conspired to absolutely blow up the little golden foxen to whatever proportions her petite yet dense stature will bear — her baby belly's absolutely huge, sticking out a good ways in front of her and capped with a delightfully protruding navel and a gentle patch of rosy-red skin. If one puts it in perspective, it's really not that ridiculous, but Kohaku is so tiny that it just makes her overstuffed womb look all the larger on her frame. You know that she's no stranger to bearing oversized burdens all over the place given her job, but even so to see her so deliciously and obscenely laden, so ripe and heavy, so full and rich and warm with growing life — all while cradling her huge, kit-bearing self and trying to look mad and pouty while being all needily frustrated inside... Well, that's Kohaku for you. The naughty little creature that she is keeps on sneaking caresses and pets to her heavy tummy when she thinks no one's looking, which is more often than plausible deniability would permit. Her chest, too, has filled out somewhat along with her womb, ending up at Ds and gaining enough weight to sag and rest comfortably atop the protruding shelf of her midriff. Capped with light brown nipples and tender, swollen areolae, both her milkers have remained comparatively small compared to the rest of her, but the denseness of the deliciousness is just fine considering how taut and springy they've remained. Teardrops aren't Kohaku's style, but the little golden fox's bosom has become full-bodied enough to properly demonstrate the energy with which all of her bounces back from anything. But below the waist is where poor little Kohaku has absolutely expanded, perhaps even more than her tummy. As the kit within her womb readies to enter the world, Kohaku's hormonal body has prepared itself for the event by making her original bottom-heavy pear figure even more blatant, channeling whatever maternal energy she has to spare into her hips and widening them at the deepest level. Combined with a fortitude borne of years of walking all over the place, this birth's going to be easy regardless of how large her baby ends up. Even the little golden foxen's waddling has gained a slight wiggle to it, those expanded cheeks of her derriere smushed together and rubbing with each step while her lustrous hair spills all over it and outlines its shape. It really does feel like all of Kohaku's unrealized dreams at growing up like some of the colonial kitsune have materialized as growing out, which her body does with a vengeance. ] ] ] [kohaku.anyKids |After having had her child, Kohaku's tails have returned to their old energetic, twitchy demeanor; what hasn't faded is the marked improvement in the quality of the little golden kitsune's fur. Various fantasies run through your mind as you eye her maternally-improved tails — of bolsters, of pillows, of warm, fluffy clothing and eager nuzzles. You must've been staring at Kohaku hard enough to burn a hole through her self-consciousness, for she pouts and clutches her tails closer to herself. |[kohaku.pregStage 0 2 4 |If Kohaku's hair is a mess, her tails are immaculately groomed. Numbering four in total, they're fat, fluffy, and promise to be an absolute joy to touch and hold if you ever got the chance to do so. The same color of spun gold as her hair from base to tip, they constantly flick and twitch in accordance with her energetic, extroverted nature, refusing to simply lie at rest. |Kohaku may be too distracted these days to properly do her hair, but the same can't be said for her tails. In accordance with basic foxen hygiene and public decency standards, she's still kept up with their grooming — even so, that alone can't explain the absolute lustre that they've gained to match her hair. Maybe being with child [kohaku.wellFed |and the hormonal mess she's become has opened avenues for all the nutrition you've been putting into her body to make her even more lustrous from head to toe |has some lesser-known benefits for her kind, all the excess energy running off the kit in her tummy making her fur rich beyond compare ]. That's not to mention how much more sensitive they've gotten, either... |Kohaku's hair may be an absolute wild patch, but she's at least tried to do her tails. It's nevertheless a half-hearted process at best from how obscenely sensitive they've become, growing more receptive to affection like the rest of her. [kohaku.wellFed |And the glint of each strand of spun gold that makes up her tail fur... such a lustrous coat can only come from a properly nourished little creature whose body is in the midst of blossoming |There's something about being so heavy with child that fills a little creature like Kohaku with energy, and some of that energy has gone into making her tail fur absolutely delightful not just in its warm golden color, but also its smooth texture ]. If she were to be clipped and something suitable made out of her fur... oh, it would be sacrilege to do so, but the final garment would be worth a king's ransom. Instead of twitching or swaying behind her, all four of Kohaku's tails cling close to her waist, hips and thighs. It's as if they intend to support the weight of her hefty womb, forming a defensive cocoon of golden fluff and helping her hands to warm and cradle the kit growing within. ] ] Most importantly, though, is the pendant that hangs about Kohaku's neck by a thick gold chain. Nestled in her bosom is the unmistakable deep blue hue of a warpstone shard, reminding you that you're not the only one able to use such portals throughout the realm. This is probably why she's got so much more time to dither about the storehouse while making forays of her own... an unfair advantage over most other merchants, to be sure. "

rows.original: [flags.KOHAKU_SHOPPED |[pc.ra kitsune |[rand |"It is my pleasure to serve the champion of our divine lord," Kohaku says, curling her tails about her as she formally gestures for you to follow her. "Please, allow me to see you to the storehouse floor; I will gladly introduce today's offers at your leisure, nojya." |"You honor me with your patronage, champion," Kohaku says as she formally gestures for you to follow her to the storehouse floor. "Please, allow me the privilege of assisting you with your choices today, nojya." ] |[rand |"Sure, I wouldn't mind showing you around," Kohaku says as she levers herself off her seat and joins you. "It's always nice to have someone to talk to, especially an outsider. Get a new perspective on things, nojya. "Let's get down to the floor, though — if you're looking to buy, there are some pretty nifty things that might just catch your eye." |"If you're looking to buy, I'm your fox," Kohaku says with a grin as she hops to her feet and waves you over. "Last trip out of the den brought some pretty interesting things in; I'd be happy to introduce them to you. Just come down to the floor with me, and we'll see if anything catches your eye." ] ] |So, what exactly does she sell here anyway? Judging by the look of the storeroom, it's probably a general goods store... Kohaku looks a little thoughtful; she's probably never quite had to explain this to an outsider before. "Well, a bit of this and a bit of that, nojya. One of my tasks here is to keep inventory of goods brought into the storehouse, determine what we have sufficient numbers of as to be surplus to the den's requirements, then prepare them for trade with other peoples for things we cannot easily produce ourselves. So to be honest, what I am permitted to sell to you, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|friend], may very well change from day to day, nojya." Day to day? That sounds rather volatile for goods that are supposed to be in surplus. "Typically, I will not sell essentials and staple goods; those are reserved for the den's use, nojya. However, there are things which we have either received in trade, or imported from the Old Country, that you might find useful, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|friend]. I sincerely believe it would be to your benefit if you stopped by often and check in on what I have available... I'll guarantee you a good price, nojya. "Also, sometimes I do get in things that you'd be hard-pressed to find anywhere else... I like going places and talking to people, and it's hard to stop being a merchant even after hours, you know? It may be tooting my own horn a little too loudly, but I can guarantee you that you'll never find anywhere else with such deals in the Marches, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|friend]." All right, you think you get it. Rotating stock, special deals, what's on sale could change day by day. Is that it? "You forgot cheap prices, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|friend]." Oh, of course. Now is that it? Kohaku wiggles her ears. "Just so, nojya. Now, if you'll let me take you down to the storehouse floor..." ]
rows.translation: [flags.KOHAKU_SHOPPED |[pc.ra kitsune |[rand |“能够为我们的神圣主宰的冠军服务，是我的荣幸。”琥珀卷着尾巴，正式地示意你跟随她。“请允许我陪您去仓库楼层吧，届时我会很乐意在您有空的时候向您介绍今天的优惠活动，诺雅。” |“冠军，你能光顾我，真是我的荣幸。”琥珀一边说着，一边正式地示意你跟随她前往仓库的楼层。“请允许我今天为您的选择提供帮助，诺雅。” ] |[rand |“当然，我很乐意带你参观一下。”琥珀一边说着，一边从座位上站起来，加入了你的行列。“有可以倾诉的对象总是很好的，尤其是某个外来的陌生人。这样就能从不同的角度看待问题，诺雅。” 不过，让我们来说说具体的产品吧——如果你有兴趣购买的话，有一些相当不错的商品可能会吸引你的注意。 |“如果你打算购买，那我正是你需要的那个人。”琥珀笑着跳起来，挥手示意你过来。“上次离开洞穴时，带回了一些相当有趣的东西；我很乐意向你们介绍它们。跟我一起来到地面吧，看看有没有什么能引起你们的兴趣。” ] ] |那么，她在这里到底卖些什么呢？从储藏室的情况来看，这应该是一家杂货店吧…… 琥珀看起来有些若有所思，她可能以前从未有机会向外人解释过这件事。“嗯，这个有点，那个也有点，诺雅。我在这里的任务之一就是清点被存入仓库的货物，确定哪些货物的数量充足，多余了我们的需求，然后把这些货物准备好，用来与其他部落进行交易，以换取那些我们自己难以生产的东西。所以说实话，我被允许卖给你的这些货物，[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|朋友]，很可能每天都在发生变化，诺雅。” 每天都在变化吗？对于那些本应该处于过剩状态的货物来说，这种情况似乎显得相当不稳定。 “通常情况下，我不会出售生活必需品和日常用品；这些都是为我们自己的用途准备的，诺雅。不过，也有一些东西是我们通过贸易获得的，或者是从旧国进口来的，你可能会觉得它们有用，[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|朋友]。我真心认为，如果你能经常来看看我有什么商品，那对你肯定是有益的……我保证你会得到一个优惠的价格，诺雅。” “另外，有时候我确实能搞到一些在其他地方根本找不到的东西……我喜欢去各种地方、和人们交流，而且即使过了工作时间，我也很难停止自己作为一个商人的身份，你懂我的意思吧？也许我有点自吹自擂了，但我可以向你保证，在这些边境地区，你绝对找不到其他地方有这样的优惠条件，[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|朋友]。” 好吧，你以为自己明白了吧？商品轮换、特价优惠，哪些商品在打折也会每天都在变化。就是这么回事吗？ “你忘了便宜的价格，[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|朋友]。” 哦，当然。那么，就这些了吗？ 琥珀摇了摇耳朵。“就这样，诺雅。现在，如果你允许的话，我带你去仓库那一层吧……” ]

rows.original: There's been something you've been meaning to ask... "Yes?" In your interactions with [pc.ra kitsune|your adopted people|the kitsune], you've noticed that they use iron instead of bronze for all kinds of purposes. Weapons, tools, cooking implements... it's a little surprising, considering how bronze is superior and far easier to work; you just need to cast it and it's done, whereas iron is so much more troublesome. Why's that? "Oh-ho. You have quite the sharp eye, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|friend]; I was going to bring it up sometime. But the answer's quite simple, to be honest here: we just don't have any tin where we come from, nojya." No tin? Well, yeah, one can't make bronze without tin, but it's hard to imagine an entire nation without tin, even if it is a bunch of islands. Those are pretty big islands with mountainous interiors and everything, and there's no meaningful amount of usable tin? "It is what it is. There's plenty of iron, but what there is to be had is of exceedingly poor quality. To hear my father talk about it, getting good quality iron out of the local ore is like squeezing blood from a stone." ...Wow. Kohaku grins, more than a little rueful. "You'd be surprised. The tanuki have perfected the art of building homes without using a single nail, something that would be unthinkable here in the Marches. Apparently the planks and boards are fitted together in a pattern that's quite sturdy — they also do a kind of chestnut roofing that's held down with stones, nojya. People adapt to their environment, don't they?" Ingenuity can't overcome some problems, though. "Oh, really? We've managed to do what we can with what we have, nojya. Although there is something..." Hmm? "For the last forty years now, there's been a standing imperial edict regarding prospecting in foreign lands. Anyone able to secure a reliable supply of high-quality iron for the Old Country will receive a personal commendation from the Emperor himself. It's one of the reasons why my father left his homeland before I was born, nojya. "I'm not a prospector, but I do buy and sell. Oftentimes the natives of these parts will find iron alongside copper and tin... a by-product in small quantities, often regarded as trash since it's hard to work with the same methods bronze uses. I buy those up at very nice prices, and resell it back over at the Old Country. Ingots or scrap are ideal, but even ore will do, nojya. "If you find any useful base metals you're willing to part with, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|friend], I'd be more than willing to give you very competitive prices on them — what comes out of the Marches is of surprisingly high quality. Not surprising, since the bull-men make a living from it alone." All right, so to get it clear: she's buying metal at a premium. "Well, not so much buying as exchanging for a service. If you supply me with some metal bits, I'm sure I could dig up some extra old stock around the storehouse, nojya. It would certainly serve as extra motivation..." All right, you're getting the picture here. With that, Kohaku's melancholy vanishes, replaced with her usual bright cheeriness. "Hokay, so long as we understand each other! Now, is there anything else I can do for you, nojya?"
rows.translation: 有件事你一直想问…… 是吗？ 在你与的互动中[pc.ra kitsune|你收养的人|那只狐狸妖精]你一定注意到了，他们在各种用途上都使用铁而不是青铜。无论是武器、工具还是烹饪器具……考虑到青铜其实更为优越，且加工起来也容易得多——只需要将其铸成所需的形状就可以了，而铁的加工过程则要麻烦得多。那么，为什么他们会选择铁呢？ 哦哦，你的眼力还真不错啊。 [pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|朋友]我本来打算找个机会提这个问题的。但说实话，答案很简单：在我们来自的地方，根本就没有这种东西，nojya。 没有锡吗？嗯，确实，没有锡就无法制造青铜，但很难想象一个国家会完全没有锡，哪怕它是由许多岛屿组成的。那些岛屿面积都相当大，内部还有山脉等各种地形，却没有任何数量的锡可以用来使用，这确实很难理解。 事实就是如此。虽然这里的铁矿资源很丰富，但提取出来的铁质量却极差。听我父亲说，要从这些当地的铁矿中获取高质量的铁，简直就像想从石头里榨出血来一样困难。 ……哇。 琥珀露出略带无奈的笑容。你会感到惊讶的。那些狸猫已经掌握了不用一颗钉子就能建造房屋的技术，而在边境地区，这种做法简直是不可思议的。显然，他们将木板按照某种非常牢固的构造方式拼接在一起；此外，他们还会使用栗子壳作为屋顶材料，再用石头将其固定下来。人们总是会适应他们所处的环境，不是吗？ 再高的智慧也无法战胜这一点。一些不过，还是存在一些问题。 哦，真的吗？我们已经尽了自己所能，利用手头现有的资源来完成了任务，诺雅。不过……还是有一点事情…… 嗯？ 在过去的四十年里，朝廷一直颁布着关于在海外地区进行矿产勘探的法令。任何能够为祖国带来稳定的高质量铁矿供应的人，都将获得皇帝亲自颁发的表彰。这也是我父亲在我出生之前就离开旧国的原因之一，诺雅。 我并不是个采矿者，但我确实从事买卖交易。这些地区的土著人们经常会在开采铜和锡的过程中发现铁……这种金属只是少量产生的副产品，因为用青铜铸造的方法来加工铁非常困难，所以通常被视为废料。我会以相当不错的价格把这些铁买下来，然后转卖到老家去。无论是铸块还是废铁都适合交易，其实就算是矿石也行，没问题的。 如果你发现了任何有用的贱金属，并且愿意将其让出的话， [pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|朋友]我非常乐意为您提供具有竞争力的价格——来自那些边境地区的商品质量其实相当高。这也并不奇怪，因为那些从事这些贸易的人都是以此为生的。 好的，为了让大家明白：她是在以较高的价格购买金属。 嗯，与其说是购买，不如说是用这些金属零件来换取一项服务。如果你能提供这些零件，我肯定能在仓库里找一些闲置的旧零件出来，诺雅。这肯定会成为额外的动力…… 好了，你现在应该明白我的意思了。 说完这些，小红的忧郁立刻消失了，取而代之的又是她那惯常的开朗笑容。好的，只要我们彼此理解就好！现在，还有什么我可以为你做的吗，诺雅？

|按理说我现在应该在工作，但现在已经没什么意义了，诺雅，”琥珀疲惫地笑着说，“只要有那个工具包在，只要巢穴的女首领能理解我的处境，那就没什么关系了。如果你想聊天，我随时都愿意！她看起来简直累坏了。她当初确定自己应该来这里吗？更别提还要和你谈话了。 Is she that desperate for company that she wants you to visit every day? "[pc.ra kitsune |My apologies if I implied that, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. I would never dare make such an imposition upon our divine lord's champion. I-I am far beneath your Eminence's station. |Oh no no no. I'm being quite honest in saying that it would be to your advantage, nojya. ]" Well, you can't say that the prospect of happening to chance upon rare goods isn't appealing. You'll whirl on by when you can. |"I am proud to state we are well stocked for any sudden emergency[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. This, of course, is purely theoretical, but we could conceivably last out a siege long enough for aid from the Old Country to arrive, let alone from the minor dens in the colonies. Logistics is a careful game one does not play without care or regard." She has great confidence in herself and her work. "I was trained by some of the best who were available to someone of my social station[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. I merely stand on their shoulders, nojya." |"Today's a fairly quick day, I don't think. With nothing coming in and everything as it should be, I'm really tempted to call it a few hours in advance and give everyone in the storehouse some precious free time, nojya. I know everyone needs it since that time last month but no one will actually ask for it out of politeness, so it's up to me to notice these things and act accordingly. Being aware of the needs — not necessarily wants — of your subordinates is part and parcel of having responsibility for them, especially when everyone is too polite to ask for things they desperately need, nojya..." ] ] ] "

rows.original: How's business going in the storehouse?
rows.translation: 仓库里的业务进展得怎么样？

rows.original: [var0 |[rand |"Rumour has it that Takahiro saw an orc who could walk on water during one of his trips out. Don't you think that's interesting, nojya? Orcs always look like they would sink straight to the bottom of a lake or ocean — [pc.ra orc |I mean, just look at you, no offense meant |they're always just so solid-looking ]. I wouldn't imagine they float well." [party.has arona |Arona chuckles throatily. "She's not wrong, you know. We don't bother with longships for nothing." ] Well, it's conceivable if someone used magic or something — "Nope, no magic, no amazing sandals, no nothing. Just bare feet, nojya." Hmm... "I mean, I could see some of the boreal elves actually managing that — they always look so light and graceful, even their womenfolk. But this is something else altogether." |"The last crop of adzuki beans were amazing. I'm going to make so much taiyaki I won't be able to eat it all myself, nojya! Then I'll have to share before it goes bad... not that I mind. It's a great way to make friends!" Does she ever think of anything but taiyaki? [party.has kiyoko |Beside you, Kiyoko looses a discreet cough. "Now then, beloved. Taiyaki is clearly important to the girl. It is nice to have a favorite food one can indulge in from time to time." Oh, and what would hers be? "Oh, there are a few. I do love inarizushi, and you're well aware of our daughter's predilection for everything related to peaches, but..." she looks straight at you and licks her lips with her little tongue. "Like I said, there are a few." ] Kohaku [pc.ra kitsune |eyes shift, and she squirms under your gaze. "Well, I do, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. |huffs. "Of course I do! ] But there's something amazing about taiyaki from start to finish... preparing the red bean paste, followed by the batter... taking out the mould that was my mother's before it became mine... the smell that comes out when the batter's cooking is wonderful, nojya. I've had the chance to eat many kinds of things while traveling on business, and not even the Winter City can compare to hot taiyaki that I've made myself. "I can probably let you have some if you don't believe me, nojya..." Uh, um, if you want some you'll probably buy it outright. Equivalent exchange and all, you know — can't let her give you things just like that. [pc.ra kitsune |"That's okay, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. You've already repaid me more than enough by allowing me to share the wonders of taiyaki with you, nojya. |"That's true, but you're not bound by that particular divine law, nojya. I'm sure you can accept a gift without feeling indebted to me, can't you? ]" Uh, um, okay... "Call it a free sample, nojya. Like I said, great adzuki beans this year[pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]." |"Several batches of migrants ago, there was amongst them a woman with only one tail, nojya. Don't you think that's strange[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]? Even a kit fresh out of the womb has two tails; she must have been one cursed fox for something like that to happen to her. "I wonder what happened to that one, though. She headed out into the wilderness... and hasn't been seen since. These lands are dangerous, and people do meet with unfortunate happenstances when out there, nojya. People step out this side of the gate, set off to seek their fortune, and just vanish to never be seen or heard of again. Cursed fox or not, it's a bit of a sad fate, to think that no one will remember you if you die[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]..." ... "We have to depend on one another, especially in a land inimical and foreign to us, nojya. So many people fresh out of the gate are too used to accords, expectations and etiquette between peoples that do not exist here between us and the natives. It's easy to get caught up in things you used to take for granted." ] |[rand |"It is quite terrible what has happened to Kinu — I mean, the Young Lady Otomo," Kohaku begins. "[kinu.isInari |While she is the strong, silent type as far as such things apply to girls, I know for a fact that everyone in the fields respects the work she puts in alongside them, and the expertise she does it with, nojya. That there is a young woman who knows what she's doing and isn't above getting her hands dirty for a good cause, and people in the colonies appreciate that |She is so beautiful, and so courteous to everyone according to their station; everyone cannot help but like her at this point for the simple reason that she can make everyone feel wanted and in their place ]. The mere thought of the Young Lady Otomo coming to harm has a lot of people deeply upset and angry, and there's the occasional talk of reprisal. I really hope it doesn't come to that, nojya." You're perfectly fine with reprisals... so long as they're directed at the right people; you have half a mind to go and hunt them down yourself. You don't want the foxen just striking out at anyone willy-nilly; it goes without saying that such would be bad. "Such things can quickly escalate out of hand, nojya. I hope everyone's emotions are constrained by the fact that we do not have the numbers for any kind of serious outward intervention, and things can pass until coller and more rational heads can prevail. I don't do the kind of business that profits from violence, nojya..." |"The matron has ordered me to open the storehouse to both high and young lady Otomos, nojya. Anything that they may desire to be used in the reconstruction efforts is to be given to them without question." That's really kind of them, and you're really grateful for all the support that's being given to your family in their time of need. Rebuilding and replacing what was lost in the raid would certainly be a lot slower if they had to source their material themselves, too.[kiyoko.numKits 4 | | And that's not to mention all the labor that's being borrowed in the bargain... ] "Just between you and me, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]the matron is really determined to see her liege succeed. She considers it part of her penance, you see... in any case, I've been kept busy sourcing things I don't usually have reason to acquire very much of, nojya." You hope it hasn't been too much trouble... "Oh, no no no, none at all[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]! Perish the thought, I am glad I am able to help, nojya! It's good to see everyone rallying around the young lady Otomo — in a sense, she has truly become the jewel of the colonies. [kinu.isInari |Hardworking and unafraid to get her hands dirty when need be — she really speaks a lot more to the people here than the perfumed princesses across the ocean in the capital, living lives of luxury! Not just that, but she can make herself look good while doing it, nojya! I wish I could work as hard as Kinu without getting myself dirty all over... how does she do it? |Just hearing her speak is enough to make one enamored of her voice... ah, it's so captivating. If I were a more suspicious girl, I'd have wondered if she was using magic to affect our minds... no, shame on me for daring to speak ill of her like that, nojya! ]" You're just really, really glad that Kinu is in such good hands while you're away, that so many people are willing to help, and as you've seen, fight and possibly die for her. It's a good thing that she's across the ocean and stuck in the colonies, lest she make waves in the Old Country..." "The high lady Otomo did abdicate for a reason, nojya... one of them being marking her line as truly being one of us here." |"Everyone has been showering the young lady Otomo [kiyoko.numKits 2 3 |and her sister |and her siblings ]with gifts whenever they show up here, nojya. No one wants to see [kiyoko.numKits 2 |them |her ] unhappy... I myself always take a little more time to cook up some extra taiyaki when I prepare any for myself. Kinu really loves my taiyaki; the honey glaze coupled with the red bean filling is to die for. [kinu.isInari |She doesn't say anything, but she always breaks from her fieldwork |She's always so busy with the many tasks the matron's setting her these days ]to come and try it when I drop by with some, nojya. Everyone wants to see her happy, and I'm counted amongst those people, of course." Wow... "There's nothing strange about it, nojya; it's but the first divine law of equivalent exchange. Kinu would do, and has done the same for any of us if we were in the same straits as her — [kinu.isInari |she wouldn't be obvious about it and would probably even hide it was the fact that it was her who helped out or gave a gift if possible, but we'd all know it was her — ]that's just the way things work. I've been to many places, visited many peoples, and while I of course don't have the full picture I still think that this aspect of how we do things is better than anywhere else I've been. People just want to help each other out and the young lady Otomo happens to be the latest recipient, nojya. That's all." Still, you must thank her and everyone else for watching out for your daughter when you're out on the road. Having to be away from your fox-family for long periods of time can be a drag, but you'll be able to rest a lot better knowing that Kinu has so many people watching out for her welfare in your absence. "Consider it reciprocity for all the work she has put in here without expecting compensation or reward, nojya. Kinu is here at noon every day [kinu.isInari |working the fields with everyone else |in the matron's office ], rain or shine, and doesn't go home before stopping at the shrine in the evening when Mai arrives. That's some dedication, and people notice — you'd think there'd be jealous people and there probably are, but they're probably too ashamed to do anything about it, ahahaha. Princesses are divine and untouchable as a matter of course, and Kinu is ours. Anyone who raised a hand against the colonial princess would be in for a terrible time. "So don't worry about any more nasty raiders coming to harass your daughter, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. |okay? ] Now that we know they're coming and they won't be able to jam the gate in the same way again, we'll be able to rush over at the first sign of trouble, nojya." Thanks again. You really mean it. Kohaku beams. "It's really good to have friends, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]so make a lot, okay? It's hard to go through life alone even if you have so many other comforts." |Kohaku looks a little furtive as she considers your question, making sure none of her underlings are in earshot before speaking. "There's been a bit of tension in the den, nojya. People are very unhappy that an attempt was made on [kiyoko.numKits 2 3 |the lives of the young lady Otomo and her sister |the lives of the young lady Otomo and her siblings |the life of the young lady Otomo ] — I would even go to say a few are outright enraged at what happened to [kiyoko.numKits 2 |them |her ]. Princesses — hime are divine and untouchable, and even though the High Lady Otomo has abdicated, that changes nothing in the nature of her bloodline. On a more practical level, this may be our only chance for the colonies to gain respectability, and be seen as just another province instead of a dumping ground for criminals and other unsavoury characters." That doesn't sound good. You're Kinu's sire and have the most reason to be furious over what happened to her[kiyoko.numKits 2 | and the rest of your family ], but you know where to direct your anger. Hopefully it doesn't blow up to the point of demanding reprisals blindly, that would be bad. Really bad. "The people of this land are mostly decent and ordinary like everyone else, nojya. A bit backward, but that's only to be expected what happened here two centuries ago. Someone is gathering followers with fear and inspiring them to lash out at us. It is sure that the natives have some reason to fear us kitsune, but I would like to disbelieve that we are horrible demons just yet." The most compelling deceptions are usually centered about a grain of truth, yes. It's what makes them so damning. "I'm doing what I can to dispel misconceptions when I make a caravan and head out, but there is only so much I can do, nojya. The fact still remains that if I were to be discovered for what I am under my disguise, my end would not be a pleasant one. You can walk freely amongst the native peoples of this land[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ] — I am not sure what exactly someone like you could do to help the situation, but if the opportunity presents itself, please do what you can, nojya." You'll do your best to ensure that cooler heads prevail and things don't spiral out of control. If the one who should be the most aggrieved urges a rational, calculated response, then no one else should brook argument.[pc.ra kitsune | After all, are they going to talk back to the divine champion [pc.himHer]self? ] |"After what's happened, I'm being more careful about moving my caravans, nojya. I never really needed to worry that much about security on the trip; my bodyguards are mostly for when I'm in native settlements... but now that someone or something has been revealed to be actively hunting us, everyone's being more cautious. [pc.ra kitsune |But with you around, your Eminence, I'm sure you'll be hunting them right back, won't you, nojya?" Right now there aren't any concrete leads, but once you find a trail worth following you damn well are going to be sitting down the bastards who hurt your daughter for a nice little talk. "Of course someone like your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship would not let such a slight upon you and your family go unresolved, nojya. Best of fortune to you, your Eminence, and be careful." Given that they were afraid of you to the point where they waited for both Kiyoko and you to be away from home before descending upon the den, a head-on confrontation is unlikely. Rather, you'd be more worried about a stab in the back if these people dared to target you in the first place. |You should be more careful on the roads too. If these people were daring enough to target Kinu, you might be next, nojya." Frankly, you're hoping they'll try — it'll save you the time hunting those bastards down. Why go to them when you can make them come to you? "Ah, that is one way to see it, nojya. Sometimes I forget that not everyone is a peaceful procurer of goods like I am. Well, if you are going to hunt those who hurt the young lady Otomo, I can only wish you the best of fortune. It will be a relief to not have to worry about being targeted on the roads again." Mm. ] "Stay safe, okay? The roads are getting more dangerous by the day, nojya. We can always partake of The Ways Between, but even so some legwork to the final destination is always needed." ] |[rand |"Truly, I didn't know what to do when Kinu told me to run, nojya. On one hand, my life is clearly nothing compared to hers; on the other hand, if someone like her gives me such an order, I am bound to obey." The little golden fox looks glum. "I didn't know whether to obey or disobey, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]and that bothers me to no end. I'm just glad that she made it out of that confrontation alive, nojya. "Between you and me, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ], would you have forgiven me if... if something had happened to her because I did not disobey her orders to flee?" ...That's a heavily loaded question that you don't know if you can answer. Emotionally, you suspect that you might not be able to forgive Kohaku if something happened to Kinu, despite your daughter's display of self-sacrifice. "I know[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." Kohaku presses her hands against her face, although there's no smile there. "I wouldn't have been able to forgive myself, so... it was a foolish thing to ask, nojya. Each and every fox here in the den would be willing to die for Young Lady Otomo if it came down the choice between their life and hers." You shake your head. Does Kinu really commands that kind of respect? Kohaku gives you a little sad smile. "[pc.ra kitsune |You wear the form his divine lordship gave you so well, sometimes I forget you weren't born one of us, your Eminence. ]But it's more than love and respect, although that certainly makes the efforts more genuine than they ever could have been. It is..." Kohaku's mouth moves as if she's about to speak, then she gives up and settles back with a sigh. "I'm sorry." To see the little chatterbox at a loss for words is a miracle in and of itself, you can't really blame her for that. You'll leave it at one of those cultural differences, then. |"I must still travel through the torii gates and be about my business, nojya. Even though one can take additional precautions, my basic duties must still be carried out with the utmost diligence." That's quite dangerous, given what happened to her. "It is, nojya. Strictly speaking, the colonies are self-sufficient in essential goods, and if it came down to that I could walk on foot in disguise, without my caravan; there is a native village to the south with a reasonable market." Yes, you know. "Luxuries will be in short supply if it comes down to a lockdown on travel through the torii gates, but that's why they're luxuries, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |nojya ]. It's taken a long time for even the seat of the governor to achieve a small amount of comfort, nojya. We colonials are no strangers to hardship, what with living on the frontier, we'll make do without if it comes to that." |You can't help but notice that Kohaku sounds more stiff and uneasy when talking about the matter. "Well... I really wanted to tell both you and High Lady Otomo, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |I really did! ] But then I didn't know if Kinu wanted me to, so... well, that doesn't matter anymore, nojya. Since you know all about it already, I can speak all I want!" You smile and shake your head. It must have been terrible for the little chatterbox not to be able to spread gossip, especially when she was personally involved in the events. Kohaku wiggles her large ears in excitement. "I know, right? I just... it was a harrowing experience, and I'd always considered the Ways Between safe. To be waylaid like that... it's terrifying and exciting at the same time! And to see Young Lady Otomo fight — [kinu.isInari |she must have a will of stone to look such foes in the eye and not flinch, nojya! Like a rock, unbreakable, weighty and striking with terrible force! Indomitable, I think that's what the word is? Yes, yes! |her movements flow like water, the spitting image of her lady mother down to the smallest detail! Perhaps even better, no disrespect to the high lady, of course! Yes, everyone has seen her take instruction from the provost, but to see the young lady go at it in earnest is a sight I will not forget anytime soon, nojya! ]" There you go, that's something of Kohaku's usual excitable self coming back to her. She's not the kind of girl who takes well to being contemplative and morose, so it's nice to see her abuzz with energy again. If she wants to be of use to Kinu, then why doesn't she go and tell everyone about your dearest daughter's exploits? After all, now that the cat's out of the bag, there's no reason to hold back any more, is there? "I'll go do just that, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |nojya ]!" |"Both my life and the lives of everyone on that caravan — we owe them to Young Lady Otomo[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. That is... for her to value my life this much, it is an honor beyond compare, nojya. There's no way I could ever hope to repay her as things stand, but I am still obliged to try." You're not exactly sure how these things work in her culture, but it's undoubtedly a big deal. "Indeed, nojya. Even though High Lady Otomo has officially abdicated her position, everyone still sees her as the den matron's rightful liege, regardless of whatever she may have signed away. And for her heir to take such a personal interest in the preservation of our lives, to be willing to fight for us instead of the other way around..." Kohaku raises her hands to her cheeks. "It is very poignant, nojya. Like a classical tale from an era long ago before the shogunate, when everything was so romanticised." |She's still going out there after all this has happened? "Someone has to, nojya. Luxuries are less of a matter now, but the milk runs continue. Historically, trade and business have still continued in times of war; mere trouble like this should be no problem for a dedicated quartermaster like me[pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence ]. Although..." Although? "Kazuo and Rindo have insisted that I take four of their best — and more importantly, disposable — puppets in addition to my usual retinue when I travel through the Ways Between, nojya. That shouldn't bother me as much as it does, since I use their creations to do heavy lifting here in the storehouse, but I guess it's harder to disguise what they are while out there. I usually have to hide them under a cloth or something in the back of the cart when out amongst other peoples." Well, it's for her own protection. If she's made out to be a target again, Kinu won't be around to rescue her this time. Kohaku gives you a sheepish smile and folds her ears forward. "I know, nojya. I'd certainly not dare ask such a boon from young Lady Otomo twice..." ] ]
rows.translation: [var0 |[rand |有传言称，贵弘在某次外出时看到了一只能够在水面上行走的兽人。你不觉得这很有趣吗，野良？毕竟兽人看起来总是会立刻沉到湖泊或海洋的底部才对[pc.ra orc |我的意思是，看看你现在的样子吧，无意冒犯。 |它们的外观总是那么结实、可靠。 ]我真不敢想象它们会浮得很好。 [party.has arona |阿罗娜轻声笑了起来。你知道，她说的没错。我们不会无缘无故地使用长船的。 ] 嗯，如果有人使用了魔法之类的东西，那么这是完全有可能的。 不，没有魔法，没有神奇的凉鞋，什么都没有。就只是赤脚而已，真的。 嗯…… 我的意思是，我觉得有些极北精灵或许真的能够做到这一点——他们看起来总是那么轻盈、优雅，就连女性也是如此。但这次的情况完全不同。 |上一次收获的红豆真是太棒了。我打算做很多红豆汤团，自己都吃不完呢，诺吉亚！到时候肯定得分给别人，不然它们就会坏掉……不过我并不介意，这倒是个结交朋友的好方法啊！ 她难道从来只想着天妇罗这件事吗？ [party.has kiyoko |在你身旁，清子轻轻地咳嗽了一声。那么，亲爱的。显然，太郎烧对那个女孩来说非常重要。能够偶尔享用自己喜欢的食物，确实是一件很愉快的事情。 哦，那她的会是什么呢？ 哦，有那么几个。我确实很喜欢桃子卷，而且你也知道我们女儿对所有与桃子相关的东西都特别感兴趣，但是……她直视着你的眼睛，然后用她的小舌头舔了舔嘴唇。就像我说的，有几个这样的例子。 ] 琥珀[pc.ra kitsune |她的目光躲开了你的视线，然后在你的注视下坐立不安起来。嗯，我是这样的，我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]。 |哼了一声。当然啦！ ]但从开始到结束，制作天妇罗的过程确实有一种令人惊叹的魅力……准备红豆酱，然后调制面糊……使用我母亲曾经用过的模具，后来它就成了我的……当面糊开始加热时散发出来的香味，真是美妙极了。在出差的过程中，我有机会品尝过很多种美食，但即便是冬城里的美食，也远远比不上我自己做的热天妇罗。 如果你不相信我，或许我可以给你一些看看，诺雅…… 呃，如果你想要的话，大概会直接买下来吧。毕竟得进行等价交换之类的，不能让她就这样把东西送给你的。 [pc.ra kitsune |没关系，我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]诺贾，你让我能够与你一起分享太扬花的美好，这已经让我得到了远远超过我应得的回报。 |确实如此，但你并不受那条特定神律的约束，诺雅。我相信你可以接受这份礼物，而不会觉得欠我什么，对吧？ ]" 呃，好吧…… 就当是免费样品吧，nojya。就像我说的，今年这些红豆真的很不错。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]。" |在之前的几批移民中，其中有一位女性只有一条尾巴，诺雅。你不觉得这很奇怪吗？[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]就连刚出生的小动物也有两条尾巴；发生这种事，她肯定是一只被诅咒的狐妖吧。
