We need harmonious relations with other people as much as anyone else." But they aren't quite dumping outright criminals onto the colonies, are they? "Thank his divine lordship that's not the case, nojya; Nakano would die even more inside if he had to shepherd convicts around. A most shameful and humiliating assignment that would be[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]." |"It's strange to learn about distant history in books and stories, nojya. These lands are so relatively peaceful compared to the stories of the Godswar, it's hard to believe. But then we have people like High Lady Ōtomo and the den matron who lived through it and saw the horrors... hearing the former speak in the plaza about her time centuries ago gives one pause, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady].|doesn't it?]" Hmm, yeah. "I'm personally very glad she's here with us[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. It puts a perspective on things, that no matter how relatively dangerous the frontier is compared to the mostly tamed lands across the ocean it could be much, much worse, nojya." |"Now that the High Lady Ōtomo is with us once more, the den matron is looking a lot more peaceable these days[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. Everyone in the den knows that the former has officially forgiven the latter... the matron's shameful failure to defend her liege is legendary back across the ocean and told by parents to their children as a cautionary tale. "Responsibility flows upwards, status and prestige flow downwards, nojya. I won't lie that a terrible chunk of the colonies' poor reputation is because she is the governor here, and has been so for generations... and it's not because she has governed inadequately or anything. High Lady Ōtomo formally forgiving her won't erase the stain of shame on her name and soul, but it will go a long way to helping everyone once the word gets out." |"High Lady Ōtomo is so elegant and refined in her speech and movements, nojya. I wish I had a little more time to study and practice mimicking her, then I could be as elegant and refined as her whenever I wanted to. But it wouldn't really see that much use, nojya. I wouldn't be able to pull it off back in the Old Country, and here it'd just be weird amongst the natives." Besides... mimicking other people all the time isn't good; one can lose sense of oneself. You do like her energetic little personality as it is, and it'd be a shame to lose that. Kohaku puts her little fingers together. "Well, I suppose that is true[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. But even so... aah, the sheer grace in being able to move like that, it makes my heart flutter. It is an attraction on such a higher level than any simple charms I could possess..." ] "

rows.original: [kinu.isInari |[rand |"Eeeeh. You're Kinu's [pc.mf|dad|mom], right[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]?" That's correct. Is something the matter? "Well, Kinu has been getting kinda close to Hitoshi, nojya. Well, not just kind of close, real close, to be exact. Like, um —" Kohaku's face colors and she starts tapping her knuckles together — "this close, nojya. I saw it myself when I went with the team to pick up the pickles yesterday..." Pray, do tell. What did Kinu get up to? You know that she's trying to be a good girl, but when it comes down to it, her mother did birth her and all... "It was so romantic, nojya. Like, she was hugging him all the time while he was loading the pickle jars onto the wheelbarrow, just pressing herself against him and flattening her huge chest against his muscular body. There in the early morning sun with the field work going on in the background... all we'd have needed was a good musical backdrop and it'd have been perfect, nojya. So moving — perfect setup for a romantic comedy." Oh no, Kohaku's got that stupid smile of hers again, that truly idiotic open-mouthed swoon that the little kitsune always gets when she starts pairing people up in her head. Oh, she's entirely convinced that what she saw happened, but that has absolutely no bearing whatsoever on how much truth there is in the tale she's telling. Well, was there anything else your firstborn kitsune daughter was doing? "Um? Well, Kinu was totally touching him. Not inappropriately, but — well, maybe just a bit. But not enough that I or any of the storehouse team could've outright accused her of being lewd instead of merely being friendly and affectionate, nojya. It didn't help that Hitoshi didn't seem to care at all... he's such an enormous man, nojya. Kinu was practically clinging off him, and he didn't even notice her weight. Ehehehehe. That'll make for some interesting situations once they really become an item, won't it?" Wait wait wait wait wait. What — "Eh? Everyone already knows that those two are going steady, nojya. It's all over the den — all over the — oh. Ah. Um. Kinu didn't tell you[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]? I figured her parents would have known she was getting close to a boy, even if they didn't know the details..." [party.has kiyoko |A small hiss behind you draws your attention, a sound that instinctively sets your teeth on edge. What fur your beloved kitsune wife has is all fluffed up, her eyes narrowed and lips twisted in a furious grimace. You've never seen her this absolutely livid before — [kiyoko.pregStage 1|it's not healthy for anyone, let alone pregnant women to be this upset... |already you can visualise the gears turning in her head, cranking out a devious, ill-tempered and unbelievably cruel ruse to be inflicted upon someone... ] Um... ? "Don't worry, beloved," Kiyoko whispers. "Let's just continue with our adventure — there'll be plenty of time for me to deal with a wayward child later on. I'm not about to let her ruin our time together to boot." ] Yes, yes. You'll... you'll have to see about talking to Kinu sometime. Clearly there's been a breakdown in communication somewhere, and she wasn't trying to hide personal details of her life from you. |"Kinu always comes in every week or other week and orders a huge sack of salt, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|nojya]. I mean —" she spreads her arms as wide as she can — "a really, really huge sack of salt. She may be as short as I am, but Kinu can really carry a lot when she puts her mind to it. She's a strong girl like me! "I don't have that much reason to complain, since she's always willing to repay more than what the salt's worth in produce, but one person requisitioning too much of one thing can cause problems, nojya. I haven't had the heart to tell her that she should slow down some[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], but since I have to get salt from across the ocean it has the potential to go out of hand if it gets any worse. Some of the exploratory digs have managed to find rock salt, but not in the amounts necessary to be really exploitable in any meaningful manner." What does she do with all the salt, anyway? You've looked around Kiyoko's den, and there aren't any huge mountains of salt lying around, so presumably all the stuff has to end up being used somewhere, right? "I hear it's pickles, nojya." Pickles, huh? "Well, one way of doing it is to pack jars or barrels with salt, let the juices leach out of the fruits or veggies being pickled, and allow the stuff to stew. It's... different from using brine or vinegar, nojya, and uses a bit more salt. But even so... that would mean a lot of pickles, too. I know Kinu likes making and eating pickles, especially with her rice, but I'm not sure if that still warrants that much salt..." |"Kinu does a lot of good work around the den, so everyone respects her for that. The matron places a lot of value on honest, practical work, and her being able to contribute in this fashion even though she's got her own fields back at home to tend to really serve as an inspiration to us all, nojya. They say it really isn't work if you're doing something you enjoy doing[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], and most people take that as something you just pay lip service to... but I think she really does enjoy it, and familiarity hasn't bred contempt so far. I like talking to people, but even for me there're days where I just want to laze around in the storehouse and eat taiyaki, nojya." It's good that your daughter is getting popular — one of the concerns about her growing up in the Astral Plane was that she wouldn't get to interact with anyone outside of her immediate family. "We-ll[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]... she's pretty quiet, and to be frank people prefer her that way. Kinu... she tends to speak her mind a little too honestly for a lot of peoples' comfort, nojya. Honesty is one thing, tact is another..." You did teach her to be honest with herself and her feelings, as well as have a strong sense of right and wrong. It's not surprising that she turned out this way. "Ah. Well[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], it can't be helped, then. Still, it's not as if she's disliked or anything, nojya. It's just that she could be more popular if she wanted to be... but she doesn't care for that kind of thing, right?" |"Your daughter is a very pious young woman, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|nojya]. Every other day, I see her pass by the storehouse on the way to the shrine to make offerings. Like my mother would say, it's great to see young people respectful of divinity and all, nojya." Maybe she's going there to see Mai. "Well, there's no reason it can't be both[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. She is very good friends with Mai. Little wonder that she always makes her trips in the evening after field work and all..." Hmm... "She's just a very spiritual person like Hitoshi, nojya. That's the impression I get, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|anyway], and it's probably why they're so compatible with each other. That calm ability to be completely at peace with oneself, others and the world... it's not my style, but I can see the merits in it." |"The sticky rice that Kinu brings in is the best, nojya! We get to make all kinds of fun stuff with it, especially all kinds of mochi — the taste! The texture! Even without any kind of filling or flavoring, it'd be good enough to eat on its own[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]! Everyone can't get enough of it, and no sooner has she brought in more for salt or oil that it vanishes; I've got orders to backfill up to here!" Kohaku raises her hands up to the tips of her ears. Is it that good compared to what they produce over here? "Eeeeh? Everything that Kinu produces is pretty great, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|nojya]! It's just that the sticky rice is one of the best, and she manages to get a whole one or two extra harvests in any growing season! No one knows how she manages to get it done, nojya, but she does! Giving her a helping hand in getting her home and fields set up was the best investment the den matron ever made, nojya!" ] |[rand |"Eeeeh. The young lady Ōtomo has been coming over at least twice every week to use the womens' baths for a little while now." That's interesting. You're pretty sure that the baths at Kiyoko's place are more than adequate. Well, maybe it's better to wash up on the way home than afterwards, and it sounds like more a social activity than anything else. "Well, she says that the atmosphere we have here is very nice, and she's not wrong. We take a lot of pride in how spick and span they keep the place; it's better than drawing water from a well and dumping it over your head. But I think that's not all..." Oh? "Merchants have to be able to read their customers, after all. Ehehehe — it's no secret that your little girl's tits are absolutely massive[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], and her figure befitting a lady of her stature. Only Mikoto is more pronounced than she is, and I'm pretty sure they've 'accidentally' swapped clothes on occasion. The men are disturbed, the women are envious. I'm not sure who she learned to flaunt her stuff from, but she does it very effectively." Ohhhh snap. Your little girl's growing up and discovering what she can make other people do. Well, she is her mother's daughter, after all — an incredibly beautiful lady from an impeccable lineage, refined to the point where a single movement gracefully displays her elegance. Pfahahahaha. Kohaku chews her lip and shifts her eyes, ears twitching. And what about her? Is little Kohaku jealous? "Eeeeeh. There's no point in getting envious over what I could never have had in the first place, nojya. Besides, with someone as small as me, they'd really look out of place. I have good hips; I should play to my strengths instead of wanting things I can never have, nojya." That's nice. But she and Kinu are roughly just as tall... if it's just height, why would a nice rack look good on Kinu and not her? Kohaku's lip-chewing intensifies as she starts twiddling her fingers. "[pc.ra kitsune|Now you're just teasing me, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|You meanie]..." |"The young lady Ōtomo looks so elegant and refined all the time, just like her mother. That being said, all the things she uses to look that way are surprisingly simple, nojya. I would know, because she requisitions them from me. That someone can use simple oils and common herbs to make her tails so lustrous... it speaks volumes about the nature of beauty and glamour[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]." And that would be? "That they're not things that you can acquire or buy, nojya. Any good merchant will tell you that. Looking good on the surface will get your foot in the door, perhaps, but in order to cinch the sale you need to at least be able to feign sincerity. The best ones get to the point where they believe their own pitch themselves. Beauty and glamour, as with so many other things... it's about who you are, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|nojya]. Not something you can buy, something you can borrow, or something you can steal. And the young lady Ōtomo has it in spades." |"Oh! Something interesting happened the other day[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. The young lady Ōtomo challenged me to a game of shogi in the evening after I got off work. I didn't see any reason to say no, so I went ahead and accepted, nojya." If it's Kinu, you can already guess as to how it went. Didn't she know how good Kinu is at strategy board games? "Oh, of course I knew[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]! I don't pride myself on being the den gossip for nothing! But you see, I managed to get her interested in perhaps laying her hands on an imported set straight from the Old Country, nojya. More authentic. If I cinch that kind of trade with someone like her, losing twenty times over would be worth it!" You sigh. Kinu might be smart, but you're reminded just how easily she can be blindsided due to her upbringing. It's only a matter of time before your daughter catches on to Kohaku's shenanigans, but until that happens, this little fox is going to make out like a bandit. Well... it'll be good for Kinu in the long run. Better it happen to her in the guise of a tiny little fox like Kohaku instead of a situation where being hoodwinked really matters. |"Hmm... oh! As part of her duties with the matron, the young lady Otomo will come out to the treetop plaza twice every week and give lessons to any kits who want to attend, nojya. Traditionally, it is usually those from priestly clans who would impart this kind of education in addition to what kits are taught at home, but no one is going to deny a well-educated princess like her, eeh? By all accounts, her lessons are useful and easy to understand, so it's quite clear why the matron has her doing this sort of thing[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]." If Kinu's anything like her mother, it's not surprising that she has a way with children in particular. Training for the future, while being useful at it in the process... how practical. "The kits who do show up don't mind coming, especially since she passes along to them all the sweets she receives from others, nojya. I suppose that's one way to get the young interested in learning..." |"Oh! The young lady Otomo is known for being incredibly beautiful[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]! She has turned many heads ever since she made her debut here... I'm sure that if she and Nakano weren't an item, she'd have suitors lining up at her door all the way into her night, nojya!" And is little Kohaku jealous? "Eeeeh? Me? Jealous? Maybe a little[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], but attracting so much attention makes me a little uneasy, nojya. Is it a sin to be as beautiful as the young lady Otomo? Maybe not, but I'd feel as if I were being punished for having committed one, Having eyes on me all the time..." she shivers. "It's not something I want, nojya. The young lady Otomo is well-equipped to deal with that kind of attention, and I'm not." ] ]
rows.translation: [kinu.isInari |[rand |呃……你是小娟的[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]对吧？[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]？" 没错。有什么问题吗？ 嗯，小娟最近和仁的关系变得有点亲密了，nojya。嗯，不仅仅是有点亲密而已真实的确切地说，是靠近。就是，嗯……琥珀的脸色瞬间变了，她开始用指关节敲打起来—— 就差这么一点了，诺雅。昨天我和团队一起去取腌菜的时候，亲眼看到的…… 快说说吧，小娟到底干了什么？你知道她一直都想做个好女孩，但说到底，还是她妈妈的影响太大确实生下她，以及她的一切…… 真是太浪漫了，诺亚。他就那么把腌黄瓜罐子装到手推车上，而她却一直紧紧抱着他，将自己的身体紧紧贴在他的肌肉结实的背上。在清晨的阳光下，背景中还有田野里的劳作声……只要再配上一段优美的音乐，那就完美了，诺亚。真是太感人肺腑了——简直是浪漫喜剧的完美场景啊。 哦不，小红又露出了她那副愚蠢的笑容，每当她开始在脑海中为别人牵线搭桥时，总是会露出那种傻乎乎的、张大嘴巴的表情。哦，她完全相信自己所看到的一切都是真实发生的，但这也丝毫不能说明她所讲述的故事有多少真实性。 那么，你的第一个女儿——那只狐妖女孩，还做了些什么呢？ 嗯？其实，小娟确实有在触碰他。并不是不恰当的触碰，但是……嗯，也许有点过分吧。不过还不至于到让我或者仓库团队的任何人都能够直接指责她行为不端的地步，只能说她的举动有些过于亲昵而已，nojya。更糟糕的是，仁似乎根本不在乎……他身材那么高大，nojya。小娟几乎是紧贴着他，而他甚至都没有感觉到她的存在。呵呵呵呵，等他们以后……肯定会出现一些有趣的情况的。真的变成一件物品，不是吗？ 等等等等等等。什么—— 呃？大家早就知道那两个人在交往了，真的。这个消息已经传遍了整个圈子——哦，对了。小娟应该没有告诉你吧[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]我想她的父母应该会知道她正在和一个男孩交往吧，即使他们不知道具体的细节…… [party.has kiyoko |你身后传来一阵轻微的嘶嘶声，这个声音立刻让你警觉起来，本能地让你感到一阵紧张。你那可爱的九尾狐妻子的全身毛发都竖了起来，她的眼睛紧闭着，嘴唇扭曲成一副愤怒的表情。你从未见过她如此愤怒过[kiyoko.pregStage 1|对于任何人来说，这种情绪波动都是不健康的，更不用说孕妇了…… |你可以想象，她的脑子里正在飞速转动，想出一个个阴险、恶毒且残忍至极的计谋，准备用来对付别人…… ] 嗯……？ 别担心，亲爱的。清子轻声说道。我们继续我们的冒险吧——以后有的是时间来管教那个任性的孩子。我可不会让她破坏我们在一起的时光。 ] 是的，没错。你得找时间跟小娟谈谈。显然， somewhere沟通出现了问题，她并不是故意要隐瞒自己生活中的私人细节。 |小娟几乎每周都会来，每次都会订购一大袋盐。 [pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|诺雅]我的意思是——她尽可能地张开双臂—— 真的，真的真是个了不起的女孩。她虽然和我一样个子不高，但一旦下定决心，她真的能承受很多事情。她和我一样，是个坚强的女孩！ 其实我并没有太多理由抱怨，因为她总是愿意用价值远超过盐价的物品来偿还我的帮助，但是如果有人一次性索要过多的东西，确实会惹麻烦，诺雅。我实在没有勇气告诉她应该适可而止一些。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]但由于我必须从大洋的另一边获取盐分，如果情况进一步恶化，这个问题就有可能变得难以控制。虽然一些探索性挖掘活动确实找到了一些岩盐，但这些盐的储量远远不足以实现真正的商业化开采。 她把那些盐都用来做什么呢？你已经仔细检查了清子的藏身处，那里并没有堆积如山的盐，所以这些盐肯定都被用在了什么地方吧？ 我听说那些是腌菜，诺贾。 泡菜，哈？ 嗯，有一种方法就是把盐装入罐子或桶中，让腌制的水果或蔬菜中的汁液渗出来，然后让这些食材慢慢腌制。这种方法……与使用盐水或醋不同，需要使用更多的盐。不过，这样一来……也需要腌制大量的食材啊。我知道小娟很喜欢制作和食用腌制品，尤其是搭配米饭吃，但我不确定是否真的需要用到那么多盐…… |小娟在巢穴里做了很多有益的工作，因此大家都很尊重她。族长非常重视那些诚实且务实的行为，而她虽然在家里还有自己的事务要处理，却依然能够以这种方式为团队做出贡献，这确实给我们所有人树立了榜样，nojya。人们都说，如果做的是自己喜欢的事情，那就根本算不上是工作。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]大多数人认为这只是嘴上说说而已……但我觉得她真的是乐在其中，而且到目前为止，熟悉并不会让人产生反感。我喜欢和别人聊天，但就连我也有不想出门，只想在仓库里懒洋洋地坐着，吃着太卷饼和野菜的时候。 你的女儿越来越受欢迎，这真是件好事——当初担心她在星界中成长时，会遇到的一个问题就是她无法与自己的直系亲属之外的人进行交流。 我们——[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]……她性格相当内敛，说实话，人们反而更喜欢她这样的性格。至于小娟……她说话总是太直率了，这让很多人感到不适。诚实是一回事，但讲究分寸才是另一回事…… 你确实教导她要对自己和自己的感受保持诚实，同时也要有明确的是非观念。因此，她变成现在这个样子也就不足为奇了。 啊，好吧[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]那也没办法了。不过，她也不是那种会……的人。不喜欢或者别的什么，诺雅。只是如果她愿意的话，她本可以更受欢迎的……但她并不在乎这类事情，对吧？ |你的女儿是一位非常虔诚的年轻女子。 [pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|诺雅]每隔一天，我就会看到她路过仓库，然后前往神社进行祭拜。用我母亲的话来说，看到年轻人如此尊重神灵，真是件好事啊，诺雅。 也许她去那里是为了见舞。 嗯，没有理由不能两者兼备。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]她是和舞是非常要好的朋友。难怪她总是在野外工作结束后，晚上才去旅行…… 嗯…… 她就像仁一样，是一个非常富有灵性的人，诺贾。我就是这么觉得的。 [pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|无论如何]这也可能是它们之间能够如此兼容的原因吧。那种能够让自己、他人以及整个世界都处于平静状态的能力……虽然这不是我的风格，但我确实能认识到它的优点。 |小娟带来的糯米真是太棒了，nojya！我们可以用它做出各种各样有趣的东西，尤其是各种团子——那味道啊，那口感啊！即使不加任何馅料或调味料，单独吃就已经非常美味了。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]大家都对它垂涎三尺，她刚买来一些用来调味，这些东西就立刻被抢光了；我接到的命令是必须把库存补充到这个水平才行！小白将双手举到了耳尖的位置。 rows.raw: " [kinu.isInari |[rand |"Eeeeh. You're Kinu's [pc.mf|dad|mom], right[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]?" That's correct. Is something the matter? "Well, Kinu has been getting kinda close to Hitoshi, nojya. Well, not just kind of close, real close, to be exact. Like, um —" Kohaku's face colors and she starts tapping her knuckles together — "this close, nojya. I saw it myself when I went with the team to pick up the pickles yesterday..." Pray, do tell. What did Kinu get up to? You know that she's trying to be a good girl, but when it comes down to it, her mother did birth her and all... "It was so romantic, nojya. Like, she was hugging him all the time while he was loading the pickle jars onto the wheelbarrow, just pressing herself against him and flattening her huge chest against his muscular body. There in the early morning sun with the field work going on in the background... all we'd have needed was a good musical backdrop and it'd have been perfect, nojya. So moving — perfect setup for a romantic comedy." Oh no, Kohaku's got that stupid smile of hers again, that truly idiotic open-mouthed swoon that the little kitsune always gets when she starts pairing people up in her head. Oh, she's entirely convinced that what she saw happened, but that has absolutely no bearing whatsoever on how much truth there is in the tale she's telling. Well, was there anything else your firstborn kitsune daughter was doing? "Um? Well, Kinu was totally touching him. Not inappropriately, but — well, maybe just a bit. But not enough that I or any of the storehouse team could've outright accused her of being lewd instead of merely being friendly and affectionate, nojya. It didn't help that Hitoshi didn't seem to care at all... he's such an enormous man, nojya. Kinu was practically clinging off him, and he didn't even notice her weight. Ehehehehe. That'll make for some interesting situations once they really become an item, won't it?" Wait wait wait wait wait. What — "Eh? Everyone already knows that those two are going steady, nojya. It's all over the den — all over the — oh. Ah. Um. Kinu didn't tell you[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]? I figured her parents would have known she was getting close to a boy, even if they didn't know the details..." You did teach her to be honest with herself and her feelings, as well as have a strong sense of right and wrong. It's not surprising that she turned out this way. "Ah. Well[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], it can't be helped, then. Still, it's not as if she's disliked or anything, nojya. You're pretty sure that the baths at Kiyoko's place are more than adequate. "Well, she says that the atmosphere we have here is very nice, and she's not wrong. We take a lot of pride in how spick and span they keep the place; it's better than drawing water from a well and dumping it over your head. But I think that's not all..." Oh? "Merchants have to be able to read their customers, after all. Kohaku chews her lip and shifts her eyes, ears twitching. And what about her? Is little Kohaku jealous? "Eeeeeh. "[pc.ra kitsune|Now you're just teasing me, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|You meanie]..." |"The young lady Ōtomo looks so elegant and refined all the time, just like her mother. rows.original: [rand |[var0 |[rand |"I didn't say this, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]but I think Mai secretly resents the fact that Miko's had children of her own, nojya." You couldn't tell, but then again Mai is always so cold under that exterior that reading her can be impossible at times. No doubt Kohaku is more familiar with her, though. "Oh, it's not just me, other people have noticed as well. They say it's because she can't smoke as she pleases in her own home anymore, since there're kits around, but I think it's more than that, nojya. The two sisters have been joined at the hip ever since they were born, and they still sleep in the same bed to this day... again, I didn't say this, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]but it feels like the kids are coming between them, and instead of being Miko's sister she's now just the aunt of her kits, nojya..." That's... well. Sobering. But these things happen, as bitter as they may be. "You have to wonder if Miko will feel the same way when Mai has kits of her own. Imagine this... now what's going to happen when either of the two get married, nojya? I wouldn't want to be the one caught between the two of them, no no!" Okay, you can't help but chuckle a bit at that. But clearly the answer to that is to set them up with another twin pair, so they'll all go at each other. Problem solved! Kohaku's eyes shift at that; you can clearly see the gears turning in her head along with perhaps the clink of coin. "An interesting proposition[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. I'll be sure to keep it in mind if I find any likely suitors for the pair, nojya." W-wait, you weren't entirely serious — "It's a good idea, nojya." |"I think it's a fine thing that Miko's had kits, nojya." Really? Even given all the, uh, personal circumstances surrounding the pregnancy and birth? You'd have expected that the general social consensus would have been one of quiet disdain, even if everyone is too polite to say it out loud given Miko's social station. "Well, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]it's less on a personal level than it is on a social level. How do I put it?" Kohaku tilts her head to the side and lowers a ear. "For Miko or anyone else to have kits and be happy about it, it means that she's got confidence in the future, nojya. I don't think there've been any births in the colonies now for a handful of years now — while I don't manage to travel to all the camps on a regular basis, especially the most outlying ones, I still manage to get most of them. It's important that people have hope, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship. |isn't it? ]" Well, morale is important to any endeavor, that's true. But some might argue that Miko having kits might not be the best way to go about it. "I don't know about that, nojya. One of the local leaders shows such confidence in the future that she's willing to have kits under such circumstances... it's a lot of skin in the game[pc.ra kitsune |, isn't it, your Eminence? |! ] Leading by example, although we don't want people to follow the likes of Miko exactly..." That, you can agree with. |"Oh! Oh[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]! I heard that the matron finally picked Mai over Miko as her successor, nojya! Isn't that so exciting? rows.original: [var0 |"While the den matron doesn't really have much use for merchandise out of the ordinary, she'll ask me on occasion to run messages and letters for her, especially to her clan holdings out in the provinces. She's technically in exile, although no one is going to stop her if she wants to step through the portal for a bit. Even so... it's still better that I do the message running, nojya. "It's... not so bad when it's just one leap[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ], but making five or six gate jumps in a day upsets the stomach terribly and makes me all kinds of nauseous, nojya. Still, I soldier on bravely in service of the Kurokawa clan. The shame of emptying your stomach by the roadside is nothing compared to the shame of being unable to fulfill the task laid out before you by your superior, let alone the den matron or even worse, the governor of the western imperial colonies." That's... quite dedicated of her. "Only to be expected in the line of duty, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |nojya ]!" |"One way or the other, everyone owes the den matron a lot[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. For example, take me — I owe her for my position, my education, and a place to stay while having the chance to do useful work. It's these obligations that make things go as smoothly as they do in the den — equivalent exchange and all make sure you give as good as you get and get as good as you give. That's why it's such an important divinely mandated law to live by. Everyone who's a good egg respects the matron and her opinions, and we don't care for what bad eggs think, nojya." |"I kind of feel sorry for the den matron, nojya. Back in the Old Country, they use her as a cautionary tale as to what can happen to you if you happen to commit some of the most unforgivable sins in the land and just happen to catch the Trickster's eye. If he takes a personal interest in your case... expect the sentencing to be fair, but ultimately cruel in ways you hadn't imagined possible[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. She's not the stuff of myths and legends — anyone can make the trip to the colonies and see that she's still around, and that just drives home the point all the more, nojya. What she allowed to happen was truly a failure of the highest order that under any circumstances would have demanded at least her own life, but..." You don't know all the cultural implications, but it seems to you like a very heavy-handed case. "People can repent, but the scales still need to be balanced and penance made." Kohaku sighs and plants her elbows on the table. "Nothing can be done about it, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |nojya ]." |"The den matron has an intense dislike of loafers and busywork, nojya. This den might be the most comfortable and secure settlement in the entirety of the western colonies, and even so life is much more hands-on than a small city back in the Old Country. The dens are kept to sizes small enough for everyone to be familiar with each others' faces and quickly sort out the lazybones who aren't pulling their own weight. "The same goes for busywork. If people aren't actually doing any work, she doesn't want them shuffling around for appearances' sake — that's common on the other side of the ocean, but she won't have any of it here, nojya. If the day's tasks are properly dealt with and there's nothing more to be done, I'm to let everyone off early instead of keeping them here just because they're supposed to be there." That's a rather nice way of looking at it. Heck, you can think of several Marchers who would give people busywork just to keep people occupied... "As the gossip goes, it was a problem when the matron was a shrine maiden back at her clan's holdings. She'd finish her tasks for the day or for the time being, and simply be assigned some piece of busywork like already sweeping up the path she'd just finished clearing. It got to the point where she learned to work not well or quickly, but to finish her tasks right on time to avoid being given more to do. That's an attitude she absolutely wants to stamp out as colonial governor[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. We need people who will be motivated to actually do quick, efficient work right the first time, because nature and natives alike aren't going to let up on us." |"Eheheh. There is one thing the den matron asks me to get when I'm out." Yes? "She has a weakness for youkan, one of the main ingredients of which is agar or gelatin. The natives here don't know how to make gelatin from animals, and we're a long way from the ocean to get any seaweed. Importing it is hence the only option... at least we can get adzuki beans and honey locally. I do my best, nojya. Even if she doesn't need to eat anymore as a yasha, it's one of the few mercies she's allowed to indulge in after more than two centuries of not-death. I... feel sorry for her[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ], so I always make sure to have some powdered agar on hand, if nothing else." ... Kohaku's face falls. "I'm sorry, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |nojya ]. It's easy to get depressed when talking about the den matron." |The moment the den matron's name leaves your mouth, Kohaku's normally-jovial demeanor sours. Turning her eyes towards you with an uncharacteristically dour expression, the plucky little fox appears deathly serious. "[pc.ra kitsune |Your Eminence |[pc.name] ]... I do hope you're aware that some, ah... rumors have been spreading regarding yourself and the matron, nojya." Despite your best efforts, you can't hold back a slight wince. Guess the rumor mill's already started up... what has she heard? Kohaku's concerned expression doesn't diminish in the least, and there's an uncomfortable atmosphere in the cramped storehouse. She shifts a little, averting her eyes as she mutters out a reply. "W-well...[pc.ra kitsune | forgive me, your Eminence, but | ] it was said that the two of you, ah... had 'relations', nojya." You see... and who, pray tell, was saying that? Instantly, Kohaku begins stammering awkwardly, doing her level best to avoid giving you a straight answer. "Ah, it– um, well, I had, um... it's just the local talk, n-nothing more. Rumors are notoriously hard to verify, nojya, let alone track down their source." ...Right. "Ah, and even if such a thing were true, I would scarcely be one to judge, of course!" [kohaku.anyKids |Turning her gaze towards your daughter, napping quietly, Kohaku mutters softly. "[silly |I just hope your proclivities haven't been passed down |Hopefully, those rumors don't persist long enough to trouble our daughter ]. Such a thing would be troublesome indeed, nojya." |." Kohaku relaxes a bit, her smile returning. "People are free to live their lives as they see fit, nojya; you're no exception to that." ] Just as quickly as it arrived, Kohaku's grim mood passes. Smiling at you, the diminutive kitsune clears her throat, before speaking once more. "At any rate, what else had you wished to speak about, nojya?" ]
rows.translation: [var0 |虽然那位巢穴的女首领其实并不太需要那些普通的商品，但她偶尔会让我帮她传递消息和信件，尤其是寄往她那些位于各省的族人领地。严格来说，她现在处于流放状态，不过如果她想穿过传送门去那些地方，也没人会阻止她。不过……还是由我来负责这些传递工作比较好，诺雅。 只要是一次跳跃的话……其实也没那么糟糕。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]不过，一天之内进行五到六次这样的跳跃确实会让人肠胃不适，感到一阵阵恶心，真是难受极了。不过，为了黑川家族，我还是勇敢地坚持着。在路边吐得一干二净，这种羞耻感与无法完成上级布置的任务相比，简直算不了什么；更不用说让家族首领或更糟糕的，是西部帝国殖民地的总督失望了。 她真是……太用心了。 这是在执行任务时意料之中的事。 [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] |诺雅 ]！" |不管怎样，每个人都欠那位巢穴女主人很多。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]比如说我吧——我的职位、受教育的机会，以及有地方住、还能做有意义的工作，这一切都欠她的。正是这些义务，才使得一切能够像在那个群体里那样顺利进行——这种等价的交换确保了每个人都能得到自己应得的，同时也付出自己应尽的。因此，遵守这一法则才是如此重要，因为它仿佛是上天赋予我们的准则。每一个正直的人都会尊重族长和她的意见，至于那些坏人怎么想，我们才不在乎呢，nojya。 |我其实挺同情那位巢穴女首领，诺雅的。在那个古老的国家，人们用她的故事来警示人们：如果你犯了这个地方最不可饶恕的罪行，而又恰好引起了那个狡猾者的注意……那么，无论判决结果多么公平，最终带来的惩罚都会是你根本无法想象的残酷。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]她根本不是那些神话传说中的传奇人物——任何人都可以前往殖民地亲眼看到她依然活着，这一事实反而更加清楚地证明了这一点，诺雅。她所允许发生的一切，确实是一次极其严重的失败，在任何情况下，这种失败至少应该让她付出生命的代价，但是…… 你并不了解其中所有的文化含义，但在你看来，这个处理方式似乎过于严厉了。 人们可以忏悔，但仍然需要让天平重新恢复平衡，并付出相应的赎罪代价。琥珀叹了口气，将肘部放在桌子上。对此无能为力， [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] |诺雅 ]。" |这个聚居地的领导者极其厌恶那些游手部好闲、不务正业的人，诺雅。虽然这个聚居地可能是整个西部殖民地中最舒适、最安全的栖息地，但生活节奏仍然比旧国的小城市要忙碌得多。我们把这些聚居地控制在适当的规模范围内，这样每个人都能熟悉彼此的面孔，也能迅速识别出那些不努力工作、逃避责任的人。 忙乱的工作也是如此。如果人们实际上并没有在认真工作，她就不会允许他们只是为了表面好看而无所事事地忙来忙去——这种做法在海洋的对岸很常见，但在这里她是绝对不会允许的，nojya。如果当天的任务已经妥善完成，没有其他事情需要处理了，我就应该让所有人早点下班，而不是仅仅因为规定要求他们留在那里，就强迫他们继续待着。 这么说来确实挺有道理的。说真的，有好多“引导者”就是专门通过布置一些琐碎的任务来让人们保持忙碌状态…… 据传闻，这个问题其实可以追溯到她还是族中祭司少女的时候。她每天完成当天的工作后，往往会被安排一些琐碎的任务，比如重新清扫自己刚刚清理过的道路。久而久之，她逐渐养成了这样一种习惯：不求把工作做得好或快，只要能按时完成任务就行，这样就能避免被分配更多的工作。而作为殖民地的总督，她绝对不能容忍这种态度的存在。[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]我们需要那些有动力能够一次性完成快速、高效工作的人，因为无论是自然环境还是当地居民，都不会给我们任何宽容或机会。 |嘿嘿嘿，窝主让我出去的时候买一样东西。 嗯？ 她有一个弱点幽玄其中的主要成分之一就是琼脂或明胶。这里的土著人们并不知道如何从动物身上提取明胶，而我们距离海洋也很远，根本无法获取海藻。因此，进口明胶就成了唯一的办法……至少我们还可以在当地买到小豆和蜂蜜。我会尽我最大的努力的，诺贾。虽然身为夜叉，她已不必进食，但经历两个多世纪的不死岁月后，这已是她能够享受的少数慰藉之一。我……真同情她[pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] ]因此，我总是会准备一些琼脂粉在手边，至少这样总没坏处。 琥珀的脸沉了下来。对不起， [pc.ra kitsune |我的[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ] |诺雅 ]一提到那个女头目，就很容易让人感到沮丧。 |当你说出那只母狐妖的名字的那一刻，琥珀原本欢快的心情立刻变得阴沉起来。她以一种不同寻常的严肃表情将目光转向你，这只勇敢的小狐妖此刻显得格外认真。[pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |[pc.name] ]……我真心希望你能够知道，有些关于你和女院长诺雅的传闻正在四处流传。” 尽管你已经尽力避免，但还是忍不住微微皱起了眉头。看来那些谣言已经开始传开了…… 她听到了什么？ 小白的担忧神情丝毫没有减轻，狭小的仓库里弥漫着一种尴尬的气氛。她微微挪动了一下身子，避开了视线，低声回答道。 嗯……[pc.ra kitsune | 请原谅我，阁下，但是…… | ]有人说你们两个，啊……有某种关系，诺雅。 你知道吗……究竟是谁说的这种话呢？ 科哈克立刻结结巴巴地开始说话，竭力避免给出一个直接的答案。 啊，这个嘛……其实只是些当地的传言而已，并没有其他意思。谣言本来就很难被证实真实性，更别说追踪它们的来源了。” ……对吧。 “啊，就算真的有这样的事情是确实，我当然也不太适合担任评判者的角色！ [kohaku.anyKids |将目光转向你正在安静地午睡的女儿，小红轻声说道。[silly |我只希望你的那些癖好没有遗传下来。 |希望那些谣言不会持续太久，以免给我们的女儿带来麻烦。 ]这种事情确实会带来很多麻烦，诺雅。 |琥珀稍微放松了一些，她的笑容重新浮现起来，说道：‘人们都有权按照自己的方式生活，诺贾；你也不例外。 ] 就在它出现的同时，小红那阴郁的情绪也消失了。这个小小的狐妖对你笑了笑，清了清嗓子，然后再次开口说道： “无论如何，你还有什么想说的吗，野矢？ ]
rows.raw: " [var0 |"While the den matron doesn't really have much use for merchandise out of the ordinary, she'll ask me on occasion to run messages and letters for her, especially to her clan holdings out in the provinces. She's technically in exile, although no one is going to stop her if she wants to step through the portal for a bit. Even so... it's still better that I do the message running, nojya. "It's... not so bad when it's just one leap[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ], but making five or six gate jumps in a day upsets the stomach terribly and makes me all kinds of nauseous, nojya. Still, I soldier on bravely in service of the Kurokawa clan. The shame of emptying your stomach by the roadside is nothing compared to the shame of being unable to fulfill the task laid out before you by your superior, let alone the den matron or even worse, the governor of the western imperial colonies." That's... quite dedicated of her. "Only to be expected in the line of duty, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |nojya ]!" |"One way or the other, everyone owes the den matron a lot[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. For example, take me — I owe her for my position, my education, and a place to stay while having the chance to do useful work. It's these obligations that make things go as smoothly as they do in the den — equivalent exchange and all make sure you give as good as you get and get as good as you give. That's why it's such an important divinely mandated law to live by. Everyone who's a good egg respects the matron and her opinions, and we don't care for what bad eggs think, nojya." |"I kind of feel sorry for the den matron, nojya. Back in the Old Country, they use her as a cautionary tale as to what can happen to you if you happen to commit some of the most unforgivable sins in the land and just happen to catch the Trickster's eye. If he takes a personal interest in your case... expect the sentencing to be fair, but ultimately cruel in ways you hadn't imagined possible[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. She's not the stuff of myths and legends — anyone can make the trip to the colonies and see that she's still around, and that just drives home the point all the more, nojya. What she allowed to happen was truly a failure of the highest order that under any circumstances would have demanded at least her own life, but..." You don't know all the cultural implications, but it seems to you like a very heavy-handed case. "People can repent, but the scales still need to be balanced and penance made." Kohaku sighs and plants her elbows on the table. "Nothing can be done about it, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |nojya ]." |"The den matron has an intense dislike of loafers and busywork, nojya. This den might be the most comfortable and secure settlement in the entirety of the western colonies, and even so life is much more hands-on than a small city back in the Old Country. The dens are kept to sizes small enough for everyone to be familiar with each others' faces and quickly sort out the lazybones who aren't pulling their own weight. "The same goes for busywork. If people aren't actually doing any work, she doesn't want them shuffling around for appearances' sake — that's common on the other side of the ocean, but she won't have any of it here, nojya. If the day's tasks are properly dealt with and there's nothing more to be done, I'm to let everyone off early instead of keeping them here just because they're supposed to be there." That's a rather nice way of looking at it. Heck, you can think of several Marchers who would give people busywork just to keep people occupied... "As the gossip goes, it was a problem when the matron was a shrine maiden back at her clan's holdings. She'd finish her tasks for the day or for the time being, and simply be assigned some piece of busywork like already sweeping up the path she'd just finished clearing. It got to the point where she learned to work not well or quickly, but to finish her tasks right on time to avoid being given more to do. That's an attitude she absolutely wants to stamp out as colonial governor[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ]. We need people who will be motivated to actually do quick, efficient work right the first time, because nature and natives alike aren't going to let up on us." |"Eheheh. There is one thing the den matron asks me to get when I'm out." Yes? "She has a weakness for youkan, one of the main ingredients of which is agar or gelatin. The natives here don't know how to make gelatin from animals, and we're a long way from the ocean to get any seaweed. Importing it is hence the only option... at least we can get adzuki beans and honey locally. I do my best, nojya. Even if she doesn't need to eat anymore as a yasha, it's one of the few mercies she's allowed to indulge in after more than two centuries of not-death. I... feel sorry for her[pc.ra kitsune |, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] ], so I always make sure to have some powdered agar on hand, if nothing else." ... Kohaku's face falls. "I'm sorry, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ] |nojya ]. It's easy to get depressed when talking about the den matron." |The moment the den matron's name leaves your mouth, Kohaku's normally-jovial demeanor sours. Turning her eyes towards you with an uncharacteristically dour expression, the plucky little fox appears deathly serious. "[pc.ra kitsune |Your Eminence |[pc.name] ]... I do hope you're aware that some, ah... rumors have been spreading regarding yourself and the matron, nojya." Despite your best efforts, you can't hold back a slight wince. Guess the rumor mill's already started up... what has she heard? Kohaku's concerned expression doesn't diminish in the least, and there's an uncomfortable atmosphere in the cramped storehouse. She shifts a little, averting her eyes as she mutters out a reply. "W-well...[pc.ra kitsune | forgive me, your Eminence, but | ] it was said that the two of you, ah... had 'relations', nojya." You see... and who, pray tell, was saying that? Instantly, Kohaku begins stammering awkwardly, doing her level best to avoid giving you a straight answer. "Ah, it– um, well, I had, um... it's just the local talk, n-nothing more. Rumors are notoriously hard to verify, nojya, let alone track down their source." ...Right. "Ah, and even if such a thing were true, I would scarcely be one to judge, of course!" [kohaku.anyKids |Turning her gaze towards your daughter, napping quietly, Kohaku mutters softly. "[silly |I just hope your proclivities haven't been passed down |Hopefully, those rumors don't persist long enough to trouble our daughter ]. Such a thing would be troublesome indeed, nojya." |." Kohaku relaxes a bit, her smile returning. "People are free to live their lives as they see fit, nojya; you're no exception to that." ] Just as quickly as it arrived, Kohaku's grim mood passes. Smiling at you, the diminutive kitsune clears her throat, before speaking once more. "At any rate, what else had you wished to speak about, nojya?" ] "

rows.original: [rand |"Nakano drinks more than he should. The matron's already told me to forbid him more than his current allotment, but even so I still think he's somehow managing to get his hands on more than that, nojya. Knowing how close he was with Takahiro when he was a child, I think he's pressuring the latter into indulging him straight from the source." Does he have a drinking problem or something? "Not in and of himself, I think. It's just that he's been under a lot of stress for the last couple of years, and it's finally getting to him, nojya." Perhaps you could do something about it[pc.ra kitsune|. Not that you're going to flex your divinely-appointed authority all over him or anything like that, but having someone in such a position who isn't his great-great-grandmother speak to him might help.|, even if you're an outsider. Sure, he might be disinclined to listen to you, but it's got to be worth a try.] "He's just desperate to do something, anything to earn recognition from the Old Country, nojya. Couple of years ago he was asking me when my father would come around again, because he wanted to go prospecting with them. I told him that was completely stupid because he didn't know the first thing about finding minerals, and my father already has enough bodyguards. He didn't take it well..." Glory hounds. Always with something to prove... "He's of the warrior class, yet he is a bushi without a war to fight; I can only imagine what kind of position he must be in, nojya. Well, now that demons are entering this world, he'll be able to slay them all he wants." Kohaku scowls and makes to spit, then thinks better of it. "[pc.ra kitsune|Uh, ah, please forgive that indiscretion, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]. I... I have no excuse for my behavior, nojya." Forgiven. The little golden-furred kitsune bows hurriedly. "Thank you greatly." Mm-hm. "]But one way or the other, he's hoping to distinguish himself so badly that I hope he doesn't do something idiotic because of it and bring shame to the Kurokawa clan. That'd be the height of irony." |"It is to our eternal shame that we have no professional metalworker here, and the shame is doubled for poor Nakano, nojya. Every warrior worth his or her salt knows how to care for a blade, of course, but polishing and sharpening stones only take one so far before reforging needs to be done, especially if one sees practical action much of the time." There are no skilled metalworkers in all the families of fluffy foxen here? "Such artisan clans enjoy renown and honor, as well as the potential patronage of the noble and wealthy, nojya. Why would any of them come to this colonial backwater far away from opportunity, connections and their own people? It is much easier for them to request for the raw materials we find to be shipped over, and manufactured goods to come the other way. Is not portal technology grand[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]? "While his subordinates are okay with replacement blades, hafts and the like as imports, he insists on making the trip over to get his own blade and great armor done up properly. I can't really blame him, since the former is an ancestral heirloom and all, but it is a lot more trouble than it otherwise would be, nojya. While I try to anticipate their demand and have a backfill of the things they need, emergencies happen[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. This goes doubly so when there are only seven of you trying to keep the peace on the frontier..." |"Nakano doesn't like me, nojya. He says that I've gone native." Knowing him and the imperial hardliner he is, the way he phrased it was probably overly hard and prickish, but... is there merit to his words despite all that? "That's the hard part, isn't it[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]? It's more than wearing traditional dress and bowing and scraping to people. Since I was young, I've always wanted to try and fit in, nojya. I figured people would like me if I acted like them... but now some days I wonder if there's nothing uniquely me about being me except maybe eating taiyaki, nojya. That's hardly a personality[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. "In the really rural mountainous areas of the Old Country where people like me come from, they believe that if someone draws a picture of you, you lose a fragment of you that goes onto the paper. And if you were to draw thousands upon thousands of portraits of yourself, you would vanish, nojya. It's... it's just a superstition[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], one that leads people to treat portraits and paintings of people with respect, but even so, when I mimic someone, does a piece of me get exchanged with a piece of them? "Uh, ah, ahahahaha! I'm just talking too much, nojya. Never mind[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], it's just a silly superstition, that's all, and Nakano is just a hard ass to the point even his family is fed up with him!" |"Amongst the goods and migrants coming through the torii gates these days is the occasional character looking to hide out from justice in the colonies, nojya. Everyone going through the gates has to be vetted and approved by the priestly clans, but the lengths to which some of these no-good nasties will go is quite impressive. If they do get through, it's Nakano's job to go out into the wilderness and hunt them down before they irreparably damage our reputation amongst the natives, nojya." And what does he do when... of course, you didn't need to ask. That was a stupid question. "He executes them on the spot[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]." That's... "If they weren't declared no-face before attempting to escape justice by fleeing to the colonies, they are so. It then becomes the duty of every morally upstanding subject of the Cherry Blossom Throne to put them down by what means are available to them[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. It misses several nuances, especially the shame cast upon everyone else in one's circles, but the closest thing that the Belharan Empire had was the declaring of someone an outlaw, nojya. A kitsune who has been declared no-face has almost certainly given into the hunger if they haven't already, and needs to be put down like the animal they have become. Sometimes... you need a merciless hardliner like Nakano who will not lose sleep over taking another's life in the name of honorable duty. Such people have their uses[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]] — regardless of where you are in the world or which people you are amongst, what is the guard but the biggest, strongest gang around?" |"Have you actually had Nakano try to read some of his poetry to you?" No, mostly because you don't understand the spoken language, and the written one even less. A small mercy for language barriers, if nothing else. Kohaku wipes her brow. "Well, that's a small relief, nojya. One can recognize and appreciate the man's determination, and yet absolutely hate the form that it takes[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. I've dabbled in it myself and that coupla behind me's the only one I feel comfortable enough putting on display. Well, I suppose someone in his position needs to be bold and brash, or else he'd have folded long ago, nojya." ]
rows.translation: [rand |中野喝酒的习惯实在太过分了。宿舍管理员已经叮嘱我，要限制他饮酒的量，不能让他超过现有的限额，但即便如此，我还是觉得他总能想办法弄到更多的酒来，真是让人头疼。考虑到他小时候和贵弘关系那么亲密，我猜他应该是直接在贵弘那里得到了纵容。 他是不是有饮酒问题之类的问题呢？ 我认为，并不是他本身有什么问题。只是在过去几年里，他承受了太多的压力，而这些压力终于开始对他产生影响了，诺亚。 或许你可以想办法解决这个问题。[pc.ra kitsune|并不是说你就要对他行使那种天赐的权威之类的，但拥有这样一个职位的人不是他的高祖母与他交谈或许会有帮助。|即使你是个外人，也应该尝试。当然，他可能不愿意听你的意见，但至少值得一试。] 他只是迫切地想做点什么，任何事情都行，只要能得到老家的认可就行，诺雅。几年前他还问我父亲什么时候会再来，因为他想跟着他们一起去勘探矿藏。我告诉他那简直太愚蠢了——他根本不懂如何寻找矿物，而且我父亲已经有足够的保镖了。他当时可不太高兴…… 那些追逐荣耀的人。总是想着要证明些什么…… 他属于战士职业，然而武士没有战争需要参与，我只能想象他现在处境该有多艰难，诺雅。不过，现在既然恶魔进入了这个世界，他就可以随心所欲地消灭它们了。琥珀皱起了眉头，想要吐口水，但最终又改变了主意。"[pc.ra kitsune|呃，啊，请原谅我的冒失，我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]。 我……我的行为确实没有任何借口，诺雅。 被宽恕了。 那只金毛小狐迅速地鞠了一躬。非常感谢您。 嗯。 "]但无论如何，他都希望能够让自己脱颖而出。我只希望他不会因此做出什么愚蠢的事情，以免给黑川家族带来耻辱。那样的话，就真是太具有讽刺意味了。 |我们这里没有专业的金属工匠，这真是我们永远的耻辱；而对于可怜的中野来说，这种耻辱更是加倍了。当然，任何称得上是真正的战士，都知道如何保养自己的武器，但仅仅进行打磨和淬火是远远不够的，最终还是需要重新锻造武器——尤其是对于那些经常需要实战的战士来说。 这里所有的毛茸茸的狐妖家族里都没有熟练的金属工匠吗？ 这样的手工艺家族自然会享有声誉与荣誉，也更容易获得贵族与富人的赞助，诺雅。那么，他们为什么还要来到这个远离机会、缺乏人脉、远离家乡的偏远殖民地呢？对他们来说，要求我们将所需的原材料运过去，然后再把制造好的商品运回来，显然要方便得多。毕竟，传送门技术本身就是一项了不起的发明啊[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]？ 虽然他的下属们愿意使用进口的替换刀刃、刀柄之类的物品，但他却坚持亲自去采购属于自己的刀刃和精美的盔甲，以确保它们能够得到妥善的制作。其实我也不能怪他，毕竟那些东西都是他的祖传遗物。不过，这样做确实麻烦多了，诺亚。虽然我会尽力预测他们的需求，并准备一些替代品以应对紧急情况，但意外总还是会发生啊。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]当只有七个人在努力维护边境的和平时，这种情况就更加明显了…… |中野不喜欢我，诺贾。他说我已经‘入乡随俗’了。 了解他以及他那保守的立场，他这样的表达方式或许确实过于严厉和刻薄了，但是……尽管如此，他的话里难道没有一点道理吗？ 这才是难点所在，对吧？[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]？这不仅仅意味着穿着传统服装、对人们恭敬有礼。从小我就一直想要努力融入群体，真的。我以为如果我表现得像他们一样，人们就会喜欢我……但现在有时候，我会想，作为我自己，除了喜欢吃天妇罗之外，是否真的没有任何独特的之处呢？这根本算不上是一种个性啊。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]。 在那个古老国家的偏远山区，像我这样的当地人相信，如果有人为你画了画像，你就会失去一部分自我，那部分自我就会留在画纸上。而如果你画了成千上万的自己的肖像，最终你就会消失不见，nojya。这……只是一种迷信而已。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]这样一种方式，能够让人们以尊重的态度来对待人物的肖像和绘画作品。然而，即便如此，当我模仿某个人时，我的一部分自我是否会与他们的那一部分自我相互置换呢？ 呃，哈哈，哈哈哈！我只是说得太多了，没什么大不了的。算了吧。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]那只不过是一个愚蠢的迷信罢了，中野只是个固执到了连他的家人都对他感到厌烦的人而已！ |在那些通过这些途径运送过来的商品和移民之中鸟居这些天，这些“大门”其实是那些试图在殖民地逃避法律制裁的坏人们的藏身之处。所有想要通过这些“大门”的人，都必须经过祭司家族的审查和批准。不过，有些这些卑鄙之徒为了达到目的所使出的手段，实在令人印象深刻确实必须把他们抓回来，中野的任务就是进入荒野，在他们对我们的声誉造成不可挽回的损害之前把他们捉回来，野谷。 那么，当……发生的时候，他会怎么做呢？当然，你根本不需要问这个问题。那真是个愚蠢的问题。 他当场就将他们处决了。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]。" 那真是…… 如果他们在试图逃往殖民地以逃避法律的制裁之前，还没有被认定为‘无面者’，那么现在他们确实已经是了。因此，对于每一个秉持道德准则的‘樱花王座’子民来说，利用一切可行的手段将他们消灭，就是自己的责任。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]它忽略了几种微妙的差别，尤其是那种会让一个人所在圈子中的其他所有人感到羞耻的后果。但在贝尔哈兰帝国，最接近这种惩罚的方式就是将某人宣布为“不受欢迎的人”——也就是“无面者”。一旦一只狐妖被宣布为“无面者”，那么它几乎肯定会饿死，如果它还没有饿死的话；而这时，人们就应该像对待一只动物一样，将其处死。有时候……你需要像中野这样的人，一个毫不留情、坚决果断的人。为了履行所谓的“光荣职责”，他们甚至不惜牺牲他人的生命。这类人确实有其存在的价值。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]] — 无论你身处世界的哪个角落，无论你与哪些人在一起，所谓“守卫”，不就是最庞大、最强大的势力罢了？ |你真的让中野试着读过他的一些诗给你听吗？ 不，主要是因为你听不懂口语，更不用说书面语言了。至少，语言障碍也算是件还算“仁慈”的事情吧。 小白擦了擦额头。嗯，这总算让人稍微宽慰了一些，诺雅。人们确实能够认识到并欣赏这个人的决心，但同时也会极其厌恶他表达这种决心的方式。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]我自己也尝试过，而那些我完成的作品，也是唯一让我觉得有勇气拿出来展示的。嗯，我想处于他这样的位置上，一个人就必须敢于冒险、敢于突破常规，否则早就放弃了，对吧。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"Nakano drinks more than he should. The matron's already told me to forbid him more than his current allotment, but even so I still think he's somehow managing to get his hands on more than that, nojya. Knowing how close he was with Takahiro when he was a child, I think he's pressuring the latter into indulging him straight from the source." Does he have a drinking problem or something? "Not in and of himself, I think. It's just that he's been under a lot of stress for the last couple of years, and it's finally getting to him, nojya." Perhaps you could do something about it[pc.ra kitsune|. Not that you're going to flex your divinely-appointed authority all over him or anything like that, but having someone in such a position who isn't his great-great-grandmother speak to him might help.|, even if you're an outsider. Sure, he might be disinclined to listen to you, but it's got to be worth a try.] "He's just desperate to do something, anything to earn recognition from the Old Country, nojya. Couple of years ago he was asking me when my father would come around again, because he wanted to go prospecting with them. I told him that was completely stupid because he didn't know the first thing about finding minerals, and my father already has enough bodyguards. He didn't take it well..." Glory hounds. Always with something to prove... "He's of the warrior class, yet he is a bushi without a war to fight; I can only imagine what kind of position he must be in, nojya. Well, now that demons are entering this world, he'll be able to slay them all he wants." Kohaku scowls and makes to spit, then thinks better of it. "[pc.ra kitsune|Uh, ah, please forgive that indiscretion, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]. I... I have no excuse for my behavior, nojya." Forgiven. The little golden-furred kitsune bows hurriedly. "Thank you greatly." Mm-hm. "]But one way or the other, he's hoping to distinguish himself so badly that I hope he doesn't do something idiotic because of it and bring shame to the Kurokawa clan. That'd be the height of irony." |"It is to our eternal shame that we have no professional metalworker here, and the shame is doubled for poor Nakano, nojya. Every warrior worth his or her salt knows how to care for a blade, of course, but polishing and sharpening stones only take one so far before reforging needs to be done, especially if one sees practical action much of the time." There are no skilled metalworkers in all the families of fluffy foxen here? "Such artisan clans enjoy renown and honor, as well as the potential patronage of the noble and wealthy, nojya. Why would any of them come to this colonial backwater far away from opportunity, connections and their own people? It is much easier for them to request for the raw materials we find to be shipped over, and manufactured goods to come the other way. Is not portal technology grand[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]? "While his subordinates are okay with replacement blades, hafts and the like as imports, he insists on making the trip over to get his own blade and great armor done up properly. I can't really blame him, since the former is an ancestral heirloom and all, but it is a lot more trouble than it otherwise would be, nojya. While I try to anticipate their demand and have a backfill of the things they need, emergencies happen[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. This goes doubly so when there are only seven of you trying to keep the peace on the frontier..." |"Nakano doesn't like me, nojya. He says that I've gone native." Knowing him and the imperial hardliner he is, the way he phrased it was probably overly hard and prickish, but... is there merit to his words despite all that? "That's the hard part, isn't it[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]? It's more than wearing traditional dress and bowing and scraping to people. Since I was young, I've always wanted to try and fit in, nojya. I figured people would like me if I acted like them... but now some days I wonder if there's nothing uniquely me about being me except maybe eating taiyaki, nojya. That's hardly a personality[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. "In the really rural mountainous areas of the Old Country where people like me come from, they believe that if someone draws a picture of you, you lose a fragment of you that goes onto the paper. And if you were to draw thousands upon thousands of portraits of yourself, you would vanish, nojya. It's... it's just a superstition[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], one that leads people to treat portraits and paintings of people with respect, but even so, when I mimic someone, does a piece of me get exchanged with a piece of them? "Uh, ah, ahahahaha! I'm just talking too much, nojya. Never mind[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], it's just a silly superstition, that's all, and Nakano is just a hard ass to the point even his family is fed up with him!" |"Amongst the goods and migrants coming through the torii gates these days is the occasional character looking to hide out from justice in the colonies, nojya. Everyone going through the gates has to be vetted and approved by the priestly clans, but the lengths to which some of these no-good nasties will go is quite impressive. If they do get through, it's Nakano's job to go out into the wilderness and hunt them down before they irreparably damage our reputation amongst the natives, nojya." And what does he do when... of course, you didn't need to ask. That was a stupid question. "He executes them on the spot[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]." That's... "If they weren't declared no-face before attempting to escape justice by fleeing to the colonies, they are so. It then becomes the duty of every morally upstanding subject of the Cherry Blossom Throne to put them down by what means are available to them[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. It misses several nuances, especially the shame cast upon everyone else in one's circles, but the closest thing that the Belharan Empire had was the declaring of someone an outlaw, nojya. A kitsune who has been declared no-face has almost certainly given into the hunger if they haven't already, and needs to be put down like the animal they have become. Sometimes... you need a merciless hardliner like Nakano who will not lose sleep over taking another's life in the name of honorable duty. Such people have their uses[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]] — regardless of where you are in the world or which people you are amongst, what is the guard but the biggest, strongest gang around?" |"Have you actually had Nakano try to read some of his poetry to you?" No, mostly because you don't understand the spoken language, and the written one even less. A small mercy for language barriers, if nothing else. Kohaku wipes her brow. "Well, that's a small relief, nojya. One can recognize and appreciate the man's determination, and yet absolutely hate the form that it takes[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. I've dabbled in it myself and that coupla behind me's the only one I feel comfortable enough putting on display. Well, I suppose someone in his position needs to be bold and brash, or else he'd have folded long ago, nojya." ] "

rows.original: [rand |"Hitoshi is always so capable, nojya. The quantities of fresh veggies he brings in for shipping usually are too much for the storehouse to hold, so he fills me in when my wagon's about to leave for big cities like Tychris. It might just be fresh veggies, but you can still get a pretty good price on them where there're many mouths to feed, especially when your goods are of as high quality as the stuff Hitoshi comes up with. "With pickles and other processed foods, I can range a little further because I don't have to explain why all this exotic produce is still fresh despite supposedly having been moved months over long distances. Those do even better, nojya. You wouldn't imagine how much preserved fruit goes for in Jassira — or at least, preserved fruit that isn't dates, figs, or that kind of stuff." |"I've got to admit[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], Hitoshi scares me a little. I'm already so small and he's such a giant man; every time he comes close, I feel like he could pick me up or crush me without even noticing it, nojya. It's not his fault, he's very nice and kind-hearted, but I can't help but feel what he makes me feel. Maybe the problem is that I'm just so tiny..." |"He may not look it at a first glance, but Hitoshi is a very good tailor, nojya. One of the few things he requisitions often are bolts of cloth so that he can put together his own clothing, and a bit more for his family. Our Hitoshi may be a simple man, but that doesn't mean he doesn't have good designs for other people. Did you know that he was the one who tailored Miko and Mai's uniforms for them?" Him? Hitoshi? But those are so... risque, and he's such a simple, good-natured guy. One can hardly imagine someone like him putting together outfits like that. "I think he just wants to make his family happy[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]], and so if that's what Miko and Mai want, that's what he makes for them. He's a pretty good handyman all around, so naturally sewing things together is also included in that list of skills. No wonder the den matron likes him so much." |"Hitoshi doesn't seem to like girls very much. Or guys, for that matter. Or anything of anything at all, nojya. When I pass by the fields to open the storehouse in the morning, he's already in them; he's also there when I close up shop in the evenings. It's not strange for him, he's been like that since he was a kit, but one wonders if it's just his nature or if something happened to him to turn him that way. "Me? I think he does it to get away from Miko and Mai, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|nojya]. Those two are very, very noisy, and I can see why a man would come to learn to love peace and solitude when there's so little of it to be had around those two. Any woman he's going to end up marrying is definitely going to share his love of calm and serenity, I can tell you as much." |"Hitoshi is always very kind and willing to help me whenever I need some extra hands in for heavy lifting. Usually the puppet takes care of the worst of it, but sometimes it's the number of hands that're needed, or the goods are too fragile to be trusted to an automaton, or Kazuo has taken his toy back to see how well it's holding up. Hitoshi, big boy that he is, doesn't ask why, doesn't say no, and doesn't hold back when helping others out, nojya. Nor does he ask for any kind of recompense for his efforts, which makes me feel bad because I'm obligated to give something back to him in reciprocity. Equivalent exchange and all, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|nojya]. "It just makes me worry that someone is going to take advantage of that selflessness, you know? Guess it's for the best that he was born in the colonies, in a den like this one where everyone knows each others' face and can nip that kind of nonsense in the bud, nojya. He's definitely not a man made for large groups of people." ]
rows.translation: [rand |仁总是这么能干，nojya。他每次带来的新鲜蔬菜数量通常都多到仓库根本存放不下，所以每当我的马车准备前往提克里斯这样的大城市时，他都会提前告诉我这些情况。虽然这些只是普通的新鲜蔬菜，但在需要养活大量人口的地方，你仍然可以从中获得不错的利润——尤其是当你的商品质量像仁带来的这些那样高的时候。 有了腌制品和其他加工食品，我就能够应付得更自如了，因为我不必解释为什么这些看似经过长途运输、已经存放了好几个月的异国特产仍然保持新鲜。那些食品的表现更是出色，诺雅。你绝对想象不到，在贾西拉，腌制品的市场需求有多大——至少是指那些不是枣子、无花果之类的腌制品。 |我必须承认[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]仁太郎确实会让我有点害怕。我这么小，而他是个那么高大强壮的男人；每次他靠近我，我都会觉得他甚至可能不经意间就把我举起来或者压扁，真的。这不是他的错，他其实非常友善、心地也很好，但我就是会感到这种害怕。也许问题就在于，我实在太渺小了…… |乍一看可能不会觉得，但宏是个非常出色的裁缝，诺贾。他经常订购布料，就是为了自己制作衣服，也会为家人准备一些。我们的宏虽然是个朴实的人，但这并不意味着他不会为别人设计漂亮的衣服。你知道吗？正是他为米可与舞量身定制了她们身上的制服。 他？仁？但这些设计未免太……大胆了，而他是个如此单纯、善良的人。简直无法想象他会挑选这样的服装来搭配。那个。 我觉得他只是想让家人开心而已。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]所以，如果米可与舞就是想要这样的东西，他就会为她们制作。他各方面都是个相当能干的忙人，因此缝制各种东西自然也属于他的技能范围。难怪女头目会这么喜欢他。 |浩人似乎不太喜欢女孩子……其实，男孩子他也不喜欢。总之，他对任何事情都提不起兴趣，诺贾。每天早上我去田野里打开仓库的时候，他就已经在那里了；晚上关店的时候他也在那里。对他来说，这并不奇怪，从他还是个小孩子的时候就是这样的。不过，人们还是会想：这是他的天性，还是发生了什么事情才让他变成了这样呢？ 我？我觉得他这么做是为了远离米可与舞。 [pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|诺雅]那两个人实在太吵了，我完全能理解为什么有人会想要学习去珍惜宁静与独处——在他们的周围，这种宁静与独处实在是太难找到了。而任何他最终选择娶来的女人，都会肯定地他一定会分享自己对宁静与平和的热爱，这一点我可以肯定。 |每当需要有人帮忙搬重物时，仁总是非常热心、乐于提供帮助。通常情况下，那些机器人会承担最繁重的任务，但有时候确实需要更多人手；或者有些货物太脆弱，无法交给自动机器来处理；又或者一夫会把他的‘玩具’拿回去，看看它的状况如何。浩，作为一个大男孩，他从不问为什么，从不拒绝，帮助别人时也从不会犹豫，诺贾。他也不会为自己的付出要求任何回报，这让我感到有些内疚，因为我觉得自己有义务以同样的方式回报他。等价交换，就是这样。 [pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|诺雅]。 我只是担心会有人利用他的这种无私精神，你懂我的意思吧？其实他出生在这样的殖民地，大家彼此都认识，能够及时制止这种荒谬的行为，或许反而是件好事。他显然不适合待在大型人群中。 ]

rows.original: [rand |"So, I think Takahiro has a crush on Azami. Or maybe it's the other way around, nojya. It's one or the other, I'm pretty sure of it." She seems pretty gleeful about it, despite her not being involved. Kohaku makes a little pouty face. "Love is the most interesting thing to gossip about, nojya! The rise and swirl of people and passions, the cold depths and explosive heights! How can one not be excited[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]?" From what you've seen of the two of them, they're always arguing about something or the other. That really doesn't bode well for them being an item, if that's what she means. "Eeeeeeh, you'll understand in time, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|friend]. Hate isn't the opposite of love, indifference is, nojya! Hate... it's merely a different face of the same coin, I tell you." Beaming in a big, open-mouthed smile that shows all her little pointy fangs, Kohaku raises her hands to her cheeks and swoons. "They'll be arguing as usual, and then things get a little too heated... and before you know it, the two of them will find themselves in a, uh, compromising position, nojya" Oh boy. She's not listening to you at all, lost in her fantasies as it is. How much of this tale has any actual standing in truth, and how much sprung out of her imagination, only the gods know. "It happens more often than you'd think, nojya! I'm being completely serious about this! Mark my words, they'll eventually end up together!" Yeah. You can imagine a few people who might have choice words to say about that possibility, but nothing's going to tear this romantic little thing away from her dreams. |"By right, goods produced for distribution and export are supposed to come to me so I can get them down on the books before they're claimed by households, nojya. Takahiro circumvents that by giving his produce directly to people in exchange for favors and the like. That isn't so bad in and of itself, but it makes my head ache when the matron's explicitly stated that certain people aren't supposed to have any more than certain amounts of liquor. The ledgers can take it, but my name is on the line, [pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. It's very vexing, especially when he's the recalcitrant kind." And nothing has been done about it so far? "Liquor, no matter how high or low-quality it is, is an essential component of maintaining morale no matter where you go or who you are amongst[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. This goes doubly so when you are here in the colonies... many people drink more than they ought to their first few months here. Producing it locally is much more efficient and safe than relying on imports, which is why Taka has some degree of protection, nojya. One can only see how far his profession will protect him from social repercussions..." |"Every now and then, Taka will ask me to get a bunch of native drinks and liquors for study, usually the strongest stuff that they have out there. I don't doubt that he actually studies them, nojya. At the same time, I also don't doubt that he drinks the lot after he's done with them — if he hasn't already as part of his examination of the local drinks. The stranger, the weirder, the more exotic, the better received it is, nojya. I'm not entirely sure I should be doing this for him, but... I do have cause to owe him favors every now and then, and there are worse things he could ask of me as repayment." Like? "Like drinking the things he ends up fermenting as results of his studies, nojya. See, they have these clear spirits in Tychris they make from potatoes, and he got it into his mind to try and do something like that with potatoes and rice, and —" Okay, you get the idea. "I have no idea how his liver hasn't already given up, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|nojya]. It's amazing." |"You know, the rumours say that Taka is looking for a lost relic of Keros, and that's why he spent so much time out there in the wilderness. There's just one problem with that story..." Yes? "It's not as if you can't just walk up to the shrine and petition for an audience with the Trickster, nojya. Other grand kami might be insulted, but his divine lordship himself grants audiences to people from all walks of life[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. I've even seen him personally come down to have dinner with the matron and her family — I was told to throw open the storehouse and see what delicacies we had on hand. Oh, and he plays with the chopsticks. "But point being... if you're looking for a treasure of his divine lordship's, why wouldn't you just ask him about it? He's a lot closer to us than the other of the Seven, so what's the worst that could happen, really? He won't play a prank on you unless you did something to deserve it, so there's nothing to fear, nojya. The only reason why I think Taka doesn't just ask is that he doesn't really want to find it and it's a pretext for wandering about in the wilderness. He might even believe it himself — lots of people do that kind of thing, tell themselves things that are at odds with their actions." |"Once, I was heading to the baths with some liquor — there's nothing better than cold liquor in a hot bath — and ran across Taka on the way. He teased me that I shouldn't be drinking, because I was too young, nojya. That I look like a child because I'm so small. And that wasn't the only time[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]! He teases me all the time for my height!" Pouting, Kohaku grabs her chest and bunches up her hand-filling lady lumps, then slides her fingers down past her waist. "Do I look like a child[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]? Does a child have any of these, nojya? I'm short and cute... but I'm not a child! People take me seriously!" Hey, hey, maybe she's getting a little too worked up. Kohaku heaves and pants. "I-I'm so sorry[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. I don't know what came over me, nojya. A thousand apologies, I — I — I can't stand it when Taka teases me, he knows how to hit all my weak spots and leave me all tingly and fuming." ]
rows.translation: [rand |所以，我觉得贵弘对茜有好感。或者也可能是相反的情况，诺耶。总之肯定是其中一种，我非常确定。 尽管她并没有参与其中，但她看起来似乎对此感到非常高兴。 小花撅起了小嘴。爱情才是最值得人们闲聊的话题，诺雅！人们的情感起伏与纠葛，那些冰冷深渊与激烈高潮……谁能不对此感到兴奋呢？[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]？" 从你观察他们的情况来看，他们总是为各种各样的事情争吵。如果她的意思是说他们是否是一对情侣的话，那么这种情况确实不太乐观。 呃……你迟早会明白的。 [pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|朋友]恨并不是爱的反面，冷漠才是！恨……其实只是同一枚硬币的另一面而已，我告诉你。科哈克露出一个灿烂的笑容，那笑容中露出了她那小小的尖牙，她将双手放在脸颊上，仿佛要晕过去一般。他们又会像往常一样争吵起来，然后事情就会变得有点失控……不知不觉间，他们俩就会陷入一种，呃，尴尬的境地，诺雅。 哦天啊，她根本没在听你说话，完全沉浸在自己的幻想之中。这个故事中有多少内容是真实发生的，又有多少是她的想象出来的，只有神才知道。 这种事情发生的频率比你想象的要高得多，诺雅！我是认真的！相信我，他们最终一定会在一起的！ 是啊。你可以想象，有些人可能会用一些刻薄的话语来评价这种可能性，但没有什么能够破坏她对这份浪漫梦想的执着。 |按照规定，那些用于销售和出口的商品应该先交到我手里，这样我才能在这些商品被家庭们领取之前把它们记录在账本上，明白吗，nojya？不过，贵弘却通过直接把商品送给人们来换取他们的帮助或好处，从而规避了这一规定。本身来说，这倒也不是什么坏事，但问题在于，女管家明明规定了一些人不能领取超过规定数量的酒类。虽然账本上可以记录这些交易，但我的工作声誉可就牵涉进来了[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]这真的让人非常恼火，尤其是当他还是那种固执己见的人的时候。 到目前为止，还没有采取任何措施来解决这个问题吗？ 无论酒的质量如何，无论你身处何地、与谁为伍，它都是维护士气的重要因素。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]在殖民地这里，这种情况更为明显……很多人来到这里的头几个月里，饮酒量都会超过应有的限度。在当地生产这些饮品，要比依赖进口更加高效和安全，这就是为什么塔卡能够得到一定的保护，诺贾。人们只能拭目以待，他的这份职业能在多大程度上保护他免受社会舆论的冲击…… |偶尔，贵弘会让我去买一些当地的饮品和酒类用来研究，通常是他们店里最烈的那些。我毫不怀疑他确实是会研究这些酒的，nojya。同时，我也相信他在研究完之后会把它们都喝掉——当然，如果在他研究这些当地饮品的过程中还没有把它们喝光的话。陌生人越奇怪、越异国情调，往往就越容易受到欢迎，诺雅。我其实不太确定是否应该为他做这件事，但是……我确实有时候欠他人情，而且他要求我做的这些事情，其实也没什么比这更糟糕的了。" 喜欢吗？ 就像喝下他通过研究最终酿造出来的那些饮品一样，诺亚。你知道，在提克里斯，他们用土豆酿造出那种清澈的酒，而他突然想到，也可以用土豆和大米来尝试制作类似的东西…… 好的，你明白我的意思了。 我完全不明白他的肝脏怎么还没坏掉[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]|诺雅]真是太神奇了。 |你知道，有传言说塔卡正在寻找凯罗斯遗失的遗物，这就是他为什么在荒野里耗费了那么多时间的原因。不过，这个故事其实有一个问题…… 嗯？ 又不是说你不能直接走到那座神社前，请求与那位弄臣见面，诺贾。其他那些宏伟的建筑神明他可能会受到冒犯，但他的神圣陛下本人会接见来自各行各业的人们。[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]我甚至亲眼看到他亲自下来与那位女主人及其家人共进晚餐——有人让我把仓库里的东西都拿出来，看看我们手头有哪些美味佳肴。哦，对了，他还喜欢玩筷子呢。 但关键在于……如果你在寻找他那位神圣主人的宝藏，为什么不直接询问他怎么会那样做呢？他其实比另外六个人更亲近我们，所以最坏的情况又能怎样呢？除非你做了什么惹他生气的事，否则他不会捉弄你的，所以没什么好害怕的，nojya。我认为贵弘之所以不直接去寻找，可能是因为他其实并不想找到它，只是把寻找这个理由当作在荒野中闲逛的借口罢了。说不定他自己也真的相信这个借口——很多人都会这样，对自己说一些与自己的行为相矛盾的话。 |有一次，我带着一些酒去泡澡——在热水澡中喝冷酒，没有比这更惬意的了——在路上遇到了贵弘。他开玩笑说我不应该喝酒，因为我太年轻了，还说因为我个子太小，看起来就像个孩子。而这种事情并不只发生过一次[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]他总是拿我的身高来取笑我！ 嘟着嘴，小红双手按在胸口，将那些让她的手显得丰满的肉肉捏了捏，然后手指顺着腰线滑了下去。我看起来像小孩子吗？[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]诺雅，我这些特征中有哪一点符合儿童的特点呢？我个子矮小，还很可爱……但我已经不是小孩子了！人们都是认真对待我的！ 嘿，嘿，也许她有点太激动过度了。 小花不停地喘着粗气。我、我真的很抱歉[pc.ra kitsune|我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]]我不知道自己当时是怎么了，诺雅。真的很抱歉，我……我实在受不了塔卡取笑我，他太知道如何触到我的痛点了，让我既尴尬又恼火。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"So, I think Takahiro has a crush on Azami. Or maybe it's the other way around, nojya. It's one or the other, I'm pretty sure of it." She seems pretty gleeful about it, despite her not being involved. Kohaku makes a little pouty face. "Love is the most interesting thing to gossip about, nojya! The rise and swirl of people and passions, the cold depths and explosive heights! How can one not be excited[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]?" From what you've seen of the two of them, they're always arguing about something or the other. That really doesn't bode well for them being an item, if that's what she means. "Eeeeeeh, you'll understand in time, [pc.ra kitsune|my [pc.mf|lord|lady]|friend]. Hate isn't the opposite of love, indifference is, nojya! Hate... it's merely a different face of the same coin, I tell you." Beaming in a big, open-mouthed smile that shows all her little pointy fangs, Kohaku raises her hands to her cheeks and swoons. "They'll be arguing as usual, and then things get a little too heated... and before you know it, the two of them will find themselves in a, uh, compromising position, nojya" Oh boy. She's not listening to you at all, lost in her fantasies as it is. How much of this tale has any actual standing in truth, and how much sprung out of her imagination, only the gods know. "It happens more often than you'd think, nojya! I'm being completely serious about this! Mark my words, they'll eventually end up together!" Yeah. You can imagine a few people who might have choice words to say about that possibility, but nothing's going to tear this romantic little thing away from her dreams. |"By right, goods produced for distribution and export are supposed to come to me so I can get them down on the books before they're claimed by households, nojya. Takahiro circumvents that by giving his produce directly to people in exchange for favors and the like. That isn't so bad in and of itself, but it makes my head ache when the matron's explicitly stated that certain people aren't supposed to have any more than certain amounts of liquor. The ledgers can take it, but my name is on the line, [pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. It's very vexing, especially when he's the recalcitrant kind." And nothing has been done about it so far? "Liquor, no matter how high or low-quality it is, is an essential component of maintaining morale no matter where you go or who you are amongst[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. This goes doubly so when you are here in the colonies... many people drink more than they ought to their first few months here. Producing it locally is much more efficient and safe than relying on imports, which is why Taka has some degree of protection, nojya. One can only see how far his profession will protect him from social repercussions..." |"Every now and then, Taka will ask me to get a bunch of native drinks and liquors for study, usually the strongest stuff that they have out there. I don't doubt that he actually studies them, nojya. At the same time, I also don't doubt that he drinks the lot after he's done with them — if he hasn't already as part of his examination of the local drinks. The stranger, the weirder, the more exotic, the better received it is, nojya. I'm not entirely sure I should be doing this for him, but... See, they have these clear spirits in Tychris they make from potatoes, and he got it into his mind to try and do something like that with potatoes and rice, and —" Okay, you get the idea. It's amazing." |"You know, the rumours say that Taka is looking for a lost relic of Keros, and that's why he spent so much time out there in the wilderness. There's just one problem with that story..." Yes? "It's not as if you can't just walk up to the shrine and petition for an audience with the Trickster, nojya. Other grand kami might be insulted, but his divine lordship himself grants audiences to people from all walks of life[pc.ra kitsune|, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]]. I've even seen him personally come down to have dinner with the matron and her family — I was told to throw open the storehouse and see what delicacies we had on hand. Oh, and he plays with the chopsticks. "But point being... if you're looking for a treasure of his divine lordship's, why wouldn't you just ask him about it? He's a lot closer to us than the other of the Seven, so what's the worst that could happen, really?
