rows.original: Komari is being too sensitive about all of this. Mai meant only the best for her, and she should take the gift in the spirit in which it was given, which is far more important than some slight that was never intended in the first place. True, it might have hurt, but there's no way Mai could understand or even imagine things from her perspective as an undying yasha; she's holding Mai to an impossible standard.
rows.translation: 麻里对这一切反应得太敏感了。麻只是出于好意才送她这份礼物的，她应该以礼物原本的意图来接受它，这才是最重要的，远比那些根本不是故意造成的小误会重要得多。诚然，这份礼物可能会让她感到受伤，但以一个永生不灭的存在的角度来看，麻根本不可能理解，甚至无法想象她的感受。亚莎她对舞的要求实在高得不可能实现。
rows.raw: "Komari is being too sensitive about all of this. Mai meant only the best for her, and she should take the gift in the spirit in which it was given, which is far more important than some slight that was never intended in the first place. True, it might have hurt, but there's no way Mai could understand or even imagine things from her perspective as an undying yasha; she's holding Mai to an impossible standard."

rows.original: "Say what?" "That's right, what are you saying, girl?" You look thoughtful and raise a finger to your lips. "I meant exactly what I said. Hitoshi's the one at fault here." "..." "..." "Y... yes, that's right. It's all my fault, everything is my fault!" Hitoshi winces, scratching the backs of his ears, but it looks like he's decided to go along with your ruse. "So if you would... so please, Gran, Mai... just stop fighting and make up already." "..." "..." At last, the twitch in Mai's eye fades. "I... I weren't serious none 'bout what I jus' said. I'm sorry, Granny." And in that case, I'll show deference to my boy Hitoshi and accept the gift." Komari heaves a small sigh; the words must be harder to say than you can imagine. "Thank you." Well, it looks like that's settled. To be completely honest, you don't doubt Hitoshi could have broken them up at any point, but his stance on things was simply far too passive for him to have been of any use there. Oh well... "I think that's dealt with, then." Casting an eye on the gifted garment in the den matron's hands, you offer the both of them a small smile. While you came up here on business, there's no way anyone's mind is suited for paperwork and accounts right now. "I think we could all do with a little relaxing music. Will you be joining us, Hitoshi?" "I... just remembered I have somewhere else to be." He coughs, turning tail. "Please excuse me." "Now then. Where do you keep the koto, Mai...?"
rows.translation: 你说什么？ 没错，你到底想说什么，姑娘？ 你看起来若有所思，还把一根手指放在嘴唇上。我说的就是这个意思，这次真的是仁的错。 "……" "……" 是……是的，没错。都是我的错，一切都是我的错！仁志皱了皱眉头，挠了挠耳朵，但看起来他决定配合你的计谋了。所以，如果你们能的话……拜托了，奶奶、舞……不要再吵架了，赶紧和好吧。 "……" "……" 终于，舞眼角的颤动消失了。我……我刚才说的话并不是认真的，对不起，奶奶。 在这种情况下，我会尊重我的朋友仁，并接受这份礼物。麻里轻轻叹了口气；那些话肯定比你想象中更难以说出口。谢谢。 好吧，看来这件事已经解决了。说实话，你也不会怀疑仁在任何时候都有可能阻止他们分开，但他的态度实在太消极了，根本无法起到任何作用。唉…… 我想那个问题已经得到解决了。看到女巢长手中那件精美的衣物，你向她们俩微微一笑。虽然你是为了公事来到这里的，但此刻，谁的心思也不会放在文件和账务上吧。我觉得我们都需要一些轻松的音乐来放松一下。仁，你也会加入我们吗？ 我……刚想起来我还有别的地方要去。他咳嗽了一声，然后转身逃跑了。请原谅我。 那么，舞，你把古筝放在哪里了……？
rows.raw: ' "Say what?" "That's right, what are you saying, girl?" You look thoughtful and raise a finger to your lips. "I meant exactly what I said. Hitoshi's the one at fault here." "..." "..." "Y... yes, that's right. It's all my fault, everything is my fault!" Hitoshi winces, scratching the backs of his ears, but it looks like he's decided to go along with your ruse. "So if you would... so please, Gran, Mai... just stop fighting and make up already." "..." "..." At last, the twitch in Mai's eye fades. "I... I weren't serious none 'bout what I jus' said. I'm sorry, Granny." And in that case, I'll show deference to my boy Hitoshi and accept the gift." Komari heaves a small sigh; the words must be harder to say than you can imagine. "Thank you." Well, it looks like that's settled. To be completely honest, you don't doubt Hitoshi could have broken them up at any point, but his stance on things was simply far too passive for him to have been of any use there. Oh well... "I think that's dealt with, then." Casting an eye on the gifted garment in the den matron's hands, you offer the both of them a small smile. While you came up here on business, there's no way anyone's mind is suited for paperwork and accounts right now. "I think we could all do with a little relaxing music. Will you be joining us, Hitoshi?" "I... just remembered I have somewhere else to be." He coughs, turning tail. "Please excuse me." "Now then. Where do you keep the koto, Mai...?" '

rows.original: Blaming Hitoshi might get those two calmed down enough to at least sort this out. It's not right and nor does it make the slightest lick of sense, but those two are clearly emotional and reason isn't going to work. If it'll keep the peace, then you're sure he'll understand.
rows.translation: 责备仁或许能让那两个人冷静下来，至少让他们把这件事解决掉。这并不正确，也根本毫无道理可言，但那两个人显然情绪激动，讲道理是行不通的。只要这样能维持和睦，他肯定能理解的。
rows.raw: "Blaming Hitoshi might get those two calmed down enough to at least sort this out. It's not right and nor does it make the slightest lick of sense, but those two are clearly emotional and reason isn't going to work. If it'll keep the peace, then you're sure he'll understand."

rows.original: You are not going to blame Hitoshi for something he had absolutely no part in and didn't even know of until he stepped in here. That isn't right.
rows.translation: 你绝不会为了一件仁根本没有参与、甚至直到他走进这里之前都毫不知情的事情而去责怪他。这样是不对的。
rows.raw: "You are not going to blame Hitoshi for something he had absolutely no part in and didn't even know of until he stepped in here. That isn't right."

rows.original: Stepping into [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|granny's|the den matron's] chambers, you're greeted by the sight of not just Komari herself, but Mother at her side by the window. Your [silly|okaa-sama|mother] [kiyoko.pregStage 2 |has a miniature tree in a porcelain basin balanced atop her big, pregnant belly as she waddles over to set it down on the windowsill by another one side by side |is carefully carrying a miniature tree in a porcelain basin, hefting it onto the windowsill with a grunt of effort beside another one of its kind ]. Together, liege and retainer step back to admire their handiwork in the wan sunlight streaming into the room. "It takes you back, does it not? We used to do this so often as girls..." Mother reaches out, adjusts her basin just a little for the tiny leaves and branches to catch the light perfectly. "Simply being here, doing this... it is but a small feat of shaping, yet it makes my heart ache." "Indeed, would you look at my bonsai, Myobu-sama. Such hue and vibrancy to the bark, such fine pruning... what do you think? It's truly a splendid bonsai, isn't it? I daresay there's none better in the world." "Hmmnn." Mother raises a finger to her lips. "I would say that my technique and results are better, Komari. My bonsai has that —" "...Begging your pardon, my liege, I do not mean to be contentious... but no, it does not." Kiyoko considers that for a moment. "Komari, you know that I am not in the habit of lying to spare peoples' feelings." "...It can't be better. There's no bonsai in the world that's better than my Ryunosuke bonsai." Liege and retainer lock gazes for several seconds at this sudden show of most uncharacteristic and shameful defiance, then Mother mulls it over for a little while more. "Ryunosuke. Wasn't that the name of... ah." "..." "Perhaps I was wrong," Mother continues. "Your bonsai truly is a fine and unparalleled work of shaping, Komari." "Isn't it? Don't you agree, Myobu-sama?" "Yes." Slowly, Mother picks up the basin again, hefting it up in her hands[kiyoko.pregStage 2| and using her pregnant belly for support]. "I'm afraid I must leave you now, though. [kiyoko.numKits 1|Kinu needs|my children need] me back at the den." "Safe travels, my liege." You step aside and duck out of sight behind a nearby pillar as Mother sweeps past you on her way out, her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails trailing behind her grandiosely with utmost refinement, as always. Part of you wonders if you should go help your mother with her burden, but you know that approaching her right now might complicate matters in an awkward way. Still, [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|granny's|the den matron's] going to be in a melancholy mood after this... [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |you ought to make your business quick and be back in the fields before long |you ought to be on your toes around her today ].
rows.translation: 踏入[kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|奶奶的|巢穴的女首领]一进入房间，你们看到的不仅是有香织本人，还有站在窗边的母亲。 [silly|大人|母亲] [kiyoko.pregStage 2 |她摇摇摆摆地走过去，将那个装在瓷盆里的微型树木放在窗台上，让它与另一个微型树木并排摆放着——她那隆起的、怀孕的腹部上还稳稳地托着这个瓷盆呢。 |他小心翼翼地捧着一个装在瓷盆里的微型树木，费了些力气才把它放在窗台上，旁边还放着另一棵同样的树木。 ]国王与他的随从一起后退几步，欣赏着在昏暗的阳光照耀下显现出的他们的杰作。 这会让你回想起过去，对吧？我们小时候经常一起做这种事情……母亲伸手调整了一下水盆的位置，使得那些细小的叶子和树枝能够完美地接收到光线。仅仅因为能够在这里，做这样的事情……虽然这只是微不足道的举动，但却让我感到无比欣慰。 确实，您看我的盆景吧，Myobu-sama。树皮的色泽如此鲜艳，修剪得也如此精巧……您觉得怎么样？这真的是一件绝妙的盆景，不是吗？我敢说，世界上没有比这更出色的了。 嗯……母亲将手指放在嘴唇上。我得说，我的技术和成果都更出色，小丸。我的盆景就是体现了这一点—— ……恕我直言，我的君主，我并非有意与您争论……但事实上，确实如此。 清子思考了片刻。麻里，你知道我并不习惯为了不伤害别人的感情而说谎。 ……再好不过了。世界上没有任何盆景能比我的龙之介盆景更出色。 领主和随从们盯着这一突如其来的、完全违背其性格且令人羞耻的反抗行为，凝视了好几秒钟。随后，那位母亲又仔细思考了片刻。龙之助……那个不是……啊。 "……" 也许我错了。母亲继续说道。你的盆景确实是一件精美绝伦、无与伦比的艺术作品，小丸。 不是吗？您不也是这么认为的吗，宫本大人？ 是的。慢慢地，母亲再次拿起那个盆，将它举到了手中。[kiyoko.pregStage 2| 并用她隆起的腹部作为支撑]。 不过，恐怕我现在必须离开你了。 [kiyoko.numKits 1|小娟需要|我的孩子们需要]把我带回巢穴。 祝您旅途平安，我的君主。 你赶紧退到一边，躲到附近的一根柱子后面，这时母亲正从你身边走过[kiyoko.kiyokoTails]她的尾巴依旧优雅地摇摆着，一如既往地显得那么高贵。你心里有些犹豫，是否应该去帮母亲分担这份负担，但你也知道，现在去接近她，反而可能会让事情变得更加复杂，甚至引发尴尬的局面。 不过，还是[kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|奶奶的|巢穴的女首领]看完这个之后，我肯定会陷入忧郁的情绪中…… [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |你最好尽快完成手头的事，然后尽快回到田里去 |今天你在她面前可得格外小心谨慎才行 ]。

rows.original: Some time ago... You wonder why Mother has summoned you here, now of all times. It's still early in the morning... you have to [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |be out tending to the fields — even though you've been up since the crack of dawn, the weeding's still half-done and the thought of leaving anything incomplete really chafes at you. Still, it's Mother's summons, and if she's calling you all the way here to granny's chambers then it has to be important. She even told you to make yourself presentable, so you even went and took the time to scrub yourself down from head to toe... that's got to be enough, right? |see to the restoration works, [kiyoko.numKits 8 |give Aya, Tatsumi and Asagiri their directives for the day before you can tend to other matters |guide the hands granny was so kind to lend you in restoring your home ]. It's not as if you wouldn't be heading out to granny's later in the day... but then again, a refined lady like you doesn't harbour such contentious thoughts. Mother must have a good reason for summoning you all the way to the den matron's chambers at the crack of dawn, and she even told you to make yourself presentable at that. Even having your best clothes on, bathing from head to toe and brushing out your tails... you feel a little inadequate. The way Mother phrased it, this is going to be something important and merely decent isn't going to cut it, and yet time is what it is... ] Standing in the doorway, you announce yourself, and are met by [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|granny's|the den matron's] voice in reply. "Enter." Waiting for you within are both Mother and [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|Granny|Matron] Komari, but there's one more personage between them at the table: a four-tailed kitsune woman clad in soft furs of red, orange and black that leave her shoulders exposed, as well as platform sandals. She looks to be about your age and would be as tall as you, too, but her footwear gives her enough additional height to peer down the length of her nose at you. Finely and foxily-featured, bearing distinct cheeks streaked with red pigment and a delicate expression that no doubt hides the iron will beneath... no doubt high nobility, like you. And to prove it, there's her hair. You've yet to see [kiyoko.numKits 4|anyone with white hair and fur outside of your brothers and sisters|anyone else with white hair and fur except you], but it's done up in flowing tresses, marked with red ribbons and held in place by a couple of hairpins. White hair and fur... someone from another of the twelve Divine Clans, then. [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Suddenly, you realize that you are very, very inadequate — even Mother, who wears the same style of yukata all the time, has put on her best finery for the occasion. Even Granny Komari has put on her best finery. And here you are, standing in your fieldwork clothes, sticking out like a sore thumb. While you aren't the most keen at dressing up, at least you know enough to realize the amount of shame you're casting upon both Mother and Granny Komari must be astronomical. Damn it. Well, best foot forward. Turning tails and fleeing would just make the situation worse. |Not that you don't know who this is — even if you don't recognize the face, Mother and Matron Komari have taught you enough to know what the Fujiwara crest looks like, emblazoned on her chest just under her smallish rack. Your mind races, trying to evaluate your relative social standing to hers and choosing the appropriate greeting given your social stations ] — "Kinu, this is Kotone Fujiwara," Mother begins. "All the way across the ocean by torii gate, she is here in full official capacity as a witness on behalf of the Cherry Blossom Throne. While she may be your junior in relative standing, please give her all due respect that her position entails." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Witness? What's she here to witness? |And as a Fujiwara, of course. Don't want to anger her relatives. But that part doesn't need to be said. The bigger question is, what's she here to witness? ] Then, you notice the scroll laid out on the table — exquisite calligraphy in the manner of all official documents, and the imperial seal. No doubt prepared by a professional scribe... [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |"Something of great import is happening here, Mother, and you didn't tell me until it was about to happen?" Of course, it would be just like her; you've come to expect as much from your mother since you were young. "You do not have any means to change the necessity of this decision, and to be frank, neither do I. It can't be helped. I will not throw our family situation and the balance of powers across the ocean into disarray." "Then why call me here in the first place, if I can't do anything about it?" "It's still something you need to witness." |You bow your head. "It looks like an important decision, Mother." "It is. Even if neither of us can change the necessity of what has to happen, I still want you to be here. To be informed." "I trust you to make the best decisions for us all, Mother, as you have done since I was but a kit." Mother smiles thinly, but warmly. "Ah... while it certainly is flattering to be deferred to, someday you must make your own decisions, daughter." ] It's [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|Granny Komari|Matron Komari] who defuses the situation before it can spiral any further — or at least, tries to. "Maybe she should read the document for herself. Let the girl draw her own conclusions." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Yes, and there's no %"maybe" about that. Whatever's going on here, you want to know |You would be much obliged ]. Stepping forward to the table, keenly aware of all three pairs of eyes on you, it takes but a moment for you to pore over the document in its entirety. Then at last... the full realization of what Mother intends to do here hits home, why she needs an imperial witness to the signing — and they had gone to such lengths to send a member of the second most prominent clan in all of the Old Country. She's signing away her birthright — and by extent, yours as well. You read it again, just to be sure, but there's soon no doubt in your mind that Mother intends to formally renounce all of her claims in favor of the descendants of her sister's line. The lands, the holdings, any claims to the clan's coffers, any political weight or ability to make decisions... Mother would retain her rank and title and be expected deference, especially as one who was brought back from the brink of death by divinity itself, but effectively, she's formally abdicating in favor of her now long-dead sister. Which is what de facto has been happening for a long while, but to see it spelled out like this... A lump forms in your throat. Now you see why Mother wanted you in on this, and why everyone's all dressed up. But even so... "Kinu." Mother is as somber as can be. "Allow me to be direct. Given the chance... would you want to be the den mother of the Otomo clan? Be counted amongst the heads of the twelve clans who are seated about his Imperial Majesty at court? Live across the ocean alternately in the clan's ancestral holdings and the capital, direct and shape policy, have everyone who bore the Otomo name be obligated to accede to your wishes no matter how great or small? A life within those fine, perfumed halls, surrounded by scheming and intrigue from the ministries? Is this a life you could lead?" The answer is immediately clear to you. "No. "[kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |It would have no reality." Kotone's voice drops several degrees. You thought it couldn't get any colder, but it does. "It would have no reality, you say. That is an interesting perspective." Gods, you're not going to let yourself be intimidated, even if she is a Fujiwara. If you can stand up to Mother, you can stand up to some snotty vixen. "I've lived here and known little else. All the people I've ever cared about are with me in the colonies. All my daily work... I'm able to see it come to fruition before my eyes. My vision... is more than endless gridlock and bickering, even if it's done in court. In a city, I would not feel the earth under my feet, would not have my quiet, would not be able to smell fresh sap or the scent of spring water. "I understand my heritage and roots, but they do not form the stem or the branches. They inform what I've been, but will not dictate where I'll go. And being over the ocean, in a life I cannot imagine and by all accounts would hate utterly... I would be ill-served to serve the Cherry Blossom Throne that way. "So yes. It would have no reality. I am content where I am." |I will not abandon my people." "Interesting. Do explain." "If it came to that, I could cross the ocean. I could take up residence in the capital, in my ancestral holdings, direct and lead as den mother amongst the twelve. But the people here who rely on me... no, they depend on me — I cannot, will not abandon them for my ambitions. What kind of leader would I be, what kind of stewardship could I enact if I were the kind of den mother who would do that? Those here in the colonies, they're the ones I've come to know, have ruled; I know their needs best, and they have few in good standing to represent said needs. Colonials are already looked down upon, and I won't take away what little they have." Kotone's voice drops several degrees. You thought it couldn't get any colder, but it does. "I see. Very noble, forsaking your birthright for the people. Self-sacrificial in the extreme." "Less self-sacrificial, and more understanding of where my duties lie." ] [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Mother just turns away, her fact red with... anger? Regret? Shame? "It's better this way. Everyone gets what they want |Mother looks a little sad. "You might have made a good princess, my daughter... but if you were in a position to be, you wouldn't have had the chance to exist to begin with ]. This is for the good of the realm, that we remain here in the colonies. Even if I sign this formal renouncement... Kuzunoha's descendants will always suspect me of wanting to take back what they imagine is rightfully mine. It is best we stay here in the colonies... we can serve his divine lordship and advance his interests better this way." The words are unspoken, but you can all but read them: exile, without being called exile. "Very well, then." Kotone puts her hands together. "Myobu-sama, if you would place your seal... Colonial Governor, yours as well. I will then formally witness the signing, and be back across the ocean posthaste once the torii gate is ready. This land puts a chill in my bones." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Gods, you just want to punch this bitch. The veiled insults, the stuck-up attitude, the sheer amounts of passive-aggression rolling off this damned Fujiwara vixen that've gotten even Mother and Granny Komari all cowed... the clan name may mean a lot to them as they were born and raised across the ocean, but as far as you're concerned it means nothing to you. You can't imagine the life that you would've had, dealing with such pompous pricks on a daily basis. Living as a princess would suck, and you're immensely glad you're not one. Mother can sign away your birthright for all you care — you'll make one here that's worth having, with your own two hands. |For a few moments, you feel a little sad that you won't have the chance to properly put this bitch in her place. The veiled insults, the stuck-up attitude, the sheer amounts of passive-aggression rolling off this damned Fujiwara vixen that've gotten even Mother and Granny Komari all cowed... you know your genealogies by heart and understand why everything is the way it is, but... Curse it all. Has no one learned anything from his divine lordship's return to the world, or the chastisements he so carefully delivered centuries ago? Is this how everything's going to play out time after time? Being a princess might not be so bad... in the colonies. Sure, Mother is signing away your birthright, but like she said, it's for the best. ] With all the solemnity of an imperial concubine, Mother conjures a spark of foxfire on the tip of her index finger. Carefully, she presses it upon the bottom of the scroll, and lines of glowing blue spread outward from her fingertip, forming into the intricate, arcane pattern of your mother's signature. The essence of her foxfire is indelibly and uniquely hers, something no other kitsune, let alone other person, would be able to copy. [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|Granny|Matron] Komari does the same, and Kotone is about to place her seal in her position as imperial witness when Mother stops her with a raised hand. "Myobu-sama?" "A moment, please. Kinu, you too." Kotone frowns. "Having your daughter as a signatory is not in the books, Myobu-sama." "Perhaps it will put my relatives' hearts and minds better at ease if my heir also unequivocally states that she has understood and accepted what I am about, and that she will not contest the decision. Further reinforcing my position by gaining my heir's acceptance of her fortunes cannot hurt, can it?" "No, I suppose it cannot." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |You step forward to the table and dredge up your seal from the depths of your memories. Have you ever used it in an official capacity? If you have, you don't remember it in the least... but as you light your finger with foxfire and move to press it down upon the paper, your mind goes back to when Mother and you worked out a seal for you together. You were more interested in the magical aspect of the exercise than the heraldry involved, even if you learned both anyway, but those were happier times — no, not necessarily happier, but simpler. Mother and you in the same room, laughing together... She hardly does that any more. Part of you wants it all back, but you know that your days as a child with three tails are gone forever, and this is the future that was made. A future where you're now signing your birthright away because it has no meaning to you any more, if it ever did to begin with. |You step forward to the table, and summon your seal to mind; with how often Matron Komari has you be a witness to her documents, you're well-practiced at this. Try as you might, you can't help but read through the document once more even as your finger's outstretched, poised to give your acknowledgement; every single clause, every single agreement as to what Mother is giving up — and hence, you will be, too — No. It would be nice, but you need none of this. Like Nakano, you'll build something up from nothing, despite every force from your ostensible homeland being arrayed against you. 你去处理吧。当琴音从你身边掠过、渐渐远去时，你胃里的那种紧张感只会愈发强烈。 [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |虽然你的工作服很干净，而且在你看来也还算得体，但它们终究还是工作服，实在不适合参加这样的场合。无论你如何洗澡、清洗，泥土和树液的味道早已渗透进你的皮肤、毛发，甚至深入你的骨骼之中。这一点，是无可改变的。这个这就是为什么你会讨厌遇到的那么多人…… |虽然有些震惊，但并没有因此动摇——事实就是如此。或许你应该去找米可，和她好好谈谈吧……你的未来姑表妹总是充满各种大胆的想法。即使你们最终想不出什么具体的解决办法，至少聊一聊也会让你感觉好一些…… ]
rows.raw: " Some time ago... You wonder why Mother has summoned you here, now of all times. It's still early in the morning... you have to [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |be out tending to the fields — even though you've been up since the crack of dawn, the weeding's still half-done and the thought of leaving anything incomplete really chafes at you. Still, it's Mother's summons, and if she's calling you all the way here to granny's chambers then it has to be important. She even told you to make yourself presentable, so you even went and took the time to scrub yourself down from head to toe... that's got to be enough, right? |see to the restoration works, [kiyoko.numKits 8 |give Aya, Tatsumi and Asagiri their directives for the day before you can tend to other matters |guide the hands granny was so kind to lend you in restoring your home ]. It's not as if you wouldn't be heading out to granny's later in the day... but then again, a refined lady like you doesn't harbour such contentious thoughts. Mother must have a good reason for summoning you all the way to the den matron's chambers at the crack of dawn, and she even told you to make yourself presentable at that. Even having your best clothes on, bathing from head to toe and brushing out your tails... you feel a little inadequate. The way Mother phrased it, this is going to be something important and merely decent isn't going to cut it, and yet time is what it is... ] Standing in the doorway, you announce yourself, and are met by [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|granny's|the den matron's] voice in reply. "Enter." Waiting for you within are both Mother and [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|Granny|Matron] Komari, but there's one more personage between them at the table: a four-tailed kitsune woman clad in soft furs of red, orange and black that leave her shoulders exposed, as well as platform sandals. She looks to be about your age and would be as tall as you, too, but her footwear gives her enough additional height to peer down the length of her nose at you. Finely and foxily-featured, bearing distinct cheeks streaked with red pigment and a delicate expression that no doubt hides the iron will beneath... no doubt high nobility, like you. And to prove it, there's her hair. You've yet to see [kiyoko.numKits 4|anyone with white hair and fur outside of your brothers and sisters|anyone else with white hair and fur except you], but it's done up in flowing tresses, marked with red ribbons and held in place by a couple of hairpins. White hair and fur... someone from another of the twelve Divine Clans, then. [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Suddenly, you realize that you are very, very inadequate — even Mother, who wears the same style of yukata all the time, has put on her best finery for the occasion. Even Granny Komari has put on her best finery. And here you are, standing in your fieldwork clothes, sticking out like a sore thumb. While you aren't the most keen at dressing up, at least you know enough to realize the amount of shame you're casting upon both Mother and Granny Komari must be astronomical. Damn it. Well, best foot forward. Turning tails and fleeing would just make the situation worse. |Not that you don't know who this is — even if you don't recognize the face, Mother and Matron Komari have taught you enough to know what the Fujiwara crest looks like, emblazoned on her chest just under her smallish rack. Your mind races, trying to evaluate your relative social standing to hers and choosing the appropriate greeting given your social stations ] — "Kinu, this is Kotone Fujiwara," Mother begins. "All the way across the ocean by torii gate, she is here in full official capacity as a witness on behalf of the Cherry Blossom Throne. While she may be your junior in relative standing, please give her all due respect that her position entails." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Witness? What's she here to witness? |And as a Fujiwara, of course. Don't want to anger her relatives. But that part doesn't need to be said. The bigger question is, what's she here to witness? ] Then, you notice the scroll laid out on the table — exquisite calligraphy in the manner of all official documents, and the imperial seal. No doubt prepared by a professional scribe... [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |"Something of great import is happening here, Mother, and you didn't tell me until it was about to happen?" Of course, it would be just like her; you've come to expect as much from your mother since you were young. "You do not have any means to change the necessity of this decision, and to be frank, neither do I. It can't be helped. I will not throw our family situation and the balance of powers across the ocean into disarray." "Then why call me here in the first place, if I can't do anything about it?" "It's still something you need to witness." |You bow your head. "It looks like an important decision, Mother." "It is. Even if neither of us can change the necessity of what has to happen, I still want you to be here. To be informed." "I trust you to make the best decisions for us all, Mother, as you have done since I was but a kit." Mother smiles thinly, but warmly. "Ah... while it certainly is flattering to be deferred to, someday you must make your own decisions, daughter." ] It's [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|Granny Komari|Matron Komari] who defuses the situation before it can spiral any further — or at least, tries to. "Maybe she should read the document for herself. Let the girl draw her own conclusions." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Yes, and there's no %"maybe" about that. Whatever's going on here, you want to know |You would be much obliged ]. Stepping forward to the table, keenly aware of all three pairs of eyes on you, it takes but a moment for you to pore over the document in its entirety. Then at last... the full realization of what Mother intends to do here hits home, why she needs an imperial witness to the signing — and they had gone to such lengths to send a member of the second most prominent clan in all of the Old Country. She's signing away her birthright — and by extent, yours as well. You read it again, just to be sure, but there's soon no doubt in your mind that Mother intends to formally renounce all of her claims in favor of the descendants of her sister's line. The lands, the holdings, any claims to the clan's coffers, any political weight or ability to make decisions... Mother would retain her rank and title and be expected deference, especially as one who was brought back from the brink of death by divinity itself, but effectively, she's formally abdicating in favor of her now long-dead sister. Which is what de facto has been happening for a long while, but to see it spelled out like this... A lump forms in your throat. Now you see why Mother wanted you in on this, and why everyone's all dressed up. But even so... "Kinu." Mother is as somber as can be. "Allow me to be direct. Given the chance... would you want to be the den mother of the Otomo clan? Be counted amongst the heads of the twelve clans who are seated about his Imperial Majesty at court? Live across the ocean alternately in the clan's ancestral holdings and the capital, direct and shape policy, have everyone who bore the Otomo name be obligated to accede to your wishes no matter how great or small? A life within those fine, perfumed halls, surrounded by scheming and intrigue from the ministries? Is this a life you could lead?" The answer is immediately clear to you. "No. "[kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |It would have no reality." Kotone's voice drops several degrees. You thought it couldn't get any colder, but it does. "It would have no reality, you say. That is an interesting perspective." Gods, you're not going to let yourself be intimidated, even if she is a Fujiwara. If you can stand up to Mother, you can stand up to some snotty vixen. "I've lived here and known little else. All the people I've ever cared about are with me in the colonies. All my daily work... I'm able to see it come to fruition before my eyes. My vision... is more than endless gridlock and bickering, even if it's done in court. In a city, I would not feel the earth under my feet, would not have my quiet, would not be able to smell fresh sap or the scent of spring water. "I understand my heritage and roots, but they do not form the stem or the branches. They inform what I've been, but will not dictate where I'll go. And being over the ocean, in a life I cannot imagine and by all accounts would hate utterly... I would be ill-served to serve the Cherry Blossom Throne that way. "So yes. It would have no reality. I am content where I am." |I will not abandon my people." "Interesting. Do explain." "If it came to that, I could cross the ocean. I could take up residence in the capital, in my ancestral holdings, direct and lead as den mother amongst the twelve. But the people here who rely on me... no, they depend on me — I cannot, will not abandon them for my ambitions. What kind of leader would I be, what kind of stewardship could I enact if I were the kind of den mother who would do that? Those here in the colonies, they're the ones I've come to know, have ruled; I know their needs best, and they have few in good standing to represent said needs. Colonials are already looked down upon, and I won't take away what little they have." Kotone's voice drops several degrees. You thought it couldn't get any colder, but it does. "I see. Very noble, forsaking your birthright for the people. Self-sacrificial in the extreme." "Less self-sacrificial, and more understanding of where my duties lie." ] [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Mother just turns away, her fact red with... anger? Regret? Shame? "It's better this way. Everyone gets what they want |Mother looks a little sad. "You might have made a good princess, my daughter... but if you were in a position to be, you wouldn't have had the chance to exist to begin with ]. This is for the good of the realm, that we remain here in the colonies. Even if I sign this formal renouncement... Kuzunoha's descendants will always suspect me of wanting to take back what they imagine is rightfully mine. It is best we stay here in the colonies... we can serve his divine lordship and advance his interests better this way." The words are unspoken, but you can all but read them: exile, without being called exile. "Very well, then." Kotone puts her hands together. "Myobu-sama, if you would place your seal... Colonial Governor, yours as well. I will then formally witness the signing, and be back across the ocean posthaste once the torii gate is ready. This land puts a chill in my bones." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Gods, you just want to punch this bitch. The veiled insults, the stuck-up attitude, the sheer amounts of passive-aggression rolling off this damned Fujiwara vixen that've gotten even Mother and Granny Komari all cowed... the clan name may mean a lot to them as they were born and raised across the ocean, but as far as you're concerned it means nothing to you. You can't imagine the life that you would've had, dealing with such pompous pricks on a daily basis. Living as a princess would suck, and you're immensely glad you're not one. Mother can sign away your birthright for all you care — you'll make one here that's worth having, with your own two hands. |For a few moments, you feel a little sad that you won't have the chance to properly put this bitch in her place. The veiled insults, the stuck-up attitude, the sheer amounts of passive-aggression rolling off this damned Fujiwara vixen that've gotten even Mother and Granny Komari all cowed... you know your genealogies by heart and understand why everything is the way it is, but... Curse it all. Has no one learned anything from his divine lordship's return to the world, or the chastisements he so carefully delivered centuries ago? Is this how everything's going to play out time after time? Being a princess might not be so bad... in the colonies. Sure, Mother is signing away your birthright, but like she said, it's for the best. ] With all the solemnity of an imperial concubine, Mother conjures a spark of foxfire on the tip of her index finger. Carefully, she presses it upon the bottom of the scroll, and lines of glowing blue spread outward from her fingertip, forming into the intricate, arcane pattern of your mother's signature. The essence of her foxfire is indelibly and uniquely hers, something no other kitsune, let alone other person, would be able to copy. [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|Granny|Matron] Komari does the same, and Kotone is about to place her seal in her position as imperial witness when Mother stops her with a raised hand. "Myobu-sama?" "A moment, please. Kinu, you too." Kotone frowns. "Having your daughter as a signatory is not in the books, Myobu-sama." "Perhaps it will put my relatives' hearts and minds better at ease if my heir also unequivocally states that she has understood and accepted what I am about, and that she will not contest the decision. Further reinforcing my position by gaining my heir's acceptance of her fortunes cannot hurt, can it?" "No, I suppose it cannot." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |You step forward to the table and dredge up your seal from the depths of your memories. Have you ever used it in an official capacity? If you have, you don't remember it in the least... but as you light your finger with foxfire and move to press it down upon the paper, your mind goes back to when Mother and you worked out a seal for you together. You were more interested in the magical aspect of the exercise than the heraldry involved, even if you learned both anyway, but those were happier times — no, not necessarily happier, but simpler. Mother and you in the same room, laughing together... She hardly does that any more. Part of you wants it all back, but you know that your days as a child with three tails are gone forever, and this is the future that was made. A future where you're now signing your birthright away because it has no meaning to you any more, if it ever did to begin with. |You step forward to the table, and summon your seal to mind; with how often Matron Komari has you be a witness to her documents, you're well-practiced at this. Try as you might, you can't help but read through the document once more even as your finger's outstretched, poised to give your acknowledgement; every single clause, every single agreement as to what Mother is giving up — and hence, you will be, too — No. It would be nice, but you need none of this. Like Nakano, you'll build something up from nothing, despite every force from your ostensible homeland being arrayed against you. That way, they'll have no choice but to acknowledge the strength of the colonial-born. ] "Kinu." You realize that you've been standing stock-still for several moments, your finger poised above blank paper. "[kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|Sorry|My apologies]. I — I will not delay any further." Pressing your finger to the fine mulberry paper, you feel foxfire seep out and trace your seal under Mother's and [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|Granny|Matron] Komari's. There, it's done. The last to sign to document is Kotone; she burns her version of the Fujiwara crest upon the very bottom, looks over the scroll, and nods. She rolls it up, ties it up with a length of red string, and rises to her feet. "This will do. I will return this to the capital with utmost haste; once the emperor and ministries have ratified this abdication, copies will be dispatched to the sitting den mother and to you, of course." The undertone is clear as crystal: I want out of this backwater village as quickly as possible. [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0|Granny|Matron] Komari bows. "I will have the torii gate prepared with utmost urgency." "See to it." As Kotone sweeps past you and leaves, the tightness in the pit of your stomach only intensifies. [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Though clean and — as far as your estimation is concerned — presentable, your work clothes are still work clothes, hardly fit for an occasion like this. No matter how you bathe and scrub, the smell of earth and sap is ingrained into not just your skin and fur, but your very bones at this point. This, this is why you hate so many of the people you come across — Granny Komari clears her throat, her voice hitting your thoughts just so and slicing through them like a blade. "Kinu!" The look in her eyes is clear: don't do anything rash. |Despite being clad in your best finery for the occasion, you can feel how inadequate you are as a colonial to someone who has the resources, refinement and backing of that sort. You know you're far outclassed, the proper order of things be damned, and while anger is perhaps too strong a word and what you shouldn't be feeling right now, the feeling of disdain certainly is mutual, if nothing else. ] Submissively, you bow your head and force yourself to still until the imperial witness' footsteps have faded. "Well," Mother says. "That went better than what I would have expected." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Not that it would have amounted to very much, given how low Mother's expectations for you already are |Indeed. You understand just how much of a risk Mother took in involving you in all of this, even if you don't fully realize the implications ]. What you've just done... despite its reality, it all feels like a dream. [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |What good is a birthright you have no roots in? |The suddenness of it all... perhaps Mother meant to throw you off-guard? No, that's not right. ] "I... I need to lie down," you say at last. Not exactly the full truth, but not a lie, either. "This has all been very sudden." "It must be. Please." Remembering your manners, you quietly bow and take your leave. [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Maybe Mai is rubbing off more on you than you thought — you have been spending more and more time with your future cousin-in-law these days; she's one of the few people you can stand to be around for any extended length of time. You don't want to end up completely dead inside like she is... but at the same time, her ability to take most things in stride is admirable. |Shaken, but not stirred — that's how it is. Maybe you should go find Miko, talk it over — your future cousin-in-law is always full of bold ideas. Even if the two of you come up with nothing concrete, talking about it will make you feel better... ] "

rows.original: [var0 |Approaching Komari, you inform the den matron that you've done as she asked and made good your introductions. Setting down her brush, she acknowledges your words with a nod and invites you to take a seat with a flick of one of her many tails. "And quite satisfactorily, too. Now that you're acquainted with everyone and shown that you can at least cooperate with us, we can begin. Give me a little while to finish this, and I'll make time for you, [pc.race]." She just sent you on a little meet-and-greet, and now she's going to make you wait even more? Komari shrugs[silly|| and says something in her native tongue, then catches herself and speaks in Belharan]. [silly|「しょうがない — I mean, i|"I]t can't be helped. Matters of divinity take precedence over all, I'm afraid, and that goes doubly for someone in my position. Even you will have to wait a little." The completely bland matter-of-fact way in which this nine-tailed grandma says it — [pc.isDK |it sets your teeth on edge. It'd have been better if there was actually some perceptible malice behind it, but the blaise way in which she expects you to put up with the wait as if — as if you were one of them and are just supposed to accept it |it's just more than a little annoying. While you can understand her priorities, the way she just expects you to put up with the wait as if — as if you were one of them and take it as things being the way they are ] — — Well. There is nothing to be done, is there? Damn it, if you don't watch yourself, these foxes are going to end up rubbing off on you more than you know it, and not necessarily in the fun fashion. You'll just step outside for a bit and give her the few minutes she requested...
rows.translation: [var0 |走近麻里，你告诉巢穴主母，你已经照她说的做了，也好好完成了自我介绍。她放下画笔，点头认可你的话，又甩了甩众多尾巴中的一条，示意你坐下。 “而且完成得相当令人满意。既然你已经认识了所有人，也证明了你至少能和我们合作，那我们就可以开始了。给我一点时间把这个弄完，之后我会抽空见你，[pc.race]。” 她才刚让你做了一圈小小的见面问候，现在又要让你继续等？ 麻里耸了耸肩[silly||，用她的母语说了些什么，随后又意识到这一点，改用贝尔哈兰语说道]。[silly|“しょうがない — 我是说，没|“没]办法。神性的事务高于一切，恐怕如此；而对我这种位置的人来说，就更是如此了。就算是你，也得稍微等一等。” 这位九尾老奶奶把话说得完全平淡而理所当然—— [pc.isDK |这让你牙根发痒。要是其中真有一丝能察觉到的恶意，反倒还好些；可她那副淡然的样子，仿佛你就该忍受这种等待，仿佛——仿佛你也是她们中的一员，只能理所当然地接受这一切 |这实在有点让人恼火。你能理解她的优先事项，但她就是这么理所当然地期待你忍受等待，仿佛——仿佛你也是她们中的一员，把这当成事情本该如此 ] — ——好吧。也确实没什么可做的，不是吗？该死，要是不注意的话，这些狐狸迟早会在不知不觉间影响到你，而且还不一定是有趣的那种方式。 你还是先出去一会儿，给她那几分钟时间吧……

The completely bland matter-of-fact way in which this nine-tailed grandma says it — [pc.isDK |it sets your teeth on edge. It'd have been better if there was actually some perceptible malice behind it, but the blaise way in which she expects you to put up with the wait as if — as if you were one of them and are just supposed to accept it |it's just more than a little annoying. While you can understand her priorities, the way she just expects you to put up with the wait as if — as if you were one of them and take it as things being the way they are ] — — Well. There is nothing to be done, is there? Damn it, if you don't watch yourself, these foxes are going to end up rubbing off on you more than you know it, and not necessarily in the fun fashion. You'll just step outside for a bit and give her the few minutes she requested... "

rows.original: |Komari looks up at you. "Well, [pc.name]? Have you made those few introductions Y-you're working on it.I've asked you to?" "Sometimes it can be hard to open up to new people, especially if the two of you got off on the wrong foot to begin with. Stepping on each others' tails and all. Still, it has to be done if misunderstandings are cleared up. Now then... I must insist on you being on speaking, if not familiar terms with the people you are going to be dealing with if you're going to be doing anything meaningful around here. "You're already going to be drawing enough stares as [a] [pc.race] as it is, no need to make things worse. Once the people hear that their leaders have given you their stamp of approval, you'll find them much more welcoming than they would have been otherwise. So really, it's to your benefit to simply bite down on the arrowhead, as one of your own sayings goes." Like it or not, she's right. When it comes down to it, how hard can making a few introductions be? Maybe it's best to put off the procrastinating and just get this over with so you can move matters forward... In order to interact meaningfully with Komari, you'll need to make nice with those who live in her little fiefdom. Best get to it[silly|, because I really don't want to have to account for seventy billion states in which you are or aren't acquainted with X or Y character, which is why I'm going to make you jump through all these hoops]. ]
rows.translation: |麻里抬头看着你。嗯， [pc.name]你把那些介绍内容准备好了吗？ 你正在处理这件事，我不是已经要求你了吗？ 有时候，向新认识的人敞开心扉确实是一件困难的事，尤其是当你们一开始就相处得不太顺利的时候。互相误会、彼此排斥，这些都是很常见的情况。不过，如果想要消除这些误会，就必须迈出这一步。那么……我必须坚持要求你，如果你想在这里取得任何实质性的进展，就必须与你未来要打交道的人建立良好的沟通关系，至少要达到能够正常交流的程度。 你身为[pc.race]本来就会引来不少目光，既然如此，就没有必要让事情变得更糟了。一旦人们得知他们的领导已经给予了你支持，他们会比原本更加热情地欢迎你。所以说，按照你们自己的一句话来说，接受这个现实其实对你是有利的。 不管你愿不愿意承认，她是对的。说到底，介绍几个人又有什么难的呢？也许最好的办法就是别再拖延了，赶紧把这件事搞定，这样才能让事情继续向前发展…… 要想与麻里进行有意义的互动，你就必须与居住在她那小领地里的那些生物们搞好关系。最好现在就着手去做这件事。[silly|因为我真的不想去处理那些关于你是否认识某个角色之类的复杂情况，所以才要让你经历这些繁琐的步骤]。 ]

rows.original: [rand |You step forward and approach, but Komari isn't at her floor desk — instead, the den matron is staring contemplatively out one of the many windows, lost in her own thoughts. She notices you as you draw near, though, and [pc.ra kitsune |turns to give you a small bow. "Why, if it isn't [pc.mf|his Eminence himself|her Eminence herself] |gives you a small nod. "I was half-expecting your arrival ]. Is there something I can do for you today?" |You step into the chamber to find Komari tending to an absolutely adorable miniature tree in a porcelain basin, pruning it with what looks to be a pair of tiny shears. A small woman tending to a small tree with small tools — there's something poignant about this picture that can't quite be placed into words. Waiting a little while only has her get even more absorbed into this delicate procedure, and eventually you announce yourself by clearing your throat softly. Only then does the den matron notice you. [pc.ra kitsune |"Ah. Of course, so that was what I was feeling. Forgive me, your Eminence — I will be with you posthaste |"Oh. I didn't see you there. I'd thought you would show up sometime about now, but couldn't foretell exactly when." For someone who has the gift of foresight, it's quite awkward for her to be taken by surprise like this. "It is more a matter of perception than knowledge ]. When one has all the time in the world, it is but a slip of the mind to lose track of it... still. Is there something you need of me today?" |Entering the front of the matron's quarters, you find Komari at her books, fingers carefully flicking up and down along an old, lacquered abacus; the beads clack with very final-sounding notes to them as she moves them up and down. She notices you as you approach the low desk, though, and sets aside the lot, perhaps looking a little relieved for an excuse to pry herself away from the tedium of book-keeping. "Welcome[pc.ra kitsune|, your Eminence]. You've arrived at quite the opportune time — I was just about to set myself aside for the moment." Set herself aside? That's a strange way of putting it... at least, in Belharan. "Perhaps it would be better to say I was expecting you and contrived to make myself available at this moment, then. I was not wrong, and you are here — and now that you are, is there something I can do for you?" |Stepping into the brightly lit room, you find Komari by the window, several paper charms stuck to the sill and fluttering about in the breeze. The den matron is looking over something in her hands — a contraption of metal, living wood and fine moving parts — but sets it down on the windowsill and turns to you as you approach. "[pc.ra kitsune |Always a pleasure to receive you here, your Eminence. It's nice to have someone on relatively equal footing to speak to once in a while, wouldn't you agree? That being said, is there something I can help you with?" |Ah, you're here. Mai said you might be arriving about now... which provides me with an excuse to set this aside for the moment. ]" Did you come at a bad time? "Oh no, no. I was merely inspecting the artificer's latest creation to make sure it wouldn't go awry. Fascinating in its own right, yet largely impractical, much like its creator. As above, so below, as your people are fond of saying — now then, is there something I can do for you?" ] Oh, you might be here, but certainly there's no need to stand on ceremony. [pc.ra kitsune |Being who you are, you certainly have the authority to ease the mood of this meeting, don't you? |You're just a bumbling outsider, after all, and one can be forgiven for being informal with one, right? ] "Ah, well..." [party.has kiyoko |[rand |"Come now, Komari," your beloved fox-wife says from your side. "Or do I have to order you to be at ease?" "Oh, [silly|My|Lad] — Kiyoko, I suppose you have me there. I can hardly disobey my liege, can I?" |From your side, your beloved fox-wife clears her throat. "I say, Komari, do you still make those honey-glazed cakes with red bean filling? It would be nice to taste those together once again after a couple centuries apart. I tried making some on my own, but they're never quite the same; maybe it's because it's a provincial recipe." Something passes between retainer and liege that you don't quite grasp but nevertheless palpably feel, and Komari eventually bows her head as tension drains from the air. "Miko is quite the capable girl in that regard; if you are staying long enough, I'll have some sent up." "That will suffice." |"There, there," your fox-wife purrs from beside you. "Would you take a little time off to speak candidly with your liege and her consort?" "Why of course, [silly|My|Lad] — Kiyoko. I... ah, it just has been too long." "It has indeed," your fox-wife agrees. "Which is why we should take the time to speak in a more relaxed setting, should we not?" ] ] Komari flicks one of her many tails in your direction and has a seat drawn up for you[party.has kiyoko|, along with one for your fox-wife]. You take your time making yourself comfortable while she settles in across from you, nestled comfortably in the faded fur of her many tails. Sitting down when you have that much fluff behind you must be a little hard, but she's clearly used to it at this point. [var0 |At length, Kinu comes up to the [party.has kiyoko|three|two] of you, taking small steps with a tray in her hands. Ever the picture-perfect portrait of refinement and elegance, your fox-daughter serves the [party.has kiyoko|three|two] of you fine cups of steaming, bitter-smelling tea. "Good girl," Komari tells her, dismissing your daughter with a gentle wave. "Be productive and occupy yourself while [party.has kiyoko|your parents and I|we] talk, all right?" Kinu says nothing, but dips her head and gives a shallow bow before retreating behind the screens. Komari sniffs at the steam rising from her cup and looses an appreciative sigh before picking it up. "[party.has kiyoko |[rand |Your daughter is incredibly bright yet possessed of much humility, Kiyoko. Her education has been quite impeccable and has proven quite useful in helping out around here." "The greatest teaching one can be taught is the ability to teach oneself. She has begun to grasp that. I am satisfied with her upbringing." "Do you think..." "Ah, no. She is a colonial, as I understand it. A land across the ocean would have no reality for her, no matter how her blood may call for it." "Ah. Pity |Your daughter is quite the popular one around here, even given the comparatively short time she has been known. People instinctively like her because she's able to intuit what they're thinking and feeling... despite the difference in station, she's able to make them feel at ease." "Hmm... are you sure it's not just because she's an Ōtomo?" "Come now. If that were the case, both you and I would know |Quite the fine figure your daughter cuts there, Kiyoko... just like you in the ways that matter most. She'll go far." "She will." A short pause. "I would have liked to meet your daughter sometime, Komari. You always spoke of the kits you wanted to have, back in the day. Oh well, it can't be helped — I suppose I will have to content myself with my daughter being familiar with your descendants." "Ah... it is as you say ] |What a wonderful daughter you have[pc.ra kitsune|, your Eminence]. She certainly has a bright future ahead of her... and so it falls to us to create the conditions for that possibility to be realized ]. Now that we are settled in, shall we begin?" ]
rows.translation: [rand |你走上前去，靠近她，却发现麻里并没有坐在她的书桌前——相反，这位宿舍管理员正凝视着窗外，似乎陷入了沉思。不过，当你靠近时，她还是注意到了你。 [pc.ra kitsune |转身向你轻轻鞠了一躬。哎呀，难道不是这样吗[pc.mf|阁下本人|她本人] |微微点了点头。我其实有点期待你的到来。 ]今天有什么我可以帮您的吗？ |你走进那个房间，看到麻里正在一个瓷盆里照料着一棵极其可爱的小树，她似乎用一把小小的剪刀来修剪它。一个身材娇小的女人用小巧的工具照料着一棵小树——这一幕充满了某种令人动容的美感，这种感觉实在难以用言语来表达。等了一会儿，她反而更加专注地投入到这个细致的过程中去了，直到你轻轻清了清嗓子，才有人注意到你的存在。 这时，洞穴的女主人才终于注意到了你。 [pc.ra kitsune |啊，当然，我刚才就是这种感觉。请原谅我，尊贵的阁下——我会立刻赶去陪您的。 |哦，我之前没注意到你在那里。我本来以为你应该会在这个时候出现，但实在无法准确预测你会在什么时候到来。 对于一个具备预见能力的人来说，被这样突然抓住把柄，确实是一件相当尴尬的事情。 这更多是一种感知问题，而非知识问题。 ]当一个人拥有无穷的时间时，忘记时间的流逝其实只是一时的疏忽而已……不过，今天你有什么需要我帮忙的吗？ |走进女管家的住所，你看到麻里正埋头读书，她的手指仔细地在一台古老的漆制算盘上上下移动；算盘上的珠子随着她的操作发出清脆的声音。当你走近那张矮桌时，她注意到了你，于是把算盘放在一旁，或许也觉得终于有借口可以摆脱这些繁琐的记账工作了，脸上露出了一丝如释重负的表情。 欢迎来到[pc.ra kitsune|，阁下]你来得正是时候——我正好打算暂时放下手头的工作。 把自己放在一边？用这种方式来表达的话，确实有点奇怪……至少在贝尔哈兰是这样认为的。 或许这么说更合适：我其实一直在等你，所以特意安排了自己在这个时刻出现。我的预料没有错，你果然来了——既然你来了，有什么我可以帮你的吗？ |走进那间灯火通明的房间，你看到麻里站在窗边，几张纸制护身符粘在窗台上，在微风中轻轻飘动。这位女首领正仔细端详着手中的某个物件——那是由金属、活木以及精密的活动部件组成的装置——但当你靠近时，她将那个物件放在窗台上，然后转过身来看着你。 "[pc.ra kitsune |能在这里接待您，真是我的荣幸，阁下。偶尔能与地位相当的人交谈，确实是一件愉快的事情，您不也这么认为吗？那么，有什么我可以帮您的吗？ |啊，你来了。梅说你应该差不多这个时候到……这正好给了我一个理由，可以把这件事暂时搁置一下。 ]" 你来得不是时候吗？ 哦不，不是这样的。我只是在检查那位工匠的最新作品，以确保它不会出问题而已。这件作品本身确实很有趣，但实用性却很低，就像它的创造者一样。正如你们常说的‘上如所下’——那么，现在有什么我可以帮您的吗？ ] 哦，你可能已经到了，不过实在没有必要拘泥于礼节。 [pc.ra kitsune |作为你这样的一个人，你当然有能力让这次会议的氛围变得轻松愉快，不是吗？ |毕竟，你只是一个笨手笨脚的外人，别人对你不客气一点，也是可以理解的，对吧？ ] 啊，好吧…… [party.has kiyoko |[rand |过来吧，麻里。你心爱的狐狸妻子也在为你说话。还是说，我必须得订购这样你就能放心了吧？ 哦， [silly|我的|小伙子] — 清子，我想你应该是想让我这么做吧。我几乎不可能违抗我的主公的命令，对吧？ |在你这边，你心爱的狐妖妻子清了清嗓子。我说啊，麻里，你还在做那种红豆馅的蜜糖烤饼吗？时隔几个世纪之后，能再一起品尝一次该多好啊。我试着自己做过，但味道就是不一样；也许是因为这是个地方性的食谱吧。 在封臣与领主之间，存在着某种你尚未完全理解，但却确实存在的联系或关系。感受到最终，随着紧张气氛逐渐消散，麻里也低下了头。在这方面，米可确实是个能力很强的女孩；如果你能多待一段时间，我会让她准备一些送上来给你。 这样就可以了。 |好了，好了。你的狐妖妻子正在你身旁轻轻打着呼噜。您能否抽出一点时间，与您的君主以及她的伴侣坦诚地谈一谈？ 当然了， [silly|我的|小伙子] — 清子。我……啊，只是太久没有见面了。 确实如此。你的狐妖妻子也同意。因此，我们应该找一个更加轻松的环境来交谈，不是吗？ ] ] 小蚊子用它那众多的尾巴中的一条指向你的方向，然后为你准备了一个座位。[party.has kiyoko|还有一个是给你的狐狸妻子用的。]你慢慢调整自己的姿势，让自己坐得舒服些，而她则坐在你对面，舒适地依偎在她那些褪色的尾巴毛皮中。当你身后有这么多毛茸茸的东西时，坐下肯定会有些困难，但显然她已经习惯了这种情况。 [var0 |终于，小娟走了过来。 [party.has kiyoko|三|两个]你们中间，有一位女子，手中端着托盘，迈着轻柔的步子走着。她永远都是那种优雅与高贵完美的象征，你们的那位狐妖女儿，正在为大家服务[party.has kiyoko|三|两个]为你准备了几杯热气腾腾、香气扑鼻的苦茶。 好姑娘。麻里对她说道，同时轻轻挥了挥手，表示对你们女儿的漠不关心。多做点事，让自己有事可做吧。 [party.has kiyoko|你的父母和我|我们]说话吧，好吗？ 纪久没有说话，只是低下了头，轻轻鞠了一躬，然后退到了屏风后面。麻里闻了闻自己杯子里升起的蒸汽，满意地叹了口气，然后拿起了杯子。"[party.has kiyoko |[rand |清子，你的女儿非常聪明，同时又十分谦虚。她的教育背景也非常出色，这些品质在这里确实帮了大忙。 一个人能学到的最重要的本领，就是学会自我学习。她已经开始领悟到这一点了。我对她的成长过程感到很满意。 你认为…… 啊，不。据我所知，她属于那种殖民地出身的人。对于她来说，大洋彼岸的土地根本不存在，无论她的血脉如何呼唤她去那里。 啊，真可怜。 |你的女儿在这里相当受欢迎，尽管她为人所知的时间还相对较短。人们本能地喜欢她，因为她能够敏锐地理解他们的想法和感受……尽管身份地位有所不同，她依然能让人们感到自在。 嗯……你确定这不仅仅是因为她是大友家的人吗？ 快过来。如果真是那样的话，你和我应该早就知道了。 |清子，你的女儿真是个漂亮的女孩……在最重要的方面，她和你一模一样。她一定会取得成功的。 她会的。短暂的停顿。我其实很想有空见见你的女儿，麻里。你以前总是提到那些你想要拥有的小动物……唉，也没办法了——我想，只要我的女儿能认识你的后代们，也就算是满足了。 啊……确实如你所说。 ] |你真是个了不起的女儿啊。[pc.ra kitsune|，阁下]她确实拥有光明的未来……因此，我们有责任为这一可能的实现创造条件。 ]现在我们已经安顿下来，可以开始了吗？ ]

"Miko is quite the capable girl in that regard; if you are staying long enough, I'll have some sent up." "That will suffice." |"There, there," your fox-wife purrs from beside you. "Would you take a little time off to speak candidly with your liege and her consort?" "Why of course, [silly|My|Lad] — Kiyoko. I... ah, it just has been too long." "It has indeed," your fox-wife agrees. "Which is why we should take the time to speak in a more relaxed setting, should we not?" ] ] Komari flicks one of her many tails in your direction and has a seat drawn up for you[party.has kiyoko|, along with one for your fox-wife]. You take your time making yourself comfortable while she settles in across from you, nestled comfortably in the faded fur of her many tails. Sitting down when you have that much fluff behind you must be a little hard, but she's clearly used to it at this point. [var0 |At length, Kinu comes up to the [party.has kiyoko|three|two] of you, taking small steps with a tray in her hands. Ever the picture-perfect portrait of refinement and elegance, your fox-daughter serves the [party.has kiyoko|three|two] of you fine cups of steaming, bitter-smelling tea. "Good girl," Komari tells her, dismissing your daughter with a gentle wave. "Be productive and occupy yourself while [party.has kiyoko|your parents and I|we] talk, all right?" Kinu says nothing, but dips her head and gives a shallow bow before retreating behind the screens. Komari sniffs at the steam rising from her cup and looses an appreciative sigh before picking it up. "[party.has kiyoko |[rand |Your daughter is incredibly bright yet possessed of much humility, Kiyoko. Her education has been quite impeccable and has proven quite useful in helping out around here." "The greatest teaching one can be taught is the ability to teach oneself. She has begun to grasp that. I am satisfied with her upbringing." "Do you think..." "Ah, no. She is a colonial, as I understand it. A land across the ocean would have no reality for her, no matter how her blood may call for it." "Ah. Pity |Your daughter is quite the popular one around here, even given the comparatively short time she has been known. People instinctively like her because she's able to intuit what they're thinking and feeling... despite the difference in station, she's able to make them feel at ease." "Hmm... are you sure it's not just because she's an Ōtomo?" "Come now. If that were the case, both you and I would know |Quite the fine figure your daughter cuts there, Kiyoko... just like you in the ways that matter most. She'll go far." "She will." A short pause. "I would have liked to meet your daughter sometime, Komari. You always spoke of the kits you wanted to have, back in the day. Oh well, it can't be helped — I suppose I will have to content myself with my daughter being familiar with your descendants." "Ah... it is as you say ] |What a wonderful daughter you have[pc.ra kitsune|, your Eminence]. She certainly has a bright future ahead of her... and so it falls to us to create the conditions for that possibility to be realized ]. Now that we are settled in, shall we begin?" ] '

rows.translation: 和[silly|麻里来一场酣战|麻里来一场激战]。

rows.original: [var0 |You take out the orb, lay it on the table, and remind Komari that she'd promised to do something about this once things had settled down in the den. As far as you're concerned, things have settled down pretty well for you and her to be sitting here chatting and sipping tea. Komari says nothing for a few seconds, the faint glow of her eyes brightening at the sight. At last, she plants both hands on the table's edge, reaches for her cane, and heaves herself to her feet. "I... I've been putting this off long enough, you're right. Perhaps... no, I will not be as cowardly as to not see this through to the end. Come then, [pc.ra kitsune|divine champion|[pc.name]]. We'll contact my master and see what can be done about the Lady Otomo. Do you mind if I hold the amulet while we make our way there?" No, of course you don't mind. If you did, you wouldn't have entrusted this to her in the first place. Gratitude, acknowledgement, perhaps fear and regret — you've never seen so much conveyed in a little dip of one's head, but the kitsune are masters of saying much with the smallest of gestures. Amulet in one hand and cane in the next, Komari shuffles out of her chambers and down towards the roots of the tree. |Right, there's something you needed to ask. You take out the amulet with its orb, set it on the table, and clear your throat. You found this piece while trawling some old kitsune ruins, and given that its make is clearly of her people's she'd be the most obvious person to ask, with it looking to be a religious piece and all. Does she — Komari looks like she's going to choke and faint, the den matron's fingers trembling and knocking against the table's surface. Blinking a few times — an eminently odd motion when one has no pupils — she steadies herself with a deep breath and faces you directly. "How did you come by this?" With no reason to hold back, you tell her everything. Coming across the ruined shrine in the woods near Hawkethorne, entering the cave in the back beyond the gemmed doors, the mural, the amulet hidden within an age's worth of dust and debris. Kiyoko manifesting in your dreams, speaking of her captivity. [kiyoko.numKits 1|Her asking for your life energy, and eventually bearing your child[kiyoko.numKits 2|ren]. ]Memories that feel as if they were dreams, mostly because they were — dreams that nevertheless were real, perhaps more than real. The words come unbidden, directly plucked from the back of your mind and flowing from your lips without further hesitation. While she listens, Komari fiddles with the simple amulet, testing the orb's old but gleaming surface with her fingertips. The den matron has her bouts of melancholy, but this is something else altogether; when you finally finish the tale, you notice that the tea has grown cold. Has it really been that long? Komari coughs and turns the amulet over in her hands. "Well. You've said as much... now it's time for me to shed some light on your situation. This amulet used to be mine; it was the keepsake of my family. Even my name... it means 'little ball' in your tongue, [pc.name]; I suppose my parents thought it funny. A family treasure... I lost it about two hundred and fifty years ago, not long after I arrived in this part of the world on divine orders to aid in this front of the Godswar... "I remember that day, I had been out with the harpies... Sorra's creatures were more civilized back in the day, but they were still insufferable, flighty creatures. Me and mine returned to find the den utterly ruined; the wraiths' minions had struck while we were out. Try as I might, I couldn't find the amulet of transference any more, one of the keys to our lord's Dream." A dream...? "You know it better as the Astral Plane. The Living Gods each have dreams, realms formed from... well, even I'm not sure myself. But we do know that they are sovereign in that domain; it is where their presence is most real, for lack of a better word to describe it." [flags.ARCHWAY_BOTH_SAVED |You know this to be true — after all, Nareva herself explained it to you, though the explanation was no less cryptic than anything else the serpent goddess said. |Interesting... ] Kiyoko must have escaped into the orb then, and it had lain buried in the debris for centuries until you came along. "With the family heirloom lost, I could not face my relatives. As the Lady Otomo's retainer, allowing her to die from my negligence meant I deserved death. The shame was too great... but my divine lord had other ideas. It would be a waste, he said, for my talents to be lost in such a manner... I would be exiled here with those who would stay alongside me, and keep a foothold for his influence in these foreign lands. By all rights I should have paid for my mistake with my life, but my Lord has seen fit to be magnanimous and give me a second chance. Perhaps this exile was the cowardly option, but today, I think I would have preferred death. Turning me into a yasha and forcing me to watch generations of my descendants age, wither and die while I remain unchanging... each time I perform the funerary rites, I desire more and more to simply be one with the land." Kiyoko was with her? "Kiyoko and I, although our positions in our clans were similar, the fact that she came from the twelve families and I did not meant that I was merely fit to be her retainer at best." A small smile appears on Komari's face as her ears fold forward. "Tell me, what do you know of Lady Otomo's past?" Well... come to think of it... Kiyoko's never told you that much about her life story. Not that she's ever been evasive or anything, but it just never really came up in daily conversation. You know she had a somewhat religious upbringing and something of her education, but the question of her standing in kitsune society never came up, mostly because there weren't any other kitsune around. "You didn't know who she was, had only just met her, and even so, acceded to an unsettling, if not downright disturbing request, wanting no compensation. Ah, such willingness to help... the wicked of this world would be so eager to take advantage of that." Is there a problem? Komari thinks a moment, then shakes her head. "Never mind. If the two of you are content together like this, it's for the better. It's not as if it means anything, not this far from the Old Country. Kiyoko was — I mean, is my liege and friend, and after all these years, I can only wish the best for her if she's found happiness." ... Is there a way to get Kiyoko out of the astral plane? That's why you showed her this to begin with. "Very likely, although it's something I'm not able to do under my own power. I'll have to ask my divine lord to intercede... and for that, we need to head down below. Do you mind if I hold this on the way?" No, of course you don't mind. If you did, you wouldn't have entrusted this to her in the first place. Gratitude, acknowledgement, perhaps fear and regret — you've never seen so much conveyed in a little dip of one's head, but the kitsune are masters of saying much with the smallest of gestures. Amulet in one hand and cane in the next, Komari shuffles out of her chambers and down towards the roots of the tree.[party.hasCompanions | You throw a glance back, leaving [party.compNames] to the tea and refreshments before hurrying after her. ] ]
rows.translation: [var0 |你取出那个球体，放在桌上，然后提醒麻里，她曾经承诺过，等巢穴里的局势稳定下来后，一定会处理这件事。在你看来，现在局势已经稳定多了，你们可以坐在这里聊天、喝茶了。 麻里沉默了几秒钟，看到那个球体后，她眼中的光芒突然亮了起来。最终，她把双手放在桌边，拿起了手杖，站了起来。我……我确实拖延得太久了，你说得对。也许……不，我一定要现在就去做。不是连这点勇气都没有，不敢坚持到底。那就来吧。 [pc.ra kitsune|神圣冠军|[pc.name]]我们会联系我的主人，看看能为奥托莫小姐做些什么。在我们去那里的路上，由我来保管这个护身符，你没有意见吧？ 不，你当然不会介意。如果你会介意的话，一开始就不会把这件事托付给她了。 感激、认可，或许还有恐惧与懊悔——你从未见过一个人仅仅通过轻轻低头就能表达出这么多情感，但狐族确实擅长用最微小的动作来传达丰富的情感。一手拿着护身符，另一手拄着拐杖，麻里缓缓走出了自己的房间，朝着那棵树的根部走去。 |对了，有件事你需要问问。你把那个带着圆球的护身符拿出来，放在桌子上，然后清了清嗓子。你是在翻找一些古老的狐族遗迹时发现这个物品的，而且由于它的制作工艺明显属于她们的族群，所以她应该是最合适询问的人选。毕竟这个东西看起来显然具有宗教意义。她—— 麻里看起来像是快要窒息昏过去了一样，那个巢穴的女首领手指在颤抖，不断地敲打着桌面。她眨了几下眼——对于一个没有瞳孔的人来说，这个动作显得格外奇怪——然后深吸一口气，稳住了身体，直接面对着你。 你是怎么得到这个的？ 你没有理由隐瞒，于是把一切都告诉了她。你在鹰棘镇附近的森林里发现了那座被毁的神社，穿过那些镶嵌着宝石的门，进入了后面的洞穴，看到了那面壁画，以及那件被层层灰尘和杂物掩盖起来的护身符。基约科还会出现在你的梦中，向你讲述她被囚禁的遭遇。 [kiyoko.numKits 1|她吸取你的生命能量，最终还为你生下了孩子。[kiyoko.numKits 2|ren]。 ]那些仿佛是梦境般的回忆，其实大多确实就是梦境——然而这些梦境却是真实的，甚至可能比现实更加真实。这些话语不请自来，直接从你脑海的深处浮现出来，然后毫无迟疑地从你口中流淌而出。 在她聆听着的故事中，麻里不停地摆弄着那个简单的护身符，用指尖轻轻触摸着那颗表面虽然老旧却依然光亮的球体。这位巢穴的女首领偶尔也会陷入忧郁之中，但这一次的情况却截然不同；当你终于听完这个故事时，才会发现茶已经凉透了。真的已经过去这么久了吗？ 麻里轻咳了一声，然后将那枚护身符在手中翻来覆去地查看。嗯，你已经说得很清楚了……现在该由我来解释一下你的情况了。这个护身符曾经是我的；它是我家族的传家宝。甚至我的名字……在你们的语言中，它的意思就是‘小球’。 [pc.name]；我想我的父母觉得这很有趣。一件家族传家宝……大约在两百五十年前，就在我奉神之命来到这个地区协助进行这场神战之后不久，我失去了它…… 我记得那天，我和那些女妖们一起外出去了……索拉创造的生物们当年还算比较‘文明’，但它们依然是一些难以忍受、性格古怪的生物。当我们回来时，发现它们的巢穴已经被彻底毁坏了——那些幽灵的爪牙在我们外出期间发动了攻击。无论我怎么努力，都无法找到那枚转移护身符了，那可是我们主人实现梦想的关键之一啊。 一个梦想……？ 你们更清楚，因为这些领域被称为‘星界’。那些‘生神’们各自拥有自己的梦想，那些由他们的意志形成的领域……嗯，就连我本人也不太确定具体细节。但我们确实知道，他们在自己的领域里拥有至高无上的权力；那些地方就是他们存在意义最为集中的地方。真实的因为实在没有更好的词语来形容它。 [flags.ARCHWAY_BOTH_SAVED |你深知这是事实——毕竟，娜瑞瓦本人就是这么向你解释的，不过她的解释和其他那位蛇女神说过的话一样，同样令人费解。 |有意思…… ] 那么，清子一定是逃进了那个球体里，而那个球体在废墟中埋藏了几个世纪，直到你的出现。 随着家族传家宝的丢失，我再也无法面对我的亲人。作为大友夫人的随从，因为我的疏忽而导致她死去，这意味着我活该死。这种耻辱实在太大了……但是我的主人另有打算。他说，让我的才能就这样白白浪费掉，实在太可惜了。…我将会和那些愿意与我并肩作战的人一起被流放到这里，在这些异国他乡为他的势力坚守阵地。按常理来说，我应该用生命来偿还自己的过错，但我的主宽宏大量，给了我第二次机会。或许这种流放才是懦弱的选择，但如今，我想我宁愿选择死亡。被变成妖怪，被迫眼睁睁看着自己的后代一代又一代地衰老、枯萎、死去，而自己却始终不变……每次举行葬礼仪式时，我都会越来越渴望能够与大地融为一体。" 清子和她在一起吗？ 我和清子虽然在我们各自的家族中担任着相似的职位，但因为她出身于十二大家族，而我并非其中之一，这意味着至多我也就只配担任她的随从罢了。麻里的脸上浮现出一丝微笑，她的耳朵也向前耷了下来。告诉我，你对大友夫人的过去了解多少？ 嗯……仔细想想……纪代子其实从未跟你详细讲过她自己的生活经历。并不是说她故意回避这个话题，只是日常对话中从来没涉及到这个内容。你知道她接受的是带有宗教色彩的教育，也了解她的一些成长背景，但关于她在狐族社会中的地位，却从来没有人问过，主要是因为周围根本没有其他狐族成员。 你根本不知道她是谁，才刚认识她而已，却还是答应了那个令人不安、甚至可以说是极其困扰的请求，而且还不要求任何回报。啊，这种乐于助人的精神……这个世界上那些心怀不轨的人肯定会迫不及待地利用这一点。 有什么问题吗？ 麻里思考了一会儿，然后摇了摇头。没关系。如果你们俩这样在一起也能开心，那也是好事。反正这也没什么大不了的，离老家也不远。基约子曾经——我是说，她现在也是我的领主与朋友，经历了这么多年的时光，如果她找到了幸福，我只能为她感到由衷的高兴。 …有没有办法让清子离开那个星界呢？你当初给她看这些东西，不就是为了这个目的吗？ 很有可能，不过这超出了我的能力范围。我必须请我的神明主宰出面干预……为此，我们得下到下面去。路上让我拿着这个，你没意见吧？ 不，你当然不会介意。如果你会介意的话，一开始就不会把这件事托付给她了。 感激、认可，或许还有恐惧与懊悔——你从未见过一个人仅仅通过轻轻低头就能表达出如此多的情感，但狐族确实擅长用最微小的动作来传达丰富的意思。一手拿着护身符，另一手拄着拐杖，麻里缓缓走出了自己的房间，朝着那棵树的根部走去。[party.hasCompanions | 你回头瞥了一眼，然后离开了。 [party.compNames]在匆忙追赶她之前，先去喝点茶、吃点点心吧。 ] ]
