"With the family heirloom lost, I could not face my relatives. As the Lady Otomo's retainer, allowing her to die from my negligence meant I deserved death. The shame was too great... but my divine lord had other ideas. It would be a waste, he said, for my talents to be lost in such a manner... I would be exiled here with those who would stay alongside me, and keep a foothold for his influence in these foreign lands. By all rights I should have paid for my mistake with my life, but my Lord has seen fit to be magnanimous and give me a second chance. Perhaps this exile was the cowardly option, but today, I think I would have preferred death. Turning me into a yasha and forcing me to watch generations of my descendants age, wither and die while I remain unchanging... each time I perform the funerary rites, I desire more and more to simply be one with the land." Kiyoko was with her? "Kiyoko and I, although our positions in our clans were similar, the fact that she came from the twelve families and I did not meant that I was merely fit to be her retainer at best." A small smile appears on Komari's face as her ears fold forward. "Tell me, what do you know of Lady Otomo's past?" Well... come to think of it... Kiyoko's never told you that much about her life story. Not that she's ever been evasive or anything, but it just never really came up in daily conversation. You know she had a somewhat religious upbringing and something of her education, but the question of her standing in kitsune society never came up, mostly because there weren't any other kitsune around. "You didn't know who she was, had only just met her, and even so, acceded to an unsettling, if not downright disturbing request, wanting no compensation. Ah, such willingness to help... the wicked of this world would be so eager to take advantage of that." Is there a problem? Komari thinks a moment, then shakes her head. "Never mind. If the two of you are content together like this, it's for the better. It's not as if it means anything, not this far from the Old Country. Kiyoko was — I mean, is my liege and friend, and after all these years, I can only wish the best for her if she's found happiness." ... Is there a way to get Kiyoko out of the astral plane? That's why you showed her this to begin with. "Very likely, although it's something I'm not able to do under my own power. I'll have to ask my divine lord to intercede... and for that, we need to head down below. Do you mind if I hold this on the way?" No, of course you don't mind. If you did, you wouldn't have entrusted this to her in the first place. Gratitude, acknowledgement, perhaps fear and regret — you've never seen so much conveyed in a little dip of one's head, but the kitsune are masters of saying much with the smallest of gestures. Amulet in one hand and cane in the next, Komari shuffles out of her chambers and down towards the roots of the tree.[party.hasCompanions | You throw a glance back, leaving [party.compNames] to the tea and refreshments before hurrying after her. ] ] "

rows.original: Out into the courtyard, down the stairwell and through the fields Komari strides, you hurrying in her wake[party.hasCompanions | and leaving [party.compNames] behind in her chambers. Like it or not, you get the feeling that whatever happens next is going to be for your eyes only ]. As short as she is, there's no mistaking the den matron's imperious and resolute manner, and lesser foxes slip away from her path as she makes her way towards the kitsune shrine. As luck would have it, both Miko and Mai are on duty at the moment, and while they greet their great-great-grandmother with mischievous smiles the sisters' playful demeanour evaporates the moment their ancestor raps the ground with her cane. "Make preparations. I must commune with his lordship this moment. I... I will not put it off any longer." "Ain't no problem, granny. I'll jus' send th' remainin' petitioners away all quick-like." "You do that, girl. Miyuki! Don't just stand there!" Perhaps shocked into action by her great-great-grandmother's brusque manner, Miyuki bows and hurries off. Komari guides you to a small water tank, where she gets a ladle and washes her hands and rinses her mouth, then guides you through the same. [pc.ra kitsune |While you shouldn't feel awkward while going through the ritual purification, what with being Keros' champion and all, Komari still makes you feel like a child with the way she's going about it. |You're not entirely sure you're supposed to go through with what looks like a purification ritual, what with not being a foxen and all, but if Komari's telling you to do it then it's probably fine, right? ] By the time she's gotten out the salt — a small bag tied so tightly as to be airtight — and sprinkled a pinch over your shoulders, Miko and Mai have returned, falling to either side of Komari as she strides into the small shrine. The day's offerings are still on the altar before the statue of the Trickster, and the two sisters part to either side of it as their great-great-grandmother steps forward, puts her hands together and starts speaking in her mother tongue. She hasn't even gotten halfway through the first sentence before Keros apparates in the shrine, cutting her prayer off. The speed at which it happens is shocking — there's no fading in, no transmutation of stone to flesh. One moment the likeness of the Living God is in the recess, a cold statue, the next he's rolling his limbs and stepping down by the altar's side, giving Miko's ass a hefty swat with one hand while the other picks up a huge, juicy peach from the altar. "Don't stand on ceremony, Komari." Many-colored robes sweep dramatically across the plinth in its recess as Keros steps off and eyes the den matron. He tosses the peach into the air, swats it with one of his nine tails, and it arcs through the air to land perfectly in Mai's hands. "I came as soon as you requested my presence. Can't have my favorite servant all huffy and out of sorts, can I?" He's saying the words — and your mind swears that he did, but your ears swear with equal vehemence that nothing of the sort passed them. [flags.KEROS_MET |The Trickster turns to you and gives you a friendly nod. "And if it isn't [pc.name], too! Well, what a pleasant surprise! I take it the both of you are in together on some kind of mischief? Now then, what's the matter?" |The colors on his clothing, they continuously shift and swirl against a backdrop of white, not moving when you're looking at them but very clearly having changed when you turn your gaze away and back again. His eyes dart from Komari to you, and then the Trickster's smile widens. "Ah! Komari, you didn't say we were having such fine company over today — no doubt your partner in mischief, I take it? Welcome, [pc.name] — I take it my servant has treated you well?" There were some misunderstandings when you first met, but — hey, did you ever tell him your name at any point? You're [pc.bg acolyte|a bit rusty on your theology since you left your acolyte past|not in any position to know], but is he supposed to be omniscient? "Might be. Who knows? Thing is, though, that people are talking about you, [pc.name]. It's not just demons who want your soul, and we're all willing to negotiate instead of just grabbing it like all sorts of horrible monsters would do. But... that's another matter for another time; just know that you're quite popular in several circles, that's all. Isn't it better that we're already on speaking terms? Saves having to do all the introductions and things, frightfully boring at times. [flags.ARCHWAY_BOTH_SAVED |In the blink of an eye, Keros is by your side, leaning in to whisper conspiratorially into your ear. "Oh, and by the by... you do know our little secret. While I do like how you managed to talk circles around poor Nareva... I'd urge you to keep that knowledge to yourself. Not that anyone would ever believe you to begin with, but it could prove problematic for you if you went around spreading that kind of thing. "I'm not threatening you, but simply making a statement of fact; there are forces out there, not necessarily affiliated with us, that would not take kindly to that sort of knowledge being public. We don't need more silly fools mistakenly reaching for apotheosis through mass murder. ] "Now then, what's the matter?" ] Wordlessly, Komari holds out the amulet to her patron deity, who whistles appreciatively before taking it from her. He toys with it for a bit, running the metal through his fingers while murmuring to himself, all the while casting glances at both you and Komari. Maybe it's a trick of the light in the shrine, but the patchwork colors on his robes swirl faster, as if a rainbow in a mist freshly stirred up by the wind. "Ah-ha. So that's how it is. [pc.name] has done us quite the service indeed, [pc.ra kitsune|not that I would expect anything less from my handpicked champion|and we're quite indebted to [pc.himHer] for [pc.hisHer] efforts]." Komari bows her head, but says nothing. "You do understand that while these efforts are admirable and demonstrate your contrition, it will not shorten the duration of your penance. Perhaps you shouldn't have been so hasty in assuming your liege was dead like everyone else... even if she was, after a fashion. But such words are meaningless now." More silence. Time for you to put this heavy mood to an end. So... if he knows what's going on, can he get Kiyoko out? You've gone all the way to the top, and surely the puck has to stop here, right? "Hmm..." Yes?
rows.translation: 走出庭院，沿着楼梯向下，穿过田野，麻里大步前行，而你则急忙跟在她身后。[party.hasCompanions | 然后离开[party.compNames]在她的内室里。不管你愿不愿意，你都会觉得，接下来发生的一切都将只有你一个人看到。 ]尽管她个子不高，但那种威严而坚定的气质却让人一眼就能认出来。当她朝着狐神祠走去时，那些地位较低的狐妖都会自动避开她的道路。幸运的是，此时米可与舞都在值班。当她们用调皮的笑容迎接这位曾祖母时，可一旦这位祖先用她的手杖敲击地面，姐妹俩那嬉戏的态度立刻就消失了。 做好准备，我现在就必须去与他大人会面。我……不能再拖延了。 没问题的，奶奶。我马上就把剩下的请愿者们都打发走。 加油啊，女孩。美雪！别只是站在那里不动！ 或许是被她的高祖母那直率的态度吓了一跳，美雪立刻鞠了个躬，匆匆离开了。麻里带你来到一个小型水槽前，她拿了一把勺子，先洗了手部，又漱了口，然后也让你照做了同样的事情。 [pc.ra kitsune |虽然在进行这种仪式性的净化过程时，你不应该感到尴尬，毕竟你是凯罗斯的冠军嘛，但麻里执行这个仪式的方式，还是让你觉得自己像个小孩子一样。 |你其实不太确定自己是否真的应该进行这个看起来像净化仪式的动作，毕竟你又不是狐狸啊，但既然麻里让你这么做，那应该没什么问题吧？ ]等她取出那小袋盐——那袋盐被扎得严严实实，完全不透空气——然后往你的肩膀上撒了一点点，米可和舞也已经回来了，她们站在麻里的两侧，而麻里则大步走进了那座小神社。当天的祭品仍然摆在戏弄者雕像前的祭坛上，两位姐妹分别站在雕像的两侧，这时她们的曾曾祖母走上前，双手合十，开始用她的母语说话。她甚至还没读完第一句话，凯罗斯就已经出现在神龛里，打断了她的祈祷。 这一幕发生的速度快得令人震惊——没有任何渐显的过程，也没有石头变成肉体的变化。前一刻，这位活生生的神明还静立在角落里，如同一座冰冷的雕像；下一刻，他便活动起四肢，走到祭坛旁，一只手狠狠地拍了一下米可的屁股，另一只手则从祭坛上摘下一个又大又多汁的桃子。 别客气了，麻里。当凯罗斯走下来，注视着那个巢穴的女首领时，五颜六色的长袍在基座上划出一道引人注目的轨迹。他将那个桃子抛向空中，用自己九条尾巴中的一条将其接住，桃子划过空中，精准地落在了舞的手中。你一要求我过来，我就立刻赶来了。我可不能让我最喜欢的仆人整天闷闷不乐、心情糟糕，对吧？ 他说着那些话——而你的内心却坚信，他确实但是你的耳朵却坚决地声称，根本没有听到过这样的声音。 [flags.KEROS_MET |那个诡计之神朝你点了点头，露出友好的表情。要是不是这样的话[pc.name]，也是啊！真是太惊喜了！我看你们俩一定是合起伙来搞什么鬼把戏吧？那么，到底发生了什么事呢？ |他衣服上的颜色在白色背景的映衬下不断变幻、旋转——当你注视它们时，这些颜色似乎静止不动，但当你移开视线再重新看回去时，就会发现它们确实发生了变化。他的目光在麻里和你之间来回扫视，然后诡计之神般的角色露出了更加灿烂的笑容。 啊！麻里，你之前可没说今天会有这么有趣的客人来——想必是你的同伙吧？欢迎大家到来！ [pc.name]那么，我的仆人应该没有亏待你吧？ 你们初次见面时确实存在一些误会，但是——嘿，你有没有告诉过他你的名字呢？你[pc.bg acolyte|自从你离开了你的追随者之后，你的神学知识似乎有些生疏了啊……|根本无从知晓]但他真的应该具备全知的能力吗？ 也许吧。谁知道呢？不过，现在大家都在谈论你[pc.name]想要得到你的灵魂的并不只是恶魔，我们所有人都愿意通过谈判来解决问题，而不是像那些可怕的怪物那样强行夺取它。不过……这个话题留到以后再谈吧；总之，你可以知道，在很多圈子里你都相当受欢迎，仅此而已。既然我们已经能够坦诚地交流了，这不是更好吗？这样就省去了各种繁琐的介绍环节，那些过程有时候真的很无聊。 [flags.ARCHWAY_BOTH_SAVED |转瞬间，凯洛斯就出现在你身边，凑近你的耳朵，神秘兮兮地低语起来。哦，顺便说一下……你应该知道我们的小秘密吧。虽然我挺欣赏你如何把娜瑞瓦弄得晕头转向的，但我还是建议你把这件事保密。反正也没人会相信你，但如果你把这种事情传出去，反而会给你带来麻烦的。 我并不是在威胁你，只是陈述一个事实：外面确实有一些势力，它们不一定与我们有关联，它们不会乐意看到这类信息被公之于众。我们可不需要再有那些愚蠢之徒通过大规模杀戮来妄图达到所谓的‘英雄’地位。 ] 那么，到底发生了什么事？ ] 麻里一言不发地将护身符递给了她的守护神。守护神满意地吹了声口哨，然后接过了它。他仔细地摆弄着这个护身符，用手指轻轻抚过它的金属表面，同时自言自语地低语着，目光不时在你和麻里身上扫过。也许是因为神殿里的光线效果，他长袍上那些拼接而成的颜色似乎旋转得更快了，就像是被风吹动后重新焕发生机的彩虹一般。 啊哈，原来如此。 [pc.name]确实帮了我们大忙。 [pc.ra kitsune|倒也不是说，我对自己精心挑选的这位英雄会有什么不高的期望|我们确实非常感激他们。 [pc.himHer]为了[pc.hisHer]各项努力]。" 麻里低下了头，但什么也没说。 你应该明白，尽管这些努力令人钦佩，也体现了你的悔意，但它们并不会缩短你所需的赎罪时间。或许你当初不该如此草率地认为你的主君已经像其他人一样去世了……尽管从某种意义上来说，她确实已经去世了。不过，现在说这些也已经毫无意义了。 更多的沉默…… 是时候结束这种重型的氛围了。那么……如果他知道发生了什么，他能把清子救出来吗？你已经走到了最后一步，想必现在该是取得胜利的时候了拥有就到这里吧，对吧？ 嗯…… 嗯？

rows.original: "She did make a request of you, did she not?" That... she did. Kiyoko asked you for a dose of your bodily energy, as she put it, said it was a way forward to freeing her. But for your own reasons, you'd rather not do the deed personally, and would prefer to pass on this duty to someone else. To that extent, you'd rather return the amulet to him and let him sort it out himself, get [pc.isDK |some other schmuck |someone else ] to do the deed. He doesn't have a problem with that, does he? "I... well..." The Trickster sighs. "After hearing of the details from Komari, I was hoping that you'd be willing; you are quite the unique [pc.mf |man |woman ], after all. Nevertheless, if you came all the way here, then you've had ample time to change your mind should you want to, and I can respect your reasons. Thank you, then, for returning my descendant to me." You hand over the amulet, and Keros tucks it away in his robes. With your job done, that's the last you'll ever see of it. "Now then, a suitable reward... I think I have just the thing." Just as quickly as Keros made the amulet disappear, he turns his palm, and a rod-shaped device appears in his hand. The deity passes it on to you with a smile, and even at this distance you can feel the magic emanating from it. "There've been some troubles lately, and my people came across this in the conflict. Strange artifice, indeed — Nareva would love to get her hands on it, but I think its story isn't over just yet, and it would most definitely be a done deal if it's rotting away in one of her vaults. While the rod's useless for its intended purpose, it's still quite the potent catalyst. I'd like to see what kind of future you can give it — there's the promise of a good yarn to be spun." Received the control rod. [pc.isDK |Feels like a bad trade, but hey, knowing stories about the gods and this one in particular, you're glad to have gotten something out of the deal. |At least there aren't going to be any unexpected consequences to this particular trinket. Probably. Hopefully. ] "Please forgive me, but you've just made me a very busy god. Once again, your efforts are appreciated, [pc.name]. Do petition me again when the both of us aren't pressed for time." After giving you a bow, the deity clambers up onto the plinth again, and just like that, the figure's stone once more, although in quite the different pose than he was in previously. You can feel the tension in the air drain as Miko and Mai share glances with each other, then at their great-great-grandmother. "Well," she says, heaving a sigh and shaking out her golden fur, "that didn't quite go the way I'd expected it to. I'll... I'll leave you to your thoughts now; I know I need to be alone with mine. Mikoto, Miyuki, please attend to me." The sisters dip their heads, then fall in by Komari's side as the den matron departs, leaving you alone in the shrine. A sense of closure hangs heavy in the air... but the deed's done, the exchange's made, and there's no point in second-guessing your decisions.
rows.translation: 她确实向你提出了请求，对吧？” 嗯……是的。如清子所说，她向你请求借用一部分你的能量，称这是帮助她解脱的唯一方法。但出于你自己的原因，你并不愿意亲自去做这件事，而是想把这个责任推给别人。因此，你宁愿把那个护身符还给他，让他自己来处理这件事。 [pc.isDK |某个别的混蛋 |其他人 ]就是做那件事吧。他应该没有意见吧？ “我……嗯……”那个调皮鬼叹了口气，“在听完小毬告诉我的那些细节之后，我其实希望你会愿意的；你是确实独一无二[pc.mf |男人 |女性 ]毕竟，也是这样。不过，如果你大老远地来到这里，那么你肯定有足够的时间改变主意，如果你们真的想改变主意的话，我完全可以理解你们的理由。那么，感谢你们把我的后代还给了我。 你将护身符交给了他，而凯罗斯则将其收进了自己的长袍里。一旦你完成了任务，那就再也不会见到它了。 “那么，现在该给予适当的奖励了……我想我正好有适合的东西。” 就在凯罗斯让那个护身符消失的瞬间，他转动手掌，一只棒状的装置便出现在他的手中。这位神明微笑着将它交给了你，即使隔着这样的距离，你也能感受到从中散发出的魔力。 “最近发生了一些麻烦，我的族人在冲突中发现了这个东西。确实是一件奇怪的工艺品——娜瑞瓦肯定很想要得到它，但我认为它的故事还没有结束。如果它只是被丢在她的某个仓库里慢慢腐烂，那可就太可惜了。虽然这根棒子无法实现其最初的设计用途，但它仍然是一种相当强大的催化剂。我很想看看你能用它创造出什么未来——它肯定能被用来编织出一些非常出色的东西来。 收到了控制棒。 [pc.isDK |这似乎是一笔不划算的交易，但嘿，了解了关于这些神明的故事，尤其是这个故事之后，你就会觉得自己得到了什么值得的东西。某个东西没门儿。 |至少，这个小玩意儿不会带来任何意外的后果。大概吧。希望如此。 ] 请原谅我，但你刚刚让我变成了一位非常忙碌的神明。再次感谢你的付出。 [pc.name]等我们俩都没有时间忙别的时候，再来向我祈求吧。” 鞠了一躬之后，这位神明又爬回了基座上，就这样，那个石像又恢复了原来的形态——只不过现在的姿势与之前完全不同了。当米可与舞相互对视，然后又将目光转向她们的曾曾祖母时，空气中紧张的气氛似乎渐渐消散了。 “唉，”她叹了口气，摇动着金色的毛发说道，“事情的发展并没有像我预想的那样。我……现在就让你独自思考吧；我知道我也需要独自静下心来。美琴、美雪，请陪在我身边。” 姐妹俩低下了头，随后跟在麻里的身后离开了，只留下你独自一人在神社里。一种圆满的感觉弥漫在空气中……但事情已经完成，交易也已经达成，再事后反思自己的决定也没有任何意义了。
rows.raw: " "She did make a request of you, did she not?" That... she did. Kiyoko asked you for a dose of your bodily energy, as she put it, said it was a way forward to freeing her. But for your own reasons, you'd rather not do the deed personally, and would prefer to pass on this duty to someone else. To that extent, you'd rather return the amulet to him and let him sort it out himself, get [pc.isDK |some other schmuck |someone else ] to do the deed. He doesn't have a problem with that, does he? "I... well..." The Trickster sighs. "After hearing of the details from Komari, I was hoping that you'd be willing; you are quite the unique [pc.mf |man |woman ], after all. Nevertheless, if you came all the way here, then you've had ample time to change your mind should you want to, and I can respect your reasons. Thank you, then, for returning my descendant to me." You hand over the amulet, and Keros tucks it away in his robes. With your job done, that's the last you'll ever see of it. "Now then, a suitable reward... I think I have just the thing." Just as quickly as Keros made the amulet disappear, he turns his palm, and a rod-shaped device appears in his hand. The deity passes it on to you with a smile, and even at this distance you can feel the magic emanating from it. "There've been some troubles lately, and my people came across this in the conflict. Strange artifice, indeed — Nareva would love to get her hands on it, but I think its story isn't over just yet, and it would most definitely be a done deal if it's rotting away in one of her vaults. While the rod's useless for its intended purpose, it's still quite the potent catalyst. I'd like to see what kind of future you can give it — there's the promise of a good yarn to be spun." Received the control rod. [pc.isDK |Feels like a bad trade, but hey, knowing stories about the gods and this one in particular, you're glad to have gotten something out of the deal. |At least there aren't going to be any unexpected consequences to this particular trinket. Probably. Hopefully. ] "Please forgive me, but you've just made me a very busy god. Once again, your efforts are appreciated, [pc.name]. Do petition me again when the both of us aren't pressed for time." After giving you a bow, the deity clambers up onto the plinth again, and just like that, the figure's stone once more, although in quite the different pose than he was in previously. You can feel the tension in the air drain as Miko and Mai share glances with each other, then at their great-great-grandmother. "Well," she says, heaving a sigh and shaking out her golden fur, "that didn't quite go the way I'd expected it to. I'll... I'll leave you to your thoughts now; I know I need to be alone with mine. Mikoto, Miyuki, please attend to me." The sisters dip their heads, then fall in by Komari's side as the den matron departs, leaving you alone in the shrine. A sense of closure hangs heavy in the air... but the deed's done, the exchange's made, and there's no point in second-guessing your decisions. "

rows.original: You... you've done as Keros asked. There've been several consequences to this, but... ah, you've done it. There shouldn't be any problem now, should there? "Hopefully not, although I'm not going to speak for his divine lordship; even I can only guess at his means and ends. But let's go down and see, shall we?" [party.hasCompanions |Leaving [party.compNames] behind with the tea and snacks, you hurry after Komari as she rises and sweeps her way out of her chambers |With that, Komari rises and sweeps her way out of her chambers, leaving you to hurry after her. ]. There's something of that same heaviness that surrounds Komari on her way back down to the shrine, although it's more muted now and a lot more resignation than anything. As luck would have it, both Miko and Mai are in attendance at the shrine again today, and they sweep aside to let their great-great-grandmother enter. Inside, Keros is already apparated and picking at the day's offerings, a lazy smile upon the kitsune god's face as he sweeps around to face you, robes and tails billowing dramatically in the motion. "Marvelous work your people are doing, Komari. Every generation's producing better and better harvests; everything here's worthy of my name as a god of agriculture. Don't look so surprised, I had a feeling you'd be looking for me today and decided to meet you halfway. That's something none of the other Seven will ever do for their own, heh." "My lord, the amulet —" "Like I said, I had a feeling you two would be showing up today. Great work, really magnanimous, couldn't be prouder of [pc.ra kitsune|my handpicked champion|you, [pc.name]]. Now, you have the lovely little trinket?" Of course. You palm the amulet with its inlaid orb, and hand it to Keros. The vulpine deity turns it over in his hands, then raises it to his nose and sniffs it in a fashion that strikes you as distinctly animalistic.
rows.translation: 你……你按照凯洛斯的要求做了。这样做带来了一些后果，但是……啊，你总算是完成了任务。现在应该不会再有什么问题了吧？ 但愿不会吧，虽然我也没资格代表他的神圣陛下发言；就连我，也只能够猜测他的目的和手段罢了。不过，我们还是下去看看吧，怎么样？ [party.hasCompanions |离开[party.compNames]茶水和小吃都准备好了，你赶紧去追麻里吧，她刚刚起身，正准备离开她的房间呢。 |说完，麻里站起身来，大步走出了她的房间，留下你急忙跟在她的后面。 ]当麻里重新回到神社时，她身上依然笼罩着那种沉重的气息，只不过现在这种感觉已经减弱了许多，更多的是一种无奈与接受。幸运的是，今天米子和小舞都在神社里，她们立刻让开道路，让这位曾祖母能够进入神社。里面，凯罗斯已经出现了，他正悠闲地翻看着今天的食物。这位狐面神明脸上带着懒散的微笑，转身面向你，他的长袍和尾巴在动作中剧烈地摆动着。 麻里，你的子民们做得真是太棒了。每一代人都能够获得越来越好的收成；这里的一切都配得上我作为农业之神的称号。别这么惊讶，我就知道你今天会来找我，所以决定主动见面。其他六位神明可从来不会为自己的子民这么做，呵呵。 大人，这个护身符—— 正如我所说，我就觉得你们俩今天会来。干得真棒，真是太慷慨了，我真是为你们感到无比骄傲。 [pc.ra kitsune|我精心挑选的英雄|你， [pc.name]]现在，你得到了这个可爱的小饰品了？ 当然可以。你将那枚镶嵌着圆球的护身符拿在手中，然后递给凯罗斯。这位狐妖神明将护身符在手中翻来覆去，接着把它举到鼻子前闻了闻，那种闻的方式显得非常具有动物特性。

rows.original: "Yes, everything's in order," Keros says after a moment's further study of the orb. "I'll have to fashion her a brand-new physical form, but thanks to your [kiyoko.numKits 16|rather copious donations|help], that shouldn't be a problem any more. I'll have to take this back for fixing afterwards, but the most important part of all this will still be with you, won't it?" You would have said something to that, but are cut short by the god himself leaning in and giving you a friendly nudge in the ribs with an elbow, followed by a wink. "All right, then. Let's begin." A hushed silence falls over the shrine's interior, and you feel the air begin to saturate with power, enough to make your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] crawl and tingle with — no, this is not fear, but more like a coiled spring waiting to be unleashed, a sense of childish excitement, perhaps. You cast a glance at Komari, but the den matron looks completely nonplussed about the situation — either she's put on a mask of stone, or familiarity truly breeds contempt. Keros' red, slitted eyes begin to gleam with a faint golden light, the selfsame light that slowly coleasces about the amulet's orb. Frowning in concentration, the vulpine deity makes a quick motion with his hand and hangs the amulet upon empty air, suspended by its chain with nothing to hold it up. Nevertheless, it remains aloft, and the golden light grows stronger and stronger by the moment, gathering and intensifying; peering in from the sidelines, Miko and Mai look as if they're ready to take cover should anything go awry. But it doesn't. Slowly, the light grows and intensifies, shaping itself into the figure of a woman that's very distinctly familiar. Energy pours outwards from the orb in a thin stream, feeding the light, and then when it slowly fades the perfect, demure form of Kiyoko stands before you, her entrance wreathed in a small shower of golden-amber sparkles. She opens her eyes, those lovely jade-green eyes, shuffles on her feet, clearly unused to this new sense of balance, and cries out as she falls forward. You step up and grab your fox-wife before she can land on her [kiyoko.pregStage 2|pregnant belly|face], and she sinks gratefully into your arms and [pc.chest]. "You did it, [pc.name]. You did it. I waited and hoped, dared to believe... and you did it!" Keros isn't done, though. As you watch, the thin thread of golden light widens and spins faster, and another figure emerges, one that you feel that you ought to know but can't quite place your finger on: she's wearing [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |a full-length kimono that goes all the way down to her ankles and with equally long sleeves, white and deep blue alike with a sash of purple about her midriff, and a soft leaf-print pattern in the same color. Part of her hair's been done in a lovely if homely braid, while the rest hangs free all the way down her hips which push outward against the skirts of her clothing, only divested in two by her five luxuriant tails. There's even a cute, if unkempt fringe that falls forward from under the headscarf she's wearing, and the collar of her kimono is laced with rich, luxuriant fur. |a dress much in Kiyoko's style, but much, much shorter, provocatively so yet not enough to be outright lewd; improper in certain settings, perhaps, but not outright scandalous. What lack of material there is in her skirts and top is made up for in the long folds of her silken sleeves, exquisitely dyed and bearing a leaf-print pattern; the sash about her waist is threaded with gold and fine patterning. Her hair, long and exquisite, falls all the way past her butt, where her five lovely tails part it in two, and her figure strains against her clothing even though she moves barefoot with ease. ]. But the silvery-white hair, blue eyes with their white pupils... not to mention her colors of blue, white and purple... but the bell anklet about her foot, not to mention its twin in the form of a choker about her neck, is a dead giveaway. Oh. Oh. "[kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Hey, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]," Kinu says, looking a little sheepish as she scrambles off her knees and to her feet, pushing the hair out of her eyes. "It's been a while... |It has been some time since we last met, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Perfectly poised, Kinu clasps her hands in front of her and gives you a small bow. "Thank you for doing this for Mother. It means so much to her. ]" She... she was a child when you last saw her, and — you have to admit, the change is sudden and drastic... what happened to your little, precocious daughter? "She grew up, of course," Kiyoko says as she leans into you, pushing her warmth into yours. Her [kiyoko.numKits 8 32|ripe|motherly|pert] breasts push against your [pc.chest] as your fox-wife nuzzles your shoulder[kiyoko.pregStage 2|, making the fecund firmness of her baby bump all the more prominent]. "You didn't think that she would remain a child forever, did you, beloved? I did my best in raising her, [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |even if... well... nevermind. This is supposed to be a happy occasion. |and I think... well, the results speak for themselves, don't they? ]" Ah. It's just... all very sudden. You look Kinu up and down again, young woman that she's grown into, then sigh and lean into your fox-wife's embrace. Life is good. [kiyoko.numKits 2 |Keros isn't done, though. The vulpine deity spins out another thread, and another, and another, until the remainder of Kinu's siblings come tumbling out into reality. [kiyoko.numKits 2 3 8 16 32 |Now you've got two teenaged foxes on your hands instead of one... satisfied with a job well done, Keros dusts his hands off while Kinu hurries over to pick up her sibling from the shrine's floor. "Well, that looks like everyone. Quite the happy family you've got here, the two of you — which brings us to our next point." |One by one, a bunch of two and three-tailed kitsune come tumbling out of the orb, falling into open air and onto the shrine's floor. Some are teenaged, a little younger than Kinu is, the others still kits, even if older. The soft flumph of fur on tatami sounds repeatedly, followed by whimpering and whiffs of breath until the god's done extricating your entire fox-family. Satisfied with a job well done, Keros dusts his hands off while Kinu hurries over to help up her siblings from the shrine's floor. "Well then, that's your entire family. Quite the fine bunch of kits the two of you've managed to make while at it, I'd say." Grinning, Keros claps his hands once, twice, thrice. "Happy, healthy, and eager to be upstanding members of society." |It happens slowly at first, brothers and sisters emerging one by one, then picks up speed as the light intensifies. Before long, two and three-tailed kitsune kits are pouring out into the shrine, filling the space in front of the altar and forcing everyone to take a step back. Kinu rushes over to help up her siblings and get them in order, but the squirming mess of ears and tails still takes a little time to get sorted out. There're a handful who are teenagers almost Kinu's age, but most are either at that awkward age, or still children. "Well then, that's your entire family. Quite the fine bunch of kits the two of you've managed to make while at it, I'd say." Grinning, Keros claps his hands once, twice, thrice. "Happy, healthy, and eager to be upstanding members of society." |Knowing full well what's coming, you swallow hard as one kit emerges, then another, then another until the entire space in front of the shrine is filled with fluff and tails, and even then they're still coming. Kinu hurries over to help up her siblings and get them away from the pile, but the sheer number of two and three-tailed kitsune kits is startling now that they're all gathered in so small a space. Were... were you really that busy with Kiyoko, for so many children to have grown in her womb? Komari's usually placid expression is thin-lipped, a mixture of bemusement and shock. "Oh my. Oh my. Quite impressive." While a handful or two of Kinu's siblings are teenagers like she is, only slightly younger, most of the kits are either children or at that awkward age — not quite kits, but neither young men and women like Kinu. As she parts the sea of fluff and gets everyone out of the dogpile, your eldest fox-daughter quickly establishes a roll call and makes sure no one's missing. You don't know how hard it is to surprise a god, but Keros himself looks damn well incredulous at the sheer number of progeny you and Kiyoko have managed to produce. While Kinu gets everything in order as her mother's faithful majordomo, the vulpine deity looks over the scene and shrugs helplessly. "Ah, this takes me way back. Kiyoko Otomo... you really are a woman after your ancestor's heart, aren't you? A big, happy family... quite the fine bunch of kits the two of you've managed to make while dallying with each other, I'd say." Grinning, Keros claps his hands once, twice, thrice. "Hale, healthy, and eager to be upstanding members of society." |You know what's coming. Keros himself... looks like he doesn't. You've never actually seen a god surprised — what does it take to surprise a god, anyway? — but the vulpine deity's lazy, bemused expression turns to one of apprehension, then outright shock as kit after kit emerges into reality. It's slow at first, but as the golden threads whip themselves into a blur more and more of Kinu's siblings land atop each other in a heap in front of the altar. Ever the faithful majordomo to her mother, your eldest daughter hurries forward to help up her brothers and sisters, but they just keep coming and coming — Komari's usually placid expression is thin-lipped, a mixture of bemusement and shock; even the cheerful Miko and stone-faced Mai are a little pale at the sight. "Oh my. Oh my. Quite impressive." The shrine is simply too small to hold so many fox kits within its four walls, so it happens that a stream of fluffy two and three-tailed kitsune emerge into the adjoining gardens through the back door, Kinu marshaling them with practiced ease. Your fox-daughter sets up a roll call even as more and more of your family emerges from the Astral Plane before Keros' disbelieving eyes, and even you're a little overwhelmed by the fact that all those are your children. You look back at Kiyoko. How... how did she manage for what must be years? Sure, it's not as if you didn't know this was happening, but seeing it all at once... Your fox-wife gives you a mysterious smile and leans in to give you a quick peck on the lips. "By the time you've had your thirty-first... the thirty-second really isn't that much more work." But finally, the last of your kitsune children is up and running, leaving Keros to shrug helplessly and give the two of you a weak grin. "Oh, dear. Oh dear indeed. Kiyoko Otomo, you really are trying to outdo my poor, beloved Chizuru, aren't you?" Chizuru? "Chizuru Otomo. Your wife's distant ancestor, and one of my twelve concubines. She was... ah, it's not time to go into that. Let's get you all settled, shall we?" ] ] As the dust finally settles and the golden threads wane, Keros flips the amulet over in his palm and a brilliant shower of golden-amber sparkles erupts into the air, floating down upon the entire shrine before dissolving into nothingness. The colors on the vulpine deity's otherwise white robes swirl in motion as he tucks away the amulet and rubs his hands together in satisfaction. "A most heartwarming sight, indeed. Komari, I'll return you the amulet once I'm done with fixing it up; it might take a little while but it'll be something for me to do when I'm not otherwise occupied with the situation. All of this didn't have to be that dramatic, but I thought it appropriate for the occasion. Would've been a bit anticlimactic if I'd just gone and done it without the bells and whistles, eh?" No response. "Komari? Eh?"
rows.translation: 是的，一切都已经安排妥当了。凯罗斯在进一步研究了那个球体一段时间后说道。我得为她创造一个全新的身体形态，不过多亏了你的帮助[kiyoko.numKits 16|数额相当可观的捐款|帮助]那应该不会再成为问题了。之后我需要把它拿回去修理，但所有这些中最重要的部分仍然会留在你身边，对吧？ 你本来也想说些什么的，但就在这时，那位神明亲自凑了过来，用肘子友好地戳了戳你的肋骨，然后还眨了眨眼。 好吧，那我们开始吧。 神龛内部陷入一片沉寂，你感觉到空气开始充满了力量，这种力量足以[pc.skinFurScalesNoun]全身都充满了紧张与兴奋——不，这并不是恐惧，更像是一根被紧紧绷住的弹簧，随时准备释放出来，或许是一种孩子般的兴奋感吧。你瞥了眼小栗，但那位巢穴的女首领对这一切似乎完全毫无反应——要么她是装作一副无动于衷的样子，要么就是长时间的相处真的让她产生了厌烦之情。 凯罗斯那双红色的、裂开的眼睛开始散发出微弱的金色光芒，这种光芒同样也在那枚护身符的球体上慢慢聚集起来。这位狡黠的神祇皱着眉头，集中精神，迅速挥了挥手，将护身符悬挂在半空中——它的链条使它悬在那里，而没有任何其他东西支撑它。然而，它依然高高悬挂在那里，那金色的光芒每时每刻都在变得愈发强烈，不断聚集、愈发耀眼；站在一旁观看的米可与舞看起来，仿佛随时准备在情况出现变故时躲起来。 You've never actually seen a god surprised — what does it take to surprise a god, anyway? — but the vulpine deity's lazy, bemused expression turns to one of apprehension, then outright shock as kit after kit emerges into reality. It's slow at first, but as the golden threads whip themselves into a blur more and more of Kinu's siblings land atop each other in a heap in front of the altar. Ever the faithful majordomo to her mother, your eldest daughter hurries forward to help up her brothers and sisters, but they just keep coming and coming — Komari's usually placid expression is thin-lipped, a mixture of bemusement and shock; even the cheerful Miko and stone-faced Mai are a little pale at the sight. "Oh my. Oh my. Quite impressive." The shrine is simply too small to hold so many fox kits within its four walls, so it happens that a stream of fluffy two and three-tailed kitsune emerge into the adjoining gardens through the back door, Kinu marshaling them with practiced ease. Your fox-daughter sets up a roll call even as more and more of your family emerges from the Astral Plane before Keros' disbelieving eyes, and even you're a little overwhelmed by the fact that all those are your children. You look back at Kiyoko. How... how did she manage for what must be years? Sure, it's not as if you didn't know this was happening, but seeing it all at once... Your fox-wife gives you a mysterious smile and leans in to give you a quick peck on the lips. "By the time you've had your thirty-first... the thirty-second really isn't that much more work." But finally, the last of your kitsune children is up and running, leaving Keros to shrug helplessly and give the two of you a weak grin. "Oh, dear. Oh dear indeed. Kiyoko Otomo, you really are trying to outdo my poor, beloved Chizuru, aren't you?" Chizuru? "Chizuru Otomo. Your wife's distant ancestor, and one of my twelve concubines. She was... ah, it's not time to go into that. Let's get you all settled, shall we?" ] ] As the dust finally settles and the golden threads wane, Keros flips the amulet over in his palm and a brilliant shower of golden-amber sparkles erupts into the air, floating down upon the entire shrine before dissolving into nothingness. The colors on the vulpine deity's otherwise white robes swirl in motion as he tucks away the amulet and rubs his hands together in satisfaction. "A most heartwarming sight, indeed. Komari, I'll return you the amulet once I'm done with fixing it up; it might take a little while but it'll be something for me to do when I'm not otherwise occupied with the situation. All of this didn't have to be that dramatic, but I thought it appropriate for the occasion. Would've been a bit anticlimactic if I'd just gone and done it without the bells and whistles, eh?" No response. "Komari? Eh?""

rows.original: Now that Kinu[kiyoko.numKits 1 2 3|'s| and her sibling's| and her siblings have] left the shrine, the den matron steps forward to the two of you, her eyes half-lidded. Slowly, she takes off her jewelled headdress and hands it to Miko; this is followed shortly by her cane, which goes to Mai. As the sisters watch wide-eyed, their great-great-grandmother lowers herself to her knees and presses her forehead to the ground at Kiyoko's feet in a full kowtow. "Myobu-sama." Kiyoko detaches herself from your embrace, her smile suddenly gone. "What are you doing, Komari?" Wait. You're sure they're not speaking Belharan, and yet you can understand them perfectly. Looking around, you see the Trickster give you a small wave and knowing wink... oh, right... "No matter how much I've tried to make things right over the centuries, I cannot be forgiven for not being there when you needed me the most. Because of my worthlessness as your retainer, it is my fault that you died and... and..." "Komari, I was the one who sent you out to join the harpies that day. Would you have disobeyed me if it meant saving my life? No, that is a pointless question. It's not your fault. How could you have known what would happen?" Gathering up her skirts, Kiyoko crouches down by her retainer's lowered head. "Please, rise." "The Kurokawa and Otomo clans have been joined as servants and masters for generations. For such incompetence, I should have paid with my life. Because of your death, the Twelve Divine Clans were thrown into politicking and would have gotten out of control had his divine lordship not put down his foot. Myobu-sama, if you do not punish me appropriately then you too will suffer shame. I... I don't want that." "Then let me suffer it. Enough. I won't have any more of this — if you still call me your liege, then I command you to stop this groveling and —" Komari raises her head to look at her liege, and you hear a sharp intake of breath as Kiyoko fights the impulse to scream and recoil. Perhaps for the first time since you first knew her, your fox-wife looks absolutely and completely terrified, her eyes narrowing to slits and face ashen. Slowly, she raises her trembling hands to her cheeks before slowly turning to look at Keros. "My lord... what have you done to my retainer?!" The vulpine deity sticks his arms in his sleeves, his usually jovial face a mask of ice. "I have transformed her into a yasha." "W-why?" "Komari Kurokawa is not allowed to die until she has completed her penance for her failure; part of this penance is completing the task that you were sent over the ocean to begin. It has been two and a half centuries since the end of the Godswar, Kiyoko Otomo. How do you think she is here before you?" Keros is silent for a second or two, then clears his throat. "If she were not so, then you would never have received this apology, and she would never have the chance to make absolution." "I... how long have you been tortured by this, Komari?" Balling her fists, Kiyoko's gaze turns pleading. "I am the one who was wronged. Can I not —" "No. It cannot be helped." "It cannot be helped, but I will do it nonetheless. It may not absolve her, but I will say it anyway. If I had not perished that day, I would not have met [pc.name]. I would not have given birth to my daughter Kinu. I would not have had, even if it was in a gilded cage, the happiest times of my existence with my family." Rising to her full five feet, Kiyoko puts on her imperious air like a coat, her entire demeanour shifting in the blink of an eye, her words crisp, deeply intoned and heavily formal. "Komari Kurokawa, you have said as much and your failure has tormented you deeply enough. So, my good and faithful retainer... I will forgive you." Keros' face is as impassive as ever while he watches Kiyoko reach down and take Komari by the hands, helping her up. The den matron is unsteady and slow to respond, but you know it's not because of any physical frailty on her part. "I do not deserve this, Myobu-sama." "If you want to serve me and make amends, Komari, then I must make a selfish request of you. No doubt you have lived far longer than you ought to as a yasha, but I would have you be my retainer for one more lifetime. Many things have no doubt changed in the world while I was gone, and I imagine that my return will cause no small amount of trouble across the ocean, even if I have his divine lordship's blessing. Will you guide me through this?" "Command me." "Later. For now, I must attend to my daughter and beloved, especially the latter. I imagine [pc.heShe] must feel awkward, listening in on a conversation [pc.heShe] cannot comprehend." With that, Kiyoko turns back to you. "I'm sorry to keep you waiting, beloved. There were several things... no, it would be more correct to say some of my past caught up with me." That's all right. How does she feel? [kiyoko.pregStage 2|Your fox-wife pats her big, pregnant belly|Kiyoko looks away and toys with her hair, running it between thumb and forefinger]. "Quite good, all things considered." "And that settles everything quite nicely," Keros says as he steps towards everyone. "Komari, please leave us and make the appropriate arrangements for the Lady Otomo. Courtly proceedings take so long these days... but I'm sure if you use my name matters will speed up somewhat. There are a few more matters which I must attend to with regards to your liege." You eye Komari as she stumbles off, Miko and Mai grabbing their shaking, sniffling great-great-grandmother by the arms and leading her off. Now then, what matters would those be? "Why, the matter of the Lady Otomo's room and board, of course. For her and her [kiyoko.numKits 1 2 8 32 |most beloved daughter |most beloved children |many children |entire brood ], to be precise — as much as Komari is long-suffering, I don't imagine [kiyoko.numKits 8 32|several more|an entire horde of|a handful of] hungry mouths to feed is her idea of a good day. Before, the Astral Plane provided you all with all you needed, but that's not going to be the case any more, obviously. Kiyoko, call your [kiyoko.numKits 2|children|daughter] and let's be on our way." Kiyoko closes her eyes and dips her head in a small bow. "Your lordship is generous." "I am only cruel to those deserving of it. Extricating you from your prison and leaving you without means or measures would be quite remiss of me, would it not?" As Keros finishes speaking, Kinu returns from outside the shrine, [kiyoko.numKits 1 2 3|looking a little more nervous than she was when she left|her sibling in tow|her siblings in tow]. "Ah, excellent. Now, then..." The vulpine deity claps his hands and your surroundings melt away, replaced by that of [dayNight|warm sun|cool moonlight] and a gentle breeze. With a start, you realize that you know this place — how could you not? It's where all this began, the ruined shrine in the Old Forest... Kiyoko and the rest of your foxy family stand by your side, looking at the dilapidated ruins they now stand in, hemmed in by the crater. "Oh dear," your fox-wife murmurs. "Time has not been kind to my old home." "And it will be your home again, Lady Otomo. Now that you have returned amongst us, there is much you need to do — that which you were tasked with when you departed the Old Country. Komari has worked tirelessly for the last two and a half centuries to bring that vision into reality, but much still needs to be done." "Yes, my lordship." "Aha." Having regained some of his old good humor, Keros steps over to the nearest moss-covered, overgrown building and raps on it with his knuckles. Instantly, age and decay fade from weathered stone and aged wood, leaving it solid and pristine. The architecture, already in foreign, Old Country style, becomes even more prominently so when new, leaving you to marvel as centuries simply fall away. "Now, let's move on to the next one..." The vulpine god repeats the process with two more buildings, washing away their decrepit and abandoned state with a flick of his wrist. Once more, like sunlight creeping across a wall, the wave of change and rejuvenation restores each one to its former... well, glory might be pushing it, but sufficiency will do to describe the situation. It's not as glamorous as Kiyoko's previous accommodations, not in the least, but better this than a gilded cage, right? "There we go, accommodations for you and yours. I won't give you everything, but neither will I leave you with nothing to get started with. After all, I am not completely heartless, regardless of what the legends sometimes say. There will be much work that needs to be done in restoring this place and eventually making it even better than it was, but these will be serviceable quarters for you and yours in the meantime. Quite humble for a heritor of divine blood, really, but I'm sure you'll manage just fine." "Your lordship is magnanimous."
rows.translation: 现在，小娟[kiyoko.numKits 1 2 3|的| 以及她的兄弟姐妹们| 以及她的兄弟姐妹们也都……]离开神社后，那位族长夫人缓缓走到你们两人面前，双眼半闭着。她慢慢地摘下自己佩戴的珠宝头饰，递给了米可；紧接着，她又将手杖交给了舞。在姐妹们惊愕的目光注视下，这位曾祖母双膝跪地，将额头贴在清子的脚边，行了一个标准的叩头礼。 宫本大人。 清子从你的怀抱中挣脱出来，她的笑容突然消失了。你在干什么，麻里？ 等等。你确定他们说的不是贝尔哈兰语，然而你却能完全听懂他们的话。环顾四周，你看到诡计之神朝你微微挥手，还冲你使了个会意的眨眼……哦，对了…… 几个世纪以来，我付出了无数努力想要弥补自己的过错，但我终究无法被原谅——因为在你们最需要我的时候，我却不在你们身边。作为你们的守护者，我却如此无能，以至于导致了你们的死亡……还有…… 麻里，那天就是我让你去加入那些女妖们的。如果违抗我的命令就能救我的命，你会这么做吗？不，这个问题毫无意义。这不是你的错，你怎么可能预见到会发生什么呢？基约科撩起裙摆，蹲在了那个侍从低垂着的头旁。请站起来。 黑川氏与乙羽氏世代为主从关系。正因为我的无能，我才应该付出生命的代价。由于我的死，十二神族陷入了政治纷争，若非那位神君出面制止，局势恐怕会失控。宫部大人，如果您不对我进行适当的惩罚，您也会蒙羞的。我……我绝不希望这样。 那就让我承受吧。够了。我再也不想经历这些了——如果你还继续称我为你的领主，那么我命令你不要再这种卑躬屈膝的行为了—— 麻里抬起头望着她的领主，这时你听到一阵剧烈的吸气声——清子强忍住想要尖叫和后退的冲动。或许自从你第一次认识她以来，这是你第一次看到她露出如此恐惧的表情：她的双眼紧紧地眯成了一条缝，脸色也变得煞白。她缓缓地将颤抖的双手抬到脸上，然后慢慢转过头去，望向了凯罗斯。 我的大人…… 你到底对我的头发做了什么？！" 那位狡黠的神明将双臂插进袖子里，他那平日里总是洋溢着欢乐的面容此刻仿佛被冰霜覆盖了一般，变得冷峻而严肃。我已经把她变成了夜叉。" 为、为什么？ 在完成对自己失败的赎罪之前，黑川麻里是不被允许死亡的；而这份赎罪的一部分，就是完成你们被派往海外去执行的那个任务。自‘神战’结束以来，已经过去了两个半世纪了，乙女清子……你认为她是如何先于你们来到这里的呢？凯罗斯沉默了一两秒钟，然后清了清嗓子。如果她不是这样的，那么你永远也不会收到这份道歉，她也就永远没有机会获得宽恕。 我……麻里，你忍受这种痛苦已经有多久了？拳头紧握，清子的目光中充满了恳求。是我受到了不公正的对待。难道我就不能…… 不，这是无法避免的。 虽然这有些无奈，但我还是决定去做。这样做或许无法让她得到解脱，但我还是要说出来。如果那天我没有死去，也就不会遇见她了。 [pc.name]我永远不会生下我的女儿小娟。即使是在一个金光闪闪的笼子里，我也不会拥有与家人共度的那些最幸福的时光。基约科身高足有五英尺，她像套上外套一样立刻展现出那种威严的神情，她的整个举止在瞬间发生了变化，她说话时语气清晰、抑扬顿挫，而且极具正式感。黑川麻里，你已经说得太多了，而你的失败也让你深受折磨。所以，我这位忠诚可靠的仆从…… 我会原谅你的。。" 当基约科俯身扶起麻里时，凯罗斯的表情依旧毫无波澜。这位巢穴的女首领行动迟缓、显得有些不稳，但显然，这并不是因为她的身体有什么问题。 我并不配得到这个，宫本大人。 如果你真的想为我效力、弥补过错的话，麻里，那我必须提出一个自私的要求。毫无疑问，你的寿命已经远远超过了正常应该拥有的长度夜叉但我希望你能再担任我的随从，陪伴我度过余生。在我离开的这段时间里，世界上肯定发生了许多变化。我想，即使得到了那位神圣君主的祝福，我的归来也必然会在海外引发不少麻烦。你愿意帮助我度过这段艰难的时光吗？ 命令我吧。 稍后吧。现在，我必须去照顾我的女儿和我的爱人，尤其是后者。我想[pc.heShe]听着别人谈话，肯定会觉得挺尴尬的吧。 [pc.heShe]完全无法理解。 说完这句话，清子便转身面向你。很抱歉让你等待了，亲爱的。有些事情……不，更准确地说，是我过去的一些经历找上了我。 没关系。她现在感觉怎么样？ [kiyoko.pregStage 2|你的狐狸妻子轻轻抚摸着自己那圆滚滚的、已经怀孕的肚子|清子将目光移开，开始摆弄自己的头发，用拇指和食指把头发来回拨弄着]。 总体来说，相当不错。 这样就把所有问题都解决得很好了。凯罗斯一边走向大家，一边说道。麻里，请你离开我们，为奥托摩夫人做好相应的安排。如今宫廷的手续实在太过繁琐……不过我相信，如果你利用我的名义，事情应该会快一些。关于你的主君，我还有几件事情需要处理。 你注视着步履蹒跚的麻里，而米可与舞则扶着那位颤抖着、抽泣不止的曾祖母的胳膊，将她带了出去。那么，这些事情究竟有什么重要的呢？ 嗯，当然是关于奥托摩小姐的食宿问题了。毕竟她和她[kiyoko.numKits 1 2 8 32 |最心爱的女儿 |最受宠爱的孩子们 |很多孩子 |整个一窝幼崽 ]准确来说——尽管麻里一直都很忍耐，但我认为她也不会忍受到这种地步。 [kiyoko.numKits 8 32|还有几件|一大群|一小把]对她来说，能够填饱饥饿的肚子才算是美好的一天。过去，星界空间为你们提供了所需的一切，但显然，这种情况再也不会发生了。纪代子，快打电话吧[kiyoko.numKits 2|孩子们|女儿]那我们就出发吧。 清子闭上眼睛，轻轻低头行了一个礼。您的慷慨真是令人敬佩。 我只会对那些罪有应得的人施以残酷的惩罚。如果你被从囚笼中解救出来，却没有任何生存的手段或条件，那未免太不负责任了，不是吗？当凯罗斯说完话后，小娟从神社外面走了回来。 [kiyoko.numKits 1 2 3|看起来比她离开时还要紧张一些|带着自己的兄弟姐妹一起|带着她的兄弟姐妹们]。 啊，太好了。那么，现在…… 那位狐族神明拍手一声，你周围的环境立刻消失了，取而代之的则是[dayNight|温暖的阳光|凉爽的月光]还有轻柔的微风。当你开始移动时，你突然意识到自己熟悉这个地方——怎么可能不熟悉呢？这一切都是从这里开始的，就是那片古古林中的废弃神社……清子以及你那些机灵的家人都站在你身边，望着眼前这些已被毁坏的遗迹，而这些遗迹现在被那个陨石坑所包围着。 哦，天哪。你的狐狸妻子在低语。时间并没有对我的旧国怀有丝毫怜悯。 而这里也将再次成为您的家园，大友女士。如今您回到了我们中间，还有许多事情需要您去完成——那些在您离开故国时就被赋予的任务。在过去的两个半世纪里，麻里为实现这一愿景付出了不懈的努力，但仍然有许多工作有待完成。 是的，大人。 啊哈。凯罗斯重新找回了几分往日的幽默感，他走到最近那座长满苔藓、杂草丛生的建筑前，用指关节敲了敲它的表面。瞬间，那些被岁月侵蚀的石块和腐朽的木头仿佛恢复了原有的模样，变得坚固而完好无损。这座原本就具有异国风情的老式建筑，在经过这样的处理后，其独特风格更加凸显出来，让人不禁惊叹于几个世纪的时间竟然能够如此轻易地被抹去。现在，让我们进入下一个环节…… 这位狡黠的神明又用同样的方法处理了另外两座建筑，仅仅轻轻一挥手腕，就使它们摆脱了破败与荒废的状态。再一次，就像阳光悄然洒在墙面上一样，那股变革与复兴的力量让每一座建筑都恢复了它曾经的……嗯，虽然“辉煌”或许有些夸张，但“完好”应该已经足以形容这种变化了。当然，这些建筑远没有纪代子的先前住所那么奢华，但总比被关在金笼子里要好吧？ 好了，这里有为你和你的家人准备的生活用品。我不会给你所有你需要的东西，但也不会让你一无所有、无法开始新的生活。毕竟，我并不是完全地无情，尽管传说中有时会提到其他说法。要恢复这个地方并最终让它变得比原来更好，还需要做很多工作，但在那之前，这些住所已经足够你们使用了。对于一位拥有神之血脉的继承者来说，这些条件确实相当简陋，但我相信你们一定能应付得来。 您的慷慨真是令人钦佩。

"If she were not so, then you would never have received this apology, and she would never have the chance to make absolution." "I... how long have you been tortured by this, Komari?" Balling her fists, Kiyoko's gaze turns pleading. "I am the one who was wronged. Can I not —" "No. It cannot be helped." "It cannot be helped, but I will do it nonetheless. It may not absolve her, but I will say it anyway. If I had not perished that day, I would not have met [pc.name]. I would not have given birth to my daughter Kinu. I would not have had, even if it was in a gilded cage, the happiest times of my existence with my family." Rising to her full five feet, Kiyoko puts on her imperious air like a coat, her entire demeanour shifting in the blink of an eye, her words crisp, deeply intoned and heavily formal. "Komari Kurokawa, you have said as much and your failure has tormented you deeply enough. So, my good and faithful retainer... I will forgive you." Keros' face is as impassive as ever while he watches Kiyoko reach down and take Komari by the hands, helping her up. The den matron is unsteady and slow to respond, but you know it's not because of any physical frailty on her part. "I do not deserve this, Myobu-sama." "If you want to serve me and make amends, Komari, then I must make a selfish request of you. No doubt you have lived far longer than you ought to as a yasha, but I would have you be my retainer for one more lifetime. Many things have no doubt changed in the world while I was gone, and I imagine that my return will cause no small amount of trouble across the ocean, even if I have his divine lordship's blessing. Will you guide me through this?" "Command me." "Later. For now, I must attend to my daughter and beloved, especially the latter. I imagine [pc.heShe] must feel awkward, listening in on a conversation [pc.heShe] cannot comprehend." With that, Kiyoko turns back to you. "I'm sorry to keep you waiting, beloved. There were several things... no, it would be more correct to say some of my past caught up with me." That's all right. How does she feel? [kiyoko.pregStage 2|Your fox-wife pats her big, pregnant belly|Kiyoko looks away and toys with her hair, running it between thumb and forefinger]. "Quite good, all things considered." "And that settles everything quite nicely," Keros says as he steps towards everyone. "Komari, please leave us and make the appropriate arrangements for the Lady Otomo. Courtly proceedings take so long these days... but I'm sure if you use my name matters will speed up somewhat. There are a few more matters which I must attend to with regards to your liege." You eye Komari as she stumbles off, Miko and Mai grabbing their shaking, sniffling great-great-grandmother by the arms and leading her off. Now then, what matters would those be? "Why, the matter of the Lady Otomo's room and board, of course. For her and her [kiyoko.numKits 1 2 8 32 |most beloved daughter |most beloved children |many children |entire brood ], to be precise — as much as Komari is long-suffering, I don't imagine [kiyoko.numKits 8 32|several more|an entire horde of|a handful of] hungry mouths to feed is her idea of a good day. Before, the Astral Plane provided you all with all you needed, but that's not going to be the case any more, obviously. Kiyoko, call your [kiyoko.numKits 2|children|daughter] and let's be on our way." Kiyoko closes her eyes and dips her head in a small bow. "Your lordship is generous." "I am only cruel to those deserving of it. Extricating you from your prison and leaving you without means or measures would be quite remiss of me, would it not?" As Keros finishes speaking, Kinu returns from outside the shrine, [kiyoko.numKits 1 2 3|looking a little more nervous than she was when she left|her sibling in tow|her siblings in tow]. "Ah, excellent. Now, then..." The vulpine deity claps his hands and your surroundings melt away, replaced by that of [dayNight|warm sun|cool moonlight] and a gentle breeze. With a start, you realize that you know this place — how could you not? It's where all this began, the ruined shrine in the Old Forest... Kiyoko and the rest of your foxy family stand by your side, looking at the dilapidated ruins they now stand in, hemmed in by the crater. "Oh dear," your fox-wife murmurs. "Time has not been kind to my old home." "And it will be your home again, Lady Otomo. Now that you have returned amongst us, there is much you need to do — that which you were tasked with when you departed the Old Country. Komari has worked tirelessly for the last two and a half centuries to bring that vision into reality, but much still needs to be done." "Yes, my lordship." "Aha." Having regained some of his old good humor, Keros steps over to the nearest moss-covered, overgrown building and raps on it with his knuckles. Instantly, age and decay fade from weathered stone and aged wood, leaving it solid and pristine. The architecture, already in foreign, Old Country style, becomes even more prominently so when new, leaving you to marvel as centuries simply fall away. "Now, let's move on to the next one..." The vulpine god repeats the process with two more buildings, washing away their decrepit and abandoned state with a flick of his wrist. Once more, like sunlight creeping across a wall, the wave of change and rejuvenation restores each one to its former... well, glory might be pushing it, but sufficiency will do to describe the situation. It's not as glamorous as Kiyoko's previous accommodations, not in the least, but better this than a gilded cage, right? "There we go, accommodations for you and yours. I won't give you everything, but neither will I leave you with nothing to get started with. After all, I am not completely heartless, regardless of what the legends sometimes say. There will be much work that needs to be done in restoring this place and eventually making it even better than it was, but these will be serviceable quarters for you and yours in the meantime. Quite humble for a heritor of divine blood, really, but I'm sure you'll manage just fine." "Your lordship is magnanimous."'

rows.original: Just then, Kinu comes running up from the distance, [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |practically tripping over herself in her elation. Fists balled, face screwed up, your fox-daughter looks like she's going to burst from all the excitement bouncing off inside of her. "[kinu.Dad]! Mom! Look! Look at all the open space out there by the west! And the water, such water! And the grass, and most of all, the soil! This is even better than it was in our old home!" Kiyoko looks around at the ruined remains of her old home and forces a weak smile. "Of course, Kinu. But let's take things one step at a time, all right? While we do have a roof over our heads, perhaps we should think of seeing to the actuality of our living conditions before getting all excited about such possibilities." |her bare feet excitedly pattering up the dirt trail until she realizes whose company she's in and falls back into a more refined, ladylike gait. "[pc.mf|Father|Mother], Mother, look! All these old buildings — such richness, such architecture, did you really stay here before, Mother? I can't wait to get these all restored and —" "One thing at a time, Kinu," Kiyoko chides gently. "Let us get you[kiyoko.numKits 3| and your siblings] settled in first and some sort of daily routine established, then perhaps we can see to the remainder of the restoration works." ] Keros himself laughs at the sight, a full, hearty belly laugh; he really is very jovial for a kitsune. "What a precocious child. And such enthusiasm, too — I'm sure she'll have no trouble whatsoever [kiyoko.numKits 6|charming several fine hands from Komari's to come and help with the restoration works once those get under way|marshaling her siblings into getting this place all nice and tidy once you've all gotten settled in]. But come. I've got one last thing I've got to give you to get you started." Humming to himself, Keros practically skips down the now much less overgrown dirt trail and approaches two broken, stumpy posts set into the ground by the crater wall. Cocking his head to the side, the vulpine deity studies the setup for all of two minutes before stepping forward and giving the broken post a sharp rap with his knuckles. There's a popping noise, a brief flash with an accompanying shower of sparkles, and standing where the twin stumps were is a small but serviceable torii gate, the air between the posts swirling ominously like a heat mirage. "My lord, I —" "Hmm, I think I'll tell Komari about the changes to her gate network later. Really want to see her face when new faces start showing up in her den. But yes, I've just given you a small but workable gate — the woods are getting more dangerous for travel, as I'm sure you're well aware of at this point, and then there's the situation to deal with, too. Either way, you'll want you and yours to be able to visit Komari and her people safely, so here we are. It's the least I can do, and that's all I have for my little welcoming gifts to you, descendant of mine. I hope you find your return to the land of the living to your liking, dear." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Running up, Kinu gives Keros a big hug, throwing her arms about his floofy robes and tails and squeezing tight |Carefully approaching her patron deity, Kinu gives Keros a deep bow that clearly conveys her grateful attitude ]. Chuckling, the fox-god reaches out and tousles her hair. "Aah, you're such an affectionate and adorable little dear — much like my own firstborn by Chizuru. May all your noble efforts be blessed, child. Be sure to invite me to your wedding, okay? Nothing more auspicious like having a god amongst your guests. Oh! One more thing. You'll probably want to remain here for a while, [pc.name], get things sorted out with your fox-wife. In that case..." [party.hasCompanions |Rolling up his sleeves, Keros thrusts his arms into thin air and takes hold of something, then heaves. A moment later, [party.compNames] [party.som||comes|come] tumbling out of nothingness and into existence, their sudden fall broken by the soft, unkempt grass by the torii gate. "Shouldn't forget about your friends," the vulpine deity says with a smirk. "I'm sure everyone wants a piece of this joyous occasion." [party.comp cait brint brienne atugia etheryn arona berwyn einin azyrran |Cait lands on her tush with a soft full-body jiggle, her staff following her a moment later, giving her a sharp rap to the head before clattering on the earth. "Owww... and I was just about to taste the steamed buns, too! Who — oh! [pc.Name]! So this is where you went?" |Brint lands on the grass with a surprised %"oomph", shaking his head at the sudden change of scenery. The big hunk of beef struggles to his feet, looks around, then finds you. "I can't say I didn't get my wish when I wanted to experience new things. First that Ways Between place, now being yanked around through thin air... are we going to sail the ocean on a ship next? That's an adventure I'd like to try someday." |Tumbling out of thin air, it takes a little while for Brienne to come to a stop, the cowgirl's voluptuous form giving her a bit more rolling distance than most would imagine.[silly| You're tempted to make a joke about cow tipping, but perhaps that would be going a bit too far, would it?] "O-ow! Hey, watch it!" the hefty cowgirl says as she struggles to her feet. "For a skinny guy like that to have so strong a grip, though..." |"Oh! Hey! Wha —" Atugia begins before picking herself up and looking around as she dusts herself off. "Oh, it's you, [pc.name]. Look, I'm used to Carmen summoning me back and forth all over the place for years now, but this has got to be something else. Wasn't bad or anything, but... you've got to give a[pc.mf||nother] girl some warning before you do something like that, right?" |Completely caught off surprise, Ryn comes tumbling head over heels onto the grass, clearly disoriented by the sudden change of scenery. Your elf friend rubs her head, blinking as she adjusts to her new surroundings, then fixes her gaze on you. "Oh! [pc.name]! When someone grabbed me from behind, I was worried — no, that was silly. Alissa... of course. Nothing's wrong." A miniature panic attack? "You could say that, I suppose, but everything's all right now. Where are we, though?" |Arona's up and on her feet in a flash, ready to give battle; when she sees you, though, the orcess relaxes marginally and her face contorts into a scowl. "Ah, it's just you. Damn it, did you have to do that? I was about to get three of those furry cumrags on my dick, and they were more than willing..." Indeed, Arona's hefty cock is hanging out of her leathers, slowly softening now that there's no source of vulpine temptation in front of her. With a huff, she shoves it back in, then rolls her shoulders as she hefts her weapon. "So... you yanked me all the way here for?" |Yipping, Berwyn lands on the grassy earth, his hands firmly affixed to his hat lest it fall off at the most inopportune moment. After all, a wizard is nothing without his hat, is he? You step over to the dogboy and help him up, hat, staff and all; his tail wags appreciatively as he rights himself and looks around. "Hey, thanks for that. Was about to try some of that shaved ice stuff when someone grabbed me from behind and... where are we, anyway?" |Einin looks utterly terrified as Keros pulls her into view, lifting the little mecian off the ground as her legs windmill in the air in an appropriately comical fashion. It's only when she spots you that she relaxes marginally, her feet slowing slightly in their reflexive motions. "What — what was that for?" There's a clear, accusatory note in her voice. "I'm a fox. You're a mouse. Foxes catch mice, it's what we do, and we do it well. Now then, my apologies for the sudden displacement, but [pc.name] has need of you. Here." Einin squeaks as he drops her onto the ground. Her instincts and reflexes kick in all right, her body preparing to turn the fall into a roll, but there isn't enough height and she flops on her belly, looking sheepish. "What a jerk," she mumbles, dusting herself off as she scrambles to her feet. "Well, I'm here, I guess." |Her diaphanous wings buzzing at the air in a bid to keep her balance, Azyrran emerges from nothingness and lands on her butt. The hive knight tries to look nonplussed at the sudden change of scenery, struggling to keep a stiff upper lip, but calms right down when she sees you're here. "Well, that was a trip." ] |Yes? ] "I don't think there's anything more to be done on my part right now," Keros continues. "On your part, though... well, as they say, daylight's a-wasting. Idle hands are my plaything and all that, you know. And as for you, [pc.name], if you need to find me, you know where to look. I may even be motivated to come seek you out — there's a lot someone like you could do for me, with adequate compensation, of course. "Now, if you'll excuse me." It should be impossible — it has to be impossible, but Keros manages to pull his colorful robes and nine tails about himself, binding himself in the voluminous fluff and winking out of existence in the blink of an eye. You're left standing there for a moment until Kiyoko and Kinu come up to you, mother and daughter [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality |giving each other glances but nevertheless in accord for now |beaming with joy ]. "Now that his divine lordship's gone, there's something we have for you, too, beloved. I had a feeling this would come to pass soon, and your daughter and I prepared something for the occasion that you would also find useful in your travels." Reaching into her yukata, Kiyoko pulls out a simple length of white silk cloth, folded many times over on itself. Lining the edges and running along the middle are a multitude of tiny red cross-stitches, the thread fine yet incredibly strong. "A thousand-stitch belt. Mother and I wove the charms into the cloth together," Kinu adds. "We spared no expense in its creation; it is as powerful as they come." Reaching forward, Kiyoko presses the sash into your hands. "Traditionally, each stitch was to be made by a different woman, but I think it carries more meaning if we split the job between us. May it bolster you in your time of need as you did for us for so long." You have received the senninbari. Looking into your faithful fox-wife's eyes, you feel like there should be something more said, that this exchange should be longer, but sometimes the deepest meanings are carried without words. Kiyoko bows her head and looks down, biting her lip, then turns to Kinu. "Come now. While his divine lordship has been generous in the extreme, there is much we have to do to make a house a home and we have to take stock of his gifts.[kiyoko.numKits 8| Gather your brothers and sisters — life is not going to be as easy from here on out.]" With that, mother and daughter retreat into what looks to be the shrine's main building, leaving you alone with your emotions, whatever they may be. The amulet of union has been removed from your inventory; from now on, you may find Kiyoko in her old home when she is not in your active party. You can access this location from near where the kitsune shrine in the Old Forest was, or go to and from it via the torii gate in the kitsune den.
