|汪汪”，贝尔温落在了长满草地的地上，他双手紧紧抓住自己的帽子，生怕它在最不合适的时刻掉下来。毕竟，一个巫师如果没有帽子，那他还算什么巫师呢？ 你走过去帮助这个小狗男孩站起来，他的帽子和法杖都还在手上；当他站稳身体环顾四周时，他的尾巴兴奋地摇动着。 嘿，谢谢你。我正打算试试那种刨冰呢，结果有人从后面抓住了我就……我们现在到底在哪儿呢？ |当凯罗斯将艾宁拉到视线范围内时，她看起来惊恐万分——她的双腿在空中疯狂地乱蹬，样子显得十分滑稽。直到她看到了你，她的动作才稍微放松了一些，双腿的乱蹬也慢了下来。 什——什么？那个为什么？她的声音中明显带着指责的意味。 我是一只狐妖，而你是一只老鼠。狐妖的任务就是抓老鼠，这是我们的天职，而且我们也做得非常出色。那么，对于这次突然的变动，我表示歉意，但是[pc.name]需要你的帮助。在这里。 艾宁被扔到地上时发出了一声吱吱声。她的本能和反应能力立刻发挥了作用，身体试图将这次坠落转化为一个翻滚动作，但由于高度不够，她最终只能趴在地上，看起来有些尴尬。 真是个混蛋。她一边嘟囔着，一边拍掉身上的灰尘，慌忙站了起来。嗯，我想，我应该是到这儿了吧。 |她的半透明翅膀在空气中振动，试图保持平衡，阿兹兰从虚无中出现，落在了她的屁股上。这位蜂群骑士试图表现出若无其事的样子，努力强忍着内心的慌乱，但当你出现时，她立刻平静了下来。 哎呀，那可真是段有趣的经历啊。 ] |嗯？ ] 我想目前我这边没有什么需要再做的了。凯罗斯继续说道。在……上你的不过，嗯，就像人们说的，时间不等人。闲着的手可是我的玩物，你懂的。至于你[pc.name]，如果你需要找到我，你知道该去哪里找。我甚至可能会主动去找你——当然，前提是得到适当的报酬，因为像你这样的人，确实能为我带来很多帮助。 现在，如果你们不介意的话，我先告辞了。 这应该是不可能的——绝对不可能。拥有这简直是不可能的事，但凯罗斯却成功地套上了自己那件色彩斑斓的长袍，甩动那九条尾巴，将自己裹在那一团蓬松的布料里，转眼间就消失得无影无踪。你站在那里愣了一会儿，直到清子和小犬母女俩走过来。 [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality |彼此交换着眼神，但眼下还是达成了共识 |喜笑颜开 ]。 既然您的神圣主公已经离开了，我们也有一些东西要送给您，亲爱的。我就觉得这件事很快就会发生，所以我和您的女儿为这个场合准备了一些东西，相信这些在您的旅途中也会派上用场。 清子从和服里取出一块白色丝绸布料，这块布料被反复折叠了几层。布料的边缘和中间都绣着许多细小的红色十字纹样，线虽然很细，但却异常结实。 这条千针缝制的腰带，是我和母亲一起将那些吉祥图案编织到布料上的。小娟补充道。 我们在制作它的过程中不惜花费任何代价；它确实是目前最强大的同类产品之一。 基约科向前伸出手，将腰带递到了你的手中。传统上，每一针都是由不同的女性来完成的，但我觉得如果我们共同来完成这项工作，它会赋予更多的意义。愿这份帮助能在你需要的时候为你带来力量，就像你长期以来为我们所做的那样。 你已经收到了仙人棒。 凝视着你那忠贞的狐妖妻子的眼睛，你觉得应该还有更多话要说，这段对话应该更长一些，但有时候，最深层的含义其实无需言语就能表达出来。清子低下头，咬着嘴唇，然后转向纪夫。 快过来吧。虽然他的主公非常慷慨，但我们还有很多事情要做，才能让这个房子真正成为一个家，我们也必须仔细清点他赠送的物品。[kiyoko.numKits 8| 召集你的兄弟姐妹吧——从现在开始，生活不会再那么轻松了。]" 说完之后，母女俩便走进了那座神殿的主建筑里，将你独自留了下来，让你去面对自己的情感，无论那些情感是什么。 团结护身符”已从你的物品栏中移除；从现在开始，当清子不在你的当前队伍中时，你可以去她以前的家中找她。你可以从古林里的狐神祠附近找到这个地点，或者通过其他途径前往那里。鸟居狐妖洞的入口。
rows.raw: ' Just then, Kinu comes running up from the distance, [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |practically tripping over herself in her elation. Fists balled, face screwed up, your fox-daughter looks like she's going to burst from all the excitement bouncing off inside of her. "[kinu.Dad]! Mom! Look! Look at all the open space out there by the west! And the water, such water! And the grass, and most of all, the soil! This is even better than it was in our old home!" Kiyoko looks around at the ruined remains of her old home and forces a weak smile. "Of course, Kinu. But let's take things one step at a time, all right? While we do have a roof over our heads, perhaps we should think of seeing to the actuality of our living conditions before getting all excited about such possibilities." |her bare feet excitedly pattering up the dirt trail until she realizes whose company she's in and falls back into a more refined, ladylike gait. "[pc.mf|Father|Mother], Mother, look! All these old buildings — such richness, such architecture, did you really stay here before, Mother? I can't wait to get these all restored and —" "One thing at a time, Kinu," Kiyoko chides gently. "Let us get you[kiyoko.numKits 3| and your siblings] settled in first and some sort of daily routine established, then perhaps we can see to the remainder of the restoration works." ] Keros himself laughs at the sight, a full, hearty belly laugh; he really is very jovial for a kitsune. "What a precocious child. And such enthusiasm, too — I'm sure she'll have no trouble whatsoever [kiyoko.numKits 6|charming several fine hands from Komari's to come and help with the restoration works once those get under way|marshaling her siblings into getting this place all nice and tidy once you've all gotten settled in]. But come. I've got one last thing I've got to give you to get you started." Humming to himself, Keros practically skips down the now much less overgrown dirt trail and approaches two broken, stumpy posts set into the ground by the crater wall. Cocking his head to the side, the vulpine deity studies the setup for all of two minutes before stepping forward and giving the broken post a sharp rap with his knuckles. There's a popping noise, a brief flash with an accompanying shower of sparkles, and standing where the twin stumps were is a small but serviceable torii gate, the air between the posts swirling ominously like a heat mirage. "My lord, I —" "Hmm, I think I'll tell Komari about the changes to her gate network later. Really want to see her face when new faces start showing up in her den. But yes, I've just given you a small but workable gate — the woods are getting more dangerous for travel, as I'm sure you're well aware of at this point, and then there's the situation to deal with, too. Either way, you'll want you and yours to be able to visit Komari and her people safely, so here we are. It's the least I can do, and that's all I have for my little welcoming gifts to you, descendant of mine. I hope you find your return to the land of the living to your liking, dear." [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |Running up, Kinu gives Keros a big hug, throwing her arms about his floofy robes and tails and squeezing tight |Carefully approaching her patron deity, Kinu gives Keros a deep bow that clearly conveys her grateful attitude ]. Chuckling, the fox-god reaches out and tousles her hair. "Aah, you're such an affectionate and adorable little dear — much like my own firstborn by Chizuru. May all your noble efforts be blessed, child. Be sure to invite me to your wedding, okay? Nothing more auspicious like having a god amongst your guests. Oh! One more thing. You'll probably want to remain here for a while, [pc.name], get things sorted out with your fox-wife. In that case..." [party.hasCompanions |Rolling up his sleeves, Keros thrusts his arms into thin air and takes hold of something, then heaves. A moment later, [party.compNames] [party.som||comes|come] tumbling out of nothingness and into existence, their sudden fall broken by the soft, unkempt grass by the torii gate. "Shouldn't forget about your friends," the vulpine deity says with a smirk. "I'm sure everyone wants a piece of this joyous occasion." [party.comp cait brint brienne atugia etheryn arona berwyn einin azyrran |Cait lands on her tush with a soft full-body jiggle, her staff following her a moment later, giving her a sharp rap to the head before clattering on the earth. "Owww... and I was just about to taste the steamed buns, too! Who — oh! [pc.Name]! So this is where you went?" |Brint lands on the grass with a surprised %"oomph", shaking his head at the sudden change of scenery. The big hunk of beef struggles to his feet, looks around, then finds you. "I can't say I didn't get my wish when I wanted to experience new things. First that Ways Between place, now being yanked around through thin air... are we going to sail the ocean on a ship next? That's an adventure I'd like to try someday." |Tumbling out of thin air, it takes a little while for Brienne to come to a stop, the cowgirl's voluptuous form giving her a bit more rolling distance than most would imagine.[silly| You're tempted to make a joke about cow tipping, but perhaps that would be going a bit too far, would it?] "O-ow! Hey, watch it!" the hefty cowgirl says as she struggles to her feet. "For a skinny guy like that to have so strong a grip, though..." |"Oh! Hey! Wha —" Atugia begins before picking herself up and looking around as she dusts herself off. "Oh, it's you, [pc.name]. Look, I'm used to Carmen summoning me back and forth all over the place for years now, but this has got to be something else. Wasn't bad or anything, but... you've got to give a[pc.mf||nother] girl some warning before you do something like that, right?" |Completely caught off surprise, Ryn comes tumbling head over heels onto the grass, clearly disoriented by the sudden change of scenery. Your elf friend rubs her head, blinking as she adjusts to her new surroundings, then fixes her gaze on you. "Oh! [pc.name]! When someone grabbed me from behind, I was worried — no, that was silly. Alissa... of course. Nothing's wrong." A miniature panic attack? "You could say that, I suppose, but everything's all right now. Where are we, though?" |Arona's up and on her feet in a flash, ready to give battle; when she sees you, though, the orcess relaxes marginally and her face contorts into a scowl. "Ah, it's just you. Damn it, did you have to do that? I was about to get three of those furry cumrags on my dick, and they were more than willing..." Indeed, Arona's hefty cock is hanging out of her leathers, slowly softening now that there's no source of vulpine temptation in front of her. With a huff, she shoves it back in, then rolls her shoulders as she hefts her weapon. "So... you yanked me all the way here for?" |Yipping, Berwyn lands on the grassy earth, his hands firmly affixed to his hat lest it fall off at the most inopportune moment. After all, a wizard is nothing without his hat, is he? You step over to the dogboy and help him up, hat, staff and all; his tail wags appreciatively as he rights himself and looks around. "Hey, thanks for that. Was about to try some of that shaved ice stuff when someone grabbed me from behind and... where are we, anyway?" |Einin looks utterly terrified as Keros pulls her into view, lifting the little mecian off the ground as her legs windmill in the air in an appropriately comical fashion. It's only when she spots you that she relaxes marginally, her feet slowing slightly in their reflexive motions. "What — what was that for?" There's a clear, accusatory note in her voice. "I'm a fox. You're a mouse. Foxes catch mice, it's what we do, and we do it well. Now then, my apologies for the sudden displacement, but [pc.name] has need of you. Here." Einin squeaks as he drops her onto the ground. Her instincts and reflexes kick in all right, her body preparing to turn the fall into a roll, but there isn't enough height and she flops on her belly, looking sheepish. "What a jerk," she mumbles, dusting herself off as she scrambles to her feet. "Well, I'm here, I guess." |Her diaphanous wings buzzing at the air in a bid to keep her balance, Azyrran emerges from nothingness and lands on her butt. The hive knight tries to look nonplussed at the sudden change of scenery, struggling to keep a stiff upper lip, but calms right down when she sees you're here. "Well, that was a trip." ] |Yes? ] "I don't think there's anything more to be done on my part right now," Keros continues. "On your part, though... well, as they say, daylight's a-wasting. Idle hands are my plaything and all that, you know. And as for you, [pc.name], if you need to find me, you know where to look. I may even be motivated to come seek you out — there's a lot someone like you could do for me, with adequate compensation, of course. "Now, if you'll excuse me." It should be impossible — it has to be impossible, but Keros manages to pull his colorful robes and nine tails about himself, binding himself in the voluminous fluff and winking out of existence in the blink of an eye. You're left standing there for a moment until Kiyoko and Kinu come up to you, mother and daughter [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality |giving each other glances but nevertheless in accord for now |beaming with joy ]. "Now that his divine lordship's gone, there's something we have for you, too, beloved. I had a feeling this would come to pass soon, and your daughter and I prepared something for the occasion that you would also find useful in your travels." Reaching into her yukata, Kiyoko pulls out a simple length of white silk cloth, folded many times over on itself. Lining the edges and running along the middle are a multitude of tiny red cross-stitches, the thread fine yet incredibly strong. "A thousand-stitch belt. Mother and I wove the charms into the cloth together," Kinu adds. "We spared no expense in its creation; it is as powerful as they come." Reaching forward, Kiyoko presses the sash into your hands. "Traditionally, each stitch was to be made by a different woman, but I think it carries more meaning if we split the job between us. May it bolster you in your time of need as you did for us for so long." You have received the senninbari. Looking into your faithful fox-wife's eyes, you feel like there should be something more said, that this exchange should be longer, but sometimes the deepest meanings are carried without words. Kiyoko bows her head and looks down, biting her lip, then turns to Kinu. "Come now. While his divine lordship has been generous in the extreme, there is much we have to do to make a house a home and we have to take stock of his gifts.[kiyoko.numKits 8| Gather your brothers and sisters — life is not going to be as easy from here on out.]" With that, mother and daughter retreat into what looks to be the shrine's main building, leaving you alone with your emotions, whatever they may be. The amulet of union has been removed from your inventory; from now on, you may find Kiyoko in her old home when she is not in your active party. You can access this location from near where the kitsune shrine in the Old Forest was, or go to and from it via the torii gate in the kitsune den. '

rows.original: Komari's gaze flickers at that, wandering to the shelves that line the chamber. [party.has kiyoko |Before she can say anything, though, Kiyoko gently sets down her tea cup on the low table with a very final and resounding knock of porcelain on wood. "It's all right, Komari. You have my express permission — we are going to sit here and have a pleasant conversation, the three of us. While we are talking, your great-great granddaughters [kinu.isHime|and my daughter ]are going to come up with youkan and dorayaki, and everything's going to be just fine. While my forgiveness cannot obliviate the need for penance, it can buy you a small respite from such. "Now then, sit back down and ease your mind." Komari breathes out heavily and forces herself to relax. "It will be as you wish, [silly|Myōbu-sa|Lady Ōto] — I mean Kiyoko. Gods. I've yet to come to terms with you sitting and speaking to me... please, forgive my weakness." Your beloved fox-wife merely closes her eyes and sips her tea. "Ah, how long has it been? More than two centuries, as I understand it? Yet some things never change, and this is one of them. Come now then, where are the desserts to accompany our relaxing conversation?[kiyoko.pregStage 1| I have a kit in my belly, and would like to taste something sweet before the day is out.]" |[pc.ra kitsune |You clear your throat, and she snaps her attention back to you. "Forgive me, my [pc.mf|lord|lady]. I allowed my mind to wander unduly." It's all right. She's here and attending to the handpicked champion of her patron deity — there can't be anything more pressing or important than that, right? You'd imagine it'd be enough for her to drop everything and take a moment to have a pleasant conversation with someone who serves the same deity as her. "Yes, of course. I just need a moment." |You give her a small nod, and she snaps her attention back to you. "Pardon me. I was lost in thought." It's all right, she looks like she's been on edge lately. Well, lately is relative; you haven't known her very long in the scheme of things. "Of course, of course. I merely needed a moment to gather myself." ] ] Now then. Perhaps you should put forward a topic of conversation...
rows.translation: 麻里的目光在那处停留了一下，随后移向了摆满房间的书架。 [party.has kiyoko |然而，在她还能说些什么之前，清子轻轻地将茶杯放在矮桌上，那瓷杯与木桌相碰发出的声音清脆而响亮。 没关系，麻里。我正式允许你——我们三个人就坐在这里，愉快地聊聊天吧。在聊天的时候，你的曾曾孙女们[kinu.isHime|还有我的女儿 ]将会想出办法来幽玄以及豆沙糕一切都会好起来的。虽然我的宽恕无法消除你需要赎罪的事实，但它至少能让你暂时摆脱这种困扰。 那么，现在坐下来，放松一下吧。 麻里深吸一口气，强迫自己放松下来。就会如你所愿的。 [silly|妙法寺|大登女士] — 我是说清子……天啊，我至今还是无法接受你竟然能坐在这里和我说话……请原谅我的软弱吧。 你心爱的狐妖妻子只是闭着眼睛品着茶而已。啊，这么久过去了啊？据我所知，已经超过两个世纪了吧？不过有些事情永远都不会改变，这件事就是其中之一。那么，快说说吧，用来陪伴我们轻松聊天的甜点在哪里呢？[kiyoko.pregStage 1| 我肚子里装着一套“装备”，在今天结束之前，真想尝点甜的东西。]" |[pc.ra kitsune |你清了清嗓子，她这才将注意力重新转向你。原谅我，我的[pc.mf|领主|女士]我的思绪不由自主地开始飘忽。 没关系。她现在在这里，正在照顾她所信仰的神明挑选出的这位英雄——没有什么事情比这更紧急、更重要的了，对吧？你应该会认为，她放下一切，花一点时间与一个信仰同一位神明的人愉快地交谈，就已经足够了。 是的，当然可以。我只需要一会儿时间。 |你轻轻地向她点了点头，她立刻又将注意力重新集中在你身上。对不起，我刚才走神了。 没关系，她看起来最近确实有些紧张。不过，“最近”这个时间范围其实也挺相对的——毕竟你认识她的时间还不算太长。 当然，当然。我只是需要一点时间来整理一下思绪而已。 ] ] 那么，或许你应该提出一个话题来开始谈话吧……

rows.translation: 你有件事一直想问。麻里是凯罗斯的女祭司——如果我没弄错的话，应该可以称她为神殿的守护者。你肯定想了解一下那些狐妖族是如何举行婚礼的……

rows.original: [rand |"The secret to living a life as comparatively long as I have is to simply take things one day at a time. When faced with a challenge that seems daunting or insurmountable, it's always best to break it down into several smaller and far more manageable goals. That, at least, helps to keep matters in perspective and allows you to better plan out the path you need to take to get things done in a timely manner. "Where I come from, there's a saying that very roughly translates to 'just for today.' Not that one shouldn't keep the future in view, but when one is asked to bear the unbearable then it's better to empty one's mind and focus on getting through the day. Despite paying lip service to such, most people don't really want tomorrow to be different; they want tomorrow to be like today because they know they can live through today. "There's that, of course, and the realization that not everything is within your power to change. Sometimes... matters truly can't be helped, and it takes experience to discern what's worth spending your precious time and energy on, and what's going to end up in a futile endeavor. I remember when I was younger... I was so excited to sail the ocean in service of my liege. Ah, to be full of ideals and the vigor with which to pursue them once more." |"When [party.has kiyoko |you left us, my lady, much was thrown into disarray. The expeditionary force was reduced to no more than two dozen, and our ostensible allies were tenuous at best. We didn't even speak their language to a functional degree, and had to rely on his divine lordship's providence to communicate with them. rows.translation: [rand |能够活到我这样的年纪，秘诀就在于一天天地过好每一天。当遇到看似艰巨、无法克服的挑战时，最好的办法就是将其分解成若干个更小、更容易应对的目标。这样至少可以帮助我们保持正确的视角，从而更有条理地规划前进的道路，确保能够及时完成各项任务。 在我成长的地方，有句俗语，大致可以翻译成“就今天这一天而已”。这并不是说人们不应该考虑未来，但当面临无法承受的负担时，最好暂时忘掉一切，专心度过这一天。然而，尽管很多人口头上会这么说，但实际上并没有人真正这样做。真的他们希望明天能与今天不同；他们希望明天依然和今天一样，因为他们知道自己能够熬过今天。 当然，还有这样一种认识：并不是所有事情都可以在你的能力范围内去改变。有时候……有些事情确实无能为力，而只有通过经验，才能分辨出哪些事情值得你投入宝贵的时间和精力，哪些努力最终只会徒劳无功。我记得在我年轻的时候……我曾经非常渴望能够为我的君主效力，去远航于海洋之上。啊，那时候我是多么充满理想，也多么有决心去追求它们啊。 |当[party.has kiyoko |夫人，您离开后，一切都陷入了混乱。远征军的人数减少到了二十多人，而那些所谓的盟友也根本不可靠。我们甚至无法流利地使用他们的语言，因此只能依靠那位神圣君主的庇护来与他们沟通。作为您的随从，我在幸存者中地位最高…… 清子的表情十分平静，难以揣测其中的情感倾向。你做得很好，将原本糟糕的局面扭转成了令人十分满意的结果。虽然你为我效力只有两年时间，但显然你比大多数人更加努力，成功应对了我不幸离世所带来的种种挑战。麻里……虽然我无法免除你应履行的赎罪责任，但请记住，我已经原谅了你。 即便如此…… |不幸的是，大友夫人不幸遇难，远征军的人数减少到了不超过二十人，而我们那些名义上的盟友，充其量也只能算是一些靠不住的力量。我们甚至无法流利地使用他们的语言，因此只能依靠那位神圣君主的庇护来与他们进行沟通。作为她的随从，我在幸存者中地位最高…… 从表面上看，她确实把一个糟糕的局面扭转了过来，尽管这花费了一些时间。 情况本来可能会更糟，也有可能变得更好。理想情况下，根本就不会出现这种糟糕的局面，而我们……我…… ] 麻里的声音渐渐消失了，她侧着头望向附近的窗户，仿佛希望在那昏暗的光线中捕捉到什么。最终，这个巢穴的女首领转过身来，微微撇了撇嘴。抱歉我突然提到了这个话题。现在确实不是讨论这个的时候…… |根据家族记载，黑川一族历来都是从事神职工作的家族。在我的故乡，我们掌管着几座重要的神社，不过我们之所以出名，主要是因为曾作为大友一族的精神顾问为他们提供服务。即便在这个地区，那些为七大氏族服务的人神明即使在你们这些精英中间，这种信仰也备受尊崇；试想，在我的家乡，宣称与神灵的后代有着奴隸般的隶属关系，那该是一种怎样的体验啊。 [party.has kiyoko |因此，按照两家之间约定的习俗，清子说道，大户人家的三女儿后来成为了大友家继承人的侍女。 |一切就是这么开始的，对吧？ ] 麻里沉默了一会儿。事实就是如此。但回到正题……在某些方面，当神秘的事物不断侵入你的日常生活时，你会逐渐对此习以为常；毕竟，熟悉会让人产生轻视之情。当某种东西无处不在时，你就会开始忽视它，不再去关注它了。这片土地上的原住民与他们的神明建立关系的方式与众不同——精神领袖与普通民众之间存在着一种距离感，这种距离使得人们对神明怀有一种敬畏之情，实在没有更好的词语来形容这种感觉了。我并不是说这好还是坏……但这种行事方式与我或我同类的人们的习惯截然不同。在这里，命令、修道院、小教堂……世俗与神圣之间的界限划分得比我在自己熟悉的地方要清晰得多。但话说回来，这就是这些人的行事方式，不同的民族确实需要遵循不同的规则来生活。 |她在大洋彼岸还有家人吗？ 是的，但是…… 但是呢？ 从官方角度来看，我确实是一个流亡者。不过，被宣布为“无面者”其实比这还要糟糕——你可以把这种处境理解为被列为逃犯，而这种惩罚通常只会施加在战士阶层的人身上。但是，让我在值班期间眼睁睁看着大友夫人死去，这种事情绝对不能被轻易忽视。 [party.has kiyoko|即使她已经原谅了我，我……|我]如果对于这样的失误没有对我施加适当的惩罚，那么这对所有相关人员来说都会带来更大的耻辱。在那个时候，唯一能够改变我的命运的人，就是他的神圣主宰本人……而他确实这么做了。 你开始明白事情会朝着什么方向发展了。所以……在她自己看来，她已经死了？ ……它应该表面上是这样，但实际上并没有那么糟糕。我的一些后代尽管血脉中带有那层污点，还是设法回到了这里。后来，我终于把米可与舞召到殖民地，让她们接受训练，成为我的继承人。我也可以偶尔独自返回故乡，而且有时候还会有正式的召唤。只要把这些事情处理得隐秘一些，现实与表面上的情况就可以有所不同；无论有没有诅咒，作为一位神明的事实，确实让我的处境变得有利许多。 |听到这些故事[pc.ra kitsune|当地居民|你的子民]在我遇到的那些人中，有很多都一心只想尽可能长时间地活下去。然而，那些真正做到了这一点的人……无一例外地都是心理变态者，缺乏感情，或者是因为某些不幸的境遇才被迫如此的。有些事情听起来比实际情况要美好得多……而那种苦涩的本质，往往并不容易被立刻察觉。希望米科或舞能够接替我担任总督一职，而他的神圣地位也能让我与这片土地融为一体。我再也无法死亡了……至少不是你们所理解的那种死亡。不过，放弃我的意识与自我意识，对于这个目的来说，已经算是死亡了。 是的，米可与舞不就是她的继承人吗？那么，这难道不意味着她至少希望凯罗斯能在她们能够继承她的位置之前，认为她的赎罪已经完全完成了吗？ 在过去的三代人里，我一直在培养继承人。随之而来的是简短的回复。心中怀着一个渺茫的、或许只是徒劳的希望：但愿这一生能够成为那位至高无上的主决定我的赎罪已然完成、而我也能有他人来接替我的位置的那一年……然而，不知道这段苦难何时才会结束，本身就已经成为了这种惩罚的一部分；而更令人难以忍受的是，根本无法预知这种痛苦何时才会终结。不过，或许也有那么一点慰藉吧——那位至高无上的主已经向我承诺是必须有一个结局——而在我替我的君主圆满完成她的任务之前，这个结局是不会到来的。 作为亚莎这其实蕴含着几个意义。最显而易见的一点是，从这一刻起，我不再变老了——既不会老到还保留着一丝少女时的模样，也不会老到变得弯腰驼背。我有时候会想，是不是因为我已经停在了这个阶段，因为人们往往都是这样预期我本希望自己看起来是那样的，但我从来都没有机会去验证这个理论是否正确。 还需要什么吗？我不需要吃饭、喝水、睡觉，也不需要做那些人们为了维持生命而必须做的事情。我可以如果我想做的话，就可以去做——至少这能让人心情平静，但严格来说，这并不是必须的。我知道自己有血液，至少在某种程度上是有的，而且我的皮肤很容易淤青，但即使受伤了，我也不会流血。我不确定如果有人试图把我切成碎片会发生什么，但我相信他的神圣主宰肯定也考虑到了这种可能性。 几个世纪前，常青女士曾多次试图毒害我。但每一次尝试都以失败告终——因为我不仅喝下了她下的毒药，还通过她雇来来骚扰我的那些雇佣兵，给她回了一封措辞严厉的信。 [evergreen.killed|嗯，我想这个问题应该不会再存在了吧，对吧？|从那以后，她不再试图直接攻击我，而是把注意力转向了卡门，因为卡门至少是一个更容易对付的目标，而且没有“天心之主·八月尊者”那样的个人保护。也许她已经意识到，什么都不做才是最糟糕的选择——因为这样几乎不需要付出任何努力，不过我也不敢完全判断她这种怨恨的程度究竟有多深。]" 你可以理解为什么人们会被这样的前景所吸引。这是一种外甜内苦的东西，外表看似诱人，实则充满危险。 至少我知道自己是在受到惩罚。卡门和奥克萨娜……啊，只有那些真正无情无义的人才能够忍受这种生活，更别说还乐在其中了。 ]

I can do them if I want to — and it soothes the mind, if nothing else, but it's not strictly necessary. I know I have blood — at least, after a fashion — and I bruise well enough, yet if I get cut, I don't bleed. I'm not sure what would happen if someone were to try and hack me to pieces, but I'm sure his divine lordship has covered that angle, too. "A couple of centuries ago, Evergreen tried to poison me a couple of times. Every attempt ended in failure as I drank her poisons and sent a strongly-worded letter back to her via the mercenaries she'd hired to trouble me. [evergreen.killed|Well, guess that's not going to be a problem any more, is it?|Since then, she's stopped trying to attack me directly and has focused her attention on getting back at Carmen, who at least is a softer target and doesn't have the personal protection of the August Master At The Center Of Heaven. Maybe she's realized that doing absolutely nothing is the most terrible thing she can do for the least effort involved, although I wouldn't judge the extent of her spite.]" You can see why people would be tempted by such a prospect. A bitter poison coated with a sweet outer layer, deceptively and dangerously appealing. "At least I knew I was being punished. Carmen and Oxana... ah, only the truly heartless could put up with, let alone enjoy such an existence." ] "

rows.original: [pc.ra kitsune |"Now that you're one of us, I'm able to tell you a few more things about the den..." You're all ears — anything to help you understand more about your new role and station in the scheme of things. [rand |"Such sacred trees... they are not just places for us to live in. Each one represents the effort of one generation to the other; they are not owned, but stewarded. One generation receives it from the previous, and it is to be kept for the generation who will come after; it is not something that you can do with as you wish as if it were your property. Such a mindset can be extended to all things... I may be the sole kitsune who has had the fortune of being able to witness the growth of one from seed to sapling to what it is today. "Twenty years for it to grow large enough to accommodate a single family comfortably. A hundred for it to resemble that which you see today. Perhaps such a timespan is insignificant to those who live natural lives of millennia like the boreal elves, which is why their druids have different relationships with their own wyld trees, but once rooted, these sacred cherry blossom trees not only provide a bulwark against mere mundane forces, but more importantly, the supernatural. That is vitally important, because the colonial struggle is primarily not one of dealing with the flesh-and-blood inhabitants, but convincing the land itself to turn to us. The boreal elves have long since abandoned these woods in favor of the glaciers further north, but the land remembers their touch and is reluctant to move on." |"These sacred cherry blossom trees... they are not grown in the sense you would be familiar with, but made, and often giften directly from divinity itself. Even if one could wait for the requisite centuries, one cannot simply take a seed from this very tree and hope to grow another like it. The elven druids who cling onto their old ways in these woods... they've certainly tried to figure out how these work, and their powers stem from similar sources as ours. If any of the native peoples could have done it, it would have been them, and yet they've failed. "It's in the blood, you see. Only kitsune may plant a symbol of the Cherry Blossom Throne and expect it to flourish. For all the elves' knowledge and the power of their wyld trees that still remain, it is simply a matter of their metaphysical nature. Just as the kami of these lands refuse to heed us and need to be converted, so will their calls be rebuffed. If they had enough time, perhaps they might have used that knowledge to develop something of their own, but the same pride that led the druids to reject their own people will prevent them from learning anything useful from their study of our sacred tree. Such a tragedy." |"This sacred tree that we've made our den in protects us from not just the physical, but is also a spiritual bulwark. To be precise, one would not be wrong to say it's a kami in its own right... all of them are very much alive and possessed of some measure of awareness, if not what we would understand as intelligence." For her to have grown this fortress from a sapling alone, she must dote on it very much. Komari looks a little sheepish at that. "Ah... I still remember. The first thing that happened when I returned to this land as an exile was for his divine lordship to press the seed into my hand and instruct me to plant it. So I did. The tree is... it is the only amongst my children who has yet to pass from me so quickly. And as for its relation to us... well, I would like to say it is a symbiotic one. Much of my time that isn't spent dealing with matters of state is devoted to the tree's care, although in recent years Mikoto and Miyuki have proven themselves quite adept at lifting that burden off my shoulders. They can do so much if only they were capable of focusing their attentions for more than a few hours at a time..." |"For all that they expressed interest in the ways of my craft, Carmen and Oxana never understood the fundamentals behind the stewardship of living things, especially the latter. They imagined that I was forcing the sacred tree to grow and twist itself into shapes according to my desires and contrary to its nature, which could be nothing further from the truth. A garden has the touch of artifice to it, yet it works best when it behaves in accord the nature of the things that grow with. Letting it run rampant without guidance produces no useful results, and yet forcing it to be what it is not makes the effort so much more tiresome, if not outright impossible. Simply allowing a river to run the course it really wants to is a lot easier than damming and diverting its flow. "In the end, it did not matter. Once I got wind of what the two of them were up to and what they truly intended, I threw them out from my midst. Carmen I may have regretted a little in doing so, but Oxana... nothing good has come out of that witch and the many so-called daughters she has." [party.has atugia |"You can't blame Carmen for what she was doing," Atugia says sullenly from across the room. "She was just trying to —" "Protect everyone, I know. And in order to do that, she had to live longer than what her body would allow by its nature, which was why she had a particular interest in both the curse I was under and the hunger we foxes suffer as a people. Protect her subjects from Oxana's depredations and worse, in exchange for a small tithe of chi from each one of them. Wholly reasonable." "Then you ain't supposed to speak of her like she's some kind of criminal or somethin'." "I appreciate you speaking up for your mistress, but from all accounts she is beginning to realize that maybe this may not have been the best idea, after all. Outliving everyone and everything you care for takes its toll on the mind... residing alone in a dreary old stone castle with only her faithful long-lived retainers, never showing her face amongst the people she rules for fear of beginning to care for them... at least it is more wisdom than Oxana ever had." ] |"Kazuo has been quite invaluable in making improvements to the den in the last few years. Of course, I have to constantly provide oversight, or else he does tend to go overboard... there's a reason why he's here in the colonies, after all. Still, I daresay that his knowledge of engineering and artifice rivals my own; it's a relief to have someone actually knowledgeable to discuss alterations with before actually trying to implement them on a small scale." Even though you know better, you're still wrapping your mind about a priestess being involved in technology like this. "Back in my homeland, the line between the spiritual and physical is faint and easily crossed, if it is there at all to begin with. You will come to learn the truth of this in time, especially as you get used to your new body, your Eminence. Eventually, it will be second nature to you." ] |[rand |"You've been here for a little while now," Komari says, eyeing you. "What do you think of this place?" It's... strange. Certainly nothing you'd have expected just from looking at it from the outside, where it appears to be nothing more than a tree, even if it's a very big and impressive one. From the inside, though... that's another matter altogether. You certainly wouldn't have expected running water, let alone running warm water inside what by all appearances is a living thing. It reminds you of stories of old Belhar where fountains in the public streets were fed by aqueducts that carried water from miles away, only in a different fashion. "The sacred tree doesn't merely appear to be a living thing, it is a living thing. The resources provided to a people in their native lands affect their outlook and the way they approach matters... while the people of Belhar concerned themselves with fire, stone and metal and their development directed that way, we learned to manipulate plants and other living creatures... mostly plants, though." Your gaze follows Komari's finger as she points at a miniature tree in a porcelain basin on the windowsill, then gestures at the room about her. "As above, so below. The core principles are the same, it is just a matter of scale and complexity. And as for the results... you can compare the den to any of the old ruins lying about and see for yourself. Form follows function." |It's a little hard to believe that a hundred families can live in the den and still have so much room left over for common grounds. You know the tree is large, but you didn't imagine that it would be that large. "Just because these are the colonies doesn't mean we have to live in hovels with dirt floors like the snobs back in the capital imagine we do," Komari replies. "With the struggles people must face in a foreign land inimical to them, the least I can do is to provide beautiful yet simple accommodations for everyone. Living stacked atop each other in cage-like homes without any hint of open space or greenery is not conducive to a healthy spirit or meaningful existence; if the den must by necessity have many families living together, then at least their closeness should be impinge upon their lives. Just because we are on the borders does not mean that we should allow beauty to be stolen from our lives. "Besides, this is the seat of the colonial governor. Wouldn't do to fail to keep up appearances, would it?" |Are all kitsune dens like this? Foxes living in trees? "No, no. By far, no. Back in the Old Country, you would be considered privileged to live in one of these. The Imperial Palace is one, as are the holdings of the twelve Divine Clans... no. Most build as you do, although without the benefit of metal, which is far too precious to be wasted on trivialities like construction. If you were a poor warrior looking for an arch for an entryway, hmm... you would grow two small pines a little way apart and convince them to bend into each other, form a lovely piece to greet those who arrived at your doorstep. Building a wall — letting the plants sink their roots into the mortar and bind it all together ever stronger than it would have been otherwise. Nature causes the works of the Belharan Empire to fall into ruin; when properly stewarded and guided, it strengthens ours." That's... hard to believe. But then again, you're sitting in this very chamber where it's hard to tell where the tree ends and floorboards and beams begin. "You make do with the tools you have and the resources available to you. You shape, and in turn are shaped by your creation. It's quite lovely. Get to return to your point... there are other small colonies of our kind in this land, and they very definitely do not have the protections afforded by a sacred tree." |You've seen the fields that lie on ground level, ensconced between the root of the tree, and are quite impressed with how they're set up. Does everyone stay fed on what's a relatively small plot of land? "It is a fine system, isn't it? We got by well enough before, but my boy Hitoshi has improved things to the point where there's enough surplus to either sell to the natives or send to our people further ahead on the front. He's a good boy, and it shows. Nature does love him so." Ah, ever the doting great-great-grandmother, to have such praise for her descendant. But back to the point... "We don't have much arable land back in the Old Country, and the tanuki are always hungry; getting the most out of the fields while ensuring you don't tax them may not be particularly glamorous, but nevertheless is a respected art. One of the things I tried to do when a permanent colony was established on this side of the ocean was to pick crops that would grow best under the local climate, mostly winter crops that could survive frost. There were a few false starts and lean times when we figured out what would work best, but we got through them in the end. "Things are better now, of course. Having the fields inside of the tree means that the soil is warmer, and we can better control growing conditions with greater precision. I'm content to leave the matter to my boy Hitoshi these days — he's certainly proven himself capable enough." |Is the kitsune den going to get any bigger? It's already impressive as it is — what happens when one wishes to make alterations or renovations, if such things are possible? "I think this is about as far as I would like to take things. Growth is not something that should be undertaken merely for its own sake, and any plan that relies on infinite expansion of anything is bound to fail. Living space for a hundred families is sufficient... there are other dens further ahead closer to the wilderness that could use more hands to help tame their surroundings. "As for alterations... suffice to say that it takes some time and care in order to reshape a living being the way you need to it be and yet is harmonious with its nature. That was something that Evergreen could never quite grasp — or more likely, wilfully refused to do so. I'm afraid I cannot divulge further details, and even if I could even the base concepts would take some time to explain." |Living here must be quite comfortable — the kitsune den is certainly quite luxurious compared to other settlements you've seen in your travels. Running water is but the least of the small wonders you've seen these foxes able to enjoy — indoor plumbing and foxfire lamps to light the branches at night are but a few of the other minor miracles the kitsune have managed to work here. "Why, that's very flattering. But I was around when the empire still stood, and had the chance to see several cities before they were sacked — Belhar certainly knew how to do opulence for its upper crust, and if you travel to Tychris you can still see a pale shadow of what once was. Not that I considered such places beautiful or desirable to live in — quite the opposite — but you might have understood their sense of aesthetics better. "If you ask me, I think the main difference between our peoples is that those on this side of the ocean believe that living in good environments with scents, sights and sounds that are pleasing and uplift the spirit is a matter that comes after having a warm place to sleep and a full belly. Placing survival before other more intangible needs is understandable, but it is not our way. Even the lowest of the low can appreciate the warmth and light of a pleasant sunrise." ] ]
rows.translation: [pc.ra kitsune |既然你已经成为我们的一员了，我可以再告诉你一些关于这个藏身处的事情…… 你们都洗耳恭听——任何能够帮助你们更好地了解自己在整个体系中所扮演的角色和位置的信息，我都愿意分享。 [rand |这样的神圣树木……它们不仅仅是我们的居所。每一棵树都象征着一代人向下一代人传递的辛勤努力与传承；它们不属于任何人，而是需要被人们共同守护的。这一代人从上一代人手中接过这些树木，就有责任将它们留给未来的后代；它们不能被我们随意处置，就如同它们是我们的私有财产一样。这种思维方式可以应用到所有事情上……或许我是唯一一只有幸亲眼见证它从一颗种子成长为一株小树，最终变成如今这个样子的狐狸。 需要二十年的时间，这些樱花树才能长得足够大，足以让一个家庭舒适地居住在其中；再需要一百年的时间，它们才会变成如今这样的模样。对于那些像北方精灵那样过着长达数千年的自然生活的人来说，这样的时间跨度或许微不足道，正因如此，他们的德鲁伊与自己所守护的野生树木之间也存在着不同的关系。然而，一旦这些神圣的樱花树扎根生长，它们不仅能抵御那些普通的世俗力量，更重要的是，还能抵御超自然的力量。这一点至关重要，因为殖民斗争的本质并不在于与那些有血有肉的居民打交道，而在于让这片土地本身愿意接纳我们。北方精灵早已放弃了这些森林，转而前往更北方的冰川地带，但这片土地依然记得他们曾经的存在，因此迟迟不愿放弃这些地方。" |这些神圣的樱花树……它们的生长方式与你所熟知的完全不同，它们是神明亲自创造出来的，往往还会作为礼物直接赐予人类。即使有人能够等待上几个世纪，也无法仅仅取下这棵树的种子，就期望培育出另一棵一模一样的树来。那些在这些森林中依然固守着古老传统的精灵德鲁伊……他们肯定尝试过弄清楚这些力量的运作原理，他们的能力与我们来源相同。如果这些土著民族中有人能够做到这一点，那肯定会是他们，然而他们还是失败了。 这其实是与生俱来的能力，你明白吗？只有狐族才能种植樱花王座的象征，并让它真正茁壮成长。尽管精灵们拥有丰富的知识，他们的野树也依然拥有强大的力量，但这一切其实都源于他们的超自然本质。就像神明这些地方的人们拒绝听从我们的教导，必须被改变才行，否则他们的请求也会被驳回。如果他们有足够的时间，或许可以利用这些知识来发展属于自己的东西，但正是那种让德鲁伊们拒绝自己人民的傲慢，使他们无法从对我们神圣之树的研究中学习到任何有用的东西。真是太悲剧了。 |这棵我们将其作为栖息之地的神圣树木，不仅能够保护我们免受身体上的伤害，更是我们的精神支柱。确切地说，称它本身就是一位神明也不为过……它们全都活着，也具备一定程度的意识，尽管这种意识可能并非我们所理解的那种智能。 她能够仅凭一棵幼苗就培育出这样的堡垒，想必对她来说，这棵树意味着无比珍贵的意义。 听到这里，小鹤显得有些害羞。啊……我仍然记得。当我以流放者的身份回到这片土地时，第一件发生的事就是，他的神圣主君将那颗种子交到我的手中，命令我将其种下。于是我就照做了。那棵树……它是我的所有后代中，唯一一颗还没有那么快就从我身边消失的。至于它与我们之间的关系……嗯，我想说这是一种共生关系。在我那些没有用于处理国家事务的时间里，有很大一部分都是用来照料这棵树的，不过近年来，美琴和美雪已经证明她们完全有能力帮我分担这份责任。如果他们能够一次集中注意力几个小时以上，那么他们就能完成很多事情了…… |尽管卡门和奥克萨娜表现出对我这种创作方式的兴趣，但她们从未真正理解过照料生物的基本原理，尤其是奥克萨娜。她们以为我是在强迫那棵神圣的树木按照我的意愿生长、扭曲成我所希望的形状，从而违背了它的自然规律，而事实却完全相反。花园虽然带有人为设计的痕迹，但只有当它的布局符合其中生长的植物的自然规律时，才能达到最佳效果。如果不加引导，任其自由生长，根本无法获得任何有用的结果；而强行让它违背自身的生长规律，只会让这种努力变得徒劳无功，甚至根本无法实现。只需让河流按照它自然的流向流淌即可。真的想要做到某件事，往往比强行改变它的发展方向要容易得多。 最终，这其实并不重要。当我了解到他们俩的真正意图后，我就将他们赶出了我的生活。对于卡门，我或许会为此感到有些后悔，但奥克萨娜……那个女巫以及她那些所谓的‘女儿们’，从来就没有带来过任何好事。 [party.has atugia |对于卡门所做的那些事，你不能责怪她。阿图吉娅从房间的另一头闷闷不乐地说道。她只是想…… 保护每一个人，我明白。而为了做到这一点，她必须活得比她的身体本身所能承受的时间更长，因此她对我所承受的诅咒，以及我们狐狸一族所面临的困境，格外关注。保护她的子民免受奥克萨娜的侵害，甚至更严重的威胁——作为交换，她只要求我们缴纳一小部分贡品罢了。气他们每个人都是这样做的。完全合情合理。 那你就不应该把她说得好像她是什么罪犯之类的。 我很感谢你为你的女主人挺身而出，但据种种迹象来看，她似乎也开始意识到，这个决定或许并不是最好的选择。活得比所有你关心的人和事都要久，这种经历会对人的心理造成很大的负担……独自居住在一座阴森古老的石堡里，只有那些忠心耿耿、寿命悠长的仆从陪伴在侧；从不出现在她统治的人民中间，生怕因此开始关心他们……至少，这种做法比奥克萨娜以往的所作所为要明智得多。 ] |在过去的几年里，一夫在改进那个基地方面发挥了极其重要的作用。当然，我必须不断地对他进行监督，否则他确实会有些做得过火……毕竟，他之所以会被派到这些殖民地来，也是有一定原因的。不过，我敢说，他在工程技术和制造工艺方面的知识简直可以与我的水平相媲美；在真正尝试小规模实施这些改进之前，能够有这样一个真正懂行的人与我们一起讨论，实在是件令人欣慰的事情。 尽管你心里很清楚，但还是忍不住去想，为什么一位女祭司会参与到这样的科技领域中来。 在我的旧国，精神与物质之间的界限本来就很模糊，甚至根本不存在这样的界限。随着您逐渐适应自己的新身体，您终会明白这个道理的，尊贵的阁下。最终，这会成为您的本能。 ] |[rand |你在这里已经待了一段时间了。麻里盯着你说道。你觉得这个地方怎么样？ 这……真是奇怪。从外表看，它确实只是一棵树，而且是一棵非常高大、令人印象深刻的树，因此你绝对不会想到里面会有流动的水，更不用说还有其他设施了。不过，从里面看的话……那就完全是另一回事了。温暖在那些看似有生命的物体内部，存在着水。这让人联想到关于古老贝尔哈的故事——在那些公共街道上的喷泉，都是由从数英里外引来的水道供应水量的，只不过这里的运作方式有所不同罢了。 那棵神圣的树，看起来不仅仅是一株有生命的植物，它是一个有生命的存在。人们在其故乡所获得的资源会影响他们的观念以及他们处理各种事务的方式……而贝尔哈尔的人民专注于火、石与金属的研究，他们的发展方向也因此而确定；我们则学会了如何操控植物以及其他生物……不过，主要是植物而已。你的目光跟随麻里的手指——她指向窗台上瓷盆里那棵微型树木，然后又环顾了一下周围的房间。上如是，下亦如是。核心原则始终不变，只不过规模和复杂程度会有所不同而已。至于结果……你可以将这个洞穴与周围那些古老的遗迹进行比较，亲自看看就知道了。形式总是服务于功能的。 |很难相信，一百户家庭能够居住在那个洞穴里，而且还能留下这么多空间作为公共区域。你知道那棵树很大，但你应该没有想到它会这么大。那个大的。 仅仅因为这些是殖民地，并不意味着我们就必须像那些住在首都的势利小人一样，住在地面满是灰尘的简陋小屋里。麻里回应道。考虑到人们在异国他乡必然会面临种种困境，我至少应该为大家提供美观而舒适的居住环境。如果人们不得不挤在那些像笼子一样的房子里生活，周围没有任何开阔的空间或绿意，那么这样的环境肯定不利于保持健康的心态或拥有有意义的生活。如果确实有很多家庭不得不共同居住在一个空间里，那么至少这种紧密的生活环境应该能为他们的生活带来一些积极的影响。仅仅因为我们地处边境，并不意味着我们就应该让美好的事物从我们的生活中被夺走。 此外，这个是殖民地总督的官邸。毕竟，维持表面的体面是必不可少的，不是吗？ |所有的狐妖巢穴都是这样的吗？狐狸都住在树上吗？ 不，不。绝对不是这样。在老家，能够住在这样的房子里就已经是莫大的荣幸了。皇宫就是这样的，十二个神族的宅邸也都是……不，大多数人的房子都是像你这样建造的，只不过他们没有金属这种资源，因为金属太珍贵了，不可能被浪费在建造房子这种小事上。如果你是一名穷苦的战士，需要为入口处制作一根拱门，嗯……你可以种两棵相隔一定距离的小松树，然后让它们互相弯曲，从而形成一道美丽的拱门，用来迎接那些来到你家门口的人。建造一堵墙——让植物将根系深入到灰浆之中，从而使整个结构变得更加坚固。大自然往往会破坏贝尔哈兰帝国的建筑；而如果能够正确地利用和引导大自然的力量，它反而会增强我们的建筑。" 这……真的很难相信。不过话说回来，你现在就坐在这个房间里，根本分不清哪里是树干，哪里是地板或横梁。 你只能利用手头现有的工具和资源来创造事物，同时，这些创造物也会反过来影响你。这种过程其实相当奇妙。回到正题……在这片土地上，还有其他一些我们同类建立的小型聚居地，而它们显然没有那棵神圣树木所提供的保护。 |你们应该已经看到了那些位于地面上的田地，它们被树木的根部环绕着，这样的布局确实让人印象深刻。那么，在这么一块相对较小的土地上，大家是否都能获得足够的食物呢？ 这确实是个不错的系统，不是吗？以前我们也能应付得来，但我的儿子Hitoshi把这套系统改进得非常好，现在我们甚至有剩余的产品，既可以卖给当地人，也可以送给前线那些需要支援的同胞。他真是个好孩子，这些成果就是最好的证明。大自然确实偏爱他啊。 啊，这位充满爱心的曾曾祖母，竟然对自己的后代给予了如此高的评价。不过，还是回到正题吧…… 在故乡，我们的可耕地并不多，而且那些貉总是饿着肚子；如何在保证不破坏农田生态环境的前提下最大限度地利用这些土地，虽然这项工作并不显得多么光彩夺目，但却是一门备受重视的技艺。当在这片海洋的另一边建立了永久性的殖民地之后，我尝试做的事情之一就是选择那些能够在当地气候条件下生长得最好的作物，主要是那些能够耐受霜冻的冬季作物。在确定哪些作物最适合当地环境的过程中，我们遇到了一些挫折和困难，但最终还是克服了它们。 现在情况当然好多了。将田地设置在树丛内部，可以让土壤保持更温暖的状态，我们也能够更精确地控制种植条件。这些日子，我把这件事交给了我的儿子Hitoshi来处理——他确实证明了自己有能力胜任这项工作。 |那只狐狸的巢穴还会再变大吗？它现在的规模已经相当可观了——如果想要对它进行改造或修缮，这样的事情是否可行呢？会发生什么呢？ 我想，我已经做到我想做的最大限度了。发展并不应该仅仅为了发展本身而进行，任何依赖无限制扩张的计划都注定会失败。为一百户家庭提供居住空间已经足够了……在更远的地方，靠近荒野的地方，还有其他的栖息地需要更多人帮忙来改善它们的环境。 至于这些修改……可以说，要想将一个生物重塑成你所需要的样子，同时又让它保持与自身本性的和谐，这确实需要花费一定的时间和精力。而这一点，常青女士始终无法真正理解——或者更确切地说，她是故意拒绝去理解的。恐怕我无法透露更多细节了，即便能说，这些基本概念也需要花一些时间来解释才行。 |住在这里肯定非常舒适——与你在旅途中见过的其他定居点相比，这只狐狸的巢穴确实相当豪华。自来水仅仅是这些狐狸能够享受的诸多便利中最为基础的一项；室内管道设施以及用来在夜晚照亮树枝的狐火灯，也只是这些狐狸在这里创造出来的诸多小奇迹中的一小部分而已。 哎呀，这么说真是太抬举我了。不过我在帝国还强大的时候就在那里生活过，也有机会看到好几座城市在被摧毁之前的样子——贝尔哈尔确实很懂得如何为上层阶级营造奢华的环境。如果你去蒂克里斯，仍然能看到那些曾经辉煌景象的淡淡痕迹。不过我并不认为那种地方很美，也不觉得适合居住……恰恰相反，但你或许能更好地理解他们的审美观念。 在我看来，我们两个民族之间的主要区别在于：生活在海洋这一边的人民认为，拥有令人愉悦、能够振奋精神的美好环境——包括那些美好的气味、景象和声音——才是在确保有温暖的住所和充实的饮食之后才应该追求的东西。将生存置于其他更为抽象的需求之前，这种做法是可以理解的，但这并不是我们的方式。即便是社会中最底层的人，也能感受到美好日出带来的温暖与光明。 ] ]
rows.raw: ' [pc.ra kitsune |"Now that you're one of us, I'm able to tell you a few more things about the den..." You're all ears — anything to help you understand more about your new role and station in the scheme of things. [rand |"Such sacred trees... they are not just places for us to live in. Each one represents the effort of one generation to the other; they are not owned, but stewarded. One generation receives it from the previous, and it is to be kept for the generation who will come after; it is not something that you can do with as you wish as if it were your property. Such a mindset can be extended to all things... I may be the sole kitsune who has had the fortune of being able to witness the growth of one from seed to sapling to what it is today. "Twenty years for it to grow large enough to accommodate a single family comfortably. A hundred for it to resemble that which you see today. Perhaps such a timespan is insignificant to those who live natural lives of millennia like the boreal elves, which is why their druids have different relationships with their own wyld trees, but once rooted, these sacred cherry blossom trees not only provide a bulwark against mere mundane forces, but more importantly, the supernatural. That is vitally important, because the colonial struggle is primarily not one of dealing with the flesh-and-blood inhabitants, but convincing the land itself to turn to us. The boreal elves have long since abandoned these woods in favor of the glaciers further north, but the land remembers their touch and is reluctant to move on." |"These sacred cherry blossom trees... they are not grown in the sense you would be familiar with, but made, and often giften directly from divinity itself. Even if one could wait for the requisite centuries, one cannot simply take a seed from this very tree and hope to grow another like it. The elven druids who cling onto their old ways in these woods... they've certainly tried to figure out how these work, and their powers stem from similar sources as ours. If any of the native peoples could have done it, it would have been them, and yet they've failed. "It's in the blood, you see. Only kitsune may plant a symbol of the Cherry Blossom Throne and expect it to flourish. For all the elves' knowledge and the power of their wyld trees that still remain, it is simply a matter of their metaphysical nature. Just as the kami of these lands refuse to heed us and need to be converted, so will their calls be rebuffed. If they had enough time, perhaps they might have used that knowledge to develop something of their own, but the same pride that led the druids to reject their own people will prevent them from learning anything useful from their study of our sacred tree. Such a tragedy." |"This sacred tree that we've made our den in protects us from not just the physical, but is also a spiritual bulwark. To be precise, one would not be wrong to say it's a kami in its own right... all of them are very much alive and possessed of some measure of awareness, if not what we would understand as intelligence." For her to have grown this fortress from a sapling alone, she must dote on it very much. Komari looks a little sheepish at that. "Ah... I still remember. The first thing that happened when I returned to this land as an exile was for his divine lordship to press the seed into my hand and instruct me to plant it. So I did. The tree is... it is the only amongst my children who has yet to pass from me so quickly. And as for its relation to us... well, I would like to say it is a symbiotic one. Much of my time that isn't spent dealing with matters of state is devoted to the tree's care, although in recent years Mikoto and Miyuki have proven themselves quite adept at lifting that burden off my shoulders. They can do so much if only they were capable of focusing their attentions for more than a few hours at a time..." |"For all that they expressed interest in the ways of my craft, Carmen and Oxana never understood the fundamentals behind the stewardship of living things, especially the latter. They imagined that I was forcing the sacred tree to grow and twist itself into shapes according to my desires and contrary to its nature, which could be nothing further from the truth. A garden has the touch of artifice to it, yet it works best when it behaves in accord the nature of the things that grow with. Letting it run rampant without guidance produces no useful results, and yet forcing it to be what it is not makes the effort so much more tiresome, if not outright impossible. Simply allowing a river to run the course it really wants to is a lot easier than damming and diverting its flow. "In the end, it did not matter. Once I got wind of what the two of them were up to and what they truly intended, I threw them out from my midst. Carmen I may have regretted a little in doing so, but Oxana... nothing good has come out of that witch and the many so-called daughters she has." [party.has atugia |"You can't blame Carmen for what she was doing," Atugia says sullenly from across the room. "She was just trying to —" "Protect everyone, I know. And in order to do that, she had to live longer than what her body would allow by its nature, which was why she had a particular interest in both the curse I was under and the hunger we foxes suffer as a people. Protect her subjects from Oxana's depredations and worse, in exchange for a small tithe of chi from each one of them. Wholly reasonable." "Then you ain't supposed to speak of her like she's some kind of criminal or somethin'." "I appreciate you speaking up for your mistress, but from all accounts she is beginning to realize that maybe this may not have been the best idea, after all. Outliving everyone and everything you care for takes its toll on the mind... residing alone in a dreary old stone castle with only her faithful long-lived retainers, never showing her face amongst the people she rules for fear of beginning to care for them... at least it is more wisdom than Oxana ever had." ] |"Kazuo has been quite invaluable in making improvements to the den in the last few years. Of course, I have to constantly provide oversight, or else he does tend to go overboard... there's a reason why he's here in the colonies, after all. Still, I daresay that his knowledge of engineering and artifice rivals my own; it's a relief to have someone actually knowledgeable to discuss alterations with before actually trying to implement them on a small scale." Even though you know better, you're still wrapping your mind about a priestess being involved in technology like this. "Back in my homeland, the line between the spiritual and physical is faint and easily crossed, if it is there at all to begin with. You will come to learn the truth of this in time, especially as you get used to your new body, your Eminence. Eventually, it will be second nature to you." ] |[rand |"You've been here for a little while now," Komari says, eyeing you. "What do you think of this place?" It's... strange. Certainly nothing you'd have expected just from looking at it from the outside, where it appears to be nothing more than a tree, even if it's a very big and impressive one. From the inside, though... that's another matter altogether. You certainly wouldn't have expected running water, let alone running warm water inside what by all appearances is a living thing. It reminds you of stories of old Belhar where fountains in the public streets were fed by aqueducts that carried water from miles away, only in a different fashion. "The sacred tree doesn't merely appear to be a living thing, it is a living thing. The resources provided to a people in their native lands affect their outlook and the way they approach matters... while the people of Belhar concerned themselves with fire, stone and metal and their development directed that way, we learned to manipulate plants and other living creatures... mostly plants, though." Your gaze follows Komari's finger as she points at a miniature tree in a porcelain basin on the windowsill, then gestures at the room about her. "As above, so below. The core principles are the same, it is just a matter of scale and complexity. And as for the results... you can compare the den to any of the old ruins lying about and see for yourself. Form follows function." |It's a little hard to believe that a hundred families can live in the den and still have so much room left over for common grounds. You know the tree is large, but you didn't imagine that it would be that large. "Just because these are the colonies doesn't mean we have to live in hovels with dirt floors like the snobs back in the capital imagine we do," Komari replies. "With the struggles people must face in a foreign land inimical to them, the least I can do is to provide beautiful yet simple accommodations for everyone. Living stacked atop each other in cage-like homes without any hint of open space or greenery is not conducive to a healthy spirit or meaningful existence; if the den must by necessity have many families living together, then at least their closeness should be impinge upon their lives. Just because we are on the borders does not mean that we should allow beauty to be stolen from our lives. "Besides, this is the seat of the colonial governor. Wouldn't do to fail to keep up appearances, would it?" |Are all kitsune dens like this? Foxes living in trees? "No, no. By far, no. Back in the Old Country, you would be considered privileged to live in one of these. The Imperial Palace is one, as are the holdings of the twelve Divine Clans... no. Most build as you do, although without the benefit of metal, which is far too precious to be wasted on trivialities like construction. If you were a poor warrior looking for an arch for an entryway, hmm... you would grow two small pines a little way apart and convince them to bend into each other, form a lovely piece to greet those who arrived at your doorstep. Building a wall — letting the plants sink their roots into the mortar and bind it all together ever stronger than it would have been otherwise. Nature causes the works of the Belharan Empire to fall into ruin; when properly stewarded and guided, it strengthens ours." That's... hard to believe. But then again, you're sitting in this very chamber where it's hard to tell where the tree ends and floorboards and beams begin. "You make do with the tools you have and the resources available to you. You shape, and in turn are shaped by your creation. It's quite lovely. Get to return to your point... there are other small colonies of our kind in this land, and they very definitely do not have the protections afforded by a sacred tree." |You've seen the fields that lie on ground level, ensconced between the root of the tree, and are quite impressed with how they're set up. Does everyone stay fed on what's a relatively small plot of land? "It is a fine system, isn't it? We got by well enough before, but my boy Hitoshi has improved things to the point where there's enough surplus to either sell to the natives or send to our people further ahead on the front. He's a good boy, and it shows. Nature does love him so." Ah, ever the doting great-great-grandmother, to have such praise for her descendant. But back to the point... "We don't have much arable land back in the Old Country, and the tanuki are always hungry; getting the most out of the fields while ensuring you don't tax them may not be particularly glamorous, but nevertheless is a respected art. One of the things I tried to do when a permanent colony was established on this side of the ocean was to pick crops that would grow best under the local climate, mostly winter crops that could survive frost. There were a few false starts and lean times when we figured out what would work best, but we got through them in the end. "Things are better now, of course. Having the fields inside of the tree means that the soil is warmer, and we can better control growing conditions with greater precision. I'm content to leave the matter to my boy Hitoshi these days — he's certainly proven himself capable enough." |Is the kitsune den going to get any bigger? It's already impressive as it is — what happens when one wishes to make alterations or renovations, if such things are possible? "I think this is about as far as I would like to take things. Growth is not something that should be undertaken merely for its own sake, and any plan that relies on infinite expansion of anything is bound to fail. Living space for a hundred families is sufficient... there are other dens further ahead closer to the wilderness that could use more hands to help tame their surroundings. "As for alterations... suffice to say that it takes some time and care in order to reshape a living being the way you need to it be and yet is harmonious with its nature. That was something that Evergreen could never quite grasp — or more likely, wilfully refused to do so. I'm afraid I cannot divulge further details, and even if I could even the base concepts would take some time to explain." |Living here must be quite comfortable — the kitsune den is certainly quite luxurious compared to other settlements you've seen in your travels. Running water is but the least of the small wonders you've seen these foxes able to enjoy — indoor plumbing and foxfire lamps to light the branches at night are but a few of the other minor miracles the kitsune have managed to work here. "Why, that's very flattering. But I was around when the empire still stood, and had the chance to see several cities before they were sacked — Belhar certainly knew how to do opulence for its upper crust, and if you travel to Tychris you can still see a pale shadow of what once was. Not that I considered such places beautiful or desirable to live in — quite the opposite — but you might have understood their sense of aesthetics better. "If you ask me, I think the main difference between our peoples is that those on this side of the ocean believe that living in good environments with scents, sights and sounds that are pleasing and uplift the spirit is a matter that comes after having a warm place to sleep and a full belly. Placing survival before other more intangible needs is understandable, but it is not our way. Even the lowest of the low can appreciate the warmth and light of a pleasant sunrise." ] ] '
