rows.original: [var0 |[kiyoko.isFree |[rand |"Truth be told, I'm a little concerned about Lady Otomo living back in her old home. While it's true that more than two hundred years have passed and she's no doubt patched the oversight in the defenses that allowed the wraiths to come in and attack in the first place, I still can't bring myself to have the peace of mind she exhibits about the whole matter. Yet getting that point across without being argumentative or contentious is a struggle. Ah..." If it's for her safety, you're sure that Kiyoko will understand. "She assured me that everything is fine and that she'll be working with his divine lordship himself to ensure that nothing of the sort ever happens again. And even so, I can't shake off the feeling of unease — it may have happened more than two centuries ago, and yet when the Lady Otomo and her daughter showed me their revitalised home all I could see were the bodies." You try to prod Komari for more on the subject, but the den matron's clammed up and refuses to say another word on the matter. Given what happened and what's happened to her as a result of it, you're not surprised that merely thinking of Kiyoko's home reopens old wounds in her psyche. However, if it comes down to it, Komari's thoughts on keeping both your fox-wife and [kiyoko.numKits 1 |daughter |children ] safe could be invaluable. Maybe another time... |"Everyone's very excited about the establishment of a new den on the frontier — it's been a while since such has happened. For obvious reasons, we kitsune are quite careful about where we choose to put down roots. This goes doubly so because of Lady Otomo being who she is — word's already buzzing about and people want to have a go at earning favor with a den mother by helping with the reconstruction and restoration of her home." The sounds a bit counterintuitive, you have to say. The reason Keros didn't restore everything is because he wanted Kiyoko and her own to earn anything beyond a subsistence level on their own. "I suppose galvanising others to aid you with your encompassing charisma counts, doesn't it?" Komari replies with a thin smile. "That daughter of yours... [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |she doesn't say much, but people have noticed how hard she works around here and feel like they have to give something back. It's not much, but the people who do have the conscience to repay her put in their all. That, and they respect Hitoshi, and since they've become an item you can imagine what happened. |oh, she's a vixen with a magnetic personality, all right. All she has to do is smile, and everyone's falling over themselves in their rush to help her. Put up beams and walls? Roofing? Treat wood? ] Suffice to say that we foxes are just doing what we've always done out of necessity — looking out for each other. It's that way back in the Old Country, too; everyone gets together to re-thatch roofs knowing full well that when the time rolls around in the year, they'll be the beneficiaries of the village's efforts. It all works out." [party.has kiyoko | "It does indeed," your fox-wife adds. "Putting your time into other trustworthy people is one of the most important things you can do. Of course, cultivating a culture of trust necessitates harsh punishments for those who would betray that trust... everything has its price." ] |"When she was younger, the Lady Otomo lived in a palace grown into a sacred tree much like this one, only far grander in scope. You could wander the halls for days and not cover the entirety of the place. When I first arrived with my parents as a girl, I got lost with ease and had to be retrieved by the palace guard — that was rather shameful." [party.has kiyoko |Kiyoko chances a thin smile. "I remember that. Your parents and mine chastised you soundly for wandering off, but I forgave you. They chastised me for that, too, saying that leniency was unbecoming of someone who would hold high office, that simply letting off wrongdoers like that would cast their shame unto me." "..." |And now she's living in a serviceable, if homely shrine. No matter how you cut it, that's quite the drop in her standard of living. "She knew she would get as much when she volunteered to lead the colonial effort in this new land across the ocean. Somehow, I doubt that my liege cares very much for these things past a certain point. Have you ever noticed that she wears the same clothes day in, day out? She has ten or more or the exact same garments." ] Right. Everyone's working hard to get the place not just restored, but made even better than what it was before. While your fox-wife may not care overly much for comfort, let alone luxury, you owe it to her to at least try and give her the kind of ease she used to have back on the Astral Plane, even if you can't manage a palace. "Well, we all have a lot of work in front of us, I'm sure," Komari replies. "I and mine are already aiding the Lady Otomo as much as we're able to... I'm sure that if you conferred with her or your daughter, they'll certainly have things for you to do, if you're that earnest." |"Now that Lady Otomo is back, everyone's a little on edge. Someone of her station being in the vicinity, even if she's not living in the den proper, sets minds to worrying and wondering, you know? Generally in our history, events become interesting when someone of great import like her deigns to draw near and notice you... and usually not for the better. But with [silly |Myobu-sama |Lady Otomo ], there's really nothing to fear." [party.has kiyoko |"Oh dear." Raising two fingers to pull up the corners of her lips in a faux smile, your fox-wife practically oozes droll amusement from her person. "Is it perhaps something with my face, Komari? I would certainly not want to give unease to anyone unless they deserved it." ] As far as you understand these things, Kiyoko is near, if not at the very top of the social hierarchy of the Marches' kitsune, isn't she? You're sure that once everyone's appraised of her friendly and non-interventionist attitude towards what has traditionally been Komari's domain, they'll realize quickly that things are still business as usual and settle down just nicely." "Mm. We have a saying, 'Heaven is high and the Emperor is far away.' That works out just well until the Emperor decides to tour the provinces, and Heaven itself decides to accompany his descendant for the ride because he thinks it would be amusing. It'll blow over, as you say... but in the meantime, I'm not entirely convinced that the surfeit of laxity is altogether a bad thing in itself. Everyone wants to prove their worth to the den mother and her daughter... so don't mind if I enjoy the show for a bit." |"There's some hope amongst the people here that now that we have a den mother living in the colonies with us, we might actually get some proper political representation across the ocean," Komari begins. "I don't want to be a wet blanket, but... this is not likely to happen." Hmm. Why not? "Lady Otomo is not formally one any more, not in the political sense. Her sister's line succeeded her after her... ah, unfortunate departure, and for her to try and claim her old political position — if she even wants it now — is not out of the question were she to truly challenge her claim, but it would cause severe political upheaval. As far as things on the other side of the ocean would go, it's largely business as usual. Not that it's necessarily a bad thing, but she's not going to be able to wield the kind of political influence they're hoping she'll be able to. They're basically setting themselves up for a letdown, and it hurts my heart to see it." In the physical and metaphysical sense, though... "Oh, that's something you've experienced for yourself." Indeed. ] |[rand |"Many of our interactions with other peoples in our homeland are governed not just by law, but by ancient customs that stretch back generations; these are necessary not just because of our natures, but also of other's natural inclinations. How to approach the other, what to expect, the recourse that a wronged party can take for infringement, and so forth. Obtaining what we need is much less fraught with tension than it is over here in the colonies." You understand. The kitsune are not a people who have much tolerance for uncertainty, and neither do the locals of the Marches for all the dangers the land poses. Recent events have not made this any better. "Five generations is too short a time in which to form raw bonds from not just nothing, but a negative impression to begin with. The mercenaries Oxana used to — well, still sends — are easily convinced that we are bloodthirsty monsters. The best deceptions have a grain of truth to them to make them all the more plausible and convincing. "My personal hope in allowing you [party.som | |and your companion |and your companions ]entry here is that you'll bring your experiences back to your people and tell them what you honestly feel about us and the truth of your interactions with us foxes. In that case... please interact as freely as you'd like with the denizens of this den in goodwill." |"Are you settling in here well?" As best as you can be, you suppose. Everything is so... alien, for lack of a better word to put it; the novelty will fade with time as you grow used to the den and its environs, but for now you think you'll enjoy it as best as you can, while it lasts. "Well, just remember that it goes both ways — the locals here may very well find you interesting as well. [pc.ra kitsune |Having a divine champion here on the frontier where one would be most needed makes the most sense, but even so they are not sure how to best approach you given your origins, your Eminence. Please forgive any reticence on their part. |If nothing else, an outsider walking around here openly is something unprecedented, so pardon any curious — or fearful — stares you may garner. ] You're sure your magnanimity can extend as to overlook a few curious stares. |"I'm sure you've already realized that we have little use for Belharan coin here in the den," Komari begins. "Well, any coin for that matter. There is simply not very much to buy. No settlement would allow any of us in to do commerce openly, nor would any merchant worth their salt attempt to do business with bloodthirsty monsters liable to suck out your soul through your nose or whatever it is the natives believe about us. Little Kohaku is the only kitsune around the den whom which your money will be good for anything." You can understand your electrum being of limited use around these parts; Evergreen herself is in a bit of a similar situation to boot. What what about amongst themselves, or exports and imports to the Old Country? Don't those warrant some form of whatever currency foxes and 'nuki use on the other side of the ocean? "Locally, the den is small enough for everyone to be treated as one big family. People requisition what they want from Kohaku, and she handles all commerce going through the portal. Nakano keeps some of his money because he enjoys taking a half-day to visit relatives across the ocean when he can, [kinu.isHime |more now that he's got your daughter in tow |but that's for his personal use, and he certainly doesn't spend it here in the colonies ]. It's a little strange, but it works because we trust each other. It's not perfect, but everyone knows everyone else well enough to quickly suss out the untrustworthy and skiving. It wouldn't work on a larger scale, but..." You're seeing where this is going. "It probably wouldn't work for another people altogether, for what it's worth. Being bloodthirsty monsters has a way of getting people to stick with each other. Either way, if you have any business, just bring it up with our little golden fluffball." |"Are you having trouble speaking to anyone? [pc.ra kitsune |His divine lordship may have changed your appearance and nature, but speaking our native language... well, it's certainly not beyond his ability to grant you that kind of knowledge, but knowing him, he probably wanted the amusement of watching you struggle at learning it |We mostly speak our own native language amongst ourselves, although the younger and more distantly removed generations are growing increasingly familiar with Belharan. It's been an interesting observation across the decades, if nothing else ]." No, no. Everyone's been very polite and accommodating in making themselves understood when you're around. You're a guest here, and any conversation not in Belharan is probably one you shouldn't be snooping in on anyway. "Someday when you have the time, I'll have to at least try to teach you our language. Spoken is achievable for most non-native speakers, if they put in the effort to tease apart casual, respectful, formal and humble language. The written word, though... pictograms are what trip up most would-be enthusiasts. His divine lordship likes to joke that we designed our language, spoken and written alike, to keep out foreigners in accordance with our historical policy of isolationism; it's hard to rebut that, especially since he was there when it all got started." Hm. "[pc.ra kitsune |Even so, your Eminence, it wouldn't do for the divine champion of Keros himself to be ignorant of the language, eh |Even so, I'm sure you're willing to give it a go, aren't you ]?" You'll give some thought to it when this mess with the demons is all sorted out. |"The kids who left the door open on their way out the last time have been properly chastised for their inattentiveness in placing everyone in potential danger. I'm sure that no one else is going to be walking right on into the den like you did for a good long while now." Guess you were just lucky, eh? "Some might say fated. Peace and lack of consequences breeds complacency and laxity; it's been an excruciating and tiresome two and a half centuries to get the den's immediate surroundings as safe as they are, and the end result is that everyone forgets all the efforts that made the place as relatively peaceful as it is. Young people these days!" Well, given what Kas is sparking around the Marches, she'd better tighten up security about these parts — and after a few run-ins with her minions, you're sure these young folks will see the wisdom of her words soon enough. |"Evergreen put up a wall of thorns about the entrance to the Frostwood, you say? Yes, I knew about it. No, I didn't care, because it's all the better for me and mine and if she's the one expending the effort keeping it maintained, I don't see why I should care. That hussy thinks that she's the one keeping the terrors of the Frostwood out; well, from my perspective the wall's keeping her and hers from getting into mischief about these parts. Well, less mischief than they normally do." ] ] |[rand |I know this shouldn't need to be said, but do talk to your daughter some more whenever you can. [kinu.isInari |While she prefers to be alone most of the time, that doesn't mean that she doesn't want to reach out, or that you wouldn't be welcome. Kinu may be quite stubborn, but even rocks can change their shape over time if you keep on chipping away quietly at them. |She may keep on a pleasant face so much of the time, but that is partially because the people are so sensitive to the moods of their beloved princess. She knows that if she allows herself to be upset, they will be too; it is part and parcel of her job. Yet at the same time, the brave face does not necessarily mean that she is truly well. She is quite adept at hiding her emotions, after all. ]" Yeah, you will, especially in the wake of all that has happened. "You can tell that it troubles her — not just the errors she made in the heat of the moment, the sting of failure from being defeated by the invaders, and the loss of much of what has been built since the den was resettled. What she needs, perhaps, is someone who is not from her root culture to speak with her, someone who does not necessarily have the same notions of failure and shame that we do and she feels she can open up to without necessarily being judged for her failure. She is rather too hard on herself..." Such is the fate of the overachieving daughter who faces her first true failure that she cannot explain or rationalise away to herself. Komari closes her eyes and leans back in her seat. "Harsh, but accurate. Such is her fate." |"While I know much of the talk regarding the attempt on your family's life has been centered about your daughter, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]I would caution you to be careful as well. By her own recounting of the events, your firstborn daughter [kiyoko.numKits 2 3 |and her sister |and other children ]were attacked because those rogues neither dared get to you or the High Lady Otomo directly; they deliberately chose a moment when the both of you would not be at home to strike. Now that they have met with partial success, they will grow more bold and desperate alike." Does she mean that these people, whoever they are, may be planning an attempt on you or Kiyoko next? "I cannot say for sure; there is too much conjecture to be certain, and probably some misdirection in the mix. We ourselves have noted some disappearances in the outlying camps on the border in the last few months, but we always thought... well, some people come to the colonies to vanish." Vanish? "To hide, to let themselves loose, and sometimes, to just give up and die far away from home where their passing will not bring further shame to their clan name. It has been this way for years; some who are sentenced to banishment to the colonies simply wander out into the wilderness and don't return, or meet unfortunate ends. This land is a cold, hard mistress. But now... we may have a more sinister explanation for the recent spate of disappearances." She doesn't say... "I urge you once more, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, please be careful. You have declared where your allegiances lie in the deepest and most profound fashion possible |please be careful. You have lain with and sired children by what they deem a demoness ]; no doubt these people regard you as a traitor to your own kin. Beyond the dens' immediate environs, I cannot guarantee your safety." If you were looking to be safe, you wouldn't be on this quest in the first place, you wouldn't be going on adventures. "That is the case, yes, but still... please come home safely to your daughter[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. That is all I ask." |"Be careful out there. These people who attacked your daughter may have been ruffians led by a pompous rogue, but someone of considerable power is backing them." She's sure? "I am absolutely sure[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Torii gates are based upon the technologies which inform the operation of the waystone idols of Old Belhar, and those are still functional despite literal centuries of being exposed to the elements in the harshest of climates. To deliberately override the protocols of one of our gates and jam its function to its owners requires considerable magical knowledge to begin with; to be able to compress such a spell into a focus and have it activated by someone who by all appearances was untrained says even more. "The enemy we are facing here is dangerous and powerful. Please do not underestimate it, whatever it may happen to be. Ruffians and rogues like those who attacked your daughter are plentiful and cheap; a mastermind is not." |"Ah... in that moment when I received the news that the Young Lady Otomo's residence was under attack, I was truly brought back years..." It must have been hard on her to realize that the same thing was happening again, more than two centuries later. "By rights, the High Lady Otomo is my liege. And should she pass before his divine lordship sees fit to end my penance, the Young Lady Otomo will be my liege in her stead. To allow your daughter to perish... when it happened to her mother, I was cursed; should it happen to her, I do not know if his divine lordship would bear another failure on my part. Once already I have failed the Otomo clan in so grievous a manner, and once it will remain." To hear Kinu tell it, she came at them with everything she had. "I... did not want to take chances. The last time, it was just the ten of us and the harpies against the wraiths' flesh-puppets and worse. At least now all we faced were no more than forty ruffians." Flesh-puppets, huh. Kinu mentioned their bodies were changed, had begun to change, were changing... the invaders were not quite wholly flesh and blood, either. "The autopsy results of the two corpses we retrieved are both... interesting and disturbing. More disturbing than Kazuo himself, which is a small feat in and of itself. Still... circumstances were different this time. Allow me to express my resolve that no further harm will come to the Otomo holdings in the colonies." Is that all right? You know her people are terribly stretched as-is. If she laxes security on her own people... "If we cannot even protect the High Lady Otomo, her family, and her holdings, what good are we?" |"After examining the silver rod used to jam the torii gate, we've managed to discover a heretofore undiscovered exploit in the enchantment architecture that would have allowed someone else to override the security protocols. This is quite important as a lot of movement of people and goods throughout the empire now happens by means of the gates; this would not only have allowed whoever it was to prevent use, but also redirect the destination completely. Kazuo and I have sent our findings back across the ocean with utmost haste, this is quite the important concern. "But with this problem fixed, at least if they make another attempt on your daughter's life they won't be able to prevent us from using the gate the same way that they did the last time. A small mercy that something good has come out of all this." ] |[rand |So, what does Komari make of all this business? Is travel through the Ways Between off-limits for kitsune now? The den matron looks pensive, putting her hands together as she considers her answer. "To be sure, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]I've certainly forbidden all frivolous travel until circumstances change. As quartermaster of the storehouse, Kohaku is the only one who has reason to travel from the den as part of her duties. Anything else is out of the question for now." And the gates... "Are safe, at least the one here in my seat of governance. Those on the other side of the ocean are much the same; no one will be forcing them open. That is why I suspect your daughter's assailants ambushed her in the Ways Between. Ever since the fall of Belhar, we are the only ones who have used the Ways Between for travel for a time now, but the old waystone idols about the empire and indeed, the world, still stand and are very functional." There is no way to secure the Ways Between, then. You've been there, the place is vast. Komari shakes her head. "Just so[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. That plane of existence is complex; we could no more patrol it meaningfully than we could patrol the rolling downs of the Belharan Heartland. Either way, Kinu should be fine coming and going from her home to this place; the gate that directly connects the two is a very minor one and the distance small, so the time spent in transit is negligible. Think of it as a direct tunnel through the Ways Between, if you will. However, while she most certainly enjoyed her trip with Kohaku to [kinu.isInari |Willowpast |her family's holdings ], there will be no further travel until this situation is resolved." |Has she got any kind of idea on just who these people are and why they're after the kitsune? "As Kinu has already told you, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]they claim to be local people who take considerable offense at our presence here and have decided to do something about it. Yet they look nothing like any natives of these lands, or even this continent. If they are what they claim to be, then their bodies have changed considerably from the people they once were." You shudder at the memory of Kinu describing her assailants and the strange white masquerade-esque masks they wore. The fox-morph, though, he looked perfectly normal, which was odd. Raphael, that was his name? "I would not put any stock in that being the man's true name — given Kinu's description of his flamboyant behavior, it would be par for the course. But given Kinu's tale as to what he was able to do and how nothing much she did worked in the least, the man has certainly been changed on the inside, if not the outside." ... Komari sighs and raises a hand to her cheek. "It's hard to draw any concrete conclusions; the most both the artificer and I have to work with are witnesses' tales and a single control rod that was left behind the last time. That being said, given what residue we were able to clean off the weapons of Kohaku and her bodyguards... Kazuo is beside himself with excitement at the prospect of having a corpse to dissect. "Please be careful, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]. Whoever — or more likely, whatever — is behind this threat to your daughter and indeed, all of us, it is more than capable of shaping flesh like clay into forms that should not be viable, yet are despite all that. That would indicate considerable power, certainly enough to warrant extreme caution." |"While my great-great-grandson Nakano has persevered for years as provost without asking for assistance from the capital, the boy has finally swallowed his pride and officially requested aid for the colonial regiment. I could see his cheeks burn and tails thrash as he composed the missive, but he did it anyway. To weigh one duty against another and have to choose is such a classical dilemma, even if the form it took this time is somewhat new and interesting." Oh? "It is a complicated matter, to be sure. The very people whom he wishes to earn recognition from look down upon him for being born in the colonies, inasmuch as they would have looked down on provincials in eras past. My poor great-great-grandson is determined to prove himself by comporting himself well despite the blatantly inadequate resources afforded him... [kinu.isInari |but now that the life of the young lady Otomo has been put at stake here, he has clearly decided that matters of divinity supercede his own interests." You would damn well hope that he'd put Kinu's life above that of whatever political game he's playing here. Komari's face is impassive at that. "Mmm. She is his future liege, after all. That, and family as well, once the matter of her engagement with Hitoshi is settled. I would be sorely upset with my dear Nakano if he didn't get his priorities straight |but now that he has a future liege, a bearer of divine blood and a fiancee to look out for, his priorities have shifted not inconsiderably. While I'm still not fully enamored of his engagement to Kinu, at least it has done him some good." Kinu must be something, to be able to take such an ornery bastard in hand. Komari smiles wryly and turns her palms upwards. "It is what it is[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. The poor boy may not want to admit it openly, but she has him eating out of her hand, as your saying goes. There is a sense of genuine earnestness about young Kinu that he responds to, knowingly or not, and I do believe he would lay his life down for her even were he not obliged to do so by the traditions and code and his kind. "That, and she has been encouraging, if not outright nice about his poetry ]. So many matters vex the poor boy these days, partly — no, mostly because of you[pc.ra kitsune |r Eminence. I have no doubt that his divine lordship is chuckling away somewhere watching the boy tie himself into knots over your station and achievements ever since you came to be with us | and your deeds in the time you've been with us. I'm sure that you've been no small source of amusement for his divine lordship since day one ]." Komari gives you a thin-lipped smile. Given that the question has been asked, does she think the Old Country will actually send any tangible help? "As things stand, unlikely." You shake your head. Don't they care what happens to the colonies? Or Kinu, for that matter? Isn't she supposed to be of divine descent and untouchable? Shouldn't — "[pc.ra kitsune |Your Eminence, p |P ]lease be reminded that her mother has abdicated any claim to the clan line and holdings.Even so, blood is blood... if the imperial court is anything like when I saw it last, there will be back and forth amongst the twelve as to what exactly is to be done — of course a threat to the life of someone of divine descent cannot be ignored, but the details matter. And so they will drag things out, and maybe one or two will hope that Kinu quietly gets herself killed so she is no longer a problem." That's... "Politics. We colonials have been on our own for centuries now[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ], and I don't expect that to change in any meaningful manner until they start feeling squeezed across the ocean." |"Don't worry about your daughter while she's over here in my home, she'll be watched and in good hands. I already allowed one Otomo to die on my watch, and it's not something that'll ever happen again." ... "The people love her, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]they really do. [kinu.isInari |Even if she's a girl of few words, they see how nature favors her, how she is showered with the gifts of the earth, and are inspired — while the rest of the world does not recognise this aspect of him, Keros is a god of rice and the harvest back in the Old Country, after all. Rest assured that there'll always be at least one pair of eyes on her at all times, and she can continue to work our fields in peace |There is something about Kinu that draws the eyes of people that is more than just a pretty face, and she uses it well. Rest assured that there'll always be at least one pair of eyes on her at all times, and she can continue her education unimpeded by the attempts on her life ]. You'll leave it to her, then, to let Kinu lead as normal a life as possible despite all the craziness going on around in the world. There are so many problems in the world that you can't be everywhere at once, as much as you'd like to — it's good that your daughter has many people watching out for her well-being. Would that she learns to appreciate them more than she already does. Komari gives you a little bow of her head. "I'm [pc.ra kitsune |honored by your confidence in me, your Eminence |touched ]." |Given that travel across the ocean is nixed for the time being, has she faced any difficulties communicating with the capital or whoever it is up the hierarchy from her in the Old Country? Komari gives you a thin smile. "Usually, the capital is more than content to leave us alone save if we have some great find to report, or if there's some request or the other for goods. The colonies enjoy the dubious honor of a high and unprecedented degree of autonomy that even the backwater provinces did not historically enjoy; I am a cursed being, punished for my failure, leading people who while not outright criminal are either misfits and rejects or the descendants of such." That's a harsh way to put it. "But a genuine and correct one [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]," she says, bowing her head. "I understand the desire to speak well of the people whom you have aided and enjoy the company of, but the fact of the matter is what it is, without illusion." ... "Either way, missives from the capital, though I am bound to obey, have tended to be troublesome for me in the past. I am perfectly capable of making my own independent decisions as colonial governor, and with Kiyoko backing me up one certainly cannot say that I am lacking in authority to function in such a capacity. That travel back to and from the Old Country is not advisable at the moment... is quite relaxing. A silver lining to the cloud, as the native saying goes." ] ]
rows.translation: [var0 |[kiyoko.isFree |[rand |说实话，我有点担心大友夫人回到她原来的住所居住。虽然已经过去了两百多年，她肯定也修补了那些当初导致幽灵入侵的防御漏洞，但我还是无法理解她为何能对这件事如此放心。不过，要在不引起争论的情况下表达我的担忧，确实是一件挺困难的事……啊…… 如果这是为了她的安全，你相信清子一定会理解的。 她向我保证，一切都已经恢复正常，她还会亲自与那位尊贵的大人合作，确保此类事情再也不会发生。然而，我还是无法摆脱那种不安的感觉——虽然那件事发生已经超过两个世纪了，但当大友夫人和她的女儿向我展示他们重新修复后的家园时，我看到的却只有那些尸体。 你试图进一步追问麻里关于这个话题的细节，但这位女首领闭口不谈，拒绝再透露任何信息。考虑到之前发生的事情，以及这些事情对她造成的影响，你并不感到惊讶——仅仅提到清子的家，就足以让她的心灵再次受到创伤。不过，归根结底，麻里对于如何同时保留你的狐狸妻子和……这个问题的想法，其实也很明确。 [kiyoko.numKits 1 |女儿 |孩子们 ]安全可能至关重要。也许下次再谈吧…… |大家都对在边境建立新的据点感到非常兴奋——毕竟已经有一段时间没有发生过这样的事情了。对于我们这些狐族来说，选择在哪里安家自然是非常谨慎的。而考虑到大友夫人的身份，这种谨慎更是必要。现在到处都在流传着这样的消息，人们都想要通过帮助重建和修复她的家园来赢得这位据点领袖的青睐。 不得不说，这些设定听起来有点违反常理。凯洛斯没有恢复一切，是因为他希望清子和她自己能够通过自己的努力获得超出基本生存所需的资源。 我想，凭借你那极具感染力的魅力去激励他人帮助你，这也算是一种方法吧？麻里带着一丝淡淡的微笑回应道。你那个女儿…… [kinu.kinuAdultPersonality 0 |她话不多，但大家都注意到了她在这里是多么努力工作，因此觉得应该回馈些什么。虽然这些回报并不丰厚，但那些有良知的人都会全力以赴。再加上他们都很尊敬仁，所以你可以想象接下来会发生什么。 |哦，她可真是个有着迷人魅力的女人啊。她只要微微一笑，所有人都会争先恐后地来帮助她。搭建梁柱？铺设屋顶？处理木材？这些对她来说都不过是小菜一碟罢了。 ]可以说，我们狐妖们只是出于生存的需要在做我们一直以来都在做的事情——互相照顾。在古老的旧国也是如此，大家会齐心协力重新铺设屋顶，因为大家都清楚，到了当年特定的时候，这些努力将会给整个村庄带来好处。这样，一切都会顺利地运转下去。 [party.has kiyoko | 确实如此。你的狐狸妻子补充道。将你的时间和精力投入到其他值得信赖的人身上，这是你能做的最重要的事情之一。当然，要营造一种信任的氛围，就必须对那些辜负这种信任的人施以严厉的惩罚……凡事都有其代价。 ] |在她年轻的时候，大友夫人住在一座规模远比这座宏伟得多的宫殿里，那座宫殿也是一棵变成了神圣树木的建筑物。你在那些大厅里闲逛上好几天，也未必能走完所有的地方。我小时候第一次和父母一起来到那里的时候，很容易就迷路了，还得让宫殿的卫兵来把我找回来——那真是件挺尴尬的事。 [party.has kiyoko |清子勉强挤出了一个淡淡的微笑。我记得这件事。你的父母和我的父母都因为你走失而严厉地责备了你，但我原谅了你。他们确实责备了你我正因为如此，人们才会说，对一个身居高位的人来说，宽大处理是不合适的；如果就这样放任那些作恶的人逍遥法外，他们的耻辱就会降临到我身上。 "……" |现在，她住在一个虽然简陋但还算舒适的地方。无论如何来看，这确实意味着她的生活水平下降了。 她当初自愿承担在这片大洋对岸的新土地上领导殖民事业时，就知道自己会得到这些回报。不过，我怀疑我的主君其实并不太在意这些事情……你有没有注意到，她每天都穿着一模一样的衣服？她拥有十件甚至更多的完全相同的衣物。 ]
