Well, given what Kas is sparking around the Marches, she'd better tighten up security about these parts — and after a few run-ins with her minions, you're sure these young folks will see the wisdom of her words soon enough. |"Evergreen put up a wall of thorns about the entrance to the Frostwood, you say? Yes, I knew about it. No, I didn't care, because it's all the better for me and mine and if she's the one expending the effort keeping it maintained, I don't see why I should care. That hussy thinks that she's the one keeping the terrors of the Frostwood out; well, from my perspective the wall's keeping her and hers from getting into mischief about these parts. Well, less mischief than they normally do." ] ] |[rand |I know this shouldn't need to be said, but do talk to your daughter some more whenever you can. [kinu.isInari |While she prefers to be alone most of the time, that doesn't mean that she doesn't want to reach out, or that you wouldn't be welcome. Kinu may be quite stubborn, but even rocks can change their shape over time if you keep on chipping away quietly at them. |She may keep on a pleasant face so much of the time, but that is partially because the people are so sensitive to the moods of their beloved princess. She knows that if she allows herself to be upset, they will be too; it is part and parcel of her job. Yet at the same time, the brave face does not necessarily mean that she is truly well. She is quite adept at hiding her emotions, after all. ]" Yeah, you will, especially in the wake of all that has happened. "You can tell that it troubles her — not just the errors she made in the heat of the moment, the sting of failure from being defeated by the invaders, and the loss of much of what has been built since the den was resettled. What she needs, perhaps, is someone who is not from her root culture to speak with her, someone who does not necessarily have the same notions of failure and shame that we do and she feels she can open up to without necessarily being judged for her failure. She is rather too hard on herself..." Such is the fate of the overachieving daughter who faces her first true failure that she cannot explain or rationalise away to herself. Komari closes her eyes and leans back in her seat. "Harsh, but accurate. Such is her fate." |"While I know much of the talk regarding the attempt on your family's life has been centered about your daughter, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]I would caution you to be careful as well. By her own recounting of the events, your firstborn daughter [kiyoko.numKits 2 3 |and her sister |and other children ]were attacked because those rogues neither dared get to you or the High Lady Otomo directly; they deliberately chose a moment when the both of you would not be at home to strike. Now that they have met with partial success, they will grow more bold and desperate alike." Does she mean that these people, whoever they are, may be planning an attempt on you or Kiyoko next? "I cannot say for sure; there is too much conjecture to be certain, and probably some misdirection in the mix. We ourselves have noted some disappearances in the outlying camps on the border in the last few months, but we always thought... well, some people come to the colonies to vanish." Vanish? "To hide, to let themselves loose, and sometimes, to just give up and die far away from home where their passing will not bring further shame to their clan name. It has been this way for years; some who are sentenced to banishment to the colonies simply wander out into the wilderness and don't return, or meet unfortunate ends. This land is a cold, hard mistress. But now... we may have a more sinister explanation for the recent spate of disappearances." She doesn't say... "I urge you once more, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, please be careful. You have declared where your allegiances lie in the deepest and most profound fashion possible |please be careful. You have lain with and sired children by what they deem a demoness ]; no doubt these people regard you as a traitor to your own kin. Beyond the dens' immediate environs, I cannot guarantee your safety." If you were looking to be safe, you wouldn't be on this quest in the first place, you wouldn't be going on adventures. "That is the case, yes, but still... please come home safely to your daughter[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. That is all I ask." |"Be careful out there. These people who attacked your daughter may have been ruffians led by a pompous rogue, but someone of considerable power is backing them." She's sure? "I am absolutely sure[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. Torii gates are based upon the technologies which inform the operation of the waystone idols of Old Belhar, and those are still functional despite literal centuries of being exposed to the elements in the harshest of climates. To deliberately override the protocols of one of our gates and jam its function to its owners requires considerable magical knowledge to begin with; to be able to compress such a spell into a focus and have it activated by someone who by all appearances was untrained says even more. "The enemy we are facing here is dangerous and powerful. Please do not underestimate it, whatever it may happen to be. Ruffians and rogues like those who attacked your daughter are plentiful and cheap; a mastermind is not." |"Ah... in that moment when I received the news that the Young Lady Otomo's residence was under attack, I was truly brought back years..." It must have been hard on her to realize that the same thing was happening again, more than two centuries later. "By rights, the High Lady Otomo is my liege. And should she pass before his divine lordship sees fit to end my penance, the Young Lady Otomo will be my liege in her stead. To allow your daughter to perish... when it happened to her mother, I was cursed; should it happen to her, I do not know if his divine lordship would bear another failure on my part. Once already I have failed the Otomo clan in so grievous a manner, and once it will remain." To hear Kinu tell it, she came at them with everything she had. "I... did not want to take chances. The last time, it was just the ten of us and the harpies against the wraiths' flesh-puppets and worse. At least now all we faced were no more than forty ruffians." Flesh-puppets, huh. Kinu mentioned their bodies were changed, had begun to change, were changing... the invaders were not quite wholly flesh and blood, either. "The autopsy results of the two corpses we retrieved are both... interesting and disturbing. More disturbing than Kazuo himself, which is a small feat in and of itself. Still... circumstances were different this time. Allow me to express my resolve that no further harm will come to the Otomo holdings in the colonies." Is that all right? You know her people are terribly stretched as-is. If she laxes security on her own people... "If we cannot even protect the High Lady Otomo, her family, and her holdings, what good are we?" |"After examining the silver rod used to jam the torii gate, we've managed to discover a heretofore undiscovered exploit in the enchantment architecture that would have allowed someone else to override the security protocols. This is quite important as a lot of movement of people and goods throughout the empire now happens by means of the gates; this would not only have allowed whoever it was to prevent use, but also redirect the destination completely. Kazuo and I have sent our findings back across the ocean with utmost haste, this is quite the important concern. "But with this problem fixed, at least if they make another attempt on your daughter's life they won't be able to prevent us from using the gate the same way that they did the last time. A small mercy that something good has come out of all this." ] |[rand |So, what does Komari make of all this business? Is travel through the Ways Between off-limits for kitsune now? The den matron looks pensive, putting her hands together as she considers her answer. "To be sure, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]I've certainly forbidden all frivolous travel until circumstances change. As quartermaster of the storehouse, Kohaku is the only one who has reason to travel from the den as part of her duties. Anything else is out of the question for now." And the gates... "Are safe, at least the one here in my seat of governance. Those on the other side of the ocean are much the same; no one will be forcing them open. That is why I suspect your daughter's assailants ambushed her in the Ways Between. Ever since the fall of Belhar, we are the only ones who have used the Ways Between for travel for a time now, but the old waystone idols about the empire and indeed, the world, still stand and are very functional." There is no way to secure the Ways Between, then. You've been there, the place is vast. Komari shakes her head. "Just so[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. That plane of existence is complex; we could no more patrol it meaningfully than we could patrol the rolling downs of the Belharan Heartland. Either way, Kinu should be fine coming and going from her home to this place; the gate that directly connects the two is a very minor one and the distance small, so the time spent in transit is negligible. Think of it as a direct tunnel through the Ways Between, if you will. However, while she most certainly enjoyed her trip with Kohaku to [kinu.isInari |Willowpast |her family's holdings ], there will be no further travel until this situation is resolved." |Has she got any kind of idea on just who these people are and why they're after the kitsune? "As Kinu has already told you, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, ]they claim to be local people who take considerable offense at our presence here and have decided to do something about it. Yet they look nothing like any natives of these lands, or even this continent. If they are what they claim to be, then their bodies have changed considerably from the people they once were." You shudder at the memory of Kinu describing her assailants and the strange white masquerade-esque masks they wore. The fox-morph, though, he looked perfectly normal, which was odd. Raphael, that was his name? "I would not put any stock in that being the man's true name — given Kinu's description of his flamboyant behavior, it would be par for the course. But given Kinu's tale as to what he was able to do and how nothing much she did worked in the least, the man has certainly been changed on the inside, if not the outside." ... Komari sighs and raises a hand to her cheek. "It's hard to draw any concrete conclusions; the most both the artificer and I have to work with are witnesses' tales and a single control rod that was left behind the last time. That being said, given what residue we were able to clean off the weapons of Kohaku and her bodyguards... Kazuo is beside himself with excitement at the prospect of having a corpse to dissect. "Please be careful, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]. Whoever — or more likely, whatever — is behind this threat to your daughter and indeed, all of us, it is more than capable of shaping flesh like clay into forms that should not be viable, yet are despite all that. That would indicate considerable power, certainly enough to warrant extreme caution." |"While my great-great-grandson Nakano has persevered for years as provost without asking for assistance from the capital, the boy has finally swallowed his pride and officially requested aid for the colonial regiment. I could see his cheeks burn and tails thrash as he composed the missive, but he did it anyway. To weigh one duty against another and have to choose is such a classical dilemma, even if the form it took this time is somewhat new and interesting." Oh? "It is a complicated matter, to be sure. The very people whom he wishes to earn recognition from look down upon him for being born in the colonies, inasmuch as they would have looked down on provincials in eras past. My poor great-great-grandson is determined to prove himself by comporting himself well despite the blatantly inadequate resources afforded him... [kinu.isInari |but now that the life of the young lady Otomo has been put at stake here, he has clearly decided that matters of divinity supercede his own interests." You would damn well hope that he'd put Kinu's life above that of whatever political game he's playing here. Komari's face is impassive at that. "Mmm. She is his future liege, after all. That, and family as well, once the matter of her engagement with Hitoshi is settled. I would be sorely upset with my dear Nakano if he didn't get his priorities straight |but now that he has a future liege, a bearer of divine blood and a fiancee to look out for, his priorities have shifted not inconsiderably. While I'm still not fully enamored of his engagement to Kinu, at least it has done him some good." Kinu must be something, to be able to take such an ornery bastard in hand. Komari smiles wryly and turns her palms upwards. "It is what it is[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. The poor boy may not want to admit it openly, but she has him eating out of her hand, as your saying goes. There is a sense of genuine earnestness about young Kinu that he responds to, knowingly or not, and I do believe he would lay his life down for her even were he not obliged to do so by the traditions and code and his kind. "That, and she has been encouraging, if not outright nice about his poetry ]. So many matters vex the poor boy these days, partly — no, mostly because of you[pc.ra kitsune |r Eminence. I have no doubt that his divine lordship is chuckling away somewhere watching the boy tie himself into knots over your station and achievements ever since you came to be with us | and your deeds in the time you've been with us. I'm sure that you've been no small source of amusement for his divine lordship since day one ]." Komari gives you a thin-lipped smile. Given that the question has been asked, does she think the Old Country will actually send any tangible help? "As things stand, unlikely." You shake your head. Don't they care what happens to the colonies? Or Kinu, for that matter? Isn't she supposed to be of divine descent and untouchable? Shouldn't — "[pc.ra kitsune |Your Eminence, p |P ]lease be reminded that her mother has abdicated any claim to the clan line and holdings.Even so, blood is blood... if the imperial court is anything like when I saw it last, there will be back and forth amongst the twelve as to what exactly is to be done — of course a threat to the life of someone of divine descent cannot be ignored, but the details matter. And so they will drag things out, and maybe one or two will hope that Kinu quietly gets herself killed so she is no longer a problem." That's... "Politics. We colonials have been on our own for centuries now[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ], and I don't expect that to change in any meaningful manner until they start feeling squeezed across the ocean." |"Don't worry about your daughter while she's over here in my home, she'll be watched and in good hands. I already allowed one Otomo to die on my watch, and it's not something that'll ever happen again." ... "The people love her, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]they really do. [kinu.isInari |Even if she's a girl of few words, they see how nature favors her, how she is showered with the gifts of the earth, and are inspired — while the rest of the world does not recognise this aspect of him, Keros is a god of rice and the harvest back in the Old Country, after all. Rest assured that there'll always be at least one pair of eyes on her at all times, and she can continue to work our fields in peace |There is something about Kinu that draws the eyes of people that is more than just a pretty face, and she uses it well. Rest assured that there'll always be at least one pair of eyes on her at all times, and she can continue her education unimpeded by the attempts on her life ]. You'll leave it to her, then, to let Kinu lead as normal a life as possible despite all the craziness going on around in the world. There are so many problems in the world that you can't be everywhere at once, as much as you'd like to — it's good that your daughter has many people watching out for her well-being. Would that she learns to appreciate them more than she already does. Komari gives you a little bow of her head. "I'm [pc.ra kitsune |honored by your confidence in me, your Eminence |touched ]." |Given that travel across the ocean is nixed for the time being, has she faced any difficulties communicating with the capital or whoever it is up the hierarchy from her in the Old Country? Komari gives you a thin smile. "Usually, the capital is more than content to leave us alone save if we have some great find to report, or if there's some request or the other for goods. The colonies enjoy the dubious honor of a high and unprecedented degree of autonomy that even the backwater provinces did not historically enjoy; I am a cursed being, punished for my failure, leading people who while not outright criminal are either misfits and rejects or the descendants of such." That's a harsh way to put it. "But a genuine and correct one [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]," she says, bowing her head. "I understand the desire to speak well of the people whom you have aided and enjoy the company of, but the fact of the matter is what it is, without illusion." ... "Either way, missives from the capital, though I am bound to obey, have tended to be troublesome for me in the past. I am perfectly capable of making my own independent decisions as colonial governor, and with Kiyoko backing me up one certainly cannot say that I am lacking in authority to function in such a capacity. That travel back to and from the Old Country is not advisable at the moment... is quite relaxing. A silver lining to the cloud, as the native saying goes." ] ] "

rows.original: Would she have any opinions on the others who live under her care?
rows.translation: 对于那些由她照顾的人，她是否有什么看法呢？
rows.raw: "Would she have any opinions on the others who live under her care?"

rows.original: [pc.ra kitsune |[rand |Komari gives you a small, wistful smile. "During the time of the Celestial Restoration, our divine lordship walked the length and breadth of the Old Country for ten whole years, surveying his domain and power base. Of course, he had no need to do so, but he just liked the travel and the opportunity to get involved in the lives of people. "Before my exile came into effect, I followed him for the first of those ten years, swept the ground behind his nine tails as he journeyed the land. It was like the legends come to life — he, a living god, would enter a teahouse, order rice and beans for the both of us, then compose a poem on the spot about the beauty of autumn leaves. If he was in a good mood, he would buy liquor for everyone until they were dead drunk, then pay and leave without partaking himself." Sounds like a jolly fellow to be around. "He was, until you did something to deserve his ire. Sometimes he was merciful if he felt like it, sometimes he would make sure you would never live it down. For two months of the winter, he assumed the guise of a tanuki hawker, complete with a noodle cart. While my cooking skills were sufficient, they expanded considerably during that time by sheer necessity owing to the outrageous things he would promise our customers. And would the other gods have mercy on those who tried to swindle the chubby raccoon-man who looked like an easy mark, because he didn't. "That's what fundamentally makes the way we view divinity different from how it's viewed on this side of the ocean, I believe. None of the other Seven really do this sort of thing. They speak to paladins, prophets, seers, kings and queens... people of grand import and substance, or those who have dedicated their lives to them. They don't have the time to roll around in leaf piles one morning before heading in to chew out the entirety of the Ministry of the Left after lunchtime. I was with our divine lordship but for one year out of those ten, but reputedly everyone was very well-behaved when he was afoot. He takes the time to toy with and tease everyone... and it's left its mark on how his worshippers relate to him." |"His divine lordship drops by every two or three weeks to have dinner with me and mine. It's one of the only occasions where the shrine is actually closed, because... well, there's not much point when the Trickster himself is walking in the gardens, is there?" He must enjoy her company to want to see her a lot. "Ah... he says I'm the only servant of his who has lasted longer than a century or so. Being with us is one of his greatest joys, and yet we are not really truly lost to him after our deaths, no? Even so, sitting and having a meal... it's eye-opening to know that such a simple matter is meaningful to even a god like him. "He says it's like having a family once more when I gather the children and eat with him. The wife and twelve concubines he created for himself... their descendants still are around today and I'm sure any of them would be happy to receive him, but he says there's something about them that's lacking... something that is there when I call Mikoto, Miyuki, Nakano and Hitoshi to the table and we give thanks for the food in the presence of the Trickster himself. After all, to us he is the deity of rice and agriculture... my boy Hitoshi is usually so stone-faced, but he gets all dazed when his divine lordship himself invites him over to sit by his side. "He tells stories. Plays with the chopsticks. Makes jokes. And when we're done, he wipes his mouth, thanks us and is out the door with his tails. This... is not something you would expect the god who sentenced me to my penance to do. But he does it anyway." |"Hmm. You're the first divine champion of the Trickster in a long time and the only one not born kitsune, so may I ask you a question, your Eminence? It may quite possibly be somewhat intrusive." Well, best to hear it and then make a decision, no? Komari mulls this over for a minute, the glow in her eyes fading a little as she scratches her chin. "Hmmmnn. Do you feel any great difference inside of you ever since you became one of us, your Eminence? A shift, perhaps? Or an emptiness? You... well, allow me to put it bluntly. You have not begun to suffer the hunger as I do, as Mikoto and Miyuki do, as we all do. I am simply beginning to wonder as to some theories I have about our nature, that's all." Keros hasn't completely claimed your soul yet, if that's what she's wondering. As far as you understand these things, it's in a state of being-here-yet-not-quite there, and he's even given you a decoy of sorts as he knows there're several rather nasty characters out for it as well. The moment you shuffle off this mortal coil, though, or something close enough to it... "Yes, I wouldn't try to finagle out of the terms of the agreement if I were you. Especially not by trying to live forever. Just look at me." Oh, you would dare nothing of the sort. Besides, there's a pretty decent afterlife waiting for you, and that's a promise. Doesn't sound too bad for a lifetime of service... but to answer her question, you don't really feel that different inside. Not that it necessarily means anything — the most important changes of this sort are imperceptible to the one it's happening to, you hear — but as far as you're concerned you're still who you are, appearances notwithstanding. "Hm. Interesting. I wouldn't go as far as to say you're not one of us — if his divine lordship says you are, then that is the case — but there's probably one final step you have to take that won't come into play until your dying day. That would account for the... ah, discrepancies. Forgive me, I mean no offense, but I am merely telling it as it is." None taken. |"How are you acclimatising to your new form, your Eminence?" Komari asks. "The chaotic energies that were causing the high degree of mutability in your body should be mostly suppressed now, although there may be powerful or unforseen edge cases that may still slip through. Well, if that does happen, you just have to return to our divine lord and he'll set you straight." You're fitting in very well, and she's a dear for asking. It's a relief to be able to eat fruits, wines, stews and more without worrying about transforming into some kind of horrible chimaera. Sure, you could always just stuff your face again to change back, maybe with the aid of a little alchemy, but it could get irritating if you had a form you wanted to stick in. "And well, you more or less do." The fact that kitsune aren't really able to be changed drastically through any means should help, too. "Well, his divine lordship explained it to me once. It's less that we're resistant to changes, but more than we're incredibly prone to changes. This is what we look like, what we are, and our bodies know that. If you tried to change a kitsune away from his or her base form, it's not so much that the change doesn't take effect, but he or she changes back to the position of least energy so rapidly that no one ever notices. Like how water always tries to find the lowest point, you know? You can try to pick up water, but it just slips through and runs downhill again." And the end result is no different from as if they were immutable. "The differences do matter when one gets into certain details, your Eminence, but from a layman's point of view, you're right. Either way, I'm glad to hear that you're enjoying who you are, because if you aren't there's no backing out of this kind of deal. But you knew that before you said yes, of course." Of course. |"A little advice from one servant of the Trickster to another: it really isn't as hard as it might sound. By virtue of our divine lord's nature, we have a lot more autonomy and leeway to make our own decisions than those dedicated to the other great kami do. But with this freedom to act comes the implicit trust that we won't do anything in our standing as Keros' servants to bring shame upon his name... and of course, that we won't abuse that freedom. "Just remember that, and you won't go wrong." ] |[rand |"For all that we kitsune are prim and proper in our daily dealings, you would expect our patron deity to be much the same, wouldn't you? Well, yes and no. I've spoken face-to-face with his divine lordship many times, and he's always been the relaxed sort. Always uses plain language when speaking, a perfectly casual posture... he's the nice kind of friendly fox you can have a comfortable chat with. Thinks nothing of dropping by to say hello just because he was bored, and speaks his mind plenty." That sounds about right for his reputation as a trickster god, yes. But there's the other side of him... "...That you don't want to run afoul of," Komari says with a small sigh. "The laws that have bound and shaped the kitsune people for generations... he was the one who set them for our benefit, and woe betide the one who runs afoul of them and piques his interest enough to personally step in. Being declared outlaw, or even worse, no-face and being hunted down by your own is a tender mercy compared to some of the things our divine lordship has done to the admittedly very much deserving. And the Law of Equivalent Exchange... that is one which transgressors he takes a very dim view of. My anger at Mikoto and Miyuki during that whole business with Evergreen's bag... it was as much for them as it was at them. On the off-chance he decided to take a personal interest in their case..." Ah. You understand. "My fate is terrible enough, yet proportional to my failings. I cannot complain that it is overly cruel, and yet..." |"Unlike some Tiran and Lumian orders, service to his divine lordship requires neither celibacy nor abstinence. There wouldn't be entire clans of servants to the gods if we weren't allowed to take consorts, would there?" As far as you understand things, he's pretty permissive on such matters. "Don't get me wrong, there are still several schools of thought which promote asceticism, but those teachings are more philosophy and less theology. I took a husband in my day, and had a pretty large family to boot. Custom has it that if a priest or priestess dies, their consort usually fills their role. It's not uncommon for most shrines to be in the control of one family or the other, passed down from one generation to the next." |"One of the things I've noticed in my two or so centuries of exile across the ocean is that the way the locals handle worship of the Seven. More distant, and yet more reverent in their own way. Maybe I'm biased and only have seen a small slice of how religious rites are conducted amongst the natives, but from what I can tell most of the common folk make a show of piety once or twice a week and are content to set it aside for the rest of the time. "We don't work that way — if anything, we're more like the elven druids who still remain. Less impressive, but more constant observance spread throughout one's daily life. I suppose it's a result of how easily one can divide the divine and the mundane — they're more easily partitioned here, but where I come from the two are heavily interwoven." |"I really enjoy organising the festivals all year-round. Mikoto and Miyuki help me, of course, and a good matsuri is a good mood-raiser. Young people these days don't really think that much of propriating kami, be it the local forces or their own ancestral spirits, but everyone likes an excuse to goof off. Doubly so since life in the colonies and on the frontier is more in-your-face than anything else. Of course, I remember everything and try to keep the traditions straight — even if I have to make some changes because of where we are, ahaha. The point, as always, is to honor kami, from the great Seven to the littlest wilderness spirit." A foxen festival might be nice to see sometime; unfortunately, you're never around when these things happen. "The major observances are shared across the entirety of the Old Country, but every province and prefecture has its own unique customs and festivals. The dominion of the Cherry Blossom Throne is colorful that way; we believe in keeping things as localised as possible, where possible. Maybe you'll be fortunate enough to drop in when a festival's under way; it's not a sight an outsider gets to see from a neutral perspective." And what other perspectives might there be for a filthy foreigner like you? "Ah, that of a honored guest and benefactor, of course. What else? The hospitality and pleasure young folks are willing to show these days makes even me blush, oh dear." |"Many of the rites and rituals used by us originate from legends of the earliest times when his divine lordship Keros walked the land with his wife and concubines. The deeds of both him and those he met along the way... propriating kami aside, the rituals serve to tell those stories, if in a highly abridged form. From the steps needed to hear why local spirits are angry to ritual purification and exorcism, many of the rituals which Mikoto and Miyuki perform in their duties as shrine maidens are in essence a re-enactment of the events. I still remember when his divine lordship first came upon Miyuki in the midst of an o-harai great cleansing — ah, how he wept, and I dared not ask why. "Of course, since the kami of this land across the ocean differ from that of the Old country, I've had to make a couple of adjustments to reach out to them instead. Yet throughout all this, I've tried my best to keep the symbolism true to the source — his divine lordship has reviewed the rituals and has had no complaint, and there really isn't any greater authority on the subject than him..." ] ]
rows.translation: [pc.ra kitsune |[rand |小茧茧向你露出了一个略带忧伤的微笑。“在天启复兴时期，我们的神圣君主在旧国各地走遍了整整十年，巡视他的领地与势力根基。当然，他并没有这么做的必要，但他就是喜欢旅行，也喜欢有机会参与到人们的生活当中去。” “在我被流放之前，在那十年的头几年里，我一直跟随着他。每当他游历各地时，我都跟在他身后，为他那九条尾巴扫净身后的地面。这一切简直就像传说活了过来——他身为活生生的神明，会走进茶馆，为我们两人点上米饭和豆子，然后当场即兴作一首赞美秋叶之美的诗。如果他心情好，还会为大家买酒，直到所有人都烂醉如泥，之后他付了钱便离开，自己却一滴也不沾。” 听起来他是个挺快活的家伙，和他在一起一定很愉快。 “他确实是这样，除非你做了什么惹他动怒的事。他有时心情好便会宽恕你，有时又会让你永远都抬不起头来。那年冬天有整整两个月，他装扮成一个卖面的狸猫小贩，还配了一辆面摊车。我的厨艺本来还过得去，可那段时间里，因为他总对我们的顾客许下些离谱的承诺，我纯粹是被逼着把厨艺大大提升了一番。至于那些想糊弄这个看起来很好骗的胖浣熊人的人，其他神明会不会怜悯他们呢？因为他可不会手软。” “我认为，正是这一点从根本上让我们看待神性的方式与大洋彼岸不同。其他七神其实都不会做这种事。他们只跟圣骑士、先知、预言家、国王和王后交谈……都是些举足轻重、有分量的人物，或是那些把一生奉献给他们的人。他们可没时间在某个早晨在落叶堆里打滚，午饭后又要去把左务部上下骂个遍。在那十年里，我只与我们的神圣陛下相处了一年，但据说只要他在场，每个人都表现得非常规矩。他乐于花时间逗弄和戏弄每一个人……这也影响了他的信徒与他的相处方式。” |“他的神圣陛下每隔两三周就会来看我，和我们一起吃饭。这是神殿少数几个会真正关门的场合之一，因为……嗯，当戏弄者本人在花园里散步的时候，关门也没什么意义，不是吗？” 他一定很享受与她相处的时光，才会想经常见到她。 “啊……他说我是他所有仆从里唯一一个活了超过一个世纪左右的。与我们在一起是他最大的乐趣之一，而我们死后也并不会真正从他那里消失，对吧？即便如此，坐下来共进一餐……知道这样一件简单的事对像他这样的神也有意义，真是让人大开眼界。” “他说，当我把孩子们叫到一起和他吃饭时，感觉就像重新有了一个家。他为自己造的那位妻子和十二位妾室……她们的后代如今仍在，我相信他们中任何一个都会乐于接待他，但他说她们身上少了点什么……而当我叫美琴、美雪、中野和仁到桌边，在戏弄者本人面前为食物致谢时，那种东西就在那里。毕竟对我们来说，他就是稻米与农业之神……我的儿子仁通常总是面无表情，可当神圣陛下亲自邀他坐到自己身边时，他就会变得恍恍惚惚。” “他会讲故事。玩弄筷子。讲笑话。等我们吃完，他擦擦嘴，向我们道谢，然后就带着他的尾巴出门了。这种事……实在不是你想象中那个判我受罚的神会做的。但他偏偏就是这样。” |“嗯。您是许久以来第一位戏弄者的神圣冠军，也是唯一一位并非狐妖出身的，所以能否容我问您一个问题，尊贵的阁下？这问题很可能有些冒昧。” 嗯，最好先听听再做决定，不是吗？ 麻里琢磨了一会儿，她眼中的光芒稍稍黯淡下去，同时挠了挠下巴。“嗯……自从您成为我们中的一员后，您内心是否感觉到什么巨大的变化，尊贵的阁下？也许是某种转变，又或者是一种空虚？您……好吧，容我直说。您还没有像我一样、像美琴和美雪一样、像我们所有人一样开始遭受那种饥饿。我只是开始琢磨我对我们天性的一些理论，仅此而已。” 如果她是在疑惑这件事的话，凯洛斯其实还没有完全占据你的灵魂。就你所知，那种状态可以说是“既在这里、又不完全在这里”；而且他还给了你某种诱饵，因为他知道还有好几个相当危险的家伙也在觊觎它。不过，等你咽下最后一口气，或者发生什么差不多接近的事…… “是的，如果我是你，我不会试图钻协议条款的空子。尤其不会靠追求永生来钻空子。看看我就知道了。” 哦，你绝不敢做那种事。再说，有一个相当不错的来世在等着你，这是说好的。为一辈子的侍奉换来这样的结果，听起来不算太糟……但要说回答她的问题，你内心并不真的觉得那么不同。倒不是说这一定意味着什么——你听说，这类最重要的变化对正在经历它的人来说是察觉不到的——但就你自己而言，尽管外表变了，你还是你。 “嗯，有意思。我不敢说你不是我们中的一员——如果神圣陛下说你是，那你就是——但可能还有最后一步你得走，而那一步要到你的大限之日才会起作用。这大概就能解释那些……啊，出入之处了。请原谅，我无意冒犯，只是实话实说。” 没有，我并没觉得被冒犯。 |“尊贵的阁下，您适应自己新的形态还顺利吗？”麻里问道。“那些曾导致你身体出现高度变异的混乱能量现在应该基本被压制住了，不过也许还有一些强大或无法预见的边缘情况仍可能漏过来。嗯，如果那确实发生了，你只要回到我们的神明大人那里，他就会帮你纠正过来。” 你适应得非常好，她这么关心真是贴心。能放心地享用水果、葡萄酒、炖菜等食物，不用担心会变成某种可怕的奇美拉，这真是让人松了口气。当然，你随时可以再大吃一顿变回去，也许借助一点炼金术的帮助，但如果你有一个想保持住的形态，那就可能会变得很烦人。 “嗯，你差不多就是这样。” 狐妖其实无法通过任何手段被大幅改变，这一点应该也会有帮助。 “嗯，神圣陛下曾经向我解释过。与其说我们抗拒变化，不如说我们极其容易变化。这就是我们的样子，这就是我们本来的面貌，我们的身体知道这一点。如果你试图把一只狐妖改变得偏离其基础形态，并不是变化没有生效，而是他或她会以极快的速度变回能量最低的状态，以至于没有人会注意到。就像水总是要找到最低点一样，你明白吧？你可以试着把水捧起来，但它就是会从你手里滑落，然后再次往低处流去。” 最终的结果与它们本就不可改变并无二致。 “这些差异确实是有影响的，尊贵的阁下，一旦涉及到某些细节，但从外行的角度来看，您说得没错。不管怎样，我很高兴听到您喜欢自己现在的样子，因为如果您不喜欢，这种交易可没法反悔。当然，您答应之前就已经知道了。” 那当然。 |“一位戏弄者的仆从给另一位的一点建议：这事其实并没有听起来那么难。由于我们神明大人的天性，我们比那些侍奉其他伟大神明的人拥有多得多的自主权和自由，可以自己作决定。但这种行动的自由也伴随着一种不言而喻的信任：我们不会以凯罗斯仆从的身份做出任何有辱他名声的事……当然，还意味着我们不会滥用这种自由。” “只要记住这一点，你就不会出错。” ] |[rand |“尽管我们狐狸一族平日待人接物都端庄得体，你们大概会以为我们的守护神也差不多吧？嗯，既对也不对。我曾多次面对面地与神圣陛下交谈，他一直都是很随和的那种。说话总是用平白的语言，姿态极其随意……他是那种友善的狐狸，可以和他舒舒服服地聊天。他会因为无聊就顺路过来打个招呼，而且也很爱说出自己的想法。” 这确实符合他作为戏弄者的名声。但他还有另一面…… “……那是你绝对不想惹上的，”麻里轻叹着说道。“那些世代以来约束并塑造了狐族的律法……正是他为我们的利益而设立的，谁要是违反了它们又引起了他的兴趣，让他亲自出手，那就有难了。被宣布为不法之徒，或者更糟，被除名并遭自己人追猎，与我们神圣陛下对那些——诚然是罪有应得的人——所做过的一些事相比，都算是仁慈了。还有等价交换法则……对违反者他可是深恶痛绝的。在常青女士的包那整件事上，我对美琴和美雪的火气……那份怒气既是对她们的，也同样是为她们而发。万一他决定亲自过问她们的案子……” 啊。你明白了。 “我的命运已经够惨了，但与我的过失是相称的。我不能抱怨它过于残酷，可是……” |“与某些提兰和卢米安教团不同，侍奉神圣陛下既不要求独身也不要求禁欲。如果我们不被允许娶妻纳妾，就不会有整个氏族的人去侍奉诸神了，不是吗？” 就你所知，他在这类事情上相当宽容。 “别误会，如今仍有几个提倡苦修的流派，但那些教义更偏哲学而非神学。我当年也嫁过丈夫，还生了一个相当大的家庭。按照习俗，如果一位祭司或女祭司去世，他们的配偶通常会接替他们的职位。大多数神社由一个或另一个家族掌控、代代相传，这并不罕见。” |“我在这两个世纪左右的跨海流亡中注意到的一件事，就是当地人对七神的崇拜方式。更疏远，却又以他们自己的方式更虔诚。也许我有偏见，只见过原住民举行宗教仪式的很小一部分，但据我所知，大多数普通百姓每周做一两次虔诚的样子，其余时间便心安理得地把它搁在一边。” “我们不是这样——要说的话，我们更像那些尚存的精灵德鲁伊。没那么引人注目，但更持续不断的奉行贯穿于日常生活中。我想这是因为神圣与世俗很容易被分开——在这里两者更容易被分隔，而在我来自的地方，这二者是紧密交织的。” |“我真的很喜欢一年到头组织这些祭典。当然，美琴和美雪会帮我，而一场好的祭典很能提振人心。如今的年轻人其实不太把安抚神明当回事，无论是当地的神灵还是自家的祖先之灵，但谁都喜欢找个借口偷懒。殖民地和边疆的生活比什么都更直来直往，就更是如此了。当然，我记得所有事，也尽量把传统理清楚——即使因为身处何地不得不做些改动，啊哈哈。重点一如既往，是敬奉神明，从伟大的七神到最微小的荒野之灵。” 真希望能有机会看到一次狐狸的祭典；可惜这类活动举行时你总是不在场。 “重要的祭典是整个旧国共同遵行的，但每个省和国都有自己独特的习俗与节日。樱花王座治下就是这样丰富多彩；我们信奉在可能之处尽量保持本地化。也许你会走运，正好赶上某场祭典；那不是外人能从旁观角度看到的景象。” 再说，像你这样一个肮脏的外国人还能有什么别的角度呢？ “啊，当然是作为贵客和恩人的角度了。还能有什么呢？如今的年轻人愿意表现出的殷勤和热情，连我都觉得脸红，哎呀。” |“我们使用的许多仪式与典礼都源自最早时代的传说，那时神圣陛下凯罗斯与他的妻子和妾室们一同行走于大地上。他以及他途中遇见的人们的所作所为……且不说安抚神明，这些仪式的作用就是讲述那些故事，尽管是极度节略的形式。从得知当地神灵为何发怒所需的步骤，到仪式性的净化和驱邪，美琴和美雪在履行神社少女职责时所执行的许多仪式，本质上都是对那些事件的重演。我至今还记得神圣陛下第一次遇到正处于大祓大净化之中的美雪时的情景——啊，他哭得多么伤心，而我不敢问为什么。” “当然，由于大洋彼岸这片土地上的神明与旧国的不同，我不得不做几处调整，改为向他们沟通。不过在这整个过程中，我尽力让象征意义忠于本源——神圣陛下审查过这些仪式，也没有任何异议，而在这个问题上确实没有比他更大的权威了……” ] ]
rows.raw: " [pc.ra kitsune |[rand |Komari gives you a small, wistful smile. "During the time of the Celestial Restoration, our divine lordship walked the length and breadth of the Old Country for ten whole years, surveying his domain and power base. Of course, he had no need to do so, but he just liked the travel and the opportunity to get involved in the lives of people. "Before my exile came into effect, I followed him for the first of those ten years, swept the ground behind his nine tails as he journeyed the land. It was like the legends come to life — he, a living god, would enter a teahouse, order rice and beans for the both of us, then compose a poem on the spot about the beauty of autumn leaves. If he was in a good mood, he would buy liquor for everyone until they were dead drunk, then pay and leave without partaking himself." Sounds like a jolly fellow to be around. "He was, until you did something to deserve his ire. Sometimes he was merciful if he felt like it, sometimes he would make sure you would never live it down. For two months of the winter, he assumed the guise of a tanuki hawker, complete with a noodle cart. While my cooking skills were sufficient, they expanded considerably during that time by sheer necessity owing to the outrageous things he would promise our customers. And would the other gods have mercy on those who tried to swindle the chubby raccoon-man who looked like an easy mark, because he didn't. "That's what fundamentally makes the way we view divinity different from how it's viewed on this side of the ocean, I believe. None of the other Seven really do this sort of thing. They speak to paladins, prophets, seers, kings and queens... people of grand import and substance, or those who have dedicated their lives to them. They don't have the time to roll around in leaf piles one morning before heading in to chew out the entirety of the Ministry of the Left after lunchtime. I was with our divine lordship but for one year out of those ten, but reputedly everyone was very well-behaved when he was afoot. He takes the time to toy with and tease everyone... and it's left its mark on how his worshippers relate to him." |"His divine lordship drops by every two or three weeks to have dinner with me and mine. It's one of the only occasions where the shrine is actually closed, because... well, there's not much point when the Trickster himself is walking in the gardens, is there?" He must enjoy her company to want to see her a lot. "Ah... he says I'm the only servant of his who has lasted longer than a century or so. Being with us is one of his greatest joys, and yet we are not really truly lost to him after our deaths, no? Even so, sitting and having a meal... it's eye-opening to know that such a simple matter is meaningful to even a god like him. "He says it's like having a family once more when I gather the children and eat with him. The wife and twelve concubines he created for himself... their descendants still are around today and I'm sure any of them would be happy to receive him, but he says there's something about them that's lacking... something that is there when I call Mikoto, Miyuki, Nakano and Hitoshi to the table and we give thanks for the food in the presence of the Trickster himself. After all, to us he is the deity of rice and agriculture... my boy Hitoshi is usually so stone-faced, but he gets all dazed when his divine lordship himself invites him over to sit by his side. "He tells stories. Plays with the chopsticks. Makes jokes. And when we're done, he wipes his mouth, thanks us and is out the door with his tails. This... is not something you would expect the god who sentenced me to my penance to do. But he does it anyway." |"Hmm. You're the first divine champion of the Trickster in a long time and the only one not born kitsune, so may I ask you a question, your Eminence? It may quite possibly be somewhat intrusive." Well, best to hear it and then make a decision, no? Komari mulls this over for a minute, the glow in her eyes fading a little as she scratches her chin. "Hmmmnn. Do you feel any great difference inside of you ever since you became one of us, your Eminence? A shift, perhaps? Or an emptiness? You... well, allow me to put it bluntly. You have not begun to suffer the hunger as I do, as Mikoto and Miyuki do, as we all do. I am simply beginning to wonder as to some theories I have about our nature, that's all." Keros hasn't completely claimed your soul yet, if that's what she's wondering. As far as you understand these things, it's in a state of being-here-yet-not-quite there, and he's even given you a decoy of sorts as he knows there're several rather nasty characters out for it as well. The moment you shuffle off this mortal coil, though, or something close enough to it... "Yes, I wouldn't try to finagle out of the terms of the agreement if I were you. Especially not by trying to live forever. Just look at me." Oh, you would dare nothing of the sort. Besides, there's a pretty decent afterlife waiting for you, and that's a promise. Doesn't sound too bad for a lifetime of service... but to answer her question, you don't really feel that different inside. Not that it necessarily means anything — the most important changes of this sort are imperceptible to the one it's happening to, you hear — but as far as you're concerned you're still who you are, appearances notwithstanding. "Hm. Interesting. I wouldn't go as far as to say you're not one of us — if his divine lordship says you are, then that is the case — but there's probably one final step you have to take that won't come into play until your dying day. That would account for the... ah, discrepancies. Forgive me, I mean no offense, but I am merely telling it as it is." None taken. |"How are you acclimatising to your new form, your Eminence?" Komari asks. "The chaotic energies that were causing the high degree of mutability in your body should be mostly suppressed now, although there may be powerful or unforseen edge cases that may still slip through. Well, if that does happen, you just have to return to our divine lord and he'll set you straight." You're fitting in very well, and she's a dear for asking. It's a relief to be able to eat fruits, wines, stews and more without worrying about transforming into some kind of horrible chimaera. Sure, you could always just stuff your face again to change back, maybe with the aid of a little alchemy, but it could get irritating if you had a form you wanted to stick in. "And well, you more or less do." The fact that kitsune aren't really able to be changed drastically through any means should help, too. "Well, his divine lordship explained it to me once. It's less that we're resistant to changes, but more than we're incredibly prone to changes. This is what we look like, what we are, and our bodies know that. If you tried to change a kitsune away from his or her base form, it's not so much that the change doesn't take effect, but he or she changes back to the position of least energy so rapidly that no one ever notices. Like how water always tries to find the lowest point, you know? You can try to pick up water, but it just slips through and runs downhill again." And the end result is no different from as if they were immutable. "The differences do matter when one gets into certain details, your Eminence, but from a layman's point of view, you're right. Either way, I'm glad to hear that you're enjoying who you are, because if you aren't there's no backing out of this kind of deal. But you knew that before you said yes, of course." Of course. |"A little advice from one servant of the Trickster to another: it really isn't as hard as it might sound. By virtue of our divine lord's nature, we have a lot more autonomy and leeway to make our own decisions than those dedicated to the other great kami do. But with this freedom to act comes the implicit trust that we won't do anything in our standing as Keros' servants to bring shame upon his name... and of course, that we won't abuse that freedom. "Just remember that, and you won't go wrong." ] |[rand |"For all that we kitsune are prim and proper in our daily dealings, you would expect our patron deity to be much the same, wouldn't you? Well, yes and no. I've spoken face-to-face with his divine lordship many times, and he's always been the relaxed sort. Always uses plain language when speaking, a perfectly casual posture... he's the nice kind of friendly fox you can have a comfortable chat with. Thinks nothing of dropping by to say hello just because he was bored, and speaks his mind plenty." That sounds about right for his reputation as a trickster god, yes. But there's the other side of him... "...That you don't want to run afoul of," Komari says with a small sigh. "The laws that have bound and shaped the kitsune people for generations... he was the one who set them for our benefit, and woe betide the one who runs afoul of them and piques his interest enough to personally step in. Being declared outlaw, or even worse, no-face and being hunted down by your own is a tender mercy compared to some of the things our divine lordship has done to the admittedly very much deserving. And the Law of Equivalent Exchange... that is one which transgressors he takes a very dim view of. My anger at Mikoto and Miyuki during that whole business with Evergreen's bag... it was as much for them as it was at them. On the off-chance he decided to take a personal interest in their case..." Ah. You understand. "My fate is terrible enough, yet proportional to my failings. I cannot complain that it is overly cruel, and yet..." |"Unlike some Tiran and Lumian orders, service to his divine lordship requires neither celibacy nor abstinence. There wouldn't be entire clans of servants to the gods if we weren't allowed to take consorts, would there?" As far as you understand things, he's pretty permissive on such matters. "Don't get me wrong, there are still several schools of thought which promote asceticism, but those teachings are more philosophy and less theology. I took a husband in my day, and had a pretty large family to boot. Custom has it that if a priest or priestess dies, their consort usually fills their role. It's not uncommon for most shrines to be in the control of one family or the other, passed down from one generation to the next." |"One of the things I've noticed in my two or so centuries of exile across the ocean is that the way the locals handle worship of the Seven. More distant, and yet more reverent in their own way. Maybe I'm biased and only have seen a small slice of how religious rites are conducted amongst the natives, but from what I can tell most of the common folk make a show of piety once or twice a week and are content to set it aside for the rest of the time. "We don't work that way — if anything, we're more like the elven druids who still remain. Less impressive, but more constant observance spread throughout one's daily life. I suppose it's a result of how easily one can divide the divine and the mundane — they're more easily partitioned here, but where I come from the two are heavily interwoven." |"I really enjoy organising the festivals all year-round. Mikoto and Miyuki help me, of course, and a good matsuri is a good mood-raiser. Young people these days don't really think that much of propriating kami, be it the local forces or their own ancestral spirits, but everyone likes an excuse to goof off. Doubly so since life in the colonies and on the frontier is more in-your-face than anything else. Of course, I remember everything and try to keep the traditions straight — even if I have to make some changes because of where we are, ahaha. The point, as always, is to honor kami, from the great Seven to the littlest wilderness spirit." A foxen festival might be nice to see sometime; unfortunately, you're never around when these things happen. "The major observances are shared across the entirety of the Old Country, but every province and prefecture has its own unique customs and festivals. The dominion of the Cherry Blossom Throne is colorful that way; we believe in keeping things as localised as possible, where possible. Maybe you'll be fortunate enough to drop in when a festival's under way; it's not a sight an outsider gets to see from a neutral perspective." And what other perspectives might there be for a filthy foreigner like you? "Ah, that of a honored guest and benefactor, of course. What else? The hospitality and pleasure young folks are willing to show these days makes even me blush, oh dear." |"Many of the rites and rituals used by us originate from legends of the earliest times when his divine lordship Keros walked the land with his wife and concubines. The deeds of both him and those he met along the way... propriating kami aside, the rituals serve to tell those stories, if in a highly abridged form. From the steps needed to hear why local spirits are angry to ritual purification and exorcism, many of the rituals which Mikoto and Miyuki perform in their duties as shrine maidens are in essence a re-enactment of the events. I still remember when his divine lordship first came upon Miyuki in the midst of an o-harai great cleansing — ah, how he wept, and I dared not ask why. "Of course, since the kami of this land across the ocean differ from that of the Old country, I've had to make a couple of adjustments to reach out to them instead. Yet throughout all this, I've tried my best to keep the symbolism true to the source — his divine lordship has reviewed the rituals and has had no complaint, and there really isn't any greater authority on the subject than him..." ] ] "

rows.original: You spend a few minutes catching Komari up on the events that transpired outside the Grave of Saints, and your encounter with the masked assassin on the mountainside. When you're done, the governor frowns and clenches her hand around the head of her cane. "My apologies, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |Champion ], for the trouble one of my countrywomen has caused you. I assure you that if she dares to show herself within the colony's territory, she will meet the same fate as all her faceless kin: a swift end, in Keros' name." You ask if Komari knows who the woman was — she's the governor, after all, and the kitsune here are her responsibility! "Yes," she says evenly, "but I cannot be expected to keep tabs on every single vixen that passes through the torii gate. Slender and dark-haired describes half the women in the arcology; you understand." You understand Komari's holding out on you. She knew the assassin was a faceless the moment you brought her up. Komari sighs. "I cannot say for certain who she is, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence |[pc.name] ]. However, I am not entirely ignorant of who crosses into my domain. Twenty years ago, a young woman who matches the description you gave me entered the colony: young, pretty, reclusive, carrying little more than a blade, bow, and her clothes. She had papers indicating she was the sixth daughter of a small household from the outer islands, and was shipped off for one of those small, embarrassing infractions that once would get you banished to the outer provinces. Not an uncommon reason for coming to the colonies..." But? "... But her documents were forged, albeit by an expert's hand. It was enough to buy her time to settle. Still, a missive followed her some weeks later from the Old Country, asking that we keep watch for a wanted murderer who had become faceless in Keros's eyes: a young miss Ōshiro Shizuka. She had killed a masterless samurai by draining his chi completely, and then fled the islands before the Emperor's justice could find her. Unfortunately, by the time we were alerted to her true identity, she had already disappeared into the woods. Azami and Nakano's fathers were dispatched to track her down, but were unable to apprehend her. I am sorry to say that their failure has resulted in harm coming to your comrades, and for that you have my sincere apologies." Komari bows her head to you and tucks down her ears. "If it is indeed Miss Ōshiro, understand that she is a hardened killer and must be dispatched without mercy. Anyone who lays with her does so at the risk of their lives, to say nothing of her apparent skill with a blade." You'll keep that in mind. Now what was that about a samurai she killed? The governor's brow furrows. "I am not privy to the details, beyond the fact that he too was a suspected criminal. A bandit, perhaps, or kidnapper. I cannot say if they were in league, or if Ōshiro had fallen prey to him and sought revenge. Nevertheless, to use the Trickster's gifts to take another life is a capital crime, no matter the victim's own moral failings; if the precedent is set that it is permissible to drain someone dry because of that person's crimes, one would discover a sudden explosion of criminality in short order. It would have been more honorable to use a blade then, at least, as she has clearly proven able to today." A dead end for now, it seems. You thank the governor for her time.
rows.translation: 你花了几分钟时间向麻里讲述了在圣徒墓地外发生的一系列事件，以及你在山坡上与那个戴面具的刺客的遭遇。 当你讲完之后，那位女省长皱起了眉头，紧紧握住了她的手杖。“实在抱歉[pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |冠军 ]对于我的一位同胞给您带来的麻烦，我向您保证：如果她敢出现在这个殖民地的领土上，她将会和她那些无名同类的下场一样——以凯罗斯的名义，她也会很快遭到惩罚。 你问麻里是否知道那个女人的身份——毕竟她可是这里的统治者，而这些狐妖们也都是她的责任范围之内！ “知道，”她平静地回答，“但我不可能去监视每一个经过神社大门的狐妖。苗条且黑发的女性，其实占了这座生态城中一半的女性人口；你应该明白这个道理吧。” 你也应该明白，麻里之所以迟迟没有向你坦白真相，是因为她从你提到那个刺客的那一刻起，就明白那是一个没有任何身份背景、面目模糊的人。 麻里叹了口气：“我实在无法确定她到底是谁[pc.ra kitsune |阁下 |[pc.name] ]然而，我并不是完全不知道哪些人会闯入我的领地。二十年前，有一位符合你描述特征的年轻女子进入了这个殖民地：她年轻、漂亮、性格孤僻，随身携带的只有一把刀、一张弓以及自己的衣物而已。她持有相关文件，证明自己是外岛上一个普通家庭的第六个女儿，而正是因为那些微不足道、却足以让人被流放到边远地区的过错，她才被遣送到了那里。这确实是人们来到殖民地的常见原因……” “但是呢？” “……不过她的文件是伪造的，不过伪造者是个高手。这份伪造文件足以让她有时间安顿下来。然而，几周后，旧国却发来了一封信，要求我们留意一个在凯罗斯眼中已经变得面目模糊的通缉犯——那位名叫大城静香的年轻小姐。她通过吸干那名无主武士的生命力，杀死了他。气她彻底逃走了，在皇帝的正义之力能够抓住她之前就离开了那些岛屿。不幸的是，当我们得知她的真实身份时，她已经消失在森林里了。阿兹米和中野的父亲们被派去追捕她，但却没能将她抓回来。很遗憾，他们的失败导致了你的同伴们受到伤害，对此我表示由衷的歉意。 麻里向你低头，把耳朵也藏了下去。 “如果她真的是大城小姐的话，你要明白，她是个冷血的杀手，必须毫不留情地除掉她。任何与她发生关系的人，都是在拿自己的生命去冒险，更不用说她显然还精通刀法这一点了。 你一定要记住这一点。那么，她所杀的那个武士到底是怎么回事呢？ 州长的眉头紧锁：“我并不了解其中的细节，只知道他同样也被怀疑是罪犯——也许是个强盗，或者是个绑匪。我无法确定他们是否是同伙，也不知道大城是否成了他的受害者而因此选择了报复。但无论如何，利用欺诈者的能力夺取他人的生命无疑是一种重罪——无论受害者本身有哪些道德缺陷。如果人们认为因为某人的罪行就可以剥夺他的生命，那么很快，犯罪率就会急剧上升。那么，使用刀刃进行战斗反而会更加光荣——至少，从她今天的表现来看，她显然具备这样的能力。 看来目前这是个死胡同了。你感谢了那位州长抽出时间与你会面。

rows.original: [rand |[var0 |[rand |"Hm. It has come to my attention that Miko has been loaning herself out as a wet nurse on the sly; the silly girl thinks I don't know. Well, I do." That's not necessarily a bad thing, is it? "No, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]it's not. But given that I was young once, and very much like her, I know exactly what's going through her mind. Pardon my language, but — 'oh no, my tits are so full, so heavy, and so tender. Just squeezing and mauling them isn't doing anything, and my kits get full so quickly. If only I had an excuse to give suck and get a good dose of perverse pleasure out of it in the bargain...' See, that's what my poor great-great-granddaughter is thinking, because I was there once." You take it Komari didn't offer her services as a wet nurse back in her day, though... "It was sorely tempting, [pc.ra kitsune |my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |I have to admit ]. But even if I wanted to, no one would have taken me up on the offer, given my — ah — circumstances at the time. In retrospect, it was for the best." So, she's not going to do anything about wet nurse Miko? "The girl has exceeded me in that regard — I'm still in two minds as to whether we could rightly call her a cow at this point. At least her body isn't so absolutely bloated as it was just before she gave birth. So long as it's constructive and she's being seen as helpful, it's more than what her antics usually bring about and really, all I can reasonably hope for. There are worse things my great-great-granddaughter can do than ingratiate herself to other people and — " Komari sighs and closes her eyes as she forces the words out — "do something useful with herself in the process." |"Ah, Mikoto, Mikoto, what am I to do with her. Her appetite is boundless, her hunger insatiable; despite my best efforts, her innate gluttony has driven her to conceive kits by her sheer bodily hunger. It is not her fault that she is what she is, and yet her attitude is exceedingly troubling; it is not that she does not show remorse or contrition for her actions, but rather is fickle to the point where she forgets her recent acts without a care." Maybe having had children will settle her down. Komari looks absolutely incredulous for a moment, then sighs and shakes her head. "I don't know, really, I don't. Caring for those younger than her has been the only thing I can trust Mikoto with and not worry about, but even so...! I would like to be optimistic, but when you've lived as long as I have this particular hue and cry gets old the umpteenth time it plays out." So far, so good. Look, you can admit your agency in this whole matter as well, and you'll keep an eye on Miko while you're about. That may not necessarily be much, but it — and more — are what you can do to help the situation while you're around the den. "The girls have always wanted a little sister to dote on, but a child of one's own is quite different from that. I cannot say that my unease is assuaged, but at this point there is little that can be done about the matter. My only hope is that Mikoto does not dig herself deeper into this hole, silly girl that she is." |So, she's finally made a decision as to her successor. "The issue was forced," Komari replies matter-of-factly. "After having had a happy accident, as you might put it, there was no way things could continue as they were." Is... is it really that bad? The den matron doesn't answer for a second or two, then removes her headdress and mops her brow with the back of a hand. You note that there's no sweat to begin with. "Copulative activity is the most favored means of reciprocity for many of us, and keeping oneself mindful the consequences of one's actions is important. Mikoto was taught as she approached maturity and majority alike how to feed via sexual congress without conceiving. It was — is — a most fundamental matter, and failing to do so also would have meant she did not have the presence of mind to restrain herself as she ought, especially given her unique affliction. "I will not mince my words, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ]. There was a good chance you might have died when indulging my silly great-great-granddaughter. That there was intervention timely enough to save the both of you before something truly untoward happened does not diminish the seriousness of that fact. To say that it would be bad for [pc.ra kitsune |his divine lordship's own handpicked champion |someone ] to perish on our watch to something as preventable as that would be an understatement." All right, you're getting the idea of how terribly this must weigh on Komari. "If I had simply let Mikoto get away with it, it would have weighed a little too heavily on my impartiality as governor for the people to overlook — her shame would have stained me as well. So no. She has been properly chastised, not that her duties are going to be any lighter now that she is no longer in the running for the position of my successor.[pc.ra kitsune | | And far be it from me to reproach someone who may not have known the so-called proper etiquette, but given the aura my idiot great-great-granddaughter must have been exuding at the time, you must have been really courting death to want to copulate with that. ]" ] |[rand |"Mikoto is a troublesome child at times. Her appetite is boundless, her hunger insatiable; if not for her strict religious upbringing with its emphasis on the laws his divine lordship has laid upon us as a people, who knows what her innate gluttony may have driven her to do. It is not her fault that she is what she is, and yet she cannot be allowed to do as her nature dictates she would — not just for the sake of others, but to avoid imperiling her own spirit as well. A fine line to tread, and sometimes I am willing to overlook minor transgressions... and sometimes I am not." |[flags.MAI_PREG_ANN |So, she's finally made a decision as to her successor. "The issue was forced," Komari replies matter-of-factly. "After having had a happy accident, as you might put it, there was no way things could continue as they were." Is... is it really that bad? The den matron doesn't answer for a second or two, then removes her headdress and mops her brow with the back of a hand. You note that there's no sweat to begin with. "Of my two great-great-granddaughters, I had hoped that Miyuki would ultimately prove herself more conscientious — her main failing was, as you should be well-aware by now, her drug dependency to remain largely functional. Both her sister and I have attempted to persuade her over the last decade or more to wean herself of that need... but as you can see, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]a single loose beam in the supports can bring an entire building down. If the lower beams are not set straight, the upper ones will be crooked." You've heard rumors that Mai's dosage was no accident... "I'm not surprised; people will believe whatever makes them comfortable. Me, I've witnessed enough cruelties of simple fuckle chance to believe she could've made a honest, careless mistake, as meticulous as she usually was. It's easier to believe misfortune the act of some malicious, unseen hand rather than one's own oversight to avoid the blame from falling on oneself. If there were someone behind my great-great-granddaughter's mishap that evening, well, I don't have any evidence of it." So... she's not really mad at you for knocking up Mai? "I will not mince my words, [pc.ra kitsune |your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship |[pc.name] ]. There was a good chance you might have died when indulging my silly great-great-granddaughter. That there was intervention timely enough to save the both of you before something truly untoward happened does not diminish the seriousness of that fact. To say that it would be bad for [pc.ra kitsune |his divine lordship's own handpicked champion |someone ] to perish on our watch to something as preventable as that would be an understatement. "[pc.ra kitsune |Allow me to speak even more freely and bluntly, then, as one 'favored' servant of the August Master at the Center of Heaven to another |So there is that ]. Yes, you had agency in precipitating this situation. However, I will not overlook my great-great-granddaughter's agency in it either, which is far greater. The circumstances have chastised her enough, but her duties are not going to be any lighter now that she is no longer in the running for the position of my successor.[pc.ra kitsune | | And far be it from me to reproach someone who may not have known the so-called proper etiquette, but given the aura my idiot great-great-granddaughter must have been exuding at the time, you must have been really courting death to want to copulate with that. ]" |"Mikoto and Miyuki are unique in that between them, there is no clear successor when it comes to who should inherit according to our custom. Hence, I am quite free to assess them on their merits and keep them in competition with each other for the role until I make a final decision, which is still years off at this point. It is a luxury that I know full well few are able to enjoy. "At the same time... it's no secret that neither sister makes any major decision without consulting the other, so if you have one, you may as well have the other in the bargain." Between the two of you, who does she favor? "This is no secret, either; Miyuki is in the lead as far as I'm concerned. Then again, I suspect Mikoto is perfectly fine with letting her sister take the reins with these matters; the child is a little too scatterbrained to deal effectively with matters of state. She'll be far more useful as her sister's mouthpiece when it comes to getting people to accept policy." ] ] ] |Miko and Mai have mentioned that they're able to see auras, but you've never managed to get an adequate explanation out of them for what that exactly entails. To be frank, you suspect that they don't know it themselves in the same way fish live all their lives surrounded by water and don't give it much thought. Komari chuckles. "That's one way to put it, I suppose. Although to be honest, I'm not sure if I could give you a more thorough explanation. It's a gift that crops up in various priestly clans of foxes — the Kurokawa included — and tends to skip a few generations before surfacing in the bloodline again. Suffice to say that Mikoto and Miyuki have expanded consciousnesses when it comes to perceiving the supernatural and metaphysical; they have another sense that you or I don't. Miyuki describes it as shades of color laid over objects, Mikoto as a certain intangible quality or the other in her vision, as well as accompanying sensations in her veins. What soon became clear to their parents was that they were seeing and hearing things that couldn't be perceived unaided by most people. "When I learned of this, I sent for them to join me on this side of the ocean — they weren't very much more than bratty kits at that point, and their family was more than glad to have me take the duo off their hands. Untutored, someone who can see auras is quite the handful, and my dear descendants needed a lot of learning to keep their talents under control. "Such gifts never come without their price, of course. Mikoto's particular neurosis is quite evident in her insatiable appetite, but even Miyuki's inability to feel very much of anything is likely her mind and body adapting to the constant din she must be experiencing from the world around her. I have no definitive evidence of such, of course, and having known nothing else, Miyuki herself wouldn't be able to tell the difference. But... it is not a fine existence where one has to continually smoke winterstem just because the relaxing stupor it induces is more feeling, more alive than one's sober state of mind. Do not pity my great-great-granddaughters, but do not envy them, either." |You do have a question. Why do Miko and Mai speak the way they do? Even when they're speaking Belharan, they roll their vowels and slur their words, as if they can't be bothered to open their mouths to enunciate their speech properly. It makes the resultant drawl sound lazy, for lack of a better word to describe it. The vast majority of the other kitsune in the den don't speak this way, you've noticed. There's a certain lilt and musical quality to the way foxen speak Belharan which you assume is an effect of their mother tongue, but what Miko and Mai do is another kettle of fish altogether. "It's my fault. The two of them were born in one of the rural mountain provinces, and that's how they speak over there in my hometown. I myself made the effort to correct my speech patterns when it was decided that I would be the Lady Otomo's retainer, but I never had the heart to do so for those two. Colonials are looked down upon even more than provincials, so what would it matter? At least, that was what I thought at the time. If there's any shame in the way Mikoto and Miyuki speak, then it's on my shoulders, not theirs." Her other descendants don't speak like that, though. A nod. "Hitoshi and Nakano are fifth-generation colonials born and bred. They grew up here, and most of the people in the den are descended from immigrants from near the central coastal regions. Overcrowding near the capital, you see, amongst other reasons." |[flags.MAI_PREG_ANN |"For the longest time, the girls have desired a little sister to dote on," Komari says with a small sigh. "That was what they would ask me for every new years' when they were kits. I had to explain to them quite carefully that a younger sister wasn't something that they could just ask for as if it were some kind of present, but that didn't stop them from pestering their granny for one until they were about twelve. Of course, the capricious ways of fate means my great-great-granddaughter goes out and makes a child of her own. At least I hope that sates both of their desires for a little while..." Or maybe Mai having one of her own will just inspire Miko to go out and get one for herself. "Oh, I'm aware," Komari grumps. "Believe me[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence | you ], I'm well aware. While I thought I could put it off for another year or two, I've already seen to sifting through reasonable matches for my other great-great-granddaughter. If she wishes to indulge as well, then I too have something to learn about not procrastinating on important matters. I suppose that these two are no longer girls, for all that they might act like them, and if they wish to be thrown into the deep end then they're more than welcome to it." |"For the longest time, the girls have desired a little sister to dote on," Komari says with a small smile.
