The circumstances have chastised her enough, but her duties are not going to be any lighter now that she is no longer in the running for the position of my successor.[pc.ra kitsune | | And far be it from me to reproach someone who may not have known the so-called proper etiquette, but given the aura my idiot great-great-granddaughter must have been exuding at the time, you must have been really courting death to want to copulate with that. ]" |"Mikoto and Miyuki are unique in that between them, there is no clear successor when it comes to who should inherit according to our custom. Hence, I am quite free to assess them on their merits and keep them in competition with each other for the role until I make a final decision, which is still years off at this point. It is a luxury that I know full well few are able to enjoy. "At the same time... it's no secret that neither sister makes any major decision without consulting the other, so if you have one, you may as well have the other in the bargain." Between the two of you, who does she favor? "This is no secret, either; Miyuki is in the lead as far as I'm concerned. Then again, I suspect Mikoto is perfectly fine with letting her sister take the reins with these matters; the child is a little too scatterbrained to deal effectively with matters of state. She'll be far more useful as her sister's mouthpiece when it comes to getting people to accept policy." ] ] ] |Miko and Mai have mentioned that they're able to see auras, but you've never managed to get an adequate explanation out of them for what that exactly entails. To be frank, you suspect that they don't know it themselves in the same way fish live all their lives surrounded by water and don't give it much thought. Komari chuckles. "That's one way to put it, I suppose. Although to be honest, I'm not sure if I could give you a more thorough explanation. It's a gift that crops up in various priestly clans of foxes — the Kurokawa included — and tends to skip a few generations before surfacing in the bloodline again. Suffice to say that Mikoto and Miyuki have expanded consciousnesses when it comes to perceiving the supernatural and metaphysical; they have another sense that you or I don't. Miyuki describes it as shades of color laid over objects, Mikoto as a certain intangible quality or the other in her vision, as well as accompanying sensations in her veins. What soon became clear to their parents was that they were seeing and hearing things that couldn't be perceived unaided by most people. "When I learned of this, I sent for them to join me on this side of the ocean — they weren't very much more than bratty kits at that point, and their family was more than glad to have me take the duo off their hands. Untutored, someone who can see auras is quite the handful, and my dear descendants needed a lot of learning to keep their talents under control. "Such gifts never come without their price, of course. Mikoto's particular neurosis is quite evident in her insatiable appetite, but even Miyuki's inability to feel very much of anything is likely her mind and body adapting to the constant din she must be experiencing from the world around her. I have no definitive evidence of such, of course, and having known nothing else, Miyuki herself wouldn't be able to tell the difference. But... it is not a fine existence where one has to continually smoke winterstem just because the relaxing stupor it induces is more feeling, more alive than one's sober state of mind. Do not pity my great-great-granddaughters, but do not envy them, either." |You do have a question. Why do Miko and Mai speak the way they do? Even when they're speaking Belharan, they roll their vowels and slur their words, as if they can't be bothered to open their mouths to enunciate their speech properly. It makes the resultant drawl sound lazy, for lack of a better word to describe it. The vast majority of the other kitsune in the den don't speak this way, you've noticed. There's a certain lilt and musical quality to the way foxen speak Belharan which you assume is an effect of their mother tongue, but what Miko and Mai do is another kettle of fish altogether. "It's my fault. The two of them were born in one of the rural mountain provinces, and that's how they speak over there in my hometown. I myself made the effort to correct my speech patterns when it was decided that I would be the Lady Otomo's retainer, but I never had the heart to do so for those two. Colonials are looked down upon even more than provincials, so what would it matter? At least, that was what I thought at the time. If there's any shame in the way Mikoto and Miyuki speak, then it's on my shoulders, not theirs." Her other descendants don't speak like that, though. A nod. "Hitoshi and Nakano are fifth-generation colonials born and bred. They grew up here, and most of the people in the den are descended from immigrants from near the central coastal regions. Overcrowding near the capital, you see, amongst other reasons." |[flags.MAI_PREG_ANN |"For the longest time, the girls have desired a little sister to dote on," Komari says with a small sigh. "That was what they would ask me for every new years' when they were kits. I had to explain to them quite carefully that a younger sister wasn't something that they could just ask for as if it were some kind of present, but that didn't stop them from pestering their granny for one until they were about twelve. Of course, the capricious ways of fate means my great-great-granddaughter goes out and makes a child of her own. At least I hope that sates both of their desires for a little while..." Or maybe Mai having one of her own will just inspire Miko to go out and get one for herself. "Oh, I'm aware," Komari grumps. "Believe me[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence | you ], I'm well aware. While I thought I could put it off for another year or two, I've already seen to sifting through reasonable matches for my other great-great-granddaughter. If she wishes to indulge as well, then I too have something to learn about not procrastinating on important matters. I suppose that these two are no longer girls, for all that they might act like them, and if they wish to be thrown into the deep end then they're more than welcome to it." |"For the longest time, the girls have desired a little sister to dote on," Komari says with a small smile. "That was what they would ask me for every new years' when they were kits. I had to explain to them quite carefully that a younger sister wasn't something that they could just ask for as if it were some kind of present, but that didn't stop them from pestering their granny for one until they were about twelve. Looking back on it, it was rather cute, but it was still quite exasperating when I was the one who had to put up with them." Don't they have each other, though? "Yes, but even if Mikoto is the elder of the two, she and Miyuki see each other as equals. What they wanted was someone who was obviously their junior whom they could spoil and pamper — [kiyoko.isFree |and your daughter fits the bill perfectly. Ever since she came on the scene, those two have been all over her, playing the part of doting elder sisters perfectly. I'm not sure whether young Kinu is altogether too willing to be the recipient of so much attention, but knowing those two, they're not going to take no for an answer, are they?" Kinu has always played the part of elder sister to her siblings for as long as she's been alive. Maybe it'll be a good thing for her to be on the other end of thing for once. "You say that, but those two have a tendency to overdo things. I'll keep an eye on them as much as I'm able, but you should talk to Kinu from time to time and get her side of the story as well. I'm sure she'll have plenty of lurid tales to tell before long." |I'm a little surprised they didn't just go out and make friends with any of the other girls their age just to scratch that itch. For a couple of years, I thought that little Kohaku might have ended up as their pet, but nothing came out of that. I suppose those two are just so unique in their own way that it's hard for them to relate to other people, and that just makes them desire that kind of intimacy even more." You can understand their desire for a younger sibling, but maybe Miko and Mai are just a little too old for that, heh. They're grown women, after all. "I wouldn't know about that. From the way they act some days, I could swear they're still just girls getting into all sorts of stupid trouble. Miyuki serves as an anchor for her sister, but sometimes her weight isn't enough to stop Mikoto and she gets dragged along for the ride." ] ] |[flags.MAI_PREG_ANN |[rand |"Hm. It has come to my attention that Mai has been loaning herself out as a wet nurse on the sly; the silly girl thinks I don't know. Well, I do." That's not necessarily a bad thing, is it? "No, [pc.ra kitsune |your Eminence, ]it's not. In fact, it's not a bad solution to her dilemma where [mai.anyKids |her daughter's appetite simply doesn't keep up with her mother's production |she is aching and overfull, but without any recourse to relief ] — she may not be her sister, but the girl's still reasonably endowed. I was young once, and can easily imagine what's going on in her mind, because such urgency tends to bypass usual sensibilities. Pardon my language, but — 'oh no, my tits are so full, so heavy, and so tender. [mai.anyKids |My daughter simply doesn't nurse enough and i |I ]t's all got to go somewhere, so it may as well not go to waste.' That's what the girl's thinking, given that I trained her to be responsible." Well, that doesn't sound so bad. What's the problem with it, then? "I just wish she'd told me about it beforehand instead of going out and doing it on her own. Miyuki is still in a rather volatile state, and given that she's chosen to put herself into the hands of both me and her sister, I would rather she consult with the both of us before implementing solutions, regardless of how sensible they may appear at the time. We don't need her making another mistake in her current condition. "Don't get me wrong — so long as it's constructive and she's being seen as helpful, it's more than what her antics usually bring about and really, all I can reasonably hope for. There are worse things my great-great-granddaughter can do than ingratiate herself to other people and — " Komari sighs and closes her eyes as she forces the words out — "hopefully stabilize herself in the process." What does she see going wrong, then? Mai having an emotional breakdown in, uh, a compromising position? "That? I suppose it could happen, but I'm personally more concerned with the long-term effects of winterstem on her body and whether it's accumulated over the years, how long it would take to cleanse her systems of that drug —[mai.anyKids | While I'm worried about any potential effects even trace amounts might have had on her daughter, any damage that would've happened is more or less done already. No, ] my worry is that she may have inadvertently spread trace amounts of that drug around through her milk. The people of this part of the world may have a long history of using winterstem, but we don't, and it worries me. There may be nothing to it at all, but I would rather not take the risk and find out." |She's heard the rumors, right? About why Mai went off her leash that night? "You mean the unsubstantiated hearsay that her winterstem was somehow sabotaged? Yes, I have[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]." Komari taps her chin and thinks a moment. "My first instincts, both in knowing my great-great-granddaughters and the nature of talk as it goes around my seat of governance, is to dismiss it: the likely case is that it's either just people seeking an explanation and order in the capricious nature of existence, or it's that little golden ball seeking to cook up gossip for her own entertainment." So, she's disinclined to look into it? "I can't say that I'm terribly motivated[pc.ra kitsune |, your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship ]. I have looked into it because one had a lot of free time when one doesn't need to sleep, but without anything concrete to go on there simply aren't any leads to chase down. Hence, a cursory inspection of the matter has been enough to satisfy me, unless circumstances change." Hm... "It's not like this has been the first time that it's happened," Komari adds with a sigh. "Nor the second, for that matter. And for someone like me who has witnessed enough cosmic injustice, the desire to believe that everything happens for a reason is not as strong as it is in many of my subjects. Miyuki says that she double-checked everything and that she had properly compounded her medication that evening, but of course she would say such a thing and there is no one else to corroborate that claim. "And do allow me to be blunt to perhaps see the good that might be made of this mess — even if the circumstances are less than ideal, my great-great-granddaughter has finally found the will to wean herself of that damnable drug and face the pain that she was so deathly afraid of. If someone did indeed sabotage Miyuki's winterstem, I'm in half a mind to thank him or her for the service." |Is it okay for Mai to continue going out in public and continuing her usual work when she's still adjusting to not being able to smoke? She might have another episode like the one that sparked all this. "That is true[pc.ra kitsune |, your Eminence ]. On the other hand, it is vitally important that the girl return to some semblance of structure in her life — there is never any perfect solution, so I have simply made the decision that has the fewest number of drawbacks. Mikoto is helping her sister in dealing with her mental state with several traditional techniques, as well as some manuals which I have managed to procure from my connections in Macah. Ordinarily, I would not consider the latter, but the difference in my great-great-granddaughters' afflictions is such that the methods applied by Mikoto are not wholly suitable for Miyuki." It's good to see that they're working towards getting Mai's condition under control without the use of winterstem, but that doesn't quite address your concerns... "Yes, it's fine. It's not without its perils, but nothing is. Rest assured that both I and her sister are keeping an eye on her; the important thing is that she continue to deal with the world and other people while going through this. Avoidance of pain was the reason she's in the position she is in now, and there is no reason for me to permit that folly any longer. We don't want to shut Miyuki away from the world, we want her to be able to engage it on her own terms. And if she finds it hard... well, Mikoto did warn her that the longer she put it off, the more miserable the adjustment would be." Harsh. Fair, but harsh. "[pc.ra kitsune |Your [pc.mf |lord |lady ]ship, I can understand your concern, both for the girl's safety and of those around her |I don't blame you for being concerned; from your perspective, this might seem cruel and risky ]. But as the girl herself has so recently learned, promises from the gods aside, there are few assurances in life. So many years spent building her up with the expectation that she would be in line to succeed me, and now it's fallen to her sister. However, that should not prevent her from acting." ] |"The outfits Mikoto and Miyuki wear... just be appraised of the fact that they are very definitely not standard when it comes to shrine maiden uniforms," Komari says with a small sigh. "They do have much more proper ones we use for official ceremonies or when receiving dignitaries... but the ones that they don for their day-to-day duties are most unorthodox, to put it lightly." Well, she is the chief religious authority around these parts, as you understand it. Couldn't she have done something? "Well, there is one person who outranks me in the colonies. Guess who it is?" The Trickster himself. Of course. "His divine lordship likes their take on the traditional shrine maiden garb. He says it's very fitting. Form-fitting, more like... and then he said he wouldn't mind it if they wore them more when they went about the rites. And so they went and made more sets, and they're walking around in them every day, by divine order..." You have to admit, from what you know of the deity himself, that's very much like him. "I should have known better." ] ] "

rows.original: [rand |"I have a lot to thank Azami's ancestors for, even if she herself doesn't really know it," Komari tells you. "Directly in the wake of my exile, when almost all of polite society had shunned me, Azami's great-grandfather endured his own shame by sticking his neck out for me when I needed it most. The vast majority who accompanied me back across the ocean on the first official colonial expedition either had their own shame to hide or were under imperial command, but he accompanied me here of his own free will. Before time's fire consumed him, I promised [silly|Ishida-san|Azami's great-grandfather] that I would look after his line in these new lands, and have honored that promise." He sounds like the kind of friend anyone would be honored to have. "He was not a very good [silly|yamabushi|spiritualist], but that made him a great friend. By associating himself with me after my fall, [silly|Ishida-san|Azami's ancestor] willingly took on a burden of shame and stain on his spirit that drew him away from enlightenment. By rights, he should have eschewed worldly relationships and distanced himself from me like everyone else, yet gave that up for my sake; Faced between his lifepath and a friend, he chose me, and I understand enough of [silly|shugendo|his beliefs] to have some idea of what he did by setting aside the Way for a friend. "I cannot speak for our divine lord Keros, but I think he would have approved — tacitly, of course." |"Please forgive Azami if she performs her job a little overzealously. She understands the full weight of her station... that, and that dedicated streak of hers runs in the family. A more lax concierge would have perhaps assigned someone to do the job and be done with it, but she insists on performing the task herself as much as she is able." |Komari looks thoughtful. "To be frank, Azami is getting to be of that age — young enough to still be of marriageable age, old enough that one should start to be concerned. While it is true that she has siblings, I did make a vow to look after her line..." That's all well and good, but what does Azami herself think of it? "Oh, what does that matter to old meddlesome ladies with nothing better to do with their free time?" A chuckle. "Across cultures, races, distances, high or low, it's all the same: getting young people together is the pastime of old ladies like me all over the face of Savarra. I was young once, you know; all you have to do is make it feel like it just happened of its own accord, and she'll go along with it without complaint. Heh, I already have some ideas in mind." |"Azami and Miyuki used to play together a lot when they were younger," Komari says with a wistful sigh. "Their personalities weren't too different back then — quiet and stone-faced with few words and more action. Then they started to become women in their own right, and, ah, the straight-laced Azami didn't quite agree with how Miyuki would approach things. Despite their personalities still remaining similar at base, the way they expressed themselves... ah, let's just say Miyuki's constant smoking was irritating to her. I think they fell away from each other completely when she and Mikoto started wearing those things they call shrine maiden outfits... Azami stopped associating with her completely, and that would make sense. It's truly a shame they weren't able to see eye to eye, although given how they were I don't see how it could have worked out well. Having to choose between your beliefs or your friends is never an easy decision." |"The girl is never late, you know," Komari muses. "In the ten years since I officially appointed her to the position, Azami has never been late with her weekly report on the lay of the land and the movements of the peoples within. She doesn't always have something that's new or of import, but she's always thorough and never late. Not once. That's something I like about her and think Mikoto and Miyuki could stand to learn from. Not that those two would make the effort to be as on-point... Azami simply has it in her blood, while those two don't." ]
rows.translation: [rand |我有许多事情要感谢浅美家族的祖先们，尽管她自己可能并不清楚这一点。麻里会告诉你的。就在我被流放之后，当几乎所有上流社会的人都与我断绝往来时，阿扎米的曾祖父在我最需要帮助的时候，毅然站出来支持我，承受了由此带来的耻辱。那些随我一起参加第一次官方殖民探险、与我一起跨越大洋的人，要么也有自己的耻辱需要掩盖，要么是受帝国命令才与我同行的；而他却完全是出于自己的意愿陪伴我来到这里的。在时光的摧残将他吞噬之前，我曾向他承诺[silly|石田先生|浅海家的曾祖父]我承诺会在这片新土地上照顾好他的家族事务，并且一直恪守着这个承诺。 他听起来是那种任何人都会感到荣幸能够结为朋友的人。 他并不是一个非常出色的人。 [silly|山伏|通灵者]但这反而让他成为了我的好朋友。在我遭遇挫折之后，他选择与我在一起，与我同行。 [silly|石田先生|浅海的祖先]他自愿承担了那些令他心灵蒙羞的负担，这些负担使他远离了觉悟之路。按常理来说，他本应该像其他人一样远离世俗的纷扰，与我保持距离，但他却为了我放弃了这一切；在人生道路与友谊之间，他选择了后者，而我也足够理解他的这种选择。 [silly|修验道|他的信仰]才能稍微理解他为何会为朋友舍弃自己的道路。 我无法代表我们的神圣领袖凯罗斯发表意见，但我想他肯定会表示赞同的——当然，是默许而已。 |如果阿兹米在执行工作时表现得有些过于热情，请大家原谅她。她非常清楚自己职责的重要性……而且，她这种敬业的精神其实也是家族的传统。如果是一位态度较为松懈的礼宾人员，或许会派别人去完成这项工作，但她却坚持要尽自己所能亲自去完成它。 |麻里看起来若有所思。说实话，阿扎米已经到了那个年纪——还年轻，仍处于适婚年龄；但年纪也不小了，确实该让人开始担心了。虽然她有兄弟姐妹，但我确实立下过要照顾她的后代的誓言…… 这一切听起来都很不错，但阿兹米本人又是怎么看待这件事的呢？ 哦，那是……什么来着？那个这些事情，对于那些闲暇时光无事可做、喜欢管闲事的老太太们来说，难道真的那么重要吗？一阵轻笑。无论跨越何种文化、种族，无论距离远近，无论地位高低，道理都是一样的：让年轻人聚在一起，才是关键。那个这是像我这样的老妇人们在萨瓦拉各地都会喜欢的消遣方式。你知道，我也曾经年轻过；你只需要稍加努力就可以了。感受到就好像这是自然而然发生的一样，她也会毫无怨言地配合下去。呵呵，我其实已经想好了一些办法了。 |在年轻的时候，绫美和美雪经常一起玩游戏。麻里带着一丝怅惘叹息道。那时候，她们的性格并没有太大差别——都安静内敛，话不多，更喜欢用行动来表达自己。后来，她们开始逐渐成为独立的个体，而严谨的阿扎米显然不太认同美雪的处理方式。尽管她们的性格本质上仍然相似，但表达方式却有所不同……嗯，这么说吧，美雪总是抽烟，这真的让她感到很烦躁。我认为，当她和美琴开始穿上那些被称为“神社少女装”的衣服之后，她们的关系就彻底疏远了。……阿兹米彻底不再与她来往了，这也情有可原。她们无法达成共识，实在是一件遗憾的事。不过，考虑到她们的性格，我觉得这种结果也在意料之中。在信仰与友谊之间做出选择，确实从来都不是一件容易的事。" |你知道，这个女孩从来不会迟到。麻里陷入了沉思。在我正式任命她担任这一职务的十年时间里，阿兹米从未迟交过她每周提交的关于当地情况以及各民族动向的报告。她的报告内容并不总是包含什么新鲜或重要的信息，但她做事总是非常认真、细致。永远不会从不迟到。这一点我真的很欣赏她，而且我认为美琴和美雪也应该向她学习。不过，那两个人应该不会刻意去做到这么准时……亚纱美天生就具备这种素质，而那两个人则没有。 ]

rows.original: [rand |"My boy Nakano was born on this side of the ocean, making him a colonial. His parents live in one of the more distant settlements... ever since coming here to be at his granny's side, though, he hasn't looked back." It seems a little cold. "His calling is still to his clan, just a little closer to the center of power, that's all. We realize things for what they are, no more, no less. If anything, his immediate family is glad to see one of their own be elevated to such status. It is no loss, quite the opposite." But still cold. "At the highest peaks of his calling, my boy would be expected to forsake everything. His material possessions, his relatives, his relationships, everything except single-minded devotion to his liege. Which, as good fortune would have it, happens to be me in my position of colonial governor. At least I have his welfare in mind and am inclined to try and not give him orders that would bring him personal shame in the course of fulfilling his honorable obligations to me." This level of zealotry is not something you're familiar or comfortable with. "Or is it just that we're more honest and direct about it? As I understand it, there are militaristic religious orders in this part of the world that demand loyalty from their members above any other ties, going so far as to closter their members and ask them to renounce all ties from their previous lives. Lumia's valkyries... ah, such cold, single-minded dedication. I think the simple difference is that you do not ask yourselves what you would do if you were ordered to slay your friends because they were working against the aims of your order. The Lumians would obey, citing the glory of their goddess... and we would too, citing honorable service to a rightful liege." |"Please forgive my boy Nakano any slights, intentional or otherwise, he may give you. If they become too troublesome, please speak to me about them. [pc.ra kitsune |Even though you are now one of us, I can guess that he still harbours resentment not so much towards you, but to divinity itself for choosing you over one of our own. He knows this is terribly shameful, to not merely be contentious towards his liege, but to divinity itself... and even so, emotions are what they are. So when he is doing his utmost to be polite to you and give you the respect deserving of your station, your Eminence, I must humbly ask you not to needle him any further. There is little you can do to him that he is not already doing to himself. |While you have my express permission to enter and leave as you please, the decision is as ash in his mouth, even as he does his best to obey me. But that is the way of his kind... many of the acts required by the fidelity to his liege and family, of which I am both, bring shame upon his sensibilities and spirit. Sometimes shame in unavoidable in some form, and it truly cannot be helped... which is why my boy chafes against it so. He truly believes that this is not necessarily the case, and yet... "One way or another, I must ask of you not to needle him any further. There is little you can torment him with that he is not already inflicting upon himself in some capacity. ]" You'll try, but he ought to remember that you have bounds that can be overstepped, too. Having problems isn't an excuse to foist their unsavoury fruits onto other people — and to be frank, that goes doubly so in this society of ever-so-polite foxen. |"It's quite the impossible position Nakano's found himself in. The very people he wishes to earn recognition from in the capital look down upon him for being born a colonial, and yet his ethos demands his absolute obedience and loyalty to them. With this sham of an appointment, they've put him in quite the impossible position... which he's determined to succeed at anyway." Can he do it? "I did say it was an impossible position, but he truly believes that a man who is unafraid of death cannot be defeated even by overwhelming odds. That when he empties his mind and treats all other foes on the field as illusions, they part before his blade like water before stone. And that..." ...Is not something unheard of, even in this part of the world. Lupine berserkers have achieved legendary feats of strength while under battle-lust. "If it were merely but feats of battle and the clash of arms. This is far more than that... securing the frontier with seven fighting hands, himself included. The powdered pomps in the capital mean for my great-great-grandson to fail, and when he does they will mock him for not being just a colonial, but of the lineage of a disgraced exile to boot. Nakano's plan is to succeed despite their intent and wrest that commendation from their hands, but... ah, he is so beautifully, beautifully insane like so much of our warrior caste." I-is she hearing herself? She's talking about her own descendant here! "There's nothing that can be done about it, truly. Those like my boy have been the wellspring of tragic literature since the dawn of time. Truly, it cannot be helped." You just shake your head. Maybe you should stop discussing this right now before you dig up something more about kitsune culture you would really rather not have known. |"If you see Nakano with liquor of any sort, you have my permission to confiscate it on the spot. I've strictly rationed the amount he's allowed to have from Kohaku, but he keeps on getting more from goodness-knows-where, although I suspect that no-good brewer. If he complains, invoke my name and let him know the shame that's involved in [pc.ra kitsune|needing the divine champion [pc.himselfHerself] to step in with his problem|having an outsider step in to help with his problems]. Whatever his troubles are, drinking isn't going to solve anything." |"Has he asked you to partake of his poetry just — no, of course he wouldn't have. Not that you would have understood any of it, begging your pardon." Is Nakano's poetry really that bad? A terrible quality that transcends even languages and afflicts the unfortunate victim regardless of one's understanding of the words being spoken? Or it is something more mundane that relies on being able to understand the words on paper to inflict its terrible wrath upon the helpless? Komari raises a finger to her lips. "Eeh. Now that's a good question. I wouldn't say it's that bad, but at the same time if this got out to the other side of the ocean he would never live it down. I just wish he would spend more time on his painting instead, but he truly insists on bravely facing down what any sane person would recognize as a lost cause. Oh, brave, brave child of mine — and suicidally determined, too. Maybe one day he'll actually make it. I'm not going to hold my breath, though — he's been trying for at least the past three years without much in the way of improvement." |So, you've been wondering. If Nakano's a warrior, he's probably expected to keep his skills sharp, isn't he? And yet... you haven't actually seen him train... "Oh, he doesn't do it here. Please be reminded that the entirety of the western colonial garrison, which he has been placed in command of, numbers seven including himself. Those are even less than Azami's wildlings, who only have the roam of our immediate surroundings. And because they number seven, they do not warrant anything at all from his superiors in the capital, or at least that's what they say. The colonies... we are poor. No dojo. No barracks. No proper logistics. No anything and everything. His appointment as taisa is a sham. His fighting men and women... they are not quite dishonored in their standing as bushi, but everyone is here in the colonies for a reason. I do my best to surreptitiously aid my boy in my standing as governor, but he wants to succeed under his own strength. The poor boy truly believes that if he struggles enough, divinity will lend him and his strength to succeed despite being cast adrift. I have begged his divine lordship for any kind of boon he can grant poor Nakano. The Trickster finds the situation interesting, though, and wants to see how far my boy can be pushed before he has to step in with succor. "So to answer your question, we do not have what he needs here. When he wishes to muster his command, he steps through the torii gate to one of the dens further along the line and closer to the wilderness — there, he makes do with what he and his have set up under the trees and on the grass. The makeshift affair is terribly inadequate... but it really can't be helped, can it? My poor boy is the victim of political winds blowing back across the ocean, and here we have seven brave souls to keep the peace in all of the colonies. With such severe understaffing, he's had to work out several interesting systems of quickly mustering everyone when needed and bringing them to bear... it breaks most of what he's been taught and the methods are most unorthodox, but necessity is the mother of invention, is it not?" ]
rows.translation: [rand |我的儿子中野出生在海洋的这一边，因此他属于殖民地居民。他的父母住在一些较为偏远的定居点……不过自从他来到这里，陪伴奶奶生活以来，他就再也没回过那些地方。 似乎有点冷。 他的使命依然与他的家族息息相关，只不过现在他的地位更接近权力中心而已。我们只是如实看待事情的本质，不多也不少。事实上，他的直系亲属们看到自己人获得了这样的地位，反而感到高兴。这根本不是什么损失，恰恰相反。 但还是挺冷的。 在我儿子的职业生涯中，当他达到巅峰时，他必须放弃一切——他的物质财富、亲人、人际关系，唯有对君主的绝对忠诚除外。而幸运的是，这个君主正是我，作为殖民地总督。至少我会关心他的福祉，也会尽量避免下达那些会让他在我面前蒙羞的命令，从而帮助他履行对自己应尽的忠诚义务。 这种极端的狂热情绪，是你所不熟悉、也不习惯的。 还是说，我们只是更加坦诚和直接地表达了这一点而已？据我所知，在这个地区，有一些带有军事色彩的宗教组织，它们要求其成员将忠诚置于其他一切关系之上，甚至会将成员封闭起来，要求他们放弃与前世的所有联系。卢米娅的英灵们……啊，那种冰冷而坚定的忠诚。我想，关键就在于你们从未问过自己：如果被命令杀死那些与自己组织的目标背道而驰的朋友，自己会怎么做。卢米安人会遵从命令，因为他们会以他们的女神的荣耀为理由……而我们也会这么做，因为我们会以忠诚地为一位合法的君主服务为理由。 |请原谅我的儿子中野可能对您造成的任何冒犯，无论是有意还是无意的。如果这些冒犯给您带来了麻烦，请随时与我联系。 [pc.ra kitsune |尽管你现在已经成为我们的一员了，但我能猜到，他心中仍然怀有怨恨——这种怨恨并非针对你，而是针对神明本身，因为神明选择了你而非我们中的一员。他明白，这种行为是多么可耻：不仅对他的君主心存不满，甚至对神明本身也不敬。即便如此，情感终究就是情感。因此，当他竭尽全力地对您保持礼貌，给予您与您的地位相称的尊重时，我必须恳请您不要再对他加以刁难了。您对他所能做的那些事，其实他已经对自己做了很多很多。 |虽然我明确允许他自由进出，但对他来说，这个决定依然如同嘴里的灰烬一般令他难受，尽管他一直在尽力遵从我的意愿。但这就是他这种人的本性……许多出于对君主和家庭的忠诚而必须履行的行为——而我恰恰就是他的君主和家庭——都会让他的感情和心灵感到羞耻。有时候，这种羞耻感确实无法避免，也确实无能为力……这就是为什么我的孩子会如此抗拒这些规定的原因。他真心认为事情本不该如此，然而…… 无论如何，我都必须请你不要再折磨他了。你已经用各种方式让他痛苦了，而他现在也在以自己的方式让自己承受痛苦。 ]" 你会尝试的，但他也应该明白，你的忍耐也是有限度的，这些限度一旦被突破，后果也会很严重。遇到问题并不意味着就可以把自己的麻烦转嫁给别人——坦白说，在这个充满虚伪礼貌的社会里，这种行为更是不可接受的。 |中野所处的处境确实非常棘手。那些他在首都希望获得认可的人，正是因为他出身于殖民地家庭而看不起他；然而，他的信念却要求他必须对他们绝对服从、忠诚。通过这种名存实亡的任命，他们把他推入了这样一个进退维谷的境地……但无论如何，他都决心要成功摆脱这个困境。 他能做到吗？ 我确实说过那是一个毫无胜算的处境，但他坚信，一个无所畏惧的人，即使面对压倒性的劣势，也绝不会被击败。他认为，当自己抛开杂念，将战场上的所有敌人都视为幻象时，那些敌人就会像水遇到石头一样，在他的剑锋前纷纷退散。而且…… 即使在这个地区，这样的现象也并非闻所未闻。在战意驱使下，狼族狂战士们展现出了令人惊叹的力量。 如果这仅仅只是战斗与武器的碰撞，那么这一切就远不止于此了……他亲自用七只‘战斗之手’来守护边境。而首都里那些盛大的仪式，其实意味着我的曾曾孙将会失败，而当他失败时，人们会嘲笑他不仅是一个殖民者，还是一个声名狼藉的流亡者的后裔。中野的计划就是不顾他们的意图，一定要取得成功，把那项荣誉从他们手中夺过来……不过啊，他真的太疯狂了，和我们这个战士阶层的人一样，疯狂得如此美妙。 她……她自己听到自己在说什么吗？她现在说的可是她自己的后代啊！ 真的，对此无能为力。像我这样的角色，从古至今一直都是悲剧故事的主角。唉，这确实是无法避免的。 你只是摇了摇头。或许现在就应该停止讨论这个话题了，否则你可能会了解到更多关于狐妖文化的信息，而这些知识你其实并不想知道。 |如果你们看到中野带着任何酒类，都可以当场没收。我已经严格限制了他可以从琥珀酒厂获得的酒量，但他还是从不知哪里搞到了更多的酒，我怀疑那些酒都是那个不靠谱的酿酒师提供的。如果他抱怨，就以我的名义告诉他，这种行为是多么可耻[pc.ra kitsune|需要那位神圣的英雄[pc.himselfHerself]来解决他的问题|让外人介入来帮助他解决这些问题]无论他遇到了什么麻烦，喝酒都无法解决任何问题。 |他有没有请你去欣赏他的诗作呢？其实……不，他当然不会这么做的。更何况你也不可能理解那些诗的意思，实在是对不起。 中野的诗真的有那么糟糕吗？那种糟糕的质量甚至能够超越语言的障碍，无论人们是否理解其中的话语，都会让不幸的读者感受到它的伤害？还是说，这种糟糕的效果其实只是因为人们需要理解纸面上的文字，才会让这些文字对无助的读者产生伤害呢？ 麻里将一根手指放在嘴唇上。呃，这倒是个好问题。我不敢说它是那个这确实很糟糕，但同时，如果这件事传到了大洋对岸，他永远也无法释怀。我真希望他能把更多时间花在绘画上，但他却坚持要勇敢地去面对那些任何理智的人都会认为毫无希望的事情。哦，我这个勇敢的孩子……同时也充满了自杀般的决心。也许有一天他真的会成功吧。不过我也不会抱太大希望——至少在过去三年里，他一直在尝试，但却几乎没有取得任何进展。 |所以，你一直在想：如果中野是个战士，那么他肯定应该时刻保持自己的技能处于最佳状态，对吧？然而……你其实从未见过他进行训练…… 哦，他在这里并不负责这项工作。需要提醒的是，他负责指挥的整个西方殖民地驻军，包括他在内，只有七个人。这个数字甚至比阿扎米的那些野人还要少——那些野人至少还能在我们周围的区域活动。由于他们的编号是第七，所以他们根本不可能从首都的上级那里得到任何支持或帮助，至少他们是这么说的。这些殖民地……我们一无所有。没有道场，没有营房，没有完善的后勤保障，什么都没有。任命他为大佐不过是个幌子。他的战士们……作为武士的身份倒不算蒙羞，不过每个人来到殖民地都有自己的原因。作为总督，我一直在暗中尽力帮助我的儿子，但他更希望依靠自己的力量取得成功。这个可怜的孩子真的相信，只要他足够努力，即使身处困境，上天也会赐予他力量，帮助他取得成功。我曾恳求他的尊贵主人为可怜的中野赐予任何形式的帮助。不过，这个调皮捣蛋者觉得这种情况很有趣，他想看看我的孩子能被逼到什么地步，才会需要他出面提供援助。 所以，要回答你的问题，我们这里并没有他所需要的东西。当他想要召集他的部队时，他只需穿过鸟居那是通往沿线另一处隐蔽处的入口，那处距离荒野更近一些。在那里，他和他的同伴们只能在树下或草地上搭建简陋的住所。这些临时搭建的庇护所实在简陋至极……但也没别的办法了，不是吗？我那个可怜的孩子，其实是那些跨洋传来的政治风浪的受害者。而在这里，有七位勇敢的人正在努力维护所有殖民地的和平。由于人手严重不足，他不得不想出一些巧妙的办法，在需要时迅速召集所有人并让他们投入行动。…这些方法与他所学的大部分内容都相悖，而且极其非传统，但需求才是发明之母，不是吗？ ]

With such severe understaffing, he's had to work out several interesting systems of quickly mustering everyone when needed and bringing them to bear... it breaks most of what he's been taught and the methods are most unorthodox, but necessity is the mother of invention, is it not?" ] "

rows.original: [rand |"The most aggravating thing about that man is that he's perfectly capable of doing skilled, useful labor when the mood takes him. That there's the problem — when the mood takes him. No one should be doing work 'when the mood takes them', it's a daily essential of life anywhere. To have a man like him waste his actual talents instead getting drunk and seeking treasure in the wilds... the latter wouldn't be so bad if he brought back anything of note that was useful, like enough knowledge from which to piece together an accurate map. He's just so drunk he trips over his own feet half the time." Why hasn't she done anything concrete about him, then? A glint enters Komari's dead, glowing eyes. "What makes you think we haven't? Most respectable people will have nothing to do with him. If he weren't constantly plying my great-great-grandson with drink off the books, I'd complain about him a lot less." This... "When we have low-lying problems with people, we just box them in. Give them a nice position out of the way where they can't really do any harm, and leave them there until either they improve themselves, or the situation changes. Most people won't explicitly put it that way, or even consciously know they're doing it, but that's how it goes. Very polite and efficient." Now, they just send them to the colonies. "That's for problems that are slightly more aggravated and where boxing doesn't quite help... and let's be frank, where would we send Taka to? His family farm? At least here his slovenliness and drunkenness are carefully rendered harmless... or at least, relatively harmless." |"If the man weren't so much of a wastrel, there'd actually be pretty good demand for his liquor. It's one of the reasons I haven't given up on him yet. It's such a shame — his parents were such upstanding folk, inasmuch as I remember them. Individuals and faces of people you don't know very well tend to blur into one another when you get to my age..." Is there a chance he could get better? "Well, of course! Weren't you listening to me speak? If you want to try, you're more than welcome, but people will look down upon you for so much as speaking to the man. His reputation is as sour as the dregs of his rice liquor." |"As strange as it may seem, I think Takahiro and Azami may have something for each other. Even though the latter is openly repulsed by the former, they used to get along better before he took to the drink..." Huh. "It's problematic because I know the girl wants to get married, but she's earned enough of a reputation as a schoolmarm that no sane man would want to be her consort. Hence, we need an insane man to do it — and I suppose drunkenness is as harmless as it gets. If nothing else, it would be humorous to see them try and live with each other." She can't be serious about that, can she? "I honestly don't know myself." |"I just hope that the man's home for good this time. He may be a wastrel, but he's our wastrel, and it won't do for him to be wandering around getting into all kinds of trouble out there. At the very least if he stays here there's a chance that he might actually do some useful work." He's left before? "Repeatedly. I could understand it if he were prospecting or even charting new, unexplored lands... but let's not speak about it, it just makes me sad. If he's so interested in finding one of our divine lord's artifacts, why doesn't he just come up and ask the Trickster himself? I usually have his divine lordship over for dinner once a month, if not twice." ]
rows.translation: [rand |那个男人最让人恼火的地方在于，当他想做的时候，他完全有能力完成那些需要技巧、有用的工作。问题就在这里——只有在他想做的时候才会去工作。在任何地方，工作都应该是一种日常必需的行为，而不是取决于某人的心情。让这样一个人才白白浪费自己的才能，而不是去喝酒或在荒野里寻宝……如果他能带回一些有用的东西，比如足够多的信息来绘制出一张准确的地图，那么后一种做法倒也不算太糟糕。他喝得烂醉如泥，有一半的时间都是被自己的脚绊倒的。 那么，她为什么还没有采取任何具体的行动来对付他呢？ 麻里的那双毫无生气、却闪烁着光芒的眼睛里突然闪过一丝光芒。你凭什么认为我们没有采取行动呢？大多数正派的人都不会和他有任何来往。要不是他总是不停地给我曾曾孙子提供各种酒喝，我也不会这么频繁地抱怨他了。 这个…… 当我们与某些人之间存在一些小矛盾或分歧时，我们就会把他们隔离起来。给他们安排一个安全的位置，让他们无法造成任何伤害，然后就让他们待在那里，直到他们改正自己的行为，或者情况发生变化。大多数人可能不会明确地这样去做，甚至自己也没有意识到自己在这样做，但事实就是如此。这种方式既礼貌又高效。 现在，他们只是把这些东西送到殖民地去了。 那是针对那些情况稍微严重一些、拳击训练并不能有效解决的问题……说实话，我们该把隆也送到哪里去呢？让他去经营家族农场吗？至少在这里，他的懒惰和酗酒行为不会造成太大的危害……或者至少，危害相对较小。 |如果那个男人不是那么挥霍无度的话，他的酒其实会很有销路的。这也是我还没有放弃他的原因之一。真是太可惜了——据我记忆，他的父母都是非常正直的人。到了我这个年纪，那些你不太熟悉的人，他们的形象往往就会在记忆中变得模糊不清…… 他还有可能好转吗？ 嗯，当然可以！你刚才不是在听我讲话吗？如果你想试试的话，非常欢迎你，但是别人会因为你敢和那个男人说话而看不起你。他的名声可糟糕了，就像他喝的米酒剩下的残渣一样差劲。 |虽然听起来有些奇怪，但我认为贵弘和浅美之间或许存在着某种特殊的情感。尽管浅美公开表示对贵弘反感，但在他开始酗酒之前，他们之间的关系其实还算不错…… 哈。 这确实是个问题，因为我知道那个女孩想要结婚，但她给人的印象实在太像个严守规矩的教师了，根本没有哪个神志清醒的男人会愿意娶她。所以，我们需要一个神志不太清醒的男人来促成这件事——而我觉得喝醉应该算是最不会造成坏后果的方法了。至少，看着他们努力尝试共同生活，应该会挺有趣的吧。 她不会真的那么想吧？ 说实话，我甚至不了解自己。 |我只希望这次他能真正安定下来。他虽然是个游手好闲的人，但毕竟是我们家的人，让他在外面到处漂泊、惹是生非实在不行。至少如果他留在这里，还有可能做一些有用的事情。 他之前离开过吗？ 反复这样。如果他是在进行勘探，甚至是在探索那些尚未被人类发现的新土地，那我还能理解……但说实话，这真的让我感到很难过。如果他真的那么渴望找到我们那位神圣领袖的遗物，为什么不去直接去找那位‘戏弄者’本人询问呢？我每个月至少会邀请他的神圣领袖来吃一次饭，有时候甚至会请两次。 ]

rows.original: [kohaku.anyKids |[rand |"Kohaku came in and spoke with me today while holding her daughter — the girl was interested in making her position of storehouse quartermaster a hereditary position, at least for one generation. While I'm glad that she's inspired to take a greater interest in the future, I also have my reservations about the matter. After all, it's not customary for positions in the civil service to be formally hereditary — her daughter may have a leg up on other candidates by being immersed in the task since young, but the child must still eventually outdo the other candidates during selection." Even though the child is but an infant, Kohaku's absolutely convinced that she's going to be a perfect fit for the job down the line. "I'm not surprised, because I've been there before — we always want to think the best of our own children." Komari sighs. "That, and there's some truths to inclinations and talents running in bloodlines. That being said, it really is too early to tell, and it's not as if traits don't skip a generation or two, after all. Kohaku's own parents might have been shorter than average, but the cut of her figure is something that neither of them possessed." So, out of curiosity, what did she say? "I told that that while I wouldn't rule it out, I wasn't going to base important assignments upon the charisma of an infant as perceived by her mother and that she should speak to me again in a dozen years." So in short, she told Kohaku that it was complicated. A smile. "You really are catching onto how people talk about here." Hey, at least she didn't say it was difficult. That would have been an absolute no. To be honest, you think she just wants to keep the warpstone pendant in her family. It's technically still Komari's, right? That if Kohaku lost her position for some reason and very certainly had no prospects of ever going out to caravan, she'd have to return it? "There is some truth to what you say. While she was with child and had to hand over the pendant to whoever was heading the caravan... yes, there was a clear reluctance to allow it to leave her possession. The girl's started thinking of the artifact as her own, I'd say... but enough for her to want to rope her newborn daughter into it? "No. I've seen enough of the girl's real nature to know that while she might want it, I don't believe she wants it that badly." That's a relief, then. |Komari looks thoughtful and taps her chin. "While I've now permitted her to resume leading trade caravans from the den, Kohaku's come to me of her own accord and asked to be phased out from such activities. She's put forward one of her subordinates as her most likely replacement in this regard, so that the transition should proceed smoothly... I'm not entirely sure it's possible, though. It's more than just knowing the routes and talking to people — I don't think anyone else in the colonies has the gift of mimicry that she has, the kind of gift honed by an entire childhood desperate to please others." ...This is about her kit, isn't it? "Mm-hm. Even if the caravans are day trips and always back by evening thanks to her ability to use waystones and the torii gate network, I think the poor child feels extremely guilty about leaving her daughter in Hotaru's care while she's gone. No doubt the sting of abandonment from her younger days still remains." You've noticed. She's gone so far as to set up a crib in her little perch at the storehouse so she can keep an eye on the infant at all times. One might be worried as to whether Kohaku's getting a little too overprotective. "Don't you worry, I'll keep an eye on the situation. It's not that hard to make time when you don't have to sleep, after all." A chuckle. "But for now, I don't think it's a cause for concern — if anything, it's actually quite cute. I remember fretting all the time with my first child, and it wasn't until the third that I correctly figured out what warranted alarm and what didn't. With some luck, she'll settle into the role well enough. "In either case, I've acceded to her request — it's something that'll take a number of months to achieve, but someone else will eventually receive the waystone pendant and lead the caravans in her place. If anything, this came at a good time — I'm seeing some changes in the near future which will give me the opportunity to keep her busy at home with expanded duties in a slightly different direction. Poor Kobayashi won't have to hurt every time she hands her baby to Hotaru to be cared for the day." About the first part, though... Kohaku does eventually want her daughter to inherit her position, even if it's years down the line. "Oh yes, I remember that. Well, it's not like the idea of bench-warmers is unknown to us, nor is it upsetting if one's upfront about it. I understand that the concept's locally understood, if dressed up in prettier clothes. Regency and all." |"Tch. I was privately wondering if the girl's proportions would return to something slightly more sensible after she'd birthed the kit, but Hotaru tells me that she hasn't gone down one bit, not even an inch. It's true that just about all of the colonial women do get more curvaceous while with child, an effect that's only grown more pronounced with successive generations, but it's a two steps forward, one step back thing. Little Kohaku, though, has clearly forgotten to take that step back. I must say, I'm disturbed and fascinated by it all at once." With you, it's more the latter than the former, but you can understand her perspective. A sigh. "It's just that those proportions remind me of a daruma. I —" A what, now? "A children's toy where I come from. It's a fat-bottomed doll that rocks back upright when you try to push it over, partly because it's got such a wide base and partly because so much of its weight is concentrated in its bottom. Much like what the poor girl's become, although I really don't recommend trying to push her over to see if she'll roll back up." It — well — you know it shouldn't be possible, but now that Komari's mentioned it, the temptation is there. It really does look like Kohaku's going to be carrying an extra wiggle in her step and sway in her tail from now on, then? "And given the trend, I'll predict that it'll be moreso after she's had another. I wonder what effect this will have on how future generations look, if his divine lordship deigns to keep me around that long." |So... she's not mad at you for your role in all of this? "Like most things that happen, there's the good, and there's the bad," Komari replies with a sigh. "Since you're not to blame in all of this, I see no reason to make you the subject of my displeasure. If you want to know the details, you can ask little Kobayashi herself, although I think that this might be one of the few things in all of Savarra that she might not want to gossip about. Then again, she somehow let slip that it was her who kicked you in the back of the knees and got herself into this mess, so... well, we'll see." That particular anecdote is going to be chasing you around the den for the foreseeable future, isn't it? "You should be glad; it absolves you of responsibility for the situation. If I didn't know as much, I might be considerably more upset at you than I already am. Not that futile anger ever solves anything by definition, even if it's cathartic at times. "Whatever the case, since you're not responsible for the bad, I'd prefer to focus on the good that's come from this entire situation when it comes to you. Far more preferable, isn't it?" |This is an odd question, but Komari does know that Kohaku's made a crib for your daughter right next to her desk, right? You take it that this isn't a common thing around these parts? "Take it from an old woman: it's wise to keep your loose children at hand at all times," she answers with a cackle. "But yes, I gave her permission to do as much, so I know of it." Huh. Kohaku actually asked? "Well, not in so many words. We did that little social dance where a subordinate needs something, but it would be improper to ask directly. Therefore, it falls upon the senior to intuit from context, subtext and other hints as to what exactly it is the subordinate wants and to magnanimously grant it out of the blue. Thus, the exchange reflects well on both parties, and as an added bonus is absolute obtuse and indecipherable to any outsiders." ... "But yes. The poor girl just doesn't want her daughter to have the same experiences she had, so I was willing to indulge her even if the details of the request were a little unorthodox. There may have been some concerns about a very young kit in the storehouse, but it's removed enough from all the heavy goods that I don't believe it poses an elevated risk of accident. That, and asking the girl to pass off her kit to Hotaru or me every morning would have broken her heart, and I can't have that; it's not as if she'd be able to get anything useful done if I'd forced the issue. Part of efficient management is understanding your people, after all." So she's letting Kohaku keep the kit with her at all times. "Just so." ] |[kohaku.pregStage 1 |[rand |Admittedly, you've been curious. How has Kohaku's family taken the news that she's pregnant? "Family. Ah, family." Komari deflates a little. "Practically speaking, I am her family. No, her parents are still in this world, but one can hardly prospect while remaining safe and sound in the bosom of civilization. They return once a year to settle their obligations with the government — that is to say, me — but otherwise are out there seeking the motherlode." So they don't know yet. "Like I said, [pc.ra kitsune |champion, ]for practical intents and purposes I am her family; she was left in the care of the colony at a young age and I took her in. When you've existed as long as I have, it's nice to have a child about the house for a decade and a half or so. Keeps the mind occupied and positive. I suppose her blood kin will eventually find out when they return here to settle their accounts, not that I expect this change to be more than a footnote on the story of their grand adventure of discovery. Meanwhile, their daughter has brought in more high-grade iron in a few short years than they have in all their absence. Rest assured that I'll be pressing both points home while harping on how they've wasted the last decade and a half fruitlessly the next time they come around." The note of dry melancholy in Komari's voice is unmistakable, and you shake your head. No wonder why Kohaku feels so strongly about this impending child. "That may be one part of it, yes. But to answer your question, [pc.ra kitsune |divine champion, ]I am fully aware of her condition and the challenges that are likely to follow. Perhaps I'm even favorably disposed to her situation to an inordinate degree; she was, and still is, one of the better kits I've fostered in my time. "While I can't say that I'm fully on board with the events that led to these circumstances, I also know it's not your fault. Playing up her cuteness and appeal has gotten the child through many sticky situations in the past, but the cold indifference of cosmic injustice cares little for petulant yet adorable displays." Perhaps you can guess: it can't be helped and nothing can be done about it? Komari smiles thinly. "[pc.ra kitsune |Why, divine champion, you're starting to truly become one of us if even you are beginning to understand the long-suffering spirit of our people |Well, I see something's rubbed off onto you, for you to come to that understanding ]. But no, it can be helped and there are indeed many ways in which I can do something to make her life easier in the days to come. The other half of the question is whether the poor child will swallow her pride and accept it." That's where you come in, then. "If you could change her mind on several points, that would be appreciated." |You hear that Komai's stopped Kohaku from going out on caravan while she's with child? "Yes. I've instructed her to delegate it to one of her underlings, and to pass on the waystone necklace to whoever it is while they're out. Needless to say, there is almost no external trade for the time being, be it with the Old Country, in this locale, or in any of her usual haunts that the old imperial waystone network afforded. Few are as adept at disguise and mimicry as Kohaku, and it'll take time for us to work something out." Huh, she seems quite calm about the matter. You'd have expected her to be more angry about it. "It is not a serious problem[pc.ra kitsune |, divine champion ]. This place is designed to be self-sufficient and to survive a siege if necessary; if anything, I should thank you for helping bring about this situation to test my fallbacks should external connections suffer disruptions. Allow me to be blunt: the kind of people who are banished to, or are desperate or insane enough to voluntarily come to the colonies are those who can be expected to bear the lack of a few creature comforts." All right, then... "If you're concerned and wish to do something about the situation, [pc.ra kitsune |divine champion, ]I would [pc.ra kitsune |humbly ]suggest that you bring things in during your visits and sell them to her. While I can't guarantee that the storehouse can give you an excellent price for the goods — I foresee that currency will swiftly be in limited supply for strange and inexplicable reasons — the moral satisfaction of helping out Kohaku should more than make up for it, no?" |So, Komari's not mad at you for knocking up the storehouse quartermaster? "Hmm. Were I two centuries younger, I might have[pc.ra kitsune |, divine champion ]. But I'd like to imagine I've become a little more discerning since then. To be sure, having kits out of wedlock can pose problems, but here in the colonies they are more material than social ones. No one expects very much from the dregs of society, after all." Barring the implications of that last statement... you'd like to talk about the first bit. Komari really isn't mad at you? "To be honest, I was half-expecting something like this to happen. The dear child has always been a people-pleaser and adept at mimicry... when she was younger, she tried to change herself to fit in with the people around her, and achieved little save for missing the chance to figure out who she really was inside. I thought I set her as straight as one can be in that regard, but it does seem like she's backslid somewhat after leaving my care. "All the young people are having children these days, a good sign that they have confidence in the future. I suppose she wanted to follow the trend at some level and blend in, but didn't want to go the long way. Not that I'm saying she consciously planned all of this, but we want what we want, even if we don't consciously know it." That's somewhat of a relief to hear. If this is how it went down after Kohaku had planned it... "As I understand the events, she kicked you in the back of the knees with great and careful deliberation when you realized what was going on and tried to withdraw, forcing you to spend your seed inside her," Komari says with a straight face. "Having experienced similar impulses when I was her age, I will say that this pins a good deal of the blame squarely on her. It began like any other beneficence and you tried to stop once you realized that something was amiss. I don't think any fair-minded judge would hold you responsible for what happened." That's surprisingly open of her. But of course, fair-minded is the operative phrase here. A thin smile. "Yes. Either little Kohaku has agency as a person, makes her own decisions, and lives with them — or she's just a helpless waif who just has things happen to her and nothing is ever her fault. One can't have it both ways." That, and you can only wonder how that particular fact about her kicking you in the back of the knees got about. Only Kohaku and you were there, and you certainly haven't told anyone in the den. "I'm sure she let it slip while bragging without realizing the full implications of what she was saying. Which isn't like her, to be sure, but then she's been most unlike herself ever since her belly started to swell with child." Komari chuckles. "Well, unlike herself in a way that could only be expected of her, if you get what I mean. Either way, she's going to have a hard time pinning the blame on anyone but herself and one moment of greedy indulgence. "Either way, I wouldn't be too concerned about it. I'll be keeping a close eye on her, for amusement value if nothing else." |Would it be possible for Komari to keep an eye on Kohaku for you while you're out of the den? It might be too much to ask the colonial governor herself to have a personal hand in the matter, but she's also one of the few people whom you know in this place who also are in a position to do something meaningful... "Oh, I already am, don't worry about it. For example, the dear child knows that any time she needs a moment's respite, she's more than welcome to leave her post and take the rest of the day off." But she won't do that. Not just because the work will still be there when she gets back, but also she feels the responsibility to be the last one to leave after all her subordinates are gone. "You might consider it a test of whether she's able to swallow her pride and accept necessary help. Don't look at me like that — as I said, she has my full permission to do as she pleases, so the only thing keeping her from acting is herself." She's using this as a test? "It's under pressure that our true natures are revealed. For someone who wears as many layers as my dear little Kobayashi, this should be interesting to see, or at least for those around her. The girl and her future prospects... I want to see if she's learned something from her childhood or not. Just how much has she invested into her persona of being cute and conscientious, I wonder? Will she break herself before she can overcome her pride? For someone who has to fit people where their talents and inclinations are best suited to their tasks, that's extremely pertinent information." |You have to ask, since Komari's had the chance to observe multiple generations of kitsune over the years — is what's happening to Kohaku normal? "There are many things happening to little Kobayashi that could be considered normal or not normal. You'll have to be more precise, I'm afraid." Her body, that is. She was already pear-shaped to begin with, but after having conceived just about all of the excess weight has gone into the lower half of her body to produce quite the exaggerated figure. You'd have expected her to balance out up top, or at least keep her current proportions, not... well, this. "Curiouser and curiouser," Komari replies with a smile. "Why would you expect her to 'balance out', as you put it, with a more maternal body?" Because... well... "Do you dislike what she's becoming? Oh wait, don't answer that question. Instead, I'll answer yours — it's not 'normal' by the colonies' standards, but I wouldn't expect it to apply to her anyway. Do remember that little Kobayashi is but a second-generation immigrant, so I would expect a minimal if any effect the locale has had on here, as opposed to the older colonial bloodlines who have been here for five or so. Whatever it is, she or her parents brought it over with them from the Old Country. "To be fair, we haven't had many people from that part of the coast — maybe one or two. They don't do that much to warrant deportation to the colonies, poor things either behave themselves or do something to warrant execution. Something about the local culture, I believe." So long story short, she has no idea? Komari scratches her chin thoughtfully. "To be honest, I find the prospect rather exciting. The general trend of the colonials has been to grow more robust with each generation, in accordance with the local environment and what, hmm, nutrition is available. If this is what's happening to the dear child after having conceived once, I wonder what would happen on her third or fourth. It's a good thing we don't have to watch our numbers that stringently as we do across the ocean — I do want to see how little Kobayashi's bloodline mixes with others in time to come and what effects it might have on her descendants. That's assuming of course, that his divine lordship sees fit to keep me around that long. "Oh, don't look at me that way. When you get to my age, this is one of the few pleasures left to the world-weary." ] |[rand |"Kohaku is such an adorable little thing, it's no surprise that several eligible men already have their eyes on her. So great is her allure, the fact that she's a merchant in all but name doesn't faze them in the slightest. No, little Kohaku isn't exactly the ideal specimen of kitsune womanhood, but that infectious energy... haa, it reminds me of one of my sisters. That was so long ago..." "And don't think she doesn't know it, either — she is a businesswoman, after all. Not letting others know you're leaning upon your leverage for all it's worth is a tool of the trade, after all. Whatever other skills Kohaku may have, remember that deception is one of them." |There's something you've been wondering — even when she's speaking Belharan, Kohaku has this cute little verbal tic that she sometimes tacks onto the end of sentences. "Nojya", or something like that, was it? While you get that it probably means something in her native tongue, Komari would probably be the one to make most sense of it, especially since asking Kohaku herself about it would be a little awkward. "Kohaku's family comes from one of the coastal bay areas in the Old Country," Komari explains. "You could consider it a regional accent of sorts, I suppose — formally, it's used to soften one's words and make them sound more yielding and less forceful in a bid to sound polite. It's somewhat archaic, which is why it's still only in use in that particular coastal region." Huh, that's interesting. Is it actually possible to figure out someone's roots from how they speak? "The Cherry Blossom Throne has been a lot less interested in unifying the spoken word amongst its subjects than, say, Belhar used to do back in the day. Those who are formally educated or do business with the capital do beat their regional accents and dialects out of their language and adopt the imperial standard, but otherwise yes, it is possible to guess at what part of the country someone hails from if they speak in certain fashions. Those who settle in the colonies come from all over the Old Country, and Kohaku herself is but only of the second generation removed from her homeland. That she subconsciously keeps some of her old mannerisms when not outside of the den is unsurprising — she has to spend so much time pretending to be someone she isn't, so it's good for her that she has something of her own to anchor herself to who she is." |"Heh. Nakano really gets overly concerned about Kohaku 'going native', as he puts it. That she adopts their style of dress when out doing business with them is unavoidable, but to continue doing so while in the safety of the den... I think she only really dresses up for festivals and important occasions, otherwise she clothes herself as the natives do." And what does she think about it? Komari appears to ignore your question. "They really have their own ways of dealing with their problems, you know. Kohaku... mimicry is her forte, and she so badly wants to fit in with others that she might very well lose track of who she is to begin with. The natives of this land are friendly enough to her when they think she's a catfolk... but let that mask slip, and few can deny it'd be a very different situation. Then again, complete rejection of what this land across the ocean has to offer is something that she can't do, not just because of her job, but it wouldn't be in her to do so. It's a fine line between worlds some of these kits have to walk, and I don't really envy them for it." |"Landing Kohaku into the position of storehouse manager was fortunate to happen when it did," Komari tells you. "While most positions tend to run in families, her predecessor wished to return to the Old Country with his family, leaving the post vacant. The girl had a decent head for numbers, plenty of charisma, and looked completely adorable and harmless to boot. While her father was off in the wilds prospecting, I taught his daughter how to turn her apparent weakness into a strength. Now... ah ha ha. She'll rob you blind and you'll be smiling while she does it." It's hard to believe. "That's the point. Big, smiling face and bright eyes. Large, perky ears when compared to her head. Small, curvaceous and earnest. The sort of adorable creature you want to buy something from just to bring a smile to her face. Every time she goes out with our surplus to somewhere like Tychris, she always manages to get good deals. Personal charms and a silver tongue, much like her father — I couldn't ask for more from the girl. Frankly, my only hope is that her kits will inherit those talents so I don't have to worry about staffing her position for the next generation." |"You've noticed that the girl carries a waystone key on her, haven't you?" You've seen the blue stone on the pendant about her neck, yes. It never leaves her person, you've noticed. "It's on loan from me; every merchant who's represented the den has worn it while they've held the post. While you don't need a key to enter The Ways Between from a torii gate, being able to use the old waystone idols to get from place to place in the Marches is a blessing, and makes the girl's task so much easier. Less travel means less time in dangerous territory, less risk, and a lot more ability to respond quickly to and capitalise on situations, surpluses and shortages than a normal merchant would. I decided a few generations ago that I didn't need it, so it would be better in the hands of someone who could make better use of it than I could." Which leaves the question of where she got her key in the first place. Komari waves off the question. "Oh well. The Godswar was a terrible time. Used to be that almost every watered-down aristocrat of the Empire had one of these to zip from place to place unseen... pity so many of them perished in those times." |"It's a little amusing how things have turned out between Kohaku and her father, to be honest," Komari tells you. "He uprooted their family to come to the colonies in search of iron and other metals... while he's had some finds over the years, Kohaku has garnered more than he's ever had by trade, or simply going up to people and offering to cart away their mining waste. It'll probably change if the local people ever figure out how to work iron effectively... but for now when everyone's fixated on bronze, little Kohaku is making out like a bandit and snatching up huge amounts of high-quality hematite and other useful ores the locals consider worthless by-products of tin extraction." That's the ideal situation when it comes to business, though, isn't it? One man's trash being another man's treasure? It must sting Kohaku's father for his daughter to outdo him like that, though... "Oh, by no means. The man was plenty jovial the last time he dropped by the den about a half-year ago. I think the prospecting is just a cover for what he really wants to do: go out into the mountains and wilds and have grand adventures with his wife and hirelings. His daughter's inherited a lot of that, although her adventures involve sneaking into native settlements while in disguise and no one being the wiser. That, and she appreciates the luxury of sleeping in one's futon at the end of the day instead of a straw roll." So, the iron trade is doing well, then? "Never been better, and it's thanks to the girl. Ah, wouldn't it just burn up my dear great-great-grandson to learn that a merchant had received an imperial commendation before he did — and with the sheer volume she's been shipping back through the torii gate each month, she's well on the way to one. Who knew simply buying it from the locals would be so much more efficient, if less secure, than digging it up yourself?" ] ] ]

|今天，小白抱着她的女儿来找我谈话。那个女孩希望将自己的“仓库军需官”这一职位设为世袭职位，至少让这一职位能够遗传给下一代。虽然我很高兴她对未来表现出如此浓厚的兴趣，但对此事我也有些顾虑。毕竟，在公务员系统中，职位通常并不是世袭的。虽然她的女儿因为从小就接触这些工作而可能比其他候选人更有优势，但在最终选拔过程中，她仍然必须证明自己的能力比其他候选人更强。" 虽然这个孩子还只是个婴儿，但琥珀坚信，她将来一定会非常适合这份工作。 “我并不感到意外，因为我也曾经有过同样的经历——我们总是希望自己的孩子能够做到最好。麻里叹了口气，说道：‘确实，有些天赋和性格特征确实是与遗传有关的。不过，现在下结论还为时过早——毕竟，这些特征有时也会隔一两代人才会在下一代身上体现出来。虽然小白的父母身高可能略低于平均水平，但她的体态却是他们两人都没有的。" 那么，出于好奇，她到底说了什么？ “我当时说的是，虽然我不排除这种可能性，但我不会根据婴儿母亲对婴儿魅力的主观判断来决定重要的任务安排，而且她应该再过十年再来找我谈这件事。 简而言之，她告诉琥珀，这件事很复杂。 一个微笑：“你真的开始学会这里人们说话的方式了。” 嘿，至少她没有说这事情很难办。那绝对是不可接受的。说实话，你难道认为她只是想把那枚扭曲石吊坠留在自己家族里吗？从法律上讲，那东西仍然属于小玛丽，对吧？如果琥珀因为某种原因失去了自己的地位，而且根本没有任何机会再参加商队旅行，那么她就必须把那枚吊坠归还回去，不是吗？ 你说的确实有一定道理。当她怀着孩子，不得不把那枚吊坠交给负责带领商队的那个人时……没错，她显然很不情愿让它离开自己的手中。我想，那个女孩已经开始把这件文物当作自己的东西来看待了。不。我已经足够了解这个女孩的真实性格了，因此我知道，虽然她可能想要这样做，但我认为她并没有那么强烈的愿望。那可真是让人松了一口气。 |麻里显得若有所思，轻轻敲着下巴说道：“虽然我现在已经允许她重新带领商队出行，但琥珀主动来找我，表示希望逐渐退出这类活动。她还推荐了自己的一名下属作为最有可能的接替者，这样过渡过程应该会顺利进行。不过，我并不是完全确定这是否可行。这不仅仅意味着要熟悉路线、与人们交流——我认为，在殖民地里，没有人拥有她那样的模仿能力，那种因为整个童年都在努力取悦他人而锻炼出来的能力。……这应该是关于她的技能组合的，对吧？” “嗯，没错。凭借路石与鸟居网络，商队的行程即使要花上一整天，也总能在傍晚前返回，我想这个可怜的孩子一定对自己在离开时把女儿托付给萤照顾感到非常内疚。毫无疑问，她年轻时所经历的被抛弃的痛苦至今依然萦绕在她的心头。 你注意到了吗？她甚至在仓库里的那个小角落里搭了一个婴儿床，这样就能随时照看那个婴儿了。有人可能会担心，琥珀这样做是不是有点过于保护孩子了。 别担心，我会密切关注情况的。毕竟，当你不需要睡觉的时候，安排时间其实并不难。”他轻笑了一声，“不过目前来看，这并不值得担心——反而还挺可爱的呢。我记得生第一个孩子的时候，总是忧心忡忡，直到第三个孩子出生后，我才终于弄清楚什么情况真的需要担心，什么则不需要。希望她也能顺利适应这个角色吧。 无论如何，我都已经答应了她的请求——虽然这需要花费数个月的时间才能完成，但最终会有人接过那枚路标吊坠，代替她来带领商队。事实上，现在正是实施这个计划的最佳时机：不久的将来我会遇到一些变化，这些变化会让我有机会让她在家里承担一些新的职责，从而让她有更多的事情可做。可怜的小林女士再也不用每次把宝宝交给萤照顾时都那么担心了。 至于第一部分……其实，琥珀确实希望自己的女儿能够继承自己的位置，哪怕要等很多年之后。 “哦，对了，我记得这件事。嗯，我们其实并不排斥有‘替补者’这样的存在，如果有人直截了当地表达这个想法，我们也不会感到不快。我明白，在这个地方，这个概念已经被人们接受了，只不过人们会用一些更美好的说法来表达它罢了。比如‘摄政时期’之类的。 |啧，我之前还在私下想，那个女孩在生下孩子后，她的身材比例会不会恢复得稍微合理一些，但萤告诉我，她的身材一点都没有变差，甚至丝毫没有下降。的确，几乎所有在殖民地生活的妇女在怀孕期间都会变得更加曲线优美，而且这种变化在后代中表现得更加明显，但这种情况往往是‘前进两步，后退一步’的。然而，琥珀却显然忘记了要退后那一步。我必须说，这一切既让我感到不安，同时又让我着迷。 有你在，情况更偏向后者，而不是前者，但你可以理解她的立场。 一声叹息。“只是那些比例让我想起了达摩像。我——” 什么？现在又说起这个来了？ 在我家乡，这是一种儿童玩具。它是一个胖乎乎的玩偶，当你试图把它推倒时，它会重新直立起来——这部分是因为它的底部非常宽，另一部分则是因为它的重量主要集中在底部。就像那个可怜的女孩最终变成了那样……不过我真的不建议去试着推她，看看她会不会又重新变回原来的样子。 嗯，你知道，这本不该成为可能的事情，但既然小毬提到了这一点，这种诱惑就出现了。从现在开始，琥珀的步态和尾巴的摆动方式确实会变得不一样起来，对吧？ “而且根据目前的趋势来看，我敢预测，在她再生一个孩子之后，这种变化会变得更加明显。我很好奇，如果他的神圣主宰愿意让我继续留在这里，这种变化会对未来几代人的外貌产生什么样的影响。 |那么……她并没有因为你在这一切中所扮演的角色而生你的气吧？ “就像大多数事情一样，其中既有好事，也有坏事，”小丸叹了口气回答道，“既然你在这件事上并没有责任，我觉得也没有理由让你成为我不满的对象。如果你想了解详细情况，可以直接去问小小小林本人，不过我觉得这可能是整个萨瓦拉地区为数不多的几件她可能不愿意被人议论的事情之一。不过，她还是不小心透露了，其实是她自己踢了你一脚，才让自己陷入了这种麻烦之中，所以……嗯，我们就等着看吧。” 这个故事在未来的日子里肯定会一直萦绕在你的脑海里，不是吗？ “你应该感到庆幸才对——这个故事让你摆脱了对这件事的责任。如果我了解得没有这么多，我可能会对你更加恼火。当然，这种徒劳的愤怒其实并不能解决任何问题，尽管有时候它确实能让人宣泄情绪。 “无论如何，既然这些负面后果并不是你的责任，那么在考虑与你相关的这一系列事件时，我更愿意关注其中那些积极的一面。这样不是要好得多吗？ |这问题有点奇怪，不过小毬应该知道，琥珀在你女儿的书桌旁边专门为她准备了一个小床，对吧？你觉得在这种地方，这种做法应该不算常见吧？ “以一个老妇人的经验来说，随时让年幼的孩子待在身边总是明智的，”她咯咯笑着回答，“不过，我确实允许她这么做了，所以我知道这件事。 哈，小白居然真的问了？ “嗯，其实也没说得太直白。就是那种下属有需求，但直接开口请求又显得不太合适的情况。所以，上级就需要通过上下文、潜台词等各种暗示来理解下属到底想要什么，然后慷慨地主动给予。这样，双方的关系才能得到很好的维护，而且最重要的是，这种交流对外人来说完全就是莫名其妙、无法理解的。 不过，确实如此。那个可怜的女孩只是不希望自己的女儿经历她曾经经历过的那些事情，所以即使她的要求有些不寻常，我也愿意满足她。虽然仓库里有一个年纪很小的孩子，可能会让人有些担心，但它被放在了所有重物的旁边，因此我认为它并不会增加发生事故的风险。另外，如果每天早上都要求那个女孩把她的工具交给萤或者我，肯定会让她很难过，而我绝对不能这样做；毕竟，如果我强行要求她这么做，她根本就无法完成任何有用的工作。毕竟，高效管理的关键在于了解你的团队成员。 所以她允许小白一直把这套装备带在身边。 “只是这样而已。 ] |[kohaku.pregStage 1 |[rand |诚然，你一直很好奇——小白的家人对于她怀孕的消息有何反应？ “家人啊……”麻里有点泄气地说道，“实际上，我就是她的家人。不，她的父母还活着，但一个人如果能够平安无恙地生活在文明的怀抱中，就很难去追求那些远大的目标了。他们每年会回来一次，去履行他们对政府的义务——也就是履行他们对我的义务——但除此之外，他们就会去寻找那些所谓的“宝藏”了。 所以他们还不知道这件事。 就像我之前说的， [pc.ra kitsune |冠军， ]说到底，我就是她的家人；她在很小的时候就被留在了那个殖民地，后来我收留了她。像我这样活了这么久的人，能有这样一个孩子在家里陪伴自己大约十五年，真的是件很幸福的事情。这样的孩子能让人的生活充满乐趣，也能让人的心态保持积极乐观。我想，当她的血亲们回到这里来算账时，最终会发现这一切的。不过，我认为这种变化在他们那段伟大的探索冒险故事中，只不过是一个微不足道的插曲罢了。与此同时，他们的女儿在短短几年时间里，带来的高级铁矿资源，比他们在整个离开期间所获得的还要多。可以放心，下次他们再来的时候，我一定会着重强调这两点，同时指出他们是如何在过去的十五年里白白浪费时间的。” 从小毬的声音中可以明显听出那种淡淡的忧郁，你只能摇摇头。难怪琥珀会对这个即将到来的孩子如此在意。 “这可能是原因之一，没错。但为了回答你的问题[pc.ra kitsune |神圣的冠军， ]我完全了解她的状况，也清楚未来可能会面临哪些挑战。或许，我对她的处境甚至抱有超出常人的同情；在她还是我的培养对象的时候，她就是我最看重的角色之一，现在依然如此。 虽然我不能说我完全认同导致这种局面的一系列事件，但我也知道这并不是你的错。过去，利用她的可爱和吸引力确实帮助这个孩子度过了许多棘手的局面，但那种冷漠无情的‘宇宙法则’根本不会在意这些任性却又惹人喜爱的行为。也许你可以猜到：这是无法避免的，也没有什么办法可以改变它吧？ 麻里微微一笑。[pc.ra kitsune |哎呀，神圣的勇士，看来你也开始真正理解我们人民的坚韧与忍耐精神了，你简直已经成为了我们中的一员了。 |嗯，我看有东西粘在了你身上，才会让你产生那样的理解吧。 ]但是，并非如此。可以有人会提供帮助，而且确实有很多方法可以让我在未来的日子里为她的生活带来便利。问题的另一部分在于，那个可怜的孩子是否能够放下自己的骄傲，接受这些帮助。 那么，这就需要你的帮助了。 “如果你能在几个关键问题上改变她的想法，那将是非常有帮助的。 |你听说小梅在琥珀怀孕期间阻止她参加商队旅行了吗？
