rows.original: Discuss her relationships with and thoughts about various people.
rows.translation: 探讨她与各种人的关系，以及她对他们的看法。
rows.raw: "Discuss her relationships with and thoughts about various people."

rows.original: [kinu.isInari |[rand |"To be frank, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it's hard to care about a lot of what other people think, or being liked by other people. The right thing to do doesn't have to be the popular thing to do — in fact, since so many people go along to get along, it's more likely to be the opposite, to be honest. Finding someone who actually lives by principles and has enough of a spine to stand up for them instead of getting all passive-aggressive is a rarity and I can respect that; it's why I can at least give Mother that for pushing back against me. But being all wishy-washy means that you can be bought, it's just a matter of finding the right price. I can't say I can stand for that kind of attitude in the people I deal with." That kind of attitude isn't going to win her many friends. Your fox-daughter sniffs. "[pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I honestly don't care for the social approval or any status conferred by people who'll change their minds depending on what's convenient at the moment. It turns my stomach. The question is: is it right? If so, I'm doing it, no matter who might resent me for taking action." |"You know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], pickling is really fascinating. There's a lot you can do with just salt, vinegar and a few spices, and if you do it right you can end up with ready-to-eat food that'll keep for years. Traditionally, it's mostly turnips, cucumbers, cabbage and that kind of stuff, but I've been inspired by some of the native foods to try and do it to other stuff, too. Fish, meat, even boiled eggs. A bunch of experiments went bad to begin with, but at least they're keeping now. No one else's willing to try them except Hitoshi, though, and that doesn't really count because he'll eat anything that's remotely edible." It's a kind of a hobby for her, isn't it? Kinu folds her arms and pouts. "It's not just a hobby, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it's an art. You learn this kind of stuff from your grandparents, and pass it along to your grandkids when the time comes. Entire families have their own secret recipes for making all kinds of pickles." Maybe she's overblowing it a little? We-ll. Maybe just a little. Still, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. There's really something calming about sitting down with a couple jars, vinegar, and a knife and getting to work. Not that I'm going to ask you to approve of it, but I'm just hoping my feelings about pickling come across strongly, as they should, right?" |"Think it was when I was about thirteen when Mom let me cook meals unsupervised. She said that she'd have let me do it younger, but my body still had a ways to catch up with the rest of me and that she didn't want me burning the house down because this or that was too heavy for me to carry. "I still cook as much as I can; it's pretty relaxing going through the motions. That, and it's a joy to be able to do it for everyone else." And most certainly your darling daughter would never abuse her position to make everyone eat her favorites any more than they ought to, yes? Kinu bites her lip and turns her gaze askance. "Well, uh, maybe a bit more than would be warranted. Certainly not to unhealthy levels, at any rate. It's a small price to pay to have big sis do all the cooking, right? It's not as if kenchin soup is bad for you or anything..." |"In between growing other crops and letting the land fallow, it's important to grow soybeans and adzuki beans to replenish the soil. I don't really mind the work that goes into that — since we don't have the works for it here, I send the soybeans to Granny Komari's to be fermented, and we get back tofu, miso and all that good stuff. It's also really easy to bribe Miko and Granny Komari with adzuki beans, since they really love dishes made from them. It's not as if they don't have the means to grow either on their own, but everyone always says anything that comes from my fields is extra-great. "I dunno, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It's a good feeling to be able to bribe people like this. Makes you feel recognized, even if it's maybe for the wrong reasons." |"When I have time early in the morning, I like to come out here by myself and play my shakuhachi. [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], there's just something very calming and sublime about playing music while the sun rises over the fields. It's a moment that comes by every day unless there's bad weather, but it's still one that I want to capture perfectly in music someday. Ephemeral beauty like that... you can't take it for granted that it'll come around again." Mm. She plays alone? Does she play for anyone else? "We-ll... sometimes Granny Komari will ask me for a private performance. [silly|Ishida-san|Azami]'s ancestor used to play it too, so it holds good memories for her. Mai also knows how to play it some and enjoys the instrument's tone... and sometimes I'll also play for Hitoshi, although I don't know if he likes my playing or not. But that aside, my music is mostly for myself and the fields." Huh. Isn't that a little lonely? "Should it be, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? I don't play the shakuhachi to become popular or well-liked. I just want... it's not just the sunrise over the fields, or the morning fog, or the perfect blossoms of a plum tree. There's so much natural beauty that can be captured in the world about us, and although Mother wanted me to learn the koto I think the shakuhachi is better for expressing that beauty. That, and I can play it wherever I want; you can't really do that with a koto, can you?" |"There are so many things we can't make on our own, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it's getting me down. Back in the astral plane, whenever I needed something I'd get Mother to conjure it up for me... it's not that I mind the work involved, but that's the problem, we're just one family and can't possibly get everything we need by ourselves. Granny Komari has already given Mother and I so much, and even she isn't self-sufficient in that plenty of goods get sent to and from the colonies. It... irks me, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. What if something happened? Would I have to disguise myself and go into that native settlement down south?" She knows that going into Hawkethorne alone is dangerous. Her mother manages it because you're always with her and can vouch for her behavior — however, it's likely that she'd receive the same treatment as any old harpy trying to sneak in: chased off at best, riddled with arrows at worst. Kohaku entrusts her life to her disguise when doing business with the peoples of the Marches; as much of a prodigy as Kinu is, you don't think her skills at disguise and mimicry match Kohaku's. "Nhhhm... well, that is true. I shouldn't want to do something just because you tell me not to, and your reasoning's sound, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I just..." She's at that age. Worrying for everyone's sake is to be expected for someone in her position as her mother's heir, but worrying about what can't be changed is pretty silly. If she's concerned about her supply lines being cut, she can look into getting in touch with some of the other dens further along the frontier. Maybe that'll help. |"You know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I used to hate getting up in the mornings when I was really little. Then I used to get sleepy after lunch... do you remember me telling you that?" You think you do. "Now I feel all odd if I don't get up at the crack of dawn." Raising a hand to rub her cheek, your fox-daughter squirms in place. "Ahaha... I guess I'm not as bad as Mai — she sleeps during the day and is awake at night for her vigil at the shrine. But... it really feels like my body has grown a lot since I was a kit, you know? Shed off childish desires and stopped being so much of a lazy slug?" You can't say it's just because of her body; the lifestyle she's fallen into as she's grown up has plenty to do with it, too. That, and the attitude she's taken towards life. With so much energy brimming over in her spirit, how is there any way her body could ever succumb to sloth? "Ahaha. Thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. There's so much to be done in a day that I have to force myself to turn in on time." She's still young; best to enjoy the strength of youth while it lasts. |You've noticed that she mostly has crops over here — that, and a handful of carp that live in the paddies and pools. Has she ever considered keeping poultry, perhaps? Or maybe some other animals, like a pig? You've heard they're pretty good at converting table scraps into meat. "Oh. Eh." Kinu looks thoughtful a moment. "Hitoshi keeps ducks in his paddies, but they do pretty much the same thing that the carp do here, which is to eat pests that get in despite the charms. I think I considered chickens once, but for some reason that never came through... it's not that I hate animals or anything, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it's just that I don't feel as much for them, I guess. Maybe someday I'll be able to put together a coop and all, but not today." Plants are her true calling, aren't they? "Well, when you put it that way, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]... it's hard to deny it." |Does she ever think that some of the methods and techniques she's trying out with her own fields will ever make a difference? "Hey, you're starting to sound like Mother when you ask this question. Are you being genuine, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]?" Yes. "To be honest, I don't know; I'm just doing what I do because it's... it couldn't be any way otherwise, that's the only way I can put it. Do the birds question why they fly, or fish why they swim? It's not as if I make what I'm doing a secret, so if it spreads beyond the colonies and helps other people, that's great, but it doesn't really matter to me. I just like being here with the cool dirt under my feet, that's all. There really isn't any other way to explain it. "Don't get me wrong, I know I'm prone to talking peoples' ears off about the subject if they know something about it as well; I just don't really care if it does make a difference or not, or if I'm recognized for my efforts or not. It's not as if I've made any worthy breakthroughs to date, so it's probably best that I not get ahead of myself to begin with, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." |"Time waits for no man, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I know it's going to sound silly, but trusting my hunches isn't all bad. Later when I put it all together in my head, I usually find that my hunch was right and my intuition was working faster than my logic in delivering the answer. "Not that I'm saying I like to be rash or anything, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], of course one shouldn't be stupid, but seizing the moment and taking the initiative puts you in a better starting position regardless of what it is you're doing. Moving first means you set the tune to which other people are dancing, and not the other way around." ] |[rand |"It feels good to be liked, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. While I did not expect to become so popular in so short a time, the kindness and deference which Matron Komari's people have shown me is amazing; it makes me feel all good inside." Color rises to your fox-daughter's cheeks as she clasps her hands before her bosom, her ears turning down and sideways. "I... I want more of it, to be completely honest. If it will make them happy and like me more for it, I feel inspired to do anything. Anything to just see someone else smile and hear them call my name when I walk by. It... it feels so good." While it's good that your darling daughter is becoming well-known about these parts, perhaps she should be careful about flatterers and sycophants. Becoming easily flattered is quite a dangerous trait for one in her position to have. "Worry not, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]; I will be just fine. The people around these parts are ours; I am sure they do not mean me any harm, and if anything happens then it would certainly be inadvertent. It is not too hard to guess at what people are really thinking if you know what to look for, you know. I just want people to like me. Whyever would I betray that trust by suspecting others needlessly, and thus put myself at a disadvantage by sowing animosity where none was ever needed in the first place? I have easily picked up on ill-intentioned people in the past; there is nothing to worry about." So's being overconfident... |You can't help but notice that your daughter dearest has become pretty popular amongst the other kitsune in Komari's den; it's a good thing that after a childhood of having only her immediate family for company while growing up, Kinu isn't just adept at mixing well with others, but well-liked to boot. "Mother taught me much of etiquette when I was younger, even though chances to put it into practice were limited. It puts peoples' minds at ease when they know how to behave in a strange social situation and can expect reciprocal behavior from the other party. With our nature being what it is and the relationships of the people around us, it is a big reason why social etiquette developed as it did in our homeland." Hmm, yes, but there's something more about Kinu that exceeds the social baseline of politeness for kitsune. You've noticed it when people speak of her to you — she's actually liked, and very much so. There's got to be something behind it, right? "Ah... well, it is not my place to speculate, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]..." Well, her place or not, you'd like to hear her own self-appraisal. "Well, if you ask me... it is because they finally now have their own princess, even though I am not really one. Ever since the colonies' official founding, Matron Kurokawa has served as their advocate in her position as governor, yet her standing is tainted by her past. They hope that now they have their own divine descendant born and raised here across the ocean, there will be someone with the power to put forth their positions across the ocean. It is... hope, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. They do not like me so much as the image of me they have created for themselves in their hopes." It's certainly one to aspire to, though. "To aspire to, that is the thing. I am not there yet. Whether for good or for ill... it is dangerous to believe too much in a fantasy that only exists in your own mind; I know it is not the real me who is favored. There... there is no polite way to put it." |"There is much natural beauty in this land, and I hope to capture it not just in painting and verse, but in music as well. When I was younger, I foolishly chafed at Mother insisting on teaching me these arts, but now I realize the wisdom of her actions. To be able to appreciate the beauty of a perfectly wrapped gift, the morning fog against the sunrise, or that of raindrops creating ripples on the surface of a clear pond... that capability is one of the things that separates us from mere beasts. The degree of civilization that is needed for people to be able to turn their minds to such contemplations instead of scrabbling about in the dirt for survival... to be able to appreciate and indulge in such arts is to remember the sacrifices our ancestors have made in our stead. "To be able to watch a light snow while attempting to capture that ephemeral wonder on my koto and immortalise it that way... it is only because of Mother, and Mother's mother, and her mother before that, that I am able to enjoy such privilege. And when I have perfected my composition, I will bequeath it upon my heir, along with all the other things that have been given unto me. Is that not a worthy goal?" |"There is more to the preparation of food than seeking to fill one's stomach. The arrangement, the colors, the aroma — more than mere satiation, a meal should engage all of the senses in pleasing harmony. I daresay that I am quite good at it at this point — or at least, Nakano finds the lunches I prepare for him quite satisfactory. Coming from a connoisseur like him who has been eating Mikoto's and Miyuki's fare all his life, that is quite the compliment." You're glad that she's finding satisfaction in so many areas of her life. For someone as serious as her — well, one would expect simple cooking to be beneath a fox of her station. "Excessive focus on one thing or the other can be problematic. For someone with a future like the one I am poised to enter, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], one is usually best served by keeping a broad view of the big picture. When I was younger, I would have times where if I had something bothering me, I would exclude all my other thoughts and focus on the problem at hand; that kind of concentration is powerful, but has its place. Like a well-prepared meal, excellence in all aspects is preferable to utter perfection in one. Matron Komari says only insects specialise that heavily." |"When I was younger, being mindful of my etiquette all the time wore on me; for example, I had to make a conscious effort to not take overly large steps in my daily affairs, or to address everyone by the proper honorifics. Now, I can see how Mother's insistence has paid off, and my life is a lot easier, my dealings with other people a lot smoother than they would otherwise have been. It is not until much later that we understand the full import of our actions and decisions, so the guidance of those who have been there before you is invaluable." Does she still need to concentrate on being polite to everyone? "Not usually; at this point, the basics are second nature to me, as they should be. But there are so many new experiences to be had these days; I am always finding some edge case or unexpected circumstance to ponder over. Being flexible and yet willing to overcomply just a little works wonders. Even those beneath your social station need to be treated with the respect they are due, after all." |"I am always happy to go over Matron Komari's and simply talk to people about the den. Although they were wary at first, I believe my face has become well-known enough for the residents to warm up to me. That I am friends with the Matron and her family helps, of course. "When wisely applied, putting your time into other people is one of the best investments you can make, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. That, and it is never boring; there are always people coming and going from the frontier dens bearing news. Even though I bear the white hair and fur of divine descent... being able to speak freely with others like this and receive a more-or-less honest answer is something I could not quite have received over the ocean. It has its advantages... and disadvantages, too. But few things in life are ever perfect." |"Sometimes I wonder what my life would have been like if I had made different choices while growing up; if I had reacted differently to some of the things that happened when I was but still a kit. Then I remember that such questions and idle daydreams are but wastes of time and help no one going forward. The carefree days of my childhood are over, and were so the moment I saw the role that I was fated to fill and the responsibilities that came with it. That was the point, I think, where I made the conscious decision to devote myself fully to becoming what I will be in the future." How old was she then? Kinu scratches her head. "Time within the Astral Plane was strange that way... but as far as my body was concerned, I think I was fourteen or so." Fourteen? To make a decision like that when she was — ah, but as her mother's heir, of course that makes sense. Truly, the loss of her childhood under the weight of her future was always a foregone conclusion. Even so, some part of Kinu will always be your daughter in that sense, no matter how old she is or who she becomes. |How is your darling fox-daughter this morning? "Thank you for asking after me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. My health is flawless today, and I am in perfect shape to carry out my duties and studies." Ah, you're just glad to have a daughter who's as robust as she is. Even the change of scenery from the Astral Plane to her mother's old home hasn't troubled her constitution any; for her to be able to achieve all the things that she does in but one day, Kinu must be practically overflowing with energy. "Your words honor me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. To tell the truth, I am healthier these days than I used to be as a kit. Back then, I would fall ill from time to time, as children do... but it feels like my body has grown up in a sense. Fetching and carrying for Matron Komari is enough of a task in and of itself without having to appear regal and refined while at it, too." Haha. She's not wrong — her body is certainly healthier-looking than her mother's when you first met her. Well, whatever her duties may be, you certainly hope that she'll continue taking good care of herself. That's the most important thing. "You should take good care of yourself when you are out there too, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." |"There is something so fine about peaches, especially when they are finely sliced and served with chilled honey syrup. Usually I do not favor sweet foods, but there is something about the natural flavor and sweetness of the fruit that makes it all so palatable." Haha, at least that's one aspect of her childhood she hasn't completely lost yet. "I planted some peach trees by the entrance to the den, but it will be some years yet before there will be any fruit worth having. If I do as well with them as I do with my flowers, they will certainly be something to talk about. If only I could get other people to share my passion for them — I suppose Mikoto does, but she likes anything that involves free food, so does she really count?" |"Whenever I talk to someone, I try to put myself in their position, if even for a moment. It helps me understand where they're coming from, and that knowledge is invaluable to helping bring about a mutual understanding." |"When I have to make a decision, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], I try to reason through what the likely results of my choices are and think until I am absolutely convinced and certain of the correctness of my actions. It may take some more time that I may not always have the privilege of having, but I believe that more time and effort will be saved in the long run if I do not have to correct errors produced by poor judgement." ] ]
rows.translation: [kinu.isInari |[rand |坦白说， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]其实，很难去在意别人的看法，也不必在意是否能够获得别人的喜爱。正确的做法并不一定就是大家都会选择的做法——事实上，由于有那么多人只是为了迎合他人而随大流，所以正确的做法往往恰恰是与大多数人相反的。找到一个真正坚守原则、有足够的勇气为自己的信念挺身而出而不是采取消极对抗的态度的人，实在是很难得的，我对此表示尊重；正因为如此，至少我能够认可Mother那种反抗我的行为。但这种优柔寡断的态度意味着你是可以被收买的，只是需要找到合适的代价而已。我实在无法容忍与我打交道的人持有这种态度。 那种态度不会让她交到很多朋友的。 你的狐妖女儿在嗅来嗅去。"[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]说实话，我根本不在乎那些会根据当下方便与否而改变自己观点的人所给予的社会认可或任何地位。这种行为让我感到反感。关键在于：这样做到底对不对？如果是对的，那我就会去做，哪怕会因此招来别人的怨恨。 |你知道， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]腌制确实是一件非常有趣的事情。只需要盐、醋和一些香料，就能做出很多美味的食品，而且如果方法得当，这些食品甚至可以保存多年。传统上，人们主要用芜菁、黄瓜、卷心菜之类的食材进行腌制，但受到一些当地食物的启发，我也尝试用其他食材来腌制，看看会是什么效果。鱼、肉，甚至煮鸡蛋。一开始有很多实验都失败了，但至少现在这些食材还能保存下来。不过，除了仁志之外，没有人愿意再尝试这些食材了——毕竟他什么能吃的东西都会吃。" 这对她来说算是一种爱好吧？ 小娟双臂交叉，撅起了嘴。这不仅仅是一个爱好， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]这可是一门艺术，相关知识都是从祖父母那里学来的，等到有合适的机会，再传给自己的孙子孙女们。整个家族都有自己的秘密配方，用来制作各种各样的腌制品。 也许她有点反应过度了？ 这——个嘛。也许确实有一点。不过， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]真的，只要准备上几罐罐头、一些醋和一把刀，然后开始动手制作，就会有一种让人感到平静的感觉。当然，我并不是希望你们能够赞同我的这种做法，但我只是希望自己对腌制食品的这份热情能够充分地表达出来，毕竟这份热情确实是真实存在的，对吧？ |大概在我十三岁的时候，妈妈开始允许我在没有监督的情况下做饭。她说，如果我再小一些，她也会让我做的，但我的身体还需要一段时间才能跟上其他方面的发育速度，她不希望因为我拿不动某些东西而导致火灾发生。 我仍然会尽可能多地做饭；做这些事情其实挺让人放松的。而且，能够为别人做饭也是一件让人开心的事。 当然，你亲爱的女儿肯定也不会利用自己的地位，强迫大家非得吃那些她最喜欢的食物，对吧？ 小娟咬了咬嘴唇，然后将目光转向了一侧。嗯，也许吧一点远远没有达到不健康的程度。无论如何，这样的代价其实不算高，让姐姐来负责所有的烹饪工作，不是吗？毕竟肯钦汤并不会对人体造成任何伤害…… |在种植其他作物和让土地休耕之间，种植大豆和红小豆来补充土壤养分是非常重要的。我其实并不介意这项工作所带来的麻烦——由于我们这里没有相应的设备，所以我会把大豆送到麻里奶奶那里进行发酵，这样我们就能得到豆腐、味噌等各种美味的产品。用小豆贿赂米可和麻里奶奶也非常容易，因为她们真的很喜欢用小豆做的菜肴。其实她们自己也有能力种植小豆，但大家总是说，我田里种出来的小豆特别好吃。 我不知道[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]能够用这种方式贿赂别人，确实是一种不错的感觉。这会让你觉得自己的努力得到了认可，哪怕这种认可可能是出于一些不正当的原因。 |每当天刚亮的时候，我有空的话，就会独自来到这里，演奏我的尺八。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]当太阳从田野上升起时，演奏音乐总有一种令人感到宁静而崇高的感觉。这样的时刻每天都会出现，除非天气不好；但我依然希望有朝一日能够通过音乐将这一瞬间完美地记录下来。这样的短暂美好……你可不能想当然地认为它还会再次出现。 嗯，她都是独自玩游戏吗？还是也会为别人而玩呢？ 嗯……有时候麻里奶奶会要求我为她进行私人表演。 [silly|石田先生|阿兹米]她的祖先也曾经演奏这种乐器，因此它对她来说充满了美好的回忆。舞也会演奏一些，她很喜欢这种乐器的音色……有时候我也会为仁志演奏，不过我不知道他是否喜欢我的演奏。不过，说到底，我的音乐主要是为了自己，也是为了那些田野而存在的。 哈，这样不是有点孤单吗？ 应该是这样吗？
