Kinu folds her arms and pouts. "It's not just a hobby, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it's an art. You learn this kind of stuff from your grandparents, and pass it along to your grandkids when the time comes. Entire families have their own secret recipes for making all kinds of pickles." Maybe she's overblowing it a little? We-ll. Maybe just a little. Still, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. There's really something calming about sitting down with a couple jars, vinegar, and a knife and getting to work. Not that I'm going to ask you to approve of it, but I'm just hoping my feelings about pickling come across strongly, as they should, right?" |"Think it was when I was about thirteen when Mom let me cook meals unsupervised. She said that she'd have let me do it younger, but my body still had a ways to catch up with the rest of me and that she didn't want me burning the house down because this or that was too heavy for me to carry. "I still cook as much as I can; it's pretty relaxing going through the motions. That, and it's a joy to be able to do it for everyone else." And most certainly your darling daughter would never abuse her position to make everyone eat her favorites any more than they ought to, yes? Kinu bites her lip and turns her gaze askance. "Well, uh, maybe a bit more than would be warranted. Certainly not to unhealthy levels, at any rate. It's a small price to pay to have big sis do all the cooking, right? It's not as if kenchin soup is bad for you or anything..." |"In between growing other crops and letting the land fallow, it's important to grow soybeans and adzuki beans to replenish the soil. I don't really mind the work that goes into that — since we don't have the works for it here, I send the soybeans to Granny Komari's to be fermented, and we get back tofu, miso and all that good stuff. It's also really easy to bribe Miko and Granny Komari with adzuki beans, since they really love dishes made from them. It's not as if they don't have the means to grow either on their own, but everyone always says anything that comes from my fields is extra-great. "I dunno, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It's a good feeling to be able to bribe people like this. Makes you feel recognized, even if it's maybe for the wrong reasons." |"When I have time early in the morning, I like to come out here by myself and play my shakuhachi. [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], there's just something very calming and sublime about playing music while the sun rises over the fields. It's a moment that comes by every day unless there's bad weather, but it's still one that I want to capture perfectly in music someday. Ephemeral beauty like that... you can't take it for granted that it'll come around again." Mm. She plays alone? Does she play for anyone else? "We-ll... sometimes Granny Komari will ask me for a private performance. [silly|Ishida-san|Azami]'s ancestor used to play it too, so it holds good memories for her. Mai also knows how to play it some and enjoys the instrument's tone... and sometimes I'll also play for Hitoshi, although I don't know if he likes my playing or not. But that aside, my music is mostly for myself and the fields." Huh. Isn't that a little lonely? "Should it be, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? I don't play the shakuhachi to become popular or well-liked. I just want... it's not just the sunrise over the fields, or the morning fog, or the perfect blossoms of a plum tree. There's so much natural beauty that can be captured in the world about us, and although Mother wanted me to learn the koto I think the shakuhachi is better for expressing that beauty. That, and I can play it wherever I want; you can't really do that with a koto, can you?" |"There are so many things we can't make on our own, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it's getting me down. Back in the astral plane, whenever I needed something I'd get Mother to conjure it up for me... it's not that I mind the work involved, but that's the problem, we're just one family and can't possibly get everything we need by ourselves. Granny Komari has already given Mother and I so much, and even she isn't self-sufficient in that plenty of goods get sent to and from the colonies. It... irks me, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. What if something happened? Would I have to disguise myself and go into that native settlement down south?" She knows that going into Hawkethorne alone is dangerous. Her mother manages it because you're always with her and can vouch for her behavior — however, it's likely that she'd receive the same treatment as any old harpy trying to sneak in: chased off at best, riddled with arrows at worst. Kohaku entrusts her life to her disguise when doing business with the peoples of the Marches; as much of a prodigy as Kinu is, you don't think her skills at disguise and mimicry match Kohaku's. "Nhhhm... well, that is true. I shouldn't want to do something just because you tell me not to, and your reasoning's sound, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I just..." She's at that age. Worrying for everyone's sake is to be expected for someone in her position as her mother's heir, but worrying about what can't be changed is pretty silly. If she's concerned about her supply lines being cut, she can look into getting in touch with some of the other dens further along the frontier. Maybe that'll help. |"You know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I used to hate getting up in the mornings when I was really little. Then I used to get sleepy after lunch... do you remember me telling you that?" You think you do. "Now I feel all odd if I don't get up at the crack of dawn." Raising a hand to rub her cheek, your fox-daughter squirms in place. "Ahaha... I guess I'm not as bad as Mai — she sleeps during the day and is awake at night for her vigil at the shrine. But... it really feels like my body has grown a lot since I was a kit, you know? Shed off childish desires and stopped being so much of a lazy slug?" You can't say it's just because of her body; the lifestyle she's fallen into as she's grown up has plenty to do with it, too. That, and the attitude she's taken towards life. With so much energy brimming over in her spirit, how is there any way her body could ever succumb to sloth? "Ahaha. Thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. There's so much to be done in a day that I have to force myself to turn in on time." She's still young; best to enjoy the strength of youth while it lasts. |You've noticed that she mostly has crops over here — that, and a handful of carp that live in the paddies and pools. Has she ever considered keeping poultry, perhaps? Or maybe some other animals, like a pig? You've heard they're pretty good at converting table scraps into meat. "Oh. Eh." Kinu looks thoughtful a moment. "Hitoshi keeps ducks in his paddies, but they do pretty much the same thing that the carp do here, which is to eat pests that get in despite the charms. I think I considered chickens once, but for some reason that never came through... it's not that I hate animals or anything, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it's just that I don't feel as much for them, I guess. Maybe someday I'll be able to put together a coop and all, but not today." Plants are her true calling, aren't they? "Well, when you put it that way, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]... it's hard to deny it." |Does she ever think that some of the methods and techniques she's trying out with her own fields will ever make a difference? "Hey, you're starting to sound like Mother when you ask this question. Are you being genuine, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]?" Yes. "To be honest, I don't know; I'm just doing what I do because it's... it couldn't be any way otherwise, that's the only way I can put it. Do the birds question why they fly, or fish why they swim? It's not as if I make what I'm doing a secret, so if it spreads beyond the colonies and helps other people, that's great, but it doesn't really matter to me. I just like being here with the cool dirt under my feet, that's all. There really isn't any other way to explain it. "Don't get me wrong, I know I'm prone to talking peoples' ears off about the subject if they know something about it as well; I just don't really care if it does make a difference or not, or if I'm recognized for my efforts or not. It's not as if I've made any worthy breakthroughs to date, so it's probably best that I not get ahead of myself to begin with, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." |"Time waits for no man, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I know it's going to sound silly, but trusting my hunches isn't all bad. Later when I put it all together in my head, I usually find that my hunch was right and my intuition was working faster than my logic in delivering the answer. "Not that I'm saying I like to be rash or anything, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], of course one shouldn't be stupid, but seizing the moment and taking the initiative puts you in a better starting position regardless of what it is you're doing. Moving first means you set the tune to which other people are dancing, and not the other way around." ] |[rand |"It feels good to be liked, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. While I did not expect to become so popular in so short a time, the kindness and deference which Matron Komari's people have shown me is amazing; it makes me feel all good inside." Color rises to your fox-daughter's cheeks as she clasps her hands before her bosom, her ears turning down and sideways. "I... I want more of it, to be completely honest. If it will make them happy and like me more for it, I feel inspired to do anything. Anything to just see someone else smile and hear them call my name when I walk by. It... it feels so good." While it's good that your darling daughter is becoming well-known about these parts, perhaps she should be careful about flatterers and sycophants. Becoming easily flattered is quite a dangerous trait for one in her position to have. "Worry not, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]; I will be just fine. The people around these parts are ours; I am sure they do not mean me any harm, and if anything happens then it would certainly be inadvertent. It is not too hard to guess at what people are really thinking if you know what to look for, you know. I just want people to like me. Whyever would I betray that trust by suspecting others needlessly, and thus put myself at a disadvantage by sowing animosity where none was ever needed in the first place? I have easily picked up on ill-intentioned people in the past; there is nothing to worry about." So's being overconfident... |You can't help but notice that your daughter dearest has become pretty popular amongst the other kitsune in Komari's den; it's a good thing that after a childhood of having only her immediate family for company while growing up, Kinu isn't just adept at mixing well with others, but well-liked to boot. "Mother taught me much of etiquette when I was younger, even though chances to put it into practice were limited. It puts peoples' minds at ease when they know how to behave in a strange social situation and can expect reciprocal behavior from the other party. With our nature being what it is and the relationships of the people around us, it is a big reason why social etiquette developed as it did in our homeland." Hmm, yes, but there's something more about Kinu that exceeds the social baseline of politeness for kitsune. You've noticed it when people speak of her to you — she's actually liked, and very much so. There's got to be something behind it, right? "Ah... well, it is not my place to speculate, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]..." Well, her place or not, you'd like to hear her own self-appraisal. "Well, if you ask me... it is because they finally now have their own princess, even though I am not really one. Ever since the colonies' official founding, Matron Kurokawa has served as their advocate in her position as governor, yet her standing is tainted by her past. They hope that now they have their own divine descendant born and raised here across the ocean, there will be someone with the power to put forth their positions across the ocean. It is... hope, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. They do not like me so much as the image of me they have created for themselves in their hopes." It's certainly one to aspire to, though. "To aspire to, that is the thing. I am not there yet. Whether for good or for ill... it is dangerous to believe too much in a fantasy that only exists in your own mind; I know it is not the real me who is favored. There... there is no polite way to put it." |"There is much natural beauty in this land, and I hope to capture it not just in painting and verse, but in music as well. When I was younger, I foolishly chafed at Mother insisting on teaching me these arts, but now I realize the wisdom of her actions. To be able to appreciate the beauty of a perfectly wrapped gift, the morning fog against the sunrise, or that of raindrops creating ripples on the surface of a clear pond... that capability is one of the things that separates us from mere beasts. The degree of civilization that is needed for people to be able to turn their minds to such contemplations instead of scrabbling about in the dirt for survival... to be able to appreciate and indulge in such arts is to remember the sacrifices our ancestors have made in our stead. "To be able to watch a light snow while attempting to capture that ephemeral wonder on my koto and immortalise it that way... it is only because of Mother, and Mother's mother, and her mother before that, that I am able to enjoy such privilege. And when I have perfected my composition, I will bequeath it upon my heir, along with all the other things that have been given unto me. Is that not a worthy goal?" |"There is more to the preparation of food than seeking to fill one's stomach. The arrangement, the colors, the aroma — more than mere satiation, a meal should engage all of the senses in pleasing harmony. I daresay that I am quite good at it at this point — or at least, Nakano finds the lunches I prepare for him quite satisfactory. Coming from a connoisseur like him who has been eating Mikoto's and Miyuki's fare all his life, that is quite the compliment." You're glad that she's finding satisfaction in so many areas of her life. For someone as serious as her — well, one would expect simple cooking to be beneath a fox of her station. "Excessive focus on one thing or the other can be problematic. For someone with a future like the one I am poised to enter, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], one is usually best served by keeping a broad view of the big picture. When I was younger, I would have times where if I had something bothering me, I would exclude all my other thoughts and focus on the problem at hand; that kind of concentration is powerful, but has its place. Like a well-prepared meal, excellence in all aspects is preferable to utter perfection in one. Matron Komari says only insects specialise that heavily." |"When I was younger, being mindful of my etiquette all the time wore on me; for example, I had to make a conscious effort to not take overly large steps in my daily affairs, or to address everyone by the proper honorifics. Now, I can see how Mother's insistence has paid off, and my life is a lot easier, my dealings with other people a lot smoother than they would otherwise have been. It is not until much later that we understand the full import of our actions and decisions, so the guidance of those who have been there before you is invaluable." Does she still need to concentrate on being polite to everyone? "Not usually; at this point, the basics are second nature to me, as they should be. But there are so many new experiences to be had these days; I am always finding some edge case or unexpected circumstance to ponder over. Being flexible and yet willing to overcomply just a little works wonders. Even those beneath your social station need to be treated with the respect they are due, after all." |"I am always happy to go over Matron Komari's and simply talk to people about the den. Although they were wary at first, I believe my face has become well-known enough for the residents to warm up to me. That I am friends with the Matron and her family helps, of course. "When wisely applied, putting your time into other people is one of the best investments you can make, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. That, and it is never boring; there are always people coming and going from the frontier dens bearing news. Even though I bear the white hair and fur of divine descent... being able to speak freely with others like this and receive a more-or-less honest answer is something I could not quite have received over the ocean. It has its advantages... and disadvantages, too. But few things in life are ever perfect." |"Sometimes I wonder what my life would have been like if I had made different choices while growing up; if I had reacted differently to some of the things that happened when I was but still a kit. Then I remember that such questions and idle daydreams are but wastes of time and help no one going forward. The carefree days of my childhood are over, and were so the moment I saw the role that I was fated to fill and the responsibilities that came with it. That was the point, I think, where I made the conscious decision to devote myself fully to becoming what I will be in the future." How old was she then? Kinu scratches her head. "Time within the Astral Plane was strange that way... but as far as my body was concerned, I think I was fourteen or so." Fourteen? To make a decision like that when she was — ah, but as her mother's heir, of course that makes sense. Truly, the loss of her childhood under the weight of her future was always a foregone conclusion. Even so, some part of Kinu will always be your daughter in that sense, no matter how old she is or who she becomes. |How is your darling fox-daughter this morning? "Thank you for asking after me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. My health is flawless today, and I am in perfect shape to carry out my duties and studies." Ah, you're just glad to have a daughter who's as robust as she is. Even the change of scenery from the Astral Plane to her mother's old home hasn't troubled her constitution any; for her to be able to achieve all the things that she does in but one day, Kinu must be practically overflowing with energy. "Your words honor me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. To tell the truth, I am healthier these days than I used to be as a kit. Back then, I would fall ill from time to time, as children do... but it feels like my body has grown up in a sense. Fetching and carrying for Matron Komari is enough of a task in and of itself without having to appear regal and refined while at it, too." Haha. She's not wrong — her body is certainly healthier-looking than her mother's when you first met her. Well, whatever her duties may be, you certainly hope that she'll continue taking good care of herself. That's the most important thing. "You should take good care of yourself when you are out there too, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." |"There is something so fine about peaches, especially when they are finely sliced and served with chilled honey syrup. Usually I do not favor sweet foods, but there is something about the natural flavor and sweetness of the fruit that makes it all so palatable." Haha, at least that's one aspect of her childhood she hasn't completely lost yet. "I planted some peach trees by the entrance to the den, but it will be some years yet before there will be any fruit worth having. If I do as well with them as I do with my flowers, they will certainly be something to talk about. If only I could get other people to share my passion for them — I suppose Mikoto does, but she likes anything that involves free food, so does she really count?" |"Whenever I talk to someone, I try to put myself in their position, if even for a moment. It helps me understand where they're coming from, and that knowledge is invaluable to helping bring about a mutual understanding." |"When I have to make a decision, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], I try to reason through what the likely results of my choices are and think until I am absolutely convinced and certain of the correctness of my actions. It may take some more time that I may not always have the privilege of having, but I believe that more time and effort will be saved in the long run if I do not have to correct errors produced by poor judgement." ] ] "

rows.original: Why doesn't she share something about her daily life with you?
rows.translation: 她为什么不愿意和你分享一些关于她日常生活的事情呢？
rows.raw: "Why doesn't she share something about her daily life with you?"

rows.original: [var0 |[kinu.isInari |[rand |"Things are pretty idyllic about these parts, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Don't worry about us when you're out there — we should be the ones worrying about you[party.has kiyoko | and Mother ], to be perfectly honest. We've got a glamour set up over the waterfall entrance, the crater walls are nice and high, and I'd like to think that I've practiced enough with the naginata and hankyu to be confident in defending the household should anything happen. Leave the den's running to me[party.has kiyoko | | and Mother ], and do what you need to do." She'll be fine, yes? "You worry too much about me, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Not that it isn't sweet, but you don't want to be stiflingly overprotective of your daughter dearest, right? I can see why Mother chose this place to set up her den all those years ago — it's a very defensible position that took overwhelming force to overrun. I can take care of myself[kiyoko.numKits 2 | and everyone else, too ], so you should be saving up some of that luck for your own use, yeah?" |"Matron Komari's people are still coming over every now and then to help us fix up the place. It's less often now than in the first stretch of time since we got settled in, but we're still far from being self-sufficient. Well, I suppose in a sense we'll never be self-sufficient, but you know what I mean. As much as is possible for a den this size, anyway. It eats away at me, but things are what they are; maybe in the future long after I'm dead we'll be able to make most of what we need by ourselves, but that's pretty long down the line." |"Yes, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], don't worry. I know that I'm not supposed to go down the road into the native village just southwest of here. There are all sorts of horrible, nasty, things in the forest and even if I don't get [silly |bad-ended |into trouble ] on the trip all it'll take is one slip-up to reveal my true nature and the townsfolk will be hounding me out of the place or even worse, swinging from a gibbet. Yes indeed, I won't go, not in the least." [party.has kiyoko |"Kinu, your [pc.mf|father|mother] and I are serious about this," Kiyoko snaps. "Your life is not a plaything to be risked for the thrill of danger. Do you understand?" Kinu looks like she's going to pout out of sheer reflex, then her brain catches up with her emotions and she turns her ears and eyes down, realizing this isn't an argument she can win. "Yes, Mother." "I know I've said it repeatedly, but your safety is at stake here and that's worth more than a couple of breaths here and there. |Somehow, you get the feeling that your daughter dearest is being a little less than completely sincere here. "Whatever do you mean, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]?" Kinu replies with a small smile. "I know full well the danger I pose to the natives as a horrible, soul-sucking vampiric creature ready and willing to drain every last drop of life from their empty husks. I certainly wouldn't place myself in mortal danger by putting myself in a position where people who believe that would be able to get their hands on me, would I?" Oh, no... "Oh no, now [pc.mf|daddy|mommy] dearest is sighing and moaning. Whatever was it that I said to upset [pc.himHer] so?" ] Ah, well. So long as she knows not to get herself into trouble. There's already enough to worry about in the Marches without your daughter going off and adding more of it to the pile. You can understand if she wants to meet up with some of the traffic going in and out of Hawkethorne, maybe barter for a few things and practice her Belharan and disguises, but going into the village itself is off-limits. At least beyond the walls, she can always flee into the forest should things go south. That's an acceptable compromise, yes? "I guess so, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." |"When we were moving out of the Astral Plane, I would wonder what kind of place we were eventually going to live in," your daughter admits. "I'll admit, I was kinda afraid we were going to go from having far too much to nothing at all. But I was being silly, wasn't I? Sure, salt doesn't turn up in the drawer when I need it, now I have to get it from Granny Komari's and lug it through the torii gate... but the basics are all still here. A roof over our heads, something to eat, and plenty of nature all around us. The water here is even better than what we used to have in the Astral Plane. |"Oh, uh, how do I feed, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? That's kind of a private question, uhm." She's not blushing one of her mother's signature weapons-grade blushes, so you can expect that it's nothing lewd and everything she can talk about. Nevertheless, if she's not willing to share, you're fine with that. "Ah, well, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it's really nothing special. People come in all the time from the north and south gates, so it's a small matter to show up with a bunch of pickles and make a... um, proposition. Nothing sexual, of course. Times are getting a little tough what with things being what they are out in the world, so it's not hard to find someone willing to give up a little chi in exchange for food that'll last for a handful of days and which will keep far longer, an equitable exchange. It's certainly a more troublesome way than how most others seek benefactors, uh... if I were to do that, it would be so much simpler. Harpies sometimes wander into the forest from the foothills, or I could go and find them, and they're always a bit too willing..." Ah, there's the weapons-grade blush of the Otomo clan's womenfolk. All right, now that you're sure that your daughter dearest[kiyoko.numKits 2 | and by extent everyone else ] is adequately fed in every sense of the word, you can rest easy and go out into the world without worrying. ] |[rand |"I worry sometimes about the state of our wards and other protections," Kinu admits to you. "There is nothing much more that we can do about the situation as it is and as we are, but I still cannot help but be a little uneasy. This is where Mother, for a lack of a better word to put it, died. The crater walls are high and our position defensible, but..." [party.has kiyoko |"My dear daughter, if you were to face what I faced that day, nothing you could do would save you," Kiyoko says matter-of-factly. "It is not something to worry about, not merely because such threats do not exist any longer, but also because there is no point in fretting over things that you cannot hope to change. Now then, make sure that the protections are adequate while I am gone with your [pc.mf|father|mother]. Perfection is impossible in this context, but sufficient is paramount. Am I clear?" Kinu bows her head. "Yes, Mother." |Well, to be fair, if she were to face down several wraiths and a horde of their minions like her Mother did that day, there would be nothing she could do to save herself. Besides, things like that don't exist any more — that was the point of the Godswar. That doesn't mean she doesn't have to keep an eye on the wards, charms and things, but there's no point in fretting over things that she can't hope to change. Perhaps looking at it this way will ease her fears. Kinu bows her head. "I will keep this in mind, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." ] |You've been wondering this for a little while — how does she... um, well, feed? It's not like she's still a kit and having her mother hand her a bit of essence every now and then... [kiyoko.numKits 4 |and then there's the matter of her having to feed her siblings when her mother is away, too. ] "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. For future reference, while I know that you do not mean anything by it, please note that this question is quite personal for our kind..." You're just concerned for her health and well-being. "Which is why I am answering it to begin with. Even considering our social standing, or any difference in social standing for that matter, unless there is evidence of wrongdoing, this is not a question that is asked in polite conversation or company." Well then. "Suffice to say that there are many people coming and going from the village to the southwest every day, both from the north and the south. Times are tumultuous, and it is not too hard to find someone willing to make an equitable exchange of some sort. Usually, it is preserves — food to last some days and regain one's strength after being made a benefactor. There are other things which have been requested — the casting of small spells, for example." So she hasn't... ah. "Not in the carnal sense, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. If I were so inclined, I would catch the stray harpy who wanders into the forest from the foothills, or seek them there myself. But I prefer things this way — it gives me an excuse to practice my Belharan with more native speakers, and I receive many lessons in opening negotiations with those who are initially on suspicious or fearful footing. Learning is more than something you merely do from a manual, after all." |"When we were being extricated from the Astral Plane, I would wonder what kind of accommodations we were eventually going to have to reside in," your daughter admits. "I admit that I was concerned that we were going to go from a life that was too easy to one that was too hard; Mother's tales aside, I did not quite know what to expect. "After living like this for a while, though... I cannot say that I would go back. There is much to be done and much to be fixed; time and effort needs to be invested into making our surroundings more comfortable yet. But my worries were just empty concerns — yes, it is true that salt does not just appear when I need it to and I have to go over to Matron Komari's to barter for more, but the basics are all still here. A roof over our heads, something to eat, and plenty of nature all around us. The water here is even better than what we used to have in the Astral Plane. "And most importantly, there are so many other people here. So much of your life consists of other people, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]; my existence would have been impoverished had I not managed to meet so many new spirits, and I would have no known it in the slightest. So... you have my utmost gratitude." |"One of the reasons Nakano is still managing to get by while severely understaffed and underfunded is how peaceful things on the frontier are. Matron Komari's spiritual efforts over the last two centuries have largely pacified the elven druids, who are not loved by their kin, either. Nor have the tanuki and her daughters been too much of a bother, since they have been at a detente for the last hundred years. Usually it is just wild beasts or errant leothrans, who are easily repelled without loss of life. "But things are changing, are they not, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]? He is going to get the war that he hungers for, is he not? You can tell it in the air, even without the need for divination. I... I worry for him. The amount of resources the Cherry Blossom Throne is willing to spare in order to protect the colonies, even to save face... I think he is overestimating it, and quite severely, too. Conflict may not bring about as much of a war chest that he imagines it will... he still believes the lords and ladies of the imperial court are on fundamentally his side. As a warrior, how could he not? They expect to command his absolute obedience, after all, even if the den matron is his most immediate superior." It's not as impossible as it seems. If Kasyrra has her way... "If it comes to that, I wonder if he would be able to swallow his pride, self-respect, whatever one wants to call it, and work with the locals. I... have my doubts. Which is why I am needed, more than ever." |"I cannot be sure why, but I have a sense of unease about me these days. There is something wrong and neither the den matron nor Mikoto and Miyuki will tell me anything about it. Well, if they even know about it in the first place." Is it Kasyrra? "No, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], it is not the demoness or any doing of hers. There is something else... if I can sense it, certainly Mikoto or Miyuki should be able to; their senses are keenly attuned to the metaphysical. Yet they tell me that nothing is out of place. I cannot quite believe that they are sensing nothing." That, or they're not telling the truth. Kinu bites her lip. "I considered that possibility, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], but then if that were the case then why would they withhold such information to the point of lying? I am deeply concerned. Some of my nights are sleepless, and others I sleep too soundly. Taking my respite with one eye open is not an option, but if I could I would." ] ] |[kinu.isInari |[rand |"I'm doing fine, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." No, she isn't. She's a terrible liar when it comes to her emotions — your little girl has always been about expressing herself directly and freely, and when she tries to do the opposite it really shows. Although in this case, it's pretty obvious what's been bothering her. "I know it's no use worrying about it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. That's what makes it so infuriating when my head insists on doing so when the rational thing to do is stop worrying about something you can't change from fretting about it. I..." Kinu deflates with a huge sigh and grabs one of her tails, bringing it about her front and hugging it like a big bolster. "I feel exceedingly stupid and pissed off with myself at the same time, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], and being that way all the time is really tiring." She doesn't look like she's been sleeping well. "It's that obvious, huh?" It most certainly is. Like you said, concealing her emotions isn't Kinu's forte. Your daughter shifts her eyes and folds her ears forward. "Yeah, I guess, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I can't sleep well, because I can't feel safe in my own chambers anymore. On particularly bad nights I have to ask Hitoshi to come in and sit by my side until I doze off. He's never said no, but I still feel bad for keeping him up like that. "I just hope this passes soon, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It's really annoying and I need to get work done instead of moping around, but I won't cooperate with myself and more often than not I get exhausted at the end of the day. After I finally fall asleep, I wake up just as tired as when I'd gone to sleep. It's not an enviable position to be in." Well, the good thing is that she's willing to talk about it, and seek help from others that she trusts with regards to her more personal well-being, even if it's but just one guy. "I don't know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Every time I have to ask Hitoshi to come and sit by my bedside until I doze off, I feel so weak and useless. This is something that I should be able to handle on my own, and yet..." You chuckle. A young couple together inside a lady's bedroom... there's no scandal? Ah, she doesn't have to give you that exasperated look, you were just kidding. Kinu folds her arms and pouts. "When half the den is treating us like we're married already and the other half inquiring when the wedding will be, I really didn't need that kind of jibe on top of everything else. It gets tiring, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I'm not about to rush into anything, especially not at a time like this." Ah, fine, fine. Just know that if she needs anything from you, she just needs to ask. You can't be here all the time and she knows it, but at the same time you're determined to do what you can with what you have. Your fox-daughter looks away and down. "All right, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." |"Every time I think back to that night and remember Raphael's face, my stomach turns. The man's an utter creep." Anyone who would dare to hurt your daughter or kill children is an utter creep. "I don't mean in that way, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. The man wore all the right things, said all the right lines, and had all the right skills, all the way down to the perfume, and it didn't change who he was one bit. When I think back on the events, there's just a complete and visceral revulsion to the man." Well, that's a good thing to hear. You'd be asking her if her head was working right if she didn't have anything but utter contempt for the likes of Raphael, especially when she's been so plain and straight with her thoughts and desires ever since she was a kit. You can give a pig a bath, dress it in finery, feed it lavish cooked meals, and at the end of the day the pig will still be a pig. Charisma isn't something you can buy or wear[pc.bg courtesan noblescion |, you know this from your old days from rubbing shoulders with the upper crust. F |— f ]inery might get someone's notice, but that's all it is, a foot in the door. It's something that you are, and while wearing nice clothes can help with one's confidence, they're not a substitute for it. As far as you understand these things, that's the vibe she was picking up from that bastard. Kinu gives you a warm, if thin smile. "Wow, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. To hear you put it so eloquently... I can't say you're wrong. That doesn't make the creep any less of a threat, though, just a more disgusting one. Can't deny that he's skilled." That's generous of her, to admit an enemy's strengths. "I mean, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], there's no point in lying to myself. As much of a creep as he was, Raphael didn't just manage to beat me, the man was openly toying with me for his amusement and would've killed me had everyone arrived just a moment later. He's got no small measure of skill, and if I don't acknowledge that and start making excuses for myself I won't be able to get to the point where I'll finally be able to wring his neck." Now it's your turn to smile. It's nice to have life goals. The way I see it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], being angry is better than being afraid. I'm not about to let the matter go until I find him and make him pay." |How's your whitest, fluffiest daughter holding up? She looks absolutely exhausted. You can understand if she hasn't gotten that much sleep of late, but even just lying down in bed and resting is better than stretching herself too thinly. "No rest for the likes of me, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]; someone in my position can't take any days off. As they say, responsibility flows upwards, and there'll be time enough to sleep when I'm dead. There's just so much to be done, so much to rebuild — the work helps keep my mind off the stuff I don't want to think about." Ah, you see. "[pc.mf|Dad|Mom]... I know you're worried about me, and I'm not going to say that I don't have problems, but I think that so long as I'm not completely destroying myself I should be allowed to work out my own matters without everyone rushing in to baby me. It's not that I'm ungrateful for everyone saving me and working so hard to rebuild the den and giving me all kinds of things, but at some point it goes a little overboard and starts to get embarrassing. "I just need to do some of this myself, pull through under my own power — I know it seems all very strange, even to me, but I'm supposed to be in a position of some authority here with more of the same in my foreseeable future. Just don't coddle me, okay?" It's hard to not do just that, though. A sigh. "I know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I know." |[kiyoko.numKits 4 |"Asagiri... now she's gone off to be a shrine maiden. She spends most of the day there now with Miko and Mai, and doesn't go home until I come to pick her up in the evenings. The poor thing's always been quiet and docile, but after what happened she's become even more so." You... you don't even have words at the moment. Just thinking about it makes you furious. "I know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I know. Maybe... maybe she wouldn't have ended up so heavily scarred if I'd gotten her help sooner instead of forcing her to wait for the better part of an hour and limp along behind me, but..." She did what she could, given the circumstances. "And the question is always, was it enough? Could it have been better?" Going through life doubting herself all the time isn't any way to live. "I don't doubt myself all the time, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. But this is a very special case." Kinu folds her ears forward and sighs. "She was going to be my second-in-command, too, do all the busy paperwork and the like I really hate. Maybe this is a better future for her instead of playing second fiddle to me — I'll have to teach Kasumi to do her work in her stead, then. But with Asagiri wearing the white and red, she does look happier — when I can bring myself to look at her. Good thing Tatsumi's taken on caring for her, or else everything would be really awkward..." You've heard it going around the den that her little sister's experienced some kind of spiritual awakening. Does she understand what that means for Asagiri? You're a little unclear on the matter; it's just one of those things that kitsune just assume you know, and you don't.[pc.ra kitsune | It can be a bit awkward being the champion of their god and not knowing the culture, to put it lightly. ] A shrug. "Beats me, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Granny Komari tried explaining it to me and I probably could've understood, but I wasn't listening at the time. It's a step in the right direction for who she's become, what she's become, and as a shrine maiden her looks won't matter as much if she garners fame for her other qualities. I think this is probably the best one can make out of a situation like hers... although that's not saying much. I just wish all this could have been on me, instead of dragging the rest of my family into it. It would've been for the better." That's not true; it most definitely would not be better if she took it all upon herself. There are plenty of people around who would care if something happened to her, and be sad for it, too. Kinu turns her ears to the sides. "Hey, thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Yeah, I know that, but it's still nice to hear someone say it out loud." |"I can't help but think back to the laborers and fields hands who were staying over at the den that night, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. All they wanted was to help out our family, maybe curry a little favor with Mother and me on the side, and they almost ended up paying with their lives for it. That's already bad enough on its own, but it was I who led them all that way, and they almost paid for their trust in me with their lives." That, fortunately and unfortunately, is part and parcel of taking responsibility and making decisions that affect peoples' lives. While you know that your daughter's been her mother's majordomo ever since she was a kit, the impacts of her decisions have never been that great or with that much potential for danger when she was living in the Astral Plane with her mother. Now... the stakes are higher, the costs of failure — and the price of success — more dear. Kinu's no longer a child, and you can only hope that the lessons of her childhood were enough to carry her into her adult life. "They weren't," Kinu replies flatly. "Not in this instance anyway, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I just... well, I don't know. I guess I feel inadequate, that's all. It's a me problem, that's all it is, and I'm sure it'll pass. Everything turned out just right, didn't it? I just need to find some way of making sure this never happens again, that's all — yeah, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I know it's far easier said than done, but still." ] |"You know what hurt me the most about this entire mess, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]?" No, you don't. It'd be interesting to hear her thoughts. "They burned the fields and paddies. What they didn't have the time to take, they torched, and what looked like it wouldn't burn easily, they trampled. Those were just plants, they didn't need to do any of that. I wouldn't have minded if they'd actually stolen the crops ready for harvest. But there was absolutely no reason to destroy everything like that, save to spite me. It's not as if they burned very well, anyway." Maybe they knew it would hurt her, that's why they did it. "If they'd had their way, I'd be dead, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. That's one thing to be said about death — you can't hurt any more when you're dead. I don't think that's it. "But back to the point... I can understand why they burned the buildings, even the derelict ones. I can understand why they looted the sheds and then burned them down. I can understand why they tried to kill me[kiyoko.numKits 2 |, my family ][kiyoko.numKits 4 | |, the people Granny Komari sent over ] — burn [kiyoko.numKits 2 |us out while we slept |me out while I slept ]. But this... there was no reason to do any of it, and it would have taken so much time and effort to do so. The depths of that spite just boggle the mind; I can't quite believe it." Well, perhaps she could look at it another way; those crops were intended to give their lives so she could survive. The time the raiders wasted in spiting her and her work by destroying the crops actually bought her enough time for help to arrive, without which she would have perished. By her own admission, it'd come down to a matter of minutes, hadn't it? Instead of appearing relieved or comforted, Kinu just looks sadder at that, gathering up one of her five tails in the crook of her hand and tapping her fingers together. Emotions flit across her features — she was always one for wearing her heart on her sleeve — and then at long last, Kinu looks away from you. "I guess that's one way to put it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." It's clear that there's a lot more going on inside her head than she's willing to talk about, but you also know now's not the best time to press your daughter. You'll ask for her thoughts some other time... although with how she's behaving, you can guess them already. ] |[rand |"I am doing very well, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. While it is true that much misfortune and malice have befallen us in so short a time, it simply means that we must make a display of fortitude and show that we cannot be beaten down. I am endeavoring to live as normal a life as I can in the wake of the raid on our home, spite the attempt to make me cower in fear since they could not take my life." Is that healthy? "There is no perfect option here, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]," Kinu replies, perhaps a little more curtly than she ought to be. "That would be to not have this misfortune have happened at all. But since what has happened has happened, we must make do — morale is exceedingly important, and I must lead by example. IRefusing to be bowed while maintaining some reasonable degree of caution, it is a better outlook than looking over one's shoulder at every turn. So many people are depending on me, and I cannot afford to indulge in bouts of self-pitying." She doesn't look like she has slept well. "Of course I have neglected to rest overmuch, [pc.mf|Father|Mother] — no one has. There are so many reconstruction efforts to oversee, and I already have spent so many valuable days off my feet in a room filled with winterstem smoke. I assure you, I get as much respite as I need to, not as much as I want to. Your concern is appreciated and you mean well, but there is no need to overly concern yourself with the nuances of my situation, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." |"It is quite clear from my conversations with people during my daily routine that no one appreciates what has been done to me. There is an air of tension about the den, like a strand of silk pulled taut... but by leading by example and pursuing a calm and measured yet vigorous response to the attempt on my life, I can soothe unease and yet not appear to be inactive upon a direct insult upon my person. While it is enjoyable to know that so many people deeply care for me to the point where harm to my person causes them to be deeply aggrieved, rash action can be problematic." That's right. You don't want the kitsune lashing out at the entirely wrong people. That would cause more problems than it solves. "At best, it would be a waste of resources," Kinu agrees. "And despite the way people live in the governor's estate, there really is not much to be spared for anything in the way of drawn-out, violent action. It would doom us all, and the effort would be wasted." Hmph. And what of her squeeze? Is he going to be running around demanding that heads be chopped off? "Oh, he already is. But at least he is looking to chop off the correct heads, at any rate." Kinu gives you a thin, sly smile. "I may have given Nakano some instructions which he may find irksome but has no choice to obey — after all, I am not only the heir to his liege's liege, but also by religion and tradition, divine and untouchable. Matron Komari is more than content to let me have his services as military provost to keep him out of trouble... or at least keep him in the right kinds of trouble which will serve to be constructive." There's something about Kinu's placid little smile that sends shivers down your spine. She's always so refined and soft-spoken, but you need to remember that this is the daughter you raised, after all. "There are no issues, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I help him with his poetry and moderate his drinking. It is something to pass the time. If I can properly guide a man like Nakano along the direction which I need him to go, I am sure I can do the same for everyone else. At the end of the day, it is a matter of properly focusing efforts and energy so that I can pry further into the matter of the attempt on my life[kiyoko.numKits 2 | and that of my family ] in a calm and measured manner without waste. Please, do not concern yourself overly with this matter or my well-being, and focus on your own tasks." |[kiyoko.numKits 4 |"Matron Komari has taken Asagiri to be a shrine maiden under the care of Mikoto and Miyuki. I cannot say that this is a bad move — given what has happened to my little sister, this is probably the best course of action." You sigh. That as it may be, you just didn't wish any of this had happened to your family. Recompense is no substitute for prevention, as it were. It's good that your children are able to recover in some measure from the attempt on their lives in their own ways, but nothing will ever be the same again. Kinu gives you a thin smile that's probably meant to be pleasant. "I am not the same person as opposed to when I was a kit, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Things change. Circumstances change. We have to assess whether they are for the better or not and act accordingly, but once a day has passed it will never come again, for better or for worse. That is something that no one can do anything about. "But back to the point. With Asagiri suddenly having a change of vocation, I suppose it falls to me to replace her. She was going to be my second, such a quiet, wispy thing good at clerical work and other such mundane matters... I suppose I shall have to train Kasumi to take her place. She's got all of this planned out, hasn't she? "Much of a den mother's business is administration, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. If I were not good at it, my worthiness of Mother's title would certainly be quite diminished, would it not? It feels strange to be picking up Asagiri every evening from the shrine when we go home... but Mikoto tells me that if she were anywhere but in the colonies, she would have to go to the Isle of the Sun for coming into possession of this kind of spiritual power. An untrained wellspring like her is a danger not just to herself, but the people around her. Needs are as needs must... so long as everything is running smoothly, this is the best I can hope for." |"I will admit, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], that there are times when I wonder if I had done something different, I could have made the situation better back during that night." She can't change what happened. "Perhaps not, but by looking back and reflecting on the past, we can avoid making the same mistakes in the future. In fact, while learning from your own mistakes already places you a cut above the rest, it is better to learn from other peoples' mistakes. Not that this is applicable in this case, but it is useful to know. "Nevertheless... could I have done something better? In retrospect, I should have realized that trying to leave the den through the waterfall grotto was a bad idea, as it was a chokepoint for an ambush and the only way in or out. Yet at the same time, trying to scale the crater walls as we were, frightened, exhausted and injured, might have been equally if not more perilous. We have to make do with incomplete information and come to decisions that can easily cost lives, so even though what has come to pass cannot be taken back, reflecting on it is nevertheless highly beneficial and of vital importance." Well, when she puts it that way, she's certainly convinced herself of the necessity of what she's doing. And has she made any progress? "Some. Matron Komari has been kind enough to give me two hours off every day from my duties, and I spend them with Nakano, going over the events and speaking of the strategies the raiders used and possible countermeasures that would produce the most impact for the least cost. He keeps me appraised of what his subordinates have been doing... while this is the first true action that he has seen, the enthusiasm with which he takes to his duties is palpable. That is something I can use." You just shake your head at that. Kinu notices the gesture, and inclines her head towards you with a small smile, ears folding forward. "Fret not overmuch, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. We are taking this and learning from it, growing stronger. Yes, so are they, presumably, but that just means we have to work harder in order to catch up, is that not the case?" ] |"Everyone has been very kind to me ever since the attempt on my life. Well, everyone is very kind to me all the time, but moreso than ever of late. I cannot go by a handful of days without small gifts, polite inquiries as to my well-being, and other helpful gestures. It is really nice to be flattered so, but I should not let it get to my head." Well, it makes perfect sense. Your darling daughter is a symbol for her people to rally around — they want to make sure that she's lacking in nothing in the wake of such a danger. Oftentimes, it's only when what you love is threatened that you suddenly stop taking it for granted and realize how important it truly is to you. "Ah ha ha. Wise words, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], wise and true. At this point, Kohaku prepares taiyaki for me every other day; I can't eat it all myself and have to spread it around. [kiyoko.numKits 2 |Aya is always running around all day and is always willing to partake of something sweet, so I am more than willing to let her have most of it |Mikoto is always hungry no matter how much she eats, so I am always more than willing to allow her to partake of what I am simply unable to stomach myself ]. It feels a little shameful to be passing on gifts like this, but the alternative would be to let them go to waste. Still, it is not the material gifts which are important, but the spirit in which they are given. The latter alone would have been sufficient for me, but things are what they happen to be. Refusing another's gift is tantamount to saying that it is worse than worthless, after all, and I would not insult anyone by doing as much." |Kinu smiles and waves a hand. "It's amazing how much can get done in so short a time when you have able and willing hands working together in coordinated concert. Would you not agree, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?" That's right — if not for the burned shells of the derelict buildings on the outskirts of the den and that the crops in the fields and paddies are newly planted, you'd never have known that this place was raided not too long ago. Whatever else you may think of the kitsune, their ability to come together at a moment's notice and finish tasks without question or complaint is impressive. "I would not say it is a trait endemic to all of us, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], but it certainly is prevalent enough to be considered useful and helpful. The quiet knowledge that you will be similarly aided in your time of need by those obligated to reciprocate works wonders for motivating even the laziest stayabouts into working, if but out of a sense of self-preservation. It certainly has made recovering from this setback a lot easier. "Of course, that also means that I am obligated to give back to the people as much as I have received from them, otherwise an imbalance will be created that has to be corrected. One should not allow these things to be taken too far — no matter how great the goodwill, riding on its back too far is always dangerous and fickle. You have to give back in equal measure to what you take out." You're just glad that your daughter has grown into such an empathic and conscientious young woman. [pc.bg nobleScion |The upper crust in so many societies, the one you came from included, so often has terrible reputations when it comes to their duties. After all, you had a front-row seat to all the antics they got up to in your past as a noble scion, one of their own |People don't usually have an actively positive view of the people who rule over them, generally tending towards indifference, but you're glad that she's turned out differently ]. Kinu has that something about her that makes people believe she cares about them and want to love her, and you're just glad that she's using it for good and not evil. Your fox-daughter clicks her tongue and tsks. "Oh, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. What jests you make." ] ] ]

]说实话，我们在瀑布入口处布置了一些装饰措施，火山口的墙壁也建得相当高。我相信，通过足够的练习，我已经掌握了使用薙刀和短刀的技巧，如果有任何情况发生，我有信心保护好这个家族。让家族的运作交给我吧。[party.has kiyoko | | 还有母亲 ]去做你需要做的事情吧。 她不会有事的，对吧？ 你太为我担心了[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]虽然这地方确实很温馨，但你也不会想过分地保护你最心爱的女儿吧？我能够理解为什么母亲在多年前会选择这个地方来安顿自己的居所——这个地方防御工事完备，要想攻占它必须付出巨大的代价。我完全有能力照顾好自己。[kiyoko.numKits 2 | 还有其他所有人也是如此。 ]所以你应该把其中一些好运留下来自己使用，对吧？ |是的， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]别担心。我知道我不应该沿着这条路前往这里西南方向的那个原住民村庄。森林里到处都是各种可怕、恶心的东西，即使我没有遇到[silly |结局糟糕 |陷入麻烦 ]在这次旅途中，只要稍有不慎，我的真实面目就会暴露出来，到时候镇上的居民肯定会把我赶出这个地方，甚至更糟——把我吊死在绞架上。没错，我绝对不会去的，绝对不会。 [party.has kiyoko
