Please, do not concern yourself overly with this matter or my well-being, and focus on your own tasks." |[kiyoko.numKits 4 |"Matron Komari has taken Asagiri to be a shrine maiden under the care of Mikoto and Miyuki. I cannot say that this is a bad move — given what has happened to my little sister, this is probably the best course of action." You sigh. That as it may be, you just didn't wish any of this had happened to your family. Recompense is no substitute for prevention, as it were. It's good that your children are able to recover in some measure from the attempt on their lives in their own ways, but nothing will ever be the same again. Kinu gives you a thin smile that's probably meant to be pleasant. "I am not the same person as opposed to when I was a kit, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Things change. Circumstances change. We have to assess whether they are for the better or not and act accordingly, but once a day has passed it will never come again, for better or for worse. That is something that no one can do anything about. "But back to the point. With Asagiri suddenly having a change of vocation, I suppose it falls to me to replace her. She was going to be my second, such a quiet, wispy thing good at clerical work and other such mundane matters... I suppose I shall have to train Kasumi to take her place. She's got all of this planned out, hasn't she? "Much of a den mother's business is administration, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. If I were not good at it, my worthiness of Mother's title would certainly be quite diminished, would it not? It feels strange to be picking up Asagiri every evening from the shrine when we go home... but Mikoto tells me that if she were anywhere but in the colonies, she would have to go to the Isle of the Sun for coming into possession of this kind of spiritual power. An untrained wellspring like her is a danger not just to herself, but the people around her. Needs are as needs must... so long as everything is running smoothly, this is the best I can hope for." |"I will admit, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], that there are times when I wonder if I had done something different, I could have made the situation better back during that night." She can't change what happened. "Perhaps not, but by looking back and reflecting on the past, we can avoid making the same mistakes in the future. In fact, while learning from your own mistakes already places you a cut above the rest, it is better to learn from other peoples' mistakes. Not that this is applicable in this case, but it is useful to know. "Nevertheless... could I have done something better? In retrospect, I should have realized that trying to leave the den through the waterfall grotto was a bad idea, as it was a chokepoint for an ambush and the only way in or out. Yet at the same time, trying to scale the crater walls as we were, frightened, exhausted and injured, might have been equally if not more perilous. We have to make do with incomplete information and come to decisions that can easily cost lives, so even though what has come to pass cannot be taken back, reflecting on it is nevertheless highly beneficial and of vital importance." Well, when she puts it that way, she's certainly convinced herself of the necessity of what she's doing. And has she made any progress? "Some. Matron Komari has been kind enough to give me two hours off every day from my duties, and I spend them with Nakano, going over the events and speaking of the strategies the raiders used and possible countermeasures that would produce the most impact for the least cost. He keeps me appraised of what his subordinates have been doing... while this is the first true action that he has seen, the enthusiasm with which he takes to his duties is palpable. That is something I can use." You just shake your head at that. Kinu notices the gesture, and inclines her head towards you with a small smile, ears folding forward. "Fret not overmuch, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. We are taking this and learning from it, growing stronger. Yes, so are they, presumably, but that just means we have to work harder in order to catch up, is that not the case?" ] |"Everyone has been very kind to me ever since the attempt on my life. Well, everyone is very kind to me all the time, but moreso than ever of late. I cannot go by a handful of days without small gifts, polite inquiries as to my well-being, and other helpful gestures. It is really nice to be flattered so, but I should not let it get to my head." Well, it makes perfect sense. Your darling daughter is a symbol for her people to rally around — they want to make sure that she's lacking in nothing in the wake of such a danger. Oftentimes, it's only when what you love is threatened that you suddenly stop taking it for granted and realize how important it truly is to you. "Ah ha ha. Wise words, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], wise and true. At this point, Kohaku prepares taiyaki for me every other day; I can't eat it all myself and have to spread it around. [kiyoko.numKits 2 |Aya is always running around all day and is always willing to partake of something sweet, so I am more than willing to let her have most of it |Mikoto is always hungry no matter how much she eats, so I am always more than willing to allow her to partake of what I am simply unable to stomach myself ]. It feels a little shameful to be passing on gifts like this, but the alternative would be to let them go to waste. Still, it is not the material gifts which are important, but the spirit in which they are given. The latter alone would have been sufficient for me, but things are what they happen to be. Refusing another's gift is tantamount to saying that it is worse than worthless, after all, and I would not insult anyone by doing as much." |Kinu smiles and waves a hand. "It's amazing how much can get done in so short a time when you have able and willing hands working together in coordinated concert. Would you not agree, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?" That's right — if not for the burned shells of the derelict buildings on the outskirts of the den and that the crops in the fields and paddies are newly planted, you'd never have known that this place was raided not too long ago. Whatever else you may think of the kitsune, their ability to come together at a moment's notice and finish tasks without question or complaint is impressive. "I would not say it is a trait endemic to all of us, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], but it certainly is prevalent enough to be considered useful and helpful. The quiet knowledge that you will be similarly aided in your time of need by those obligated to reciprocate works wonders for motivating even the laziest stayabouts into working, if but out of a sense of self-preservation. It certainly has made recovering from this setback a lot easier. "Of course, that also means that I am obligated to give back to the people as much as I have received from them, otherwise an imbalance will be created that has to be corrected. One should not allow these things to be taken too far — no matter how great the goodwill, riding on its back too far is always dangerous and fickle. You have to give back in equal measure to what you take out." You're just glad that your daughter has grown into such an empathic and conscientious young woman. [pc.bg nobleScion |The upper crust in so many societies, the one you came from included, so often has terrible reputations when it comes to their duties. After all, you had a front-row seat to all the antics they got up to in your past as a noble scion, one of their own |People don't usually have an actively positive view of the people who rule over them, generally tending towards indifference, but you're glad that she's turned out differently ]. Kinu has that something about her that makes people believe she cares about them and want to love her, and you're just glad that she's using it for good and not evil. Your fox-daughter clicks her tongue and tsks. "Oh, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. What jests you make." ] ] ] "

rows.original: Discuss recent events regarding the kitsune with your daughter.
rows.translation: 和你的女儿聊聊最近关于狐妖的那些事情吧。
rows.raw: "Discuss recent events regarding the kitsune with your daughter."

rows.original: [kinu.isInari |[rand |"I suppose I'll be grateful to Mother for one thing: she taught me, by necessity or otherwise, to teach myself. If I hadn't known better, I might have lapsed into the belief that there was nothing in the world that she didn't know — and hence, couldn't teach; I might have been content with taking what was given to me and never exploring beyond those boundaries. Now, I'm glad I'm able to have the capacity to see what I want, what would be best for the people around me, and to follow both as best as I can." |"Learning by doing and demonstration is how things ought to get done," Kinu declares. "There's a time and place for sitting down in a room poring over a book with someone staring over my shoulder, and that was when I was a kit — if there ever was such a time to begin with, to be honest. I would get so stupidly and painfully bored if Hitoshi tried to explain everything over a table; instead, we walk out to the fields together and he shows me how it's done. It's impossible to fall asleep when your body is moving, and when your blood is up and active you're more alert when it comes to learning, though." She just sounds like a more active person. With that kind of personality, it's little wonder that a more hands-on approach is best for her. "Active? I don't know about that, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]; I wouldn't say I'm a lot more active than some people I know. But I also like seeing things that I do being put into practice, knowing with concrete certainty that they're, well, practical. It feels good seeing the results of what you learned there and then." |"Mai is trying to teach me some traditional dance, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. You know, that's where her nickname comes from — it means "to dance" in our mother tongue. She says that I've got the body and balance for it." And is it something she wants to learn, herself? Kinu smiles a little, then sticks her tongue out at you. "I have the old problem of my head getting ahead of my body, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It's not like I don't know what the moves are; I just have to get my arms and legs to do what I want them to, which admittedly, eh..." You can imagine. It's like when her mother starting trying to teach her how to wield weapons, right? Now your fox-daughter looks even more sheepish than before. "Yeah, kinda... I fell on my ass once, and Mai just laughed and said it was a good thing that I had such a big tush to cushion my fall. I know what to do — I can describe in excruciating detail all the moves she taught me — but like handling the [kinu.kinuWeapon|naginata|hankyu], it's simply a matter of practice and getting my muscles used to what I want them to do. Don't worry about it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]; I'll get it all down in good time. Being able to dance like Mai does looks fun, and like you, there's nothing I can't learn if I set my mind to it. Best inheritance ever, thanks [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." |"Hitoshi's been teaching me a bunch about how the various sluices, winches and other mechanisms in the den work so that I can go back and do upkeep on the ones he installed for me at home. Sometimes, I get a little ahead of him and then we have to go to Kazuo for a better explanation of it all, because I want to know how all of it works. I can follow what Kazuo's saying sometimes, but more often than not the artificer just talks over my head and I have to ask him to repeat himself. Still, working with my hands on things other than just the earth is fun. Girl's got to know how to keep everything about her in good working order, after all — can't be relying on other people to do everything for me all the time, no matter how helpful they're willing to be." If being hands-on is how she learns better, you don't see any reason to have qualms about it. Like she one said, she's not going to be falling asleep in this class. "It feels good to have the sun on my skin, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. That, and having the energy in me to do whatever I need to do every day, instead of forcing myself to get up and go through the motions. Learning's more about teaching your mind to do things — you've got to whip your body into shape, too. Then you've got to get the two into the habit of working with each other so you don't accidentally hack of your toe or something, haha. I just feel really fit and great these days, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], and I don't believe in the slightest that I could've gotten this kind of education the way Mother wanted me to." |"While Granny Komari doesn't play the shakuhachi herself, she managed to get Nakano to lay his hands on some pieces for me on the last trip he made back to the Old Country. I'm not sure where he gets them, but I'm grateful for his efforts, at least. I think he was also grateful for the opportunity to be able to help a princess like me, even if I am a princess who goes around tilling fields." It's good to hear that she'll be able to expand her music repertoire. "They're pretty hard pieces that're supposed to have originated with monks and all, so I'm taking my time and practicing out in the fields so that I don't bother everyone with all the noise. Sounds pretty awful in the meantime, but that's part and parcel of learning. The faster you fail, the faster you figure out what you did wrong and the faster you can actually get it right. That's the important thing, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom] — fearing failure because you'll lose face or something just means that you don't learn very much in the end. If you're that afraid of failure, you won't admit that you were wrong in the first place; if you don't do that then you'll learn absolutely nothing. So, I'm perfectly fine with making all sorts of horrendous noise over the fields while I learn the pieces. It's the only right thing to do." |"One of the most important things I learned as a kit was to have some self-discipline, and that's not something anyone can teach you but yourself. This goes doubly so when Mother's around less ever since we moved out of... well, it stands to reason, doesn't it? I guess if I were less scrupulous I wouldn't have to run as tight as ship as I do in her absence, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], but I wouldn't let me do it, if you know what I mean. "To be fair, I'm kinda proud of this — it's the base on which you learn how to teach yourself other things. If you don't have self-discipline and the will to see something through once it gets boring or you hit a snag, then you're not going to ever get anything done, let alone get used to doing it well. If you always need someone watching over your shoulder and breathing down your neck before you'll actually put in effort, then there's really not much point in very much at all. If you want to be independent, you've got to be able to hold yourself accountable. That's the important thing." |"I must say, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I've improved a lot when it comes to my board games. Having a whole lot of people to play against really broadened my horizons a lot when it came to a number of plays. While I still can't beat Mai in a straight-up game of shogi or go, playing with not just her, but Granny Komari, Miko and more have really opened my eyes to a number of strategies that I wouldn't have ever conceived of on my own. Not because I'm dumb, I'm sure, but because I would never have thought to do that kind of thing." That's perfectly fine. Even a smart cookie like her has blind spots, as she ought to know full well. "It's good that I'm getting to know a whole lot of people, yeah? It's not really hard to find someone to play with after field work every evening — folks over at Granny Komari's are pretty friendly, and all I have to do is set out the board, signal that I'm open to a game, and wait. It doesn't take long for someone to come along and take up the offer. Even Nakano, straight-laced as he is, passes by for a quick game, and never complains even if he loses. And when I lose... let's just say that playing with Mai has taught me to take defeat well. Would never have gotten that kind of thing just by playing with Mother[kiyoko.numKits 2| and my siblings]." You'll see about playing with her again when you've the time. "Ah ha ha, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It won't be like when I was a kit any more. I won't go easy on you just because we're related, you know." Has she ever gone easy on you when it comes to board games? "All the time when I was a kit, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. No quarter from here on out, though. I'm a grown woman now!" |"You know how they say that there eventually comes a day when you've learned all you can from others, and from here on out the world is going to be your teacher? Well, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I'm still pretty far from that point, but I think that being here in the colonies has given me a little bit of understanding and personal experience as to the truth of that matter. I get that this is your native land and all[pc.ra kitsune| even if you did choose to become one of us], so it's not strange to you in the least, but there're so many strange and unique interactions with... well, for example, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], how the soil and climate affect some of the crops that were brought over to begin with. More than two hundred years and Hitoshi's still standing on the shoulders of those who came before him, trying to perfect their art. "It's humbling, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], to know that everything we have doesn't really belong to us; it was given for us to keep by our ancestors, and it isn't our to do as we like because we're keeping it for our kits. In the meantime, it's our job to make it better, which I am in my own way, I guess. I... I don't need to do what Mother wants me to do in order to play my part in all this; what I do is just as important, if not strictly as far-reaching as being an actual princess or whatever it was she had in mind for me." ] |[rand |"Both Mother and Matron Komari are working to teach me protocol, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Since Matron Komari does not know when she will complete her penance in the eyes of our divine lord, someone else to help shoulder her burden in representing the colonies is appreciated." Hmm, what about Miko and Mai? "Mikoto and Miyuki are of the same clan as the den matron, and thus... do not really count in that regard. Another house to help represent the western imperial colonies would help greatly in putting the appropriate amount of pressure on the other side of the ocean." It's a matter of politics, then.[pc.bg noblescion courtesan| No matter where you go, it's always politics. You left your old life in part to get away from that kind of stuff, and now it's tracked you all the way here... and latched onto your daughter. Some things never change.] "Yes, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Mother is... not always available, and so the task falls to me. Matron Komari tells me that I am quite the student, for what it is worth." |"Miyuki is attempting to teach me something of traditional dance. That is how she earned her moniker, after all — 'Mai', very simply, means 'dance' in our mother tongue. She has been dancing since a very young age, often as part of her shrine maiden duties, and I can think of no better teacher than her in this regard. While she might have talent and an excellent body suited to the art, Miyuki has clearly worked very hard to get to where she is today." Heh, she's talking about Mai when you asked her about her own education. That's so much like your daughter. "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... I did not mean to evade your question. Well... Mother knew something of dancing, but did not really have anyone else to practice with. That, and I was young at the time; I suppose I decided to wait until my body matured further and my sense of balance came into its own? Whichever the case, it is not too late to start learning, and Miyuki is clearly a master of her craft; she performs all the sacred dances during festivals. Not that Mikoto is unwilling to go on stage and put on a show, of course, but Granny Komari forbids it for obvious reasons. That, and while technically proficient, Mikoto is —" It's all right for her to talk about herself and what she's doing; it's not necessary for her to use humble language here. You want to know about your darling daughter, not anyone else. "Ah. Oh. I am doing very well. Traditional dance certainly helps me find my sense of balance and get more acquainted with my body. I feel more limber and in control of my nerves and reflexes, the way Miyuki does it... aha. She also says that since I bear divine blood, I am eligible to perform the sacred dances with her at festivals when I am skilled enough... I will admit, the idea is very thrilling. I have seen Miyuki dance at those, and while I am determined to not give up until I do achieve such a level of proficiency, I wonder how long that will take, even given my talents..." |"Ever since leaving the Astral Plane, I have been able to meet many more opponents in board games of strategy. It soon became apparent that indeed, being only able to play against my family had stunted my thinking through lack of experience with a variety of strategies — being able to play against Mikoto, Miyuki, and even Matron Komari has broadened my horizons considerably. They all employ strategies that I would never have come up with on my own, not because I was lacking in wit or intellect to do so, but simply because I would not have seen such with my frame of mind unless externally prompted. Continually losing, too... that is a good teacher of being graceful in defeat and swallowing one's pride." And a very roundabout way of saying that a youth of winning handily has not prepared her in the least for such. "Ah... I would prefer not to dwell on the shameful, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Of everyone I have played so far, I would say I enjoy games of shogi with Nakano the most. The way he strategises is... improbable. Some would say insane. But it usually works out in the end. When we're on opposite sides of the board, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], I get insight into a portion of his mind he rarely shows to anyone else, even his family. His mind is tied up into knots and inscrutable even to me; it is so exciting. Win or lose, I walk away from our games feeling most satisfied with the outcome." |"While Mother is extremely proficient at the koto, she has only been able to teach me pieces from more than two centuries ago. That is why I am exceedingly grateful for Matron Komari's efforts in sourcing new, more recent pieces from across the ocean for me to play. True, receiving instruction on a personal level is one of the simple joys that one can do for another, but there is also something to be said for trying to figure it out for yourself." So, she practices alone, then? "Sometimes. But I always make it a point to attempt any new piece for the first time with Mother. The simple joy of her having something new to play... the sheer pleasure she can take in so seemingly mundane an act is truly inspiring. After that... while I could do it by myself, why should I unless I have to? If she is around and otherwise unoccupied, there is no reason why I should not practice the koto with her. I learn far better when it is with someone, after all, and especially so when that someone is Mother." |"I am trying to involve myself more and more in small disputes informally as an arbitrator of sorts. Petty cases of no large import that do not need to be taken up to the den matron as a matter of course. Officially seeking redress would eat up valuable time and resources, and so disagreements are best smoothed over at the lowest possible level, if not the personal." She is allowed to do that? Kinu smile wanly and tosses her head of silvery-white hair, running her nimble fingers through her locks. "Even if I have no formal position or title, I am descended from divinity, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. What good is it for if I cannot exercise its authority every now and then? Resolving small disputes is an excellent exercise in learning much about people, and how to negotiate cleanly and clearly — and of course, when negotiation and discourse is not the right tool for the task at hand." It doesn't hurt that the people of the den seem to like her well enough. "It certainly helps in their acceptance of my arbitration, even when the outcome is not entirely to their liking. I am aspiring to cultivate a reputation like that of our divine lord of being hard but fair. Proportional to the situation at hand, if sometimes a little unorthodox. I think I am beginning to see that come to fruition, even if there is much to be done. Here in the colonies, everyone knows each other, and peacemaking is a skill that is preferably done on a very personal level. To be honest, I hope it stays that way." |"Matron Komari is adding to my understanding of the history of my homeland — after all, there is a two hundred and fifty-year gap in Mother's understanding as well as mine, and she has just as much to learn about the current situation as I do. Perhaps it is said that those who do not learn from history are doomed to repeat it, and those who do learn from history are doomed to watch others repeat it. For someone in my position, though, perhaps I will have the opportunity to be able to change some small part of it, which is why I am earnestly applying myself in the pursuit of such. You cannot understand where you are going if you do not know where you are coming from, as the saying goes." |"One's environment is important when one attempts to partake of any learning or education," Kinu declares. "While sometimes the venue is unavoidable, where I can I prefer to be in sunlight or out in the open." Heh. That's something that's carried over from when she was a kit. "It is conducive to have adequate light, fresh air and serene surroundings. Fewer things around that could distract one from the subject at hand. Simply going out back onto the deck and facing my garden and pond is enough most of the time. When the mind is calm and focused, one loses track of the passing of time when applying oneself to one's education. Being cooped up all day with all manner of distractions is the complete opposite of conducive." |"Some time ago I had another discussion with Mother over where my education is headed and what direction I want to take in order to achieve that. I suppose that my hope is to be able to be useful to the people of the imperial colonies, even if I am not given any formal position or title. Things are what they are here on the other side of the ocean, and the de facto is more important than the de jure, as things stand. "But to the point... the things that I must know are broad in scope and nature, and I suppose that is where the talent you passed on to me is coming in exceedingly useful. Just picking up subjects in the snap of one's fingers — I cannot thank you enough for that, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. It is an extremely useful skill to have, and an inheritance that cannot be matched." ] ]
rows.translation: [kinu.isInari |[rand |我想，有件事我确实应该感谢我的母亲：无论是出于必要还是其他原因，她教会了我如何自学。如果我没有认清这一点，我可能会误以为这个世界上没有她不知道的事情——因此也就没有什么她不能教给我的；我可能会满足于接受别人给予我的一切，而从不去探索更远的领域。现在，我很庆幸自己有能力去判断自己真正想要什么，以及什么才是对我周围的人最有益的，然后尽我所能去追求这些目标。 |通过实践和示范来学习，这才是正确的学习方式。小娟宣布道。有时候，确实需要找一个安静的地方，和别人一起坐在房间里仔细阅读一本书，而有人则会站在我的身后，盯着我看……那种时候，我就觉得自己像一个工具一样——如果真的有这样的时候的话是说实话，现在这个时机真的不太合适。如果仁试图在桌旁把一切都解释清楚，我会感到无聊至极，甚至会感到痛苦。相反，我们一起去田野里，他亲自示范给我看怎么做。当你的身体在运动时，根本不可能睡着；而且当你的血液流动得活跃起来时，你在学习方面也会变得更加专注、更加敏锐。 她听起来就是那种更活跃的人。拥有这样的性格，难怪采取更实际、更主动的方式才最适合她。 激活了？这个我就不清楚了[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我不敢说自己比一些我认识的人更活跃。但我确实喜欢看到自己所学的东西被付诸实践，能够确信这些方法确实是有效的。看到自己所学的知识带来的实际成果，那种感觉真的很棒。 |舞正在试图教我一些传统的舞蹈。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]你知道，她的昵称就是从那里来的——在我们母语中，它的意思是“跳舞”。她说我拥有适合跳舞的身体条件和平衡感。 这是她自己想要学习的东西吗？ 小娟微微一笑，然后吐了吐舌头对着你。我仍然面临着那个老问题——我的思维总是先于行动。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我又不是不想这么做。知道这些动作要怎么做呢？我只需要让自己的手臂和腿按照我的意愿来活动就行了，不过说实话，嗯…… 你可以想象，这就像她的母亲开始教她如何使用武器一样，对吧？ 现在，你的狐妖女儿看起来比之前更加害羞了。是啊，有点吧……有一次我摔了一跤，舞只是笑着说，还好我的屁股这么大，能缓冲冲击力呢。知道该怎么做呢？我可以极其详细地描述她教给我的所有动作，但就像处理那个问题一样[kinu.kinuWeapon|长刀|汉京]这只是一个需要不断练习、让肌肉逐渐适应我所要求它们做出的动作而已。别担心，没问题的。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我会及时把所有内容都记录下来。能够像舞那样跳舞，真是太棒了有趣和你一样，只要我下定决心，就没有什么是我学不会的。这是最珍贵的馈赠，真的太感谢了。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]。" I know what to do — I can describe in excruciating detail all the moves she taught me — but like handling the [kinu.kinuWeapon|naginata|hankyu], it's simply a matter of practice and getting my muscles used to what I want them to do. Don't worry about it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]; I'll get it all down in good time. Being able to dance like Mai does looks fun, and like you, there's nothing I can't learn if I set my mind to it. Best inheritance ever, thanks [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." |"Hitoshi's been teaching me a bunch about how the various sluices, winches and other mechanisms in the den work so that I can go back and do upkeep on the ones he installed for me at home. Sometimes, I get a little ahead of him and then we have to go to Kazuo for a better explanation of it all, because I want to know how all of it works. I can follow what Kazuo's saying sometimes, but more often than not the artificer just talks over my head and I have to ask him to repeat himself. Still, working with my hands on things other than just the earth is fun. Girl's got to know how to keep everything about her in good working order, after all — can't be relying on other people to do everything for me all the time, no matter how helpful they're willing to be." If being hands-on is how she learns better, you don't see any reason to have qualms about it. Like she one said, she's not going to be falling asleep in this class. "It feels good to have the sun on my skin, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. That, and having the energy in me to do whatever I need to do every day, instead of forcing myself to get up and go through the motions. Learning's more about teaching your mind to do things — you've got to whip your body into shape, too. Then you've got to get the two into the habit of working with each other so you don't accidentally hack of your toe or something, haha. I just feel really fit and great these days, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], and I don't believe in the slightest that I could've gotten this kind of education the way Mother wanted me to." |"While Granny Komari doesn't play the shakuhachi herself, she managed to get Nakano to lay his hands on some pieces for me on the last trip he made back to the Old Country. I'm not sure where he gets them, but I'm grateful for his efforts, at least. I think he was also grateful for the opportunity to be able to help a princess like me, even if I am a princess who goes around tilling fields." It's good to hear that she'll be able to expand her music repertoire. "They're pretty hard pieces that're supposed to have originated with monks and all, so I'm taking my time and practicing out in the fields so that I don't bother everyone with all the noise. Sounds pretty awful in the meantime, but that's part and parcel of learning. The faster you fail, the faster you figure out what you did wrong and the faster you can actually get it right. That's the important thing, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom] — fearing failure because you'll lose face or something just means that you don't learn very much in the end. If you're that afraid of failure, you won't admit that you were wrong in the first place; if you don't do that then you'll learn absolutely nothing. So, I'm perfectly fine with making all sorts of horrendous noise over the fields while I learn the pieces. It's the only right thing to do." |"One of the most important things I learned as a kit was to have some self-discipline, and that's not something anyone can teach you but yourself. This goes doubly so when Mother's around less ever since we moved out of... well, it stands to reason, doesn't it? I guess if I were less scrupulous I wouldn't have to run as tight as ship as I do in her absence, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], but I wouldn't let me do it, if you know what I mean. "To be fair, I'm kinda proud of this — it's the base on which you learn how to teach yourself other things. If you don't have self-discipline and the will to see something through once it gets boring or you hit a snag, then you're not going to ever get anything done, let alone get used to doing it well. If you always need someone watching over your shoulder and breathing down your neck before you'll actually put in effort, then there's really not much point in very much at all. If you want to be independent, you've got to be able to hold yourself accountable. That's the important thing." |"I must say, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I've improved a lot when it comes to my board games. Having a whole lot of people to play against really broadened my horizons a lot when it came to a number of plays. While I still can't beat Mai in a straight-up game of shogi or go, playing with not just her, but Granny Komari, Miko and more have really opened my eyes to a number of strategies that I wouldn't have ever conceived of on my own. Not because I'm dumb, I'm sure, but because I would never have thought to do that kind of thing." That's perfectly fine. Even a smart cookie like her has blind spots, as she ought to know full well. "It's good that I'm getting to know a whole lot of people, yeah? It's not really hard to find someone to play with after field work every evening — folks over at Granny Komari's are pretty friendly, and all I have to do is set out the board, signal that I'm open to a game, and wait. It doesn't take long for someone to come along and take up the offer. Even Nakano, straight-laced as he is, passes by for a quick game, and never complains even if he loses. And when I lose... let's just say that playing with Mai has taught me to take defeat well. Would never have gotten that kind of thing just by playing with Mother[kiyoko.numKits 2| and my siblings]." You'll see about playing with her again when you've the time. "Ah ha ha, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It won't be like when I was a kit any more. I won't go easy on you just because we're related, you know." Has she ever gone easy on you when it comes to board games? "All the time when I was a kit, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. No quarter from here on out, though. I'm a grown woman now!" |"You know how they say that there eventually comes a day when you've learned all you can from others, and from here on out the world is going to be your teacher? Well, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I'm still pretty far from that point, but I think that being here in the colonies has given me a little bit of understanding and personal experience as to the truth of that matter. I get that this is your native land and all[pc.ra kitsune| even if you did choose to become one of us], so it's not strange to you in the least, but there're so many strange and unique interactions with... well, for example, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], how the soil and climate affect some of the crops that were brought over to begin with. More than two hundred years and Hitoshi's still standing on the shoulders of those who came before him, trying to perfect their art. "It's humbling, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], to know that everything we have doesn't really belong to us; it was given for us to keep by our ancestors, and it isn't our to do as we like because we're keeping it for our kits. In the meantime, it's our job to make it better, which I am in my own way, I guess. I... I don't need to do what Mother wants me to do in order to play my part in all this; what I do is just as important, if not strictly as far-reaching as being an actual princess or whatever it was she had in mind for me." ] |[rand |"Both Mother and Matron Komari are working to teach me protocol, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Since Matron Komari does not know when she will complete her penance in the eyes of our divine lord, someone else to help shoulder her burden in representing the colonies is appreciated." Hmm, what about Miko and Mai? "Mikoto and Miyuki are of the same clan as the den matron, and thus... do not really count in that regard. Another house to help represent the western imperial colonies would help greatly in putting the appropriate amount of pressure on the other side of the ocean." It's a matter of politics, then.[pc.bg noblescion courtesan| No matter where you go, it's always politics. You left your old life in part to get away from that kind of stuff, and now it's tracked you all the way here... and latched onto your daughter. Some things never change.] "Yes, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Mother is... not always available, and so the task falls to me. Matron Komari tells me that I am quite the student, for what it is worth." |"Miyuki is attempting to teach me something of traditional dance. That is how she earned her moniker, after all — 'Mai', very simply, means 'dance' in our mother tongue. She has been dancing since a very young age, often as part of her shrine maiden duties, and I can think of no better teacher than her in this regard. While she might have talent and an excellent body suited to the art, Miyuki has clearly worked very hard to get to where she is today." Heh, she's talking about Mai when you asked her about her own education. That's so much like your daughter. "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... I did not mean to evade your question. Well... Mother knew something of dancing, but did not really have anyone else to practice with. That, and I was young at the time; I suppose I decided to wait until my body matured further and my sense of balance came into its own? Whichever the case, it is not too late to start learning, and Miyuki is clearly a master of her craft; she performs all the sacred dances during festivals. Not that Mikoto is unwilling to go on stage and put on a show, of course, but Granny Komari forbids it for obvious reasons. That, and while technically proficient, Mikoto is —" It's all right for her to talk about herself and what she's doing; it's not necessary for her to use humble language here. You want to know about your darling daughter, not anyone else. "Ah. Oh. I am doing very well. Traditional dance certainly helps me find my sense of balance and get more acquainted with my body. I feel more limber and in control of my nerves and reflexes, the way Miyuki does it... aha. She also says that since I bear divine blood, I am eligible to perform the sacred dances with her at festivals when I am skilled enough... I will admit, the idea is very thrilling. I have seen Miyuki dance at those, and while I am determined to not give up until I do achieve such a level of proficiency, I wonder how long that will take, even given my talents..." |"Ever since leaving the Astral Plane, I have been able to meet many more opponents in board games of strategy. It soon became apparent that indeed, being only able to play against my family had stunted my thinking through lack of experience with a variety of strategies — being able to play against Mikoto, Miyuki, and even Matron Komari has broadened my horizons considerably. They all employ strategies that I would never have come up with on my own, not because I was lacking in wit or intellect to do so, but simply because I would not have seen such with my frame of mind unless externally prompted. Continually losing, too... that is a good teacher of being graceful in defeat and swallowing one's pride." And a very roundabout way of saying that a youth of winning handily has not prepared her in the least for such. "Ah... I would prefer not to dwell on the shameful, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Of everyone I have played so far, I would say I enjoy games of shogi with Nakano the most. The way he strategises is... improbable. Some would say insane. But it usually works out in the end. When we're on opposite sides of the board, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], I get insight into a portion of his mind he rarely shows to anyone else, even his family. His mind is tied up into knots and inscrutable even to me; it is so exciting. Win or lose, I walk away from our games feeling most satisfied with the outcome." |"While Mother is extremely proficient at the koto, she has only been able to teach me pieces from more than two centuries ago. That is why I am exceedingly grateful for Matron Komari's efforts in sourcing new, more recent pieces from across the ocean for me to play. True, receiving instruction on a personal level is one of the simple joys that one can do for another, but there is also something to be said for trying to figure it out for yourself." So, she practices alone, then? "Sometimes. But I always make it a point to attempt any new piece for the first time with Mother. The simple joy of her having something new to play... the sheer pleasure she can take in so seemingly mundane an act is truly inspiring. After that... while I could do it by myself, why should I unless I have to? If she is around and otherwise unoccupied, there is no reason why I should not practice the koto with her. I learn far better when it is with someone, after all, and especially so when that someone is Mother." |"I am trying to involve myself more and more in small disputes informally as an arbitrator of sorts. Petty cases of no large import that do not need to be taken up to the den matron as a matter of course. Officially seeking redress would eat up valuable time and resources, and so disagreements are best smoothed over at the lowest possible level, if not the personal." She is allowed to do that? Kinu smile wanly and tosses her head of silvery-white hair, running her nimble fingers through her locks. "Even if I have no formal position or title, I am descended from divinity, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. What good is it for if I cannot exercise its authority every now and then? Resolving small disputes is an excellent exercise in learning much about people, and how to negotiate cleanly and clearly — and of course, when negotiation and discourse is not the right tool for the task at hand." It doesn't hurt that the people of the den seem to like her well enough. "It certainly helps in their acceptance of my arbitration, even when the outcome is not entirely to their liking. I am aspiring to cultivate a reputation like that of our divine lord of being hard but fair. Proportional to the situation at hand, if sometimes a little unorthodox. I think I am beginning to see that come to fruition, even if there is much to be done. Here in the colonies, everyone knows each other, and peacemaking is a skill that is preferably done on a very personal level. To be honest, I hope it stays that way." |"Matron Komari is adding to my understanding of the history of my homeland — after all, there is a two hundred and fifty-year gap in Mother's understanding as well as mine, and she has just as much to learn about the current situation as I do. Perhaps it is said that those who do not learn from history are doomed to repeat it, and those who do learn from history are doomed to watch others repeat it. For someone in my position, though, perhaps I will have the opportunity to be able to change some small part of it, which is why I am earnestly applying myself in the pursuit of such. You cannot understand where you are going if you do not know where you are coming from, as the saying goes." |"One's environment is important when one attempts to partake of any learning or education," Kinu declares. "While sometimes the venue is unavoidable, where I can I prefer to be in sunlight or out in the open." Heh. That's something that's carried over from when she was a kit. "It is conducive to have adequate light, fresh air and serene surroundings. Fewer things around that could distract one from the subject at hand. Simply going out back onto the deck and facing my garden and pond is enough most of the time. When the mind is calm and focused, one loses track of the passing of time when applying oneself to one's education. Being cooped up all day with all manner of distractions is the complete opposite of conducive." |"Some time ago I had another discussion with Mother over where my education is headed and what direction I want to take in order to achieve that. I suppose that my hope is to be able to be useful to the people of the imperial colonies, even if I am not given any formal position or title. Things are what they are here on the other side of the ocean, and the de facto is more important than the de jure, as things stand. "But to the point... the things that I must know are broad in scope and nature, and I suppose that is where the talent you passed on to me is coming in exceedingly useful. Just picking up subjects in the snap of one's fingers — I cannot thank you enough for that, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. It is an extremely useful skill to have, and an inheritance that cannot be matched." ] ] "

rows.original: Your daughter may be a young woman now, but that doesn't mean she can let up on her education in the slightest. Eighteen is still green and fresh-faced by kitsune standards, and she's still got a lot to learn.
rows.translation: 你的女儿虽然现在已经是个年轻女子了，但这并不意味着她可以丝毫放松自己的教育。按狐族的标准来看，十八岁仍然是个青涩稚嫩、没见过世面的年纪，她还有很多东西需要学习。
rows.raw: "Your daughter may be a young woman now, but that doesn't mean she can let up on her education in the slightest. Eighteen is still green and fresh-faced by kitsune standards, and she's still got a lot to learn."

rows.original: You've heard about this... what's up with it?
rows.translation: 你肯定听说过这个……到底是怎么回事呢？
rows.raw: "You've heard about this... what's up with it?"

rows.original: [kinu.isInari |At the mere mention of her engagement, your fox-daughter's entire demeanor shifts slightly but perceptibly, her expression turning blatantly defensive. "Yeah, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. What about it?" |When you mention her engagement, your fox-daughter's ears fold forward slightly, and there's a brief pause in her speech. "Is something the matter, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?" ] You've been hearing things about her around the den, how people are bandying about gossip that she's — well, she doesn't just have a suitor, but a fiance. That she's engaged to get married sometime in the future. [kinu.isInari |Kinu crosses her arms. "Yeah, that's right, Hitoshi and I are engaged. It was one of the first things I did after I got settled in at our new home, really. He and I hit it off pretty well, so I went to Granny Komari and asked about it. She was pretty enthused about the whole idea, so she said she'd talk to her grandson about it, and it wasn't too long after that he proposed to me. Of course, since it was my idea to begin with, I said yes." ... "Why are you bringing this up, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]?" The underlying note of contentiousness in your daughter's voice is unmistakable; she clearly expects to have to challenge you on this. "Is there a problem?" |Kinu closes her eyes and gives you a small nod. "That is correct, Nakano and I are engaged; it was one of the first things that happened after Mother and I got settled in at our new accommodations. Given that he and I were getting along excellently to begin with, Mother thought it a good idea for such a relationship to be formalized before tongues started wagging of their own accord. Matron Komari begged to differ, but Mother spoke to her and she has agreed to go forward with the matter and take developments in stride. "Once the relevant parties had all settled things, it was not too long after that he proposed to me in the — ah, proper fashion. Of course, since I was a driving force in bringing matters to bear, I accepted without hesitation." ... "I sense unease coming from you, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Kinu refills her own cup. "Does this turn of events displease you?" ] No, you're not going to stand in her way; it's clear that her mind is set on this course of action and nothing you say at this point is going to dissuade her. It's just — well, everything's been moving so quickly, and you really do wish that she'd told you that it was going to happen to begin with. [kinu.isInari |"Oh." You see Kinu relax and the hostility fades somewhat, although it's clear that your daughter is still on edge. "I don't know about how things are done in this part of the world, really, but as far as I understand it this is perfectly normal for how we do things, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I know I'm Mom's heir and all, so I've always been raised with the expectation of marrying young, yeah? I guess I didn't consider that it might be a surprise to you, since you wouldn't have any way of knowing. Sorry about that. "And as for not telling you... well, I don't know why, I thought you'd end up as much against it as Mother was. She didn't like the idea and I guess I can see why she would think that way, but it's not something that I would've agreed with. Still, if Granny Komari hadn't come and thrown her weight behind me it wouldn't have gone through nevertheless; I owe her one for that." Kiyoko was against it, huh. "Okay, so maybe she was kinda right, but I'm not really trying to get married so I can escape this house, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I'm not that desperate to be rid of Mother that I'd throw myself into a bad marriage, thanks a lot. Hitoshi's not simple, he just doesn't talk a lot, and frankly neither do I, so we get on very well. He's a nice guy, he's stable, and frankly after my childhood I think I need a lot of that where it counts, thank you very much." |"Ah." You see Kinu relax somewhat, although it's clear that your daughter is still on edge in her own genteel, passive-aggressive fashion. "It... it is easy to forget that you do not come from our background, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], and that maybe things are done differently in this part of the world. As far as I am concerned, though, this is a perfect pace of things — not too quick, not too slow. Being my mother's heir... I have always expected that I would marry soon, if not immediately after I came of age; it is one of the expected duties of my station in exchange for the privileges that I have enjoyed in life. It was an oversight that I did not consider that you might find the pace of progression to be unsettling, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], and for this I offer my apologies. "As for not telling you directly... ah, I suppose there is no hiding it. Both you and Nakano have some degree of animosity, [pc.ra kitsune |even if he has had no choice but to accept who you are and your station. It is entertaining watching him trying to work out which of his allegiances and beliefs takes precedence over the other, but his agony over the entire situation is quite real |for reasons that I should not have to expound upon ]. I had not hoped to wish to have this confrontation, even if it was inevitable, and hence kept on delaying the matter of informing you... this is, of course, a failing that is entirely on my part." Did she really think so little of you to imagine that you would get in her way if it came down to it? Uncomfortable silence. "Yes." ...Is she happy with the arrangements? "Despite Mother's laments that I should have read fewer romances when I was younger, I understand that my expectations from a marriage should be realistic, even if a girl like I once was can dream. This is bigger than the two of us, and expecting to be happy all the time is simply dooming myself to failure. Contentment is more reasonable. Nakano and I are getting along reasonably well; I think I may have even managed to inspire him to improve his poetry. This is something even his own kin have failed to do. But to answer your question, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], you need not worry about me." ] That's... that's good, you guess. Does she know how long the engagement will last? [kinu.isInari |"For a little while longer, I'd say. Not just to feel things out and get Mother over her objections, but also to make sure the preparations are right and have things settle down in the world before we can really turn our minds to that kind of stuff." |"For longer than most. This would be not just to allow people to get used to the idea and come to accept it as reality, but also to make sure the preparations for such a momentous event are properly seen to and have the world calm down a bit before we can turn our minds to such things. There is the political side of things, as spurious as it is given that Mother has abdicated her position, but I suppose it must be taken care of." ] ...Good, good. You've already missed so much of Kinu's childhood, you wouldn't want to be absent on her wedding day too, even if it were supposedly for a good reason. That's something that you wouldn't be able to live down. [kinu.isInari |"Aw, sheesh, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. You don't need to get all sentimental about it, it's just something that happens as a part of life and you're embarrassing me." Reaching over, Kinu leans in and gives you a brief hug, pulling away quickly and looking quite a bit flustered herself. "It's okay — you'll probably be done with this whole saving the world thing by the time things actually roll around to a head, so you don't have to worry about missing my wedding or anything, okay?" |"Such sentimentality coming from you, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... given that this is but a natural part of one's life, it is a little embarrassing to have you speak of it in such glowing terms." Kinu raises a hand to her face, but can't hide the color in her cheeks from showing. "Rest assured that the wedding will not be anytime soon; you will be likely to be done with the most pressing of your tasks before the date arrives, so you do not have to worry about being absent on the day." ] That's good to hear. You just... you're not entirely sure why you had such a strong reaction to all this when you found out. Maybe it's like she said, it's but a part of her growing up, but her not needing you any more the way she did when she was a child stings a little. You know it's selfish of you to want to keep her dependent just so you can feel better about it all and you shouldn't be thinking that way, but even so, it still stings. [kinu.isInari |"Well, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], think of it this way: if I don't need you any more, that just means that if I'm still with you, it's because I chose to be that way. And isn't that a lot more meaningful than me hanging around just because I have to?" |"Perhaps you should consider this, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]: if I am no longer mandated by simple need to be with you, then the fact that I am still here is because I chose to be so. In that way, is that conscious decision not far more meaningful and powerful than my presence being dictated by sheer necessity?" ] Ah, when she puts it into those words... that does make you feel better. In the future, though... you want to stay as involved in her life as you can, and as is comfortable for her. You know full well that you're gone more often than you'd like to be able to make up for all the time lost, and whatever happens, you still love Kinu as your daughter. That's important. Even if you're not in a position to make any meaningful difference in the outcomes of events pertaining to her, you still want to be informed of such when you come home to check in rather than have to hear about it from other people. [kinu.isInari |"I'll think about it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." She'll think about it? "I don't like making promises I don't know I will be able to keep." Kinu sighs. "Not because I don't want to tell you or anything, but circumstances may not... how about if I can tell you, I'll tell you, and we leave it at that? And I will do everything I can to do so, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." |"I will do my best, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Her best? That's fine, but you were expecting... you don't know, a more firm response. "If life has taught me nothing else, it is that making promises you do not know you will be able to keep is asking for trouble. Not that I wish to withhold such news from you, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], but with things being what they are now, circumstances may not allow for such. If I can tell you, then I will, and rest assured that my utmost efforts shall be focused upon letting you know. That is as much as I can give." ] Ah... well, it'll have to do. [kinu.isInari |"I think that settles that, then," Kinu says, smacking you on the back with one of her tails. "Like I said, despite how quickly the engagement came about, there'll be plenty of time before the wedding actually takes place. You don't have to worry about missing it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom] — [silly |you have the writer's guarantee that it's not going to take place in the course of this game, so there's that |I'm sure all this will be resolved before the date comes around ]. Now, can we talk about something else?" |"Well, that concludes the matter," Kinu says, giving you a small dip of her head. "Despite how quickly the engagement came about, there will be adequate time before the date of the wedding takes place. You will not have to worry about missing it in the least, [pc.mf|Father|Mother] — [silly |you have the writer's guarantee that it is not going to take place in the course of this game, so let your mind be at peace |surely your duties and other matters will be in order before then ]. Now, is there something else you would like to discuss?" ]
rows.translation: [kinu.isInari |一提到她订婚的事，你那个狐狸女儿的整个举止就发生了细微但明显的变化，她的表情明显变得戒备起来。“是啊， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]那又怎么样？ |每当你提到她订婚的事时，你那位狐妖女儿的耳朵就会微微向前耷拉下来，说话时也会暂时停顿一下。“是不是出了什么问题？ [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]？" ] 你在团队里经常听到关于她的传闻，人们都在议论着一些八卦——说她不仅有一个追求者，而且还有一个未婚夫。据说她已经订婚了，将来会结婚的。 [kinu.isInari |小娟双臂交叉说道：“没错，我和仁是订婚了。其实这真的是我搬进新家后做的第一件事之一。我们俩相处得非常融洽，所以我就去问了麻里奶奶，她对这个想法非常支持，还说会和她孙子谈谈。没过多久，他就向我提出了求婚。当然，因为这个主意本来就是我提出的，所以我当然答应了。” …… “你为什么要提起这件事呢？ [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]？”你女儿语气中那股明显的争执意味显而易见，她显然打算就此与你争论。“出了什么问题吗？ |小娟闭上了眼睛，轻轻点了点头：“没错，中野和我已经订婚了。这是在我和母亲搬到新住处后发生的第一批事情之一。由于我们俩本来就相处得非常融洽，母亲认为，在别人开始闲言碎语之前，把这种关系正式确定下来是个好主意。麻里女首领并不认同这一观点，但母亲与她谈过了，她最终同意继续推进这件事，并从容应对后续的发展。 Of course, since it was my idea to begin with, I said yes." ... "Why are you bringing this up, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]?" The underlying note of contentiousness in your daughter's voice is unmistakable; she clearly expects to have to challenge you on this. "Is there a problem?" |Kinu closes her eyes and gives you a small nod. "That is correct, Nakano and I are engaged; it was one of the first things that happened after Mother and I got settled in at our new accommodations. Given that he and I were getting along excellently to begin with, Mother thought it a good idea for such a relationship to be formalized before tongues started wagging of their own accord. Matron Komari begged to differ, but Mother spoke to her and she has agreed to go forward with the matter and take developments in stride. "Once the relevant parties had all settled things, it was not too long after that he proposed to me in the — ah, proper fashion. "Does this turn of events displease you?" ] No, you're not going to stand in her way; it's clear that her mind is set on this course of action and nothing you say at this point is going to dissuade her. It's just — well, everything's been moving so quickly, and you really do wish that she'd told you that it was going to happen to begin with. [kinu.isInari |"Oh." You see Kinu relax and the hostility fades somewhat, although it's clear that your daughter is still on edge. "I don't know about how things are done in this part of the world, really, but as far as I understand it this is perfectly normal for how we do things, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I know I'm Mom's heir and all, so I've always been raised with the expectation of marrying young, yeah? I guess I didn't consider that it might be a surprise to you, since you wouldn't have any way of knowing. Sorry about that. "And as for not telling you... well, I don't know why, I thought you'd end up as much against it as Mother was. She didn't like the idea and I guess I can see why she would think that way, but it's not something that I would've agreed with. Still, if Granny Komari hadn't come and thrown her weight behind me it wouldn't have gone through nevertheless; I owe her one for that." Kiyoko was against it, huh. "Okay, so maybe she was kinda right, but I'm not really trying to get married so I can escape this house, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I'm not that desperate to be rid of Mother that I'd throw myself into a bad marriage, thanks a lot. Hitoshi's not simple, he just doesn't talk a lot, and frankly neither do I, so we get on very well. He's a nice guy, he's stable, and frankly after my childhood I think I need a lot of that where it counts, thank you very much." |"Ah." You see Kinu relax somewhat, although it's clear that your daughter is still on edge in her own genteel, passive-aggressive fashion. "It... it is easy to forget that you do not come from our background, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], and that maybe things are done differently in this part of the world. As far as I am concerned, though, this is a perfect pace of things — not too quick, not too slow. Being my mother's heir... I have always expected that I would marry soon, if not immediately after I came of age; it is one of the expected duties of my station in exchange for the privileges that I have enjoyed in life. It was an oversight that I did not consider that you might find the pace of progression to be unsettling, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], and for this I offer my apologies. "As for not telling you directly... ah, I suppose there is no hiding it. Both you and Nakano have some degree of animosity, [pc.ra kitsune |even if he has had no choice but to accept who you are and your station. I had not hoped to wish to have this confrontation, even if it was inevitable, and hence kept on delaying the matter of informing you... this is, of course, a failing that is entirely on my part." Did she really think so little of you to imagine that you would get in her way if it came down to it? Uncomfortable silence. "Yes." ...Is she happy with the arrangements? "Despite Mother's laments that I should have read fewer romances when I was younger, I understand that my expectations from a marriage should be realistic, even if a girl like I once was can dream. This is bigger than the two of us, and expecting to be happy all the time is simply dooming myself to failure. Contentment is more reasonable. Nakano and I are getting along reasonably well; I think I may have even managed to inspire him to improve his poetry. This is something even his own kin have failed to do. Not just to feel things out and get Mother over her objections, but also to make sure the preparations are right and have things settle down in the world before we can really turn our minds to that kind of stuff." |"For longer than most. There is the political side of things, as spurious as it is given that Mother has abdicated her position, but I suppose it must be taken care of." ] ...Good, good. You've already missed so much of Kinu's childhood, you wouldn't want to be absent on her wedding day too, even if it were supposedly for a good reason. That's something that you wouldn't be able to live down. [kinu.isInari |"Aw, sheesh, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. "It's okay — you'll probably be done with this whole saving the world thing by the time things actually roll around to a head, so you don't have to worry about missing my wedding or anything, okay?" |"Such sentimentality coming from you, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... given that this is but a natural part of one's life, it is a little embarrassing to have you speak of it in such glowing terms." Kinu raises a hand to her face, but can't hide the color in her cheeks from showing. "Rest assured that the wedding will not be anytime soon; you will be likely to be done with the most pressing of your tasks before the date arrives, so you do not have to worry about being absent on the day." ] That's good to hear. You just... you're not entirely sure why you had such a strong reaction to all this when you found out. Maybe it's like she said, it's but a part of her growing up, but her not needing you any more the way she did when she was a child stings a little. You know it's selfish of you to want to keep her dependent just so you can feel better about it all and you shouldn't be thinking that way, but even so, it still stings. [kinu.isInari |"Well, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], think of it this way: if I don't need you any more, that just means that if I'm still with you, it's because I chose to be that way. In the future, though... you want to stay as involved in her life as you can, and as is comfortable for her. You know full well that you're gone more often than you'd like to be able to make up for all the time lost, and whatever happens, you still love Kinu as your daughter. That's important. Even if you're not in a position to make any meaningful difference in the outcomes of events pertaining to her, you still want to be informed of such when you come home to check in rather than have to hear about it from other people. [kinu.isInari |"I'll think about it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." She'll think about it? "I don't like making promises I don't know I will be able to keep." Kinu sighs. "Not because I don't want to tell you or anything, but circumstances may not... how about if I can tell you, I'll tell you, and we leave it at that? If I can tell you, then I will, and rest assured that my utmost efforts shall be focused upon letting you know. That is as much as I can give." ] Ah... well, it'll have to do. [kinu.isInari |"I think that settles that, then," Kinu says, smacking you on the back with one of her tails. "Like I said, despite how quickly the engagement came about, there'll be plenty of time before the wedding actually takes place. You will not have to worry about missing it in the least, [pc.mf|Father|Mother] — [silly |you have the writer's guarantee that it is not going to take place in the course of this game, so let your mind be at peace |surely your duties and other matters will be in order before then ]. Not merely the thought of not being by her side, but also never being able to live up to the expectations she has set by her example no matter how hard I work." ... |"Mother isn't perfect," Kinu says. Now that's a little surprising, coming from her mouth. With how much your fox-daughter respects Kiyoko, for her to acknowledge her mother's failings is... "...Unprecedented, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]? I would imagine not. What is it the natives say about bravery? That it is not the absence of fear, but acting in spite of it? Is it better to be exemplary by without effort, or despite one's imperfections? It's a hard question to answer, especially when the results are so similar... nevertheless, acknowledging a simple truth about someone should not be hard, especially in private." Kiyoko... has had her moments of weakness. You've seen some of them. Kinu nods. "If I have learned something growing up by her side, it is that children catch onto more than you expect them to. What comes so naturally to me has been a struggle for her, and paradoxically enough, I feel the lesser for it." ] |[rand |"Perhaps when this is all over, I will arrange for Mother and I to visit her homeland together. You can come along if you'd wish too, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], for all the stares you'd get. It's just a step through the torii gate, after all. Going with Nakano is one thing, but he is often preoccupied with business and we can never stay more than a day or two. Besides, I want to visit her ancestral lands and fiefdoms, and I think only she can do that true justice." Going back... it might be hard for Kiyoko, even if it's only for a social visit. There is much in her past that is likely to catch up with her if she were to return across the ocean, not all of it good. "...I know, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I am hoping to... work something out. But even if I am to serve in my position here in the colonies, I cannot quite remain unmoored from my roots forever, can I? Sometimes Mother makes decisions that I cannot quite comprehend, because I do not draw from the same experiences that she does... I... I am hoping that being able to go on a pilgrimage of sorts with her will at least give me a framework of her past from which I can better understand the decisions she makes, even if I may not agree with them all the time." |"Raising children is so much hard work," Kinu says after a moment's thought. "Now that I have some experience with it in managing my brothers and sisters, especially when she is away, I have ever more respect for Mother and the things she put up with when I was but a kit. Perhaps she should have been harsher on me — with how my younger siblings can torment me sometimes when she is away, I can say that I got off quite lightly with minimal discipline." Perhaps she did not want to discipline her daughter too much, to display the trust she had in her heir that she would eventually sort matters out for herself." "I suppose that is one way of looking at it." Your fox-daughter raises a finger to her lips and frowns. "I myself could not see myself being that trusting, but I am not as wise as she is. Raising children is a scary task at times, knowing you are responsible for the futures of others by setting down the correct foundation... but we cannot allow fear of what might happen paralyze us from action, can we? Which is why Mother is so brave for having had so many of us, taking so many risks and working hard to ensure we all turn out just fine. Someday, I want to do this as well." |"I always keep a little stash of amazake hidden away where even Mother can't find it. That way, when she's feeling upset or tired, I can present her with a cupful," Kinu declares, more than a little smug. "Seeing her face and refusing to answer her demands as to where I would have laid hands on such a thing... ah, it is such a terrible sin to tease your own mother, but I am sure his divine lordship will forgive me for the amusement value it must give him." It's best not to lead on her mother too much. Before she knows it, Kiyoko will be insisting she produce inarizushi on demand. "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. If that was within my power, I would gladly do it." |"Mother is capable of making herself look so excellent with a minimum of fuss, and it's all thanks to excellent daily care. She doesn't need to use much more than her own scented herb oil for her fur and a bit of foundation to smooth out her skin, but the effect is positively striking and sublime at the same time. It's better to take care of yourself every day than try and fix everything when the need arises; this attitude can be applied to all things." Well, to be fair, her mother is also quite naturally gifted in that department. "Sometimes, less is more, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Matron Komari tells me that across the ocean in the Old Country, there are kitsune and even some tanuki who paint their faces, apply all kinds of makeup, and even do their hair in a very stylised manner. I haven't actually seen any of them since Nakano never handles court business when we are together there, but it certainly sounds a little intimidating. That is probably not the desired effect. Mother's way is far more effective and direct, I would imagine." |"[pc.mf|Father|Mother], I have a question." What is it? "Has Mother ever told you anything of her family? I never really had any reason to consider it, but it struck me recently that Mother has never really spoken very much about my grandparents, or my aunts and uncles. I tried asking Matron Komari about it, since she was there with Mother when they were girls, but she told me that I was seeking answers that were not hers to give." And Komari's correct. Now, you don't know much of Kiyoko's side of the family yourself save that she once had a sister, but has she tried actually asking her mother directly? "Mother must have a reason for her silence, so asking her directly is unlikely to yield results and will probably be counterproductive, if anything." Does she not trust her mother enough to allow her to keep her secrets like that? Kinu looks conflicted for several moments, then shakes her head. "Mother is conflicted, and at some level hurting. As her daughter, I can perceive as much... and I do not wish for it to continue. My best guess is that she is trying to shield me and my siblings with her silence... but I am no longer a child, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. If only I, with all my ability, could find a way to convince her of that..." ] |[rand |"Mother is so happy whenever she's with child," Kinu muses thoughtfully. "Seeing her like that... it makes me ashamed to be a little jealous of her even as she waddles around with a big belly. It will make me a little sad to be married off and live away from Mother, but at the same time seeing her like that has inspired me to want to live a life like she does. There are few things in this world that are worth putting your time into, and other people is one of them. Doing what she does is only, I suppose, a natural and logical extension of her duties, and mine in the future, too." You won't deny that it's going to be a little hard to see Kinu grown-up and being a mother herself. From the way you viewed time, it really wasn't all that long ago when she was up to your waist and running around the hilltop barefoot. "I still prefer to wear no shoes, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." She knows what you mean. "I was merely teasing you. But even so... we cannot stay the people we once were forever. I think... I am a better person now than I was before, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], and it is in no small part by following Mother's example. And seeing her so happy and pleased with herself as she is... it makes me want to have many, many kits myself, and raise them just as she raised me. I want my heir to have the same kind of relationship I have with Mother right now." |"Hmm..." Is something troubling your dearest daughter, now? "Oh, I was just thinking, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I could not help but notice that Mother's figure has filled out quite respectably after having had so many children. To make an understatement, she looks quite fetching by any standards." It has been a small side effect of being pregnant all the time, and one that you know Kiyoko particularly enjoys, as do you. If neither of you enjoyed it, you wouldn't do it as much as the two of you do, right? A small, mischievous smile crosses Kinu's lips. "That is true, that is true. But look at me as I am right now, aha. If Mother's body has changed so drastically from being practically rail-thin as I remember her being when I was young, I can only eagerly await what will happen to mine in the future. Certainly, this is one area in which I have already surpassed Mother even before I have begun, much to my shame... I wonder if I will ever be able to rival Mikoto's exuberance in time, ahaha." |You've noticed that Kinu speaks very formally and yet warmly, perhaps even more than her mother. Is this another habit she picked up from Kiyoko? "I would call it less a habit than a carefully learned skill, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. When I was younger, Mother insisted that I treat not just my elders, but everyone with the respect they deserved, even if their station was beneath mine. Such, she was careful to impress upon me, was one of the hallmarks of an elegant, refined lady like her. "At the same time, formal speech needs not be cold and distant — there are some who say it is important to be detached, prim and proper, but I disagree. Respectful and humble speech can be warm and set others at ease without being overly familiar; it is merely a skill that one needs to cultivate carefully like any other. Mother's insistence on my good behavior when I was a child gave me the opportunity to train and practice this skill until I perfected it. I certainly would have more trouble getting people to open up to me had I not put the time into trying to communicate with them better, and minding my speech was but the first step on that path." It must have been hard for a young kit like her to understand the importance of cultivating one's etiquette since young. "Which is why in the end, it was fortunate that I felt I could trust Mother enough to simply let her make decisions that were good for me, even if I did not understand all the whys and wherefores. Not that I did not endeavor to understand the reasoning behind her decisions regarding my education, but where I did not it was very much a relief to know that she always had my best interests in mind as her daughter and heir." |"Hm. [pc.mf|Father|Mother]..." Yes? "What made you decide to help Mother to begin with? What made you want to reach out to her? From what I've heard of what happened, you had every reason to distrust her, and yet things happened as they did. Why?" That's a complicated question to ask, and a complicated one to answer. It certainly wasn't just one reason that led you to take that leap of faith and help Kiyoko at her word... but it all turned out well, didn't it? Kinu turns her gaze downward. "I..." That wasn't a real answer that you just gave her, yes. But what makes Kiyoko special, for you to have stuck with her all this time, can't really be put into words. "So you feel it too, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Maybe it's better that way, that while one can't describe it, one knows it when one sees it. |"I'm very glad Mother approves of my choice in Nakano; I can't imagine what I would have done had she objected. Of course, I was sure there was no reason for her to, but at the same time... while I would like to say that there are not many things that truly scare me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], this would be one of them. Having to choose between Nakano and Mother is not a decision I would have liked to make in the slightest. "I'm just glad all of that is over and I was just being foolish worrying about it all the while. If my sensibilities are so close to Mother's, would I ever choose to be with anyone whom she found objectionable?" ] ] ]
