|我记得在我小时候，妈妈并不总是这样的。纪久叹了口气说道。她笑得越来越多了……甚至还会时不时地对我微笑。我真的不明白发生了什么，也不清楚这一切究竟是从什么时候开始改变的……但现在的她和过去的她，简直就像白天和黑夜一样截然不同。有时候……我真的很想回到从前，回到那个我还把她当作一个普通女孩来认识的那个时候。 嗯，基代子在离开星界之后发生变化，这种可能性并非不存在。不过，她自己有没有想过，也许她自己也同样发生了变化呢？ 桐对此皱起了眉头，撅起了嘴。有那么一刻，你会怀疑她是不是在故意固执己见，但很快你就意识到，你的这位狐狸女儿确实不明白你在说什么。她或许是个聪明人，但这只意味着她能够想出各种理由来为自己那些坚决要忽略的事情找借口罢了。 什么， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]？ 我不明白你的意思——我一直都是这样的，怎么可能不是我自己呢？挖泥巴或者去采集野蜂蜜，这些和我小时候做的事情有什么不同吗？ …… |妈妈就是太固执了，总是坚持自己的方式。小娟抱怨道。 我实在想不通，自己过去为什么会那么崇拜她。 现在发生了什么？ 嗯，我们正在讨论现在水路和管道系统已经基本安装完毕，该如何继续修复洞穴的其余部分。她想修缮几栋旧房子，这样在第二天返回之前，小毬奶奶的手工人们就可以在这些房子里过夜，这样他们的工作就不会那么紧张了。而我则希望能够获得周围更多的土地，这样他们才能更顺利地开展工作。这件事最终演变成了一场争吵，而这一切都是因为她丝毫不肯让步！" 如果她期望自己的母亲能够让步，那么或许她也应该主动提出做出一些让步，这样她们俩才能达成妥协吧？ 有什么可以妥协的呢？ [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]其实我们现在并不真的需要额外的生活空间，而且那些人晚上可能更想回家陪家人，而不是留下来过夜。我明白这一点。我如果我是他们，我会这么做。清理周围的区域，让人们能够更高效地完成工作，而不用担心会被坑洞、杂物之类的东西妨碍——这才是真正重要的！你看，如果这样做确实有意义的话，我当然会同意，但显然并没有意义吧？那么，为什么仅仅为了妥协而妥协呢？ …… |在我整个童年时期，母亲从未提起过这件事。但实际上，她似乎是远在大洋彼岸的某个显赫爵位的继承人。直到我第一次去科马里奶奶家时，有人注意到了我的毛色，这件事才被曝光出来。当时闹得沸沸扬扬，我一直不明白发生了什么，直到科马里奶奶亲自来向我解释…… 作为母亲的继承人，这是否意味着我成了某种公主呢？其实我从来都不觉得自己有什么像公主一样的感觉…… 嗯，她永远都会是你的公主。 哎呀， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]……别再这样了。别讨好我了好吗？这样做并不会让任何事情变得更好。纪久向你露出了一个微笑。我的意思是……她怎么能够这么长时间以来，对我隐瞒关于我们两个人这么重要的事情呢？当然，这对我来说可能没什么意义，对她来说也可能如此，但我们的关系对很多其他人来说却非常重要，而这种影响最终也会反过来波及到我们自己身上。 你肯定，清子不告诉小娟关于自己与生俱来的权利，一定是有什么原因的。 不过小娟似乎并不太相信这个解释，她拿起自己的一条尾巴，轻轻抚摸着那洁白中带着一丝银色的毛皮。我想，也许是吧。我能想到几个原因，这些原因或许可以解释为什么母亲会做出这样的举动。但我忍不住会想……如果她有什么这么重要的事情瞒着我，那么她还隐瞒了什么其他的事情呢？ |"[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]你难道认为我在浪费自己的教育吗？ 什么？是什么引发了这个问题？ 我觉得……我觉得自己作为一名学者，学到了很多东西，但这些知识其实都永远不会被我应用到实践中去。礼仪规范、书法艺术、微积分、绘画技巧……我记得茶道仪式的每一个细节，而且我相信无论我变老多少，这些知识都不会被我遗忘；母亲将这些知识深深地刻在了我的脑海里，它们永远都不会消失，尽管在日常生活中，这些知识几乎没有什么用处。我……其实我原本是在为另一种人生做准备，而不是为了我现在过的生活。因此，我今天所做的很多事情，都是我自己学习摸索出来的，或者向别人寻求帮助才学会的。并不是母亲……我始终无法摆脱这种感觉……觉得我的教育白白浪费了，其实应该有其他人能从中受益。要是我不像你那样学习能力这么强，那我早就惹上很多麻烦了。所以，谢谢你把你的这种能力传给了我，嘿嘿。 对于这种事情，你真的不知道该说些什么。 我的意思是， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]，不是这样的完全地我想，完全是失败吧。小娟露出一个淡淡的微笑，支支吾吾地说话，显然在努力想出合适的话语。显然，在使用委婉语这方面，她并不是一个很在行的人。我原本应该学习如何塑造花卉、微型樱花以及用于造型的藤蔓，而不是大根萝卜、果树或谷物。我所学的很多知识都是靠自学获得的，我仍然记得，当我选择学习尺八而不是古筝时，母亲是多么失望…… …… |我的意思是，我并不喜欢就目前的情况来看，你的狐妖女儿悲伤地叹息道。我真希望能回到小时候拥有那样一位母亲的时光。但那些日子已经一去不复返了，我必须学会忍受这一切，直到最终能够结婚，拥有属于自己的生活。 那么，她认为什么方法可能会有帮助呢？她有没有试着联系她的母亲呢？ 小娟撅起了嘴。凯罗斯的尾巴啊，我试过一次又一次，可妈妈真的是这个世界上最固执的人了！她为什么就不能偶尔改改自己的想法，看看我是怎么看的呢？！在我还是个小孩子的时候，妈妈从来不会这么爱争论，也不会这么急躁……是什么让她变成了现在这个样子？我真的不明白！我……我现在已经成年了， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]倒也不是说我打算急着做些什么，但是……我确实很期待能找到一个好的伴侣，然后离开这个地方。 ] |[rand |我明白为什么母亲一点也不赞成我正在做的事情。小娟这样对你说，一边挠着其中一只耳朵。自从小暮奶奶向我解释说，从血统上来说我属于高等贵族，甚至拥有神灵的血脉之后，母亲在我小时候试图教给我的很多事情，都变得容易理解了。公主们是不会穿上工作服去田里铺覆盖物的，她们只会精心培育最美丽的花朵，用来制作花束。 这是不是意味着她现在开始理解她母亲的立场了？ 你说的‘开始’是什么意思？ [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]说实话，我甚至不确定自己是否真的算是公主——只不过名义上是而已。而母亲所有的头衔和自称，其实也是如此。两百年后、在半个世界之外的地方，她应该也不会试图去强行证明这些吧？在我们看来，我们和普通人并没有什么区别，这就是事实。更何况，诚实而有益的工作有什么可羞愧的呢？我为什么要为自己所做的事情感到羞愧呢？尤其是在这些殖民地，这里还有很多人连下一顿饭从哪里来都不知道啊。如果有人应该感到羞愧，那就是那些看不起那些通过辛勤劳动为自己带来食物的人！我以凯罗斯的尾巴起誓，母亲绝对不应该这样…… 好吧，好吧。尽管小娟非常强壮，但她也需要先喘口气、冷静下来，否则会因为缺氧而昏过去。 我只是希望她能接受我们目前的处境。也许，她不该再固执地坚持事情应该是什么样，而该先弄清楚现实究竟如何。" |小熊妈妈和奶奶关系非常亲密。小娟会告诉你的。据我了解，他们应该是主从关系……但从他们之间的相处方式来看，他们的关系显然超出了这种主从关系。或许，这种关系太过亲密了——毕竟，这样的社会阶层差异本应该保持一定的尊重距离才对。 不过，幸好小栗奶奶喜欢我。作为她的女儿和继承人，妈妈根本不会听我的话，但她肯定会听她身边那些人的……虽然这种做法有点本末倒置，但至少我还有希望让小栗奶奶为我说句话。 她真的认为这能改变什么吗？ 小娟耸了耸肩。我不知道，但总比让事情保持原样要好。我不能让对失败的恐惧或担心会让情况变得更糟，这些恐惧成为我前进或采取行动的障碍。你也是这么认为的，对吧？ [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]？" |前不久，我从奶奶那里得到了一些豆腐皮，于是我就把它们炸了，然后用它们做了寿司。当我把做好的寿司端给大家吃的时候，母亲首先问我的就是，我到底想从她那里得到什么。 我只是……你那位狐妖女儿的耳朵会耷下来，同时她还会把食指并拢在一起。……事情怎么会发展到这样的地步：每当我为她做她最喜欢的饭菜时，她想到的第一件事居然是我在试图收买她？ 那么，当清子为她煮kenchin汤时，她会不会也会本能地产生同样的想法呢？ 我……小娟开始用食指敲击在一起。就像我之前说的， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]事情怎么会发展到这种地步呢？ 说实话，你并不清楚。尽管在她成长的过程中，你尽了最大努力去参与她的生活，但由于星界中时间的特殊性以及你探望她的次数稀少，你永远无法亲身体验整个过程。虽然你能够从外部为她提供一些帮助和启示，但这些终究是她需要与母亲共同去面对和解决的问题。 哎呀，这可真是帮了大忙了。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]真的帮了大忙。 |你打算很快再带妈妈出去吗？ [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]？" Kiyoko has been through a lot, and you only know the fraction of it that happened after you came into the picture. "That quiet, uncomplaining, unfaltering strength is the pinnacle of kitsune womanhood, an ideal many aspire to but few realize," your fox-daughter says with a wistful sigh. "Mother truly is something." |"Mother never said anything about it in all the years I studied at her knee, but she was originally heir to the position of den mother of the Otomo clan back across the ocean. While I understood that I was receiving an education that would prepare me for a role, I always thought that it would be to succeed Mother as being... herself, for lack of a better way to put it. Certainly, the idea did not cross my mind until someone at the Kurokawa den noticed my white fur when I visited on my own for the first time. A bit of an outcry ensued, and I was rather confused and distraught until Matron Komari came and explained it to me. "Since I am Mother's heir, I suppose that makes me a princess after a manner, but I have never known any other life. I all seems very unreal to me, to have the title and little else, if even that." Well, she'll always be your princess. "Oh, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... but on a more serious note, I have trouble seeing myself as one. With the way Mother raised me, I am not sure how much this heritage will ever matter." As if to prove her point, Kinu picks up one of her sleek, silvery-white tails in her hands and starts caressing the fur, running her fingers through it and watching them part perfectly. "But remembering that day... those looks of hope that I received when I stepped into their midst... maybe this was what Mother was grooming me to be, knowingly or not. If the colonies need a princess, then I will be that princess for them. I... I am the one with a strongest claim to the position, so it would seem." Does she know why Kiyoko kept her birthright from her? Kinu continues stroking away, a distant look in her eyes. "Perhaps she did not want me to get my hopes up, to create expectations that would never come to pass. Perhaps she did not want me to grow haughty before my time. I am not entirely sure, but I have the utmost faith in Mother and her motives. She means well, after all." |"I often ask Mother for her opinion on matters where I'm unsure on how to proceed, or where I think her insight could be valuable. I think it helps." How so? "Mother has lived a long time, and has accumulated much wisdom in her time. I would be remiss if I did not at least ask for her opinion and insight on important matters, yes? If we all had to build from the ground up each generation, civilization itself would not have gotten very far. Ever since leaving our old home, I have been reminded time and time again that while I may have inherited your amazing perception of the world about us, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], using it wisely is another matter altogether. Being able to rely on Mother as a guide and draw on her experiences without going through the trouble myself is an invaluable asset." |"Sometimes when Mother is less occupied with matters of state, I will request to be allowed to do some simple chores with her. Although we do not speak much in the exchange, I think there is still much to be gained from seemingly mundane activity together. It reminds me of when I was young." Oh, that's adorable. "Mother is excellent in everything she does, even folding clothes or wiping the floor. To be able to achieve such perfection and poise in all my dealings is something I wish to be able to do someday, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Simply spending time with her is but the first of many small steps towards that final goal." |"I am most grateful to Mother for the education ] |[rand |"Whenever Mother and I have a disagreement on how to deal with my siblings, I usually defer to her," Kinu begins. "It's important for my brothers and sisters to face a united front when dealing with authority figures so that they can't play their elder sister against their mother. If there are disagreements to be had, I take them up with her in private, and explain my thoughts when the matter isn't being publicly handled. It saves her face that way." She has disagreements with her mother? Haha... while you can recall several such incidents when she was younger, it's hard to imagine Kinu as she is ever strongly disagreeing with anything Kiyoko has to say. She truly is a chip off the old block here, as the local saying goes. "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... it is not just Mother. 'Praise publicly, chastise and criticise privately' is a maxim I try to hold to as much as possible. No one enjoys being publicly humiliated, and few situations truly warrant it, so where possible I try to err on the side of caution and save my disagreement and dissension for situations where it would be less charged to discuss such. It is only polite and respectful, especially to those who expect such from me." |"Mother and Matron Komari have such a unique relationship that is so much more than liege and retainer. It is true that their situation is equally unique... but the way Mother is able to inspire such immense dedication from her and hers is amazing. "It's true that some of the deference according to her by others is because of her rank. It's also true that a lot of Matron Komari's actions is driven by her own guilt and shame. But when you tease apart those layers and peel them away, I can still see that there's something there about Mother that draws people to her, and I want to discover what it is." Her mother drawing people to her, huh... well, she certainly drew you to her when you met. And as to the result of that magnetism... well, your little darling floofer's standing right here. You've been hearing about what she's been doing out and about through the foxy grapevine, and by all estimates whatever it is that Kiyoko possesses, your daughter's inherited it, too. She just has to find that spark or whatever it is, and kindle it by intentionally and purposefully doing what her mother does by instinct. Surely that'll yield plenty of fruit, perhaps even enough to surpass her mother. Kinu looks uncomfortable at the thought, a small frown crossing her features. "Surpass Mother? Well, I suppose she would want me to, but... even the thought feels vain and reprehensible. Not that I do not understand your meaning and I suppose it is her hope for me, but at the same time... perhaps we should discuss something else?" |"Even when I leave the den someday, I would like to still be with Mother and you. It is not as if I will be likely to be going off very far, anyway — while I cannot be completely certain about the future, remaining here in the colonies where I am needed is the most likely course. Perhaps I should rephrase my words, then — I would like to still be close to Mother and you even when I have flown the nest." That's flattering and quite heartening to hear. Some days, you had wondered if she resented you because you couldn't be around as much as you'd have liked to when she was growing up. "The nature of our relationship may change, but I do not see why we cannot still be close as a family. There is no reason to throw away people with whom you have good relationships with just because there are now others who share the same status in your eyes. It is not our way — well, my way at least." |"When I was younger, I did not think very much of Mother. She was just... there, perhaps as a part of the background, someone who told me what to do and reprimanded me for tracking dirt into the house. I assumed... I assumed that she would be there forever, just as I assumed that I would remain a child forever, and the days stretching out into the distant future would continue without end just like the forest beyond the hilltop. The whole nature of the situation did not come into view until I could speak with others about what had happened and what she had gone through that I could fully appreciate her for who she was. While I had part of the picture and a not insubstantial one at that, there was so much more to reveal. "I... and now here we are as we stand today... the thought of leaving her and standing in my own shoes as the mother of my own den scares me a little. No, it scares me a lot. Mother has done so much, seen so much, endured so much, I can scarcely hope to ever truly surpass her like she wants me to do, for all the gifts that I have received from both you and her, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Not merely the thought of not being by her side, but also never being able to live up to the expectations she has set by her example no matter how hard I work." ... |"Mother isn't perfect," Kinu says. Now that's a little surprising, coming from her mouth. With how much your fox-daughter respects Kiyoko, for her to acknowledge her mother's failings is... "...Unprecedented, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]? I would imagine not. What is it the natives say about bravery? That it is not the absence of fear, but acting in spite of it? Is it better to be exemplary by without effort, or despite one's imperfections? It's a hard question to answer, especially when the results are so similar... nevertheless, acknowledging a simple truth about someone should not be hard, especially in private." Kiyoko... has had her moments of weakness. You've seen some of them. Kinu nods. "If I have learned something growing up by her side, it is that children catch onto more than you expect them to. What comes so naturally to me has been a struggle for her, and paradoxically enough, I feel the lesser for it." ] |[rand |"Perhaps when this is all over, I will arrange for Mother and I to visit her homeland together. You can come along if you'd wish too, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], for all the stares you'd get. It's just a step through the torii gate, after all. Going with Nakano is one thing, but he is often preoccupied with business and we can never stay more than a day or two. Besides, I want to visit her ancestral lands and fiefdoms, and I think only she can do that true justice." Going back... it might be hard for Kiyoko, even if it's only for a social visit. There is much in her past that is likely to catch up with her if she were to return across the ocean, not all of it good. "...I know, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I am hoping to... work something out. But even if I am to serve in my position here in the colonies, I cannot quite remain unmoored from my roots forever, can I? Sometimes Mother makes decisions that I cannot quite comprehend, because I do not draw from the same experiences that she does... I... I am hoping that being able to go on a pilgrimage of sorts with her will at least give me a framework of her past from which I can better understand the decisions she makes, even if I may not agree with them all the time." |"Raising children is so much hard work," Kinu says after a moment's thought. "Now that I have some experience with it in managing my brothers and sisters, especially when she is away, I have ever more respect for Mother and the things she put up with when I was but a kit. Perhaps she should have been harsher on me — with how my younger siblings can torment me sometimes when she is away, I can say that I got off quite lightly with minimal discipline." Perhaps she did not want to discipline her daughter too much, to display the trust she had in her heir that she would eventually sort matters out for herself." "I suppose that is one way of looking at it." Your fox-daughter raises a finger to her lips and frowns. "I myself could not see myself being that trusting, but I am not as wise as she is. Raising children is a scary task at times, knowing you are responsible for the futures of others by setting down the correct foundation... but we cannot allow fear of what might happen paralyze us from action, can we? Which is why Mother is so brave for having had so many of us, taking so many risks and working hard to ensure we all turn out just fine. Someday, I want to do this as well." |"I always keep a little stash of amazake hidden away where even Mother can't find it. That way, when she's feeling upset or tired, I can present her with a cupful," Kinu declares, more than a little smug. "Seeing her face and refusing to answer her demands as to where I would have laid hands on such a thing... ah, it is such a terrible sin to tease your own mother, but I am sure his divine lordship will forgive me for the amusement value it must give him." It's best not to lead on her mother too much. Before she knows it, Kiyoko will be insisting she produce inarizushi on demand. "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. If that was within my power, I would gladly do it." |"Mother is capable of making herself look so excellent with a minimum of fuss, and it's all thanks to excellent daily care. She doesn't need to use much more than her own scented herb oil for her fur and a bit of foundation to smooth out her skin, but the effect is positively striking and sublime at the same time. It's better to take care of yourself every day than try and fix everything when the need arises; this attitude can be applied to all things." Well, to be fair, her mother is also quite naturally gifted in that department. "Sometimes, less is more, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Matron Komari tells me that across the ocean in the Old Country, there are kitsune and even some tanuki who paint their faces, apply all kinds of makeup, and even do their hair in a very stylised manner. I haven't actually seen any of them since Nakano never handles court business when we are together there, but it certainly sounds a little intimidating. That is probably not the desired effect. Mother's way is far more effective and direct, I would imagine." |"[pc.mf|Father|Mother], I have a question." What is it? "Has Mother ever told you anything of her family? I never really had any reason to consider it, but it struck me recently that Mother has never really spoken very much about my grandparents, or my aunts and uncles. I tried asking Matron Komari about it, since she was there with Mother when they were girls, but she told me that I was seeking answers that were not hers to give." And Komari's correct. Now, you don't know much of Kiyoko's side of the family yourself save that she once had a sister, but has she tried actually asking her mother directly? "Mother must have a reason for her silence, so asking her directly is unlikely to yield results and will probably be counterproductive, if anything." Does she not trust her mother enough to allow her to keep her secrets like that? Kinu looks conflicted for several moments, then shakes her head. "Mother is conflicted, and at some level hurting. As her daughter, I can perceive as much... and I do not wish for it to continue. My best guess is that she is trying to shield me and my siblings with her silence... but I am no longer a child, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. If only I, with all my ability, could find a way to convince her of that..." ] |[rand |"Mother is so happy whenever she's with child," Kinu muses thoughtfully. "Seeing her like that... it makes me ashamed to be a little jealous of her even as she waddles around with a big belly. It will make me a little sad to be married off and live away from Mother, but at the same time seeing her like that has inspired me to want to live a life like she does. There are few things in this world that are worth putting your time into, and other people is one of them. Doing what she does is only, I suppose, a natural and logical extension of her duties, and mine in the future, too." You won't deny that it's going to be a little hard to see Kinu grown-up and being a mother herself. From the way you viewed time, it really wasn't all that long ago when she was up to your waist and running around the hilltop barefoot. "I still prefer to wear no shoes, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." She knows what you mean. "I was merely teasing you. But even so... we cannot stay the people we once were forever. I think... I am a better person now than I was before, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], and it is in no small part by following Mother's example. And seeing her so happy and pleased with herself as she is... it makes me want to have many, many kits myself, and raise them just as she raised me. I want my heir to have the same kind of relationship I have with Mother right now." |"Hmm..." Is something troubling your dearest daughter, now? "Oh, I was just thinking, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I could not help but notice that Mother's figure has filled out quite respectably after having had so many children. To make an understatement, she looks quite fetching by any standards." It has been a small side effect of being pregnant all the time, and one that you know Kiyoko particularly enjoys, as do you. If neither of you enjoyed it, you wouldn't do it as much as the two of you do, right? A small, mischievous smile crosses Kinu's lips. "That is true, that is true. But look at me as I am right now, aha. If Mother's body has changed so drastically from being practically rail-thin as I remember her being when I was young, I can only eagerly await what will happen to mine in the future. Certainly, this is one area in which I have already surpassed Mother even before I have begun, much to my shame... I wonder if I will ever be able to rival Mikoto's exuberance in time, ahaha." |You've noticed that Kinu speaks very formally and yet warmly, perhaps even more than her mother. Is this another habit she picked up from Kiyoko? "I would call it less a habit than a carefully learned skill, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. When I was younger, Mother insisted that I treat not just my elders, but everyone with the respect they deserved, even if their station was beneath mine. Such, she was careful to impress upon me, was one of the hallmarks of an elegant, refined lady like her. "At the same time, formal speech needs not be cold and distant — there are some who say it is important to be detached, prim and proper, but I disagree. Respectful and humble speech can be warm and set others at ease without being overly familiar; it is merely a skill that one needs to cultivate carefully like any other. Mother's insistence on my good behavior when I was a child gave me the opportunity to train and practice this skill until I perfected it. I certainly would have more trouble getting people to open up to me had I not put the time into trying to communicate with them better, and minding my speech was but the first step on that path." It must have been hard for a young kit like her to understand the importance of cultivating one's etiquette since young. "Which is why in the end, it was fortunate that I felt I could trust Mother enough to simply let her make decisions that were good for me, even if I did not understand all the whys and wherefores. Not that I did not endeavor to understand the reasoning behind her decisions regarding my education, but where I did not it was very much a relief to know that she always had my best interests in mind as her daughter and heir." |"Hm. [pc.mf|Father|Mother]..." Yes? "What made you decide to help Mother to begin with? What made you want to reach out to her? From what I've heard of what happened, you had every reason to distrust her, and yet things happened as they did. Why?" That's a complicated question to ask, and a complicated one to answer. It certainly wasn't just one reason that led you to take that leap of faith and help Kiyoko at her word... but it all turned out well, didn't it? Kinu turns her gaze downward. "I..." That wasn't a real answer that you just gave her, yes. But what makes Kiyoko special, for you to have stuck with her all this time, can't really be put into words. "So you feel it too, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Maybe it's better that way, that while one can't describe it, one knows it when one sees it. |"I'm very glad Mother approves of my choice in Nakano; I can't imagine what I would have done had she objected. Of course, I was sure there was no reason for her to, but at the same time... while I would like to say that there are not many things that truly scare me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], this would be one of them. Having to choose between Nakano and Mother is not a decision I would have liked to make in the slightest. "I'm just glad all of that is over and I was just being foolish worrying about it all the while. If my sensibilities are so close to Mother's, would I ever choose to be with anyone whom she found objectionable?" ] ] ] "

rows.original: Asking your daughter about her mother while Kiyoko's right here is unlikely to produce a genuine or non-diplomatic response. Perhaps you should try again later.
rows.translation: 当清子就在眼前时，问你的女儿关于她母亲的事情，很可能得不到真诚或坦率的回答。或许你应该稍后再试一次。
rows.raw: "Asking your daughter about her mother while Kiyoko's right here is unlikely to produce a genuine or non-diplomatic response. Perhaps you should try again later."

rows.original: [kinu.isInari |[kiyoko.numKits 2 8 16 32 |[rand |Your fox-daughter grins a little at the memory. "Hah... I remember when it was just me and Mother, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Just the two of us, and no one else. Haha... the look on her face when she told me I was going to have a little brother or sister pretty soon, and all the questions I asked her when her belly started to grow big and round. Then, of course, came the inevitable... "I remember not liking having to share Mother's attention at first, but that passed soon enough — or at least, I hope it was soon enough. Besides, for all the trouble a little kit can get into, not having your mother's attention on you all the time is a mixed blessing. Learning to share... that wasn't bad, either. Having siblings isn't all that bad, eh, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? "So... why don't the two of you get busy and make some more?" [party.has kiyoko | "Oh, my dear child," your fox-wife replies[kiyoko.pregStage 2|, patting her bulging baby bump] before nudging you. "We're working on that right now, aren't we, beloved?" ] |"It's my job as Big Sis to take care of everyone when Mother's away with you, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Well, it's also my duty to take care of them while she's here, so the job isn't too much different, haha. Have to make sure that everyone's clothed, fed, and the schedules set and stuck to before I can get to my own stuff for the day. This kind of stuff comes with its privileges... but it also comes with its responsibilities. Fair's fair, as they say. Can't complain." |"Miko really likes sweets, so she's pretty enthusiastic about giving them out to everyone she meets whenever she makes a bunch. I, on the other hand..." Ah, you can see the dilemma there. "Eh. That's where having little siblings comes in handy. I just take them back and foist the sweets off onto them, and they're more than happy to receive them in my stead. It's a win-win situation, as far as I'm concerned." Passing off foods you don't like onto your siblings is kind of petulant and childish, though. "Nothing can be done about it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. The amount of honey and other sweeteners Miko puts into her stuff... only the gods know why her teeth haven't all rotted yet. Just smelling them makes my head spin... I'd retch on the spot if I'd to eat them in front of her. I know, I know, I've said it often enough myself that you should eat what's in front of you, but this is something else altogether, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Give me a break." |"When Mother's gone, I'm in charge of setting and giving lessons for my younger siblings. Not that I disagree with her on the value of education and the basics thereof... but when I have my own children, I want them to... I don't know, but it's not going to be exactly what Mother taught me. I know that trying to define such a thing in what it's not is much less useful than defining it by what it is, but I still need to pull together my thoughts on this. "For now, though, since they're my brothers and sisters and not my kits, I'm sticking to the lesson plan she's set out; I'm not going to open up an easily abusable fracture point between the two of us by undermining her lessons needlessly. Whatever quarrels we may have, I do agree that we both want the best for my siblings and part of that is presenting a united front from their authority figures. This means you as well, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." |"To be quite honest, having siblings around really got me into applying myself on my studies back in the day. There's no better way to tell whether you fully and completely understand something than having to teach it to someone else; all the gaps in your understanding are inescapably laid out when you have to explain in your own words concepts that you thought you knew well." She could say that having brothers and sisters, and more importantly, being responsible for them, helps her own understanding and got her to push herself further than what she would ordinarily have done. "That's about the long and short of it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I might get annoyed at other people sometimes, but they're family, you know? It's worth expending a little more effort for them, especially since it's helping me, too." ] |[rand |"Prior to moving out to here, I always had Mother at my side, no matter how much responsibility I used to have. Now that I don't always have someone to fall back onto, it's making my job as big sister to these fluffballs all the more engaging knowing that I'm not going to get a second chance here if I mess up with them. I know I have to do things properly, and strangely enough, that knowledge and added drive is that bit of extra insurance towards making sure everything runs smoothly. "I'm personally just hoping that some of my brothers and sisters will see this independence for what it is and be inspired to take the initiative on more things instead of coming to me for assignments, or merely following the schedules. Just as I can't always have Mother watching over my shoulder, they can't always have me breathing down their necks. What you do when you think no one's watching is perhaps closest to the true you, as they say." |"Sometimes I wonder if Asagiri should have been born before I was. It'd have been better for everyone that way. She has white fur, too... that, and she plays the koto, paints, writes poetry, and is far more interested in estate management and petty politics than I am. That she's a pretty face and good at talking to people doesn't hurt, either; people who meet her for the first time like her already. "She... she's the daughter that Mother wanted and ought to have been her heir to begin with; she's a proper right princess who easily avoids offending everyone's sensibilities. Not me. I just... no, it can't be helped, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Wishing things were different isn't going to change anything..." |"Contrary to what a lot of my little siblings think, I don't assign duties arbitrarily," Kinu says with a small laugh. "Part of the art of delegation is noticing who's good at what and matching peoples' strengths to the tasks at hand. "Of course, some days I do just the opposite — we all have to do things we don't want to sometimes, and learning to take that in stride is part of growing up. That, and I want to see them work it out between themselves — whether to swap general duties on the sly, to tough it out, or something else. I won't say that I don't derive some small measure of satisfaction from watching them think for themselves and work out the details independently." |"Sometimes, I'm a bit sad when I think about it and realize that none of my brothers and sisters are as enthusiastic about working the land as I am. On one hand, I don't want anyone to follow in my footsteps just because it's what I do and they feel obligated to keep things running. On the other hand, part of me feels a little sad and disappointed that I don't have more people to guide in what I know best and to talk about new ideas with. Hitoshi is a nice guy, but he isn't always around to lend a ear. It's just kind of lonely sometimes." Has she tried to help any of her younger siblings discover an interest in agricultural science, as she calls it? "Haha, actually, that's what Kazuo calls it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. He makes it sound like a profession that's more mentally involved than scratching about in the dirt. But... I can see why it doesn't appeal to most; it's grueling work at times in all kinds of weather, you get muddy and wet, you smell of mulch and fertiliser, there are bugs and things, you get blisters because you damn well didn't wear any gloves... the list of childish complaints goes on, but you know what, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? It's hard, but at the same time it's beautifully fulfilling. Ah ha ha... "At this point, I'm just hoping that one of my own future kits will take after me strongly enough to want to work the land after me. It... it would make me happy." |"Aya has always had a mischievous streak ever since she was little. By some stroke of great and ironic misfortune, Mother named her for the opposite of how she actually behaves — if we as a family really are the descendants of the Trickster himself many times removed, I can believe it, seeing her go about it. Growing up hasn't really changed her tendency to get into all kinds of shenanigans, only the form they take, and frankly I preferred her particular brand of troublemaking when we were tiny. It was more direct, then." It sounds like she's quite exasperated by her sister's antics. "She's not dumb, and that's a lot coming from me," Kinu says with a small sigh. "I just wish she wouldn't waste so much of her energy on causing trouble that I have to go and fix. Trying to skirt the line between what's acceptable and not doesn't work on me in the slightest, but that doesn't stop her from doing it anyway." ] |[rand |"So a couple of the younger kits were tying paper wishes onto the bamboo grove by the entrance, and I couldn't help but go up and sneak a peek when they were gone. Guess what was the first one I read?" Nah, why doesn't she tell you? Kinu rolls her eyes and chances a thin smile. "It was ' I wish big sis wouldn't look so strict all the time.' I don't know about that, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Do I look strict to you?" Well, she and her mother do look quite alike when they're ticked off at the kits. "Ah ha ha ha. Seriously, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom] — it's important not to send mixed signals when you're reprimanding mischievous kits. I also have to be as strict as Mother would be, otherwise those little brats will try to play one of us off the other. So... yeah, now that I think about it, I guess I have to look so strict all the time. It's for their own good, after all." |"After all this time, Tatsumi still humors me when I ask him for a game of go or shogi, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. He's never managed to win even once ever since we were kits, but it's not from lack of trying. Whenever I ask him why he keeps at it despite the constant losses, he tells me he's learning a lot by playing with me." That's very astute of her younger brother. You can see where he's coming from. Kinu scratches her head. "Eh, I dunno, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. He doesn't seem to be learning anything — he always sticks to the same old plays and never changes his game. It's a big reason why I still keep on beating him every time." Maybe he's learning a lot, but not about the games themselves. Has she ever considered that? "Well, if you can see it where I can't, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], why don't you tell me what he's learning from playing with me, then?" Ah, she has to figure it out for herself. Telling her outright would deprive your darling daughter of an important lesson you'd like her to learn. "[pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I know what that really means is 'I just made up a bunch of stuff and don't want to have to explain it at all because it'd just expose the fact that I don't know half of what I'm saying.' That's not going to fool anyone, you know." But it is. She has to figure it out for herself. Perhaps she should start by observing her little brother closer just before and after the next game they lay together? Kinu rolls her eyes and makes an exasperated noise. |"In order to make everything work, delegation is important. Mother delegates to me, I delegate to Aya, Tatsumi and Asagiri, and they continue that down the line. It makes things run smoothly in a large family like ours." Well, her mother having to personally handle every jot and tittle herself would quickly drive her out of her mind. That, and it's good training for the future. "And that's why I don't want to be too specific with my instructions to those three, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. First, I don't want to them saying that so and so isn't their job or responsibility because Big Sis didn't tell me so — when it comes to everyone as a family, if one person fails, everyone fails. If it wasn't your job, then it jolly well is now. "Besides, I want those three to be able to think independently and not come to me all the time when the slightest problem comes up. That's Asagiri's biggest problem, really; she's reliant on other people to do her work for her too much and doesn't want to learn anything by herself. "At my mealtimes, you take what you're given, you work things out between yourselves, and if you want seconds you come over and speak up instead of sitting down there and crying for me to come over to serve you. And his divine lordship himself help any of the little ones if I see them wasting any food — a week or two of nothing but working in my fields usually disabuses them of any such notions quickly enough. "You never know when they're going to be watching, or what lessons they're going to take away from observing you, especially when you think you're on your own. That's another lesson I learned at your side, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Fox kits are naturals at playing adults, you know — if you're not prepared, they'll take the slightest bit of give you have in you and take it as far as they can. Being unbending is pretty much necessary to keep them in line — while my decisions can be harsh, perhaps even more so than Mother's, no one's going to call them unfair or undeserved when it gets down to it. I'm pretty proud of that." ] |[rand |"You know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I'm pretty happy to have such a large family around me, so kudos to you and Mother for producing one in the first place. You're just glad that she's managed to come to terms with most of her family, even if she's still at loggerheads with her mother. "Yeah. Mother... I guess we're too busy with the kits these days to have that much energy left over to yell at each other. [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], Mother says she was changing nappies and coddling babies when she was eight. "I don't need to deal with petty nonsense like someone getting one more apple than everyone else, or where the radishes should go, or what to do if someone skinned their knee. So, if there aren't enough guidelines and experience and the matter flows up to her, the situation just sets precedent for what does happen the next time it happens. "Just so." |"While delegation and trust get things done, I nevertheless do drop in unannounced from time to time just to see how things are going," your kitsune daughter informs you. [party.has kiyoko |"I'm just glad you're appreciative of what others have done for you, daughter," Kiyoko answers. "Pass along what I've given to you, and you won't go wrong." |It's good that she is mindful of her roots and gives credit where it's due. ] Kinu gives [party.has kiyoko|the both of ]you a little bow. "I... I am glad. Not that I am discounting the education that Mother has bestowed upon me, of course, but there is no amount of book learning that will the importance of, or what is involved in putting your time into other people. While it would be nice if the world were perfectly ordered and predictable, people are rarely if ever so, and mere simple responsibility has taught me much about dealing with the unforeseen and unpredictable. "So... yes. I am glad to have a family of this size about me, for all the trouble that everyone may have given me in the past. "I cannot speak for others, but Mother and I have found this a most satisfactory way of managing a large family like ours." ] ] ]

|想起这件事，你的狐狸女儿不禁微微一笑。哈……我还记得那时候只有我和妈妈在一起[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]就我们两个人，没有其他人。哈哈……当她告诉我我很快就会有一个弟弟或妹妹时，她脸上的表情，还有当她的肚子开始变得越来越大、越来越圆的时候，我问她的那些问题。然后，当然，那个不可避免的时刻也到来了…… Haha... the look on her face when she told me I was going to have a little brother or sister pretty soon, and all the questions I asked her when her belly started to grow big and round. Then, of course, came the inevitable... "I remember not liking having to share Mother's attention at first, but that passed soon enough — or at least, I hope it was soon enough. Besides, for all the trouble a little kit can get into, not having your mother's attention on you all the time is a mixed blessing. Learning to share... that wasn't bad, either. Having siblings isn't all that bad, eh, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? "So... why don't the two of you get busy and make some more?" [party.has kiyoko | "Oh, my dear child," your fox-wife replies[kiyoko.pregStage 2|, patting her bulging baby bump] before nudging you. "We're working on that right now, aren't we, beloved?" ] |"It's my job as Big Sis to take care of everyone when Mother's away with you, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Well, it's also my duty to take care of them while she's here, so the job isn't too much different, haha. Have to make sure that everyone's clothed, fed, and the schedules set and stuck to before I can get to my own stuff for the day. This kind of stuff comes with its privileges... but it also comes with its responsibilities. Fair's fair, as they say. Can't complain." |"Miko really likes sweets, so she's pretty enthusiastic about giving them out to everyone she meets whenever she makes a bunch. I, on the other hand..." Ah, you can see the dilemma there. "Eh. That's where having little siblings comes in handy. I just take them back and foist the sweets off onto them, and they're more than happy to receive them in my stead. It's a win-win situation, as far as I'm concerned." Passing off foods you don't like onto your siblings is kind of petulant and childish, though. "Nothing can be done about it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. The amount of honey and other sweeteners Miko puts into her stuff... only the gods know why her teeth haven't all rotted yet. Just smelling them makes my head spin... I'd retch on the spot if I'd to eat them in front of her. I know, I know, I've said it often enough myself that you should eat what's in front of you, but this is something else altogether, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Give me a break." |"When Mother's gone, I'm in charge of setting and giving lessons for my younger siblings. Not that I disagree with her on the value of education and the basics thereof... but when I have my own children, I want them to... I don't know, but it's not going to be exactly what Mother taught me. I know that trying to define such a thing in what it's not is much less useful than defining it by what it is, but I still need to pull together my thoughts on this. "For now, though, since they're my brothers and sisters and not my kits, I'm sticking to the lesson plan she's set out; I'm not going to open up an easily abusable fracture point between the two of us by undermining her lessons needlessly. Whatever quarrels we may have, I do agree that we both want the best for my siblings and part of that is presenting a united front from their authority figures. This means you as well, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." |"To be quite honest, having siblings around really got me into applying myself on my studies back in the day. There's no better way to tell whether you fully and completely understand something than having to teach it to someone else; all the gaps in your understanding are inescapably laid out when you have to explain in your own words concepts that you thought you knew well." She could say that having brothers and sisters, and more importantly, being responsible for them, helps her own understanding and got her to push herself further than what she would ordinarily have done. "That's about the long and short of it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I might get annoyed at other people sometimes, but they're family, you know? It's worth expending a little more effort for them, especially since it's helping me, too." ] |[rand |"Prior to moving out to here, I always had Mother at my side, no matter how much responsibility I used to have. Now that I don't always have someone to fall back onto, it's making my job as big sister to these fluffballs all the more engaging knowing that I'm not going to get a second chance here if I mess up with them. I know I have to do things properly, and strangely enough, that knowledge and added drive is that bit of extra insurance towards making sure everything runs smoothly. "I'm personally just hoping that some of my brothers and sisters will see this independence for what it is and be inspired to take the initiative on more things instead of coming to me for assignments, or merely following the schedules. Just as I can't always have Mother watching over my shoulder, they can't always have me breathing down their necks. What you do when you think no one's watching is perhaps closest to the true you, as they say." |"Sometimes I wonder if Asagiri should have been born before I was. It'd have been better for everyone that way. She has white fur, too... that, and she plays the koto, paints, writes poetry, and is far more interested in estate management and petty politics than I am. That she's a pretty face and good at talking to people doesn't hurt, either; people who meet her for the first time like her already. "She... she's the daughter that Mother wanted and ought to have been her heir to begin with; she's a proper right princess who easily avoids offending everyone's sensibilities. Not me. I just... no, it can't be helped, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Wishing things were different isn't going to change anything..." |"Contrary to what a lot of my little siblings think, I don't assign duties arbitrarily," Kinu says with a small laugh. "Part of the art of delegation is noticing who's good at what and matching peoples' strengths to the tasks at hand. "Of course, some days I do just the opposite — we all have to do things we don't want to sometimes, and learning to take that in stride is part of growing up. That, and I want to see them work it out between themselves — whether to swap general duties on the sly, to tough it out, or something else. I won't say that I don't derive some small measure of satisfaction from watching them think for themselves and work out the details independently." |"Sometimes, I'm a bit sad when I think about it and realize that none of my brothers and sisters are as enthusiastic about working the land as I am. On one hand, I don't want anyone to follow in my footsteps just because it's what I do and they feel obligated to keep things running. On the other hand, part of me feels a little sad and disappointed that I don't have more people to guide in what I know best and to talk about new ideas with. Hitoshi is a nice guy, but he isn't always around to lend a ear. It's just kind of lonely sometimes." Has she tried to help any of her younger siblings discover an interest in agricultural science, as she calls it? "Haha, actually, that's what Kazuo calls it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. He makes it sound like a profession that's more mentally involved than scratching about in the dirt. But... I can see why it doesn't appeal to most; it's grueling work at times in all kinds of weather, you get muddy and wet, you smell of mulch and fertiliser, there are bugs and things, you get blisters because you damn well didn't wear any gloves... the list of childish complaints goes on, but you know what, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? It's hard, but at the same time it's beautifully fulfilling. Ah ha ha... "At this point, I'm just hoping that one of my own future kits will take after me strongly enough to want to work the land after me. It... it would make me happy." |"Aya has always had a mischievous streak ever since she was little. By some stroke of great and ironic misfortune, Mother named her for the opposite of how she actually behaves — if we as a family really are the descendants of the Trickster himself many times removed, I can believe it, seeing her go about it. Growing up hasn't really changed her tendency to get into all kinds of shenanigans, only the form they take, and frankly I preferred her particular brand of troublemaking when we were tiny. It was more direct, then." It sounds like she's quite exasperated by her sister's antics. "She's not dumb, and that's a lot coming from me," Kinu says with a small sigh. "I just wish she wouldn't waste so much of her energy on causing trouble that I have to go and fix. Trying to skirt the line between what's acceptable and not doesn't work on me in the slightest, but that doesn't stop her from doing it anyway." ] |[rand |"So a couple of the younger kits were tying paper wishes onto the bamboo grove by the entrance, and I couldn't help but go up and sneak a peek when they were gone. Guess what was the first one I read?" Nah, why doesn't she tell you? Kinu rolls her eyes and chances a thin smile. "It was ' I wish big sis wouldn't look so strict all the time.' I don't know about that, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Do I look strict to you?" Well, she and her mother do look quite alike when they're ticked off at the kits. "Ah ha ha ha. Seriously, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom] — it's important not to send mixed signals when you're reprimanding mischievous kits. I also have to be as strict as Mother would be, otherwise those little brats will try to play one of us off the other. So... yeah, now that I think about it, I guess I have to look so strict all the time. It's for their own good, after all." |"After all this time, Tatsumi still humors me when I ask him for a game of go or shogi, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. He's never managed to win even once ever since we were kits, but it's not from lack of trying. Whenever I ask him why he keeps at it despite the constant losses, he tells me he's learning a lot by playing with me." That's very astute of her younger brother. You can see where he's coming from. Kinu scratches her head. "Eh, I dunno, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. He doesn't seem to be learning anything — he always sticks to the same old plays and never changes his game. It's a big reason why I still keep on beating him every time." Maybe he's learning a lot, but not about the games themselves. Has she ever considered that? "Well, if you can see it where I can't, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], why don't you tell me what he's learning from playing with me, then?" Ah, she has to figure it out for herself. Telling her outright would deprive your darling daughter of an important lesson you'd like her to learn. "[pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I know what that really means is 'I just made up a bunch of stuff and don't want to have to explain it at all because it'd just expose the fact that I don't know half of what I'm saying.' That's not going to fool anyone, you know." But it is. She has to figure it out for herself. Perhaps she should start by observing her little brother closer just before and after the next game they lay together? Kinu rolls her eyes and makes an exasperated noise. |"In order to make everything work, delegation is important. Mother delegates to me, I delegate to Aya, Tatsumi and Asagiri, and they continue that down the line. It makes things run smoothly in a large family like ours." Well, her mother having to personally handle every jot and tittle herself would quickly drive her out of her mind. That, and it's good training for the future. "And that's why I don't want to be too specific with my instructions to those three, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I give them a general direction in which things should go for the day or week, and leave them to sort out the details themselves. First, I don't want to them saying that so and so isn't their job or responsibility because Big Sis didn't tell me so — when it comes to everyone as a family, if one person fails, everyone fails. If it wasn't your job, then it jolly well is now. "Besides, I want those three to be able to think independently and not come to me all the time when the slightest problem comes up. That's Asagiri's biggest problem, really; she's reliant on other people to do her work for her too much and doesn't want to learn anything by herself. Why bother, when you have all these people at your fingertips who'll help you at the drop of a hat?" |"I remember mealtimes when I was younger, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Hectic and chaotic, especially when I was Mother's majordomo at the event. Now that I'm a grown woman, things... really haven't changed a lot, ha. When the time comes for me to be a mother myself, it won't be any different, will it? "You know something, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? No matter how carefully you dole out the portions, make sure each one is equal and everything's as close in size to each other, there'll always be someone who claims that so-and-so has more than they do, or their serving is smaller, or who tries to foist off food they don't like onto someone else... at some point in between all those years, I just gave up on the whining and crying and focused on making things equitable, not equal. "At my mealtimes, you take what you're given, you work things out between yourselves, and if you want seconds you come over and speak up instead of sitting down there and crying for me to come over to serve you. And his divine lordship himself help any of the little ones if I see them wasting any food — a week or two of nothing but working in my fields usually disabuses them of any such notions quickly enough. I may make it look easy, but coaxing the earth into giving up its fruits is hard work." |"I suppose I can be a little harsh when dealing with my siblings, but I'm always fair when it comes down to it. You taught me that, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." Did you? You, uh — "Kits notice more than you give them credit for, you know," Kinu says with an impish, enigmatic smile. "You never know when they're going to be watching, or what lessons they're going to take away from observing you, especially when you think you're on your own. That's another lesson I learned at your side, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Fox kits are naturals at playing adults, you know — if you're not prepared, they'll take the slightest bit of give you have in you and take it as far as they can. Being unbending is pretty much necessary to keep them in line — while my decisions can be harsh, perhaps even more so than Mother's, no one's going to call them unfair or undeserved when it gets down to it. I'm pretty proud of that." ] |[rand |"You know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I'm pretty happy to have such a large family around me, so kudos to you and Mother for producing one in the first place. While I can't say that it hasn't been without its downs, there've been more times I've smiled than I've frowned, so it's all good in the end." You're just glad that she's managed to come to terms with most of her family, even if she's still at loggerheads with her mother. "Yeah. Mother... I guess we're too busy with the kits these days to have that much energy left over to yell at each other. Not that we've changed in any way, I think, but there really just isn't the wherewithal for us to fight any more. The reasons may be suspect, but hey, it's the results that matter, right?" |"You know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], with all of my siblings calling me 'big sis' day in and day out, I already feel like a mother without actually being one. Which I guess is the point, isn't it? Training for the future? Heh..." Hey, if she's confident in handling her brothers and sisters, her own future children won't be that much more work. "Ah ha ha... [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], Mother says she was changing nappies and coddling babies when she was eight. I don't think I'm going to be inheriting any of Mother's oddities when my time comes; those came with her body being violently ripped away from her and his divine lordship choosing to preserve them out of curiosity and amusement, remember? Well, I suppose I've never been one to shy away from hard work and a challenge..." |For someone who's in charge of so many siblings, your daughter sure has a lot of free time on her hands. What's her secret? "Teaching them strong moral values so they don't get into trouble and need my intervention in the first place, and most importantly, giving them the tools with which to make good decisions and the independence to solve problems on their own," Kinu replies without a moment's hesitation. "I don't need to deal with petty nonsense like someone getting one more apple than everyone else, or where the radishes should go, or what to do if someone skinned their knee. I'd like to think that I've taught my brothers and sisters well enough that they have the wherewithal to be strong and make decisions for themselves without needing to come to me all the time. "And that suits me just fine, because I not only have enough time to work the fields, but also help out at Granny Komari's. Furthermore, when they do come to me with something that needs help, I can generally assume it's important without needing to go through the whole song and dance of asking." |"With so many hands around, fixing up what's left of this old den is going much smoother. Of course, there's still a lot to be done, given that this place is the size of a small village, so we're just reclaiming the buildings as we need to. Even the littlest kits make themselves useful by hauling materials around, haha. A little good solid physical labor is important for a child when growing up — it certainly was for me. "Most importantly, though, it means that we've almost weaned ourselves off the help that Granny Komari's been so kind to send our way since the first day. I'm not saying that it wasn't appreciated, nor am I saying that it wasn't needed, but at the same time once you get used to the idea of borrowing things from people all the time, you aren't really much more than a beggar. Other people have their worries and problems, too, and as much as they may be happy to share you're still taking their resources from them. It's shameful to be unable to self-sufficient at some kind of baseline, and that's why I'm quite glad I've enough brothers and sisters to whip into a workforce now." |"You know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], as much as I'm looking forward to getting married and being out of this place, I'll miss the hustle a little. While I'm not really into other people, family's different, yeah? It's nice and comforting to be coming in from the fields in the evening and see lights in the windows — it's perfectly fine if people don't talk to me that much, because just being around is good enough to put my mind at ease." For someone used to having a big family around them at all times, you can see how it could feel lonely all of a sudden. "It's not as if I'm going far away for good or anything like that, but there's a difference between even visiting daily and living-in, you know? It's probably still a handful of years down the road, but when it does happen..." Kinu sticks her tongue out teasingly at you and points with both fingers down at her lower belly. "...I guess Hitoshi and I will just have to make a crowd of our own, eh [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]?" Uh... "Haha, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], you should see your face right now! I — ah — sorry for teasing you, but I couldn't let that one just pass without making a shot. Sorry." ] ] |[kiyoko.numKits 2 8 16 32 |[rand |"Dealing with younger siblings is an excellent way for someone in my position to learn basic communication with others," Kinu informs you with a smile. "It teaches you patience for those who may not have your ability, responsibility and kindness for those under your charge, and trains your internal fortitude for when they turn contentious on you. I certainly would not have turned out the way I am now without having others to care for, and I thank you for that, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." |"Mother says that when she was young, her mother trained her in child-raising by using her siblings as examples on which to demonstrate and practice. Putting it like that... I do not quite know, but it sounds rather cold and clinical to me. I feel like I should take more joy and put more emotion into having a hand in raising my siblings than just... seeing them as useful practice. It is not quite rational, perhaps, and I am probably overthinking her words, but it upsets me nevertheless." [party.has kiyoko |"Kinu, I meant nothing of the sort," your fox-wife says. "I never said that they were just anything, do not let your worry and imagination run away with you. You are too kind and emotional for your own good sometimes." "Mother —" "Don't worry about it," Kiyoko continues, her tone of voice softening. "But please remember that it's not always correct to overthink things and work yourself up over something that's only in your own head. This isn't the first time such has happened, and knowing you, daughter, it won't be the last. So much time and energy gets wasted on nothing when you start to fret and panic all over the place." "Yes, Mother." |Well, hearing her relate Kiyoko's words, it sounds like she's reading too much into what she didn't say, and that's pretty dangerous. Sometimes, it's okay to take things at face value and not overthink them too much, otherwise she'll start chasing at ghosts and worries that only exist in her own mind. She's far too kind and emotional sometimes. "..." You're sure her mother meant only what she said and nothing about just using her siblings as practice. It's perfectly possible to do that and deeply care for them as well. "Yes, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." ] |"It can get quite cold out there, so I like to put together warm clothes for everyone. Scarves and jackets at a minimum to prevent anyone from catching cold on chilly days." You know, with all that fur and fluffiness on them, you might have expected Kinu and her sibling[kiyoko.numKits 3|s] to not mind the cold so much, but apparently that's not the case. "The young are who they are," your fox-daughter replies dryly. "Prevention is better than cure — there is no need to tempt fate in the least. I remember when I fell ill when I was young, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], and there is no need to risk putting anyone through that in the least. Not that it is a problem; sewing together clothes gives me a chance to exercise my creativity while ensuring that my sibling[kiyoko.numKits 3|s are| is] adequately protected against the elements. The only real misgiving I have is the lack of fabric around here — while I could learn to use a spinner and loom in a day or two, that merely shifts the problem back. I wonder if cotton and flax grow in this climate?" |"Sometimes I make candy for my sibling[kiyoko.numKits 3|s]. Not a lot, just a little — while I cannot stand the smell of sweets myself, it is useful as an occasional treat or reward for a task well done or other accomplishment. While doing well should be its own reward in an ideal world, alas, we do not exist in an ideal world. Sometimes, incentives and inducements are required... not that one should overuse them or become reliant on bribery." |"I personally do a couple of rounds every night after lights out," Kinu tells you. "I was a kit once... perhaps I still am, in a sense. But insufficient sleep means a tired fox-child, and a tired fox-child is a mostly useless fox-child. I should know." ] |[rand |"Asagiri is such a lovely younger sister to have," Kinu informs you with a small, dreamy smile. "She is just as refined as me, but even better, she knows exactly what to say to cheer me up when I am feeling under the weather. It is good that we as sisters share so many interests; a den mother will need the support of her siblings when she leaves her home to found a new den. I am sure I will be able to count upon Asagiri to aid me in the future after I am married, and it is my duty to watch out for her, too." Ah... and her little sister is being helpful now, no doubt. "But of course. I could not leave the den in the afternoons to further my education under Matron Komari if I could not entrust its running in the hands of Asagiri, Tatsumi and Aya. Responsibility flows upwards, learning flows downwards; what I am taught, is entrusted to me to be passed down to those three. But if something were to unfortunately happen to me, I would certainly pick Asagiri as my first choice for her to step into my shoes." |"Even though we are close, all of my brothers and sisters are different in some way, for all our similarities," Kinu begins. "And that is a good thing. If two people are perfectly identical, chances are that one of them is unnecessary. Happily, no two people are perfectly identical, so it all works out. "Dealing with all kinds of people and learning to handle them is an important part of my future. That sort of experience is best begun at home, with those you care for. That is why... I am quite appreciative of what Mother and you have done." |"Asagiri told me the other day that if I had not come along and scooped up Nakano before she herself came of age, she might have had set her sights on seducing him for herself." Your fox-daughter raises a finger to her lips and looks thoughtful. "I am not sure whether I ought to be flattered or alarmed. Men like him who have had a classical education, amongst other qualities, are in quite rare supply in the colonies... but then if Asagiri is telling me this up front, she probably has no intention of snatching him away from me any longer. "Perhaps I should seek to set her up with someone who is more of a match for her age and better suited to her liking. She, too, bears the divine mark of white fur, so I am sure that despite her colonial origins there will be no shortage of eligible suitors. Well, eligible might be pushing it..." |"Sometimes, Mikoto comes around in the evenings after her shrine maiden duties and asks to play with my brothers and sisters. I... find it hard to refuse her, even though I know the hour is late and one should not excite the littlest ones too much lest they have trouble falling asleep. Mikoto can be very aggressive when she has the mind to be so, although it is never in a direct or threatening way. She just... her mere presence just fills the place and chokes you out." Oh, you understand fully how forceful Miko can be without being forceful at all. "She is so much like a big child herself when playing with the kits, though. They all love her. Mikoto's impulsive nature and her sense of wonder... ah ha ha ha. She is good as an aunt who comes around occasionally bearing gifts, perhaps, but probably not as a mother, or not with the way she is handling my brothers and sisters right now. Maybe that is why she is acting that way." |"When I was younger, there were more complaints at mealtimes, but now those are mostly gone. Everyone understands that there will be foods served that some like, there will be those that others do not enjoy, and one's turn will come around eventually and there is no point in complaining. Even though I sought to lead by example with the making of desserts, this orderliness has been a long time in the making. Ah... years upon years of forcing youkan down my throat and gagging at the taste... and that was one of the sweets I was more inclined to tolerate, because it had adzuki beans in it." ] |[rand |"In order to make everything work, delegation is important. Mother delegates to me, I delegate to Aya, Tatsumi and Asagiri, and they continue that trend down the line. It makes things run smoothly in a large family like ours." Well, her mother having to personally handle every jot and tittle herself would quickly drive her out of her mind. That, and it's good training for the future. "Training is one thing, yes. I like to give clear instructions and schedules to everyone at the start of every day and week; that way everyone knows what they are responsible for and there will be no shirking or claiming that someone else was going to do it. When you know you are ultimately responsible for something and no one else is, you will apply yourself to the task more diligently. "That being said, I do not want either of those three to be afraid to ask each other or me for help if they truly need it. Part of being in a big family is that we are not alone, after all. It is a careful state of affairs to remain conscientious." |"I remember mealtimes when I was younger, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Mother would direct, and I would run around doing her bidding; years later, I am now in Mother's position, and Asagiri in mine. When the time comes for me to be a mother myself, I suppose my own heir will be at my side... "I still remember, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. It was my task to not just serve everyone, but ensure that they were sated after the meal and had no complaints. The girl who I was did not quite understand at the time that complaints of someone else having three mushrooms over their two were spurious claims designed to annoy and had motivations other than having enough to eat... of course, as I grew older and gained a deeper understanding of people and their motivations, I learned to take such complaints in stride and give them what they deserved." The small smile that Kinu gives you is nothing but pleasant and angelic, and yet nevertheless chills you to the bone. "Mealtimes are much smoother nowadays. Years upon years of doling out food to my brothers and sisters taught me so much about how people tick, and while some of it is quite disheartening, there is enough for me to feel content, if not comfortable with the way things are. We all have our failings, after all." |"Having to reprimand my brothers and sisters from time to time is an unavoidable part of being in a position of authority. However, when doing so, I try to keep in mind that we all have our moments of weakness and that no one is perfect. So long as there is genuine contrition, shame and regret in addition to actual action taken towards improving one's self and correcting the mistake in question, I am inclined to be lenient in my judgement." That's very kind of her, but she needs to make sure that her merciful tendencies aren't taken advantage of. "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... while I do not claim to possess telepathy or be infallible on the matter, I would like to imagine that I am quite adept at reading people. Then there is the matter of taking others' past behavior and standing into account... for some strange reason, I am much less inclined to let Aya off than I am Tatsumi. Cultivating a reputation for being just yet merciful... it not only raises one's esteem amongst others, but also allows one to be at peace with oneself, those around you, and the world at large." |"Ehehe. [pc.mf|Father|Mother], I will admit to a small vice..." Oh? What brought this on? "I really like calling up the littlest of my brothers and sisters, have them rest their head in my lap and cleaning their ears. It makes me feel most warm and satisfied inside to do such a thing and feel my littlest siblings squirm and yip... it makes me feel like a mother already, all fluffy and good inside." Well, that's adorable. Why does she call it a vice, though? It sounds like remarkable and caring work that she's doing. "Because I am not really doing it with their grooming or well-being in mind, or at least as the primary intent, but rather my own satisfaction. That is why I call it a vice... that my little siblings are clean and comfortable is a mere side effect. In that sense, they are doing me a favor, and not the other way around." Oh, come on. It's not any kind of sin to take pleasure in making or seeing others happy and comfortable. That's nonsense. "..." |"I always look forward to trimming day," your daughter says with a small smile. "Once, it was just mother with scissors and clippers, then it was the two of us, and now it's me, Aya, Tatsumi and Asagiri all busily clipping away at a line of our little siblings. There's always so much fluff left over on the ground after everyone's had their fur trimmed. It's even better when it's time to trim everyone's winter coats, because the fur is extra thick and warm." It sounds like a lot of work to dispose of the clippings afterwards. Kinu raises an eyebrow. "Dispose? Oh no, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], that would be a terrible waste. I get everyone to sweep the fluffy clippings together so that they can be gathered, washed, treated and then spun into thread over at Matron Komari's. The more colors, the better!" Wait. She, uh, those clothes — "No simple wool or fiber can compare to the sheer luxuriance of kitsune fox-fur, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. [pc.ra kitsune|I am sure you agree, do you not?|Having known Mother in the intimate sense repeatedly, I am sure you agree, do you not?] There is certainly not enough to fashion clothing for everyone purely from fox-fur thread, but to my brothers and sisters, it surely is no different from wearing a second skin." Then her clothes... now that you think about it, they are the same shade of white as her hair and fur... Your fox-daughter gives you a mischievous smile and raises a hand to her cheek. "Oh, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I saved up my own fur clippings for a year or two to be able to fashion this. Isn't it simply fabulous?" ] |[rand |For someone who's in charge of so many siblings, your daughter sure has a lot of free time on her hands. What's her secret? "Making sure everyone knows their role, place, and responsibilities," Kinu answers without hesitation. "It was a lot of investment to begin with, but now everything runs like water in a culvert and I do not need to handle very many concerns, because most of them are resolved at the lower levels of responsibility. By the time something filters up to me, it must have already passed by the older siblings, then Aya, Tatsumi and Asagiri. For that to happen, it must be somewhat important and I can be unreserved in immediately dropping whatever I am doing and devoting my whole and undivided attention to whatever has come up." You see. So, if there aren't enough guidelines and experience and the matter flows up to her, the situation just sets precedent for what does happen the next time it happens. "Just so." |"While delegation and trust get things done, I nevertheless do drop in unannounced from time to time just to see how things are going," your kitsune daughter informs you. "After all, the true test of one's character is how one behaves when one imagines no one is watching. While I have yet to discover any major lapses that would otherwise have been covered up, it nevertheless sets my mind at ease. That, and if you can move silently enough to creep up on a fox kit, you can move silently enough to creep up on anyone." |"Just the other day, one of my littler siblings came up and said he loved me, and that I was just as great as Mother in his eyes. While that was rather flattering, I also began to worry about upstaging Mother in her rightful role. She has done so much to raise all of us, after all, and I could not keep things running here without what I learned at her knee." [party.has kiyoko |"I'm just glad you're appreciative of what others have done for you, daughter," Kiyoko answers. "Pass along what I've given to you, and you won't go wrong." |It's good that she is mindful of her roots and gives credit where it's due. ] Kinu gives [party.has kiyoko|the both of ]you a little bow. "I... I am glad. I just feel that I should be in my proper place and station, until I get married and strike off to form a den of my own." |"When I look back on it, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], having this many siblings and being responsible for them has been the most important cornerstone of my life. Not that I am discounting the education that Mother has bestowed upon me, of course, but there is no amount of book learning that will the importance of, or what is involved in putting your time into other people. While it would be nice if the world were perfectly ordered and predictable, people are rarely if ever so, and mere simple responsibility has taught me much about dealing with the unforeseen and unpredictable. "So... yes. I am glad to have a family of this size about me, for all the trouble that everyone may have given me in the past. Mere numbers mean nothing when I have plenty of care and concern to go around; the supply of such is limited by one's will, and not by how many it has to be divided amongst. If I did not care for my brothers and sisters, it would not matter whether they numbered one, or one hundred." |"When dealing with so many siblings, it is impossible to be equal, and appeals to such are usually just fox kits getting up to their usual games. In my experience, it is far more reasonable and useful to be equitable instead, and doubly so because we see each others' faces every day and have lived together as a family all our lives. For as much as my intuition may tell me something about someone, it is no substitute for truly understanding another person from experience over an extended period of time. "I cannot speak for others, but Mother and I have found this a most satisfactory way of managing a large family like ours." ] ] ] "

rows.original: [flags.MAI_PREG_ANN|"Even after all this, I still meet up with Mai every other day to play either shogi or go with her in the evenings," Kinu tells you. "Her being a mother doesn't mean that we have to change our usual routine for it, although it's quite funny to see her managing to concentrate with a fox kit at her breast. You'd imagine minding a child during a match would distract her somewhat, but she hasn't lost any more matches than she used to before. If anything, she's winning more often..." Maybe, just maybe, it's your darling daughter who's more distracted by the sight than Mai herself. "W-what? No, of course not, [kinu.dad]! Come on now, it's just two girls playing board games, what could you be thinking of?" And now she's trying to deflect the thrust and make you the villain. Oh, come on now. "It's not like that, I'm n-not jealous of her or anything!" Kinu's expression is the perfect picture of pouty huffiness. "Her circumstances are hardly ideal — " You said absolutely nothing about jealousy. Why would she bring that up right away? While you're sure that Kinu is well-versed in the theory of social feints, her practical skill at such leaves much to be desired. If she's her mother's daughter, then it's not hard for you to surmise that seeing Mai with a child has sparked similar feelings in her. Kinu pouts even more and balls her fists, but isn't up to arguing the point with you.|"I meet up with Mai every other day to play either shogi or go with her in the evenings," Kinu tells you. "She says it's a good way to wake up before she goes on her night vigil at the shrine. I... still have to beat her. Came close a couple of times, though." Ah, you remember how much of a terror little Kinu was when she was young, the undisputed champion of board games. Now that the tables have been turned, how does it feel? "You're asking me, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]? Not great, not great at all. But it's necessary, isn't it? I've endured greater humiliation, so losing a game or two doesn't ruffle me in the least, not at all." Hmm... "I'll beat her someday. Even if it's only just once, I'll beat her someday."]
rows.translation: [flags.MAI_PREG_ANN|即便经历了这一切，我仍然会每隔一天就和梅一起玩将棋或围棋，”纪吕告诉你，“她成为了母亲，但这并不意味着我们必须改变我们平时的习惯。不过，看到她怀里抱着小狐狸却还能专心致志地玩游戏，确实挺有趣的。你可能会认为，在比赛期间照看一个孩子会让她分心，但实际上，她的比赛成绩并没有比以前差，甚至赢的次数还多了…… 也许，只是也许，真正被这个场景吸引注意力的人，其实是你的宝贝女儿，而不是梅本人。 什、什么？不，当然不是这样的[kinu.dad]拜托，不过是两个女孩在玩桌游而已，你到底在想些什么啊？” 现在她居然试图转移话题，把责任推到你身上，想让你成为坏人。哦，真是够了。 “不是这样的，我根本不是嫉妒她什么的！小娟的表情简直就是生闷气的最佳写照。她的处境确实不太理想——” 不过你根本没提到嫉妒这件事，她为什么会立刻提到它呢？虽然你认为小娟很了解社交中的虚伪表现，但她在实际运用这些技巧方面还远远不够熟练。如果她真是她母亲的女儿，那么你应该不难猜到，看到舞带着一个孩子，她肯定也会产生类似的感受。 小娟更加撅起了嘴，握紧了拳头，但她并不打算和你争论这个话题。|我每隔一天就会和舞一起玩将棋，或者晚上陪她一起去下围棋。小娟会告诉你的。她说，在去神社参加夜间祈祷之前，这是个很好的清醒方式。不过……我还是得打败她。虽然有几次差点就成功了。 啊，你还记得小时候的小小娟有多可怕吧？她可是桌游界当之无愧的冠军啊。现在形势逆转了，这种感觉怎么样？ 你是在问我[pc.mf |爸爸 |妈妈 ]不算太糟，真的不算太糟。但这也是必要的，不是吗？我曾经经历过更羞辱人的事情，所以输一两场比赛根本不会让我感到困扰，真的完全不会。 嗯…… 总有一天我会打败她。哪怕只有一次，我也一定会打败她。]
