rows.original: [kinu.isInari |[kohaku.anyKids |[rand |"Everyone's congratulating Kohaku on the birth of her kit," Kinu says with a sigh. "Can't be helped, given how much she makes herself known to just about everyone; I'm sure the novelty will die out after a little while." Maybe it's your imagination, but she seems less than enthused about the whole situation. "What tipped you off, [kinu.Dad]? Do you want me to put on a fake smile and cheery face, then lie from between my teeth?" Your fox-daughter sinks back into her mire of teenage moodiness. "Maybe spending more time with the ducks until all of this blows over would be for the best." All right, what's gotten into her? "Gods, I..." Kinu looks straight at you, the words on the tip of her tongue, then starts mumbling as she flattens her ears down and to the sides. "Fine, a kit's a kit, great days and happiness for everyone involved and the like. And then someone winds up being smart and mentions Kohaku's kit is my half-sister like it doesn't matter at all. And then someone else mentions it, and soon enough people can't talk to me about the matter at all without bringing it up at least once, like they've got some kind of strange fixation of the matter. "It was already weird enough to begin with, [kinu.Dad], but this is just creeping me out. I don't want to be constantly reminded of the fact that I have a half-sister who's young enough to be my daughter. I suppose folks mean well, but why do they have to throw that bit in when all it does is to make me feel wound up and on edge inside? Since I don't want to be a stick in the mud and ruin it for everyone, the only answer is to go live amongst the chickens, ducks and fish until it's become old news." Kinu's gathered up one of her five tails in her hands, absent-mindedly picking at the fur as she speaks. "Look, [kinu.Dad], I'm not blaming you for anything; I've heard about what happened." Does everyone, now? A ghost of a smile creeps onto Kinu's lips. "Yeah, [kinu.Dad], just like that. Everyone knows it and can't help bringing it up when speaking with you, can they? But like I said, it's not your fault; I just need to stay away for a little while until the talk dies down. Chickens are refreshingly simple creatures by comparison." |"Kohaku came by the other day and asked if I could help look after her kit while she was out on caravan for the day, what with her being my half-sister and all. Even though Hotaru and Granny Komari are more than willing to help, she wanted the kit to have a change of scenery from time to time. After all, [kiyoko.numKits 8 |I already take care of so many brothers and sisters, what's one more to the pile, right |I already have to care for all kinds of small animals, surely a baby can't be that different, can it ]?" Time for you to guess, then. She said no? "Nah, [kinu.Dad]. I made her a better offer — said I'd come up with a fur and leather carrier so she can bring her kit with her on trips. That way she won't have to bother anyone with babysitting, and I know how much she hates being away from her child. It should be fine; she's not going out into the wilderness so the harness will hold." That... knowing Kohaku and how neurotic she can get about the gremlin, that would indeed be a better option. She knows the places where she does business, and if it's still too dangerous then she can have Hotaru babysit anyway; nevertheless, being able to be as close as possible, as much as possible, is something Kohaku would appreciate during her baby's formative days. "Like I said, [kinu.Dad], I made a better offer that doesn't involve me burning up a chunk of my spare time, and she gets what she really wants." A small smile plays on Kinu's lips. "Everyone wins. It shouldn't take me long to come up with a good design with the available materials[kiyoko.numKits 4 | — I've already tried out a few on my younger siblings, so it shouldn't be too hard to scale it down to baby-size ]. It's not as if Kohaku isn't used to carrying around heavy weights long distances, anyway." ] |[kohaku.pregStage 1 |[rand |"Kohaku came by the other day and asked me for more vegetables. I always have far, far more than we can actually eat — especially turnip and daikon — so I was happy to give her a whole bunch, but I'm starting to wonder if I should've asked where all that was going. It's far too much for one person to eat alone, and yet she comes by every few days for a couple more. Is it all going to the storehouse? No, that can't be, given that our systems are separate, and her place isn't set up to keep fresh vegetables. Pickles and preserves, maybe, but not fresh..." Was it on official business from the den? "She didn't say as much, but she's never asked me for anything outside of official requests. Is something up, [kinu.dad]?" Well, her situation's changed from before, hasn't it? Kinu thinks a moment, frowning, then realization dawns in a matter of seconds. "Don't be silly, [kinu.dad], she can't be eating all of them by herself. If we were to divide the amount she asks for by the number of days between requisitions, she'd be eating a whole third of her weight in veggies alone, in addition to whatever she gets from her own allotment! I get pretty starved after working a whole day without a snack and even I don't eat that much! A tiny thing like her? I don't believe it!" If that's what she believes, presumably this has been going on for a while. She's the direct kind of girl — why doesn't she just ask Kohaku what the veggies are for, then? "[kinu.Dad]! You don't just ask someone a question like that!" Why not? It's not as if she's one for social niceties, and she knows that. Maybe there's a reason she's reluctant to ask the question? "There isn't! I just didn't think of it!" Okay, then. If Kohaku turns up that regularly, then surely she can ask the next time she shows. "I think you're taking this a bit too far, [kinu.dad]. But sure, fine. Next time she shows up, I'm inviting her in to eat and see just how much she can pack away into that tiny body of hers." |Kinu's gaze darts askance and she puts her fingers together, mumbling while her cheeks color. What was that? You didn't quite catch her words. "I said, I don't really want to talk about her, [kinu.Dad]." Aand why might that be? "It's like, everything anyone has to say about Kohaku these days is either about or related to how she's expecting, nothing else. There's still so much about her that could go into the local gossip, but no, that's the thing." Well, it is a relatively new development when it comes to major changes, and the combination of novelty and importance make for its outright domination of any gossip about the golden fox herself. Like it or hate it, it's not surprising in the least that people are talking about it. "Yeah, I get it. It's just that hearing the same thing every day gets tiring after a while. Are people that starved for excitement that they don't talk about anything new?" Given the color of her face right now, is there something else that she's not saying? "Huh. It's that obvious, [kinu.Dad]?" She was never one for hiding her feelings to be polite, so yes, it's really obvious. A sigh, an attempt by your daughter to hide her embarrassment that utterly flops. "Everyone talking about it just makes me all the more antsy to want it for myself. I had to tell myself last night that it would be obviously be a horrible idea if I badgered Hitoshi into getting me pregnant so Mom would be forced to stop dragging out our engagement. Then before I knew what I was doing, I'd told myself it was probably a bad idea, than maybe a bad idea. Gods damn it, seeing all the girls just that bit older than me get nice and round is driving me crazy with wanting it for myself despite knowing that hurrying things along with some bright idea or the other is really not going to go over well. "Do you actually know what some of the gossip says, [kinu.Dad]? About how sensitive Kohaku's become? And talking to her..." The lustfulness of a young woman fresh in the flower of her womanhood. It was to be expected, but only someone with Kinu's candor and directness could give voice to such thoughts with the raw immediacy that they deserve. And only she could turn a conversation about Kohaku into one about herself, really, although at this point it's more a tantrum than a conversation. "I want it!" Your fox-daughter balls her hands into angry fists as she rails against the cosmic injustice of the world instead of accepting it like a good little kitsune. "I want it, want it, want it! And Kohaku being a chatterbox ensures that the only thing that anyone ever talks about is how happy and round she is, and I'm going to go crazy if this keeps up for much longer! You can't imagine how this feels, [kinu.Dad]! "I hate everything and I hate myself." There, there. Maybe a cold bath after this conversation will help things. There's the waterfall pool, isn't there? Kinu groans and sighs, flattening her ears down and forward. "Yeah, you're probably right, [kinu.Dad]. Some days it feels like my brain's being twisted and is trying to escape out of my ears, even if Granny Komari says that the long engagement is to my benefit." |"Kohaku's been coming over to talk every now and then, by which I mean to talk while I pretend to listen. It really isn't hard, [kinu.Dad] — all I have to do is keep quiet, which is what I was going to do anyway, so she just goes on and on and on. After a while, it kind of reminds me of a bird singing in a tree or on one of the fences, vaguely pleasant background noise without any real meaning to it." Huh, she comes here to chit-chat? "Granny Komari's forbidden her from going on caravan, from what I hear, but she sometimes finds the time to come around in the mornings if there's no one slated to make any deliveries or collections for the day. Apparently these breaks are another thing that Granny Komari's imposed on her against her will. She doesn't want to loaf about in the den and make it obvious that she's not at work but doesn't want to stay cooped up in her chambers either, so she comes here to burn time." Oh dear. Hope Kinu doesn't mind having Kohaku around; does she get in the way? "It's okay, [kinu.Dad]. She really does want to learn how to get better at [kiyoko.numKits 4 |caring for kits |being domestic ], so I let her follow me around while I get the estate in order and she also helps out with some of the things. So far she's been more of a help than a hindrance, which is saying something. The non-stop talking is just something that [kiyoko.numKits 4 |I've learned to live with when you pack enough people into one place |you get used to after a while, like I said ]. Not a bother at all." Well, that's a good thing. Your fox-daughter could stand to make more friends her own age who aren't Mai, and Kohaku — "Nah, she's not a friend, [kinu.Dad]. That doesn't mean that we're not friendly, but I don't just go around calling people friends without considering it deeply and frankly, no one should. There's a special meaning to that word, and using it as you please cheapens it, I feel. Anyway, she's welcome to hang out and talk at me if she wants to, especially if she makes herself useful. Even better if she thinks I'm listening." |"Well, if you really want to know, [kinu.Dad], Kohaku came in yesterday evening. Said she wanted to figure out what were the best dishes for making a lot of in the shortest time possible, and how to go about it. I just found it funny, because it's not something very many people care for." She did teach the little golden fox, then? Kinu looks a little sheepish. "Yeah, I did. Not that I'd originally wanted to, but she had a way with words and convinced me to do it anyway. I shouldn't be surprised that she knows how to press buttons, but there's something about seeing in action that's another thing altogether. I let her help with dinner and the next day's cold breakfast in advance, so she presumably picked up a thing or two." ] |[rand |Your daughter breaks into a sly grin at the mere mention of Kohaku's name. "Eheheh. Kohaku is such a cute and adorable little thing, even I can't help but want to squeeze her and pet her ears, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]. Did you know that those big ears and the ball-shaped fluff in them is actually a trait of kitsune who come from the inland mountainous areas of the Old Country? I know she's a grown woman, but even so it's hard to hold back!" You can understand that feeling — you get it too every time you pass by the little storehouse manager. "I know, right, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]? It doesn't help that she can be so childish and enthusiastic about anything and everything when she's being herself!" |"To be placed in charge of the den's storehouse shows the trust that not just Granny Komari, but everyone has in you." Kinu begins. "Kohaku's handling not just the entire finances of the den itself, but all of the stocks and goods. A less scrupulous person would certainly be tempted to embezzle at least a little of that for themselves; Granny really feels safe in relying on Kohaku to find the best deals and keep the books balanced. Well, then there is the fact that if she showed the slightest sign of abusing her position for her own benefit, Nakano wouldn't hesitate to chop her head off, and most everyone in the den would cheer him on." That sounds... harsh. "It is, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ], but at the same time if you're in charge of a storehouse that size people from over a hundred families are counting on you for their fair share of salt and rice, and in a place as dangerous as the frontier. You betray that kind of trust, and it's the end of the line for you. It's just the way things work, being the flip side of foxes sticking together." |"You know, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ], I'm kind of glad I met Kohaku. I used to think I was the shortest girl around, but now there's someone who's as tall as I am. While I'm pretty resigned to having to look up to most people and never be able to reach the peaches even on the lowest of boughs, it's still nice to have someone whom I can see eye-to-eye. Craning my neck up all day long makes my head hurt after a while, you know what I mean?" Does Kohaku feel the same way? "Dunno, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]. I've tried to ask her about it several times, but someone's always trying to pat her on the head when the question comes to mind. I've long since given up on trying to get a word in edgeways." |"Kohaku looks really great when all dressed up in traditional clothing; she goes from cute to pretty just like —" your fox-daughter snaps her fingers — "that. Doubly so when she does her hair up in that bun with a braid encircling it — a crown braid, I think it's called. It's kind of a pity that she only makes the effort when heading back to the Old Country through the torii gate or during festivals, because the difference is startling — it's still her while being someone else completely, if you get what I mean. "Even so, I can't blame her for putting on her usual clothes all day. Putting up your hair like that has to really take up a lot of time, and the same goes for her formal getup. I'd know, because I like wearing my work clothes as many places as I can get away with doing..." |"Kohaku really likes taiyaki. You know what I mean, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]? The fish-shaped cakes that she sometimes sells?" Kinu gestures with her fingers, as if to mimic the act of baking one. "Like, I've tried a couple, and they're... kind of okay, I guess. I know, I don't like sweets, but even taking into account my own personal preferences I don't think there's anything really great or special about the stuff. If you ask me, her like of the pastries is rooted more in sentimental reasons than any actual like for its taste. Don't take my word for it, though." ] ] ] |[kohaku.anyKids |[rand |"Kohaku has been talking to Matron Komari about the potential heritability of her position with regards to her daughter," Kinu tells you with a sigh. "It has been going on for some time now, I am afraid. There does not appear to be any easy resolution." It sounds like a prickly situation, true. With the way kitsune work, you'd have imagined that Komari would just shut down the idea and that would be the end of that, but it looks like that's not the case. "It is indeed one of those delicate situations where you do not wish to alienate someone who is faithful and competent, [kinu.Dad]. And yet there is a problem there — Kohaku is pushing for the decision now with full confidence of her daughter's future aptitude, while Matron Komari is urging caution. As someone who will be responsible for just about everything in the colonies in the future, I sat in on the proceedings." When she describes it so dispassionately, it does sound like an open and shut case to you. Even Miko and Mai can't tell if an infant is going to be suited for a task down the line, and that doesn't even take into account the kit's future desires. "There are also some other implications... making the position hereditary, even if only for one generation, implies some degree of ownership over said position, while the privilege of appointment should be solely reserved for the den matron herself. That, and middling positions in the civil service such as the one Kohaku holds have never been explicitly hereditary for the sake of encouraging people to do better. If we give our word to let Kohaku's daughter inherit the position ahead of time, the most any of her subordinates can aspire to is being a bench-warmer while the child comes of age. That has a certain demoralizing effect, it must be said." And she's still pushing for it? "The aptitude of her daughter aside, the thrust of her argument has been that one generation building upon the foundations the last has laid is how we move forward as a people, slowly but steadily and securely. That may be true, but the den matron is of the opinion that the above is of little use if it's forward in the wrong direction. To be sure, Kobayashi is not completely wrong, but it is a prickly situation and we really do want to think the best of our children. I do not see this stopping in the foreseeable future, and do find myself looking forward to overseeing these exchanges." |You've noticed that Kohaku's become absolutely inseparable from her daughter — ever since the kit emerged from her belly, you haven't seen the little golden fox without her gremlin in tow. It's kind of cute. "A fine sentiment, [kinu.Dad]. If I may make a suggestion, you should express your delight with the child every time you see her." Aww. She doesn't need to suggest that, you're likely to do it anyway, like everyone else. Why does she feel the need to point it out, though? "From everything I have heard from my peers, Kohaku has made many attempts — sometimes rather drastic ones — since young in order to feel accepted, [kinu.Dad]. Not that she was ostracized to begin with, but feelings do not necessarily need to be rational. Even after having made herself the social focus of the den as the local gossipmonger, bringing her daughter around and having everyone fuss over the child has been the most approval she's received in a good while." Come on, now. Surely Kinu isn't so cynical as to imagine that Kohaku's using her daughter as a social prop. "Not consciously, perhaps, but the effect is undeniable, [kinu.Dad]. Furthermore, I made no value judgement on the matter, and encouraged you to make her feel at home. So please, do. It will put a smile on her face — I think she simply does not want her daughter to experience the problems of her youth. Perhaps it will pass with the novelty of the situation, but for now the inseparable nature of mother and child warms the heart." |"Do you not find it interesting, [kinu.Dad]? Matron Komari forbidding Kohaku from leaving the den on caravan while with child was a sore point for the latter, but now that permission has been granted once again she has lost much of her desire to leave for long periods of time and seems much happier for it. Not that she does not continue to trade in various places for our benefit, but there is always this gladness about her when she returns and she is looking to train one of her subordinates to lead the caravans now." It's interesting, but not surprising. Major changes in one's life often come with a reassessment of one's priorities, and it's not surprising that Kohaku's decided to take her life in a different direction. You had something similar when Kinu was born, and overall it's turned out for the better. Kinu dips her head at you. "You flatter me, [kinu.Dad]." Of course, it's not true for everyone, but having kids is a pretty big impetus for one to make some changes in one's life. That Kohaku doesn't see it as a loss in something that she wanted to do, but more a gain in something that she wants to, means that no one else should be upset about it, really. "Mhm. It is being handled in a responsible manner so as to minimize disruption inflicted upon others." |"The fact that Kohaku did not just have a smooth pregnancy, but also an enjoyable one inasmuch as it was able puts my mind at ease when it comes to the future," Kinu tells you. "I was worried that her petite nature might have resulted in complications while carrying her child, but she has done well both by herself and her daughter. Since she is the only one in the colonies who is my peer in height and approximates my physiology best, having her flourish like this without complication does make me quite anticipate the prospect, [kinu.Dad]." Maybe this is the reason why both her mother and Komari settled on such a lengthy engagement by kitsune standards. Let others go first to anticipate potential problems, as it were. Your fox-daughter gives you a smile. "I do not think that this was fully anticipated, but my elders often have more insight than me on these matters. There is still the post-natal period for me to take an interest in... as her future ruler, I have a duty to responsibly steward Kohaku and her issue, so I have taken it upon myself to alter her allotments accordingly. She can consider it a reward from me for breaking ground that I will be covering in the future. "Not all of it will be relevant, of course — for example, her concerns about not being able to make enough milk are terribly skewed by the average here, and it does not exactly correlate to production anyway. Nevertheless, it's the best I have to work with, and for that I owe her my gratitude." ] |[kohaku.pregStage 1 |[rand |"It is very gratifying seeing Kohaku becoming a mother," Kinu says with a small, pleasant and utterly inscrutable smile. "Having her come to terms with the full realization of what she has done to herself, as well as the consequences thereof, is a standing lesson to us all of the importance of being able to anticipate the fruits of our actions." Well, you think that she knew what was going to happen, she just didn't care. By the point the latter kicked in, well... "As Matron Komari says, it was a conscious decision, and I am inclined to follow her position on these matters, [kinu.Dad]. She tells me that she's been colonial governor long enough to see the population wax and wane for various reasons, and that we shouldn't panic in either case; that the younger folk are expressing enough confidence in the future to have families is a positive note and it's something to be encouraged for this portion of the cycle." You're not exactly sure that confidence in the future was what went through Kohaku's head when she did the thing, but if it makes Komari feel good about herself then that's fine. That being said, you get the impression that Kinu's trying to make some kind of point here, but if there's one there it's buried under so many layers that you're not seeing it. "Suffice to say that both Matron Komari and I am content with the way events are developing, [kinu.Dad], and that I have no opposition to the fact — quite the opposite. Why, I have even taken the initiative to increase her allotment to match her appetite, a well-deserved reward to match her excellent service to the den thus far." |"I have taken a particular interest in Kohaku while she's with child," Kinu says, ever so pleasant and refined. "While not an exact match, her particular physiology does give some insight into what will be expected of me in the future. While I am more full-bodied in contrast to her more focused nature, there is the matter of our height..." That's right, Kohaku's the exact same height as Kinu measured at the top of the head; of all the foxes in the den, Kohaku's proportions match Kinu's the most because of that alone. Even if she isn't as bottom-heavy as Kohaku, it'd make the most sense for your fox-daughter to take note of the little golden fox's pregnancy and see how she handles it. "Which, all appearances aside, has been rather well; if anything, the minor inconveniences make her more endearing, another lesson to be learned. It's best to learn from other peoples' experiences rather than your own and thus avoid any attendant risk, is it not?" It is, and hearing her speak of it so candidly... "Forgive me for any inadvertent discomfort I may have caused, [kinu.Dad]. Nevertheless, it does not diminish the need for me to care for others and in doing so, care for myself." Your fox-daughter gives you a sweet smile. "Perhaps I can offer you a drink to take your mind off matters?" |"If I may express my honest opinion, [kinu.Dad], it does feel like many of my peers are choosing to have kits these days. Matron Komari does approve in general, given that it is a vote of confidence in the colony's future, and I am inclined to agree with her. Little Kohaku is just following the trend as she does." To the point of... wait, she's serious, isn't she? Your fox-daughter nods. "I was not present to witness it personally, but Mikoto and Miyuki assure me in all seriousness that given some of the things she did when younger, it would not be far-fetched to consider it a possible motivation. A likely one, in fact, even if she would never admit it." And she believes Miko and Mai on the matter. "In this regard, yes. I corroborated their recountings of several of such incidents with others and it would appear that the storehouse quartermaster has had an interesting childhood, being raised by the den matron in her parents' absence. For example, part of her impetus for wanting to leave and travel was a childish desire to search for them... a notion that was quickly dropped, to be sure, but it was nevertheless what she wanted. "To be sure, [kinu.Dad]: I am not making excuses for what she has done, or claiming she had no agency in the matter. But while the exact form could hardly be predicted, that she did something like this, consciously or otherwise, does not surprise Mikoto, Miyuki or Hotaru." |"Does Kohaku's occasional moodiness bother you, [kinu.Dad]?" While you're aware that these emotional upsets are to be expected amongst foxen with child, it's particularly obvious in Kohaku's case because she used to be such a cheerful little thing before. Yes, you know that at least part of it is a mask she puts on to serve the storehouse customers better, but that doesn't make the contrast any less shocking. Kinu smiles and puts her fingers together in a steeple. "Understandable, so it behooves us to be even more understanding, [kinu.Dad]. As her friend and future ruler, I would exhort you to indulge her from time to time and cheer her up; this goes double for the days when she is struggling to put on a cheerful face for the sake of her customers. And remember, there are days when the pendulum swings the other way and she is extremely vibrant and energetic, so savor those as well." But of course, and thanks for reminding you. These things should be obvious, but it's easy to get caught up in the bad stuff and not pay enough attention to the good. ] |[rand |"From time to time, Kohaku will show me pieces that she has managed to secure from across the ocean," Kinu tells you. "I must confess, I am not quite sure what I should feel when I look at them. There is a sensation that I should know more about these goods she brings over, that they form a part of my roots and blood, but then I also realize that they are merchandise to be bought and sold and that diminishes some of the magic and mystique they hold. While it is said that familiarity breeds contempt, I am not sure it is supposed to be this fast-acting." |"Oh, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ]. Whatever you do, please do not call Kohaku a merchant. It makes her very sad to hear that, even if she may not show it." Well, it is what she does, isn't it? "That is... correct and not correct; I did not quite understand it myself until Mother explained it to me. The main issue is that back across the ocean, merchants are regarded as little more than thieves, because frankly they are the most unscrupulous lot in general; one cannot say that the reputation is unearned. At least the stationary ones merely swindle; the traveling ones take advantage of their transient nature to rob who they can blind and vanish into the night. "Kohaku does not do any of that and works very hard at much personal risk to better the den's fortunes, so associating her with that lot is rather unfair, I believe. That, and none of the goods or money she handles are actually hers — if they have to belong to any one person, they belong to [kinu.isInari |Granny |Matron ] Komari. Since Kohaku works fastidiously to avoid all the causes of merchants' poor reputation, I see no reason to tarnish her with that unfortunate name." |"I must confess, I am afraid of that puppet that helps with the heavy lifting in the storehouse," your fox-daughter tells you. "It is so big, it looks as if it could easily crush me in its hands. Kohaku has no fear of the artificer's creation, though — I believe she has even given it a pet name. I suppose one must be quite fearless to walk straight into native settlements and deal with them, knowing full well the consequences were one to be unmasked. I do not believe I have ever seen her afraid of anything in the time that I have known her." |"It is interesting to be able to see some of the items that Kohaku sources from different places. Since I am not able to go and see the world, nor would I wish to abandon my duties to do so, it is nice that she allows me to inspect some of the more interesting goods that she brings back from places I have only heard of, places like Jassira and Tychris. Torii gate technology is quite impressive, is it not?" The kitsune may not have come up with it on their own — the Belharans did that with the waystone idols — but they certainly honed it to a level far beyond the designers' original intentions. "Kohaku is always willing to talk about her travels, regardless of how brief they are, and the stories behind the acquisition of her latest haul, no matter how routine. No matter where her tasks for the matron take her, she is always back within a day and ready to run the storehouse without being the least bit tired. She says that thrills are but only momentary, and that going to other places — even the Old Country — remind her all the more that the people and things she cares for are here on the frontier. Of course, she says she would never have realized that by just living in the den, either...but either way, we should take pride in living here." Surely that's not the only reason she's always back within the day, though... "Haha, you are astute, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ]. Yes, it is also hard to maintain an illusory disguise when asleep, you know. Revealing their true forms, even in the relative privacy of expensive accommodations, would be too much of a risk for her and her bodyguards. The Ways Between are so convenient, are they not?" |"While I suppose being loquacious and chatty comes with being a merchant, I am not sure if it is strictly necessary for Kohaku to take it to such extremes. If I want to know about who said what to whom, if anyone had an embarrassing accident, or if Takahiro is still giving Nakano liquor he really should not be having, I merely have to ask her about it. Yes, I am glad to know that wastrel is still plying my beloved with drink, but I am not glad that everyone else in the den knows it, too. It makes me want to die of shame in his stead. "But... if you want the entire den to know a fact, no matter how small, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ], all you have to do is to let Kohaku know. I promise you, before the sun has risen the next day, it will be the talk of the town right down to the smallest detail." ] ] ] ]

[kinu.Dad]你是想让我强挤出一副假笑，装出一副开心的样子，然后在牙缝里说谎吗？”你的狐妖女儿又重新陷入了青少年时期那种情绪化的状态。“或许，多花些时间陪那些鸭子，等到这一切都过去之后，才会是最好的选择。好吧，她到底怎么了？” “天啊，我……”小娟直视着你的眼睛，话到嘴边却又停住了，然后她把耳朵贴向两侧，开始低声嘟囔起来。好吧，套装就是套装，希望所有相关的人都能度过愉快而幸福的时光。然后就有人聪明地指出，琥珀的套装其实和我是同父异母的姐妹，好像这根本不是什么重要的事情一样。接着又有人提到了这一点，很快大家和我聊天时都会至少提到一次这个话题，就好像他们对这件事有着某种奇怪的执着一样。 一开始这就已经够奇怪的了[kinu.Dad]但这真的让我感到很不自在。我并不想一直被提醒自己有一个年纪小到可以当我女儿的同父异母妹妹。我想大家都是好意，但为什么非得提到这一点呢？这样做只会让我感到焦虑和不安而已。因为我不想成为阻碍别人前进的绊脚石，破坏大家的计划，所以唯一的办法就是融入这个群体，和鸡鸭鱼们一起生活，直到这件事变成老生常谈。” 小娟把她的五条尾巴中的一条拿在手里，边说边心不在焉地拨弄着尾巴上的毛发。 看， [kinu.Dad]我并不是在责怪你什么；我听说过发生的事情。” 现在大家都知道了吗？ 小娟的嘴角浮现出一丝淡淡的微笑：“是啊， [kinu.Dad]就是这么回事。每个人都知道这件事，所以在和你说话时都会不由自主地提到它，对吧？但就像我说的，这不是你的错；我只需要暂时远离一段时间，等这件事的热度消退就好了。相比之下，鸡这类动物可真是简单得让人感到清爽呢。 |前几天，小白来找我，问我在她外出参加商队活动的时候，能否帮忙照看一下她的物品。毕竟我们算是同父异母的姐妹嘛。虽然萤和麻里奶奶也非常愿意帮忙，但她还是希望这些物品能偶尔换个环境放置。毕竟[kiyoko.numKits 8 |我已经照顾了这么多兄弟姐妹，再多一个又有什么关系呢，对吧？ |我已经要照顾各种各样的小动物了，一个婴儿应该也不会有什么不同吧，对吧？ ]那么，现在该让你猜猜看了吧。她是拒绝了吗？ “不，应该没有。 [kinu.Dad]我给了她一个更好的提议——我说我会设计一个毛皮和皮革材质的携带包，这样她就可以在出行时把所有装备都带在身边了。这样一来，她就不用麻烦别人帮忙照看孩子了，而且我也知道她有多么不愿意离开自己的孩子。应该没问题的；她又不会去荒野里，所以那个安全带肯定能起到保护作用。 不过……考虑到小红那个性格，以及她对那些小故障总是那么敏感，这个办法确实更合适一些。她熟悉自己开展业务的那些地方，如果那里仍然太危险，她可以让萤帮忙照看；不过，在宝宝成长的关键阶段，能够尽可能地靠近宝宝，对琥珀来说无疑是非常重要的。 就像我之前说的， [kinu.Dad]我提出了一个更好的方案，这个方案不会让我浪费大量的业余时间，而她也能得到她想要的东西。真的这样大家都能满意。”小娟的嘴角浮现出一丝微笑，“每个人都能得到自己想要的东西。利用现有的材料，我应该很快就能想出一个不错的设计方案。[kiyoko.numKits 4 | — 我已经在我弟弟妹妹们身上试过了几种方法，所以把它们调整成适合婴儿使用的规模应该不会太难。 ]反正小白也早就习惯了长时间背着重型的东西长途移动了。 ] |[kohaku.pregStage 1 |[rand |前几天，小白来了，问我能不能多给她一些蔬菜。我家里准备的蔬菜总是远远多于我们实际需要的量——尤其是萝卜和白萝卜——所以我很乐意给她很多，但现在我在想，当初是不是应该先问问她这些蔬菜要拿去哪里呢。一个人吃这么多未免太浪费了，可她还是每隔几天就再来拿一些。这些食物都是被送到仓库里去吗？不，不可能吧，因为我们的储存系统是分开的，而且她的住处也没有条件存放新鲜蔬菜啊。腌制品或者果酱或许还可以，但新鲜的食物就不行了……” “她是代表组织来执行公务的吗？” “她没有明确说明，但除了正式的工作要求之外，她从来没向我要过任何东西。出什么问题了吗？ [kinu.dad]嗯，她的处境确实和以前不一样了，不是吗？” The kitsune may not have come up with it on their own — the Belharans did that with the waystone idols — but they certainly honed it to a level far beyond the designers' original intentions. "But... if you want the entire den to know a fact, no matter how small, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ], all you have to do is to let Kohaku know. rows.original: [kinu.isInari |[rand |"Granny Komari usually defers so much to Mother that I was really surprised she didn't object to me and Hitoshi being an item,"Kinu says thoughtfully. "I was half-expecting her to take Mother's side and forbid us to even see each other, and that would mean we'd have to elope —" Wait, what? "Ah ha ha, you should see your face, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]. Nah, Hitoshi's too rooted in place to even entertain that kind of idea, even if I were to push it on him with all my might. But back to the point, I really was very surprised. It's not just the personal guilt and other feelings she shares with Mother from their time together, but that she's also expected to obey Mother's word unquestioningly with all the weight of tradition and authority in their formal relationship. Seriously, I'm not sure why Granny is sticking her neck out for me so badly, but I'm not about to say no to any kind of help I can get in this regard." |"Haha, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ], I remember one of the first talks Mother had with Granny Komari — she was asking if there was anything she could impart to me in order to further my education. I remember when Granny simply looked me up and down, shook her head, and said something along the lines of 'I regret to inform you that everything I can teach that this girl is willing to learn, you have already imparted to her.' I guess I get the meaning of what she was trying to say, but that's a pretty roundabout way to putting it, don't you think?" Maybe she was only trying to be polite to Kiyoko. She is Komari's liege, after all, no matter how many years separate them now. Kinu frowns and scratches her head. "I don't think that's the case, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ] — there was definitely a subtext there that I caught, but I didn't quite understand. Anyways, while I'm glad that Mother tried to teach me what she knew and succeeded in most of it, I had to learn so much of what I actually use these days from scratch, or from other people. I guess if Granny Komari grew up with Mother, they'd have had similar foundations in their education, even considering the disparity in their social rank. Maybe it'll all be clearer when I figure out what Granny Komari was trying to say." |"Because of the terms of the penance laid on her, Granny Komari doesn't need to eat, but that doesn't stop her from enjoying a bit of youkan every now and then. I don't care much for sweets myself, but I do enjoy growing adzuki beans, so things have gotten to the point where every time I bring her some she just asks what is it I want from her that I feel I need a bribe to go along with my request." Kinu gets a sheepish look on her face and sticks out her tongue at you. "Can't someone do something nice for you out of the goodness of their hearts? H-hey, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ], quit laughing! Cut it out!" Y-you're sorr — no, actually, you're not sorry in the slightest. It really is very obvious when your little fox-daughter is doing something out of the goodness of her heart, and when she's blatantly trying to win someone's favor. If she wants to appear more genuine, she just needs to do a little self-reflection on how she behaves when she's trying to do something nice for Hitoshi. "I don't get it, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]." Of course she doesn't get it. If she did, she wouldn't be in this position in the first place. Besides, it's going to take a lot more than that to pull one over on a wily old fox like Komari who's no doubt seen it all from her many descendants. |"Granny Komari's place may be the largest, safest and most comfortable den in the colonies, but that doesn't change the fact that we're still on the frontier here. But that's why I go over in the afternoons after my work in the mornings is done." One set of fields just isn't enough for a true enthusiast like her, huh? "Well, I meant more to say that I'm willing to put in my share too, but that works just as well. That, and I'm learning so many things from the way they go about stuff here. And Hitoshi got me a whole bunch of seeds from his own cultivars, and more stuff imported from across the ocean. And I know that Granny Komari's been watching me when she thinks I'm not paying attention. What old woman wouldn't keep an eye on a girl interested in her great-great-grandson?" One who has better things to do in life, presumably. "Ah ha ha. You're so funny, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]." |[flags.KOMARI_FUCKED |As you ask your fox-daughter for her thoughts on Komari, she turns to look at you with some mix of discomfort and exasperation. Taking a deep breath, Kinu rubs her temples before sighing and responding. "[pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]... what in the world did you do? You know how much I loathe gossip, but even I've heard the rumors." What does she mean? You c— You freeze in your tracks, Kinu's eyes cutting straight through you as she stares. Right, evading things isn't going to help... but Kinu's not done. "Look, [pc.mf |dad |mom ], it's really none of my business what you're doing around the den, and I'm perfectly alright with that fact. Heck, it really shouldn't be something I'm even having to think about. But seriously? Granny Komari?[silly | Have you no shame? No morals? | ]" You're a bit taken aback by the fact you're being scolded by your daughter; her tone isn't even flush with anger, but simple disappointment. You can't help but try to defend yourself a bit; as you protest that it's hardly that big of a deal, Kinu buries her head in her hands, groaning with exasperation. "[silly |Why are you like this? Can't you just not fuck every one of my acquaintances for once? |Ugggh... ] I can't believe this. I'm never gonna hear the end of it, am I?" Kinu asks, not expecting an answer. Kiyoko forgave her publicly. Wasn't that enough? "Ah... [pc.mf |Father |Mother ]. The sting of shame reaches deep into the kitsune spirit. [pc.ra kitsune |Even though you are one of us in body, you still have to join us in soul |As much as you are with us, it can still be hard for you to understand ]. Forgive me for speaking plainly, but there is no blunting the truth of this matter. Either way, it is not me or Mother or even his divine lordship who can forgive the den matron; it is herself who must do it." |"Matron Komari is quite the accomplished conversationalist," your daughter informs you in no uncertain terms. Hmm, that's eye-opening. You've spoken with the den matron on numerous occasions, and she's never struck you as anything out of the ordinary. "Well, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ], if you did figure it out, she would not have been very good at it, would she? When you simply remain quiet and let people just talk, you get to learn a lot about them if you pay attention. Doubly so if you know how to ask the right kinds of leading questions. Double that again if you are speaking the kind of language that they're receptive to at the moment. For someone in my position, I need to be able to communicate with all kinds of people, not just my family, and there is so much more to learn." |"Matron Komari and Mother have such a close friendship and tight bond that it has survived all these intervening years; it is as if they had never been separated for centuries. I would consider myself fortunate to be able to attract a retainer who was half as dedicated. Admittedly, options are rather short in the colonies." Call it a hunch, but maybe the two of them didn't start that way, but grew into that kind of relationship. "I meant something approaching that, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ]. Some people have the capability for that kind of reciprocal behavior. Others do not. You have to have something to start with, after all. It is, um... complicated." You'll say. |[flags.KOMARI_FUCKED |As the topic of the den matron comes up, Kinu's attention momentarily drifts. Appearing lost in thought for a moment, recollection dawns on her face as something clicks, and she returns her gaze to you. "Ah... [pc.mf |Father |Mother ], I do hope those 'private matters' you and Matron Komari had to attend to were not too troublesome. Nah, Hitoshi's too rooted in place to even entertain that kind of idea, even if I were to push it on him with all my might. But back to the point, I really was very surprised. It's not just the personal guilt and other feelings she shares with Mother from their time together, but that she's also expected to obey Mother's word unquestioningly with all the weight of tradition and authority in their formal relationship. Seriously, I'm not sure why Granny is sticking her neck out for me so badly, but I'm not about to say no to any kind of help I can get in this regard." |"Haha, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ], I remember one of the first talks Mother had with Granny Komari — she was asking if there was anything she could impart to me in order to further my education. I remember when Granny simply looked me up and down, shook her head, and said something along the lines of 'I regret to inform you that everything I can teach that this girl is willing to learn, you have already imparted to her.' I guess I get the meaning of what she was trying to say, but that's a pretty roundabout way to putting it, don't you think?" Maybe she was only trying to be polite to Kiyoko. She is Komari's liege, after all, no matter how many years separate them now. Kinu frowns and scratches her head. "I don't think that's the case, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ] — there was definitely a subtext there that I caught, but I didn't quite understand. Anyways, while I'm glad that Mother tried to teach me what she knew and succeeded in most of it, I had to learn so much of what I actually use these days from scratch, or from other people. I guess if Granny Komari grew up with Mother, they'd have had similar foundations in their education, even considering the disparity in their social rank. Maybe it'll all be clearer when I figure out what Granny Komari was trying to say." |"Because of the terms of the penance laid on her, Granny Komari doesn't need to eat, but that doesn't stop her from enjoying a bit of youkan every now and then. I don't care much for sweets myself, but I do enjoy growing adzuki beans, so things have gotten to the point where every time I bring her some she just asks what is it I want from her that I feel I need a bribe to go along with my request." Kinu gets a sheepish look on her face and sticks out her tongue at you. "Can't someone do something nice for you out of the goodness of their hearts? H-hey, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ], quit laughing! Cut it out!" Y-you're sorr — no, actually, you're not sorry in the slightest. It really is very obvious when your little fox-daughter is doing something out of the goodness of her heart, and when she's blatantly trying to win someone's favor. If she wants to appear more genuine, she just needs to do a little self-reflection on how she behaves when she's trying to do something nice for Hitoshi. "I don't get it, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]." Of course she doesn't get it. If she did, she wouldn't be in this position in the first place. Besides, it's going to take a lot more than that to pull one over on a wily old fox like Komari who's no doubt seen it all from her many descendants. |"Granny Komari's place may be the largest, safest and most comfortable den in the colonies, but that doesn't change the fact that we're still on the frontier here. Everyone's got to pull their weight, and there's nothing more she hates than a slacker. It's no surprise that kitsune dens around these parts are sized so that everyone reasonably knows everyone else's faces; it's a lot harder for people to skive when you know there's someone who knows your face around. But that's why I go over in the afternoons after my work in the mornings is done." One set of fields just isn't enough for a true enthusiast like her, huh? "Well, I meant more to say that I'm willing to put in my share too, but that works just as well. That, and I'm learning so many things from the way they go about stuff here. And Hitoshi got me a whole bunch of seeds from his own cultivars, and more stuff imported from across the ocean. And I know that Granny Komari's been watching me when she thinks I'm not paying attention. What old woman wouldn't keep an eye on a girl interested in her great-great-grandson?" One who has better things to do in life, presumably. "Ah ha ha. You're so funny, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]." |[flags.KOMARI_FUCKED |As you ask your fox-daughter for her thoughts on Komari, she turns to look at you with some mix of discomfort and exasperation. Taking a deep breath, Kinu rubs her temples before sighing and responding. "[pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]... what in the world did you do? You know how much I loathe gossip, but even I've heard the rumors." What does she mean? You c— You freeze in your tracks, Kinu's eyes cutting straight through you as she stares. Right, evading things isn't going to help... but Kinu's not done. "Look, [pc.mf |dad |mom ], it's really none of my business what you're doing around the den, and I'm perfectly alright with that fact. Heck, it really shouldn't be something I'm even having to think about. But seriously? Granny Komari?[silly | Have you no shame? No morals? | ]" You're a bit taken aback by the fact you're being scolded by your daughter; her tone isn't even flush with anger, but simple disappointment. You can't help but try to defend yourself a bit; as you protest that it's hardly that big of a deal, Kinu buries her head in her hands, groaning with exasperation. "[silly |Why are you like this? Can't you just not fuck every one of my acquaintances for once? |Ugggh... ] I can't believe this. I'm never gonna hear the end of it, am I?" Kinu asks, not expecting an answer. You attempt to console her, saying that at least they're just rumors. After all, Komari made an effort to maintain secrec— "And how well has that been going, given that I'm asking you about it? I—" Kinu pauses, taking a deep breath as she lets her frustration boil off. "Just... please don't go blabbing about it to people. It's awkward enough hearing about this already." [party.has kiyoko |Shifting her attention to Kiyoko, you realize your fox-wife has been silent through all of this. [silly |You barely catch her throwing away a small note, reading "ALL [pc.mf |HIS |HER ] IDEA," before stepping on the discarded piece of paper and smiling innocently |Kiyoko tilts her head quizzically, ] as Kinu speaks once more. "And Mom, please don't blame Granny Komari over it either." With that, |Rubbing her temples, Kinu softly mutters a single sentence, "I can't even blame Mom for this one, either." Before ] she composes herself, desperately moving to change the subject. "Anyways, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ], can we please talk about something else?" |"Granny Komari is a very complex person," your fox-daughter says after a moment's thought. "She's very calm, but also very cheerful at times and yet very sad underneath it is. Which, I suppose, is par for the course for someone who has lived as unnaturally a long life for us kitsune as she has. You get to experience so much... maybe that's why elves are sad all the time, eh?" ] |"You know, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ], I can talk to Granny Komari really easily. She always gets what I'm saying without needing me to repeat it, and half the time she's figured it out before I've even finished speaking. I don't get that way with practically everyone else who's in a position of authority over me, so it makes the times I get to chat with her really, really meaningful. The fact that she kinda likes me also helps a whole bunch — sure, I've still got to be respectful when I'm discussing ideas with her, but she takes my energy instride and doesn't bat an eye. Then again, she did raise Miko, so..." You've had the pleasure of holding conversation with her, and the den matron is a very good listener. That's probably it. "Yeah, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]. It certainly isn't something with me that's making the words flow as smoothly as they do, yeah? Most conversations are just people talking over each other, waiting to have the chance to speak about what they really want to, but Granny Komari really does pay attention, if nothing else. The things that people will reveal if you just let them talk on and on about themselves... heh." ] |[rand |"Matron Komari has been very exacting in my education so far. She has filled in many of the gaps that Mother was not able to, mostly because of the nature of her captivity, but now that I am possessed of greater understanding I feel like this is but smoothing out the edges and coarse corners of my learning. "However, I wish that she would not hold herself so deeply accountable for what happened to Mother. His divine lordship's sentence was harsh, but Matron Komari is truly her own greatest tormentor. Her own guilt gnaws at her so deeply, and I believe that she is using her role in my education in trying to make right some small portion of what she feels is her failure towards Mother." Kiyoko forgave her publicly. Wasn't that enough? "Ah... [pc.mf |Father |Mother ]. The sting of shame reaches deep into the kitsune spirit. [pc.ra kitsune |Even though you are one of us in body, you still have to join us in soul |As much as you are with us, it can still be hard for you to understand ]. Forgive me for speaking plainly, but there is no blunting the truth of this matter. Either way, it is not me or Mother or even his divine lordship who can forgive the den matron; it is herself who must do it." |"Matron Komari is quite the accomplished conversationalist," your daughter informs you in no uncertain terms. "Most conversations are merely people talking over each other's train of thought, waiting to have the chance to speak about what they really want to. Matron Komari listens and engages when appropriate, and this mere small action already places her well ahead in the running; I have managed to improve my ability to communicate so much more by simply watching her in action." Hmm, that's eye-opening. You've spoken with the den matron on numerous occasions, and she's never struck you as anything out of the ordinary. "Well, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ], if you did figure it out, she would not have been very good at it, would she? When you simply remain quiet and let people just talk, you get to learn a lot about them if you pay attention. Doubly so if you know how to ask the right kinds of leading questions. Double that again if you are speaking the kind of language that they're receptive to at the moment. For someone in my position, I need to be able to communicate with all kinds of people, not just my family, and there is so much more to learn." |"Matron Komari and Mother have such a close friendship and tight bond that it has survived all these intervening years; it is as if they had never been separated for centuries. I would consider myself fortunate to be able to attract a retainer who was half as dedicated. Admittedly, options are rather short in the colonies." Call it a hunch, but maybe the two of them didn't start that way, but grew into that kind of relationship. "I meant something approaching that, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ]. Some people have the capability for that kind of reciprocal behavior. Others do not. You have to have something to start with, after all. It is, um... complicated." You'll say. |[flags.KOMARI_FUCKED |As the topic of the den matron comes up, Kinu's attention momentarily drifts. Appearing lost in thought for a moment, recollection dawns on her face as something clicks, and she returns her gaze to you. "Ah... [pc.mf |Father |Mother ], I do hope those 'private matters' you and Matron Komari had to attend to were not too troublesome. [flags.KINU_KILLER_COMPLETED |I understand the current situation is... dire, to say the least, and |Given the urgency she had afforded it, ] I cannot help but grow somewhat concerned, whatever they may have been." Ah. Right. You can assure her, she doesn't have anything to worry about; you and Komari simply needed some privacy for sensitive matters. [party.has kiyoko |[silly |Behind you, Kiyoko snickers, but only smiles sweetly as you turn to face her |As you do so, Kiyoko nods, affirming your statement. "You needn't concern yourself with such frivolities, Kinu; rest assured, it's nothing of import." You catch just the slightest hint of a side-eye as Kiyoko finishes that statement, and you're silently thankful for her covering you ]. Somewhat reassured |Satisfied with your answer ], Kinu sighs with relief, tension evaporating as she relaxes. "I must say, that was quite relieving to hear. With such awful rumors spreading around, I could not help but grow worried—" Wait, rumors? What has she heard? Kinu awkwardly shifts in her seat, caught off guard by your probing. The crack in the mask is quickly sealed, however; softly clearing her throat, your fox-daughter smiles sweetly at you as she replies. "Ah... merely some unsavory gossip, the sort which spreads like a wildfire in the den. I can assure you, none such statements are anything resembling factual; were I to buy into such unsubstantiated claims, I would be a fool." ...So she doesn't believe anything she's heard? Kinu tilts her head in confusion, giving you a quizzical look. "Why would I? Matron Komari has already rebuked such claims when I asked her, as did mother; if you too deny them, clearly they are false. That is simply the way things are." ...You see. You're not about to give her reason to suspect that she's been misled, though you're not sure if she's gullible because she doesn't want to believe it. Giving her a soft nod, Kinu responds in kind, before looking you in the eyes once more. "Now then, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ], had you wished to discuss something else?" |"When I first got to know Matron Komari, it first struck me as a little odd as to why the governor would have been drawn from a priestly clan. At first, I was foolish enough to wonder if his divine lordship was showing favoritism to his own. However, as I have come to understand the spiritual nature of our struggle here that supersedes the material, the logic behind the decision became readily apparent. This entire happenstance is a useful reminder that instead of passing judgement early, I should stop and consider the entire picture first. It has certainly caused me to re-evaluate situations where I otherwise might have not." ] |"I must say, I cannot imagine myself having to live as long as Matron Komari has already, let alone for an indefinite period of time. We are, in large part, defined by our relationships to other people; furthermore, our minds are not designed to pass through the cycle of joy and pain so many times, with each instance framed by a different face. I would go insane after the third generation, perhaps. Maybe it is why the extremely long-lived peoples like various stripes of elves prefer such extensive seclusion, or find peace in the transient nature of their friends from other peoples one way or another. "It is a very cruel punishment, when one looks back upon it. Which, I suppose, fits the crime. Allowing your liege to die on your watch is one of the most terrible things one can do." ] ] "

rows.original: [kinu.isInari |[rand |"Hitoshi's cousin sure is kind of weird. He isn't energetic like Miko is, or laid-back like Hitoshi is; I'd call him more high-strung than anything else." Kinu looks thoughtful a moment, raising a finger to her lips. "To be honest, he scares me a little." How so? He isn't the threatening sort, is he? "No, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. In fact, it's quite the contrary — he's been exceedingly polite to me, and that's what's been bugging me. As far as I understand it, while he may have lived near the capital for a little while, he's never actually been this close to a — well, do I look like a princess to you, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]?" Hah, she'll always be your little princess. "C'mon, seriously. I don't know, having someone bowing and scraping at me kind of feels odd, like I'm someone else altogether. I want to tell him to stop, yet at the same time I kind of know why he's doing it and don't have the heart to tell him to act more informal, because it really does mean a lot to him. And... I have to say, there is a small part of me that does like it..." |"Nakano, he's trying so hard to be a man of culture," Kinu says with a short, barked laugh. "I say that he should just embrace who he is and stick it to the jerks across the ocean. He's trying to please folks who have it out for him, and no matter what he does he's never going to be able to win their approval even if he manages to dig himself out of the hole they dropped him in. The only way he could ever hope to achieve that is if the Emperor himself were to personally slap a commendation on his tails. Fat chance of that ever happening. "Stop trying to win approval from snobs an ocean away, and care for those who're right next to you! That's what I'd do if I were in his position, anyway. Yeah, I understand he's got a code and a way to follow and all, but at this point I'd have long since grown disillusioned with it especially with a mountain of evidence that the other side isn't holding up to their end of the bargain. Talking to him is like hammering your head against a rock, I tell you." |"So the other day, Hitoshi's cousin went and showed me a poem he had written, and asked for my opinion on it since I was educated by my mother and all..." A poem? Ah, of course. That had to be Nakano — Hitoshi just has so many cousins, it can get a little hard to keep track of them all. "Anyways, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], since he asked for my honest opinion, I gave it to him: it was a pretty awful piece of doggerel and I was doing better than that when I was eight. That kinda took the wind out of his sails out hard — he visibly deflated, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It made me kind of worried for him for a bit, but he just turned and walked away. "Like, I get that he kind of respects me because I'm supposed to be the closest thing to an actual princess or something here in the colonies, being Mother's heir and all, right? Yeah sure, it's kind of crushing for me to put him down like that, but at the same time you really shouldn't ask questions you're not prepared to get the answer to. It's not like enough people haven't told him the truth to his face already, so if he was looking for validation from me I guess he was looking in the wrong place." |"Hitoshi was telling me more about his samurai cousin the other day again, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], and the more I hear him speak the more I can't quite wrap my head about the situation. Sure, it was bad to begin with, but he's only making it worse for himself. For example, while it's true that Granny Komari doesn't have the most illustrious of pasts, she's nevertheless still colonial governor. She could pull all kinds of strings to at least help Nakano with his issues with being underfunded and maybe being understaffed, but he's so obstinate that he won't have any of it. Would be dishonorable and shameful, you see. "It's gotten to the point where Hitoshi's really the only person who's willing to give him the time of day, and thank the gods that all Nakano can really ask for him is another meal. Man looks like he could use it. It's not that other people aren't willing to help, it's that he's not going to accept help that doesn't fall into line with what his ideals state he can accept, and that really cuts out a lot of what most of us can do for him. You know what they say — that tragedies are almost always partly of the victim's own making. If he won't help us help him, then I don't think any of us are going to be bearing guilty consciences when we walk away from the disaster he's shaping up to be." |"Nakano goes back over the ocean through the torii gate every so often," Kinu says. "Ostensibly for him to liaise with folks in the Old Country for provisioning and services that he can't acquire here, but I also think he likes going there just because, visiting his distant relatives when he can. "You ever have a feeling of longing for a place you've never seen before and maybe don't know even exists, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? I think that's what got the guy. He was born here, but doesn't feel like this place is his home, you know? It's a pretty awful thing to happen to anyone, and I guess it comes with living in a land which isn't fully ours, you know? Even so, I'm not sure it's going to do him any good if he does get his wish; he's not going to be looked upon very kindly even if he were to find a permanent position in the Old Country. Sometimes, what you want isn't what you need, but in this case I really, really don't think it can be helped in the slightest. Some people are made to suffer, I guess." ] |[var0 |"Before I leave for my lessons and work with Matron Komari every day, I am sure to pack a lunch for Nakano before I depart," your fox-daughter informs you proudly. "He is so driven that I feel like it is my duty to ensure that he gets at least one decent meal in him every day; that, and I enjoy watching him eat. To have someone who appreciates not just the taste, but the color, arrangement and other aesthetics of something as deceptively simple as a boxed meal — ah, it is almost as good as one of his paintings. Mikoto says that I should use the extra space in the box to put more substance on her cousin's skinny bones, but I think Nakano is right when he says that food is meant to sustain more than the body. The spirit, senses and mind must be engaged, too." That's something only a true romantic could say. Although... how does Miko know what's in those lunches of hers? "Oh, she is always trying to wheedle a bite from me on the way. Of course I do not give her any, since even if it were not meant for Nakano a single piece missing would mar the harmony with which the meal is arranged in the lunchbox. That does not stop her from trying, mischievous as she is." |"So many people have given up on Nakano, even his own family save Hitoshi, but I feel that this is terribly unfair to him. He has been betrayed in the deepest manner by those whom he still holds the deepest respect and unquestioning obedience for; where others would have deviated from the way, he still remains steadfast in his belief. The situation may appear hopeless to even Matron Komari, but I refuse to admit defeat; those who shy away from what appears insurmountable do not go beyond their limits, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I know there is an honorable way out of the mess he has found himself in; I merely have to find it with him. I... I may be the last one who still believes in Nakano, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I cannot find it in myself to take that away from him." |"Nakano is not stupid, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], no matter what they all say. One does not delve so deeply into a classical education without a brain in that skull to back it up. Nor is he uncreative — I have seen his paintings. I know he can write more than doggerel; he just needs to unstopper whatever it is that's been holding him back all these years. It's not as if he hasn't a good command of language, after all." Now, now, back up a moment. Who's "they"? Kinu sighs in exasperation, a most uncharacteristic move coming from her. "Everyone, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Well, everyone except Hitoshi, but it is not as if he can do much about Nakano's situation. I am the only one with the ability and willingness to be able to change this for the better. The man is hurting so much, and great swathes of what he has believed in have been betrayed by the people from whom should have used his unwavering and absolute obedience for good. I... I will not join them!" Kinu... maybe if everyone else is saying something else, it might not be the case that she's the only one in all of Savarra that has this stunning insight about the man she's infatuated with, over all the other people who've known him all their lives. Sure, he may have been dealt a terrible hand by those who should have helped him, but a tragedy is often at least partly one's own fault and — "I. Don't. Care." Kinu is usually so soft-spoken and neither has she raised her voice in the slightest, but you felt her throw every scrap of her presence behind her words there. Now that's your little girl. "How can even you not understand this, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]? I quite simply do not care what landed him in this situation save for how helpful it is in finding a way to get him out with his honor and life intact! Everyone keeps on bringing it up, only as a justification for why they are leaving him in the lurch and why I should do the same thing, too! And if you saw everyone who you were supposed to have strong ties with abandoning you, would you have the will to keep on struggling against impossible odds, or not? It is heartbreaking that the only person who has stood by him the longest is Hitoshi, who is the least able to help his cousin in any meaningful manner! "I will hear no more of this. This conversation is over." |"Every day when I am done with helping Matron Komari, I like to sit down with Nakano and work with him on his art, by lamplight of course. There is something about the flickering flame that puts one in the mood for verse... "But he is improving, slowly but steadily. I do not lecture or teach him, merely sit by his side and give my honest opinion when asked to comment, and his waka truly is less and less like doggerel by the day. I showed one of his pieces to Miyuki, and she asked if it was written by [kiyoko.numKits 8|one of my little brothers|one of the den's children]!" That's an improvement from where he was. Wow. To soldier on in the face of such garish and early failures must have taken a lot of determination; a lesser man would have been long since discouraged by now. "Where others have given up on him, I see so much in Nakano, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Mother agrees with me, too. If I do not falter, than neither will he. As silly and romantic as it may sound... I truly believe that by standing by him with my mere presence, it gives him a reason to work harder and make headway. His education may have been harsh and the demands that are now being made of him are intended to break his will for the amusement of courtiers across the ocean, but there is still value in knowing that there is someone who cares enough about you to ensure you eat a beautifully-prepared lunch every day." |"Matron Komari and I had a discussion about Nakano's ambitions earlier in the day," Kinu tells you, her ears lowering a little. "She... she does not wholly approve of us being together, but since Mother is in favor of it she is going to defer to her liege. I... I am conflicted about this." Hm. "I do not want my grandmother-in-law to resent us being together — maybe if I can prove to her that she is wrong about the whole situation, she might reconsider in the light of new evidence. At the same time, she says that his ambitious is dangerous; it ties him too much to material things and the world, risks too much shame... "I would agree if he lusted over power, wealth, status or any of the worldly follies someone in his station might have been tempted by. But... Nakano has always only wanted to prove that we as colonial-born can be helpful and useful to the Cherry Blossom Throne. That is my goal for the future as well in hoping to be able to represent, in some small measure, the people in the colonies. Am I possessed of too much ambition, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]? Am I bringing shame down upon my person and my clan? "It's not wrong to say that we are driven, but to what ends... I just feel like our intentions and the fruits thereof are being unfairly maligned, and then immediately after I can only but regret that surge of contentiousness... oh, what a to-do." Yes, he's definitely rubbing off on her. As they say, when a couple spends enough time together, they start looking and acting like each other. "Father!" ] ]
rows.translation: [kinu.isInari |[rand |仁的表弟确实有点奇怪。他既没有米可那样的活力，也不像仁那样随和；我觉得他更应该被形容为容易紧张的人。纪久若有所思地停顿了一下，然后把一根手指放在嘴唇上。说实话，他确实让我有点害怕。 怎么会这样？他并不是那种会威胁别人的人，对吧？ 不， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]事实上，恰恰相反——他对我一直都非常有礼貌，而这反而让我感到困扰。据我所知，虽然他曾经在首都附近居住过一段时间，但他其实从未如此接近过……嗯，该怎么说呢？看对你来说，就像一位公主一样。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]？" 哈，她永远都会是你的小公主。 拜托，说真的。我不知道，别人对我这种阿谀奉承的态度让我感觉很奇怪，就好像我变成了另一个人一样。我想让他停下来，但同时我又明白他为什么这么做，所以也没有勇气让他别这么拘谨，因为这对他来说确实意义重大。而且……我得承认，我得承认，我内心确实有一部分喜欢这种感觉…… |中野，他真的在努力成为一个有文化的人啊。小娟发出一声短促而刺耳的笑声说道。我认为他应该接受真实的自己，然后去对付那些在太平洋对岸的混蛋。他一直在努力取悦那些与他为敌的人，但无论他怎么做，都永远无法获得他们的认可——即使他设法摆脱了他们设下的陷阱。唯一有可能让他实现这一目标的方式，就是让皇帝亲自给他颁发奖状。不过，这种可能性实在微乎其微。那个这种事情根本不可能发生。 别再试图去取悦那些远在异国他乡的势利小人了，多关心那些就在你身边的人吧！如果我处在他的位置，也会这么做。当然，我理解他有自己的原则和行事方式，但在这种情况下，我早就对这一切感到失望了——尤其是有那么多证据表明，对方并没有履行他们的承诺。跟他说话，简直就像用头去撞石头，真的。 |前几天，仁的表弟拿来给我看他写的一首诗，还问我意见，毕竟我是由我母亲教育的…… At the same time, she says that his ambitious is dangerous; it ties him too much to material things and the world, risks too much shame... "I would agree if he lusted over power, wealth, status or any of the worldly follies someone in his station might have been tempted by. But... Nakano has always only wanted to prove that we as colonial-born can be helpful and useful to the Cherry Blossom Throne. That is my goal for the future as well in hoping to be able to represent, in some small measure, the people in the colonies. Am I possessed of too much ambition, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]? Am I bringing shame down upon my person and my clan? "It's not wrong to say that we are driven, but to what ends... I just feel like our intentions and the fruits thereof are being unfairly maligned, and then immediately after I can only but regret that surge of contentiousness... oh, what a to-do." Yes, he's definitely rubbing off on her. As they say, when a couple spends enough time together, they start looking and acting like each other. "Father!" ] ] "

A pretty meal is made for everyone, a big, filling one is made for Hitoshi. That's a lot more meaningful, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." It's hard to disagree. Although... how does Miko know what's in the lunches? "Oh, she hangs around us and tries to wheedle a bite from Hitoshi every now and then. "Ehhh... that's the sort of useful-but-not-really-useful advice Mai's prone to giving." |"It wasn't so long ago that I challenged Hitoshi to who could grow the better daikon — again," your fox-daughter informs you with a snort.
