rows.raw: " [kinu.isInari |[rand |"Before I go off to Granny Komari's every day, I make sure to pack a lunchbox for Hitoshi before I leave," your fox-daughter says proudly. "Miko always says that it's not pretty enough and that I could focus more on the presentation to show him that I care, but I don't agree with that at all. Hitoshi barely looks at his lunch before he scarfs it down, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom] — I think it's much better to show him I care by packing a big and tasty lunch instead of a pretty one, appeal to the aspects of a meal he cares about and not those that he ignores. A pretty meal is made for everyone, a big, filling one is made for Hitoshi. That's a lot more meaningful, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." It's hard to disagree. Although... how does Miko know what's in the lunches? "Oh, she hangs around us and tries to wheedle a bite from Hitoshi every now and then. Worse, he indulges Miko because she's his cousin and encourages her to keep on doing it... it's always me who has to shoo her and her appetite away." |Your fox-daughter shifts her eyes to and fro, then gives you a silly grin. "I... I really like hugging Hitoshi, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. He's so much bigger and taller than me, but that just makes it all the better. I like to sneak up on him when he's working or sitting down with the lunch I made him and just wrapping my arms about his body and pressing myself against —" Whoa, whoa, you don't need to hear all of that! [party.has kiyoko |"Our daughter is a grown woman and is experiencing womanly desires," Kiyoko says with a small, resigned sigh. "I just wish... no, I will not fight with you about it in front of your [pc.mf|father|mother], Kinu. [pc.HeShe] deserves better. Not now." ] Kinu sticks her tongue out at you, and you notice the beginnings of her mother's trademark weapons-grade blush on her cheeks. "He never hugs me back, though. Just either stands there and continues what he's doing, or tells me that what I'm doing is dangerous and that I could get hurt. I don't get it, really — I'm doing what Miko's telling me to, and she never has any problems seducing anyone! If anything, what I'm doing is getting negative results; isn't it right that when a man and a woman are together, the man is expected to be the avaricious one? Oh no, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], could it be that I simply lack the charm and wiles —" What you honestly think is that she just needs to calm down and take a deep breath. People come in all stripes, after all; even a rock can be worn down, one just needs to find the correct angle to strike it from. "Ehhh... that's the sort of useful-but-not-really-useful advice Mai's prone to giving." |"It wasn't so long ago that I challenged Hitoshi to who could grow the better daikon — again," your fox-daughter informs you with a snort. "Size, weight, color, aroma — you name it, it'd be included in the judging. Turns out that we didn't need anyone to judge, because one look at the thing he came up with and I had to instantly admit he'd beaten me again. It's just like playing shogi with Mai — I can already guess the result before we've even begun, but I'm not going to pass up the challenge because this might be the first time I outdo either of them. At this point, it's more a challenge against myself than it is against them, to be honest..." |[party.has kiyoko |Padding up to you, Kinu leans forward and whispers into your ear, occasionally casting glances at her mother who is very definitely not looking at the both of you. "Hey, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I've got something to tell you, okay?" Sure, so spit it out. "But not right now. Not when, um, there're too many people around." You see one of Kiyoko's ears twitch at that, and instinctively swivel in your direction. That's not lost on Kinu, either, who winces. "Later, okay? When the fields aren't so crowded." |"I'm not completely sure I should be telling you this, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], but I've got to tell someone or else I think I'm going to explode. I can't tell Mother because she'd just get mad, I can't tell Granny Komari because she'd just brag about it to Mother, who'd just get mad, and I can't tell Miko or Mai because they'd just tease me to no end. That, and I'm definitely not telling Hitoshi himself...!" All right, then. What's got your little fox-daughter all in a tizzy like this? "You've got to promise not to tell anyone, even Mother!" You promise. Now, out with it. "Like, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], when I'm up against Hitoshi and leaning on him, I feel pretty nice and secure. So much so that I don't want to move at all and just stay there until it's time to go home. I don't think he ever notices when I do that, I don't think he ever notices anything, to be honest. But I do, and... um..." at this point, Kinu's blush has extended all the way from the bridge of her nose, through her cheeks and down her neck before disappearing into the furred collar of her work clothes. Yes, she's truly taking after her mother in more ways than one. "I feel so safe and happy just by being next to him, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. He has that kind of gravitas about him, and he loves doing the same things that I do. Miko makes fun of me, saying that I'm short enough to be his daughter, but even she can't bring herself to tease us in earnest. I just — eh —" There goes Kinu, stuttering and freezing up again. Ah, a maiden finding her first love. Hopefully it'll be the last, too. ] |"Hitoshi has what they call a stone face, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I think I'm more astute than most, but even I get it wrong as to whether he's smiling or frowning half the time. Miko and Mai have no problems telling apart his moods, though, but then again they've been with him for all of his life. "To be fair, I kind of like the challenge. He's not a dead rock, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], he just needs someone to understand what he's about and then he's as easy to read as anyone else. We're all so used to looking over our shoulders and digging for deeper meanings to remember that there're people in this world who say what they mean, as few as they are." ] |[rand |Kinu looks worried and raises a hand to her cheek. "I do not enjoy speaking ill of other people, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], but the truth is that Hitoshi scares me a little. He towers over me so terribly every time Matron Komari sends me to him on business, and I cannot help but feel at least a little intimidated by the man, even if I do not let it show. When I look at him, I cannot help but be reminded of a bear, or perhaps a giant dog on two legs. "He... he cannot help being who he is, and I cannot blame him for that, but as much as I can try to control my instinctive reaction to him, it nevertheless exists. While I am sure he is a very quiet and gentle person unless provoked and I will endeavor to be polite in all my dealings with him... I..." You're seeing where this is going. "It is like seeing a dog in the wild, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Kinu looks appropriately ashamed. "I cannot help it. He is rather scary." |"Hitoshi moves very silently despite his size, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Once, I was at the shrine making my devotions when I turned to find him behind me! Of course, Mikoto informed me that he had been standing there all the while and I was the one who had gotten between him and Keros' likeness while he was about to make an offering! "It sounds strange, I know, and it is strange to me. How can a man like that remain there and yet be all but invisible? The shrine's interior is not a big place, and yet I managed to miss him despite the fact that he was standing in what would have been my path if I had entered two steps to the left! I do not know, truth be told. Maybe he is a ninja; historically they would take the guises of common folk like farmers, but that is quite the stretch for a peaceable man like him." Perhaps, as crazy as this sounds... she just didn't notice him? "He is a giant, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. One would imagine that being that large and tall would preclude him from easily evading notice. And yet... the evidence is there. It makes no sense." |"Hitoshi possesses what we call a 'stone face', [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. That means about what it purports to — he is a man who does not wear his heart on his sleeve, and can be inscrutable to those who are not practiced in the ways of reading others." Such as her, you take it. "That, and Mikoto and Miyuki, although I suppose their ability comes more from their familiarity with their cousin and their unique way of seeing the world. At a first glance, how he appears when he is happy is about the same as when he is content, or frustrated. The trick is to forget the details and concentrate on the big picture. I will say that if nothing else, he has been a good source of practice for me." |"Do I respect Hitoshi? Well yes, I do. He clearly is someone who has carved out a niche for himself amongst the people of the den, and is content with his lot in life. There is something to be said for the attitude with which he approaches his dealings, after all, and he is an excellent example of someone who clearly garners respect and some small amount of authority without any formalised position; at most he might be considered Matron Komari's descendant, but that is hardly worth as much as one might imagine here. "I just believe that his way is not suited for everyone, just as others' ways are certainly not suited for him. One can certainly appreciate his industriousness and quiet temerity without having to also endorse that listlessness that pervades his entire being. There is so much untapped potential here; I truly do believe that one but needs to reach out and seize it to be rewarded." |"Not too long ago, I discovered that the clothes that Hitoshi wears have quite the interesting history — they were originally worn by monks while they were about simple, repetitive chores that were said to be conducive to a calm and clear state of mind. They did not get out into the general populace as work clothing until about a century or two ago. I wonder if he knows any of that, or he simply wears it because it is comfortable and allows him a good range of motion. With someone like him, it can be hard to tell." |"With someone as good-natured as Hitoshi, it would be trivially easy for someone small-minded to abuse his affable and kind nature. Mikoto teases him all the time, but thankfully it has never become any more of an issue for him. She and Nakano watch out for Hitoshi, so the man has some more... ah, sensible people looking out for his welfare, but it is nevertheless still a little worrying, is it not? If I were around Matron Komari's place more, I might join in the effort, too, but as things are I keep an eye on him when I am around." ] ] "

rows.original: [kinu.isInari |[rand |"I've never been afraid of trying anything new in my life, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], so I didn't even think of saying no when Taka handed me his latest experiment to try. I can't really say whether it was good or bad, though, although it did what strong liquor was supposed to do and put a fire in my chest and belly. He looked kind of disappointed when I told him there wasn't anything special about it, and I guess that makes sense. Kind of a letdown to try out something new only to figure out halfway that it's just the same old packaged in a shiny new bottle, isn't it?" You... suppose so? "I told him that if he actually came up with something that happened to be thoughtfully creative instead of throwing together any old thing that happened to go bad, I'd consider more of it. I don't know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. From the look on his face, he might've been glad that I was willing to be level with him, no matter how harsh I was. On the other hand, maybe I was being a little too harsh, but... bleh. Nothing's going to stop me from speaking my mind. Either Taka stops offering me his experiments, or he shapes up; both results are good with me." |"[pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I don't suppose you could talk to Taka for a bit and give him some pointers on where to find good loot? Like, you haven't been doing this for that long, and you're always coming back home laden with all kinds of stuff from your adventures. He, on the other hand, has never come back with anything remarkable, given the gossip in the den. So... maybe help him become a bit less useless or something? It's kinda awkward when you're always the treasure-seeker and never the treasure-finder even once, you know." |"So Taka dropped by the other day when I was on the other side and asked if he could have a bit of the rice from my fields for use in his experiments. I wasn't entirely sure if he was intending to tease me because I don't grow the kind used in making liquor, but he insisted that since my vegetables were certainly quite legendary there ought to be something he could do with my rice." There are... different kinds of rice? They all look the same to you. "Of course there are, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]! You wouldn't use table grapes for wine-making, would you? Nor would you serve wine grapes fresh! It's the same principle, you know!" Phew, okay. So what did she do? "I gave him a small sack and told him this was all I was going to spare. To be perfectly honest, I mostly did it just so he'd leave me alone, but now I'm kind of regretting it. What's the saying the locals have? If you pay the orc to go away, that just means you'll never be rid of him? Something like that? Ah well, I guess I ought to have thought through my actions a little more, huh [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? Maybe next time. "Then again... I'll admit to being a little curious as to what kind of unholy menace he'll manage to crate with the stuff I gave him. It ought to be good." |"The other day, Taka asked me if I could see about bartering for some — uh, native starchy tubers, I think they're called potatoes — from the people going in and out of Hawkethorne. I asked him what I was going to get for taking such a risk for him, and he said I could observe how he went about his business. "Eh, really [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I don't know if he understands what it means to let me observe. Or maybe he does, ahahaha. Either way, I was thinking of getting some actual meat for the next couple of weeks, so I guess it won't be hard for me to lug an extra sack of potatoes back home, I guess. You have to wonder what he'll manage to make from these, the guy says he can ferment anything. Someday I'll figure out if that's true... someday." |"You know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I guess Taka is a little weird, but he's not as weird as some of the other people about at Granny Komari's. He's just a drunken sot most of the time, which is fairly harmless most of the time, I suppose. The colonies have been a dumping ground for a good chunk of the Old Country's rejects for a couple of generations now; so by the measure of things mere drunkenness isn't too bad of a vice to tolerate, all things considered." ] |[rand |"While it is standard protocol to consolidate most goods in the storehouse before distribution in response to requisition, Takahiro enjoys doing the exact opposite, going as far as to increase his production on the sly so that the shortfall does not raise suspicion. I... do not enjoy this lack of personal accountability in the least. It throws the books into disorder, which is the least of my concerns — the surplus finds its way into the hands of people who should not have it, especially people I care about." She doesn't say it, but of course you know she means Nakano. "I only wish something concrete could be done about the wastrel, but Matron Komari is fairly reticent about the whole issue. I wonder why she is hesitating to follow up with punitive action, but I suppose it is not my place to ask, either." |"Takahiro offered me a drink the other day; I refused on the basic principle of it all. Not only do I wish to keep my faculties about myself and in pristine working condition should I need them on short notice, but spending your life in a perpetual state of half-drunkenness like he does is shameful to an unbelievable degree. Mother drinks cold liquor while having a hot bath sometimes, but only exceedingly rarely. "Besides, I suppose I will be pregnant almost all the time in the future, so it behooves me to not develop a taste for alcohol in any shape or form. A little extreme, but it pays to be careful when it comes to one's future. Regardless, I certainly will not tolerate any such personalities in any future den that may come under my jurisdiction. While intoxicants have their purpose in easing the hardships of life on the frontier and keeping morale up, I only wish the suppliers thereof could simply stop conforming to all the worst stereotypes with saddening regularity." |"I cannot personally attest to the veracity of this gossip, but apparently Takahiro goes missing for years on end, presumably in search of some treasure or the other. He then returns as if nothing has happened, and expects to slide back into his old position and everyone to ignore the fact that he has been gone and not contributing, with nothing to show for it. The sheer nerve of the man sets my teeth on edge on top of everything else he does!" |"Several days ago, Takahiro had the nerve to ask me for several kinds of produce from the fields here, promising a number of jars of liquor in exchange. The cheek of the man[kiyoko.numKits 12| — he knows that there are mostly children living here]! Of course, I sent him away, and told him in no uncertain terms that if he wanted to get my future husband any more drunk he'd have to do it without my assistance! I do not think it sank through to him, and I would be surprised if anything sank through into the liquor-pickled brain of his to begin with." |"I do not like to write people off, but it is quite impossible to help someone who does not wish, even at some unconscious level, to be aided. Of course, considering my antipathy towards Takahiro, I suppose my judgement is clouded as to his salvageability. Just as well that I am not the one expected to enact it in any way, shape or form — as much as I try to see the good in everyone, this is a man who actively revels in his status as an inebriated sot and a social negative. I will reiterate that when I have my own den, I will not tolerate behavior of this kind in the least. This is what gets you sent to the colonies back across the ocean, and now that we are in the colonies... haa." ] ]
rows.translation: [kinu.isInari |[rand |在我的生活中，我从来都不害怕尝试任何新事物。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]所以当贵弘把他的最新实验成果交给我让我尝试时，我甚至都没有考虑过要拒绝。不过，我实在很难说这个实验到底是好还是坏——虽然它确实起到了烈酒该有的效果，让我的胸口和腹部感到一阵灼热。当我告诉他这个实验并没有什么特别之处时，他看起来有点失望，我想这也是情有可原的。毕竟，尝试一些新东西，结果却发现它只不过是用一个闪亮的新包装重新包装过的老东西，这种感觉确实会让人有些失望，不是吗？ 你……是这么认为的吗？ 我告诉他，如果他真的能想出一些有创意、经过深思熟虑的想法，而不是随便拼凑一些碰巧失败的东西，我会认真考虑他的提议。不过我也不确定[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]从他脸上的表情来看，他或许很高兴我愿意与他坦诚相对，无论我说的话有多严厉。另一方面，也许我也有些过于太严厉点吧，不过……唉，也没什么能阻止我说出自己的想法。要么塔卡不再让我参与他的实验，要么他就改过自新；这两种结果对我来说都无所谓。 |"[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我想你能不能和贵弘聊一会儿，给他一些建议，告诉他去哪里能找到好的战利品？毕竟，你也不是每天都做这种事情的吧那个你总是长途跋涉，每次回家时都会带着从冒险中获得的各种各样的东西。而另一方面，根据窝里的那些闲言碎语，他从来没带回来过什么特别的东西。所以……也许你可以帮他变得不那么无用吧？毕竟，如果你总是那个寻找宝藏的人，而他却一次都没有找到过任何东西，这样确实有点尴尬，你知道的。 |前几天，当我不在家的时候，贵弘顺便来了，问他能不能从我田里拿一些米用来做他的实验。我当时不太确定他是不是在开玩笑，因为我自己种的米并不是用来酿酒的，但他坚持说，既然我的蔬菜已经非常有名了，那么我的米也应该不错吧。某个东西他正好需要我的米。 有……各种各样的大米吗？在你们看来，它们全都长得一样啊。 属于过程确实存在。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]！ 你总不会用鲜葡萄来酿酒吧？同样，也不会把新鲜的酿酒葡萄直接端上桌来享用吧？道理是一样的，你懂的！ 呼，好吧。那么她到底做了什么呢？ 我给了他一个小袋子，告诉他这就是我所能提供的全部帮助了。说实话，我这么做主要是为了让他别再来烦我，但现在我有点后悔了。当地人不是有句俗话吗？‘如果你用钱让兽人离开，那就意味着你永远摆脱不了他’，大概是这个意思吧？唉，看来我当初真应该再仔细考虑一下自己的行为啊。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]？也许下次吧。 不过说起来……我确实有点好奇，他用我给他的那些东西能制造出什么样的邪恶威胁来。应该会挺有意思的吧。 |前几天，贵弘问我是否可以想办法从那些经常来来去去鹰棘镇的人那里换来一些——嗯，应该是那种本土的淀粉类块茎植物，我记得它们叫土豆。我问他，为我帮他承担这样的风险，我能得到什么回报，他说我可以观察他是怎么办事的。 呃，真的吗？ [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我不知道他是否明白允许我观察意味着什么。或许他明白吧，哈哈哈。不管怎样，我正在考虑在接下来的几周里买些真正的肉来吃，所以我想，把一袋土豆带回家应该不会太难吧。真不知道他会用这些土豆做出什么来——他说他什么都能发酵。总有一天，我会弄清楚这是否是真的……总有一天。 |你知道， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我想，高田确实有点古怪，但比起麻里奶奶家里的那些人来说，他还算不算太奇怪吧。他大部分时间都只是个醉醺醺的酒鬼，不过我想，这种行为通常也不会造成什么严重的后果。这几代以来，这些殖民地一直都是旧国那些被社会抛弃的人们的落脚处；所以相对来说，仅仅是个酒鬼这样的缺点，也还算可以忍受吧。 ] |[rand |按照常规做法，应该在接到需求订单后先将大部分货物存入仓库再进行分发，但贵弘却偏偏反其道而行之，甚至还会偷偷增加产量，以确保不会出现货物不足的情况从而引起怀疑。我……实在无法忍受这种缺乏个人责任感的做法。这种做法让整个库存管理系统变得混乱不堪，而这还不是我最担心的地方——真正令人担忧的是，那些多余的货物最终会落入那些本不该得到它们的人手中。不是我受够了，尤其是那些我在乎的人。 她没有明说，但你们当然知道她指的是中野。 我真希望能针对那个挥霍无度的人采取一些具体的措施，但麻里女主管对整个事情表现得相当沉默寡言。我不明白她为什么迟迟不采取惩罚行动，不过我想，这也不是我该去追问的事情。 |前几天，隆弘请我喝酒，但我基于一些基本原则拒绝了。首先，我必须保持自己的清醒状态，以便在需要时能够立刻做出反应；其次，像他那样长期处于半醉的状态，实在是一种极其可耻的行为。母亲有时会在洗热水澡的时候喝一点冷酒，但这种情况也非常少见。 另外，我想在未来的日子里，我几乎都会处于怀孕的状态，因此我最好不要养成对任何形式的酒精的依赖。这个要求可能有点极端，但在关系到自己的未来时，谨慎总是没有坏处的。无论如何，我绝不会容忍任何未来属于我管辖范围内的地方出现这种人。虽然酒类饮品在缓解边疆地区的艰苦生活、提振士气方面确实有一定作用，但我只希望那些提供酒类的人能够不再如此频繁地符合那些令人沮丧的负面刻板印象。" |我个人无法证实这种传言的真实性，但显然，贵弘会连续多年失踪，大概是在寻找什么宝藏之类的东西。然后他又会若无其事地回来，还指望能重新回到原来的位置上，希望大家都能忽略他这段时间不在、也没有做出任何贡献的事实。除了他做的那些事之外，他这种厚颜无耻的态度真的让我感到非常愤怒！ |几天前，贵弘竟然敢向我讨要这里田里种的几种农产品，还承诺会用几罐酒作为交换。这家伙真是厚颜无耻[kiyoko.numKits 12| — 他知道这里住的主要是儿童。]当然，我把他打发走了，并且明确告诉他：如果他还想让我未来的丈夫喝得更醉的话，就必须不让我帮忙才行！我觉得他根本没听进去，而且说实话，我觉得他那被酒精浸透的脑袋根本不可能理解这些话。 |我并不喜欢轻易否定别人，但对于那些在潜意识里就不愿意接受帮助的人来说，确实很难提供任何帮助。当然，考虑到我对贵弘的厌恶之情，我的判断或许有些偏颇，无法客观地判断他是否还有被拯救的可能。幸好并不是由我来以任何方式去执行这件事——尽管我总是努力去看到每个人身上的优点，但这个男人却显然乐于享受自己作为一个酗酒之徒、一个对社会毫无贡献之人的身份。我再次强调，一旦我有了自己的地盘，我绝对不会容忍这种行为。正是这种行为才会让人被流放到大洋彼岸的殖民地去，而现在我们既然已经在殖民地了……哈。 ] ]
rows.raw: " [kinu.isInari |[rand |"I've never been afraid of trying anything new in my life, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], so I didn't even think of saying no when Taka handed me his latest experiment to try. I can't really say whether it was good or bad, though, although it did what strong liquor was supposed to do and put a fire in my chest and belly. He looked kind of disappointed when I told him there wasn't anything special about it, and I guess that makes sense. Kind of a letdown to try out something new only to figure out halfway that it's just the same old packaged in a shiny new bottle, isn't it?" You... suppose so? "I told him that if he actually came up with something that happened to be thoughtfully creative instead of throwing together any old thing that happened to go bad, I'd consider more of it. I don't know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. From the look on his face, he might've been glad that I was willing to be level with him, no matter how harsh I was. On the other hand, maybe I was being a little too harsh, but... bleh. Nothing's going to stop me from speaking my mind. Either Taka stops offering me his experiments, or he shapes up; both results are good with me." |"[pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I don't suppose you could talk to Taka for a bit and give him some pointers on where to find good loot? Like, you haven't been doing this for that long, and you're always coming back home laden with all kinds of stuff from your adventures. He, on the other hand, has never come back with anything remarkable, given the gossip in the den. So... maybe help him become a bit less useless or something? It's kinda awkward when you're always the treasure-seeker and never the treasure-finder even once, you know." |"So Taka dropped by the other day when I was on the other side and asked if he could have a bit of the rice from my fields for use in his experiments. I wasn't entirely sure if he was intending to tease me because I don't grow the kind used in making liquor, but he insisted that since my vegetables were certainly quite legendary there ought to be something he could do with my rice." There are... different kinds of rice? They all look the same to you. "Of course there are, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]! You wouldn't use table grapes for wine-making, would you? Nor would you serve wine grapes fresh! It's the same principle, you know!" Phew, okay. So what did she do? "I gave him a small sack and told him this was all I was going to spare. To be perfectly honest, I mostly did it just so he'd leave me alone, but now I'm kind of regretting it. What's the saying the locals have? If you pay the orc to go away, that just means you'll never be rid of him? Something like that? Ah well, I guess I ought to have thought through my actions a little more, huh [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? Maybe next time. "Then again... I'll admit to being a little curious as to what kind of unholy menace he'll manage to crate with the stuff I gave him. It ought to be good." |"The other day, Taka asked me if I could see about bartering for some — uh, native starchy tubers, I think they're called potatoes — from the people going in and out of Hawkethorne. I asked him what I was going to get for taking such a risk for him, and he said I could observe how he went about his business. "Eh, really [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I don't know if he understands what it means to let me observe. Or maybe he does, ahahaha. Either way, I was thinking of getting some actual meat for the next couple of weeks, so I guess it won't be hard for me to lug an extra sack of potatoes back home, I guess. You have to wonder what he'll manage to make from these, the guy says he can ferment anything. Someday I'll figure out if that's true... someday." |"You know, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I guess Taka is a little weird, but he's not as weird as some of the other people about at Granny Komari's. He's just a drunken sot most of the time, which is fairly harmless most of the time, I suppose. The colonies have been a dumping ground for a good chunk of the Old Country's rejects for a couple of generations now; so by the measure of things mere drunkenness isn't too bad of a vice to tolerate, all things considered." ] |[rand |"While it is standard protocol to consolidate most goods in the storehouse before distribution in response to requisition, Takahiro enjoys doing the exact opposite, going as far as to increase his production on the sly so that the shortfall does not raise suspicion. I... do not enjoy this lack of personal accountability in the least. It throws the books into disorder, which is the least of my concerns — the surplus finds its way into the hands of people who should not have it, especially people I care about." She doesn't say it, but of course you know she means Nakano. "I only wish something concrete could be done about the wastrel, but Matron Komari is fairly reticent about the whole issue. I wonder why she is hesitating to follow up with punitive action, but I suppose it is not my place to ask, either." |"Takahiro offered me a drink the other day; I refused on the basic principle of it all. Not only do I wish to keep my faculties about myself and in pristine working condition should I need them on short notice, but spending your life in a perpetual state of half-drunkenness like he does is shameful to an unbelievable degree. Mother drinks cold liquor while having a hot bath sometimes, but only exceedingly rarely. "Besides, I suppose I will be pregnant almost all the time in the future, so it behooves me to not develop a taste for alcohol in any shape or form. A little extreme, but it pays to be careful when it comes to one's future. Regardless, I certainly will not tolerate any such personalities in any future den that may come under my jurisdiction. While intoxicants have their purpose in easing the hardships of life on the frontier and keeping morale up, I only wish the suppliers thereof could simply stop conforming to all the worst stereotypes with saddening regularity." |"I cannot personally attest to the veracity of this gossip, but apparently Takahiro goes missing for years on end, presumably in search of some treasure or the other. He then returns as if nothing has happened, and expects to slide back into his old position and everyone to ignore the fact that he has been gone and not contributing, with nothing to show for it. The sheer nerve of the man sets my teeth on edge on top of everything else he does!" |"Several days ago, Takahiro had the nerve to ask me for several kinds of produce from the fields here, promising a number of jars of liquor in exchange. The cheek of the man[kiyoko.numKits 12| — he knows that there are mostly children living here]! Of course, I sent him away, and told him in no uncertain terms that if he wanted to get my future husband any more drunk he'd have to do it without my assistance! I do not think it sank through to him, and I would be surprised if anything sank through into the liquor-pickled brain of his to begin with." |"I do not like to write people off, but it is quite impossible to help someone who does not wish, even at some unconscious level, to be aided. Of course, considering my antipathy towards Takahiro, I suppose my judgement is clouded as to his salvageability. Just as well that I am not the one expected to enact it in any way, shape or form — as much as I try to see the good in everyone, this is a man who actively revels in his status as an inebriated sot and a social negative. I will reiterate that when I have my own den, I will not tolerate behavior of this kind in the least. This is what gets you sent to the colonies back across the ocean, and now that we are in the colonies... haa." ] ] "

rows.original: [var0 |[kinu.isInari |[rand |"Oh, you mean that weird girl who keeps on asking me questions, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]? I don't know why, but she seems to have gotten it in her head that I'm doing anything out of the ordinary when I'm working the fields. I certainly don't think I'm anything special — I'd argue that Hitoshi's more experienced than I am in this regard, but for some reason I'm the one she's been bothering. "I don't like it, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]. There's something in that half-burnt face and glassy eye that gives me the creeps; she's not a bad person, but I don't feel comfortable being around her, especially with how insistent she is on pestering me on the matter." |"Rin? It's hard not to see her every day while out in the fields — they border the gardens, after all, and even if they didn't I've to pass through them on the way to the shrine. What's the matter?" Well, you're just concerned about her social life, and that she should try to make more friends with people her age. She spent the entirety of her childhood with just her family and there wasn't really anyone on equal standing with her, and now that she has the chance... "Sheesh, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ], you're starting to sound like Mother on this point. Don't worry about it, I'll make as many friends as I need — not one more or less. Maybe we ought to have had something in common because of our white fur, if nothing else, but actual friendship kind of takes more than that." |"Oh, that girl? Yeah, I know Rin's in charge of the shrine gardens; I do have to pass through them to see Mai every evening. Aside from that..." your fox-daughter shrugs. "Her business isn't mine, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]. Kohaku keeps on trying to sell me on gossip when it comes to her, but I'm not buying any of it — yeah, whatever happened to her to make her that way is kind of sad, but it's none of my business, and I couldn't care less. Look at it this way, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ] — if I had something terrible happen to me, I wouldn't want people to be gossiping behind my back, either. Let buried demons be buried demons, right?" |Your fox-daughter raises her nose at the mention of Rindo and sniffs with clear disdain. "Hmph." What's the matter? "That girl talks to Hitoshi too much. I don't like it." They do have reason to converse on business grounds, though. Rindo's work with improving the general plant stock of the den intersects nicely with Hitoshi's job of actually producing said stock. Surely she's approached Kinu on the same matter as well? Kinu scowls; the expression does not look good on her otherwise pretty face as her five tails thrash about angrily. "She's being too friendly with him for what simple business would warrant." From all the gossip around in the den, you've figured it's the military provost the poor girl's pining for, not his agrarian cousin. In all honesty, you don't think she's about to steal your daughter's boyfriend from her; it's probably all in her imagination. "Hmph. Don't let that face and eye of hers trick you into siding with her because of a sob story, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]. That doesn't give anyone a pass to do as they like; if she does try to steal him from me, I'm not going to show a homewrecker any mercy." |"Oh, Rin? Yeah, she doesn't just have white fur, but what Granny Komari calls brands of divinity on her face as well — or at least, the half that hasn't been burned off. But that doesn't really mean anything where it counts, does it? Mother always said that kind of stuff was necessary, but not sufficient for greatness. And if she can settle down like that to be a gardener, I don't see where Mother has any reason to complain about what I do." Well, Rindo isn't just a gardener, she's a naturalist as well. "Somehow, I don't think Mother would approve of what I do even if I collated the details of the cultivation of brute beets and grottatoes and sent them across the ocean, [pc.mf |Dad |Mom ]. As far as I'm concerned, it's a cover story. In a sense, I'm kind of jealous of her, but I guess to whom much is given, much is expected and all. Besides, she grows flowers, not food." Your fox-daughter huffs, as if that last sentence is supposed to justify everything she's said about the matter. ] |[rand |"The history of the young lady Igarashi is quite sad, is it not, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ]? I only wish that I could have been here when it was all happening. Being there for people during times of need like that needs a careful touch — you want that person to know you are there for them and willing to extend a helping hand, but also do not want to wound their pride too much." You have to agree there. Although by saying that, you suppose your daughter dearest is saying she has that careful touch? Kinu smiles enigmatically. "Perhaps, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ]. Still, she seems to have worked out quite admirably — Matron Komari has taken excellent care of the girl, and she behaves in a manner that clearly shows that despite the scars on her body, none remain on her spirit. That kind of joy is something that we all can draw inspiration from, is it not?" |"The young lady Igarashi has such a fetching interest in painting; it's something that she used to do when she was young, before she had reason to come to the colonies. I've always invite her to join Nakano and me when we get together in the gardens at evening to discuss painting and our art — she always behaves so animatedly when discussing colors and inks. You can really appreciate that kind of enthusiastic spirit no matter who it comes from, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ] — it really helps move the conversation along, and she's got the most intriguing ideas. I feel like I can learn something from her, truly." |"Ah, you mean the young lady Igarashi... we are just fine, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ]. After so long with just us in the Astral Plane, I feel like I should try to get to know my peers, young people my age... there aren't too many of those in the colonies, proportionally speaking, but that makes the effort all that much easier," your fox-daughter says with a laugh. "It certainly is a different experience talking to people on the same level as you are, that is for sure. I wish we could be better friends, but I understand that it also takes a person like that some time to open up fully, perhaps over the course of years. She must have had a lot of cheap, insincere sympathy in her time to be rightfully wary of people trying to get close to her heart." |Rindo really loves her namesake," Kinu says with a smile. "Whether it's a happy coincidence, or her mother had some kind of premonition at her birth to name her that, or she developed an affectation for the flowers because of her name, I don't know. What I do know is that Matron Komari's given over a nicely-sized flowerbed over to her in the gardens for her to pursue that particular passion, and she has, to great effect. Did you know that they're usually deep blue when planted in the Old Country, but are purple when grown here? Odd, isn't it?" |"Sometimes, [pc.mf |Father |Mother ], I feel like the young lady Igarashi and I are akin to each other, and not just because we share in the markings of the blood. We might have been more than what we are, but we've learned to be content with our lot and not resent what was taken from us — or perhaps, what we could never have had to begin with. Of course, she's been doing it a lot longer than I have, so there's much I can learn from her when it comes to coming to terms with your lot in life and making the best of your situation. Not that I've suffered anything like she has... "Rindo's quiet and unassuming, but I feel inspired to do better by her story. Mother may have abdicated her birthright — and by extension, mine as well — but that's all right. It just means that I'm able to build something of my own, for my own, and lay down the foundations for my line to flourish no matter what the future holds. That's where the ethos of the Old Country truly shines, I think — individually, we may be specks compared to, say, the pale elves, but if you gather enough specks and pile them up atop each other the result towers even over the highest mountain. If I learn from the young lady Igarashi's example and allow the lessons to hold me up, I can reach higher than I otherwise could have done myself. That's what civilization is all about." ] ] |[kinu.isInari |[rand |Does it bother Kinu that you've taken someone she knows, and of her age, as your concubine? Kinu cocks her head at you and quints, folding her ears forward. "That's kind of a loaded question, [kinu.dad]." It is, but at the same time you can trust Kinu to give her completely frank and unfettered opinion on the subject, because she's your daughter. She may not have had any input on the decision, but you still want to know what she thinks of it. "Well, since you asked, [kinu.dad], I'm going to be honest about it — it doesn't really matter to me. If anything, being your concubine means that I don't have to worry about her going after Hitoshi behind my back." You have to shake your head at that. By all accounts, everyone knows that Rindo was pining after Nakano, but if Kinu's that protective of her fiance you're more than happy to help out with putting away her fears. "Yeah. Thanks, [kinu.dad], for what it's worth. Were you expecting me to be upset, disquieted or something along those lines? Like, 'what are you doing with my friends'?" That was one of the possible responses you thought you might've gotten out of her, yes, but it's not necessarily the one you were worried about — if there was something to be worried about to begin with. A shrug. "Nothing's wrong or strange with concubinage, so I hear. Across the ocean, it's supposedly a phase in many upstanding womens' lives, or that's what Mother tells me. You take her in for a handful of years, let Granny Komari deal with whatever unpleasantness that might've befallen her family, and when everything's passed she's free to move on, if that's what she desires. It's certainly not as if Rindo's prostituting herself out to you or anything, [kinu.dad]." Right, right. It's just that given how opinionated she can be about various subjects, especially when speaking with her mother, you expected a stronger response from her. Although now that you think about it, she only gives strong responses to matters that're deserving of it. "Right, [kinu.dad]. No point wasting my energy getting all worked up over things that don't need fretting over, and you taking Rindo as a concubine is one of them. What should I be bothered about? That you're going to be her benefactor or to put it more bluntly, mate with her?" There is that... Kinu waves off your words. "Eh, don't worry about it, [kinu.dad]. You know that I sneak into the nearby village sometimes, and even if I didn't there are still ways and means of getting news about what's been happening beyond these, walls, right? You're kinda famous, and given how much people will talk when they think someone's actually interested, it's not hard to get a hold on who and what you've been doing out there. If I had any objections to begin with, they've long since been deadened — so yeah, whatever. Go and fuck Rindo's brains out until she's panting and wagging all three of those bushy tails all over the place, why don't you?" ... "Oh come on, [kinu.dad]. You don't think I haven't seen animals going at it any chance they get? You don't think I've ever taken pollen from a flower and painted it on another? I work the dirt, [kinu.dad] — there's no escaping these things as a fact of life." |"You know, [kinu.dad], I'm kind of relieved that Rindo didn't move in with us under the same roof. Not that she would have, but from my understanding of the history in this part of the world, concubines tended to be live-in affairs for those who had them." You're perfectly aware of the fact that when it comes to foxes, you play by fox rules; it's been drilled so deeply into your head at this point that you can't help but find it a little annoying. That being said, the decision to let Rindo continue with her old life as much as possible was made with her welfare in mind and not Kinu's. "Oh, I understand that just fine, [kinu.dad]. Doesn't mean I can't benefit from it, though. Still, would've been awkward for the both of us — me having to see her face in the morning every day, and her having to get used to how I run things around here. I don't see the likes of Rindo ever getting used to the kind of physical labor I and everyone else here works with, Mother excepted." Yeah, you can see that not going well. Seriously, though, neither you nor Komari wanted to tear her away from surroundings that were familiar to her, and she can do everything she needs to in the line of duty as a concubine without needing to live over there. Besides, that would rather defeat the point of protecting her, given that Kiyoko's home is more exposed, the crater walls notwithstanding. "Yeah, that's right. Someone like her needs a more pleasant environment than a half-ruined outpost." Come on, it's not that bad... at least, what buildings are in use have been spruced up plenty. "And those that aren't are still half-ruined, [kinu.dad]. A whole bunch more people than a single family were originally intended to put up here all that time ago, and while they're not really in use they're still an eyesore. I've half a mind to tear down some of the really dilapidated ones so they don't risk collapsing and posing a danger to people. Rindo's used to surrounding herself with all manner of pretty things, flower girl that she is — this is not the kind of place for her." Hmm... |"Granny Komari was telling me the other day that once all of this died down and when Rindo stops being your concubine, she was thinking of marrying her off to Nakano and making her my retainer. Can you believe it?" You're of the understanding that concubinage to someone prestigious is supposed to be a phase of sorts and not permanent employment for the rest of one's existence, but the day which all that eventually comes around is comfortably far off in the future — say, [silly |about when the game comes to a close, maybe |in two or three years, maybe? You don't know exactly what Komari has in mind to help the girl out of the predicament she's in ]. And what if you want to keep her on longer, though, and she's fine with that? "Then she stays on for as long as she wants, I guess. Wouldn't think anyone would have any reason to be against that, it's between the two of you," Kinu replies with a shrug. "Personally, though, I'd want her to get on with the rest of her life, and it's not like you can't still be friends or that you can't be a benefactor to her after the fact, but [silly |like I said before, that really isn't going to be relevant at all over the course of the game, so whatever |like I said, that's for the two of you to work out. Certainly not anything I could have anything meaningful to say about, [kinu.dad] ]. But I can also see where Granny Komari is coming from, keeping a landing clear for her when she finally decides that it's over. Or maybe even before then, she needs something to do in the meantime as well, and she can't be a flower girl forever either." Yeah, you can see that, and it's not like Kinu's going to be restricted to one underling in the future... or is she? "No, [kinu.dad], there's no old law or tradition that mandates that I only have on retainer on staff, so don't worry about that. If you want Rindo's attention, you're more than welcome to it; I'm sure I can rope someone else in or something until the point where she can come along. But there's got to be that option, and while I might have sounded incredulous about the prospect when we first started speaking, it's actually quite reasonable, actually." |You've been meaning to ask for a bit, given that you've taken Rindo as your concubine — now that she doesn't have to indulge her concerns over the girl stealing Hitoshi from her, will she be putting her differences aside? "I don't know about that, [kinu.dad]. She grows flowers, I grow crops. There's a fundamental inability to agree there, that's what I'm saying. Irreconcilable differences." For all of these so-called irreconcilable differences, Rindo is completely none the wiser and even genuinely thinks Kinu's her friend for all you can tell. Really, you have absolutely no idea how this state of affairs could've persisted more than so much as a week, but apparently it's been going on since forever. You'd have imagined either Rindo would've figured it out already, or Kinu upset things badly enough that the whole matter would've been undeniable... Kinu just shrugs at that. "People believe what they want to believe, [kinu.dad]. You've no idea how amazingly strong that kind of thinking can be." The same could be said of her, really. "Like I said, [kinu.dad], she grows flowers and I grow crops. There isn't much of a meeting point when you get down to it. The way things are now aren't so bad, and they aren't going to get better if you upset them just in the hopes of reaching for something that can't be achieved." Has she tried? "You don't need to try sticking your hand in the fire to know you'll be burned, [kinu.dad]. Seriously, what kind of rhetoric is that?" It's not — you didn't mean — ah, it's like talking to a stone wall. Your fox-daughter allows herself a small smile at that as she folds her arms. "I'll take that as a compliment then, [kinu.dad]. Really, I don't see where I come into any of this. You keep Rindo as your concubine and make her happy, and that's that. You don't need to make friends with everyone in the world just to get along, really." ] |[rand |Does it bother Kinu that you've taken someone she knows, and of her age, as your concubine? Kinu cocks her head at you ever so slightly, folding her ears forward. "Forgive me, but that is quite a leading question, [kinu.dad]." It is, but at the same time you expect Kinu to give an honest answer on the subject because she's your daughter, even if you know she'll try and flavor it to be as non-confrontational as possible. She may not have had any input on the decision, but you still want to know what she thinks of it. "Well, I will answer to the fullest, and that answer is no. I am not perturbed, [kinu.dad]. It is probably for the best, given that it will take her mind off the fact that I will be marrying Nakano instead of her, and give her new goals to focus on, goals that she can achieve." You have to shake your head at that. By all accounts, everyone knows that Rindo was pining after Nakano, but if Kinu's feeling guilty over taking him away from her you're more than happy to help out with putting away her fears. "I am not feeling guilty of it in the least, [kinu.dad], so please do not concern yourself with that. Now then, if I may ask about your initial question — were you expecting me to upset with such a decision?" That was one of the possible responses you thought you might've gotten out of her, yes, but it's not necessarily the one you were worried about — if there was something to be worried about to begin with. "Ah. There is nothing wrong or dishonorable about concubinage. Across the ocean, it is a phase in many upstanding womens' lives, so Mother tells me — we are merely accommodating her person for a handful of years so that Matron Komari can deal with whatever unpleasantness that might've befallen her family. When everything has passed, she will be free to move on, if that is what she desires. Whether it is true or not, I get the impression that you are worried that it might be seen as something akin to prostitution, [kinu.dad], and that is simply not the case." Right, right. It's just that you don't want to end up stepping into a mire or anything — or at least, more than you already have by sticking your neck out for Rindo. Kinu just smiles at that. "They say that no good deed goes unpunished, but that is just a saying — you taking Rindo as a concubine is a matter that does not warrant worry. What should I find cause to be concerned about? That you will mate with her?" There is that... The smile widens. "In a sense, you are simply being her benefactor, [kinu.dad]. That, and I have my means of receiving news about your many deeds in the locality. Suffice to say that I am not the squeamish sort and am well-appraised of the facts of the world as it is. Fame is what it is, and people talk about you, [kinu.dad]. They talk about you quite a lot." ... "My only hope is that you make Rindo's concubinage a pleasant one, [kinu.dad]; she is the very picture of a long-suffering fox. Do not concern yourself with my opinion on the matter, and do what is right and necessary." |"Matron Komari was discussing with me the other day the possibility of marrying her off to Hitoshi and making her my retainer once all of this bother dies down and the danger to her has passed. It's not an unappealing prospect, I will say, not that I have any real input on it. Still, it's nice to be informed of what is going through the den matron's mind." "Then she is free to remain for as long as she wants, I expect. I would not think anyone would protest too deeply, since it is between the two of you," Kinu replies with a smile. "If you are asking for my personal opinion, though, I would want her to move on with the rest of her life, and you can still preserve the essence of your relationship without needing the name. Nevertheless, [silly |like I said before, that really isn't going to be relevant at all over the course of the game, so it is of no great import |like I said, that is for the two of you to determine, and certainly not anything I could have anything meaningful to say about, [kinu.dad] ]. But I can also see where Matron Komari is coming from, keeping a landing clear for her when she finally decides that it's over. Or maybe even before then, she needs something to do in the meantime as well, and she can't be a flower girl forever." Yeah, you can see that, and it's not like Kinu's going to be restricted to one underling in the future... or is she? "No, [kinu.dad], there is no old law or tradition that mandates that I only have on retainer on staff; just as there is no real time limit on how long you can keep her as a concubine. If you want Rindo's attention, please help yourself; I have plenty of assistance to tide me over until the point where she can come along. rows.original: [kinu.isInari |Seeing you reach out for her head, Kinu closes her eyes momentarily and draws a breath to compose herself. When she reopens them, there's something in her white pupils that wasn't there before, perhaps a soft longing that lingers as she raises her hands to her head and removes her headcloth, folding it between her hands as she stands resolute before you. Her five tails are trembling a bit, winding tightly about her feet while she waits for you to begin. "G-go ahead, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I'll do you a favor if you want to pat me on the head that badly. Sheesh..." Her ears wiggle a bit, and you take that as an invitation to firmly plant the heel of your palm atop her forehead, giving your fox-daughter a straight noogie between the eyes for old times' sake. Kinu's ears perk up at your touch, then start twitching from side to side like crazy; all five of her fluffy, silvery-white tails coil ever tighter about her body, shivering with excitement. "C'mon, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it tickles...!" Well, of course. You wouldn't do it if it didn't tickle, would you? "Nnnnn..." You move your hand from side to side, starting with the heel of your palm on one of her temples, then moving in a semicircular motion over the back of her head to the other. Back and forth, back and forth, your fingers press down upon your fox-daughter's thickly fluffed ears, pushing them down against her hair as the motions run over them. As soon as your hand leaves, though, they spring back up with an alarming amount of elasticity, twitching softly from side to side. Several white hairs spring up with each pass of your hand, flattened down by its passage before bouncing up again, determined to stand up to you. Kinu lets out a little sigh of relief, her body relaxing several degrees, her tails uncurling from about her legs and body and slowly swaying back and forth behind her, fluffy pendulums swinging in time with the motions of her body. Even as you continue moving from one ear to the other, your fox-daughter tilts her head in accordance with your petting — it's kind of cute how you can't tell if she's trying to angle for better contact with your hand, or trying to maintain some degree of respectability while still being patted on the head. As her large ears flick from side to side under the weight of your hand, you pick up speed, your fingers parting her silken, flowing hair and dancing about the base of her braid. With her relationship with her mother having soured, Kinu probably doesn't get that many headpats anymore — you might as well make each and every one memorable. With a final brush of your fingertips, you toss aside a lock of your fox-daughter's silvery-white hair and close in on her ears, tending to them one at a time. A soft exhalation, a heaving sigh escapes Kinu's lips as you start at the bases of her ears, taking the warm, cartilaginous flesh between thumb and forefinger and kneading in circular motions. Slowly, you move up the edge of her ear to the tip, feeling it strain against your hold as it tries to escape. Hooking your thumb inside, you massage the fine ear-fluff, pressing the sensitive, downy hair against warm flesh until contented fox noises rise from your daughter's lips. When you're done with one side, you shower Kinu's other large fox ear with the same quiet affection, allowing your daughter to luxuriate in the simple joy of human contact. "O-okay, that's enough!" Even though her heart clearly isn't in it, Kinu steps back and pulls her head out of your reach, her usual chaotically orderly hairstyle reasserting itself with a shake of her head. Even so, the anguished loneliness of the young woman that she is shines in her ice-blue eyes, the loss of a childhood as one grows into adult roles and responsibilities. "I'm good, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I'm not a kit any more..." Even so, she'll be good, yes? As a young woman, she probably has more reason to give you cause for worry than when she was a child. If she continues to keep everything together and do well until you next return, you'll pat her head again. "Yeah, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]..." [party.has kiyoko | |And while you know she isn't on best terms with her mother, at least the two of them could at least tolerate each others' presence for the time being? Even in the afterglow of her recent headpatting, Kinu winces. "That's a hard sell, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." ] All right, then. You'll be seeing her around. "Yeah, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I've got to go..." Before she can second-guess herself, Kinu's slipped her headcloth back on and is padding away from you, very definitely not looking back. You watch her leave for a little while, the distance between the two of you growing ever greater, then turn to be on your way. [party.has kiyoko | "She's been standoffish ever since she turned thirteen summers or so," your fox-wife says with a little sigh. "[kiyoko.numKits 2 |With her siblings, at least it was but for a little while; with her, it looks like it might last forever |With my sisters, it was but a phase of a few years; with my daughter, it looks like it may last forever ]. Then again, she was already growing to be a contrarian when she was still a child..." ... "In either case, I'm glad you can still connect to her on some level. She resents me too much for that any more." ] |Seeing you extend your hand, Kinu closes her eyes momentarily and heaves a small sigh. When she opens them again a moment later, there's a small, sheepish smile playing on her lips. Clasping her hands before her, your fox-daughter gives you a deep bow from the waist, sliding her palms down to her knees and presenting her head of silvery-white hair and ears to you. Your fox-daughter's five tails swish behind her, sleek and well-groomed as she awaits your affection.[silly| Clearly, there is a formal headpatting position amongst kitsune, and she has just assumed it with all due pomp and circumstance.] "If that is your wish, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], then I desire pampering. Go on, then. Do remember to get the spots behind my ears, if you will." Ah, so she's making demands now? Not content with receiving a gift, she's going to dictate how it must be given? "Ah, no, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I would certainly never be as insensitive or brash as to complain about the inadequacy of a gift freely given! Oh no, do perish the thought! If I did such a terrible thing, it would certainly reflect most poorly on the upbringing that Mother and you gave me! "Now then... I am perfectly ready. I humbly request that you begin at your leisure." So you will, so you will. Even though you know it's coming, the prickling warmth that meets your fingertips as you push them down into Kinu's hair is enough to catch your breath in your throat; this goes doubly so even as you sink them further and further into the silken smooth silvery-white mass, not stopping until they hit her scalp. The faint scent of exotic floral oils, light and sweet, rises into the air as you begin moving your hand back and forth, scratching from her brow to the nape of her neck and back again. Back and forth in a v-motion, you apply your affections to your fox-daughter's head, smoothing down each of her ears in turn with every pass. They don't stay down for long, springing back up mere moments after you hand's passed over, swivelling this way and that as Kinu luxuriates in the affection you're giving her. "Ah, very comfortable." While you can't see her face with her eyes trained on the ground, the tone of her voice tells you all you need to know. "You do this adeptly, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." With a slow vulpine noise of contentment, your fox-daughter pushes her head up and back against your grasp, aggressively nuzzling the back of her head against your palm. Her quintet of white tails don't swish any faster, but there's a certain gravitas to their movements that wasn't there when you began. You can only reciprocate Kinu's enthusiasm, muted as it is, by pushing your fingers fully into her hair and picking up the pace. Soft and silken, your fox-daughter's fur belies her namesake, its inviting warmth enveloping your hand and making the skin prickle all over. Such a refined young lady. You would tell her to be good while [party.has kiyoko|you and her mother are|you're] away, but she's already doing that just fine, isn't she? "It is nice to have one's efforts acknowledged, almost as good as being petted. Would you not agree?" Haha. You finish up the simple head-patting, and move on to Kinu's ears; she tilts her head upwards a little to give you better access to them. They're less fluffy to the touch than her mother's, but far, far more sensitive; Kinu doesn't have tufts in her large fox ears, but the fine hairs that line the insides of her ears press wonderfully against your thumb as you take the edge between thumb and forefinger and stroke away. With your thumb secure, you take the time to grant her wish and hook your fingers around the back of her vulpine ears, reaching for the base and digging in firmly where they join her head. This elicits a louder sigh of contentment from your fox-daughter, one that's sustained as you rub your fingers back and forth about the base of her ear. "Hmmmnnn..." With one ear finished, it's only natural to move on to the other. Kinu tilts her head the other way, the ear in question perking up and wiggling — until you catch it and lavish upon it the selfsame treatment you gave its twin. Once more, you hook your fingertips about the sensitive back, scratching up and down the base and length; your fox-daughter's quintet of tails curl about her legs and yours as she suddenly draws herself up and gives you a light embrace, arms wrapping around you. There, there... It's a long white — or at least, feels like one — but when you finally pull away and retreat to a respectable distance, Kinu has a small mischievous smile on her face. "Well, I am quite content now. Are you, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?" Y-you are. Your fox-daughter gives you a little bow. "Well then, allow me to express my gratitude for your parental affection, even though I am rightfully a little too old for such, perhaps. Ahaha. I will see you later, then. There are other tasks I must attend to for now..." With that, Kinu turns tail and leaves, a spring in her step that wasn't there before making itself known.[party.has kiyoko| Purring, your fox-wife snuggles up to you and presses the warmth of her body against yours. "And when do I get my petting, beloved?" All in good time, all in good time. "Mmmmnn... I'll hold you to that, then." ] ]

它看起来是一根长长的白色东西——至少给人的感觉是这样——但当你终于拉开距离，退到安全的地方时，你会发现小娟的脸上带着一丝调皮的笑容。 嗯，我现在挺满意的。你呢？ [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]？" 你……你真是太好了。 你的狐妖女儿向您微微鞠了一躬。那么，让我来表达一下对你们这种父母般关爱的感激吧。虽然说，对我来说，这样的关怀或许有点多余了……哈哈，回头见吧，我现在还有其他事情要处理…… 说完这句话，小娟便转身离开了，她的步伐中仿佛多了股前所未有的活力。[party.has kiyoko| 你的狐狸妻子发出呼噜声，依偎到你身边，将她温暖的身体紧贴在你的身上。 那么，到底什么时候我来让我抱抱你吧，亲爱的？ 一切都会在恰当的时候到来，一切都会在恰当的时候发生。 嗯……那我就指望你遵守这个承诺了。 ] ]
rows.raw: " [kinu.isInari |Seeing you reach out for her head, Kinu closes her eyes momentarily and draws a breath to compose herself. When she reopens them, there's something in her white pupils that wasn't there before, perhaps a soft longing that lingers as she raises her hands to her head and removes her headcloth, folding it between her hands as she stands resolute before you. Her five tails are trembling a bit, winding tightly about her feet while she waits for you to begin. "G-go ahead, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I'll do you a favor if you want to pat me on the head that badly. Sheesh..." Her ears wiggle a bit, and you take that as an invitation to firmly plant the heel of your palm atop her forehead, giving your fox-daughter a straight noogie between the eyes for old times' sake. Kinu's ears perk up at your touch, then start twitching from side to side like crazy; all five of her fluffy, silvery-white tails coil ever tighter about her body, shivering with excitement. "C'mon, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it tickles...!" Well, of course. You wouldn't do it if it didn't tickle, would you? "Nnnnn..." You move your hand from side to side, starting with the heel of your palm on one of her temples, then moving in a semicircular motion over the back of her head to the other. Back and forth, back and forth, your fingers press down upon your fox-daughter's thickly fluffed ears, pushing them down against her hair as the motions run over them. As soon as your hand leaves, though, they spring back up with an alarming amount of elasticity, twitching softly from side to side. Several white hairs spring up with each pass of your hand, flattened down by its passage before bouncing up again, determined to stand up to you. Kinu lets out a little sigh of relief, her body relaxing several degrees, her tails uncurling from about her legs and body and slowly swaying back and forth behind her, fluffy pendulums swinging in time with the motions of her body. Even as you continue moving from one ear to the other, your fox-daughter tilts her head in accordance with your petting — it's kind of cute how you can't tell if she's trying to angle for better contact with your hand, or trying to maintain some degree of respectability while still being patted on the head. As her large ears flick from side to side under the weight of your hand, you pick up speed, your fingers parting her silken, flowing hair and dancing about the base of her braid. With her relationship with her mother having soured, Kinu probably doesn't get that many headpats anymore — you might as well make each and every one memorable. With a final brush of your fingertips, you toss aside a lock of your fox-daughter's silvery-white hair and close in on her ears, tending to them one at a time. A soft exhalation, a heaving sigh escapes Kinu's lips as you start at the bases of her ears, taking the warm, cartilaginous flesh between thumb and forefinger and kneading in circular motions. Slowly, you move up the edge of her ear to the tip, feeling it strain against your hold as it tries to escape. Hooking your thumb inside, you massage the fine ear-fluff, pressing the sensitive, downy hair against warm flesh until contented fox noises rise from your daughter's lips. When you're done with one side, you shower Kinu's other large fox ear with the same quiet affection, allowing your daughter to luxuriate in the simple joy of human contact. "O-okay, that's enough!" Even though her heart clearly isn't in it, Kinu steps back and pulls her head out of your reach, her usual chaotically orderly hairstyle reasserting itself with a shake of her head. Even so, the anguished loneliness of the young woman that she is shines in her ice-blue eyes, the loss of a childhood as one grows into adult roles and responsibilities. "I'm good, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I'm not a kit any more..." Even so, she'll be good, yes? As a young woman, she probably has more reason to give you cause for worry than when she was a child. If she continues to keep everything together and do well until you next return, you'll pat her head again. "Yeah, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]..." [party.has kiyoko | |And while you know she isn't on best terms with her mother, at least the two of them could at least tolerate each others' presence for the time being? Even in the afterglow of her recent headpatting, Kinu winces. "That's a hard sell, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." ] All right, then. You'll be seeing her around. "Yeah, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I've got to go..." Before she can second-guess herself, Kinu's slipped her headcloth back on and is padding away from you, very definitely not looking back. You watch her leave for a little while, the distance between the two of you growing ever greater, then turn to be on your way. [party.has kiyoko | "She's been standoffish ever since she turned thirteen summers or so," your fox-wife says with a little sigh. "[kiyoko.numKits 2 |With her siblings, at least it was but for a little while; with her, it looks like it might last forever |With my sisters, it was but a phase of a few years; with my daughter, it looks like it may last forever ]. Then again, she was already growing to be a contrarian when she was still a child..." ... "In either case, I'm glad you can still connect to her on some level. She resents me too much for that any more." ] |Seeing you extend your hand, Kinu closes her eyes momentarily and heaves a small sigh. When she opens them again a moment later, there's a small, sheepish smile playing on her lips. Clasping her hands before her, your fox-daughter gives you a deep bow from the waist, sliding her palms down to her knees and presenting her head of silvery-white hair and ears to you. Your fox-daughter's five tails swish behind her, sleek and well-groomed as she awaits your affection.[silly| Clearly, there is a formal headpatting position amongst kitsune, and she has just assumed it with all due pomp and circumstance.] "If that is your wish, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], then I desire pampering. Go on, then. Do remember to get the spots behind my ears, if you will." Ah, so she's making demands now? Not content with receiving a gift, she's going to dictate how it must be given? "Ah, no, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I would certainly never be as insensitive or brash as to complain about the inadequacy of a gift freely given! Oh no, do perish the thought! If I did such a terrible thing, it would certainly reflect most poorly on the upbringing that Mother and you gave me! "Now then... I am perfectly ready. I humbly request that you begin at your leisure." So you will, so you will. Even though you know it's coming, the prickling warmth that meets your fingertips as you push them down into Kinu's hair is enough to catch your breath in your throat; this goes doubly so even as you sink them further and further into the silken smooth silvery-white mass, not stopping until they hit her scalp. The faint scent of exotic floral oils, light and sweet, rises into the air as you begin moving your hand back and forth, scratching from her brow to the nape of her neck and back again. Back and forth in a v-motion, you apply your affections to your fox-daughter's head, smoothing down each of her ears in turn with every pass. They don't stay down for long, springing back up mere moments after you hand's passed over, swivelling this way and that as Kinu luxuriates in the affection you're giving her. "Ah, very comfortable." While you can't see her face with her eyes trained on the ground, the tone of her voice tells you all you need to know. "You do this adeptly, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." With a slow vulpine noise of contentment, your fox-daughter pushes her head up and back against your grasp, aggressively nuzzling the back of her head against your palm. Her quintet of white tails don't swish any faster, but there's a certain gravitas to their movements that wasn't there when you began. You can only reciprocate Kinu's enthusiasm, muted as it is, by pushing your fingers fully into her hair and picking up the pace. Soft and silken, your fox-daughter's fur belies her namesake, its inviting warmth enveloping your hand and making the skin prickle all over. Such a refined young lady. You would tell her to be good while [party.has kiyoko|you and her mother are|you're] away, but she's already doing that just fine, isn't she? "It is nice to have one's efforts acknowledged, almost as good as being petted. Would you not agree?" Haha. You finish up the simple head-patting, and move on to Kinu's ears; she tilts her head upwards a little to give you better access to them. They're less fluffy to the touch than her mother's, but far, far more sensitive; Kinu doesn't have tufts in her large fox ears, but the fine hairs that line the insides of her ears press wonderfully against your thumb as you take the edge between thumb and forefinger and stroke away. With your thumb secure, you take the time to grant her wish and hook your fingers around the back of her vulpine ears, reaching for the base and digging in firmly where they join her head. This elicits a louder sigh of contentment from your fox-daughter, one that's sustained as you rub your fingers back and forth about the base of her ear. "Hmmmnnn..." With one ear finished, it's only natural to move on to the other. Kinu tilts her head the other way, the ear in question perking up and wiggling — until you catch it and lavish upon it the selfsame treatment you gave its twin. Once more, you hook your fingertips about the sensitive back, scratching up and down the base and length; your fox-daughter's quintet of tails curl about her legs and yours as she suddenly draws herself up and gives you a light embrace, arms wrapping around you. There, there... It's a long white — or at least, feels like one — but when you finally pull away and retreat to a respectable distance, Kinu has a small mischievous smile on her face. "Well, I am quite content now. Are you, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?" Y-you are. Your fox-daughter gives you a little bow. "Well then, allow me to express my gratitude for your parental affection, even though I am rightfully a little too old for such, perhaps. Ahaha. I will see you later, then. There are other tasks I must attend to for now..." With that, Kinu turns tail and leaves, a spring in her step that wasn't there before making itself known.[party.has kiyoko| Purring, your fox-wife snuggles up to you and presses the warmth of her body against yours. "And when do I get my petting, beloved?" All in good time, all in good time. "Mmmmnn... I'll hold you to that, then." ] ] "

rows.original: Lavish attention upon Kinu's head and ears.
rows.translation: 将大量的注意力集中在小娟的头部和耳朵上。
rows.raw: "Lavish attention upon Kinu's head and ears."

rows.original: [kinu.isInari |Kinu makes to remove her headscarf when you reach out for her, but as soon as she realizes that you're going for her cheeks and not her head she cringes and draws back sharply, arms raised defensively in front of her face. "[pc.mf|Dad|Mom], it's not that I don't like you or anything, but... but I don't want this. I'm not a kid any more." ... "So just let it go, okay? It's not something we can do like we used to." Your fox-daughter looks left, right, then heaves a sigh, her ears curling further downward. "This is getting awkward, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I'm going to go for now. See you tomorrow, okay?" Without waiting for so much as a by-your-leave or even a reply, Kinu turns tail and pads off across the fields. She doesn't look back. [party.has kiyoko | "Well, that's our daughter," Kiyoko says curtly, arms folded under her bosom. "She's all grown-up and independent now; doesn't need her parents any more. So be it, then." ] She's right, though. Some things have changed; the past has been consumed by time's fire, leaving only memories. And sometimes memories are best left as such... |While Kinu looks surprised when she realizes you're reaching for her face and not her head, she doesn't shy away, instead presenting a brave front as your fingertips come into contact with her soft, smooth cheek. Your fox-daughter closes an eye as you caress her brow with a thumb, gathering up her fringes and forelock into something pettable that you can press against her temples, the soft silken fur-hair exuding a gentle warmth of its own. It flows and runs like silken oil, trying to evade your grasp, but that's part of its charm, isn't it? "Ah! [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... I would request that you be careful with my foundation, yes? I put on just enough, and it would not do in the least to have it smeared all over my cheek..." You wouldn't have imagined that Kinu would be the type to need foundation, but if that's what she says. "Ah well, I hold many mysteries, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. It is part of my carefully cultivated appeal, after all." Slowly, trying not to startle Kinu, you roll your fingers back and forth against the soft flesh of your fox-daughter's cheek, watching her smile grow increasingly mischievous and knowing as you proceed apace. The cut of her face as a young woman is cleanly akin to her mother's, and she tilts her head back a little as you cup her chin in your palm, her ice-blue eyes meeting yours without faltering. Hmm... from there, it's back up her cheek again to her hairline, her hair falling through your fingers. As always, you're reminded of why Kiyoko named your daughter such — her face is adorably soft as you pet it, cheekbone to chin and back again. Her quintet of sleek white tails sway from side to side rhythmically as you gently lavish affection upon her features, until her cheeks have grown warm and a little tinge of color's risen into them. Kinu doesn't push against your touch, but neither does she shy away — affectionate, perhaps, while still being prim and proper in keeping a respectful distance and the contact wholesome. Now doesn't that feel nice? There's no need to think too deeply — for a moment, she can just forget about the responsibilities of being Big Sister and relax. "Hmmmn." A small shiver runs through Kinu's body and her outline wavers, as if she's having trouble keeping her humanoid form intact. Thinning her lips while keeping her smile, your fox-daughter reaches up and curls her fingers about your wrist, pulling downwards gently but insistently. The message is tactful, but clear: that's enough. "There, there. There will be no lack of opportunities to revisit this in the future, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]; some things are best done in small doses to keep their unique appeal fresh and intact. This has been very comforting and enjoyable, and I thank you from the bottom of my heart." Ah, well. It's with more than a bit of reluctance that you allow Kinu to guide your hand away from her face, but all good things must come to an end. It's a small mercy that you're still able to do this even after she's grown up. "If you will excuse me, then, I think I shall take my leave. This has put me in quite a good mood and I intend to spend it on constructive endeavors before it runs out. I will see you soon then, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." With a small, final bow Kinu turns tail on you and stalks off, a spring in her step that wasn't there before. [party.has kiyoko | "Ah, children grow up so fast," your fox-wife says as she steps up to your side and attaches herself to your arm. "I remember when I was but a kit, too... time certainly does fly, does it not? Well then, you can pet my face anytime you'd like, beloved." ] ]
rows.translation: [kinu.isInari |当你伸手去触碰小娟时，她试图摘下头巾，但当她意识到你的手其实是想触碰她的脸颊而不是头巾时，她立刻缩了回去，双臂防御性地举在脸前。 "[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]并不是说我不喜欢你或者有什么别的原因，但是……我真的不想要这样。我已经不是小孩子了。 …… 所以就放它走吧，好吗？我们已经不能再像以前那样去做了。你的狐狸女儿左顾右盼，然后叹了口气，她的耳朵更加耷拉了下来。这种情况越来越尴尬了[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]那我先走了。明天见，好吗？ 甚至没有等待任何许可或回应，小娟就转身跑开了，穿过田野，头也不回。 [party.has kiyoko | 嗯，那就是我们的女儿。清子双臂交叉在胸前，简短地说道。她现在已经长大了，也变得独立了，不再需要父母的照顾了。那就这样吧。 ] 不过，她说的也对。有些事情确实是这样。拥有一切都已改变；过去被时间的火焰吞噬，只剩下回忆。 而有时候，回忆就让它保持原样吧…… |当小娟意识到你其实是在触碰她的脸颊而不是头部时，她看起来有些惊讶，但她并没有躲开，反而勇敢地面对着。当你的指尖触碰到她柔软光滑的脸颊时，她闭上了眼睛。你用拇指轻抚她的额头，将她额前的毛发聚拢起来，形成一簇可以轻轻按压在她太阳穴上的柔软毛发——这些丝滑的毛发本身就散发着一种温柔的温暖。它的流动方式如同丝一般的润滑油，总试图逃避你的掌控，但这也正是它的魅力所在，不是吗？ 啊！ [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]……我恳请您小心对待我的粉底液，好吗？我只会涂一点点，如果它被涂得满脸都是，那就太糟糕了…… 你绝对想不到，小娟竟然会需要打底妆这种东西，但既然她是这么说的，那应该就是真的吧。 唉，我确实隐藏着许多秘密[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]毕竟，这也是我精心塑造的个人魅力的一部分。 你缓缓地移动手指，在女儿那柔软的脸颊上轻轻滑动，尽量不惊动她。看着她脸上浮现出的愈发调皮的笑容，你心里明白，自己正在一步步接近那个时刻。她作为年轻女孩的面容，与她母亲一模一样。当你用手托起她的下巴，让她把头稍微仰起来时，她那冰蓝色的眼睛毫不犹豫地与你的目光对上了。 嗯……从那里开始，头发又从她的脸颊垂落到发际线处，那些头发从你的手指间滑落。就像每次那样，你都会想起为什么清子给你的女儿取了这个名字——当你轻轻抚摸她的脸庞时，你会觉得她的皮肤柔软得令人心生喜爱，从颧骨到下巴，再到脸颊……一切都是那么美好。当你轻轻抚摸她的面容时，她那五条修长洁白的尾巴会有节奏地左右摇摆。不久，她的脸颊便变得温暖起来，还泛起了淡淡的红晕。小娟并不会抗拒你的触碰，但也不会躲开——她或许显得有些害羞，却依然保持着得体的举止，与你的接触始终保持着适当的距离，显得十分礼貌。 现在这种感觉是不是很舒服呢？完全没有必要想得太复杂——在这一刻，她完全可以忘记自己作为“姐姐”所承担的责任，放松一下。 嗯……小娟的身体突然一阵颤抖，她的轮廓也开始变得模糊，似乎她正在努力维持自己的人形形态。她抿紧嘴唇，却依然保持着微笑，然后伸出手指，紧紧抓住了你的手腕，轻轻但坚定地向下拉。这个动作虽然很委婉，但意思却非常明确：够了。。 好了好了，以后肯定还有很多机会再讨论这个问题的。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]有些事情最好少量地去做，这样才能保持它们独特的魅力和新鲜感。这样的体验让我感到非常舒适和愉快，我由衷地感谢你们。 啊，好吧。你虽然有些不情愿，但还是让小娟将你的手从她的脸上移开，不过所有美好的事情终究都会结束。好在即使她已经长大了，你仍然能够这样做，这也算是一种小小的幸运吧。 那么，如果你们不介意的话，我想我该告辞了。这次经历让我心情变得非常好，我打算在这段好心情还没消逝之前，去做一些有意义的事情。那么，回头见吧。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]。" 小娟轻轻鞠了个躬，然后转身离去，她的步伐中仿佛多了几分活力，这是之前所没有的。 [party.has kiyoko | 啊，孩子们长得真快啊。你的狐狸妻子走到你身边，挽着你的手臂说道。我记得当初我也只是个新手……时间确实过得飞快，不是吗？那么，你可以轻轻抚摸它我的亲爱的，你可以随时面对它。 ] ]
