[pc.name]... you don't mind if I stay, do you?" |Berwyn looks around the spread on the table, taking off his hat and holding it in both hands. "This reminds me of before when I went off to be with Matiha... with [pc.mf|Dad|Mom] and Mom and everyone else. I... kinda feel out of place, sitting in on your family time like this." |"Hope there's enough, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It's a bit shameful, but I realized I don't really know what you like, so I made a bit of everything with all kinds of flavors. There should be something in there that should be to your tastes... which means there isn't a lot of any one thing. Maybe I should have made more..." ] No, no. If nothing else, you'll need help finishing everything that's laid out here. It's a feast, no less. "I grew everything that went into these dishes," Kinu says quietly as she uncovers the dishes one by one. "Wrought them from the earth with my own hands... well, except the fish and the ginger; that last one doesn't grow too well in these soils and I've yet to figure out a way to remedy that. But the point still stands." [party.has kiyoko |Kiyoko half-parts her lips, poised to say something, then turns away and swivels her ears towards you. "I won't argue with you. Not right now, not in front of your [pc.mf|father|mother]. This is supposed to be for [pc.himHer]." Kinu turns away too, and the air between mother and daughter chills perceptibly. "For now." "For now." ] Unsurprisingly, Kinu's cooking leans heavily towards soups and salads, and there's plenty of steamed, fluffy rice out of what looks like a big wooden bucket. You sit and wait patiently as your fox-daughter serves [party.combatNames], one of the few rare times she ever acts so quiet and genteel. Some of the vegetables you recognize, others you know from having seen them in her fields, and others are considerably more alien to you, but all in all, it's a strange mixture of foreign cuisine prepared with Marches ingredients. Mostly Marches ingredients, anyway. That, and the salads are mostly pickled — your daughter really has a penchant for the things... How do they say it again? Thank you for the food? Kinu laughs. "[pc.ra kitsune |Well, since you're one of us now, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I guess you've gotta give thanks to the Trickster before eating, eh?" At least, in this setting with your daughter [party.has kiyoko|and fox-wife ]at your side, you feel like you do. |You don't have to do this, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It's not like you're from the Old Country or anything, so you don't need to give thanks to the Trickster before eating." Strictly speaking, perhaps not, but in this setting with your daughter [party.has kiyoko|and fox-wife ]at your side, you feel like you do. ] "Well, if you want to be observant, I'm not going to stop you. You just press your hands together like this... and say it after me... there. And with that, [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ][pc.mf|Dad|Mom], let's eat." With that, [party.isJustPC|the two|all] of you quietly apply yourselves to the offering Kinu's made in return for your gift. It's not gourmet, far from it — it's the kind of meal a working girl like her would sit down to at the end of a day, intended to fill the belly and regain one's strength for the rest of the day. The sourness and salt only serve to stimulate the appetite and thirst, and soon enough Kinu's ladling out extra servings of mushroom egg broth for you all. [party.comp viv cait brint brienne atugia arona etheryn berwyn |Viviane eats silently, though she constant looks around as if expecting some critique or stray remarks. |"This makes me nostalgic," Cait says as she fiddles with her chopsticks. "Hey, [pc.name]... when this is all over and we've gotten Calla back, want to head back to Jassira with me for a little bit? I'll show you the sights, introduce you to the people back at the Temple. We'll have some hot coffee together, and laugh off the past." |"Not as good as my mother's cooking," Brint says between shoveling copious quantities of rice into his mouth, "but still pretty damn good. Hey, girl... get to the point where your kids are saying the same thing that I am right now, defending their mom's cooking in front of other folks, okay? Make your [pc.mf|dad|mom] proud." |"Not as good as my mother's cooking," Brienne says between shoveling copious quantities of rice into her mouth, "but still pretty damn good. Hey, girl... get to the point where your kids are saying the same thing that I am right now, defending their mom's cooking in front of other folks, okay? Make your [pc.mf|dad|mom] proud." |"Gods," Atugia says glumly, poking at her pickles between mouthfuls of rice. "Severine and I would take turns cookin' for Carmen. Never asked if she needed to eat in that sense any more, but... we did it anyway, and she ate it. I... I wonder how the two of them are doing without me around. Maybe we could go up and check before we head off? It isn't too far away." |"Lumia's tits, not having any drink blows." Arona's long since given up fiddling with the lacquered chopsticks and is eating with her hands where possible, in true orc fashion of ignoring everyone else's etiquette. "But I guess it's only expected, isn't it, girl? You're going to be someone to your people like Hretha's to my folk, right? My sister doesn't touch the drink that much, either. Maybe I should get a couple tankards of mead down her throat when I next pop by the camp. Wouldn't that be a treat!" |Ryn has been silent throughout the whole meal, eyes turned downward towards her food. She doesn't say anything, but gives Kinu a grateful nod when the latter moves to refill her soup bowl. There's a lot going up in Ryn's head, you'd imagine, and she'll probably talk about it when the time's right. No point trying to force it out of her now. |Berwyn's been fiddling with his chopsticks all the while, trying to figure out how he's supposed to get them to work. It's kind of cute watching him trying to get the hang of the foreign utensils, but at long last he stops and picks up the spoon instead. "You don't mind if I could have some more soup, do you? This stuff is pretty nice. Never quite tasted anything like it before. You fox-people are weird, but you make good food." "But of course." Kinu moves to refill his soup bowl. "There you go." |"There you go, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]," Kinu says, beaming. "Have a bit more — this is meant to stimulate the appetite, so I'm sure you'll have plenty of room for the rest." Far for it being you to deny anything your beloved fox-daughter has prepared... ] One by one, the dishes are emptied. [party.isJustPC |It's a bit of a challenge with just the two of you, even if Kinu can really pack it away and the sour and salt really help bring out the appetite. On her own, your daughter's finished two bowls of rice and is halfway through her third, not to mention the other dishes... guess she served up what she liked, eh? Like mother, like daughter... |Even with [party.compNames] helping, there's a lot of food to get through, and you wonder if Kinu saw in her divination that you'd be bringing company as well. Didn't stop her from making too much, but you guess she wanted to prove a point, didn't she? ] "I'm full," your fox-daughter declares after a bit. And so are you. Aah, that wasn't bad. Not bad in the least; Kinu has turned out to be quite the accomplished cook. Whoever her future husband is, the lucky boy sure isn't going to go hungry, not with a wife who's as good a source of food as your darling fox-princess is. [party.has kiyoko |Kiyoko chuckles thinly. "A source of food. Even if it's a little blunt... like mother, like daughter, one supposes." ] The words have far more of an effect on Kinu than you'd expected — the blush begins on the bridge of her nose, quickly claims her cheeks, then sinks down her neck all the way into the collar of her kimono. Ah, the very distinctive blush of her mother's bloodline — with how intense it is, even the insides of Kinu's ears must be red and steaming hot by now. Shifting her eyes from side to side, your fox-daughter starts tapping her index fingers together, clearly not realizing what she's doing, much in the same way her mother unconsciously toys with her hair when she's flustered. "I... uh..." [party.has kiyoko |While Kinu is distracted, Kiyoko leans over to you and whispers into your ear. "You do know that a man has been here in our daughter's chambers, right?" Wait, what? "I can scent it, but there are other tell-tale signs. Well, she is so independent and resolute these days; added to the fact that she is left to her devices so often, I'm honestly not surprised. Hmph. Our girl probably seduced him to begin with, that's my guess." She... she seems to care less than you thought she would... "Our daughter just wants to get married and leave; just as children catch onto more than their parents imagine, the reverse also applies. Please, I know more than she gives me credit for as her mother. I was young once, and had many sisters as well." ... "She is my heir, you know. If she continues like this, there's little doubt that she's going to wind up pregnant sooner or later. Maybe that's her plan." ... ] You turn to Kinu and reach over to pat her on the head. Your fox-daughter squeaks, takes a deep breath, and forces herself to calm down, rubbing her brow with her knuckles. "Well, I... I guess that's it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I hope you liked the meal — there's so much I have to thank you for.[party.has kiyoko| And Mother too, of course.] Don't worry about cleaning up — I'll handle those and the leftovers." So much in return for such a small gift... now you're feeling kind of awkward and sheepish. "It's okay, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I mean —" Kinu turns away from [party.has kiyoko|her mother|you] and does that finger twiddling thing again. "I'm glad that I was born, okay? Even if it hasn't been a perfect life so far, I'm really glad it still happened. So this isn't just thanks for a wild melon or a peach or something, this is thanks for everything you've done for me since I was a kit. I..." Okay, you get the point. Rising from your seat a little unsteadily, you cross over to your fox-daughter and give her a pat on the head, as the situation demands. Kinu looks like she's going to protest for a moment, then melts under your touch as you push your fingers more insistently under her headcloth and into her hair. "Thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]," she says at last. "I needed that." You're going to be heading out again, so she's got to watch the den and keep things in order while you[party.has kiyoko| and her mother are|'re] out, okay? "Got it. Yeah, stay safe out there, okay?" Mm-hm. [party.has kiyoko |Taking your fox-wife's hand in your own, you step out of your daughter's chambers together, the clacking of dishes being gathered behind you. Now, is she still so mad at Kinu? "It doesn't change the root of our disagreements, you know." That's true, but is she still so mad at her daughter? "...I may be inclined to be a little more lenient for a while now." [kiyoko.pregStage 2 |Kiyoko pats her big pregnant belly. "Feeding both me and her little sibling was a conscientious act, and I will acknowledge that. I am content with our daughter's conduct for the time being." |Kiyoko tries a small smile. "If nothing else, she is mindful of her responsibilities to others — when she chooses to acknowledge them." ] You smile and pet your fox-wife between her ears. That's about as much as you can hope for, you suppose. |You will. And while you're out... hopefully she can get along better with her mother so you don't have to worry about the both of them while you're slaying demons and saving the world. Kinu rolls her eyes and makes an exasperated noise. "You just have to ask for the one thing which I can't honestly promise you, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." Yes, you know full well that it's hard, which is exactly why you're asking her for it rather than expecting it of her as a matter of course. "Okay, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I'll try. I'll make no promises, but I'll try." You smile and give your fox-daughter another pet between the ears for addition reinforcement. There, there. All right, you'll have to be off now, or you'll never get going... ]"

rows.original: "If you don't mind following me back to my place, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? I've got it waiting there for you." Ah, all right. You can afford to humor your darling fox-daughter, you've got time, after all. Kinu leads you back to her chambers, stopping at the well on the way to wash off her hands and forearms. Once back, she throws open a trunk by the wall and starts rummaging about inside, buried up to her elbows in its contents. [party.has kiyoko |"Oh dear, our daughter's let her chambers run into such disarray while we were gone," your fox-wife says despondently, raising a despairing hand to her cheek. "Always messy ever since she was a kit; I'd hoped that she'd grow out of such a lackadaisical attitude towards keeping her surroundings neat, but it looks like I'll have to reprimand her later. Again." ] "There, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]," your fox-daughter pulls her shakuhachi out of the trunk and cradles it close to her bosom with all the gentleness and care befitting a newborn babe. That bamboo flute really is precious to her. "I've been practising a few new pieces, and wanted you to be the first to hear them before I started playing over at Granny Komari's. You gave me such a fine gift last time; it'd be remiss of me if I didn't repay you in kind." Repaying the taste of fruit with the sound of music. You chuckle. Yes, this is an acceptable trade. "Let's go out back, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. A performance's got to appeal to all the senses, you know?" So it happens that Kinu leads you through another set of screen doors out to the back porch, where she sets down several cushions as [party.has kiyoko |seats for you and your fox-wife. Kiyoko [kiyoko.pregStage 2 |nestles down in the comfortable softness beside you, looking dignified every step of the way with her large pregnant belly |settles down beside you, quietly resigning herself to what's to come ]. |[party.hasCompanions |seats for [party.combatNames] |a seat for you ]. ] You make yourself at home, getting as comfortable as you can on the wooden deck, and wait to see what Kinu's got in store for you. The view that greets you from where you are is a panorama of your fox-daughter's handiwork and life — fields and paddies in the morning sunshine, framed against the greater wilderness of the crater walls. Small squares of tamed nature at the feet of the breath of the wild, as it were. Kinu's not looking at you, her eyes gazing out over her beloved lands, her back firmly up against one of the heavy wooden beams. She's completely relaxed from head to toe, easing herself into the flow of her surroundings even as her five tails sway from side to side with the gentle movements of her body. This is probably some kind of breach of etiquette, knowing the kitsune people... but your fox-daughter's clearly decided to do away with it in favor of being one with the soul of her music. With that, she raises the instrument's mouthpiece to her lips and begins to play. Slowly, music begins to fill the air as Kinu brings out her music from the depths of her being, her work-hardened fingers dancing over the flute's length as she closes her eyes in concentration. The tune is solemn with a deep and rich timbre — practically meditative and spiritual, if you allow yourself to get caught up in it. It's calming, perhaps a little too much so, threatening to lull you to sleep if you don't keep your guard up... [party.has kiyoko |"She is... considerably better than she was at it when she was younger," Kiyoko admits with a small sigh. "The sheer complexity of the instrument and lack of any proper tutoring made learning it problematic, even with the ease with which she usually picks up new skills and learning. But she refused to be a good girl and learn the koto from me instead." She didn't give up. "You could see it that way, I suppose. And now she has made something of herself, I will admit. At least all those times I sent her out of the house to stop making such a horrendous din were worth something..." ] Whatever it is Kinu's playing, however foreign-sounding the music, you nevertheless manage to feel it. It is completely, fully, and undoubtedly her, something that only she, or someone very close in spirit to her, would have been able to evoke — such richness, such haunting longing, such simple emptiness and satisfaction at the heart of it all. Kinu's fingers dance across the shakuhachi, her breath steady and measured as she coaxes her tune out of the bamboo flute with perfect precision. No more missed notes, no more going off-key, just a working girl and her music, a princess of the forests and fields as she was in her youth. Was it so long ago that she was but a tiny fox-kit running in the shade of branches, stealing wild honey and digging in the dirt with her bare hands? After all, what is a field but wilderness tamed? A garden still has to follow the laws of nature, yet cannot run completely wild lest there be no difference between the two. And above it all, that underpinning of haunting loneliness, of empty skies, vast fields and deep mountain vistas... Eventually, the music dies down, Kinu lowers the bamboo flute, and she breaks the steady rhythm of her breathing with a small sigh. She leans her head back against the beam she's up against, and stares up into the clear Marches sky. "That's all." She's just poured out her soul to you. "I've never been very good at talking to people, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Too often I say what I mean, you know?" You can imagine. That was another way of getting her point across, and a more effective one than simply trying to use words. So... [pc.bg minstrel |you might have been a minstrel before all this began, and while you're probably a little out of practice it's always good to hear what other cultures have to offer so you can use some ideas in your own music |you're not too well-versed in musical theory, but one doesn't have to be a renowned cook to recognize good food when you're eating it ]. This piece is something she figured out on her own, or...? Kinu still isn't looking at you [party.has kiyoko|or her mother], instead staring up at the sky. [rand |"No, not this time. I asked Granny Komari to see if there weren't any pieces she could help me find from across the ocean, give a growing girl something to do with her fingers. For some reason, she found that really funny, but came through nonetheless... "Haha, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], did you know that back in the Old Country, there used to be whole orders of monks who would play the shakuhachi? It got to the point where being able to play the instrument well was accepted as proof that you were a member of their order... it's still a land I will never see despite my blood, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], but even so, when I'm playing some of the pieces that inspired those selfsame people to write them centuries ago, and knowing how the days of my life inspire my own improv, I'm beginning to have some idea of what they must have felt to be able to compose such music." Hm. |"Yeah. I come up with my best pieces while in the fields, doing the dishes, or even something as simple as sweeping or wiping the floorboards. That kind of work, it empties the mind, and then you get to fill it with whatever you want; it's best when you find inspiration in the simplest of tasks. I... I don't intend to be a great composer, or even one who wants to appeal to other people, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Ultimately, I want my improv and composition to be for me, and about me, to express the world as it pertains to me. And strangely enough, when that happens, I garner some of my best pieces which everyone enjoys. ] "But look at me ramble, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Today isn't about me, it's about you. And so again... thanks for the gift, and I hope you liked what I had to give in return." "Don't take this the wrong way, but I think I'll be going. I...I need to be alone for a while. I know this is rude, but..." You understand. As she is, your fox-daughter wouldn't be of much use, anyway. "Thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. You know where to find me if you really need me." Still not turning back to you, Kinu starts out and away towards not the fields, to your minor surprise, but the waterfall by the den's entrance. One can only wonder what kind of expression she's got on her face right now that she doesn't want you to see it... [party.has kiyoko |"Well, that's that," Kiyoko says, pushing herself out of her seat[kiyoko.pregStage 2| with a little difficulty]. "She's made something of herself, I suppose, even if her behavior at the end there was incredibly wanting. Just running off like that...!" Was she like this growing up? When you were... away, that is. "It started when children get to that difficult age. Like with my brothers and sisters, I thought it'd pass as she matured out of it, but she hasn't. Getting all moody and resentful even as a young woman... ordinarily, I'd be worried about her marriage prospects, but that's not a problem, is it? I suppose I should be glad that that boy of Komari's is willing to take her, even if he is a simpleton." ...It looks like despite there being some progress forward, there's still a lot of ground between mother and daughter. Oh well, you never imagined this would be easy, would you? ]
rows.translation: 如果你不介意的话，可以跟我一起回我的住处吧。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我已经把它准备好了，就在那里等着你。 啊，好吧。你既然有时间，当然可以陪你的宝贝狐妖女儿玩玩闹闹了。 小娟带着你回到了她的房间，在路上停在了水井旁，洗了洗手部和前臂。回到房间后，她打开了墙边的一个箱子，开始在里面翻找起来，她的手臂都埋在了箱子的物品里。 [party.has kiyoko |哦天哪，我们不在的时候，我们女儿的房间竟然变得这么乱糟糟的。你的狐狸妻子绝望地说道，一边将一只充满绝望的手举到自己的脸颊上。从她还是个小孩子起，就总是把东西弄得乱七八糟的；我原本希望她能改掉这种对保持周围环境整洁毫不在意的态度，但看来我以后还是得再训斥她一次。 ] 看， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]，"你的狐女儿从箱子里取出她的竹笛，用一种只有母亲才会对新生儿表现出的温柔与细心，将它紧紧抱在怀中。那支竹笛对她来说，确实无比珍贵。我最近一直在练习几首新曲子，想在去麻里奶奶家演奏之前，先让你听听。上次你送了我这么珍贵的礼物，如果我不以同样的方式回报你，那就太失礼了。 用美妙的音乐来回报品尝水果带来的愉悦。你轻声笑了起来。没错，这样的交换确实值得。 我们去后院吧， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]你知道，一场表演必须能够吸引人的所有感官，对吧？ 就这样，小娟带着你穿过另一组屏风门，来到了后廊。在那里，她摆放了几块靠垫[party.has kiyoko |给你和你的狐狸妻子留了座位。清子[kiyoko.pregStage 2 |它安详地依偎在你身旁，那圆鼓鼓的孕肚在每一个动作中都显得那么优雅而高贵 |在你身边安静地坐下，默默地接受即将发生的一切 ]。 |[party.hasCompanions |可容纳……人[party.combatNames] |为您预留一个座位 ]。 ]你尽情地享受着这里的惬意，在木制甲板上找了个最舒服的位置坐下，等待着看看小娟会为你准备什么。从你所在的位置望去，眼前呈现出一幅由你的狐妖女儿亲手创造出来的美丽景象——在晨光中沐浴的田野和稻田，它们被火山口边缘的辽阔荒野所环绕，仿佛是大自然中的一片片被驯化的小角落，而野性的气息依然在它们周围弥漫。 小娟并没有看着你，她的目光正凝视着她深爱的旧国，背部紧紧倚靠在一根粗重的木梁上。她整个人都处于完全放松的状态，仿佛与周围的环境融为了一体；她的五条尾巴也随着她身体的轻微动作而左右摇摆。以狐族人的习惯来看，这种行为或许有些不合礼仪……但你的狐之女儿显然选择忽略这些规矩，而是选择让自己与音乐的灵魂融为一体。 说着，她将乐器的吹口贴近嘴唇，开始演奏起来。 渐渐地，音乐开始在空气中回荡——小娟从内心深处唤出了那些美妙的音符，她那经过长期练习而变得熟练的手指在 flute 上灵活地跳跃着，而她则闭着眼睛，全神贯注地投入到演奏之中。这段旋律十分庄严，音色深沉而丰富——如果你全身心地沉浸其中，就会感受到它所具有的冥想性与灵性。这种旋律具有安抚人心的效果，或许甚至有点过于舒缓了；如果你不保持警惕，它很可能会让你陷入沉睡…… [party.has kiyoko |她现在……比她年轻时的水平要好多了。清子轻叹着承认道。这种乐器的复杂性极高，而且缺乏适当的指导，因此学习它确实非常困难——尽管她通常学习新技能时总是表现得游刃有余。但她偏不按常理出牌，而是坚持要向我学习古筝。 她没有放弃。 我想，你也可以这么看。而且现在她确实取得了一些成就，这一点我得承认。至少，那些次我把她赶出家门，让她别再发出那么吵闹的声音，那些努力还是有些意义的…… ] 无论小娟正在演奏什么，无论那些音乐听起来多么陌生，你依然能够感受到它们。这种感受是彻底的、完全的，而且毫无疑问的。她这种情感，唯有她，或者那些与她心灵深处极为契合的人，才能够唤起——如此深沉的情感，如此萦绕心头的渴望，以及其中所蕴含的那种纯粹的空虚与满足感。小娟的手指在竹笛上灵活地跳跃着，她的呼吸平稳而均匀，以无比精准的方式将美妙的旋律从竹笛中演绎出来。再也不会有遗漏的音符，再也不会有走调的情况，只有一位勤奋的女孩和她的音乐，就像她年轻时那样，成为了森林和田野中的公主。 难道真的已经过去那么久了吗？那时她还只是一只在树枝的荫凉处奔跑的小狐妖，用双手偷取野蜂蜜，在泥土中挖掘…… 毕竟，田野不就是被人类驯服的荒野吗？花园虽然也要遵循自然规律，但也不能完全任其自由生长，否则就与荒野没有区别了。而最重要的是，那种挥之不去的孤独感、空旷的天空、辽阔的田野以及深邃的山景，才是这一切的基础。最终，音乐渐渐消失了，小娟放下了竹笛，她轻轻叹了口气，打破了原本平稳的呼吸节奏。她将头靠在背靠的横梁上，仰望着晴朗的三月天空。 就这些了。 她刚刚向你倾诉了自己的心声。 我从来都不擅长与人交谈。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]你知道吗，我很多时候说的其实就是我真正的想法。 你可以想象，这其实是另一种表达她意思的方式，而且比单纯使用语言更为有效。所以…… [pc.bg minstrel |在这一切开始之前，你或许曾经是一名吟游诗人。虽然你现在可能已经有点生疏了，但倾听其他文化带来的灵感总是很有帮助的——这样你就可以将自己所学到的元素运用到自己的音乐创作中 |虽然你对音乐理论的了解并不深入，但就像人们不需要成为著名的厨师就能分辨出美味的食物一样，辨别美食的品质其实并不需要深厚的专业知识 ]。 这件东西是她自己想出来的，还是……？ 琴奈仍然没有看着你。 [party.has kiyoko|或者她的母亲]而是抬头望着天空。 [rand |不，这次不行。我让麻里奶奶帮忙看看，是否能在大洋的另一边找到一些东西，让这个正在长个的女孩有点事情可以做，让她的手指也有点事情可忙。不知为什么，她觉得这个想法很有趣，但还是帮我去把事情办妥了…… 哈哈， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]你知道吗，在那个古老的国家，曾经有一整批僧侣都会演奏尺八这种乐器。甚至到了这样的地步：能够熟练演奏这种乐器，就被视为证明你属于他们那个僧团……尽管我流淌着那里的血液，但我却永远无法亲眼见到那个地方[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]然而，即便如此，当我演奏那些几个世纪前激发了那些人们创作灵感的乐曲时，当我意识到自己日常生活中的点滴经历是如何激发我的即兴创作灵感时，我开始逐渐理解他们当年创作出这样的音乐时一定是怀有怎样的情感。 嗯。 |是的，我总是在田野里劳作、洗碗，甚至是做一些像扫地或擦地板这样简单的事情时，才会产生最好的创作灵感。这样的工作能让大脑得到放松，然后你就可以把任何你想表达的东西填进其中；当你在最简单的任务中找到灵感时，效果往往最好。我……我并不是想成为一位伟大的作曲家，也不是想让我的作品去打动别人。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]归根结底，我希望自己的即兴创作和音乐作品能够真正属于我，反映我的内心世界，以此来表达那些与我息息相关的主题。说来也奇怪，当这样的目标真正实现时，我往往会创作出一些最出色的作品，而这些作品也深受大家的喜爱。 ] 但是看看我，一直在胡言乱语[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]今天不是关于我，而是关于你。所以，再次感谢你送给我的礼物，希望你也会喜欢我回赠你的东西。 别误会，我想我得离开了。我……需要一个人静一静。我知道这样有点不礼貌，但是…… 你明白的。以她现在的状况，你的那个狐妖女儿也根本没什么用处。 谢谢， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]如果你真的需要我的帮助，你知道该去哪里找我。小娟依然没有回头看向你，而是朝着与田野完全相反的方向走去——令你有些惊讶的是，她竟然走向了洞穴入口旁的瀑布那里。 人们不禁会想，此刻她脸上究竟带着什么样的表情，才会不愿意让你看到…… [party.has kiyoko |好吧，就这样吧。清子说着，从座位上站了起来。[kiyoko.pregStage 2| 费了些周折]。 我想，她终究还是取得了一些成就，尽管她最后的行为实在令人失望。就这样突然离开…… 她从小就是这样的吗？也就是在你不在家的那些时候。 这种情况在孩子们进入那个叛逆的年龄阶段时就会开始出现。我和我的兄弟姐妹们当初也以为，等她长大一些，这种行为就会消失，但事实并非如此。即使她还是个年轻女孩，也会变得情绪多变、充满怨恨……通常情况下，我会为她未来的婚姻担心，但这个问题应该不存在吧？其实，我觉得应该庆幸的是，麻里家的那个男孩愿意娶她，尽管他可能有点傻乎乎的。 ……看起来，尽管已经取得了一些进展，但母女之间的差距仍然很大。唉，谁会想到这件事会这么困难呢，对吧？ ]
rows.raw: " "If you don't mind following me back to my place, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? I've got it waiting there for you." Ah, all right. You can afford to humor your darling fox-daughter, you've got time, after all. Kinu leads you back to her chambers, stopping at the well on the way to wash off her hands and forearms. Once back, she throws open a trunk by the wall and starts rummaging about inside, buried up to her elbows in its contents. [party.has kiyoko |"Oh dear, our daughter's let her chambers run into such disarray while we were gone," your fox-wife says despondently, raising a despairing hand to her cheek. "Always messy ever since she was a kit; I'd hoped that she'd grow out of such a lackadaisical attitude towards keeping her surroundings neat, but it looks like I'll have to reprimand her later. Again." ] "There, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]," your fox-daughter pulls her shakuhachi out of the trunk and cradles it close to her bosom with all the gentleness and care befitting a newborn babe. That bamboo flute really is precious to her. "I've been practising a few new pieces, and wanted you to be the first to hear them before I started playing over at Granny Komari's. You gave me such a fine gift last time; it'd be remiss of me if I didn't repay you in kind." Repaying the taste of fruit with the sound of music. You chuckle. Yes, this is an acceptable trade. "Let's go out back, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. A performance's got to appeal to all the senses, you know?" So it happens that Kinu leads you through another set of screen doors out to the back porch, where she sets down several cushions as [party.has kiyoko |seats for you and your fox-wife. Kiyoko [kiyoko.pregStage 2 |nestles down in the comfortable softness beside you, looking dignified every step of the way with her large pregnant belly |settles down beside you, quietly resigning herself to what's to come ]. |[party.hasCompanions |seats for [party.combatNames] |a seat for you ]. ] You make yourself at home, getting as comfortable as you can on the wooden deck, and wait to see what Kinu's got in store for you. The view that greets you from where you are is a panorama of your fox-daughter's handiwork and life — fields and paddies in the morning sunshine, framed against the greater wilderness of the crater walls. Small squares of tamed nature at the feet of the breath of the wild, as it were. Kinu's not looking at you, her eyes gazing out over her beloved lands, her back firmly up against one of the heavy wooden beams. She's completely relaxed from head to toe, easing herself into the flow of her surroundings even as her five tails sway from side to side with the gentle movements of her body. This is probably some kind of breach of etiquette, knowing the kitsune people... but your fox-daughter's clearly decided to do away with it in favor of being one with the soul of her music. With that, she raises the instrument's mouthpiece to her lips and begins to play. Slowly, music begins to fill the air as Kinu brings out her music from the depths of her being, her work-hardened fingers dancing over the flute's length as she closes her eyes in concentration. The tune is solemn with a deep and rich timbre — practically meditative and spiritual, if you allow yourself to get caught up in it. It's calming, perhaps a little too much so, threatening to lull you to sleep if you don't keep your guard up... [party.has kiyoko |"She is... considerably better than she was at it when she was younger," Kiyoko admits with a small sigh. "The sheer complexity of the instrument and lack of any proper tutoring made learning it problematic, even with the ease with which she usually picks up new skills and learning. But she refused to be a good girl and learn the koto from me instead." She didn't give up. "You could see it that way, I suppose. And now she has made something of herself, I will admit. At least all those times I sent her out of the house to stop making such a horrendous din were worth something..." ] Whatever it is Kinu's playing, however foreign-sounding the music, you nevertheless manage to feel it. It is completely, fully, and undoubtedly her, something that only she, or someone very close in spirit to her, would have been able to evoke — such richness, such haunting longing, such simple emptiness and satisfaction at the heart of it all. Kinu's fingers dance across the shakuhachi, her breath steady and measured as she coaxes her tune out of the bamboo flute with perfect precision. No more missed notes, no more going off-key, just a working girl and her music, a princess of the forests and fields as she was in her youth. Was it so long ago that she was but a tiny fox-kit running in the shade of branches, stealing wild honey and digging in the dirt with her bare hands? After all, what is a field but wilderness tamed? A garden still has to follow the laws of nature, yet cannot run completely wild lest there be no difference between the two. And above it all, that underpinning of haunting loneliness, of empty skies, vast fields and deep mountain vistas... Eventually, the music dies down, Kinu lowers the bamboo flute, and she breaks the steady rhythm of her breathing with a small sigh. She leans her head back against the beam she's up against, and stares up into the clear Marches sky. "That's all." She's just poured out her soul to you. "I've never been very good at talking to people, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Too often I say what I mean, you know?" You can imagine. That was another way of getting her point across, and a more effective one than simply trying to use words. So... [pc.bg minstrel |you might have been a minstrel before all this began, and while you're probably a little out of practice it's always good to hear what other cultures have to offer so you can use some ideas in your own music |you're not too well-versed in musical theory, but one doesn't have to be a renowned cook to recognize good food when you're eating it ]. This piece is something she figured out on her own, or...? Kinu still isn't looking at you [party.has kiyoko|or her mother], instead staring up at the sky. [rand |"No, not this time. I asked Granny Komari to see if there weren't any pieces she could help me find from across the ocean, give a growing girl something to do with her fingers. For some reason, she found that really funny, but came through nonetheless... "Haha, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], did you know that back in the Old Country, there used to be whole orders of monks who would play the shakuhachi? It got to the point where being able to play the instrument well was accepted as proof that you were a member of their order... it's still a land I will never see despite my blood, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], but even so, when I'm playing some of the pieces that inspired those selfsame people to write them centuries ago, and knowing how the days of my life inspire my own improv, I'm beginning to have some idea of what they must have felt to be able to compose such music." Hm. |"Yeah. I come up with my best pieces while in the fields, doing the dishes, or even something as simple as sweeping or wiping the floorboards. That kind of work, it empties the mind, and then you get to fill it with whatever you want; it's best when you find inspiration in the simplest of tasks. I... I don't intend to be a great composer, or even one who wants to appeal to other people, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Ultimately, I want my improv and composition to be for me, and about me, to express the world as it pertains to me. And strangely enough, when that happens, I garner some of my best pieces which everyone enjoys. ] "But look at me ramble, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Today isn't about me, it's about you. And so again... thanks for the gift, and I hope you liked what I had to give in return." "Don't take this the wrong way, but I think I'll be going. I...I need to be alone for a while. I know this is rude, but..." You understand. As she is, your fox-daughter wouldn't be of much use, anyway. "Thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. You know where to find me if you really need me." Still not turning back to you, Kinu starts out and away towards not the fields, to your minor surprise, but the waterfall by the den's entrance. One can only wonder what kind of expression she's got on her face right now that she doesn't want you to see it... [party.has kiyoko |"Well, that's that," Kiyoko says, pushing herself out of her seat[kiyoko.pregStage 2| with a little difficulty]. "She's made something of herself, I suppose, even if her behavior at the end there was incredibly wanting. Just running off like that...!" Was she like this growing up? When you were... away, that is. "It started when children get to that difficult age. Like with my brothers and sisters, I thought it'd pass as she matured out of it, but she hasn't. Getting all moody and resentful even as a young woman... ordinarily, I'd be worried about her marriage prospects, but that's not a problem, is it? I suppose I should be glad that that boy of Komari's is willing to take her, even if he is a simpleton." ...It looks like despite there being some progress forward, there's still a lot of ground between mother and daughter. Oh well, you never imagined this would be easy, would you? ] "

rows.original: "Right. In fact, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I've got your gift right here." Where? "Like I said, right here." Before you know it, your fox-daughter's beaming at you and spread her arms wide to catch you in a great big hug. Her hands wrap themselves about your waist and her ears tickle your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun]. You can feel the white fur rubbing up against you even as Kinu's tails brush against your legs in broad, sweeping strokes, tickling you with their tips. Ahh. The years have been kind to Kinu, and your fox-daughter is a lot warmer these days than when she was a child; while Kinu is less fluffy than her mother is, her fur has a flowing texture to it that reminds you of a warm breeze's caress. Once again, your fox-daughter proves her namesake every step of the way, her fine fur quite possibly the best, warmest and softest material to ever grace your touch, with the exception of her mother's, of course. It must run in the family... you lean into the hug, giving Kinu several pats on the head atop her headcloth, and she heaves a sigh. "Of all the things I missed about you when you were away, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]... I missed this the most. Growing up, dealing with Mother when I was at an awkward age... I knew you didn't visit any more for a reason, but even so... "Just, uh, thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. This is for more than just the fruit." It's all right. You're together with her mother now, and your family is reunited in firm reality. She has fields, friends, family... Kinu says nothing, but flicks a ear, tickling your collarbone. You laugh and give her a final pat on the head before breaking the hug and pushing your fox-daughter's weight off you. "I don't know if you felt it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], but I really hope that you felt my gratitude passing on to you back there." Your fox-daughter scratches the back of her head and sticks her tongue out at you sheepishly. "I've never been too good at expressing myself with words, so I hope that was good enough to get the message across. Actions speak louder, you know?" Ah, of course you felt it; you felt a lot more than mere gratitude there. You're very proud of her, and how she's grown into a fine young woman. "Thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. So... is there anything else you need at the moment?"
rows.translation: 没错。事实上， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]你的礼物就在我这里。 在哪里？ 就像我说的，就在这里。还没等你反应过来，你的狐狸女儿就已经笑盈盈地朝你跑过来，张开双臂想要给你一个热情的拥抱。她的双手紧紧搂住你的腰，耳朵轻轻搔过你的[pc.skinFurScalesNoun]你可以感受到那白色的毛茸茸的毛发轻轻擦过你的身体，而小娟的尾巴则以宽阔而有力的动作拂过你的双腿，尾巴的尖端轻轻挠着你，让你感到痒痒的。 啊，这些年来，小娟过得很好，你的狐狸女儿如今也比她小时候温暖多了；虽然小娟的毛没有她母亲那么浓密，但它的毛质柔软而顺滑，让人感受到如同暖风轻拂般的舒适。你的狐狸女儿又一次证明了她与这个名字的匹配程度——她的柔软皮毛无疑是迄今为止最舒适、最温暖、最细腻的触感材料，当然，除了她母亲的皮毛之外。这种特质显然是个家族遗传的特点。你紧紧地拥抱着她，轻轻拍了拍小娟头上的头巾，而她则松了一口气。 在你离开的那些日子里，有太多关于你的东西让我感到怀念[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]……这一点我最为怀念。在成长过程中，尤其是在那些尴尬的年纪，与母亲相处……我知道你不再来看她是有原因的，但即便如此…… 只是，呃，谢谢。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]这不仅仅是为了那些水果。 没关系。现在你和她妈妈在一起了，你们的家庭终于真正团聚了。她有自己的田地、朋友和家人…… 小娟没有说话，只是轻轻动动耳朵，挠了挠你的锁骨。你笑着，最后再轻拍她的头一次，然后才松开拥抱，让这个像狐狸一样的女儿从你身上下来。 我不知道你是否感觉到了， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]但我真心希望，你们能感受到我那份感激之情正在传递给你们。你的狐狸女儿挠了挠后脑勺，然后害羞地吐了吐舌头看着你。我从来都不太擅长用语言来表达自己，所以希望我的表述能够足够清楚地传达我的意思。你知道，行动胜于言语。 啊，你当然感受到了；你感受到的远不止是一份感激之情。你为她感到非常骄傲，也为她成长为一位优秀的年轻女性而感到欣慰。 谢谢， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]那么……你现在还有其他什么需要吗？

rows.original: "Yeah, right, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. You don't mind coming with me to the shed for a bit, do you? I wasn't about to lug it around on me while I was in the fields — might get dirty or bumped around, you know? Come on, then. Let's see what your little princess of the fields has for you. Beaming, Kinu leads you around the fields until you reach the shed in question, and sitting upon one of the wooden beams piled up for storage is a large box wrapped in green patterned cloth and a simple ribbon. Picking it up, Kinu dusts a couple of wood shavings off the bottom and presents it to you with both hands. "There we go, for the bestest [pc.mf|dad|mom] in the world! Wrapped in traditional style, simple and yet meaningful — just like me!" That's so sweet of her. You take the box from your fox-daughter; it's suitably heavy, with something that rattles around inside when you move it. "Eh, nah. What's sweet is that you still manage to remember me while you're out there and care enough to bring me gifts whenever you come home. So... if you want more gifts like these, come home often and bring me lots of presents, okay? But if you don't have that many presents to give... coming home often will be enough." ... Kinu looks away and down, rubbing the backs of her ears, then breaks into a forced, cheery smile. "N-now [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], remember that you aren't supposed to open gifts while in front of the giver. It's rude. So with that in mind... is there anything else you wanted from me?" You have gained 1x kitsune gift.
rows.translation: “对了，[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]。你不介意陪我去一趟棚屋吧？我在田里干活时可不想一直带着它——你也知道，可能会弄脏，或是磕着碰着。 来吧。看看你的田野小公主为你准备了什么。 小娟笑容灿烂，领着你穿过田地，来到她所说的棚屋。一只用绿色花布包好、系着朴素丝带的大盒子，正放在一堆入库存放的木梁上。小娟将盒子抱起来，掸掉底部的几片木屑，双手捧到你面前。 “好啦，这是送给全世界最最棒的[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]的！用传统方式包装，朴素却饱含心意——就像我一样！” 她真贴心。你从狐女儿手中接过盒子；分量十足，挪动时还能听见里面有什么东西在轻轻作响。 “哎，也没有啦。真正贴心的是，你人在外面还总能惦记着我，每次回家也愿意给我带礼物。所以……要是还想收到这种礼物，就常回家、多给我带些礼物，好吗？不过，要是没有那么多礼物可送……经常回家看看就够了。” …… 小娟移开视线，垂下头揉了揉耳朵后方，随后挤出一个强作欢快的笑容。“现、现在，[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]，记住不该当着送礼人的面拆开礼物。这很失礼。所以……你找我还有别的事吗？” 你获得了1份狐妖礼物。
rows.raw: " "Yeah, right, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. You don't mind coming with me to the shed for a bit, do you? I wasn't about to lug it around on me while I was in the fields — might get dirty or bumped around, you know? Come on, then. Let's see what your little princess of the fields has for you. Beaming, Kinu leads you around the fields until you reach the shed in question, and sitting upon one of the wooden beams piled up for storage is a large box wrapped in green patterned cloth and a simple ribbon. Picking it up, Kinu dusts a couple of wood shavings off the bottom and presents it to you with both hands. "There we go, for the bestest [pc.mf|dad|mom] in the world! Wrapped in traditional style, simple and yet meaningful — just like me!" That's so sweet of her. You take the box from your fox-daughter; it's suitably heavy, with something that rattles around inside when you move it. "Eh, nah. What's sweet is that you still manage to remember me while you're out there and care enough to bring me gifts whenever you come home. So... if you want more gifts like these, come home often and bring me lots of presents, okay? But if you don't have that many presents to give... coming home often will be enough." ... Kinu looks away and down, rubbing the backs of her ears, then breaks into a forced, cheery smile. "N-now [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], remember that you aren't supposed to open gifts while in front of the giver. It's rude. So with that in mind... is there anything else you wanted from me?" You have gained 1x kitsune gift. "

rows.original: "Just a moment, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I've got it keeping warm in my place. If you wouldn't mind coming back with me?" Of course you don't mind. It's a short walk from the fields to Kinu's chambers, and your fox-daughter slides open the screen door and bids you inside. So, what's up. Turning away from you, Kinu washes her hands in a small basin out back, crosses over to the firepit that's the centerpiece of her chambers and kneels over the glowing charcoal embers. She's got something keeping warm over a grate directly in the path of the warm air rising into the room, and it's with care that she pulls it out and blows on it a few times to cool it down. Ah, that smell... salty, savoury broth, filled with vegetables of the field and wilds. You know what this is. Your fox-daughter gives you an embarrassed grin. "Am I that predictable, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]?" At times, she really is... but that's not a bad thing in and of itself. She's a good, reliable girl, and even though this means she uses herself as a locus from which to decide on gifts for other people instead of the receiver, what's important here is the spirit in which it's given. Now, she can go ahead and present you with your kenchin soup. "Ah ha ha ha. Figures it's not much of a guess then. I always feel warm and good inside after I have some, and I'm sure you'll too; everyone who's tasted my kenchin soup agrees. All right, let me get all this in order..." Within the minute, Kinu's ushered you down to the low table and sat you down before an uncovered bowl of the slowly steaming she loves so much, complete with utensils at the ready.[party.has kiyoko | She's got another one for her mother, too, and helps her down onto a cushion at the table opposite you. "Here, Mother. I made some for you, too." "That will suffice." Kiyoko's voice warms a little, and the tension in the air drains. Perhaps, for once, for you, mother and daughter can come to an accord for the person they both care about. "Thank you." Kinu dips her head and withdraws, shuffling away and holding her tails close to her body. For such a carefree spirit, she still has some regard for decorum when she has the mind to. ] "There. Please... as repayment for the gift that I so graciously received from you... drink up, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Everything's local, except for the tofu; that's from across the ocean. Soybeans don't really grow well in this soil, but I'm working on it." Across the ocean, eh? You give your fox-daughter simple fruit, and are rewarded with foreign delicacies. You truly are one lucky [pc.manWoman]. "Ah, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], well... you've done so much for Mother and I already. This is nothing by comparison..." [party.has kiyoko |"Ah, perhaps you should begin, beloved." Kiyoko flicks a ear in your direction. "The soup is getting cold." Of course, of course |Ah, enough talk. It's about time you got started; the soup is getting cold ]. You pick up the spoon, and apply yourself. Ah... does it taste so good because Kinu is so adept at coaxing the earth into giving up its fruits, or it is because it's your fox-daughter who has applied herself into preparing such simple preciousness just for you? You cast a glance at Kinu, who is standing by and trying to appear impassive; she's never been one for concealing her emotions, even when she wants to. It's very good. Better than the fruit you gave her. "Don't say such things, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I don't like it when people put themselves down just to make others feel better." No, you honestly feel that way. [party.has kiyoko |"It is very good. No matter how much we may disagree, daughter, I will not lie when it comes to which of your talents you've chosen to cultivate." ] Kinu gives [party.has kiyoko|both you and her mother|you] a long, hard gaze, then her expression softens into a smile. "All right, if you say so, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." The remainder of the repast passes in silence, until your spoon is scraping the bottom of the empty bowl. A heavy, liquid warmth sits in the pit of your stomach, and all is right with the world. Even so, though, you've got to get going. "Yeah, I've got to head back into the fields, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Stay safe out there, okay?[party.has kiyoko| That, and take care of Mother for me, all right?]" Without waiting for a reply, Kinu turns away and hurries off down the dirt trail back to her post amongst the fields. A little brash, perhaps, but you understand why. You'll leave the dishes here for her to clean up when she returns...
rows.translation: 稍等片刻， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我把它放在家里保暖了。如果你不介意的话，可以和我一起回去吧？ 你当然不会介意。从田野走到小娟的房间只需要走一小段路，你的狐狸女儿会推开门让你进去。 那么，最近怎么样？ 小娟转过身去，在屋后的一个小水盆里洗手部，然后走到她房间中央的火堆旁，在发光的炭火旁跪了下来。她把某样东西放在一个栅格上，正好位于暖空气上升进入房间的路径上，这样就能保持它的温度。她小心翼翼地把它取出来，吹了几下让它凉下来。 啊，那种味道……咸鲜的汤汁，里面充满了田野里和野外采集的各种蔬菜。你知道这是什么。 你的狐狸女儿尴尬地对你笑了笑。我真有那么容易被猜到吗？ [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]？" 有时候，她确实会这样……但这也并非坏事。她是个善良、可靠的女孩。虽然这意味着她常常会先为自己考虑，再决定送给别人什么礼物，而不是根据收礼人的需求来选择，但关键在于送礼时的心意。现在，她可以把你的“kenchin汤”呈现在你面前了。 啊哈哈，果然这么容易猜到。每次喝了我的汤之后，我都会觉得心里暖暖的、很舒服，我相信你也会这么觉得的；所有尝过我做的汤的人都是这么说的。好吧，让我先把这些事情安排好…… 不一会儿，小娟就带你来到那张低矮的桌子旁，让你坐下，面前是一碗热气腾腾的、她非常喜爱的食物，所需的餐具也已经准备好了。[party.has kiyoko | 她还为她的母亲准备了一个，然后帮她坐到你对面桌子上的垫子上。 给，妈妈，我也为您准备了一些。 这样就可以了。清子的声音变得柔和了一些，空气中的紧张气氛也随之消散了。或许，这一次，对于你们母女来说，能够为了那个你们都关心的人达成共识吧。谢谢。 小娟低下了头，然后退了回去，拖着脚步走开，同时把尾巴紧紧地贴在身体上。尽管她性格如此洒脱不羁，但当她认真起来的时候，还是会注意一些礼仪规范的。 ] 来，请喝吧……作为对我从你这里收到的这份礼物的回报……喝光它吧。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]除了豆腐之外，所有材料都是本地采购的；豆腐可是从大洋对岸运来的。虽然这种土壤并不适合种植大豆，但我正在尝试解决这个问题。 隔着大洋啊？你给自己的狐狸女儿一些普通的水果，却得到了外国的美食作为回报。你真是太幸运了。 [pc.manWoman]。 啊， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]嗯……你已经为妈妈和我做了太多事情，这点贡献相比之下简直微不足道…… [party.has kiyoko |啊，也许你应该开始了，亲爱的。清子朝你的方向甩了甩耳朵。汤要凉了。 当然，当然。 |啊，说够了。是时候开始行动了；汤都要凉掉啦。 ]你拿起勺子，开始享用起来。啊……难道这味道如此美妙，是因为小娟太擅长让大地慷慨地献出它的果实，还是因为你的狐狸女儿为了让你们品尝到这份简单的美味而付出了这么多努力呢？你瞥了眼站在一旁、努力装作若无其事的小娟——她从来都不是个善于隐藏自己情绪的人，即使她想要这么做的时候也不例外。 真的很好吃，比你之前给她的那些水果还要美味。 别这么说， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我讨厌人们为了让别人感觉好而贬低自己。 不，你是真的这么觉得的。 [party.has kiyoko |这很好。无论我们之间有多少分歧，女儿，关于你选择培养哪方面的才能，我绝不会说谎。 ] 小娟给予了[party.has kiyoko|你和她母亲两个人|你]她长久而凝视着对方，随后她的表情变得柔和，露出了微笑。好吧，既然你这么说了[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]。" 剩下的饭菜在沉默中被吃完，直到你的勺子刮到了空碗的下装。一种沉重而温暖的感受停留在你的胃里，整个世界似乎都变得如此美好。然而，尽管如此，你还是得继续前进了。 是的，我得回去田里了。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]在外面一定要注意安全，好吗？[party.has kiyoko| 还有，帮我照顾好妈妈，好吗？]" 没有等待任何回应，小娟转身沿着那条土路匆匆离去，回到了田野间的自己的岗位。或许她有点冒失，但你也明白其中的原因。等她回来后，你可以把盘子留在这里，让她来清理……

rows.original: Kinu nips over to the rim of the firepit and bends over to pick up what looks like a small statuette. As she brings it back to you, you realize what it is: a small effigy of a fox, meticulously put together from rice straw and complete with a tiny red bib tied about its neck. It could fit easily into your palm, and as Kinu presents it to you with both hands you also realize that it's also quite light. "I wove it myself. For luck." You turn the little straw fox over in your palms, wondering at the detailed, if highly stylised features. It's a lovely little figurine, that's for sure. "It will not last, but it is not meant to. The Trickster's luck can be powerful, but it is not interesting if everyone wins all the time. You have to take the good with the bad, and realize that fortune is as fickle as it is fleeting. The little straw fox will fall apart of its own accord in a few days, but it is a reminder of the transience of everything around us, and a call to enjoy things while they last." That's very erudite of her. "Thank you." Well, you'll just have to keep on giving her more gifts so that you can keep on getting more little straw foxes from her, then. Kinu chances a little smile. "I do not imagine it is intended to work that way, but the unintended and unexpected is what his divine lordship is all about. Now then, is there anything else I can help you with?" She foresaw your arrival and prepared a gift for you, but she didn't divine that? Your fox-daughter's smile widens. "I am afraid not. Once more... is there anything I can aid you with?"
rows.translation: 小娟走到火坑边缘，弯下腰捡起了那个看起来像是小雕像的东西。当她把它递给你时，你才意识到那是什么：一个用稻草精心制作的小狐狸雕像，脖子上还系着一条红色的小围巾。这个雕像小到可以轻松放在你的手掌中，而当小娟用双手将它递给你时，你也感觉到它确实非常轻。 这是我亲手编织的。为了祈求好运。 你将那只小稻草狐狸在手掌中翻来覆去，仔细观察它那些细致而极具风格化的特征。毫无疑问，这是一个非常可爱的小雕像。 这种状态不会持续太久，其实也本来就不是为了长久而存在的。骗子的运气或许很强，但如果所有人都一直获胜，那就没什么意思了。我们必须接受好事与坏事并存的事实，也要明白：命运既多变又短暂。那只小稻草狐狸过几天就会自行分解，但它提醒我们，周围的一切都是如此短暂易逝，因此我们应该在事物还在的时候好好享受它们。 她真是博学多才啊。 谢谢。 嗯，那你只能继续给她送礼物，这样你才能继续从她那里得到那些小稻草狐狸吧。 纪久露出了一丝微笑。我并不认为它是按照那种方式设计的，但恰恰正是这些意外的、不可预测的结果，才真正体现了他那位神圣主人的行事风格。那么，还有什么我可以帮您的吗？ 她预料到了你的到来，还为你准备了一份礼物，但她并没有预见到这一点吧？ 你那位狐狸女儿的笑容更加灿烂了。恐怕不能。那么再次问一下……还有什么我可以帮您的吗？

rows.original: Crossing over to a cupboard on the side of the room, Kinu draws out a large box wrapped in pretty decorated green-and-white cloth, patterned with swirls. She has a little trouble retrieving it from the high shelf, but eventually manages and returns to you with it in both hands. "A gift wrapped in traditional style, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I tried to pick out something that would be helpful to you on your travels." The wrapping may be simple, but it's clear that Kinu's spent an inordinate amount of time on the gift's presentation — there's nary a wrinkle in the cloth wrapping, and the bow about the top is incredibly elaborate. Your fox-daughter holds it out to you in both hands, and you take hold of it gingerly, a sense of ceremony descending upon the whole occasion without you knowing in the least what's really expected of you here... kitsune really have so many little behaviors and responses that they expect from each other as a matter of course, but are completely opaque to those who aren't from their homeland. The box is a little heavy, and you feel something rattling about inside when you hold it in both hands. Wonder what Kinu thought fit as a return gift for all your kindness... "Other peoples say of us that the truest of kitsune gifts are immaterial things like good fortune or wisdom, and that material items tend to dissolve into worthless sticks and piles of leaves come the sunrise. I don't have any good fortunate or wisdom to give, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], so I suppose this will have to do." Aww. Let's face it. Even if she did give you a bunch of sticks or a pile of leaves, they would be far from worthless because they came from her. That's what counts — stepping up to Kinu, you tuck her gift under an arm and pat her on the head between the ears with the other. Your fox-daughter fidgets. "That is really ticklish, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]..." Well, of course it is. You really appreciate the reciprocal gift, and if anything it's encouragement for you to give her more things in the future. "Ah. Oh. Um. Well, now that we have dealt with that, is there anything else you require of me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?"
rows.translation: 小娟走到房间一侧的橱柜前，取出了一个用装饰着漂亮花纹的绿白相间布料包裹起来的大盒子。她费了些劲才从高高的架子上取下它，最终还是成功取了下来，然后双手捧着它回到了你面前。 一份用传统方式包装的礼物， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]我试图挑选一些在您的旅途中会对您有帮助的东西。 包装可能很简单，但很明显，小娟在礼物的装饰上花费了大量的时间——包装布上没有一丝褶皱，顶端的蝴蝶结也做得极其精致。你的狐妖女儿用双手将礼物递给你，你小心翼翼地接过了它，整个场景突然间仿佛充满了一种仪式感，而你却完全不知道别人真正期望你做出什么反应…… 狐妖们确实有很多细微的行为和反应，它们将这些视为理所当然的事情，但对于那些并非来自它们故乡的人来说，这些行为和反应完全无法理解。 这个盒子有点重，当你用双手握住它的时候，能感觉到里面有什么东西在晃动。不知道小娟会想到送什么礼物来感谢你所有的善意…… 别人常说，狐妖赠送的最珍贵的礼物其实是那些无形的东西，比如好运或智慧，而那些有形的物品，往往在黎明到来时就会化作一堆毫无价值的树枝和落叶。而我，既没有好运可以给予，也没有智慧可以传授[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]所以，我想也只能这样做了。 哎呀，说实话吧。就算她给了你一堆树枝或一堆树叶，这些东西也绝对不是毫无价值的，因为它们毕竟是她亲手带来的。她这才是最重要的——你走到小娟身边，把她的礼物夹在胳膊下，另一只手轻拍她的脑袋。 你的狐妖女儿坐立不安，显得很焦躁。那真的有点痒[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]……" 嗯，当然啦。你真的非常感激这份回赠，事实上，这反而激励你在未来继续送她更多的礼物。 啊……哦……嗯，既然我们已经解决了那个问题，还有其他什么事情需要我做的吗？ [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]？"
rows.raw: " Crossing over to a cupboard on the side of the room, Kinu draws out a large box wrapped in pretty decorated green-and-white cloth, patterned with swirls. She has a little trouble retrieving it from the high shelf, but eventually manages and returns to you with it in both hands. "A gift wrapped in traditional style, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I tried to pick out something that would be helpful to you on your travels." The wrapping may be simple, but it's clear that Kinu's spent an inordinate amount of time on the gift's presentation — there's nary a wrinkle in the cloth wrapping, and the bow about the top is incredibly elaborate. Your fox-daughter holds it out to you in both hands, and you take hold of it gingerly, a sense of ceremony descending upon the whole occasion without you knowing in the least what's really expected of you here... kitsune really have so many little behaviors and responses that they expect from each other as a matter of course, but are completely opaque to those who aren't from their homeland. The box is a little heavy, and you feel something rattling about inside when you hold it in both hands. Wonder what Kinu thought fit as a return gift for all your kindness... "Other peoples say of us that the truest of kitsune gifts are immaterial things like good fortune or wisdom, and that material items tend to dissolve into worthless sticks and piles of leaves come the sunrise. I don't have any good fortunate or wisdom to give, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], so I suppose this will have to do." Aww. Let's face it. Even if she did give you a bunch of sticks or a pile of leaves, they would be far from worthless because they came from her. That's what counts — stepping up to Kinu, you tuck her gift under an arm and pat her on the head between the ears with the other. Your fox-daughter fidgets. "That is really ticklish, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]..." Well, of course it is. You really appreciate the reciprocal gift, and if anything it's encouragement for you to give her more things in the future. "Ah. Oh. Um. Well, now that we have dealt with that, is there anything else you require of me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?" "

rows.original: Smiling, your fox-daughter crosses over to the firepit and picks up a tightly-wrapped bundle of wax paper. Returning to your side, she sets it down in your arms with both hands and steps back with a bow. "It is not much, but I have prepared some of the native foods in a non-perishable fashion," Kinu begins. "Please make sure that [party.has kiyoko|Mother and ]you eat well while on your travels, and when you do, remember what and more importantly, who you are fighting for." That's very thoughtful of her. "I would have prepared a lunch box in my style, but it is important in your circumstances for form to follow function. Hence, while I have endeavored to enhance its presentation as much as possible, being nourishing, resistant to the elements and compact all took precedence. It is but a small gift for the ones that you have bestowed upon me all this time, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." You have received 1x trail rations. Ah, shucks. You step up and give Kinu a pat on the head between the ears; she bears your affection in a manner most befitting of the vulpine princess she's grown to become. Well, you'll make use of her gift in the finest fashion, you're sure. "Then that is well. Now then, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], is there anything else you need of me?" She didn't divine that? "No." Well, in that case...
rows.translation: 微笑着，你的狐女儿走到火堆旁，拿起了一个用蜡纸紧紧包裹好的包裹。回到你身边后，她用双手将包裹放在你的怀里，然后鞠了一躬退了回去。 虽然不多，但我已经把一些当地的食物加工成了可以长期保存的形式。游戏开始了。请务必确保[party.has kiyoko|母亲和…… ]在旅途中，一定要保证自己的饮食健康，而当你享受美食的时候，千万不要忘记自己为何而战，以及自己究竟在为谁而奋斗。 她真是太体贴了。 我本来想用自己擅长的方式准备一个午餐盒，但在你目前的处境下，实用性才是最重要的。因此，虽然我尽力让它看起来更美观，但营养丰富、能够抵御外界环境的影响以及体积小巧这些因素才是我最看重的。这只是一个小小的礼物，用来感谢你一直以来给予我的一切。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]。" 您已收到1份试用补给品。 哎呀，真遗憾。你走上前去，轻轻拍拍小娟的脑袋吧；她一定会以一位高贵而优雅的狐狸公主应有的方式来接受你的关爱。相信你一定会把她的这份天赋运用得恰到好处。 那就好。那么，接下来[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]还有其他什么需要我帮忙的吗？ 她竟然没有猜到吗？ 不。 那么，在那种情况下……

rows.original: A small smile spreads over Kinu's face and she closes her eyes and squares her shoulders. Before you know it, your fox-daughter has stepped forward on tiptoe, reaching [pc.heightRange 60|up|over] to give you a quick peck on the cheek. It is very warm... "There we go," your fox-daughter quips as the steps back with all the grace and poise of a princess. "Consider this my reciprocal gift for the kindness you have recently shown me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Ah, well. You give Kinu a pat on the head between the ears, eliciting a giggle from your fox-daughter.[party.has kiyoko| Standing beside you, Kiyoko just shakes her head and smiles. "Now then, daughter, let's just be sure we understand this: your [pc.mf|father|mother] is mine, and I'm not giving [pc.himHer] up. Not even for you, as much as I love you. Are we clear?" "M-mother? What are you saying?!" Kiyoko laughs. "Ehehehe. You should see your face, my dear. That was completely worth teasing you for, and... I'm not sorry. Ehehehe." ] Now, now. You came here for business with Kinu other than teasing her, and ought to be about it. Was there something you needed her for?
rows.translation: 小娟的脸上浮现出一丝微笑，她闭上眼睛，挺直肩膀。转眼间，你的狐狸女儿就已经踮起脚尖向前走了几步[pc.heightRange 60|向上|超过]轻轻亲一下你的脸颊。感觉非常温暖…… 就这样吧。你那位机智的女儿一边后退，一边以公主般优雅的姿态说着俏皮话。请将这份礼物视为我对您最近所给予我的善意的回报吧。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]。" 啊，好吧。你轻轻拍拍小娟的脑袋，这让你的狐狸女儿咯咯地笑了起来。[party.has kiyoko| 站在你身边，清子只是轻轻摇头，然后微笑着。 那么，女儿，我们必须弄清楚这一点：你的[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]这是我的，我不会放弃。 [pc.himHer]不行。即使我再爱你，也不行。我们明白了吗？ 妈、妈？你在说什么啊？！ 清子笑了。嘿嘿嘿，你看看自己现在的样子吧，亲爱的。这样的你确实值得被取笑呢……而且，我一点也不后悔。嘿嘿嘿。 ] 好了好了。你来到这里本来是和小娟谈公事的，而不是来逗她玩的，应该认真谈正事吧。是不是有什么事情需要她帮忙呢？

rows.original: With that, Kinu disappears into the adjoining chamber and emerges with her koto. The instrument should be a bit heavy for her, but it looks like she's used to toting the thing around without too many problems. Taking small, careful steps, your fox-daughter pushes open another screen door and slips out to the back deck. "[pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]if you would follow me?" By the time you've followed her out, Kinu's got everything set up; she's clearly done this ahead of time. With her koto set out on a small woven mat facing the seats that you're supposed to take, her flower garden and fish pond a backdrop for her vulpine elegance, Kinu gives you a small bow. "Please, take [party.has kiyoko|your seats|a seat]. I have recently learned a new piece, and would like [party.has kiyoko|the two of you|you] to be my first audience before I perform it for the people at Matron Komari's. Consider this a gift in return for the one that you were so kind to bestow upon me the last time. What better return gift to have than to be the first to savour some fine music?" That's... that's very kind of her. [party.has kiyoko |"Hmm." Smiling, Kiyoko steps up to Kinu and gives your fox-daughter a tap on the leg with one of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tail-tips. "And if I may inquire, which piece might that be?" "Ah, Mother, um..." "Ah, you're coloring! There's no need to be embarrassed, child. Which piece have you been practising for your [pc.mf|father|mother]?" Her cheeks and the bridge of her nose red, Kinu leans in on tiptoe and whispers into one of her mother's large ears. Kiyoko listens attentively, then her smile grows wider and positively mischievous as she steps back and foxes her gaze on your fox-daughter. "Why, I know that one too. Why don't I get my koto and we'll perform together for your [pc.mf|father|mother]? There's much I have to be thankful to [pc.himHer] for, and we can show our gratitude as one." "Ah, Mother, I —" Kinu's about to heave a deep sigh and catches herself midway, turning it into a calming breath. "While I believe it is meant to be played solo, I would be very grateful if you were there to guide me, as you always have been. It would give me a lot more confidence." "At this point, I know when you're looking for help, even when you don't know it yourself. Don't worry, my child; your mother will be with you for as long as she's able. Now... if you would wait here?" Kiyoko is good to her word. Barely a handful of minutes have departed before your fox-wife returns with her own koto and a mat. She pulls up her own cushion, nestles herself in amidst her [kiyoko.pregStage 2|big belly and ][kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails, and motions for Kinu to take her position as well. Seeing them side by side like this, working together for your sake... you can't help but smile a little at the sight of a harmonious family like this. As the saying goes, it was totally worth it. Kiyoko is circumspect, letting Kinu take the lead; she deliberately remains in the background, playing second fiddle so as to not upstage your daughter's performance. This is Kinu's hour, after all, not hers, and she knows as much. You're not quite sure what to think. The melody's definitely foreign to your ears — [pc.bg minstrel|as someone trained in the musical arts yourself, it's always nice to hear something that's out of the ordinary, perhaps pinch some of the better ideas in it for your own use|but that isn't about to dampen your enjoyment of your daughter's performance, though]. It's lively, flowing and energetic, while still oozing elegance from every note Kinu plucks from the strings. She's putting a lot of feeling and soul into her playing, that's for sure. But with the backdrop of her flower garden and her mother accompanying her... there's something to be said for the saying that the whole is greater than the sum of the parts. Your daughter is a young woman who has hope for her future, and is excited to be able to make it happen with the people around her — her mother included, of course, and you as well. Your attention turns back to Kinu as your daughter's playing reaches a peak, music filling the room and seeping into your bones. Kinu is completely focused and alert, her large fox ears perked up, the intensity of her presence palpable as her fingers fly in a blur across the koto's strings. And although her mother's the one playing the accompaniment here with her, you have the lurking suspicion that though the result would be different, Kinu wouldn't have any trouble working with any other musician at her side. What's that saying she's so fond of? That the best investment you can make is in other people? At last, though, Kinu plucks the last notes from the strings, and opens her eyes once more. Her tails are curled about her legs and thighs, and the need for approval, your approval is clear and desperate in her gaze even as her mother reaches over and gives her a reassuring pat on the shoulder. |"I hope it is to your liking." With that and a dip of her head, Kinu half-lids her eyes and applies herself to the glorious task of making music. You're not quite sure what to think. The melody's definitely foreign to your ears — [pc.bg minstrel|as someone trained in the musical arts yourself, it's always nice to hear something that's out of the ordinary, perhaps pinch some of the better ideas in it for your own use|but that isn't about to dampen your enjoyment of your daughter's performance, though]. It's lively, flowing and energetic, while still oozing elegance from every note Kinu plucks from the strings. She's putting a lot of feeling and soul into her playing, and is fully unabashed about it. But with the backdrop of her flower garden and the tranquility of her perfectly poised figure... all of these come together to form a whole that's greater than the sum of the parts, engaging all the senses. Your daughter is a young woman who has hope for her future, and is excited to be able to make it happen with the people around her — and you number amongst them, of course. Your attention turns back to Kinu as your daughter's playing reaches a peak, music filling the room and seeping into your bones. Kinu is completely focused and alert, her large fox ears perked up, the intensity of her presence palpable as her fingers fly in a blur across the koto's strings. Perhaps this is why you're on this quest, not so much for yourself but for the likes of Kinu here, to ensure that she has a future worth living in and more importantly, living for. At last, though, Kinu plucks the last notes from the strings, and opens her eyes once more. Her tails are curled about her legs and thighs, and the need for approval, your approval is clear and desperate in her gaze. ] "How did you like it, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?" Very nice, now. In that moment, your fox-daughter looks so small and vulnerable, as if she were a kit again. Then her usual nature asserts itself once more, and she lowers her gaze. "Thank you for the compliment." No, thank her for the fine performance. "Ah. Well... I suppose that is it, then." Kinu's still clearly quite embarrassed, but she rises from her seat and crosses over to help you [party.has kiyoko|and her mother ]out of your seats and back into her chambers. "Do not worry about the instruments, I will put them away later. Spending time with you [party.has kiyoko|and Mother ]is more important, after all. "Well then, now that I have directed some of our time together, perhaps you would be interested in taking the lead, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?"
rows.translation: 说完，小娟便走进了相邻的房间，片刻后拿着她的琴走了出来。这种乐器对她来说应该有点重，但看样子她已经习惯了带着它四处走动，而且毫无困难。你的狐狸女儿迈着小心翼翼的步伐，推开了另一扇屏风门，然后悄悄地走到了后院。 "[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]， [party.has kiyoko|妈妈， ]你愿意跟我一起来吗？ 当你跟着她出去的时候，小娟已经把一切都准备好了；显然她事先就做好了这些安排。她将她的古筝放在一块编织的小垫子上，摆放在你应该坐的座位对面；她的花坛和鱼塘则为她那优雅的气质提供了背景。小娟向你微微鞠了一躬。 请，拿走吧。 [party.has kiyoko|请就座。|一个座位]我最近学会了一首新曲子，非常想演奏它。 [party.has kiyoko|你们两个|你]在我为马特伦·科马里的人们表演之前，你们将是我的第一批听众。就当作是对上次你们慷慨给予我的礼物的回报吧。还有什么比成为第一批品尝这些美妙音乐的人更合适的回礼呢？ 她真是太好了……真是太善良了。 [party.has kiyoko |嗯。基约科微笑着走上前，用她的一只手轻拍了一下你的狐狸女儿的腿。 [kiyoko.kiyokoTails]小贴士。如果我可以问一下的话，那会是一首什么样的曲子呢？ 啊，妈妈，嗯…… 啊，你在画画呢！别害羞，孩子。你最近在练习哪一幅画呢？ [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]？" 她的脸颊和鼻梁都红了，小娟踮起脚尖，凑到母亲的一只耳朵旁轻声说道。清子认真地听着，随后她的笑容变得更加灿烂，眼中带着一丝调皮的神色，退后几步，用充满戏谑的目光注视着你的“狐狸女儿”。 哎呀，我也知道那首曲子。要不我拿我的古筝来，我们一起为你演奏吧？ [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]有太多事情让我感到感激。 [pc.himHer]这样，我们就能以团结一致的方式表达我们的感激之情。 啊，妈妈，我——小娟正要深深地叹一口气，却在半路上停住了，将那口气转化成了一个平静的呼吸。虽然我认为这款游戏是设计供单人游玩的，但如果你能像一直以来那样指导我，我会非常感激。那样会让我更有信心去玩。 在这个时候，我知道当你需要帮助的时候，即使你自己并没有意识到这一点。别担心，我的孩子；只要你的母亲还有能力，她就会一直陪伴在你身边。现在……你能在这里等着吗？ 清子总是言出必行。仅仅过了几分钟，这位狐狸妻子就拿来了自己的琴和一张垫子回来了。她铺好自己的坐垫，然后舒适地坐了下来。 [kiyoko.pregStage 2|大肚子…… ][kiyoko.kiyokoTails]它们也用尾巴和动作示意小娟也来到自己的位置。看到它们这样并排站立，为了你的利益而共同努力……看到这样一个和谐的家庭，你不禁会露出会心的微笑。 正如那句话所说，这一切都是值得的。 清子表现得十分谨慎，让小娟来主导一切；她刻意退居幕后，扮演配角，以免抢走你女儿的风头。毕竟，今天是属于小娟的时刻，而不是她的，她心里很清楚这一点。你实在不确定该作何反应。这段旋律，确实让你感到十分陌生[pc.bg minstrel|作为一个本身接受过音乐艺术训练的人，听到一些与众不同的东西总是令人愉悦的。或许，可以从中汲取一些好的想法，为己所用。|不过，这肯定不会影响你欣赏女儿表演的乐趣。]这种演奏风格充满活力、流畅自然，同时每一音符都流露出优雅的气息——这无疑体现了小娟在演奏中投入了大量的情感与灵魂。 而她的花园作为背景，以及她母亲的陪伴，也为这场演出增添了特别的意味。确实，有句话说得很有道理：整体往往大于各部分之和。 你的女儿是一位充满希望的年轻女性，她很兴奋能够与身边的人一起实现自己的梦想——当然，这其中也包括她的母亲以及你。当您的女儿将演奏推向高潮时，您的注意力再次被小娟吸引住了——音乐充满了整个房间，仿佛渗透进了您的骨髓。小娟全神贯注，她的那对大狐狸耳朵竖得笔直，她的专注与活力显而易见，她的手指在琴弦上飞快地移动，仿佛是一道道闪烁的光芒。虽然在这里为她伴奏的是她的母亲，但你还是会隐约觉得，即使换作其他音乐家与她合作，小娟也应该能够顺利地完成演奏任务。毕竟，结果应该不会有任何不同吧。 她所说的那句话是什么意思呢？是不是意味着，你所能做的最明智的投资就是投资于他人？ 不过，最终，小娟还是从琴弦上拨出了最后的音符，再次睁开了眼睛。她的尾巴紧紧地卷绕在她的双腿和大腿上，而那种对他人认可的需求你的尽管她的母亲伸出手来，轻拍她的肩膀以给予安慰，但她眼中的渴望与期待依然显而易见。 |希望你会喜欢它。就这样，小娟微微低下头，半闭着双眼，全神贯注地投入到创作美妙音乐的任务中。 你实在不知道该作何感想。这段旋律确实让你感到耳熟，却又似乎完全陌生[pc.bg minstrel|作为一个本身接受过音乐艺术训练的人，听到一些与众不同的东西总是令人愉悦的。或许，可以从中汲取一些好的想法，为己所用。|不过，这肯定不会影响你欣赏女儿表演的乐趣。]这种演奏风格充满活力、流畅自然，同时每一音符都流露出优雅的气息。小娟在演奏中倾注了满满的情感与灵魂，而且她对此毫不掩饰。 而她身后那片花园，以及她那姿态娴静、神情宁静的形象，更是为这种演奏增添了别样的韵味。所有这些元素共同作用，形成了一个整体，其效果远远超过了各个部分单独作用时的总和，能够触动人的所有感官。 你的女儿是一位充满对未来希望的年轻女性，她非常兴奋能够与身边的朋友们一起实现自己的梦想——当然，你也在其中。当您的女儿将演奏推向高潮时，您的注意力再次被小娟吸引住了——音乐充满了整个房间，仿佛渗透进了您的骨髓。小娟全神贯注，她的那对大狐狸耳朵竖得笔直，她的专注与投入令人感受到无比强烈的存在感，而她的手指在琴弦上飞快地移动，动作快得几乎看不清。 在那一刻，你的狐狸女儿看起来如此渺小而脆弱，仿佛又变回了那只幼崽。但很快，她那与生俱来的性格又重新显现出来，她低下了头。谢谢你的夸奖。 不，谢谢。她为了表彰其出色的表现。 啊，好吧……我想事情就是这样的吧。小娟显然还是感到有些尴尬，但她还是从座位上站起来，走过来帮你。 [party.has kiyoko|以及她的母亲 ]从座位上跳起来，赶回她的房间。别担心那些乐器，我晚点会把它们收好。现在最重要的是能和你在一起。 [party.has kiyoko|还有母亲 ]毕竟，这才是更重要的。 那么，既然我已经安排了我们共度的一些时间，或许你愿意主动来承担这个责任吧。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]？"
rows.raw: " With that, Kinu disappears into the adjoining chamber and emerges with her koto. The instrument should be a bit heavy for her, but it looks like she's used to toting the thing around without too many problems. Taking small, careful steps, your fox-daughter pushes open another screen door and slips out to the back deck. "[pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]if you would follow me?" By the time you've followed her out, Kinu's got everything set up; she's clearly done this ahead of time. With her koto set out on a small woven mat facing the seats that you're supposed to take, her flower garden and fish pond a backdrop for her vulpine elegance, Kinu gives you a small bow. "Please, take [party.has kiyoko|your seats|a seat]. I have recently learned a new piece, and would like [party.has kiyoko|the two of you|you] to be my first audience before I perform it for the people at Matron Komari's. Consider this a gift in return for the one that you were so kind to bestow upon me the last time. What better return gift to have than to be the first to savour some fine music?" That's... that's very kind of her. [party.has kiyoko |"Hmm." Smiling, Kiyoko steps up to Kinu and gives your fox-daughter a tap on the leg with one of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tail-tips. "And if I may inquire, which piece might that be?" "Ah, Mother, um..." "Ah, you're coloring! There's no need to be embarrassed, child. Which piece have you been practising for your [pc.mf|father|mother]?" Her cheeks and the bridge of her nose red, Kinu leans in on tiptoe and whispers into one of her mother's large ears. Kiyoko listens attentively, then her smile grows wider and positively mischievous as she steps back and foxes her gaze on your fox-daughter. "Why, I know that one too. Why don't I get my koto and we'll perform together for your [pc.mf|father|mother]? There's much I have to be thankful to [pc.himHer] for, and we can show our gratitude as one." "Ah, Mother, I —" Kinu's about to heave a deep sigh and catches herself midway, turning it into a calming breath. "While I believe it is meant to be played solo, I would be very grateful if you were there to guide me, as you always have been. It would give me a lot more confidence." "At this point, I know when you're looking for help, even when you don't know it yourself. Don't worry, my child; your mother will be with you for as long as she's able. Now... if you would wait here?" Kiyoko is good to her word. Barely a handful of minutes have departed before your fox-wife returns with her own koto and a mat. She pulls up her own cushion, nestles herself in amidst her [kiyoko.pregStage 2|big belly and ][kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails, and motions for Kinu to take her position as well. Seeing them side by side like this, working together for your sake... you can't help but smile a little at the sight of a harmonious family like this. As the saying goes, it was totally worth it. Kiyoko is circumspect, letting Kinu take the lead; she deliberately remains in the background, playing second fiddle so as to not upstage your daughter's performance. This is Kinu's hour, after all, not hers, and she knows as much. You're not quite sure what to think. The melody's definitely foreign to your ears — [pc.bg minstrel|as someone trained in the musical arts yourself, it's always nice to hear something that's out of the ordinary, perhaps pinch some of the better ideas in it for your own use|but that isn't about to dampen your enjoyment of your daughter's performance, though]. It's lively, flowing and energetic, while still oozing elegance from every note Kinu plucks from the strings. She's putting a lot of feeling and soul into her playing, that's for sure. But with the backdrop of her flower garden and her mother accompanying her... there's something to be said for the saying that the whole is greater than the sum of the parts. Your daughter is a young woman who has hope for her future, and is excited to be able to make it happen with the people around her — her mother included, of course, and you as well. Your attention turns back to Kinu as your daughter's playing reaches a peak, music filling the room and seeping into your bones. Kinu is completely focused and alert, her large fox ears perked up, the intensity of her presence palpable as her fingers fly in a blur across the koto's strings. And although her mother's the one playing the accompaniment here with her, you have the lurking suspicion that though the result would be different, Kinu wouldn't have any trouble working with any other musician at her side. What's that saying she's so fond of? That the best investment you can make is in other people? At last, though, Kinu plucks the last notes from the strings, and opens her eyes once more. Her tails are curled about her legs and thighs, and the need for approval, your approval is clear and desperate in her gaze even as her mother reaches over and gives her a reassuring pat on the shoulder. |"I hope it is to your liking." With that and a dip of her head, Kinu half-lids her eyes and applies herself to the glorious task of making music. You're not quite sure what to think. The melody's definitely foreign to your ears — [pc.bg minstrel|as someone trained in the musical arts yourself, it's always nice to hear something that's out of the ordinary, perhaps pinch some of the better ideas in it for your own use|but that isn't about to dampen your enjoyment of your daughter's performance, though]. It's lively, flowing and energetic, while still oozing elegance from every note Kinu plucks from the strings. She's putting a lot of feeling and soul into her playing, and is fully unabashed about it. But with the backdrop of her flower garden and the tranquility of her perfectly poised figure... all of these come together to form a whole that's greater than the sum of the parts, engaging all the senses. Your daughter is a young woman who has hope for her future, and is excited to be able to make it happen with the people around her — and you number amongst them, of course. Your attention turns back to Kinu as your daughter's playing reaches a peak, music filling the room and seeping into your bones. Kinu is completely focused and alert, her large fox ears perked up, the intensity of her presence palpable as her fingers fly in a blur across the koto's strings. Perhaps this is why you're on this quest, not so much for yourself but for the likes of Kinu here, to ensure that she has a future worth living in and more importantly, living for. At last, though, Kinu plucks the last notes from the strings, and opens her eyes once more. Her tails are curled about her legs and thighs, and the need for approval, your approval is clear and desperate in her gaze. ] "How did you like it, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?" Very nice, now. In that moment, your fox-daughter looks so small and vulnerable, as if she were a kit again. Then her usual nature asserts itself once more, and she lowers her gaze. "Thank you for the compliment." No, thank her for the fine performance. "Ah. Well... I suppose that is it, then." Kinu's still clearly quite embarrassed, but she rises from her seat and crosses over to help you [party.has kiyoko|and her mother ]out of your seats and back into her chambers. "Do not worry about the instruments, I will put them away later. Spending time with you [party.has kiyoko|and Mother ]is more important, after all. "Well then, now that I have directed some of our time together, perhaps you would be interested in taking the lead, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]?" "
