rows.original: "I was going to tend to the beehives after I was done here, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Why don't we get that out of the way, then?" That sounds like fun — a lot of sweet, sticky fun. [party.has azyrran|That's probably why Azyrran left... hornetfolk aren't beefolk, but you suppose the similarity's enough that it might be unsettling. ]Okay, you're game. "Let me put all this down at the shed and get what we need, then!" Kinu sets off at a brisk pace with you at her side, and once at the shed she sets down her tools and grabs what looks like a small censer, as well as several pieces of thick, netted clothing. She tosses you the latter and instructs you to put them on, then tucks the censer and a couple of clay jars under her arm. "This [kiyoko.numKits 4|stuff is Tatsumi's|stuff was intended for me at Mother's insistence, but I've never needed it to begin with. It might be a bit small], but I think it'll fit you just fine, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Or at least, where it counts." She's not wearing any protective gear? "Nah. Strictly speaking, I don't need to smoke them out, either — that stuff's for you, too. The bees don't sting me any more, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." Any more... which means she got stung in the past. Kinu smiles and shrugs. "It builds character. What's a scratch or two after several dozen bee stings?" She really has a lackadaisical character towards being scratched and bruised... which wouldn't be so worrying if there wasn't the risk of infection. But then again, she presumably knows how to deal with that, too... your fox-daughter's a big girl and prides herself on her independence. In a way, that makes it all better because she's here with you because she wants to be, and not because she has to be. That small change makes all the difference in the world. "Neither Hitoshi nor I care for the honey that much, [kiyoko.numKits 4|even if Asagiri adores the stuff|even if Miko's always glad to take what I'm willing to give and turn it into honey pastries and all kinds of junk food]. It's also a good thing to repay benefactors with, because simple yet rich foods are getting rarer these days amongst the natives, I hear. All of that aside, though, the importance of bees on any farm can't be understated. What I really keep them around for is the work they do in the fields and on the fruit trees." By now, Kinu's led you to the western edge of the fields up against the crater wall, where indeed, several wooden apiaries stand. You watch as your fox-daughter puts a pinch of something sweet-smelling in the censer, lights it with a snap of her fingers and a burst of foxfire, then sets it down by a big old tree at the edge of it all. "Like I said, for you, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]; I don't need it. Anyways, so this is how it's going to go: here's the trough, funnel and clay jars. I'll open up the hives and bring you the frames without as many bees as I can, you break up the honeycombs with this blade and put them in the jars. Do it over the trough, so that the loose honey gathers inside it, and when the jar's just about full with comb top it off with the loose honey and seal it. The smoke should make the bees drowsy and too lazy to sting you, but I'm not guaranteeing anything." Even that they won't sting her? "Ahahaha, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. No bee — wild or tame — has ever stung me in the last couple years. Now, put on the hat and gloves, and we can begin." The work proceeds apace. Soon, Kinu returns with the first of the frames, still with several honeybees attached, and you do your best to trust in her knowledge as you break up the combs, leaving them still capped while rich, sticky sweetness flows from the breaks in the comb. Several bees do get close onto your arms and all, but the clear white smoke rising from the censer keeps them occupied well enough. The honey that comes from Kinu's hives is clear and light as opposed to dark and golden, without the cloying sweetness that your fox-daughter so detests. Guess she's done her best to make things to her liking; once the jar is full with solid comb, you pack away what loose honey is inside and set the clay vessel aside to be sealed later. Kinu returns with another full comb, and takes the empty frame from you. "Having fun, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]?" It's useful work, for one. "So, you're saying that what you usually do [party.has kiyoko|with Mother ]isn't useful?" Now, then — "I'm just teasing you, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Here, have another one." There aren't any bee grubs in these sealed combs, are there? "Naah. I've done this long enough to be able to tell storage combs from brooding combs at a glance. It'll be fine." Applying knife to wax, you start breaking up the next comb over the trough. She's so confident in everything she does. Ah, if only you could have such confidence too... "No one starts out with confidence, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. You build that kind of stuff up from nothing by doing things, failing, trying again and finally succeeding. And when you do succeed, that helps with your confidence, you know?" One by one, you fill the jars until what Kinu eventually returns with isn't another comb-filled frame for you to break apart, but a large bucket of water to rinse the trough and funnel out with. You gather every last drop of sticky honey that you can, then let Kinu swab out the wooden trough. The scent of floral sweetness hangs in the air and on your person, bringing with it warm, fuzzy thoughts as the two of you seal the jars together. The honey's pretty raw. "Yeah, it's best that way. It isn't proper honey if it doesn't have bits of comb and pollen floating in it, I feel." Kinu washes her hands in what water's left in the bucket and wipes her brow with the back of a hand. "Thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. You were a great help this morning." Always pleased to be of help. Plus, you got to spend time with her; that's always good in your book. "Yeah. Anyways, I'm going to lug these jars back, then take a bath; I'm stick and sweet-smelling all over. You should at least wash your hands by the well or something before you go, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], you're not much better. It might seem fun for a bit, but sweet and sticky is no way to go through life." Oh, really? Kinu smirks and hefts two jars of honeycomb, one under each arm. "Yes, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. All right, I've got to be off. See you around, okay? And... come back before too long, if you can." With that, she's gone, five slightly sticky tails swishing behind her as she saunters off. Sighing, you take a look at the remaining jars, wondering if you should help Kinu with the lifting, then decide against it. You've already said your goodbyes and all... Before long, you're back on the road again, [party.hasCompanions |having collected [party.compNames] back to you |safe in the knowledge that Kinu will be fine while you're gone ].
rows.translation: 我在这里忙完之后本来打算去照料那些蜂箱的。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]那我们干脆把这件事解决掉吧？ 那听起来很有趣——一定会是非常有趣、让人乐在其中的事情。 [party.has azyrran|这大概就是阿兹兰离开的原因吧……黄蜂人虽然和牛头人不同，但这种相似性或许确实足以让人感到不安。 ]好吧，你同意了。 那我就把这些东西都放到棚子里，然后去拿我们需要的东西吧！ 小娟以轻快的步伐走在你身旁，一旦来到小屋，她就放下工具，拿起了一个看起来像小香炉的东西，还有几件厚实的网状衣物。她把那些衣物扔给你，命令你穿上它们，然后自己把香炉和几个陶罐夹在胳膊下。 这个[kiyoko.numKits 4|这些东西都是龙司的。|在妈妈的坚持下，这些东西本来是给我准备的，但实际上我从来都不需要它们。也许这些东西有点小吧……]不过我觉得它很适合你。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]或者至少，在那些重要的地方。 她没有穿戴任何防护装备吗？ 不。严格来说，我也没必要把它们熏出来——那些东西也是给你的。蜜蜂不再蜇我了。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]。" 任何更多这意味着她过去曾经被蜇过。 科努笑了笑，耸了耸肩。这能锻炼人的意志。被蜜蜂蜇上几十下，留下几道伤痕又算什么呢？ 她对于被抓伤或淤青确实显得毫不在意……要是没有感染的风险，这种态度倒也不至于让人太担心。不过，想必她也知道该如何处理这些问题吧……你的狐狸女儿已经是个成熟的大姑娘了，她一向以自己的独立性为荣。从某种意义上来说，这一点反而让情况变得好了一些，因为她是自愿选择和你在一起的想要存在，而非因为她 拥有就是这个小小的改变，却能产生巨大的影响。 我和仁都不太喜欢蜂蜜这种东西。 [kiyoko.numKits 4|即使浅雾非常喜欢这些东西……|即使米可总是乐于接受我愿意给予她的东西，然后将它们做成蜂蜜糕点或是各种垃圾食品……]用这样的方式来回报那些帮助过我们的人，也是件好事。因为据我所知，如今对于当地人来说，简单而营养丰富的食物已经变得越来越稀少了。不过，无论如何，蜜蜂在任何农场中的重要性都是不可忽视的。我之所以养蜜蜂，主要是因为它们在田地和果树上所做的工作。 此时，小娟已经带你来到了田野的西缘，那里紧邻着火山口的边缘，果然有几座木制的蜂箱矗立在那里。你看到你的狐狸女儿在香炉里放入了一些散发着甜香的物质，然后打了个响指，顿时有一团狐火燃了起来，她接着将香炉放在了边缘那棵大老树旁边。 就像我之前说的，对于你来说[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我不需要那个。总之，具体操作是这样的：这里有槽、漏斗和陶罐。我会打开蜂箱，尽量少带一些蜜蜂出来，然后你们用这个刀把蜂巢拆开，把它们放进罐子里。在操作的时候要把蜂巢放在槽上面，这样多余的蜂蜜就会流到槽里。等罐子差不多装满蜂巢后，再用多余的蜂蜜把罐子填满，然后密封起来。烟雾会让蜜蜂昏昏欲睡，从而不会去蜇你，不过我也不敢保证这一点。 就连那些东西也不会蜇到她吗？ 啊哈哈哈， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]在过去的几年里，从来没有一只蜜蜂，无论是野生的还是家养的，蜇过我。现在，戴上帽子，戴上手套，我们就可以开始了。 工作进展得相当顺利。不久之后，小娟带着第一批框架回来了，那些框架上还粘着几只蜜蜂。你只能尽力相信她的判断力，开始拆开那些蜂巢——虽然蜂巢的盖子仍然盖着，但从中裂开的缝隙中，却流淌出了浓郁而粘稠的甜汁。确实会有几只蜜蜂飞到你的手臂上，但香炉里冒出的白色烟雾足以让它们远离你。来自小娟蜂箱的蜂蜜是清澈透明的，而非那种深金色且带有浓烈甜味的蜂蜜——那种你的狐狸女儿非常讨厌的味道。看来她已经尽力把事情办得让自己满意了；当罐子里装满了结块的蜂蜜后，就把里面剩下的稀蜂蜜收起来，把那个陶罐放在一边，等以后再密封起来。小娟又拿来了另一个装满蜂蜜的罐子，同时把空罐子从你手中接了过去。 玩得开心吗？ [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]？" 首先，这是一项很有意义的工作。 所以，你是说你平时所做的那些事情[party.has kiyoko|和妈妈一起 ]不是有用吗？ 那么，现在开始吧—— 我只是在开玩笑而已， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]来，再拿一个吧。 这些密封好的蜂巢里应该没有蜂幼虫吧？ 嗯，我干这个已经够久了，一眼就能分辨出用于储存物品的蜂巢和用于培育蜂王的蜂巢。应该没问题的。 用刀划开蜡层，然后开始用梳子将剩余的蜡块从槽中梳理出来。她做任何事情都显得如此自信……啊，要是你也能有这样的自信该多好…… 没有人一开始就充满自信， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]你是通过不断努力、经历失败、重新尝试，最终取得成功，才建立起这样的成就的。而当你真正成功时，这会增强你的自信心，明白吗？ 你一个一个地把罐子装满，直到最终小娟带回的不再是一个装满梳子的框架供你拆解，而是一大桶水，用来冲洗木槽并把剩余的蜂蜜倒出来。你把每一滴粘稠的蜂蜜都收集起来，然后让小娟把木槽擦干净。空气中弥漫着花香般的甜味，也萦绕在你的身上，当你俩把罐子封好时，这种甜美的气息伴随着温暖而舒适的感受。 这种蜂蜜还相当原始呢。 是啊，这样最好。我觉得，如果蜂蜜里没有蜂巢碎片和花粉，那就算不上真正的蜂蜜了。小娟用桶里剩下的水洗手，然后用手的背擦了擦额头。谢谢， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]今天早上你真的帮了大忙。 很乐意能帮上忙。而且，你能和她一起度过时光，这对你来说总归是件好事吧。 是啊。不管怎样，我得把这些罐子拿回去，然后去洗澡——我身上到处都是黏糊糊的东西，还散发着甜味。你至少也应该去井边洗洗手再走啊。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]你也好不到哪去。一开始可能会觉得挺有趣，但整天黏黏糊糊的，总不是过日子的正确方式吧。 哦，真的吗？ 小娟露出微笑，然后把两罐蜂窝状结构的东西分别夹在两只胳膊下。是的， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]好吧，我得走了。回头见，好吗？还有……如果可能的话，尽量早点回来吧。 就这样，她离开了，五条略微粘稠的尾巴在她身后摇摆着，她慢悠悠地走开了。你叹了口气，看了看剩下的罐子，想着是否应该去帮小娟把它们搬起来，但最终还是决定不去了。毕竟你已经道过别了…… 不久之后，你又重新踏上了旅途。 [party.hasCompanions |已经收集完毕[party.compNames]轮到你了 |你可以放心地离开，因为知道小娟会在你不在的时候一切都好 ]。

rows.original: "If you want to help me out, there's always work to be done in the fields. That's not below you, right?" [pc.bg noblescion minstrel courtesan scholar |Well... in your past, you might very well have turned up your nose at manual labor of this sort as unbefitting of your station. But that's in the past, and your adventures thus far have impressed upon you the need for some degree of physical strength and hardiness, if nothing else. That, and really... you couldn't say no to your own fox-daughter, could you? |Oh, of course not; manual labor of this sort has been a long companion to you for much of your life. All right, where do you get started? ] "Great, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Let's see about putting those hands to good use, then..." [rand |Soon enough, Kinu has you pulling up ripe vegetables from rows in the dirt, using a knife-like trowel of soft iron to loosen the earth and dig up their roots so they can be easily picked and put into a large basket she's provided you with. You note that the crops she's got in these particular fields are a bunch of cabbages and root vegetables, winter crops that grow well in the cold of the Marches. Actually uprooting the veggies without damaging them is more challenging than one might imagine, given their alternately tenuous and tenacious hold on the earth. "Try not to tear the leaves if you can, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]," Kinu says as she works on another row beside you. Gods, she's really quick at this... but then she's been doing this non-stop since she was a child, hasn't she? "I can fry them up as greens, if nothing else." She really hates to see things go to waste, doesn't she? "It only makes sense to be prudent with what you have, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Needless waste, especially of food, is a sin, you know. Once you appreciate the effort that goes into bringing meals to the table, it hurts a lot more to see it all go to waste. That, and they have a saying in the Old Country: 'I may own the land, but the crops belong to Keros.' When you think about it that way, your harvest is just a blessing given by the most fickle of deities; any number of terrible things could've happened to ruin the veggies between planting and picking. No matter how much control you think you have, it can all be taken away from you in the blink of an eye." ... "C'mon [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], that's enough talk for now. Still plenty of white cabbage and leeks to bring in once we're done with the radishes." Yeah, she's right. The better part of an hour or two passes as you focus on divesting the earth of its fruits, filling one basket, then two, then tree. By the end of it all, [pc.toughnessRange 60 |you're a little sore, but it's nothing your decent constitution can't handle. You're made of sterner stuff than that; it'll take more than a little turnip-picking to bring you down, ha |you're aching in your waist and shoulders, places you didn't know you had voicing their complaint most loudly and pointedly at the sudden surge of activity. It's hard to deny that your body could use some toughening up, whether you want to admit it to yourself or not ]. Kinu herself isn't fazed in the least, grabbing one of the filled baskets by the handles and starting off towards the shed. "We're not done yet, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Surely we're not intending to leave all these out in the sun, rain and snow, are we? And... surely you're not intending to let your poor little daughter shoulder this entire burden by herself, are you?" Ha ha! Ha! Of course... not... |Before long, Kinu is showing you how to prepare the fields, while you flail around with hoe in hand and till away as if your life depended on it. Well, strictly speaking it doesn't, but your daughter's esteem of you does, and to be fair that's on the same level as the other. "Let's break up the dirt nice and good, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom] — the stuff I'm planning to plant likes the soil all nice and crumbly. Once we've loosed it up across the board, we can see about tilling some of that compost I've prepared into the field." You eye the big basket of dark, black-brown stuff by the edge of the fallow field. It doesn't smell as bad as you might've expected, but it's still not the kind of stuff you'd want to get close to even on the best of days. That, and you don't want to disappoint your darling fox-daughter, do you? The going is grueling, but your put your nose to the grindstone and back into it, especially with the handwraps that Kinu's been so kind as to provide you with. [pc.toughnessRange 60 |Sweat pours down your brow and it's still tough, but at least you've fallen into a steady pace and quickly acclimatising to the manual labor. Your shoulders, arms and waist might be voicing a little complaint after you've slept and they've had time to turn sore, but it's nothing you can't deal with |Before long, sweat's pouring down your brow in streams, and you have a newfound appreciation for how Kinu manages to do this sort of thing day in, day out. You do your best and try to set a steady pace, but the constant complaints from your waist, shoulders and chest keep throwing you off. Yeah, you need to be tougher than this for this kind of manual labor... but on the other hand, there's putting on a brave front for Kinu ]. At least you aren't going to be getting blisters on your fingers from this... "There, that's how you turn the dirt and get it all mixed in with a minimum of fuss." She looks to be enjoying herself. "You've taught me a bunch, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]; I just feel kind of glad that I'm finally able to repay the favor. That, and there're few better ways to revise what you know than to teach it to someone else. Even someone like me can get sloppy every now and then from getting lax — overconfidence, that's how they get you in the end." You could've sworn you'd heard that line before... Kinu laughs. "Wouldn't be surprised if you had, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It's one of those things that don't change no matter where in the world you are. Now then, let's see you swing that hoe again, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]..." Time ticks by and by and large you do grow more tired, but it's a good kind of tired. Anything would be, when you're here and spending time with your fox-daughter, no matter how seemingly mundane. Eventually, between the two of you the field is turned and most of the compost mixed in well with the dirt. Despite you aching from head to toe, there's a certain sense of satisfaction here that comes from a job well done. "Looks good, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]," Kinu says, steadying you by the shoulders as she takes the hoe from you. "About as well as could be expected." |Together, the two of you set off to weeding the fields — crouching down and pulling up unwanted plants by hand. Thanks to your fox-daughter's use of plenty of rich, dark mulch there aren't as many weeds as one might've expected from a field like this, but Kinu's quite exacting as the two of you go over the rows of vegetables side by side. The work itself isn't that strenuous, but being so close to the ground and duck walking back and forth all the time does make your calves and thighs ache something fierce after a while. The both of you place the gathered weeds in a basket, where they'll eventually end up as compost, or so Kinu assures you. "It's a bit of a pity, having to pull up weeds," she says with a sigh. "Some of them have a really strong will to survive, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], so make sure you get them out by the roots as well. While I can relate to their tenacity and refusal to budge, they're also threatening my leeks, so they have to go, no two ways about it. Even so, it hurts inside a little every time I have to pull up a dandelion, you know? They're so useful and you can do so many things with them, but they're also weeds of the most persistent sort. "You'd never think that farming can produce such complicated emotions in people, but maybe I'm weird like that. Hitoshi doesn't seem to get such feelings when he's tilling weeds under, but then he doesn't seem to get that much in the way of feelings to begin with. That's why when he does smile, it's that much more meaningful." Mmm... Together, the both of you ply up and down the rows, picking off the weeds as they come. [pc.toughnessRange 60 |Your legs are burning by the time you're done, but you're sure you'll be able to walk it off without too much trouble. Probably |Your legs are on fire by the time you're done, your thighs and calves promising a swift retribution tomorrow for the abuse they've taken this morning ]. Kinu picks up the flat-bottomed basket and gives it a toss, sifting out crumbs of dirt before settling it in her arms. You stand, albeit shakily, while your fox-daughter reaches up to give you a clap on the shoulder. "Great work, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Thanks so much for the help, and for being with me for a bit. It really means a lot when you have so many other things to do." You nod, head still swimming a little. ] Despite her size, Kinu is truly a robust young woman, isn't she? With a daily schedule like this, this end was truly inevitable. All done, your fox-daughter dusts off her hands and turns to you, giving you a dip of her head. "Looks like that's all there is for today, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Thanks for helping out — things got done a little earlier than they otherwise would, and that always counts for something." It's not what most people would imagine when they speak of spending time with their children, but then again Kinu isn't most people's idea of a daughter, after all. She's your idea of a daughter. "Haha, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], you flatterer. Okay, then — I'll see you around, yeah? Stay safe out there! I've got to get prepared to head over to Granny Komari's and all." With that, she's gone, all five tails swishing behind her as she saunters off. What a girl... Before long, you're back on the road again, [party.hasCompanions |having collected [party.compNames] back to you |safe in the knowledge that Kinu will be fine while you're gone ].

You do your best and try to set a steady pace, but the constant complaints from your waist, shoulders and chest keep throwing you off. Yeah, you need to be tougher than this for this kind of manual labor... but on the other hand, there's putting on a brave front for Kinu ]. At least you aren't going to be getting blisters on your fingers from this... "There, that's how you turn the dirt and get it all mixed in with a minimum of fuss." She looks to be enjoying herself. "You've taught me a bunch, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]; I just feel kind of glad that I'm finally able to repay the favor. That, and there're few better ways to revise what you know than to teach it to someone else. Even someone like me can get sloppy every now and then from getting lax — overconfidence, that's how they get you in the end." You could've sworn you'd heard that line before... Kinu laughs. "Wouldn't be surprised if you had, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It's one of those things that don't change no matter where in the world you are. Now then, let's see you swing that hoe again, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]..." Time ticks by and by and large you do grow more tired, but it's a good kind of tired. Anything would be, when you're here and spending time with your fox-daughter, no matter how seemingly mundane. Eventually, between the two of you the field is turned and most of the compost mixed in well with the dirt. Despite you aching from head to toe, there's a certain sense of satisfaction here that comes from a job well done. "Looks good, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]," Kinu says, steadying you by the shoulders as she takes the hoe from you. "About as well as could be expected." |Together, the two of you set off to weeding the fields — crouching down and pulling up unwanted plants by hand. Thanks to your fox-daughter's use of plenty of rich, dark mulch there aren't as many weeds as one might've expected from a field like this, but Kinu's quite exacting as the two of you go over the rows of vegetables side by side. The work itself isn't that strenuous, but being so close to the ground and duck walking back and forth all the time does make your calves and thighs ache something fierce after a while. The both of you place the gathered weeds in a basket, where they'll eventually end up as compost, or so Kinu assures you. "It's a bit of a pity, having to pull up weeds," she says with a sigh. "Some of them have a really strong will to survive, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], so make sure you get them out by the roots as well. While I can relate to their tenacity and refusal to budge, they're also threatening my leeks, so they have to go, no two ways about it. Even so, it hurts inside a little every time I have to pull up a dandelion, you know? They're so useful and you can do so many things with them, but they're also weeds of the most persistent sort. "You'd never think that farming can produce such complicated emotions in people, but maybe I'm weird like that. Hitoshi doesn't seem to get such feelings when he's tilling weeds under, but then he doesn't seem to get that much in the way of feelings to begin with. That's why when he does smile, it's that much more meaningful." Mmm... Together, the both of you ply up and down the rows, picking off the weeds as they come. [pc.toughnessRange 60 |Your legs are burning by the time you're done, but you're sure you'll be able to walk it off without too much trouble. Probably |Your legs are on fire by the time you're done, your thighs and calves promising a swift retribution tomorrow for the abuse they've taken this morning ]. Kinu picks up the flat-bottomed basket and gives it a toss, sifting out crumbs of dirt before settling it in her arms. You stand, albeit shakily, while your fox-daughter reaches up to give you a clap on the shoulder. "Great work, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Thanks so much for the help, and for being with me for a bit. It really means a lot when you have so many other things to do." You nod, head still swimming a little. ] Despite her size, Kinu is truly a robust young woman, isn't she? With a daily schedule like this, this end was truly inevitable. All done, your fox-daughter dusts off her hands and turns to you, giving you a dip of her head. "Looks like that's all there is for today, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Thanks for helping out — things got done a little earlier than they otherwise would, and that always counts for something." It's not what most people would imagine when they speak of spending time with their children, but then again Kinu isn't most people's idea of a daughter, after all. She's your idea of a daughter. "Haha, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], you flatterer. Okay, then — I'll see you around, yeah? Stay safe out there! I've got to get prepared to head over to Granny Komari's and all." With that, she's gone, all five tails swishing behind her as she saunters off. What a girl... Before long, you're back on the road again, [party.hasCompanions |having collected [party.compNames] back to you |safe in the knowledge that Kinu will be fine while you're gone ]. "

rows.original: "Well, if you want to help out around the place, there's always work to be done. I'm not going to say no to another pair of hands; there's always a bunch of stuff that needs fixing if you look closely enough. C'mon, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], I'll race you to the shed!" With that, she's off, quick as a bolt, her bare feet leaving little prints in the bare earth. You shake your head, smile, and decide to humor her, breaking into a brisk jog until you arrive at your destination hot on her heels. Motioning for you to wait, Kinu slips into the storage and emerges with [rand |a bunch of planks, a couple of brushes and a large sealed pot of something sour-smelling. She gives you a nod, hands you one of the brushes, then gestures for you to take a seat before tearing off the pot's seal to reveal the ink-like liquid within. What's all this, then? "We're going to be treating some wood today, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Several old buildings need fixing up, and there's always a call for more of the stuff — fences, walls, that kind of thing. I've been putting it off for a while, but since you offered to help today this should go a lot more quickly than it would otherwise[kiyoko.numKits 4|; my siblings really don't like helping out with this, and someone's got to do it]." You see. "It's not hard, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. This stuff is a mixture of soot, several juices, and a little gum; It'll help protect the wood from rot, bugs and wet. All you've got to do is to give the planks a nice and even coating, make sure the stuff gets in nice and deep, and we'll leave them out in the sun to dry. It usually takes just one pass if you do it well, but if you're not careful it might need a couple times." All right, then, you can do that. Let's get started! Kinu hefts over the first of the planks to you, you dip your brush into the thick, sour-smelling liquid, and start. The going is slow at first as you acclimatise yourself to the work, but quickly picks up speed as you get more confident about it. Your fox-daughter works quietly beside you, treating the planks one by one and laying them up against a wall to dry in the sun. "[kiyoko.numKits 4|My siblings|Some people] don't like this kind of work because it's mind-numbing, or at least that's what they say. It's boring and doesn't engage oneself. Me... I think there's value in the simple repetition of manual labor, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It gives the body something to do while my mind's set free, and I think far better and clear that I would if I were just lying down like a log. They say in the Old Country that if you lie down just after eating, you'll turn into a cow; I can certainly see where that sentiment comes from, haha. "...I won't say I've never wondered if Mother's right, if I'm wasting my talents doing manual labor about a farm when I should be — I don't know, doing politics or shaping or whatever high-status, cushy and intellectual job she no doubt had in store for me. But... the clarity and inspiration I've achieved while working with my hands is something I don't imagine normal people get when they do the same thing. That, and being able to do something and feel satisfied about it." Eventually, the both of you get a few dozen planks coated with sour soot, enough to fully stack both sides of the wall. Kinu gives you a small smile of satisfaction, retrieves the brush from you and seals the pot again. "Thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. You asking gave me the kick in the pants I needed to finally move and get this done — who knows, if you hadn't shown up and asked to help out, I might've kept on putting it off for days or even weeks, haha." You're just glad to have been of help — that, and any excuse to spend time with her is worth it. "I'm glad you think that way, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Okay, then — I'll see you around, yeah? Stay safe out there! I've got to put these away, clean up the shed and then get prepared to head over to Granny Komari's and all." |a pair of impressive-looking weighted iron knives, as well as several lengths of rope. "We're going bamboo-cutting, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Hope you're up to it." For your darling fox-daughter? You always are. Kinu just laughs and hands you one of the knives, then heads out into the sun. She leads you on to a wide grove near the den's entrance, by the waterfall. This part of Kiyoko's home has retained some of the wild, overgrown edge that was there when you first arrived, including an enormous grove of what must be bamboo. It's certainly not a plant native to the Marches, for one, and you watch patiently as Kinu steps up and begins inspecting the stems. "This stuff grows really rapidly, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Mother told me that the entire mess here all came from a couple of plants one of her subordinates brought over as ornaments and maybe a bit of personal use. Now, just look at it all, and it's only been a couple of hundred years! Stuff grows practically as fast as I can cut it." She taps one of the stems with a finger. "Strong as wood, too, and pretty light to boot. There, I think we can get started." With that, Kinu shows you how to go about felling the long-stemmed woody grasses. They're like trees, only far too thin to be so, and hollow inside. Each thwack of the heavy knife biting deep into the bamboo stem feels very, very satisfying for reasons you can't quite put into words, and Kinu hurries you aside as it topples over to the ground. "Not bad, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], but be more careful with your cutting next time. Remember, you've got to cut just above the second node from the base. All right, let's see you do this next one — it's really old and useless for construction, so we're probably going to split it up and use it for fuel or charcoal or something. You can be a bit more careless... although I still wouldn't recommend it." After a few tries, Kinu feels comfortable enough to leave you to it, and busies herself with marking out stems that're too young to be harvested, those that're only worth for firewood because of flaws or age, and those that should be cleared out to avoid overcrowding. She does pick up her knife and fell her own share of bamboo stems, but by and large you're the one doing the cutting here. Now that it matters — after all, you wouldn't be able to tell one of these things from the other, but Kinu moves amongst them easily, telling you to dispatch this one or that one with utmost prejudice. "The ones we actually plan to use for building and other lasting projects, we've got to try and treat really quickly or else the bugs and rot will get to them," Kinu explains. "Don't worry about it too much, though. That's my job." Ah. Maybe you could take a break, though? You're starting to feel it in your shoulders and waist — [pc.toughnessRange 60 |of course you're not actually aching, but you could do with a quick break before your fatigue does escalate into an actual concern |a dull, burning ache that promises to become much, much worse once you've slept and it's had time to work its way into your bones ]. The blade, heavy as it is in order to actually cut into the bamboo, has crept up on you unawares. "Haha, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. We're almost done — you take your break and leave the rest to me, okay? Only skiving is a problem — There's no shame in saying honestly that you're all tuckered out." Well, don't mind if you do. You turn around, kick a couple bamboo lengths out of the way, then settle back to watch Kinu take out the rest of the marked with her own knife. Ha... she's remarkably strong for a girl that small, and the daily work of her life has only made her thicker in body and mind. With a schedule like this... one supposes this was inevitable, wasn't it? Her growing apart from her mother? The steady thock-thock-thock of a sharp edge biting into woody grass punctuates your thoughts, and you shake your head. Kiyoko would never be caught doing manual labor like this, that's for sure. And yet, despite all their differences, they're the same where it counts... right? You shake your head, thoughts dissipating as the tall and thin bamboo stem comes crashing down to the ground. "I think that's the last one for today, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. You look all tired out, so why don't you leave me to clean up here and get all these put away? I'll have [kiyoko.numKits 4|Tatsumi and the others|some folks from Granny Komari's] come over and strip the leaves, get them all stored properly in the shed before they start to go." Well, if she says it's okay; she's the expert here, after all. You hand your knife back to Kinu, who takes it from you and graces you with a smile and a punch on the shoulder. "Good work today, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Drink some water or something before you head back out there, okay? You helped me out as much as you could, and I'm grateful for that. Now, if you don't mind me, I've got to go and round up several more hands..." |a tall stepladder, imposing enough that she has to carry it sideways with both hands. Your fox-daughter gives you a nod and smile, then tilts her head in the shed's interior. "I've got the ladder, why don't you bring out a couple of baskets, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]? We're going fruit picking." Ha. You remember when she was a kit, staring lovingly up at the peach trees. And now that she has the power of stepladders to finally deal with her small height... "C'mon, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], we're going to get mandarins, not peaches. That, and I'm too old to be doing silly things like eating myself sick on fruit. Now if you wouldn't mind, get the baskets, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." Ha! All right, all right. You nip into the shed, and moments later you're following Kinu down the dirt path towards the den's entrance and a nice grove of mandarins. They look a little wild — probably a grove from centuries ago that went feral — but Kinu's been pruning and working the fruit-bearing boughs into something more like an actual orchard that's being tended to. As she approaches the nearest mandarin tree, she sets her ladder against its trunk and gestures for you to ready the basket below. "Noticed a bunch of them getting ripe the other day, but they weren't fit for picking yet. It's a good thing that you came around when you did, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Catch what I toss down to you, okay?" She's not worried about the fruit getting bruised or something? "We're eating them ourselves, not bringing them to market. Doesn't matter how they look, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], what does matter is if you can put them in your mouth just fine and how well they keep. Now enough talk, let's get started!" Your fox-daughter may not be very tall, but it's not as if the mandarin trees are towering, either. She scrambles up the ladder, up the branches and disappears amongst the foliage for a bit. One might worry about old or breakable branches, but she clearly knows what she's about, at any rate. Little fox's been climbing trees since she was a kit, you remember... "Hey down below, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]! Catch, okay?" With that, several thick-rinded fruits fall straight down and into your basket. It's a close thing, but you manage to get them all without letting any land on the grass. Mandarins aren't her mother's absolute favorite, but it's not as if she dislikes them, either. You have some very distinct memories of her and them together... "Ah. Mother." Kinu looks a little put out by the mention of Kiyoko, then shrugs. "I wish I had more good memories of her myself, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Those that I do have are great... and I wonder if there could have been more. But that's just wishful thinking at this point. Here, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], more incoming!" Kinu tosses down another couple mandarins, and they land atop the growing pile in the basket. She climbs down, hefts the ladder over to another tree, and goes up again. This would actually be fun, if it weren't simply so hair-raising... One by one, your fox-daughter scrambles up the trees like a monkey, bringing into doubt as to whether she actually needs the stepladder at this point. Probably not, knowing her, but it gets the job done, doesn't it? Eventually, one basket fills, followed by the other; with the way she's beaming while going about the job, you get the feeling that she feels as if she's saved the best part of this whole exercise for herself. Eventually, though, the baskets are filled to the brim with ripe fruit, and one by one the two of you heft them back to the shed along with the stepladder. "Thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]," Kinu says, dusting off her hands. "It's nice to be able to cut loose and concentrate on picking while someone else handles the gathering, you know? Doing this with someone else is a lot more fun than trying to get it done by yourself — a lot less busywork that way." No worries, you enjoyed getting to spend time with her, too. So, what's she going to do with all that fruit? "Hmm. Might pulp it and make some jam Marches-style — you know, with almost no added sugar. That ought to go over well with Hitoshi." And that's fine... but just where did she learn to make Marches-style jam? It certainly wasn't from her mother. "Aha, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. That's for me to know and for you... well, it's not hard to find out, I suppose. Don't worry, I haven't done anything bad. All right then, I'll be seeing you around. Keep yourself safe out there, okay?" ] With that, she's gone, all five tails swishing behind her as she saunters off. What a girl... Before long, you're back on the road again, [party.hasCompanions |having collected [party.compNames] back to you |safe in the knowledge that Kinu will be fine while you're gone ].
rows.translation: 嗯，如果你想帮忙做点事情的话，总是有活儿可做的。我当然不会拒绝多一个人帮忙；只要仔细看看，就会发现有很多东西需要修理。来吧， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我跟你比赛，看谁先跑到那个棚子里！ 说完，她就像离弦之箭一般迅速离开了，光着脚在裸露的泥土上留下了一串浅浅的脚印。你摇摇头，笑了笑，决定陪她玩这个游戏，于是也开始小跑起来，拼命追赶，终于在到达目的地时刚好追上了她。小娟示意你稍等，然后走进储藏室，不一会儿就走了出来[rand |一些木板、几把刷子，还有一个密封得很好的大罐子，里面装着某种散发着酸味的液体。她向你点了点头，递给你其中一把刷子，然后示意你坐下，接着才撕开罐子的封口，露出里面的那种类似墨水的液体。 那么，这些到底都是些什么呢？ 今天我们要处理一些木材。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]有几栋旧房子需要修缮，而且总是需要购买更多的材料——比如围栏、墙壁之类的东西。我之前一直拖着没动手，但既然你今天主动提出帮忙，这项工作应该会进展得快很多了。[kiyoko.numKits 4|我的兄弟姐妹们真的不喜欢帮忙做这件事，但总得有人来承担这个责任]。" 你瞧。 不是这样的。坚硬， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]这种材料是由烟灰、几种果汁和少量树胶混合而成的；它能够有效保护木材，防止其腐烂、受到虫蛀或受潮。你只需要将这种混合物均匀地涂抹在木板上，确保它能够渗透到木材的深层，然后把木板放在阳光下晾干即可。如果操作得当，通常只需要涂抹一次就可以了；但如果不小心，可能就需要涂抹几次才行。 好的，那你可以开始了。我们马上动手吧！小娟把第一块木板递给你，你将画笔浸入那种浓稠且带有酸味的液体中，然后开始工作。刚开始时动作会比较慢，因为你需要适应这种工作方式，但一旦你对自己越来越有信心，速度就会逐渐加快。你的狐狸女儿也在你旁边安静地工作着，她一块一块地处理这些木板，然后将它们靠在墙上晾晒。 "[kiyoko.numKits 4|我的兄弟姐妹们|有些人]他们不喜欢这种工作，因为这种工作让人感到无聊，无法集中注意力。至少他们是这么说的。这种工作很枯燥，无法让人产生兴趣。不过我觉得，重复性的体力劳动本身也是有一定价值的。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]这样可以让我的身体有所活动，而我的思绪也能得到释放，我觉得这样思考起来会更加清晰、有条理，远比只是像木头一样躺着要好得多。在老家有句俗话，说如果饭后马上躺下，就会变成一头牛；我当然能理解这种说法的由来，哈哈。 ……我必须承认，我曾经怀疑过母亲的决定是否正确，是否我把本应用来从事政治活动、从事艺术创作，或者从事那些她肯定为我准备好的、地位崇高、工作轻松又充满智慧的职业的才华，浪费在了农活上。但是……通过动手劳动，我获得了那种清晰的思想和灵感，我想普通人做同样的事情是很难获得这样的体验的。而且，能够确实得到某样东西并因此感到满足。 最终，你们俩收集到了几十块被酸烟熏黑的木板，这些木板足以用来堆满墙壁的两侧。小娟满意地微微一笑，从你手中接过刷子，然后将锅重新盖好。 谢谢， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]正是你的询问给了我所需的动力，让我终于决定行动起来把这件事完成——谁知道呢，如果你没有出现并提出帮忙的话，我可能会把这件事推迟好几天甚至几周呢，哈哈。 你只是很高兴自己能帮上忙——只要能有机会和她在一起，任何理由都值得。 我很高兴你这么想。 [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]好的，那我们就这样吧——回头见，嗯？在外面一定要注意安全哦！我得把这些东西收起来，把棚屋清理干净，然后准备去麻里奶奶家了。 |一把外观精美的加重铁刀，还有几段绳子。 我们要去砍竹子了， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]希望你能够胜任这项任务。 是为了你亲爱的狐狸女儿吗？你总是这么关心她。 小娟只是笑了笑，递给你一把刀，然后便走向阳光中。她带着你来到了洞穴入口附近的一片宽阔的树林边，那里有瀑布流淌。清子的家的这一部分还保留着你刚来到这里时所看到的那种野生、杂草丛生的景象，其中有一片巨大的竹林——这种植物肯定不是原产于这些地区的。你耐心地观察着小娟走上前去检查那些竹茎。 这种植物生长速度非常快， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]妈妈告诉我，这里的一团糟都是因为她的一个下属带进来几株植物当装饰品，或许还有一点个人用途。现在看看这些植物，才仅仅过了几百年而已！这些植物生长的速度简直快得让我根本来不及修剪它们。她用手指轻轻敲了敲其中一根茎秆。质地坚硬如木，而且重量还很轻。好了，我想我们可以开始工作了。 就这样，小娟向你展示了如何砍伐那些长茎的木本植物。它们看起来像树木，但实际上细得根本算不上树木，而且内部是空心的。每当那把重型的刀深深地砍进竹茎时，那种感觉非常出于一些你难以用语言表达的原因，这种体验让人感到十分满足。而当小娟倒在地上时，它急忙将你拉到一边。 不错， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]不过下次切割的时候一定要更加小心。记住，你需要在离基部第二个节点稍高的位置进行切割。好了，让我们看看你接下来怎么操作吧——这个东西已经非常老旧了，根本无法用于建筑，所以我们很可能把它拆开，用来制作燃料或者木炭之类的。这次你可以稍微放松一点……不过我还是不建议你这样做的。 尝试了几次之后，小娟觉得已经足够放心了，便不再打扰你，转而去标记那些还太幼小、无法采摘的树苗，那些因为存在瑕疵或已经老化而只适合用来作为柴火的树木，以及那些需要被清除以避免过度拥挤的树木。她确实会拿起刀来，自己砍那些该砍的竹子，但总体来说，真正负责切割工作的人还是你。现在这一点很重要——毕竟，你根本无法区分这些竹子有什么不同，但小娟却能轻松地分辨它们，还会告诉你该先处理哪一根、哪一根应该留着。 那些我们真正打算用来建造其他长期项目的东西，我们必须尽快进行处理，否则漏洞和腐朽问题就会侵蚀它们。小娟解释道。 不过，你不必太担心这个。这是我的工作。 啊，或许你可以休息一下吧？你的肩膀和腰部已经开始感到不适了[pc.toughnessRange 60 |当然，你其实并没有真的感到疼痛，但在疲劳进一步恶化之前，你确实需要稍作休息。 |一种隐隐作痛的感觉，仿佛这种疼痛会在你入睡后、有更多时间深入你的骨骼时变得愈发剧烈。 ]这种刀刃之所以被设计得如此重型，就是为了能够真正切穿竹子。而它会在你毫无察觉的情况下悄悄逼近你。 哈哈， [pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]我们差不多快完成了——你可以去休息一下，剩下的交给我吧，好吗？只要不偷懒就行……老实说，大家都已经累坏了，这没什么可羞愧的。 嗯，如果你想这么做的话，也没关系。你转过身去，把几根竹子踢到一边，然后就可以坐下来看小娟用她自己的刀把剩下的那些竹子处理掉。哈……对于一个这么小的女孩来说，她的力气实在惊人，而她日常所做的那些劳动更是让她的体格和意志都变得更加坚强。以她这样的生活安排来看……这种变化其实是不可避免的，对吧？她与母亲之间的关系逐渐疏远，也是情理之中的事。 这种稳定的生活节奏咚咚咚一阵锋利的竹叶划过草木丛生的地面，这一声清脆的声音打断了你的思绪，你不禁摇了摇头。基代子绝对不会干这种体力活的，这一点可以肯定。然而，尽管她们之间存在诸多差异，在最重要的方面，她们其实是相同的……对吧？ 你再次摇了摇头，那些思绪渐渐消散，而那根高而细的竹子也终于重重地倒在了地上。 我想，今天就到这里吧。
