Within a handful of moves, you're forced to admit defeat, falling prey to Kinu's relentless assault. She's definitely improved since she was a child. On her part, Kinu looks a little disappointed at the easy victory, grinning sheepishly and rubbing her chin with thumb and forefinger. Eventually, she gives you an easygoing shrug and turns her palms skyward. "Well, guess that's that, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. I'll never go easy on you just because we're family, you know. There was nothing you could've done about the situation since you made that play there —" she points down at the board amidst the few remaining pieces — "so I decided to wrap it up as quickly as I could." That's very kind of her, you suppose. "Ehe. There's no point in dragging out someone's loss, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. Humiliating people isn't in my style. Do it quick and get it over with, yeah?" You can see her point. Still, did she have fun? "Not from the game itself, I'll admit to that. But spending time with you is always great, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]." She's still no different from when she was a kit — a honey-tongued flatterer when she puts her mind to it. |As the game proceeds apace, your fox-daughter quickly becomes a pinpoint of intense focus, her ice-blue eyes narrowing to slits as she studies the board. Humming to herself, Kinu sweeps her five tails sweep out to her front, and she hugs her own silken fur close to herself as her moves become much more methodical and much less lackadaisical. "Hmm..." It's almost as if she's enjoying being decently challenged — or at least, more of a challenge than [kiyoko.numKits 3|her siblings usually put up|she gets from playing against herself]. You're going to give it your all, too — if you lose, it's not going to be from lack of trying. The state of the battlefield that's the wooden game board shifts from moment to moment, the tides of war turning at a whim; it's hard to discern who exactly has the upper hand until out of nowhere, Kinu pulls off a series of moves that has you completely blindsided outmaneuvered in moments. You see the ambush too late, a snare amongst the innocuous grasses, and it's at that point that you retrace her moves and realize she was heading for this endgame all along. "...And there. Good show, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], but I win in the end. For a moment I thought you were going to see through me, but I decided to take the risk anyway." So, she's become the kind to set elaborate yet unassuming snares to entrap the unwary, eh? [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar| You've had the opportunity to play board games like chess and checkers in your past, and some of the strategies do carry over to these games of hers, if not completely. Hopefully, you've been able to give a your daughter new perspective on various plays that Kiyoko's home culture wouldn't be familiar with. "Weeeelll... that's one way of putting it, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]; I think I learned something from all this, and more importantly, it's nice to spend time with you when you're around. This is a social activity, after all." Heh. Is that an invitation? "Like I said, I always enjoy the time I get to spend with you, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], so you should definitely take me up on that offer!" |Well, considering that you didn't have much chance to play these sorts of board games in your past, it's not really a surprise you fell into her trap like this. She's really gotten better since she was a child. Kinu considers you with a small smile. "Well, if you got to play more, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom], who knows how you might improve? Perhaps you should play more board games with me in the future?" Oh, she doesn't have to couch it like that — you'll gladly play with her any time she wants. "Well, it still has to be said, you know. Besides, couching it in ways that're beneficial to the other party makes them more agreeable." ] Psh, isn't that just adorably devious. ] ] Eventually, though, Kinu finishes the last of her tea, stands and gives you a very lazy and unabashedly foxy stretch. "Once again, thanks, [pc.mf|Dad|Mom]. It was fun, but I've got to finish up the rest of today's work before I head on out to Granny Komari's for the afternoon. Don't worry about the board and everything — I'll put them all back when I get home in the evening." Well, if she insists. All right, then, you'll be heading off first. Getting to your feet, you give your fox-daughter a final wave before stepping on out of her chambers and into the warm morning sun; before long, you're back on the road again, [party.hasCompanions |having collected [party.compNames] back to you |safe in the knowledge that Kinu will be fine while you're gone ]. "

rows.original: "I am always up for some fine conversation — recently, I have been trying my hand at some traditional-style art, which Nakano has been helping me with. He says that at the astounding rate at which I am going, it will not be that long before he has nothing left to teach me." Kinu looks really, really pleased with herself, but underneath all that you can tell that your fox-daughter is absolutely begging for your recognition and approval. Well then. [pc.bgMulti noblescion charmer acolyte scholar minstrel |Your previous life in high society did impart some measure of knowledge in that field — both from the tutors hired for you when you were young, and from the eventual schmoozing that went on in those hobnobbing circles. If she could show you something of her work, you'd be glad to give your opinion of it from the perspective of the Belharan style. |Your previous life in high society did impart some measure of knowledge in that field — mostly because you needed to be able to hold a conversation about the subject while schmoozing about and pretend you knew much more than you actually did. Still, for what it's worth you're willing to give your opinion on her works from the perspective of the Belharan style, if that's fine with her. |While what art and artistic theory you'd had contact with in your past life was largely restricted to religious art and iconography, something is better than nothing. You'd be willing to give your perspective on her works from that angle, if that's fine with her. |Your previous life in academia certainly did expose you to several artistic concepts, even though they may not have been your primary field of study. Nevertheless, anyone in those circles was expected to have had something of a holistic education, and you certainly feel qualified and would be glad to give your opinion of it from the perspective of the Belharan style. |While your history has been in the performing arts rather than painting and the like, you've experienced and understood enough of the latter that you're reasonably confident of having some basic competency in the art theory involved. While you wouldn't say you're any kind fo expert, you'd definitely be glad to give your opinion of it from the perspective of the Belharan style. |While you don't know very much about painting and art theory, you'd be glad to do what you can. Even a peasant with an unrefined palate can at least tell if a dish is delicious or not without being a cook or gourmet. ] [pc.bg noblescion charmer acolyte scholar minstrel |Kinu visibly brightens, her ice-blue eyes lighting up and ears perking with energy. Does she... does she look embarrassed? "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... that would be an honor. Yes, obtaining comment and criticism from a foreign perspective might provide insight on a new and interesting direction... |Kinu smiles. "I always value your opinion, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. After all, like me, do you not learn quickly? Is that not my inheritance from you? I am sure you have encountered much on your travels, and furthermore, I feel that my art must be understandable by everyone to some degree, even if not everyone is capable of fully comprehending it... ]please, if you [party.has kiyoko|and Mother ]could wait here forthwith, I will show you some of my recent endeavors." With that, Kinu ushers [party.has kiyoko|the both of ]you to make yourselves comfortable at the low table by the firepit while she heads into her sleeping chambers to get the goods. [party.has kiyoko |You share a glance with Kiyoko while she's gone, meeting your fox-wife's eyes at your side. Did Kinu show much interest in painting when you were... away? You know she didn't quite have a great deal of interest in it when she was a kit. Kiyoko had taught her some poetry and calligraphy, you remember, but painting... you don't quite recall. "Hm. Our daughter had developed a little interest in that time when she was at that difficult age between a kit and a young woman. However, she did not show that much enthusiasm for painting until she took up with Komari's boy... for all his flaws, he is a fine young man in my estimation and could indeed improve considerably with keeping. No doubt he was the one who sparked our daughter's interest in all sorts of fine traditional arts, painting included. Kinu was obligated to know something of them as part and parcel of her station, but for her to pursue them so vigorously is something that can only be motivated by love of some sort." You can't say you fully approve of Nakano given his animosity to foreigners; [pc.ra kitsune|even given your new appearance and station and the knowledge that he's trying very hard to accept that, you can't shake the feeling that at some level there's a bunch of resentment|you get the distinct feeling that he barely tolerates you because his ancestor and liege demanded it of him]. But in these things, you figure that Kiyoko probably knows better than you, and wants the best for Kinu just as you do. "Indeed." It's then that your fox-daughter chooses to make her return, bearing a number of rolled-up paintings in her arms. "Please, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], Mother, here are some pieces I have completed in the last two weeks to a month in my spare time. What do you think?" |Your fox-daughter returns forthwith several moments later, bearing a number of rolled-up paintings in her arms. "Please, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], let me know what you think. I have completed these in the last two weeks to a month." ] You look over the nearest one at hand. It's [a] [rand |scene of a literal fox's wedding in full traditional style, complete with a sunlight shower while the bride's being delivered to the groom's house along a lantern-lined procession in the evening. Everyone looks pretty happy to be there despite the evening drizzle, and you can't help but wonder if this is what your daughter wants for herself — most of the bride's face is hidden under the white hood of her wedding dress. |scene of a mountain waterfall in motion, complete with several trees perched precariously upon mossy rock. Try as you might, you can't help but see similarities in what's depicted here and the waterfall that obscures the entrance to Kiyoko's home. Oh well, as they say, draw what you know, right? |rather vigorous attempt at a self-portrait. Knowing the way kitsune think, you're not exactly sure if a self-portrait is being too full of oneself for their culture — but hey, half of Kinu comes from you, for all that she's a full-blooded kitsune. If anything, the stylised manner in which she's done her own likeness in makes her look less attractive than she ought to be, which is a bit of a shame. Aren't portraits supposed to be tilted towards making their subjects look good, instead of the other way around, or do the kitsune think differently as a people? |scene of several sparrows behind a house, clustered about a solitary figure feeding them rice from a small bag. The details of whoever it is are fuzzy and imprecise, but judging by the proportions you can at the very least tell it's meant to be a kitsune child. By contrast, the sparrows are depicted in excruciating detail as they fight over the rice, right down to the blacks of their eyes. It's an interesting style, to put it mildly. ] [pc.bg noblescion charmer acolyte scholar minstrel |You spend the next few moments discussing the whys and wherefores of Kinu's painting with her, making several stylistic and color suggestions while emphasising that you're coming at this from a Belharanan point of view and the artistic traditions it carries. Even given your background and the measure of knowledge your past offers you, half the time you feel like you're just making it up as you go along or outright miseducating your daughter — how well would the blending of styles from two disparate cultures go, anyway? It'd certainly be innovative, but innovation for its own sake isn't any kind of plus, either. Well, Kinu asked for your honest opinion, so here it is. She's an adult now; the best thing you can do for her is to give your unfettered thoughts and let her sort out what she wants to keep and what she wants to discard on her own terms. |Well, since you really don't know very much about art given your background, you settle for asking Kinu to explain to you various aspects of the painting, as well as why she made certain decisions in doing what she did. Half the time you're keenly feeling your ignorance, but your fox-daughter is always concise and polite in explaining her artistic work to you. Half of what she's saying is going over your head, to be honest, not because you're dumb or anything but you simply don't have the grounding to understand the words coming from your fox-daughter's lips and you already have the feeling that she's dumbing it down as far as she can while still being correct. ] But the most important thing is... you're sitting down here with your daughter and having a good conversation about her endeavors, and if there's anything you've learned in your travels since all of this began it's that people of all races and walks of life love talking about themselves — prod anyone, and they're liable to give you their entire life's backstory at the drop of a hat. While this has been going on, Kinu heats up some tea and serves up the bitter brew in tall cups, perfect for an extended conversation. [party.has kiyoko |Not that your fox-wife has been silent, either. It's practically a relief whenever Kiyoko steps in whenever you start to flounder — at least she has the background and knowledge of her country's art style in order to properly guide and advise Kinu in that regard. She still is content to remain in the background most of the time and allow you to drive the conversation, but steps in with some advice or quip when the words begin to lull. Really, what a godsend... but that tact and etiquette in action is truly part of your fox-wife, isn't it? As your eye catches hers, she gives you a small smile and a wink. ] At last, though, you think you've exhausted yourself; besides, the sunshine filtering in from outside suggests that the day is almost at its zenith. You've taken up enough of her time... although they say that time flies when you're having fun, spending time with Kinu has the exact opposite effect — though it's no less enjoyable, being able to be with her draws mere minutes out into hours, and hours into an entire day. After poring over, discussing and gushing over your daughter's handiwork, you're pretty much mentally drained, if in a very good way. "I am glad to be able to have your opinion, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. It always matters." Kinu looks over the tea set, then starts rolling her paintings back up. "Thank you for dropping by today." Of course, of course. Any reason to spend time with your daughter as a family is a delight. A thought, though. Has she ever considered putting any of her works on display, even privately? "Mmm... I am not that skilled yet..." Not even in the dining hall or in her own quarters? Kinu gives you a small, sheepish smile. "Come now, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. That would be immensely self-conceited." [party.has kiyoko|Behind you, Kiyoko giggles, although not so quietly that you can't hear her. ]Ah well. Cultural differences and all that. "Now... [pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]if I may beg your leave, I shall put these away and wash up for my time with Matron Komari this afternoon. It has been very enjoyable being able to spend time with you[party.has kiyoko| both], and please stay safe on the roads and in your adventures out there." Yes. You'll leave her to it, then. Kinu rises and gives you a bow, which you feel obliged to return[party.has kiyoko| alongside Kiyoko]. Time to go, then— if you don't get moving, you'll never leave...
rows.translation: 我总是很乐意进行愉快的交谈——最近，我开始尝试一些传统风格的艺术创作，中野一直在帮助我。他说，以我目前的学习速度，用不了多久，他就没什么东西可以教我的了。 纪久看起来真的非常非常满意自己，但在这表象之下，你能察觉到，这个你的狐妖女儿其实是在迫切地渴望得到你的认可与赞同。那么，好吧。 [pc.bgMulti noblescion charmer acolyte scholar minstrel |你在上流社会的前世经历确实让你在那个领域积累了一些知识——这些知识既来自于你年轻时聘请的导师们，也来自于你在那些社交圈子里所进行的各种交流。如果她能向你展示一些她的作品，你一定会很乐意从贝尔哈兰风格的视角来给出你的评价。 |你在上流社会的生活经历确实让你在那个领域积累了一些知识——主要是因为你需要在闲聊时谈论这些话题，同时假装自己懂得比实际更多。不过，如果她不介意的话，你还是愿意从贝尔哈兰风格的角度来评价她的作品。 |虽然你在前世接触过的艺术形式和艺术理论主要局限于宗教艺术和图像学，但总比一无所知要好。如果你觉得她没有意见的话，你很愿意从那个角度来分享自己对她的作品的看法。 |你在学术界的经历确实让你接触到了许多艺术概念，尽管这些可能并非你主要研究的领域。不过，在那个圈子里，任何人都应该接受过较为全面的教育。因此，你觉得自己完全有资格从贝尔哈兰风格的角度来发表自己的看法。 |虽然你的背景在于表演艺术，而非绘画等领域，但你对绘画也有足够的了解和体验，因此你对自己在相关艺术理论方面具备一定的基础能力相当有信心。虽然你不会自称是专家，但如果你能从贝尔哈兰风格的角度来发表自己的看法，你肯定会很乐意这样做。 |虽然你对绘画和艺术理论了解不多，但你仍然会尽自己所能去帮忙。就像一个品味并不高雅的农民，也至少能够分辨出一道菜是否美味，即使他并不是厨师或美食家。 ] [pc.bg noblescion charmer acolyte scholar minstrel |纪久的眼睛明显亮了起来，那冰蓝色的眼眸中闪烁着光芒，耳朵也因为兴奋而微微动了起来。她……她看起来是不是尴尬？ 啊， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]…那将是一种荣幸。的确，从外国的角度获得评论与批评，或许能帮助我们找到新的、有趣的发展方向…… |纪久笑了。我一直都非常重视你的意见， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]毕竟，就像我一样，你不是学东西也很快吗？这不正是我从你那里继承来的天赋吗？我相信你在旅途中一定经历过很多事情，而且我觉得，我的艺术在某种程度上一定是能够被所有人理解的，即使不是每个人都能完全领会它的精髓…… ]拜托了，如果你[party.has kiyoko|还有母亲 ]我马上就可以过来，我会向你们展示我最近的一些成果。 就这样，小娟引领着大家前进。 [party.has kiyoko|他们两个 ]你们可以在火坑旁的矮桌旁休息，等她去她的卧室取那些东西回来。 [party.has kiyoko |当纪代子离开后，你与她对视了一眼，同时你也看到了站在你身旁的那个狐狸妻子的目光。 在你不在的时候，纪久对绘画表现出过很大的兴趣吗？你记得，当她还是个小孩子的时候，她对绘画并不是很感兴趣。纪代子曾经教她一些诗歌和书法，不过绘画……你似乎不太记得了。 嗯，我们女儿在那个介于少女与成年女性之间的叛逆年龄阶段，确实对绘画产生了一点点兴趣。不过，直到她开始和麻里的儿子交往之后，她才真正对绘画表现出浓厚的热情。尽管他有很多缺点，但在我看来，他仍然是个不错的年轻人。只要他继续努力，肯定会有很大的进步。毫无疑问，正是他激发了我们女儿对各种传统艺术，包括绘画的兴趣。作为她职责的一部分，小娟有必要了解一些关于他们的事情，但她能够如此积极地去追寻他们，这其中必定蕴含着某种情感。 鉴于中野对外国人的敌意，你不能说你完全赞同他的观点。 [pc.ra kitsune|尽管你如今的外貌、地位都发生了变化，而且他也一直在努力接受这些变化，但我还是觉得，在某种程度上，他内心依然充满了怨恨。|你会有一种明显的感觉，那就是他之所以能容忍你的存在，仅仅是因为他的祖先和上级要求他这么做而已。]但在这些事情上，你大概会认为清子比你更了解情况，她也会像你一样，希望纪久得到最好的结果。 确实如此。 就在这时，你的狐妖女儿选择了归来，她怀里抱着几幅卷起来的画作。 拜托了， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]妈妈，这是我这两周到一个月的空闲时间里完成的一些作品，您觉得怎么样？ |几分钟后，你的狐妖女儿立刻回来了，怀里抱着几幅卷起来的画作。 拜托了， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]请告诉我你的想法。我在过去的两周到一个月里完成了这些工作。 ] 你看向手边最近的一幅。画上是[rand |一场完全按照传统风格举办的狐狸婚礼：傍晚时分，新娘在灯笼照亮的队伍中被送往新郎的家，途中还有阳光洒落下来。尽管傍晚下着小雨，但在场的每个人都显得非常开心。你不禁会想，这是否就是你女儿梦寐以求的婚礼场景——新娘的脸庞大部分都被婚纱上的白色头巾遮住了。 |一幅动态的山间瀑布景象，几棵树摇摇欲坠地生长在长满苔藓的岩石上。无论你如何努力，都不得不意识到，这里描绘的场景与隐藏在清子家入口处的那道瀑布有着惊人的相似之处。唉，俗话说，画你所熟悉的吧？ |这其实是一次相当努力的自我画像尝试。考虑到狐族的思想方式，你其实不太确定这样的自我画像在他们的文化中是否算得上是过于自我表现了——不过，话说回来，尽管小娟是一只纯血的狐族，但她的血统中有一半确实来自你。事实上，她以这种风格化的方式来描绘自己的形象，反而让她看起来较少她的容貌本应该更加动人才对，这样反而有点可惜。难道画肖像的时候不应该把人物画得更加好看一些吗？还是说，作为狐狸一族，他们的审美标准有所不同呢？ |画面中，几只麻雀聚集在房屋后方，围绕着一个人影——那个人正从一个小袋子里掏出米粒喂它们。虽然那个角色的具体形象有些模糊不清，但从比例上看，至少可以判断这应该是一个狐妖的孩子。相比之下，那些麻雀却被描绘得极为细致，它们争抢米粒的场景甚至连眼睛的颜色都被刻画得一清二楚。用委婉的说法，这种绘画风格确实相当有趣。 ] [pc.bg noblescion charmer acolyte scholar minstrel |接下来的几分钟里，你与她详细讨论了小娟这幅画作的创作背景与原因，提出了几项关于风格和色彩方面的建议。同时，你也强调自己是从贝尔哈拉纳的角度出发，结合其独特的艺术传统来提出这些建议的。即便考虑到你的背景以及你过去所积累的知识，很多时候你还是会觉得自己只是在即兴发挥，或者干脆是在误导自己的女儿——毕竟，将两种截然不同的文化风格融合在一起，最终效果会如何呢？这确实是一种创新，但仅仅为了创新而创新，并不能算是什么优点。 嗯，小娟希望得到你坦诚的意见，那么我就直说了。她现在已经是个成年人了；你能为她做的最好的事情，就是毫无保留地表达你的想法，让她自己来决定哪些东西应该保留，哪些应该舍弃。 |嗯，鉴于你的背景，你对艺术确实了解得不多，所以你只能请小娟来为你解释这幅画的各个方面，以及她为何会做出那样的创作决定。很多时候，你都能清楚地感受到自己的无知，但你的狐狸女儿在向你解释她的艺术作品时，总是简洁而礼貌的。说实话，她说的有一半内容你根本听不懂。这并不是因为你笨或者有什么问题，而只是因为你没有相应的知识基础，无法理解你那个“狐狸女儿”说出的那些话。以及你已经感觉到，她在确保表达准确的前提下，正在尽可能地简化自己的表述方式。 ] 但最重要的是……你们现在正和女儿坐在一起，愉快地谈论她所做的一切。在这一切开始以来，我在旅途中领悟到的一点是：无论种族或社会地位如何，人们都喜欢谈论自己。只要稍微一引导，他们就会毫不迟疑地向你讲述自己的一生经历。而在这期间，小娟则煮好了茶，把那杯苦涩的茶倒进高杯里，正好适合长时间聊天使用。 [party.has kiyoko rows.raw: " "I am always up for some fine conversation — recently, I have been trying my hand at some traditional-style art, which Nakano has been helping me with. He says that at the astounding rate at which I am going, it will not be that long before he has nothing left to teach me." Kinu looks really, really pleased with herself, but underneath all that you can tell that your fox-daughter is absolutely begging for your recognition and approval. Well then. [pc.bgMulti noblescion charmer acolyte scholar minstrel |Your previous life in high society did impart some measure of knowledge in that field — both from the tutors hired for you when you were young, and from the eventual schmoozing that went on in those hobnobbing circles. If she could show you something of her work, you'd be glad to give your opinion of it from the perspective of the Belharan style. |Your previous life in high society did impart some measure of knowledge in that field — mostly because you needed to be able to hold a conversation about the subject while schmoozing about and pretend you knew much more than you actually did. Still, for what it's worth you're willing to give your opinion on her works from the perspective of the Belharan style, if that's fine with her. |While what art and artistic theory you'd had contact with in your past life was largely restricted to religious art and iconography, something is better than nothing. You'd be willing to give your perspective on her works from that angle, if that's fine with her. |Your previous life in academia certainly did expose you to several artistic concepts, even though they may not have been your primary field of study. Nevertheless, anyone in those circles was expected to have had something of a holistic education, and you certainly feel qualified and would be glad to give your opinion of it from the perspective of the Belharan style. |While your history has been in the performing arts rather than painting and the like, you've experienced and understood enough of the latter that you're reasonably confident of having some basic competency in the art theory involved. While you wouldn't say you're any kind fo expert, you'd definitely be glad to give your opinion of it from the perspective of the Belharan style. |While you don't know very much about painting and art theory, you'd be glad to do what you can. Even a peasant with an unrefined palate can at least tell if a dish is delicious or not without being a cook or gourmet. ] [pc.bg noblescion charmer acolyte scholar minstrel |Kinu visibly brightens, her ice-blue eyes lighting up and ears perking with energy. Does she... does she look embarrassed? "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... that would be an honor. Yes, obtaining comment and criticism from a foreign perspective might provide insight on a new and interesting direction... |Kinu smiles. "I always value your opinion, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. After all, like me, do you not learn quickly? Is that not my inheritance from you? I am sure you have encountered much on your travels, and furthermore, I feel that my art must be understandable by everyone to some degree, even if not everyone is capable of fully comprehending it... ]please, if you [party.has kiyoko|and Mother ]could wait here forthwith, I will show you some of my recent endeavors." With that, Kinu ushers [party.has kiyoko|the both of ]you to make yourselves comfortable at the low table by the firepit while she heads into her sleeping chambers to get the goods. [party.has kiyoko |You share a glance with Kiyoko while she's gone, meeting your fox-wife's eyes at your side. Did Kinu show much interest in painting when you were... away? You know she didn't quite have a great deal of interest in it when she was a kit. Kiyoko had taught her some poetry and calligraphy, you remember, but painting... you don't quite recall. "Hm. Our daughter had developed a little interest in that time when she was at that difficult age between a kit and a young woman. However, she did not show that much enthusiasm for painting until she took up with Komari's boy... for all his flaws, he is a fine young man in my estimation and could indeed improve considerably with keeping. No doubt he was the one who sparked our daughter's interest in all sorts of fine traditional arts, painting included. Kinu was obligated to know something of them as part and parcel of her station, but for her to pursue them so vigorously is something that can only be motivated by love of some sort." You can't say you fully approve of Nakano given his animosity to foreigners; [pc.ra kitsune|even given your new appearance and station and the knowledge that he's trying very hard to accept that, you can't shake the feeling that at some level there's a bunch of resentment|you get the distinct feeling that he barely tolerates you because his ancestor and liege demanded it of him]. But in these things, you figure that Kiyoko probably knows better than you, and wants the best for Kinu just as you do. "Indeed." It's then that your fox-daughter chooses to make her return, bearing a number of rolled-up paintings in her arms. "Please, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], Mother, here are some pieces I have completed in the last two weeks to a month in my spare time. What do you think?" |Your fox-daughter returns forthwith several moments later, bearing a number of rolled-up paintings in her arms. "Please, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], let me know what you think. I have completed these in the last two weeks to a month." ] You look over the nearest one at hand. It's [a] [rand |scene of a literal fox's wedding in full traditional style, complete with a sunlight shower while the bride's being delivered to the groom's house along a lantern-lined procession in the evening. Everyone looks pretty happy to be there despite the evening drizzle, and you can't help but wonder if this is what your daughter wants for herself — most of the bride's face is hidden under the white hood of her wedding dress. |scene of a mountain waterfall in motion, complete with several trees perched precariously upon mossy rock. Try as you might, you can't help but see similarities in what's depicted here and the waterfall that obscures the entrance to Kiyoko's home. Oh well, as they say, draw what you know, right? |rather vigorous attempt at a self-portrait. Knowing the way kitsune think, you're not exactly sure if a self-portrait is being too full of oneself for their culture — but hey, half of Kinu comes from you, for all that she's a full-blooded kitsune. If anything, the stylised manner in which she's done her own likeness in makes her look less attractive than she ought to be, which is a bit of a shame. Aren't portraits supposed to be tilted towards making their subjects look good, instead of the other way around, or do the kitsune think differently as a people? |scene of several sparrows behind a house, clustered about a solitary figure feeding them rice from a small bag. The details of whoever it is are fuzzy and imprecise, but judging by the proportions you can at the very least tell it's meant to be a kitsune child. By contrast, the sparrows are depicted in excruciating detail as they fight over the rice, right down to the blacks of their eyes. It's an interesting style, to put it mildly. ] [pc.bg noblescion charmer acolyte scholar minstrel |You spend the next few moments discussing the whys and wherefores of Kinu's painting with her, making several stylistic and color suggestions while emphasising that you're coming at this from a Belharanan point of view and the artistic traditions it carries. Even given your background and the measure of knowledge your past offers you, half the time you feel like you're just making it up as you go along or outright miseducating your daughter — how well would the blending of styles from two disparate cultures go, anyway? It'd certainly be innovative, but innovation for its own sake isn't any kind of plus, either. Well, Kinu asked for your honest opinion, so here it is. She's an adult now; the best thing you can do for her is to give your unfettered thoughts and let her sort out what she wants to keep and what she wants to discard on her own terms. |Well, since you really don't know very much about art given your background, you settle for asking Kinu to explain to you various aspects of the painting, as well as why she made certain decisions in doing what she did. Half the time you're keenly feeling your ignorance, but your fox-daughter is always concise and polite in explaining her artistic work to you. Half of what she's saying is going over your head, to be honest, not because you're dumb or anything but you simply don't have the grounding to understand the words coming from your fox-daughter's lips and you already have the feeling that she's dumbing it down as far as she can while still being correct. ] But the most important thing is... you're sitting down here with your daughter and having a good conversation about her endeavors, and if there's anything you've learned in your travels since all of this began it's that people of all races and walks of life love talking about themselves — prod anyone, and they're liable to give you their entire life's backstory at the drop of a hat. While this has been going on, Kinu heats up some tea and serves up the bitter brew in tall cups, perfect for an extended conversation. [party.has kiyoko |Not that your fox-wife has been silent, either. It's practically a relief whenever Kiyoko steps in whenever you start to flounder — at least she has the background and knowledge of her country's art style in order to properly guide and advise Kinu in that regard. She still is content to remain in the background most of the time and allow you to drive the conversation, but steps in with some advice or quip when the words begin to lull. Really, what a godsend... but that tact and etiquette in action is truly part of your fox-wife, isn't it? As your eye catches hers, she gives you a small smile and a wink. ] At last, though, you think you've exhausted yourself; besides, the sunshine filtering in from outside suggests that the day is almost at its zenith. You've taken up enough of her time... although they say that time flies when you're having fun, spending time with Kinu has the exact opposite effect — though it's no less enjoyable, being able to be with her draws mere minutes out into hours, and hours into an entire day. After poring over, discussing and gushing over your daughter's handiwork, you're pretty much mentally drained, if in a very good way. "I am glad to be able to have your opinion, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. It always matters." Kinu looks over the tea set, then starts rolling her paintings back up. "Thank you for dropping by today." Of course, of course. Any reason to spend time with your daughter as a family is a delight. A thought, though. Has she ever considered putting any of her works on display, even privately? "Mmm... I am not that skilled yet..." Not even in the dining hall or in her own quarters? Kinu gives you a small, sheepish smile. "Come now, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. That would be immensely self-conceited." [party.has kiyoko|Behind you, Kiyoko giggles, although not so quietly that you can't hear her. ]Ah well. Cultural differences and all that. "Now... [pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]if I may beg your leave, I shall put these away and wash up for my time with Matron Komari this afternoon. It has been very enjoyable being able to spend time with you[party.has kiyoko| both], and please stay safe on the roads and in your adventures out there." Yes. You'll leave her to it, then. Kinu rises and gives you a bow, which you feel obliged to return[party.has kiyoko| alongside Kiyoko]. Time to go, then— if you don't get moving, you'll never leave... "

rows.original: "I had intended to do some work in the garden behind my chambers this morning. That should be a suitably invigorating yet serene activity for all involved." Gardening, eh? She's got quite the impressive display out back. You'd certainly like to know how she keeps it that way. "Mother taught me a lot while I was growing up," Kinu replies with a dip of her head. "I owe much to her, especially her knowledge of shaping, to be able to have brought such beauty into our home." [party.has kiyoko |"Ehe. Oh dear child, you flatter me." Kiyoko turns to you. "Well, beloved, what happened is that our daughter was showing considerable interest in the natural world, as I'm sure you well recall. I simply showed her some simple shaping methods to pique her curiosity, and her nature did the rest. Her mind is such a powerful thing when it's not busy being mischievous and devious, and having her apply her intellect and leaning towards the problems of the natural world is certainly worthy of someone of her station. Noblewomen in the Old Country do not merely plant gardens, after all." ] Ah! Ah! With her lauding her skill so profusely, you would most certainly be humbled to be able to help her in what small way you're able to, just to have the chance to glimpse your daughter at work. "It is nothing special, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. The bulk of it is merely a lot of careful pruning, weeding and crossbreeding, that is all. I could certainly not be able to grow something like the divine tree which houses Matron Komari and her den; that is out of the reach of any mere mortal to accomplish. I —" Enough. Being humble is one thing and endemic to her culture, but there's a line between being humble and underselling herself. You've seen her works, you know they're beautiful, and you're not going to have any such self-deprecation from her. Does she understand that? "Yes, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Great. Now then, if she wouldn't mind showing you [party.has kiyoko|and her mother ]out back? "But of course. Please, follow me." [rand |Your fox-daughter leads you out the rear entrance, then circles around to a small storeroom where she pushes open a trunk and picks out a pair of gloves, followed by [party.has kiyoko|two more pairs for you and your fox-wife|another pair for you]. She slips them on, gathers up several small and fine-looking gardening tools, then heads out into the warm morning sun. "When I was younger, Mother would send me out into the forest to get flowers for my flower arrangement lessons. While there was a certain sense of adventure and excitement in the hunt, I soon discovered far more satisfaction in raising the flowers from cuttings and seeds myself. The knowledge that you have nurtured something from its very beginning to completion brings about such great satisfaction that I do not believe I can adequately describe it in mere words, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." [party.has kiyoko |"I will say that I was a little surprised when our daughter no longer wanted to hunt for flowers and grow them herself instead," Kiyoko adds with a wistful sigh. "The latter is a lot more work, and for some time I imagined she simply didn't realize the full scope of the effort she'd have to put into actually cultivating a flower garden that would eventually produce blooms worth something. But... she stuck with it. It was a very good and practical way to impart to her some basic knowledge of shaping." ] Kinu's garden is picture-perfect, lit at night by a solitary stone lantern standing in the midst of it all, surrounded by a ring of fine gravel with paths branching outwards from it. The grass is immaculately trimmed to a fine fuzz, and several pebble-ringed flowerbeds and bushes stand along the path. It's nothing fancy and you note that Kinu has done her best to make do with what materials are available to her. As for where she got the flowers... that's anyone's guess. "[pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]if you would be so kind as to assist me?" But of course. Given that you don't know very much about this particular style of gardening craft you're content to stand back and watch, holding the clippings basket while Kinu flits from flowerbed to flowerbed like a busy little bee. The pruning is slow going, but Kinu's movements are deft and exact, deliberate and precise. Even given your lack of knowledge, there's little doubt that those tiny shears of hers are taking off no more and no less than the exact amount in order to produce the best, brightest blossoms. [party.has kiyoko |While Kinu busies herself, Kiyoko makes herself useful, careful to aid but not upstage her daughter's work in her own garden. Weeding, spreading mulch, checking the stems for bugs, rot and other problems — your fox-wife knows that this is her daughter's hour and is content, at last, to be firm in the knowledge that like these flowers, Kinu is the end result of a long period of careful nurturing. A mother's pride, as it were. ] It is but simple maintenance work under the gently warm Marches sunlight and cooling breeze, but every moment spent here with your fox-daughter is completely worth it, even if you're not really doing very much. The important thing is that you're spending time with Kinu, a rare luxury in this time and day. Ah... One by one, the basket fills — unwanted flower buds, diseased or damaged ends, the odd dead caterpillar or two, worm-eaten leaves. The beauty at the top is indeed supported by a lot of often ugly hard work beneath, work that instead of shying away of, Kinu is wholeheartedly throwing herself into. She may be a refined girl, but that doesn't mean she's afraid of getting her hands dirty. Seconds tick into minutes, minutes tick into hours; the slow movement of the sun across the sky towards its zenith is the only indication of time as the [party.has kiyoko|three|both] of you make one slow round of the flowerbeds, eventually ending up at the back porch once more. Your basket is full of clippings, and Kinu gives you a small bow before graciously receiving it from you with both hands. "[pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]thank you for today. Your help is most appreciated, especially when you are usually so busy." That's all right. You got to spend plenty of time with her and there was a lot of communication all around. "But we did not speak very much." Some of the most important messages are carried across without the need for words. You reach out and give your fox-daughter a pat on the head, mussing her hair a little; she squirms and looses a little sigh. |Your fox-daughter leads you out the rear entrance, then circles around to a small storeroom where she pushes open a trunk and picks out a pair of gloves, followed by [party.has kiyoko|two more pairs for you and your fox-wife|another pair for you]. She slips them on, gathers up a pole, several hand nets and a waxed-paper bag before stepping out into the warm sunshine. Situated at the far end of Kinu's garden is a large pond filled with a handful of colorful carp and several aquatic blooms; you recognize a few species of lilies, but most of them aren't native to the Marches. Carried in from the waterfall by stone piping, clear water flows into the pond and is carried away by bamboo culverts, perforated gratings of strangely regular aquatic vines over both inlet and outlet preventing the fish from escaping. The trickle of water is constant in the air, producing a steady stream of white noise, and your fox-daughter studies the serenity of the scene for several moments before passing you a hand net. "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... if you wish to help, could you please assist in clearing out any scum and floating weeds that have gathered by the water's surface? The flowing water helps in discouraging their growth, but the flow stills by the pond's edges." But of course. You take the net and get to work, scooping out the pond muck that's gathered about the edges and bottom before laying it into a small strainer. Kinu'll send it to compost later on, or however she disposes of these things... on her part, your fox-daughter busies herself with caring for the aquatic flora of her pond, clearing their broad, flat leaves of pests and diseased spots while collecting several of the choicest blooms for later use. [party.has kiyoko |While this has been going on, Kiyoko has been feeding the fish, scattering small dried brown pellets upon the water's surface and watching the colorful carp fight over the food, churning the water's surface to frothing. Your fox-wife watches them calmly for several moments, tilting her head and wiggling her ears at the sight. "This brings me back. Daughter, where did you get these koi? They're not native to this part of the world." "Ah, Mother... they were a gift." "From?" "Um..." "Spit it out, child." "Nakano brought them in from the Old Country for me, Mother. He'd heard that I'd gotten Hitoshi to dig me a pond, and... well, he got a tub and carried them all the way in through the gate. It's a miracle they didn't die on the way here." Kiyoko is silent for several moments, then shakes her head. "I can't decide if that's the most brash, romantic, or stupid thing I've ever heard someone do." "That's what I pointed out to him, Mother. He said that the koi had a strong spirit and will to have survived this far, and that I could learn something from them." "Ever with the silly answers. Man fancies himself a poet." "He is a poet, Mother. Even if he is not a very good one." |At length, Kinu finishes harvesting the blossoms before placing their stems in a small basin of water and setting them aside. Gathering up the small bag of waxed paper in her arms, she dips her fingers within and scatters pellets of what looks like dried meat over the water's surface. The colorful carp immediately converge on the spot, fighting over the fish food and churning the water to a froth. Your fox-daughter watches them for several moments, ears twitching, then steps back with a small smile. "You have to be careful when feeding them, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. They will eat as much as you will give, and grow sick if you overfeed them. That, and you do not wish to fully satiate them anyway; a little bit of hunger will provoke them to hunt insects and other pests that congregate in their home." Ha... you remember yourself that as a child, she'd eat as many peaches as she could lay her hands on until she got sick. Either with stomachache and indigestion, or up to the point where she'd just throw up... "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... I was young then and did not have much in the way of wisdom or self-control. It is an ongoing effort..." Nevertheless, carp-raising is like child-raising in a sense. Or caring for any living thing, for that matter. The intricacies change and difficulty of doing so might be different, but the basic precepts are still the same. Kinu is silent for a little while as she scatters another handful of fish food over the water. "There is merit in that notion, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], yet I cannot say I agree wholly with it." That's all right. So long as her reasoning is sound — and you're sure it is, right? — you're content with that. After all, if two people agree with each other on everything and every matter, one of them is probably unnecessary. Probably. "And that is where I must disagree with you, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." You laugh and pet Kinu on the head. She's learning. ] At length, the carp are fed, the water is cleared, and the blossoms pruned and harvested. Beating down from above in the clear Marches sky, the sun itself reflects dully upon the pool's surface; [party.has kiyoko|your fox-wife brings in a large bucket of water drawn from the crossroads well, and all three of you take turns washing off your hands and the tools|your fox-daughter brings in a large bucket of water drawn from the crossroads well, and the both of you take turns washing off your hands and the tools]. "Well, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]thank you for lending me your assistance today. I have indeed dealt with my duties in a most swift and satisfactory manner." She's most welcome. |Your fox-daughter leads you out the rear entrance, then circles around to a small storeroom where she pushes open a trunk and picks out a pair of gloves, followed by [party.has kiyoko|two more pairs for you and your fox-wife|another pair for you]. She slips them on, gathers up a waterproofed cloth pack, then heads out into the warm morning sun. You follow your fox-daughter out to a wooden standing frame, upon which two potted trees have been placed in the warm morning light — two potted miniature trees, at that. "Bonsai," Kinu says as she unrolls the pack to reveal an entire set of tiny gardening tools and several lengths of metal-reinforced string. "One of the most mundane yet exacting applications of shaping." Mm. "This one —" Kinu indicates the small juniper to the left — "is my charge. And that one over there[party.has kiyoko | —" "Is mine," your fox-wife purrs as she slides in between the both of you, [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails wrapping about your bodies comfortingly. "This is an art that teaches one many things. Patience, attention to detail, fine manipulation of one's faculties, a sense of proper aesthetics, and more. Of course I would have taught our daughter such, no matter how silly it may appear to several outsiders. After all, what is the use of a miniature tree? One might as well ask what is the use of music, painting or any form of art, for that matter?" Whoa, she's getting defensive all of a sudden. "Ehe. Sorry. It's just..." Kiyoko taps her chin with a finger. "Old memories. Please, forgive my outburst, and let us begin." | is Mother's." You look between the two, and there's no doubt about it: you don't know much about the aesthetics in this Old Country art form, but Kiyoko's bonsai is definitely healthier and more robust-looking than Kinu's. A glance at Kinu reveals that your fox-daughter is eyeing you out of the corner of her vision, trying very hard not to make it obvious that she's watching closely. Really, now. That nervous lip bite gives it all away. You reach out and give your fox-daughter a pat between the ears — she doesn't need to use her mother as a measuring stick all the time. It's good that she's learned so much from Kiyoko and seeks to emulate her best qualities, but at the end of the day she's going to have to leave her mother's household and den sometime. Kiyoko's task is to prepare her for that day. Kinu looks down, squirming away from your petting. "I... when I was younger, I hoped that even after I grew up, I could still be close to Mother. It... I... let us not dwell upon this, please. We are here to tend to my charge, and spend time as a family." ] With that, Kinu picks up the tiny tools in her gloved hands and gets to work[party.has kiyoko|, her mother doing the same soon after]. You can only shake your head at it all — three different sizes of miniature shears, an equally small rake, leaf trimmers... where do they make all these just for this purpose? Come to think of it, both trees look pretty old despite their size. Surely your fox-family couldn't have raised them from scratch already? "Matron Komari was kind enough to supply Mother and I with cuttings from her own specimens. As you are aware, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], the shrine mother has had... a very long time to live." That would explain it. And there's no magic involved? "Only tools, string, care and time. Anything else would be sacrilegious, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Most shameful." [party.has kiyoko |"I remember doing this with Komari when we were girls," Kiyoko says with a chuckle, a wistful note in her voice. "A lady and her priestly retainer... well, a future lady and her priestly retainer arguing over whose bonsai was better. Ah, to be young again... and raising our voices until the adults came in to shush us and briskly inform the heir that the art of shaping was supposed to be a quiet and solemn endeavor." You've seen Komari. To think that she was a child once, centuries ago... haha, to think that Kiyoko was a child once, centuries ago... a tiny fox kit like Kinu once was. And now your daughter's grown, and grown quite vigorously, too. Certainly with no shortage of potential suitors to boot... ] The sheer aura of concentration is palpable here as your daughter continues working[party.has kiyoko| alongside her mother], dampening the soil, tying wire-string about the tiny branches, and very, very, very careful pruning that scarcely leaves any kind of mark on the tree. It's almost like — no, it is surgery after a fashion, with all the attendant thoroughness and exactness. And yet despite all the effort and care that went into shaping this bonsai of a tiny juniper, you wouldn't know that there'd been a hand behind it if not for its miniature size. [party.has kiyoko |Your fox-wife works quietly alongside your fox-daughter, mostly tending to her own specimen but occasionally dipping over to correct some mistake or oversight of Kinu's. By and large, though, she's content to leave Kinu to her own devices and trust her to make her own decisions, understanding that this isn't just her daughter's own creation, but also not seeking to overshadow the time Kinu's getting to spend with you. This is her hour, after all. ] You're not able to help much with the task at hand, but just watching Kinu at work and having pleasant conversation with your fox-daughter under the warm sun and surrounded on all sides by carefully curated nature is enough to make it feel all worth it. Neither does it escape you that Kinu's certainly getting a lot of satisfaction from being able to show off her accomplishments and skills to you, not just in the end product of the bonsai itself, but more importantly, the process that led up to it. She wants you to see what she's capable of and be proud of her — and you are. It can't be that long since the [party.has kiyoko|three|two] of you started, but the conversation seems to have dragged out but a small slice of time far longer than it should have. The sun has yet to reach its zenith in the clear Marches sky, but satisfied with her work, Kinu sets down her tools, cleans them carefully with a small corner of fine cloth, then sets them back into the waterproofed bag. "Thank you for assisting me today, [pc.mf|Father|Mother].[party.has kiyoko| And you for being here at my side, Mother.]" O-oh, you did nothing at all. It was no problem... "Your presence was important in getting me into the right mindset for the task at hand. In such endeavors, that is just as important as anything else." Now she's laying it on quite thickly, you'd say... ] [party.has kiyoko |Seeing this, your fox-wife chuckles, hiding her mouth behind a hand. "Ah. Well, it is almost noon now. You are due for your tasks with Komari, are you not?" "Yes, Mother." "Go ahead, wash up and make yourself ready, then. Your [pc.mf|father|mother] and I will deal with the rest of this." Kinu looks a little apprehensive at the prospect, but her emotions but flicker on her face for a fraction of a moment. Carefully, your fox-daughter hands her things to Kiyoko and you, then gives the both of you a final bow before departing, her five silvery-white tails following her into her chambers. "Come on, beloved," Kiyoko says, nudging you in the side with an elbow. "Let's pick up after our daughter, shall we?" The two of you do just that, packing away Kinu's tools back into the storeroom. Partway through it all, Kiyoko looks wistfully at the neatly arranged goods and sighs. "We should do this more often." Yes. Yes, you should. "What's that local saying that was around two centuries ago? 'Your son's your son until he takes a wife, but your daughter's your daughter all your life'? Ehe... just because our daughter's grown doesn't mean we can stop being a part of her life. And I'm honestly glad that she feels the same way, too. "All right, then — we need to get these put away and be on our way." |"Well, that will be enough for today, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. It is almost noon and I have to wash up and make myself presentable for my duties with Matron Komari. If you would please... I can handle the putting away myself." Oh, all right then. ] Before long, you're back on the road, feeling much better for having spent the morning with Kinu and reminded of why you're doing all this in the first place. Your fox-daughter is such a precious creature... she has to be protected at all costs.
rows.translation: 今天早上我本来打算在房间后面的花园里做一些活儿。这对大家来说应该既是一种能让人精神振奋的活动，又是一种宁静的体验。 园艺，是吧？她后院的园艺成果确实相当令人印象深刻。你肯定很想知道她是怎么把花园打理得这么好的。 在我成长的过程中，母亲教会了我很多东西。小娟微微低头作为回应。我欠她很多，尤其是她在造型方面的专业知识，正是这些知识让我们的家中充满了如此美好的气息。 [party.has kiyoko |呵呵，哦，亲爱的孩子，你真是太夸奖我了。清子转向了你。嗯，亲爱的，事情是这样的：我们的女儿对自然界表现出了极大的兴趣，这一点你们肯定都还记得。我只是给她介绍了一些简单的观察方法，以此激发她的好奇心，而她的天性自然而然地发挥了作用。当她的注意力没有被调皮捣蛋的事情占据时，她的思维能力其实是非常强大的。让她运用自己的智慧去探索自然界的问题，对于她这样的身份来说，实在是再合适不过了。在古老的国家，贵族女性们仅仅毕竟，还是应该种植花园的。 ] 啊！啊！当她如此过分地称赞自己的技艺时，你肯定会感到无比荣幸，能够尽自己微薄的力量去帮助她， just为了有机会看到自己的女儿在工作。 这没什么特别的， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]其实，其中大部分工作都只是仔细地修剪、除草以及进行杂交培育而已。我绝对不可能培育出像那棵承载着麻里女首领及其一众眷属的神圣树木那样的东西；那样的成就，对于任何一个普通人来说都是遥不可及的。我—— 够了。谦虚是一种美德，也是她文化中的一部分，但谦虚与过分贬低自己之间是有一条界限的。你们都看过她的作品，知道它们非常出色，因此她不可能会做出这种自我贬低的行为。她明白这一点吗？ 是的， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]。" 太好了。那么，如果她不介意的话，可以让你看看吧。 [party.has kiyoko|以及她的母亲 ]在后面吗？ 当然可以。请跟我来吧。 [rand |你的狐狸女儿带你从后门离开，然后绕道来到一个小储藏室。在那里，她推开一个箱子，拿出一副手套，接着[party.has kiyoko|再给你和你的狐狸妻子两对吧|再给你一双吧]她戴上它们，拿上几把小巧精致的工具，然后走进温暖晨光中。 在我小时候，母亲常常让我去森林里采花，用来练习插花。虽然采花的过程带有一丝冒险和刺激的感觉，但我很快发现，通过自己用插枝和种子培育花朵，所带来的满足感要大得多。那种从种子开始，亲手将它们培育成完整的花朵的过程，所带来的成就感是如此强烈，以至于我认为，用语言来描述这种感受实在是远远不够的。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]。" [party.has kiyoko |我得说，当我们的女儿不再愿意自己去采花、种植花苗时，我确实感到有点惊讶。清子带着一丝怅惘叹息道。后者是这需要付出更多的努力，有段时间我甚至以为她根本没有意识到，要想真正培育出一个最终能够开出有价值的花朵的花园，自己需要付出多少努力。但是……她坚持了下来。这种方式其实是一种非常不错且实用的方法，能让她掌握一些关于植物栽培的基本知识。 ] 小娟的花园美得宛如画卷一般，夜晚时，一盏孤零零的石灯笼矗立在花园中央，灯光照亮了整个庭院。周围铺着细碎的砾石，小路从灯笼处向外延伸开来。草丛被修剪得极为整齐，只留下一层细细的草尖；小路两旁还摆放着几个用鹅卵石围成的花坛和灌木丛。这个花园并不奢华，但你可以看出，小娟已经尽她最大的努力，利用手头现有的材料来打造这个花园。至于那些花是从哪里来的……那就只有天知道了。 "[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]， [party.has kiyoko|妈妈， ]如果您能帮帮我，那将真是太好了。 当然可以。既然你对这种园艺方式了解得并不多，那么你只需要站在一旁观看就行了，只需拿着剪下的花草，而小娟则会像一只忙碌的小蜜蜂一样，在一个花坛又一个花坛之间飞来飞去。修剪的工作进行得相当缓慢，但小娟的动作却十分娴熟、精准而从容。尽管她对此并不十分熟悉，但毫无疑问，她使用的那把小剪刀每次剪下的枝叶量都恰到好处，这样才能让花朵开得最茂盛、最鲜艳。 [party.has kiyoko |当小娟忙于自己的事情时，清子也会尽自己的一份力，小心翼翼地帮忙，但从不抢走女儿在自家花园里干活的风头。除草、铺设覆盖物、检查植株上是否有虫害、腐烂或其他问题——这位狐狸妻子深知，现在是属于女儿的时刻，因此她很满足，终于能够确信：就像这些花朵一样，小娟也是经过长时间细心照料才成长起来的。这，可以说是母亲的自豪吧。 ] 在三月温暖柔和的阳光与凉爽的微风中，这些工作其实只是简单的维护而已，但与你那狐狸女儿共度的每一刻都绝对值得，即使你并没有真正做多少事情。重要的是，你正在与小娟一起度过时候——在当今这个时代，这无疑是一种难得的奢侈。 啊…… 一个接一个，篮子被填满了——那些不需要的花蕾、病态或受损的枝条、偶尔出现的死毛毛虫，还有被虫子啃食过的叶子。那些显眼而美丽的花朵，其实都是建立在下面那些常常显得丑陋而繁琐的劳动之上的。而小娟，并没有回避这些工作，反而全身心地投入到其中。她或许是个文雅的女孩，但这并不意味着她害怕亲自动手去做一些事情。 时间一分一秒地流逝，几分钟变成几小时；太阳缓缓地在天空中移动，最终到达顶点——这一过程才是时间流逝的唯一标志。 [party.has kiyoko|三|两者都]你们沿着花坛慢慢地走了一圈，最终又一次来到了后门廊。你们的篮子里装满了剪下的花枝，小娟向你们微微鞠躬，然后双手接过了篮子。 "[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]， [party.has kiyoko|妈妈， ]非常感谢你今天的帮助。你的支持对我们来说意义重大，尤其是考虑到你平时总是非常忙碌。 没关系。你需要花很多时间和她相处，同时也要加强沟通。 不过我们并没有聊太多。 有些最重要的信息，其实并不需要用言语来表达。你伸出手，轻轻拍了拍你那个狐狸女儿的脑袋，她的头发因此有些凌乱；她扭动了一下身体，然后轻轻叹了口气。 |你的狐狸女儿带你从后门离开，然后绕道来到一个小储藏室。在那里，她推开一个箱子，拿出一副手套，接着[party.has kiyoko|再给你和你的狐狸妻子两对吧|再给你一双吧]她穿上它们，拿上一根杆子、几张捕网和一个蜡纸袋，然后走到了温暖的阳光下。 在小娟花园的尽头，有一个大池塘，里面游着几条色彩斑斓的鲤鱼，还有几朵水生植物；你能认出其中几种百合花，但大多数其实并不是原产于这些地区的。清澈的水流从瀑布处通过石砌渠道被引入池塘，然后又通过竹制涵洞排出。在池塘的进出口处，都装有由规则排列的水生植物编织而成的网状结构，这些结构能够有效防止鱼类逃逸。水滴在空气中不断滴落，发出持续的白色噪音。你的狐狸女儿静静地观察着这一幕好一会儿，然后递给你一张手网。 啊， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]……如果你愿意帮忙的话，能否请帮忙清理水面上堆积的浮渣和浮草呢？流动的水确实有助于抑制这些植物的生长，但池塘边缘的水流已经变得缓慢了。 当然可以。你拿上网兜，开始工作吧——先把池塘边缘和下装堆积的淤泥清理出来，然后放入一个小筛子中。小娟之后会把这些淤泥用来制作堆肥，或者按照她自己的方式处理这些废弃物……而你的狐狸女儿则负责照料池塘中的水生植物，清除它们宽大的叶片上的害虫和病斑，同时还会采摘一些最新鲜的花朵留作后续使用。 [party.has kiyoko |在这一切发生的同时，清子一直在喂鱼。她将一些干燥的棕色颗粒撒在水面上，然后观察那些色彩斑斓的鲤鱼们争抢食物，导致水面不断翻腾起泡沫。你的狐狸妻子静静地观察着这一幕，有时还会歪着头，摇动耳朵，似乎对这一景象感到十分有趣。 这让我想起了过去。女儿，你是从哪里弄来这些锦鲤的？它们并不是这个地区的原生品种啊。 啊，妈妈……那些都是礼物。 来自哪里？ 嗯…… 快说吧，孩子。 母亲，是中野从那个遥远的国度把它们带给我的。他听说我让仁志为我挖了一个池塘，于是……他就弄来了一个大桶，把这些东西一路搬过了大门。它们能活着来到这里，简直是个奇迹。 清子沉默了好一会儿，然后摇了摇头。我实在想不明白，这种行为到底是显得最大胆、最浪漫，还是最愚蠢。 这就是我当时跟他说的话，妈妈。他说那些锦鲤拥有强大的精神力量和意志力，才能存活到现在，而我可以从它们身上学到一些东西。 总是给出这些愚蠢的回答。这家伙还自以为是个诗人呢。 他是一位诗人，妈妈。即使他并不是非常出色的一位诗人。 |终于，小娟采完了所有的花朵，将它们的花茎放入一个小水盆中，暂时放在一旁。她拿起那个装着蜡纸的小袋子，用手指从里面取出一些看起来像干肉的小颗粒，撒在水面上。那些色彩斑斓的鲤鱼立刻聚集到了那里，争相抢夺这些鱼食，把水搅得泡沫飞溅。你的狐狸女儿静静地观察了它们好一会儿，耳朵微微动着，然后带着一丝微笑退了回去。 在喂它们的时候必须小心。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]它们会吃掉你提供的所有食物，而如果你喂得太多，它们就会生病。另外，你也不希望让它们吃得太饱；适当的饥饿感会促使它们去捕捉那些在它们栖息地附近出现的昆虫和其他害虫。 哈……你还记得吗？小时候，她总是想吃多少桃子就吃多少，直到吃坏了肚子。要么肚子疼、消化不良，要么干脆吐出来…… 啊， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]……那时我还年轻，既缺乏智慧，也缺乏自制力。这是一项需要持续努力的事情…… 然而，养鱼在某种程度上确实类似于养育孩子。或者说，照顾任何生物都是如此。具体的操作方法和难度可能会有所不同，但基本的原理却是相同的。 小娟沉默了一会儿，然后又将一把鱼食撒到了水面上。这个观点确实有一定道理。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]然而，我并不能说自己完全同意这一观点。 没关系。只要她的推理是合理的——而你肯定认为她是合理的，对吧？——你就应该对此感到满意。毕竟，如果两个人在每一件事上都能达成一致，那么其中一个人很可能就是多余的。大概吧。 在这一点上，我必须与你意见相左。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]。" 你笑着轻抚着小娟的脑袋，她说她正在学习呢。 ] 终于，鱼儿得到了喂养，水也被清理干净了，那些花朵也被修剪下来并采集起来。在三月清澈的天空下，阳光直射在水面上，反射出的光芒显得有些暗淡。 [party.has kiyoko|你的狐狸妻子从十字路口的井里打来一大桶水，你们三个人轮流洗手和清洗工具|你的狐狸女儿从十字路口的井里打来一大桶水，你们俩轮流洗手并清洗工具]。 嗯， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]， [party.has kiyoko|妈妈， ]非常感谢您今天给予我的帮助。我确实以非常迅速且令人满意的方式完成了我的职责。 她非常受欢迎。 |你的狐狸女儿带你从后门离开，然后绕道来到一个小储藏室。在那里，她推开一个箱子，拿出一副手套，接着[party.has kiyoko|再给你和你的狐狸妻子两对吧|再给你一双吧]她穿上它们，收拾好那个防水布包，然后走进温暖晨光中。你跟随你的狐狸女儿来到一个木制支架前，在温暖的晨光中，可以看到那里摆放着两盆植物——两盆盆栽植物。微缩模型尤其是那些树木。 盆景。小娟一边展开包裹，一边说道，里面有一整套小巧的园艺工具，还有几段用金属加固的绳子。这是塑造技术中最平凡却又最要求精确的应用之一。 嗯。 这个……小娟”指的是左边那株小刺柏。这是我的职责。还有那边那个[party.has kiyoko | —" 是我的。你的狐狸妻子轻轻滑到你们两人中间，发出呼噜声。 rows.raw: ' "I had intended to do some work in the garden behind my chambers this morning. That should be a suitably invigorating yet serene activity for all involved." Gardening, eh? She's got quite the impressive display out back. You'd certainly like to know how she keeps it that way. "Mother taught me a lot while I was growing up," Kinu replies with a dip of her head. "I owe much to her, especially her knowledge of shaping, to be able to have brought such beauty into our home." [party.has kiyoko |"Ehe. Oh dear child, you flatter me." Kiyoko turns to you. "Well, beloved, what happened is that our daughter was showing considerable interest in the natural world, as I'm sure you well recall. I simply showed her some simple shaping methods to pique her curiosity, and her nature did the rest. Her mind is such a powerful thing when it's not busy being mischievous and devious, and having her apply her intellect and leaning towards the problems of the natural world is certainly worthy of someone of her station. Noblewomen in the Old Country do not merely plant gardens, after all." ] Ah! Ah! With her lauding her skill so profusely, you would most certainly be humbled to be able to help her in what small way you're able to, just to have the chance to glimpse your daughter at work. "It is nothing special, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. The bulk of it is merely a lot of careful pruning, weeding and crossbreeding, that is all. I could certainly not be able to grow something like the divine tree which houses Matron Komari and her den; that is out of the reach of any mere mortal to accomplish. I —" Enough. Being humble is one thing and endemic to her culture, but there's a line between being humble and underselling herself. You've seen her works, you know they're beautiful, and you're not going to have any such self-deprecation from her. Does she understand that? "Yes, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Great. Now then, if she wouldn't mind showing you [party.has kiyoko|and her mother ]out back? "But of course. Please, follow me." [rand |Your fox-daughter leads you out the rear entrance, then circles around to a small storeroom where she pushes open a trunk and picks out a pair of gloves, followed by [party.has kiyoko|two more pairs for you and your fox-wife|another pair for you]. She slips them on, gathers up several small and fine-looking gardening tools, then heads out into the warm morning sun. "When I was younger, Mother would send me out into the forest to get flowers for my flower arrangement lessons. While there was a certain sense of adventure and excitement in the hunt, I soon discovered far more satisfaction in raising the flowers from cuttings and seeds myself. The knowledge that you have nurtured something from its very beginning to completion brings about such great satisfaction that I do not believe I can adequately describe it in mere words, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." [party.has kiyoko |"I will say that I was a little surprised when our daughter no longer wanted to hunt for flowers and grow them herself instead," Kiyoko adds with a wistful sigh. "The latter is a lot more work, and for some time I imagined she simply didn't realize the full scope of the effort she'd have to put into actually cultivating a flower garden that would eventually produce blooms worth something. But... she stuck with it. It was a very good and practical way to impart to her some basic knowledge of shaping." ] Kinu's garden is picture-perfect, lit at night by a solitary stone lantern standing in the midst of it all, surrounded by a ring of fine gravel with paths branching outwards from it. The grass is immaculately trimmed to a fine fuzz, and several pebble-ringed flowerbeds and bushes stand along the path. It's nothing fancy and you note that Kinu has done her best to make do with what materials are available to her. As for where she got the flowers... that's anyone's guess. "[pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]if you would be so kind as to assist me?" But of course. Given that you don't know very much about this particular style of gardening craft you're content to stand back and watch, holding the clippings basket while Kinu flits from flowerbed to flowerbed like a busy little bee. The pruning is slow going, but Kinu's movements are deft and exact, deliberate and precise. Even given your lack of knowledge, there's little doubt that those tiny shears of hers are taking off no more and no less than the exact amount in order to produce the best, brightest blossoms. [party.has kiyoko |While Kinu busies herself, Kiyoko makes herself useful, careful to aid but not upstage her daughter's work in her own garden. Weeding, spreading mulch, checking the stems for bugs, rot and other problems — your fox-wife knows that this is her daughter's hour and is content, at last, to be firm in the knowledge that like these flowers, Kinu is the end result of a long period of careful nurturing. A mother's pride, as it were. ] It is but simple maintenance work under the gently warm Marches sunlight and cooling breeze, but every moment spent here with your fox-daughter is completely worth it, even if you're not really doing very much. The important thing is that you're spending time with Kinu, a rare luxury in this time and day. Ah... One by one, the basket fills — unwanted flower buds, diseased or damaged ends, the odd dead caterpillar or two, worm-eaten leaves. The beauty at the top is indeed supported by a lot of often ugly hard work beneath, work that instead of shying away of, Kinu is wholeheartedly throwing herself into. She may be a refined girl, but that doesn't mean she's afraid of getting her hands dirty. Seconds tick into minutes, minutes tick into hours; the slow movement of the sun across the sky towards its zenith is the only indication of time as the [party.has kiyoko|three|both] of you make one slow round of the flowerbeds, eventually ending up at the back porch once more. Your basket is full of clippings, and Kinu gives you a small bow before graciously receiving it from you with both hands. "[pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]thank you for today. Your help is most appreciated, especially when you are usually so busy." That's all right. You got to spend plenty of time with her and there was a lot of communication all around. "But we did not speak very much." Some of the most important messages are carried across without the need for words. You reach out and give your fox-daughter a pat on the head, mussing her hair a little; she squirms and looses a little sigh. |Your fox-daughter leads you out the rear entrance, then circles around to a small storeroom where she pushes open a trunk and picks out a pair of gloves, followed by [party.has kiyoko|two more pairs for you and your fox-wife|another pair for you]. She slips them on, gathers up a pole, several hand nets and a waxed-paper bag before stepping out into the warm sunshine. Situated at the far end of Kinu's garden is a large pond filled with a handful of colorful carp and several aquatic blooms; you recognize a few species of lilies, but most of them aren't native to the Marches. Carried in from the waterfall by stone piping, clear water flows into the pond and is carried away by bamboo culverts, perforated gratings of strangely regular aquatic vines over both inlet and outlet preventing the fish from escaping. The trickle of water is constant in the air, producing a steady stream of white noise, and your fox-daughter studies the serenity of the scene for several moments before passing you a hand net. "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... if you wish to help, could you please assist in clearing out any scum and floating weeds that have gathered by the water's surface? The flowing water helps in discouraging their growth, but the flow stills by the pond's edges." But of course. You take the net and get to work, scooping out the pond muck that's gathered about the edges and bottom before laying it into a small strainer. Kinu'll send it to compost later on, or however she disposes of these things... on her part, your fox-daughter busies herself with caring for the aquatic flora of her pond, clearing their broad, flat leaves of pests and diseased spots while collecting several of the choicest blooms for later use. [party.has kiyoko |While this has been going on, Kiyoko has been feeding the fish, scattering small dried brown pellets upon the water's surface and watching the colorful carp fight over the food, churning the water's surface to frothing. Your fox-wife watches them calmly for several moments, tilting her head and wiggling her ears at the sight. "This brings me back. Daughter, where did you get these koi? They're not native to this part of the world." "Ah, Mother... they were a gift." "From?" "Um..." "Spit it out, child." "Nakano brought them in from the Old Country for me, Mother. He'd heard that I'd gotten Hitoshi to dig me a pond, and... well, he got a tub and carried them all the way in through the gate. It's a miracle they didn't die on the way here." Kiyoko is silent for several moments, then shakes her head. "I can't decide if that's the most brash, romantic, or stupid thing I've ever heard someone do." "That's what I pointed out to him, Mother. He said that the koi had a strong spirit and will to have survived this far, and that I could learn something from them." "Ever with the silly answers. Man fancies himself a poet." "He is a poet, Mother. Even if he is not a very good one." |At length, Kinu finishes harvesting the blossoms before placing their stems in a small basin of water and setting them aside. Gathering up the small bag of waxed paper in her arms, she dips her fingers within and scatters pellets of what looks like dried meat over the water's surface. The colorful carp immediately converge on the spot, fighting over the fish food and churning the water to a froth. Your fox-daughter watches them for several moments, ears twitching, then steps back with a small smile. "You have to be careful when feeding them, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. They will eat as much as you will give, and grow sick if you overfeed them. That, and you do not wish to fully satiate them anyway; a little bit of hunger will provoke them to hunt insects and other pests that congregate in their home." Ha... you remember yourself that as a child, she'd eat as many peaches as she could lay her hands on until she got sick. Either with stomachache and indigestion, or up to the point where she'd just throw up... "Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]... I was young then and did not have much in the way of wisdom or self-control. It is an ongoing effort..." Nevertheless, carp-raising is like child-raising in a sense. Or caring for any living thing, for that matter. The intricacies change and difficulty of doing so might be different, but the basic precepts are still the same. Kinu is silent for a little while as she scatters another handful of fish food over the water. "There is merit in that notion, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], yet I cannot say I agree wholly with it." That's all right. So long as her reasoning is sound — and you're sure it is, right? — you're content with that. After all, if two people agree with each other on everything and every matter, one of them is probably unnecessary. Probably. "And that is where I must disagree with you, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." You laugh and pet Kinu on the head. She's learning. ] At length, the carp are fed, the water is cleared, and the blossoms pruned and harvested. Beating down from above in the clear Marches sky, the sun itself reflects dully upon the pool's surface; [party.has kiyoko|your fox-wife brings in a large bucket of water drawn from the crossroads well, and all three of you take turns washing off your hands and the tools|your fox-daughter brings in a large bucket of water drawn from the crossroads well, and the both of you take turns washing off your hands and the tools]. "Well, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]thank you for lending me your assistance today. I have indeed dealt with my duties in a most swift and satisfactory manner." She's most welcome. |Your fox-daughter leads you out the rear entrance, then circles around to a small storeroom where she pushes open a trunk and picks out a pair of gloves, followed by [party.has kiyoko|two more pairs for you and your fox-wife|another pair for you]. She slips them on, gathers up a waterproofed cloth pack, then heads out into the warm morning sun. You follow your fox-daughter out to a wooden standing frame, upon which two potted trees have been placed in the warm morning light — two potted miniature trees, at that. "Bonsai," Kinu says as she unrolls the pack to reveal an entire set of tiny gardening tools and several lengths of metal-reinforced string. "One of the most mundane yet exacting applications of shaping." Mm. "This one —" Kinu indicates the small juniper to the left — "is my charge. And that one over there[party.has kiyoko | —" "Is mine," your fox-wife purrs as she slides in between the both of you, [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails wrapping about your bodies comfortingly. "This is an art that teaches one many things. Patience, attention to detail, fine manipulation of one's faculties, a sense of proper aesthetics, and more. Of course I would have taught our daughter such, no matter how silly it may appear to several outsiders. After all, what is the use of a miniature tree? One might as well ask what is the use of music, painting or any form of art, for that matter?" Whoa, she's getting defensive all of a sudden. "Ehe. Sorry. It's just..." Kiyoko taps her chin with a finger. "Old memories. Please, forgive my outburst, and let us begin." | is Mother's." You look between the two, and there's no doubt about it: you don't know much about the aesthetics in this Old Country art form, but Kiyoko's bonsai is definitely healthier and more robust-looking than Kinu's. A glance at Kinu reveals that your fox-daughter is eyeing you out of the corner of her vision, trying very hard not to make it obvious that she's watching closely. Really, now. That nervous lip bite gives it all away. You reach out and give your fox-daughter a pat between the ears — she doesn't need to use her mother as a measuring stick all the time. It's good that she's learned so much from Kiyoko and seeks to emulate her best qualities, but at the end of the day she's going to have to leave her mother's household and den sometime. Kiyoko's task is to prepare her for that day. Kinu looks down, squirming away from your petting. "I... when I was younger, I hoped that even after I grew up, I could still be close to Mother. It... I... let us not dwell upon this, please. You can only shake your head at it all — three different sizes of miniature shears, an equally small rake, leaf trimmers... where do they make all these just for this purpose? Come to think of it, both trees look pretty old despite their size. Surely your fox-family couldn't have raised them from scratch already? "Matron Komari was kind enough to supply Mother and I with cuttings from her own specimens. As you are aware, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], the shrine mother has had... a very long time to live." That would explain it. And there's no magic involved? "Only tools, string, care and time. Anything else would be sacrilegious, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Most shameful."
