"Thank you for assisting me today, [pc.mf|Father|Mother].[party.has kiyoko| And you for being here at my side, Mother.]" O-oh, you did nothing at all. It was no problem... "Your presence was important in getting me into the right mindset for the task at hand. In such endeavors, that is just as important as anything else." Now she's laying it on quite thickly, you'd say... ] [party.has kiyoko |Seeing this, your fox-wife chuckles, hiding her mouth behind a hand. "Ah. Well, it is almost noon now. You are due for your tasks with Komari, are you not?" "Yes, Mother." "Go ahead, wash up and make yourself ready, then. Your [pc.mf|father|mother] and I will deal with the rest of this." Kinu looks a little apprehensive at the prospect, but her emotions but flicker on her face for a fraction of a moment. Carefully, your fox-daughter hands her things to Kiyoko and you, then gives the both of you a final bow before departing, her five silvery-white tails following her into her chambers. "Come on, beloved," Kiyoko says, nudging you in the side with an elbow. "Let's pick up after our daughter, shall we?" The two of you do just that, packing away Kinu's tools back into the storeroom. Partway through it all, Kiyoko looks wistfully at the neatly arranged goods and sighs. "We should do this more often." Yes. Yes, you should. "What's that local saying that was around two centuries ago? 'Your son's your son until he takes a wife, but your daughter's your daughter all your life'? Ehe... just because our daughter's grown doesn't mean we can stop being a part of her life. And I'm honestly glad that she feels the same way, too. "All right, then — we need to get these put away and be on our way." |"Well, that will be enough for today, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. It is almost noon and I have to wash up and make myself presentable for my duties with Matron Komari. If you would please... I can handle the putting away myself." Oh, all right then. ] Before long, you're back on the road, feeling much better for having spent the morning with Kinu and reminded of why you're doing all this in the first place. Your fox-daughter is such a precious creature... she has to be protected at all costs. '

rows.original: Kinu quirks her head at you, a small smile spreading on her lips as she raises a finger to her chin. "It has been quite a while since we have played a board game together, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Might you be interested in a bout?" Why, if she is free, then yes. But isn't she occupied with many important tasks this morning as her mother's majordomo? "For someone like you, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], I can always make time." [party.has kiyoko |Your fox-wife smiles. "Don't try and wriggle out of this one, beloved. I've wanted to see you two play for a while now, too." ] What a complete and cheeky about-face hidden beneath that mask of impenetrable politeness. But that's your fox-daughter for you — she wouldn't be her if she didn't love her strategy board games from the day she was born, would she? All right, all right, you'll do it if it'll make her happy. Kinu's smile widens ever so barely as she closes her eyes and gives you a little dip of her head. The impish glee of her childhood has grown with her into something more sinister and better able to conceal itself... ah, your girl's truly grown into a young woman, hasn't she? But she's your darling daughter, and [pc.cunningRange 80 |besides, you think you have a decent-to-good chance of winning, even if she's your opponent. Kinu bites her lip, a little mischief shining through. "If that is what you say, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. But let it be know that I am not a kit any longer, and I will not hold back even if we are family." No, absolutely not. If you're going to come out on top, it's going to be in spite of her doing her best, and you absolutely forbid her from throwing the game just because she feels sorry for you. She's got to be honest and give it her all, okay? Kinu's smile broadens. "I had a feeling that you would say that; I merely wished to hear you state it in no uncertain terms. Very well, I will honor and respect your wishes." |you think you can put up a good fight, even if you're likely to lose. Who knows, you might even get lucky and wrest victory through sheer unpredictability. "Ah. What was it they call it, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]? Beginners' luck? The novice may attempt gambits more seasoned players would deem too risky or not worth one's time, and cinch victory that way.." Haha, that's one way to put it. You don't think you're that bad, though... "It is all — ahem — relative. At least I know you will do your utmost unlike some [kiyoko.numKits 4|of my siblings|of the people I know], [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Let us begin, then." ] With that, Kinu rises from her seat and motions for you to wait out in the living area while she ducks into her sleeping chambers to get the board and pieces. Soon enough, she's back, toting them under her bosom and pulling up two cushions by the firepit for the both of you. "Please make yourself comfortable, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I will serve refreshments shortly — tea and rice crackers, for old times' sake. I am looking forward to this most eagerly." Well, you know how this goes. Setting up the board while Kinu puts on the kettle with a bit of foxfire is a familiar task to you by now, and before long steam's billowing in the air, bringing with it the scent of refreshing bitterness. So it comes to pass that you and your kitsune daughter wind up facing each other down over a game of [rand|go|shogi], with tea and snacks at your side. This really makes you nostalgic... the rice crackers are as bland as ever, with but a hint of salt, but does it really matter when Kinu's on the other side of that board over there, all ready to trounce you at the slightest sign of weakness? [rand |"[pc.mf|Father|Mother]..." Yes? "This reminds me of the day Mother wished to introduce me to you." You remember it, yes. Even though it must have been years for Kinu, it hasn't been quite as long for you on the outside of that orb. Yes, you remember it just fine, as if it really had happened yesterday — you being introduced to your daughter over a game of go, with Kiyoko overseeing the both of you. She was so quiet and formal then, and now the cumulation of that personality has come to fruition — a fox every bit as elegant and refined as a princess should be, despite her surroundings. "I might not have believed it myself," Kinu admits, "And there were some places where I might have fallen off the path. That I stayed true to Mother and what she taught me was a surprise, especially considering my difficult years." She was a pretty okay surprise herself. "You flatter me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Back to that day... I was uncertain of what to expect of you, and a little afraid. Mother spoke often of you, but people are different in the flesh as opposed to from hearsay. Experiences are colored." That's the first time you've ever heard her admit to being scared of anything in her life... "It is the truth." |"[pc.mf|Father|Mother]..." Yes? "How was it when you first met Mother?" Oh? "I... well, there is this man, and I know he can do better for himself. Even his own family has given up on him and is telling me to do so, but I refuse. I have seen improvement, I have seen his will; he just needs to direct it properly and he can succeed. He needs a mountain to surmount, and I have to find it for him." Maybe she should just take a deep breath before she falls face-first onto the board from lack of air. "It is depressing, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], especially when everyone is telling me to give up. But I give up on no one, especially when they do not deserve it in the least." Well, to be honest, you can't really say for your situation with her mother because the whole thing was quite unorthodox. But first, has she tried seeking advice from anyone else? "Mikoto was —" Yeah, Miko's advice probably isn't going to cut it with the kind of character she's describing. Melodramatic flourishes probably aren't going to work, if your guess is right. Perhaps just doing what she's already been doing is just fine — showing up every day and making herself useful. "I have been helping him with his poetry and art, and making sure he eats meals right. It has been working, I just need to keep at it and not be discouraged by what everyone is saying. But some days my patience is tested..." See, that's the kind of gesture her guy probably appreciates. Show up, make herself useful, don't get in the way, and she'll eventually end up appreciated. "He smiled at me the other day, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. He never smiles, even for his family. I — oh dear. I believe I allowed myself to be carried away and said too much..." And she should have paid more attention to the board. There. "A very nice move, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. My fault for not paying attention when I should have." |"Being in the colonies is not as bad as some would have you imagine. Mother and Matron Komari have told me about some of the cities over in the Old Country across the ocean, and the politics make my blood run cold. Here, I know and can see the faces of the people whom I will eventually be beholden to, and they me. Things can get done without political gridlock. It is a freer, if poorer place. "It feels good to be liked by the people whom are beholden to you, instead of feared, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Of course, a healthy mix of both is ideal for the proper mindset towards governance, but I digress. "What I mean to say is that I like this place. It is efficient, and things happen because they are supposed to, for the good of colonials. Matron Komari has gone a long way to ensuring that, and I hope to aid her as much as I can." |"Go and shogi are fine games for someone in my position and of my heritage to dabble in. Some days, I am glad that I listened to and obeyed Mother in all things, because I could easily have strayed from this path that I am on. To not be who I am here and now... that would be unthinkable, and I would be a beast for being so unfilial. Only foxes of the field behave that way." ... "But I digress, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Did I tell you? One of the things that happened relatively early on after we emerged into this world was that Miyuki asked me if I played shogi. I was really enthusiastic about it all, up to the point where she defeated me soundly. Looking back on it, it was the only real outcome that could have been expected as I had never played anyone outside of my family. I was so inexperienced, I was unfit to serve as her opponent. "It was a learning experience. I have yet to defeat Miyuki, but am nevertheless making progress towards that goal. She may not be able to learn things as quickly as I do, but she is quicker than me in other ways I did not quite appreciate and still do not fully grasp. And that's fine." |"When I was growing up, all I wanted to be able to do was live a simple life. Enough to be content, but not overly comfortable, lean but not pinched. If people wanted more, I would not begrudge them that, but as far as my own existence went I would be happy to learn to be satisfied with what I had and take joy in the small pleasures of life. Azami tells me it is a simple, fulfilling existence, and she is living it every moment of her waking hours. "But... things are not as simple as that. I thought everything would change when Mother[kiyoko.numKits 2|, I and my siblings| and I] left the Astral Plane, and they have. There is no hiding from the world, and I must meet my responsibilities by virtue of my birth bravely, not abdicate them out of fear. Destiny cannot be sought or averted. "I cannot run from who I am, so I will confront it, and I will both do you and Mother proud, as well as all my ancestors." ] Kinu falls silent again, and for the next half-hour to a full hour or so, the room is silent, punctuated only by the gentle crackle of embers in the firepit and the snap of rice crackers. [pc.cunningRange 70 95 |Kinu's usually genial and pleasant expression has done a complete about-face into one of absolute, serious concentration, brows furrowed as her ice-blue eyes flick back and forth over the board. Those aren't just gears turning in that cute little head of hers — it's an entire assembly of deviously complex mechanisms. Seconds tick by between each of your moves, a strange gravitas suffusing your surroundings as pieces are picked up and set down with grim finality. Even though Kinu's games are familiar to you at this point, the way she plays isn't. Perhaps that's the part about this all that hits home the hardest — she's no longer a kit, she's not longer as inexperienced as she used to be, and she's no longer toying with you or holding back. Even though your beloved fox-daughter may still act childishly at times, it's not her base nature any more. The game continues to drag on. At this point, even Kinu's ears have stilled, stiff and alert on her head as she studies the pieces on the board. Then at last, the endgame. [rand| "Why, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I appear to have bested you." Why yes, she has. She has indeed won, although by the state of the board it was a very close game. Thinking back on it, there were a couple of points back there where making a slightly different move would have radically changed the game's outcome. Perhaps you should've capitalised on those opportunities, but you didn't, and this is where you are now. Hindsight may be much clearer, but one needs to know when and how to seize the now. Kinu purses her lips and eyes the board once more, raising a finger to her chin. "Well, you put up a good fight, and few people can say that. Mother and Miyuki are the only ones who are able to do such — well, Matron Komari too, but she is occupied with her duties as governor and I do not wish to impinge upon her time. "Either way, this was a very pleasant game. I have learned a few things I want to try out next time." Of course. You've enjoyed your time with her, too. | "I believe you are the victor, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Why, so you have. That's actually rather surprising. Even after all this time, there are still certain blind spots she doesn't quite take notice of, especially when she's distracted or flustered. Those have been with her since she was a kit — she's got to take more notice. "I am working hard to rectify my weaknesses." Kinu looks down at the board again and cups her chin with thumb and forefinger. "I see it now. I might have emerged the victor if I had made this play —" she jabs at the board with a finger — "and this and this twenty moves ago. But I did not, and that was my failing." Thinking with a clear head is hard enough. Doing so under pressure is a skill one needs to cultivate over time. She may have more experience now, but she's still young. Once she's a bit more focused and conscientious, perhaps with a little more guidance, you've no doubt she'll be a force to be reckoned with in the future. "Thank you for the compliment, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." So long as she remembers that there generally are more opportunities to learn from loss and failure than from coming out ahead, she'll do just fine. And yes, you quite enjoyed your time with her. ] |Kinu starts off with a strong opening and bold play, but quickly falls into a far more conservative strategy when you stymie her opening gambit. Your daughter's brows knit and furrow as she considers each move deeply, realizing that she's gotten in ahead of herself, perhaps due to simple overconfidence and impetuousness. She's taking you seriously now, and that's a good thing. As promised, she holds nothing back and gives as good as she takes. The tides of war shift back and forth on the battlefield of the wooden game board, each move by either party slow and deliberate. By this point, Kinu's lips are a thin, straight line as she cups her chin in a hand, those ice-blue eyes of hers darting back and forth across the board. She looks a lot like she used to when she was playing with you as a child... but now that she has a lot more worldly experience under her belt, your darling fox-daughter has only grown exponentially more dangerous. When it happens, it surprises you almost as much as it does her; with a final, resounding clack, you set the piece in your hand down on the board and claim victory over your daughter. "You are victorious, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. That was very educational — I would like to see you play Miyuki someday, it would be a sight to see." So you have. That doesn't mean anything, though — you could have gotten lucky, or she could have been careless. "Please do not undersell yourself, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I have to my honest with my strengths and weaknesses, and so do you if you wish to make correct decisions — bad information leads to bad choices. Although if you wish to show your victory did not come about by chance, we can play each other again sometime." You grin. Oh, you're more than up for another round any time. "Not right now, of course; I want the both of us to improve before meeting each other like this again. Not only did I learn a few things today, but I always enjoy the time we spend together. We do not get to play all the time, so that makes it extra special when we do. Absence makes the heart grow fond, as the saying goes." He, she doesn't need to lay it on that thickly. "It is the truth." |[rand |The picture of quiet concentration doesn't last long, though. Within a handful of moves, your fox-daughter has completely outmaneuvered you and forced you into a corner. Within a handful of moves, you're forced to admit defeat, falling prey to Kinu's relentless assault. She's definitely improved since she was a child. On her part, Kinu looks a little disappointed at the easy victory, frowning furiously. Eventually, she shakes her head and bites her lip. "I suppose we are done, [pc.mf|Father|Mother] — as I said, I will never go easy on you just because we are family. There was nothing you could have done about the situation since you made that play there —" she points down at the board amidst the few remaining pieces — "so I decided to wrap it up as quickly as I could." That's very kind of her, you suppose. "There is little meaning or honor in beating down on and tormenting a defeated opponent." You can see her point. Still, did she have fun? "Spending time with you is always enjoyable, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." She's still no different from when she was a kit — a honey-tongued flatterer when she puts her mind to it. |As the game proceeds apace, your fox-daughter quickly becomes a pinpoint of intense focus, her ice-blue eyes narrowing to slits as she studies the board. Humming to herself, Kinu sweeps her five tails sweep out to her front, and she hugs her own silken fur close to herself as her moves become much more methodical and much less lackadaisical. "Hmm..." It's almost as if she's enjoying being decently challenged — or at least, more of a challenge than [kiyoko.numKits 3|her siblings usually put up|she gets from playing against herself]. You're going to give it your all, too — if you lose, it's not going to be from lack of trying. The state of the battlefield that's the wooden game board shifts from moment to moment, the tides of war turning at a whim; it's hard to discern who exactly has the upper hand until out of nowhere, Kinu pulls off a series of moves that has you completely blindsided outmaneuvered in moments. You see the ambush too late, a snare amongst the innocuous grasses, and it's at that point that you retrace her moves and realize she was heading for this endgame all along. "...And there. An excellent game, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], but I am victorious in the end. I expected you to see through my gambits, but I decided to take the risk anyway." So, she's become the kind to set elaborate yet unassuming snares to entrap the unwary, eh? [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar| You've had the opportunity to play board games like chess and checkers in your past, and some of the strategies do carry over to these games of hers, if not completely. Hopefully, you've been able to give a your daughter new perspective on various plays that Kiyoko's home culture wouldn't be familiar with. "I am glad to be able to learn something from our games together, but even more so, I am glad to be spending time with you." Heh. Is that an invitation? "It is, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." |Well, considering that you didn't have much chance to play these sorts of board games in your past, it's not really a surprise you fell into her trap like this. She's really gotten better since she was a child. Kinu considers you with a small smile. "Do not be disheartened, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Practice cannot hurt, can it?" Oh, she doesn't have to couch it like that — you'll gladly play with her any time she wants. "Even so." ] Psh, isn't that just adorably devious. ] ] Eventually, though, Kinu finishes the last of her tea, stands and gives you another bow. "Thank you for the game, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Please, allow me to put away the trappings of our repast before I make ready to depart for Matron Komari's in the afternoon." All right, then, you'll be heading off first. Getting to your feet, you give your fox-daughter a final wave before stepping on out of her chambers and into the warm morning sun; before long, you're back on the road again, the memories of the game still fresh in your mind.

|你的狐狸妻子微笑了。亲爱的，别想逃避这个责任。其实我也早就想看你们两个一起表演了。 ] 在那一副看似无可挑剔的礼貌外表下，其实隐藏着如此彻底而大胆的转变。不过，这也正是你的那个“狐妖女儿”的风格吧——如果她从出生那天起就不热爱那些策略棋盘游戏，她还能是现在的她吗？好吧，好吧，只要能让她开心，你肯定愿意做的。 小娟微微一笑，闭上眼睛，轻轻点了点头。她童年时那种顽皮可爱的笑容，如今已经变成了某种更加隐秘、更加难以察觉的愉悦之情。啊，你的女儿真的已经长大成了一位年轻的女子了，不是吗？但她毕竟是你心爱的女儿啊[pc.cunningRange 80 |此外，你认为自己即使面对她这样的对手，也有相当大的胜算。 小娟咬了咬嘴唇，眼中闪过一丝调皮的光芒。如果真是你这么说的， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]但请记住，我不再是一个需要被照顾的人了，即使我们是家人，我也不会再有所保留。 不，绝对不行。如果你想取得胜利，那就必须是在她尽了最大努力的情况下才能实现；你绝对不能因为她同情你而让她放弃比赛。她必须诚实面对，全力以赴，明白吗？ 小娟的笑容变得更加灿烂了。我就觉得你会这么说；我只是想听你明确地把这话讲出来而已。好吧，我会尊重你的意愿的。 |你认为自己就算很可能失败，也能进行一场激烈的抵抗。谁知道呢，也许你会运气爆棚，凭借那种难以预测的因素反而取得胜利。 啊，他们叫它什么来着[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]新手运气？”这些缺乏经验的游戏者可能会尝试那些经验丰富玩家认为风险太大或不值得花费时间的策略，从而轻松赢得胜利。 哈哈，这么说也有道理。你难道不觉得自己那个不过，这也挺糟糕的…… 这一切啊——咳——都是相对的。至少我知道，你会竭尽全力去完成这件事，不像某些人那样。 [kiyoko.numKits 4|我的兄弟姐妹们|在我认识的人当中]， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]那么，让我们开始吧。 ] 说完，小娟从座位上站起来，示意你在客厅等着，然后她便走进自己的卧室去拿棋盘和棋子。不久之后，她回来了，把它们抱在怀里，还在篝火旁拉来了两个垫子，为你们俩准备好了坐的地方。 请随意休息， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]我马上就会准备一些点心来——为了纪念过去的时光，准备茶和米饼。我真的很期待这一刻。 嗯，你应该很清楚该怎么做。现在，当你让小娟用一点狐火烧水壶准备茶具时，这项任务对你来说已经变得非常熟悉了。不久之后，蒸汽就会袅袅升起，空气中弥漫着那种清新的苦味。于是，你和你的九尾狐女儿就会围坐在桌前，开始一起玩这个游戏[rand|开始吧|将棋]边喝茶边吃零食，这样的场景真的会让人产生怀旧之情……那些米饼依然那么淡而无味，只加了一点点盐而已，但当小娟就在对面的棋盘上，随时准备在你稍显弱小的时候击败你时，这些真的还重要吗？ 我自己可能都不敢相信这一点。小娟坦言：有些地方，我本可能会偏离正确的道路。但我始终坚守着对母亲的承诺，也坚守着她教给我的一切，这实在令人惊讶，尤其是考虑到我曾经经历过的那些艰难岁月。 她自己也给大家带来了一个相当不错的惊喜。 你太抬举我了， [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]回到那天……我并不确定会遇到一个怎样的你，甚至还有些害怕。母亲经常提起你，但人与人见面和只是听别人讲述是两回事，亲身经历带来的感受才是真实的。 这是你第一次听到她承认自己这辈子曾经害怕过什么…… 这是事实。 |“[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]……” 嗯？ 你第一次见到母亲的时候，是什么感觉？ 哦？ Well, to be honest, you can't really say for your situation with her mother because the whole thing was quite unorthodox. But first, has she tried seeking advice from anyone else? "Mikoto was —" Yeah, Miko's advice probably isn't going to cut it with the kind of character she's describing. Melodramatic flourishes probably aren't going to work, if your guess is right. Perhaps just doing what she's already been doing is just fine — showing up every day and making herself useful. "I have been helping him with his poetry and art, and making sure he eats meals right. It has been working, I just need to keep at it and not be discouraged by what everyone is saying. But some days my patience is tested..." See, that's the kind of gesture her guy probably appreciates. Show up, make herself useful, don't get in the way, and she'll eventually end up appreciated. "He smiled at me the other day, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. He never smiles, even for his family. I — oh dear. I believe I allowed myself to be carried away and said too much..." And she should have paid more attention to the board. There. "A very nice move, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. My fault for not paying attention when I should have." |"Being in the colonies is not as bad as some would have you imagine. Mother and Matron Komari have told me about some of the cities over in the Old Country across the ocean, and the politics make my blood run cold. Here, I know and can see the faces of the people whom I will eventually be beholden to, and they me. Things can get done without political gridlock. It is a freer, if poorer place. "It feels good to be liked by the people whom are beholden to you, instead of feared, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Of course, a healthy mix of both is ideal for the proper mindset towards governance, but I digress. "What I mean to say is that I like this place. It is efficient, and things happen because they are supposed to, for the good of colonials. Matron Komari has gone a long way to ensuring that, and I hope to aid her as much as I can." |"Go and shogi are fine games for someone in my position and of my heritage to dabble in. Some days, I am glad that I listened to and obeyed Mother in all things, because I could easily have strayed from this path that I am on. To not be who I am here and now... that would be unthinkable, and I would be a beast for being so unfilial. Only foxes of the field behave that way." ... "But I digress, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Did I tell you? One of the things that happened relatively early on after we emerged into this world was that Miyuki asked me if I played shogi. I was really enthusiastic about it all, up to the point where she defeated me soundly. Looking back on it, it was the only real outcome that could have been expected as I had never played anyone outside of my family. I was so inexperienced, I was unfit to serve as her opponent. "It was a learning experience. I have yet to defeat Miyuki, but am nevertheless making progress towards that goal. She may not be able to learn things as quickly as I do, but she is quicker than me in other ways I did not quite appreciate and still do not fully grasp. And that's fine." |"When I was growing up, all I wanted to be able to do was live a simple life. Enough to be content, but not overly comfortable, lean but not pinched. If people wanted more, I would not begrudge them that, but as far as my own existence went I would be happy to learn to be satisfied with what I had and take joy in the small pleasures of life. Azami tells me it is a simple, fulfilling existence, and she is living it every moment of her waking hours. "But... things are not as simple as that. I thought everything would change when Mother[kiyoko.numKits 2|, I and my siblings| and I] left the Astral Plane, and they have. There is no hiding from the world, and I must meet my responsibilities by virtue of my birth bravely, not abdicate them out of fear. Destiny cannot be sought or averted. "I cannot run from who I am, so I will confront it, and I will both do you and Mother proud, as well as all my ancestors." ] Kinu falls silent again, and for the next half-hour to a full hour or so, the room is silent, punctuated only by the gentle crackle of embers in the firepit and the snap of rice crackers. [pc.cunningRange 70 95 |Kinu's usually genial and pleasant expression has done a complete about-face into one of absolute, serious concentration, brows furrowed as her ice-blue eyes flick back and forth over the board. Those aren't just gears turning in that cute little head of hers — it's an entire assembly of deviously complex mechanisms. Seconds tick by between each of your moves, a strange gravitas suffusing your surroundings as pieces are picked up and set down with grim finality. Even though Kinu's games are familiar to you at this point, the way she plays isn't. Perhaps that's the part about this all that hits home the hardest — she's no longer a kit, she's not longer as inexperienced as she used to be, and she's no longer toying with you or holding back. Even though your beloved fox-daughter may still act childishly at times, it's not her base nature any more. The game continues to drag on. At this point, even Kinu's ears have stilled, stiff and alert on her head as she studies the pieces on the board. Then at last, the endgame. [rand| "Why, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I appear to have bested you." Why yes, she has. She has indeed won, although by the state of the board it was a very close game. Thinking back on it, there were a couple of points back there where making a slightly different move would have radically changed the game's outcome. Perhaps you should've capitalised on those opportunities, but you didn't, and this is where you are now. Hindsight may be much clearer, but one needs to know when and how to seize the now. Kinu purses her lips and eyes the board once more, raising a finger to her chin. "Well, you put up a good fight, and few people can say that. Mother and Miyuki are the only ones who are able to do such — well, Matron Komari too, but she is occupied with her duties as governor and I do not wish to impinge upon her time. "Either way, this was a very pleasant game. I have learned a few things I want to try out next time." Of course. You've enjoyed your time with her, too. | "I believe you are the victor, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." Why, so you have. That's actually rather surprising. Even after all this time, there are still certain blind spots she doesn't quite take notice of, especially when she's distracted or flustered. Those have been with her since she was a kit — she's got to take more notice. "I am working hard to rectify my weaknesses." Kinu looks down at the board again and cups her chin with thumb and forefinger. "I see it now. I might have emerged the victor if I had made this play —" she jabs at the board with a finger — "and this and this twenty moves ago. But I did not, and that was my failing." Thinking with a clear head is hard enough. Doing so under pressure is a skill one needs to cultivate over time. She may have more experience now, but she's still young. Once she's a bit more focused and conscientious, perhaps with a little more guidance, you've no doubt she'll be a force to be reckoned with in the future. "Thank you for the compliment, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." So long as she remembers that there generally are more opportunities to learn from loss and failure than from coming out ahead, she'll do just fine. And yes, you quite enjoyed your time with her. ] |Kinu starts off with a strong opening and bold play, but quickly falls into a far more conservative strategy when you stymie her opening gambit. Your daughter's brows knit and furrow as she considers each move deeply, realizing that she's gotten in ahead of herself, perhaps due to simple overconfidence and impetuousness. She's taking you seriously now, and that's a good thing. As promised, she holds nothing back and gives as good as she takes. The tides of war shift back and forth on the battlefield of the wooden game board, each move by either party slow and deliberate. By this point, Kinu's lips are a thin, straight line as she cups her chin in a hand, those ice-blue eyes of hers darting back and forth across the board. She looks a lot like she used to when she was playing with you as a child... but now that she has a lot more worldly experience under her belt, your darling fox-daughter has only grown exponentially more dangerous. When it happens, it surprises you almost as much as it does her; with a final, resounding clack, you set the piece in your hand down on the board and claim victory over your daughter. "You are victorious, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. That was very educational — I would like to see you play Miyuki someday, it would be a sight to see." So you have. That doesn't mean anything, though — you could have gotten lucky, or she could have been careless. "Please do not undersell yourself, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I have to my honest with my strengths and weaknesses, and so do you if you wish to make correct decisions — bad information leads to bad choices. Although if you wish to show your victory did not come about by chance, we can play each other again sometime." You grin. Oh, you're more than up for another round any time. "Not right now, of course; I want the both of us to improve before meeting each other like this again. Not only did I learn a few things today, but I always enjoy the time we spend together. We do not get to play all the time, so that makes it extra special when we do. Absence makes the heart grow fond, as the saying goes." He, she doesn't need to lay it on that thickly. "It is the truth." |[rand |The picture of quiet concentration doesn't last long, though. Within a handful of moves, your fox-daughter has completely outmaneuvered you and forced you into a corner. Within a handful of moves, you're forced to admit defeat, falling prey to Kinu's relentless assault. She's definitely improved since she was a child. On her part, Kinu looks a little disappointed at the easy victory, frowning furiously. Eventually, she shakes her head and bites her lip. "I suppose we are done, [pc.mf|Father|Mother] — as I said, I will never go easy on you just because we are family. There was nothing you could have done about the situation since you made that play there —" she points down at the board amidst the few remaining pieces — "so I decided to wrap it up as quickly as I could." That's very kind of her, you suppose. "There is little meaning or honor in beating down on and tormenting a defeated opponent." You can see her point. Still, did she have fun? "Spending time with you is always enjoyable, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." She's still no different from when she was a kit — a honey-tongued flatterer when she puts her mind to it. |As the game proceeds apace, your fox-daughter quickly becomes a pinpoint of intense focus, her ice-blue eyes narrowing to slits as she studies the board. Humming to herself, Kinu sweeps her five tails sweep out to her front, and she hugs her own silken fur close to herself as her moves become much more methodical and much less lackadaisical. "Hmm..." It's almost as if she's enjoying being decently challenged — or at least, more of a challenge than [kiyoko.numKits 3|her siblings usually put up|she gets from playing against herself]. You're going to give it your all, too — if you lose, it's not going to be from lack of trying. The state of the battlefield that's the wooden game board shifts from moment to moment, the tides of war turning at a whim; it's hard to discern who exactly has the upper hand until out of nowhere, Kinu pulls off a series of moves that has you completely blindsided outmaneuvered in moments. You see the ambush too late, a snare amongst the innocuous grasses, and it's at that point that you retrace her moves and realize she was heading for this endgame all along. "...And there. An excellent game, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], but I am victorious in the end. I expected you to see through my gambits, but I decided to take the risk anyway." So, she's become the kind to set elaborate yet unassuming snares to entrap the unwary, eh? [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar| You've had the opportunity to play board games like chess and checkers in your past, and some of the strategies do carry over to these games of hers, if not completely. Hopefully, you've been able to give a your daughter new perspective on various plays that Kiyoko's home culture wouldn't be familiar with. "I am glad to be able to learn something from our games together, but even more so, I am glad to be spending time with you." Heh. Is that an invitation? "It is, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]." |Well, considering that you didn't have much chance to play these sorts of board games in your past, it's not really a surprise you fell into her trap like this. She's really gotten better since she was a child. Kinu considers you with a small smile. "Do not be disheartened, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Practice cannot hurt, can it?" Oh, she doesn't have to couch it like that — you'll gladly play with her any time she wants. "Even so." ] Psh, isn't that just adorably devious. ] ] Eventually, though, Kinu finishes the last of her tea, stands and gives you another bow. "Thank you for the game, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. Please, allow me to put away the trappings of our repast before I make ready to depart for Matron Komari's in the afternoon." All right, then, you'll be heading off first. Getting to your feet, you give your fox-daughter a final wave before stepping on out of her chambers and into the warm morning sun; before long, you're back on the road again, the memories of the game still fresh in your mind. '

rows.original: "I was just about to sit down and do some scheduling for the next week," Kinu says. "[kiyoko.numKits 3 |Sibling wrangling can quickly devolve into a manner of everyone thinking everyone is going to be covering your duties if responsibilities are not clearly demarcated between individuals. The first time you claim that someone else was supposed to cover for you is also going to be your last." That sounds... vaguely threatening. "It may have been," is Kinu's crisp reply. "Just because we are family does not mean I can turn a blind eye to such nonsense; if anything, it means the opposite as I have a measure of responsibility for my siblings as charges that I would not have had for anyone else. Everyone needs to work together in a manner conducive towards overarching goals, and whoever does the coordination needs to have sufficient skin in the game, yet is detached enough from the actual work involved to negate any bias |Matron Komari may have lent us some hands to work on the restoration of our den, but they still need to be directed in the most expeditious and efficient manner. Prioritising critical infrastructure while condemning extraneous buildings while ensuring basic living conditions takes someone with an overview of the situation — someone with skin in the game, and yet is detached enough from the actual work going on to act in a manner conducive towards the overall goals ]." In short, her. "Just so. However, I am completely mortal, with all the follies that follow... it would be reassuring if you [party.has kiyoko|and Mother ]could oversee the process as I plan everyone's schedules, ensure that I do not misallocate resources or play favorites." [party.has kiyoko |"Mm. I am willing to do that, daughter dearest," Kiyoko says, coming up beside you. "But remember that someday I will not be around to supervise you." Your fox-daughter looks down and away. "I understand, Mother." "Good, good." ] That... well, if nothing else, it would be good to have some insight into how the den is actually run on a day-to-day basis. Yes, you'll look over the scheduling of [kiyoko.numKits 3|her siblings|the workers] for the upcoming week. "Thank you. Please, make yoursel[party.has kiyoko|ves|f] comfortable — I will take down the schedule and be with you forthwith." Kinu is good to her word — what she brings down from the wall and to your table is a large wooden slat with two grids and a stick of charcoal attached. Two-grids — of course, one for this week and another for the next. While there're a few characters in Kinu's mother tongue here and there, most of it is written in Belharan and legible to you... [kiyoko.numKits 3 |[rand |"I am with Matron Komari from noon till evening every day, so while I am gone both Tatsumi and Aya are in charge and fully responsible for all events in the den until I return. It will teach them some measure of independence and responsibility when they cannot immediately turn to me as Big Sister to solve their problems for them." Just as she can't always turn to her mother to solve her problems for her. "Just so. After all, what is this but practice for my future? Even if I still hope to be close to Mother after I strike out on my own... I am merely doing for those two what Mother has done for me." |"Part of the challenge of scheduling is determining who does what. Everyone has personalities and traits of their own that make them more or less suited for certain tasks, but at the same time one cannot avoid the unpleasantness of life all the time and must learn to endure. After all, as the saying goes, nothing can be done about it. "Hence, there are two contradictory goals that must be fulfilled by the schedule: that of getting the tasks done in a speedy and correct manner without being overly draining on morale, and making people perform tasks that they dislike and will do poorly in order to move them beyond their comfort zones and learn from the experience. Now that I am grown... I have a much better understanding of and appreciation for the decisions that Mother must have made in my upbringing. It is the sort of perspective that, for all my precociousness, I could not have had because of my simple lack of experience." |Hey, you notice that she's scheduling herself as well. "Well, of course. I have to keep a hand in most tasks... something as simple as doing laundry or cooking breakfast for everyone else may seem a task too trivial for someone in my position, but I like being on the ground to be able to see if everything is going as intended. Not that I do not trust my siblings... but it is always better to be able to confirm the situation for oneself." Smart girl. "It is a small indulgence of life in the colonies that I am able to have a suitable excuse for performing tasks that would be considered beneath my station in polite society, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I am able to feel like I am of use." ] |[rand |"Since I cannot be here in the afternoons, there is a lot of trust involved here in allowing the hands Matron Komari has loaned us to work freely. So far, work has been proceeding in accordance to the scheduled arrangements... it is very nice to be able to ask someone to do something and be able to count on getting it done without the need for wasted resources in constant supervision." You can imagine. It's probably the same things that happens whenever Garth gets people involved for any kind of building project in Hawkethorne and gets it done in mere days — since no one has to look over each others' shoulders all the time to see if someone is skiving, all that extra energy goes toward actually completing the task. "Sometimes Nakano's cousin Hitoshi comes as an overseer of sorts, but he is just that in name. If anything, he works harder than anyone else. It is a sight to see." |"The day's schedule ends just about the time I return from Matron Komari's, so I am always happy to be able to serve the hands she has sent us tea and minor refreshments before they return through the gate — just as I sometimes do before I leave. You can tell from their faces that the refreshments themselves are always welcome, and having them served by a young princess of considerable refinement only makes it better, does it not?" That's rather forward of her. "It is important to show your appreciation for those who are taking the time to help you. Running the place and fixing it up would be quite impossible with the few hands we have here at the moment; I am all too aware of the importance these fine people have, even if they may not recognize it themselves." |Hey, you note that she's scheduling herself in the mornings, too. "Well, of course. I have to keep a hand in most tasks... something as simple as doing laundry or cooking breakfast for else may seem a task too trivial for someone in my position, but I like being on the ground to be able to see if everything is going as intended. Not that I do not trust the hired hands... but it is always good practice to be able to confirm the situation for oneself every now and again." Smart girl. "It is a small indulgence of life in the colonies that I am able to have a suitable excuse for performing tasks that would be considered beneath my station in polite society, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I am able to feel like I am of use." ] ] At length, your fox-daughter fills up the grids on the chart, [party.has kiyoko |stopping every now and again to take instruction and advice from her mother |pausing every so often to think ]. You don't have much to say about her scheduling in and of itself, but can appreciate how your fox-daughter is going about it with a clear and methodical mind. So long as it looks all right and she seems to be knowing what she's doing, it should be fine, right? Eventually, though, Kinu sets down the charcoal stick and turns to you. "And that is it. I feel quite satisfied with the planning for next week." That's good. It has been nice spending time with her and understanding what she's up to about the place while you're gone. Even if you weren't about to help her out that much directly, being able to hear out your daughter and knowing her better with regards to how she works is always worth it. "Oh, you flatter. But thank you. I will put this back up, then, and send it out once the week turns over to the next. For now the task is done." All right, then, you'll be heading off first. Getting to your feet, you give your fox-daughter a final wave before stepping on out of her chambers and into the warm morning sun; you're back on the road again before long, safe in the knowledge that Kinu is a capable girl and will be fine while you're gone.
rows.translation: 我正准备坐下来安排下周的工作安排呢。小娟说道。"[kiyoko.numKits 3 |如果没有明确划分每个人的职责，兄弟姐妹之间的争执很快就会演变成一种“大家都认为别人会替自己完成任务”的局面。而你第一次声称应该由别人来替你承担责任，也会同时成为你最后一次这么做的机会。 这听起来……有点威胁性啊。 也许吧。这是小娟简洁而干脆的回答。仅仅因为我们是家人，并不意味着我可以对这种荒谬的行为视而不见；事实上，恰恰相反，我对自己的兄弟姐妹负有特殊的责任，这种责任是我对其他人所没有的。每个人都应该为了共同的目标而共同努力，而负责协调工作的人必须既有足够的投入，同时又能够保持一定的客观性，以避免任何偏见的出现 |虽然麻里女首领帮助我们进行了巢穴的修复工作，但这些工作仍然需要有人以最快、最有效的方式来指导进行。在优先修复关键基础设施、舍弃无关建筑的同时，还要确保人们的基本生活条件得到保障——这需要一个人既能全面了解整个情况，又与实际的工作过程保持一定的距离，从而能够以有利于实现整体目标的方式来行事 ]。" 简而言之，就是她。 正是如此。不过，我终究只是个凡人，也会犯下各种愚蠢的错误……如果你[party.has kiyoko|和母亲 ]能监督整个流程，我会安心一些，因为我会安排每个人的工作时间表，从而确保不会错误地分配资源，也不会偏袒任何人。 [party.has kiyoko |嗯，我愿意这么做，我最亲爱的女儿。清子走到你身边，说道。但要记住，总有一天，我将不再在这里监督你。 你的狐狸女儿总是低着头，不敢与人对视。我明白了，母亲。 很好，很好。 ] 那个……嗯，至少了解一下这个基地日常是如何运作的也是很有帮助的。没错，你会审阅[kiyoko.numKits 3|她的兄弟姐妹|工人们]下周的排班。 谢谢。请，您自己[party.has kiyoko||f]没问题，我会立刻把日程安排调整好，然后陪在你身边。 小娟确实说到做到了——她从墙上取下来放在你桌上的，是一块带有两个格子的大木板，还有一根木炭。这两个格子，一个用来记录这周的事情，另一个用来记录下周的事。虽然小娟的母语中偶尔会用到一些字符，但大部分内容都是用Belharan语写成的，你完全能够看懂…… [kiyoko.numKits 3 |[rand |我每天从中午到晚上都会和麻里女首领在一起，所以在我不在的时候，龙美和绫就会负责管理一切事务，直到我回来。这样，当他们不能立刻向我寻求帮助来解决问题时，就能学会一定的独立性和责任感。 正如她不能总是依靠母亲来解决自己的问题一样。 只是这样而已。毕竟，这一切不正是为我未来的成长做准备吗？即使我独立后仍然希望能够和母亲保持亲密关系……我所做的，也只是在为那两个人做母亲曾经为我做过的事情罢了。 |安排日程时面临的挑战之一就是确定每个人应该负责什么任务。每个人都有自己的性格特点，这些特点会决定他们是否适合某些工作，但与此同时，我们也必须学会忍受生活中不可避免的不愉快之处。毕竟，正如那句俗话所说，对此我们也无能为力。 因此，日程安排必须同时实现两个看似矛盾的目标：一方面是要以快速且正确的方式完成各项任务，同时避免对团队士气造成过度负面影响；另一方面则是要让人们去完成那些他们不喜欢、也难以做好的事情，从而让他们走出自己的舒适区，从中获得学习经验。如今我长大了……我更加能够理解并感激母亲在我成长过程中所做出的那些决定。这种领悟，正是由于我早年缺乏经验，尽管我天资聪颖，也根本无法拥有的。" |嘿，你有没有注意到，她也在为自己安排各种事情呢。 嗯，当然。我必须参与大多数任务……像洗衣服或者为其他人准备早餐这样的小事，对于我来说可能看起来微不足道，但我喜欢亲自动手，这样就能确保一切都在按计划进行。并不是说我不信任我的兄弟姐妹们……但亲自确认情况总归会更放心。 聪明的女孩。 在殖民地生活，这种小小的放纵让我能够找到合适的借口去从事那些在礼貌的社会中会被认为不符合我身份地位的任务。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]这样我就能感受到自己是有用的。 ] |[rand |由于我下午无法在场，因此大家非常信任Matron 小毬提供的这些帮助，让我们能够自由地开展工作。到目前为止，一切都在按照预定的计划进行……能够委托别人去做某事，并且确信他们一定会完成任务，而无需我们花费额外的资源进行持续监督，这种感觉真是太好了。 你可以想象，每当加斯在鹰棘镇组织人们进行任何建筑项目时，事情总是这样发展的——由于没有人需要时刻监督别人是否在偷懒，所以所有这些额外的精力都被用来完成实际的工作了，项目也因此能在短短几天内就完成。 有时候，中野的表弟仁会以某种监督者的身份出现，但实际上他只是名义上的监督者而已。事实上，他的工作努力程度比任何人都高，这一幕真的让人印象深刻。 |我一从麻里女首领那里回来，当天的日程就差不多结束了。因此，我总是很乐意在那些被她派来的人通过大门回来之前，为他们送上茶水和小点心——有时候，在我离开之前也会这么做。从他们的表情就能看出，这些点心总是很受欢迎，而由一位举止得体、富有教养的年轻公主来为大家服务，无疑会让这种体验变得更加美好，不是吗？ 她这样做未免太冒失了。 对于那些花时间帮助你的人，表达你的感激之情是非常重要的。以我们目前手头上有限的人力，要维持这个地方的运转并对其进行修缮，确实是件几乎不可能完成的任务；我非常清楚这些善良的人们所起到的重要作用，尽管他们自己可能并没有意识到这一点。 |嘿，你注意到她也会在早上安排自己的时间吧。 嗯，当然。我必须参与大多数任务的执行……比如洗衣服或者准备早餐这样的小事。对于我这样的职位来说，这些任务可能看起来微不足道，但我喜欢亲自动手，这样就能确保一切都在按计划进行。并不是说我不信任雇来的工作人员……不过，偶尔亲自确认一下情况总是有益的。 聪明的女孩。 在殖民地生活，这种小小的放纵让我能够找到合适的借口去从事那些在文明社会中会被认为有失身份的任务。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]这样我就能感受到自己是有用的。 ] ] 终于，你的狐狸女儿填满了图表中的所有格子。 [party.has kiyoko |不时停下来向母亲请教建议。 |时不时停下来思考一下 ]对于她安排这些事情的方式，你其实没什么可说的，但不得不承认，你的这位“狐狸女儿”做事确实有条理、有方法。只要这样下去看起来好吧，她看起来很清楚自己在做什么，应该不会有问题的，对吧？ 不过，最终小娟还是放下了炭笔，转向了你。就这样吧。我对下周的计划感到相当满意。 那太好了。能和她一起度过这些时光，了解你在不在的时候她都在为这个地方做些什么，真的是件很愉快的事。即使你并不会直接为她提供太多帮助，但能够倾听你女儿的心声，更深入地了解她的做事方式，这些都是非常有意义的。 哦，您太客气了。不过还是谢谢您。那我会把这个重新发布出来，等到新的一周开始时再发送出去。目前来说，这项任务已经完成了。 好吧，那你就先出发吧。你站起身来，向你的狐狸女儿挥了挥手，然后走出了她的房间，走进了温暖的晨光之中；不久之后，你又重新踏上了旅途，心中充满信心——因为你知道，小娟是个有能力的女孩，你在不在她身边，她都会过得很好。
rows.raw: ' "I was just about to sit down and do some scheduling for the next week," Kinu says. "[kiyoko.numKits 3 |Sibling wrangling can quickly devolve into a manner of everyone thinking everyone is going to be covering your duties if responsibilities are not clearly demarcated between individuals. The first time you claim that someone else was supposed to cover for you is also going to be your last." That sounds... vaguely threatening. "It may have been," is Kinu's crisp reply. "Just because we are family does not mean I can turn a blind eye to such nonsense; if anything, it means the opposite as I have a measure of responsibility for my siblings as charges that I would not have had for anyone else. Everyone needs to work together in a manner conducive towards overarching goals, and whoever does the coordination needs to have sufficient skin in the game, yet is detached enough from the actual work involved to negate any bias |Matron Komari may have lent us some hands to work on the restoration of our den, but they still need to be directed in the most expeditious and efficient manner. Prioritising critical infrastructure while condemning extraneous buildings while ensuring basic living conditions takes someone with an overview of the situation — someone with skin in the game, and yet is detached enough from the actual work going on to act in a manner conducive towards the overall goals ]." In short, her. "Just so. However, I am completely mortal, with all the follies that follow... it would be reassuring if you [party.has kiyoko|and Mother ]could oversee the process as I plan everyone's schedules, ensure that I do not misallocate resources or play favorites." [party.has kiyoko |"Mm. I am willing to do that, daughter dearest," Kiyoko says, coming up beside you. "But remember that someday I will not be around to supervise you." Your fox-daughter looks down and away. "I understand, Mother." "Good, good." ] That... well, if nothing else, it would be good to have some insight into how the den is actually run on a day-to-day basis. Yes, you'll look over the scheduling of [kiyoko.numKits 3|her siblings|the workers] for the upcoming week. "Thank you. Please, make yoursel[party.has kiyoko|ves|f] comfortable — I will take down the schedule and be with you forthwith." Kinu is good to her word — what she brings down from the wall and to your table is a large wooden slat with two grids and a stick of charcoal attached. Two-grids — of course, one for this week and another for the next. While there're a few characters in Kinu's mother tongue here and there, most of it is written in Belharan and legible to you... [kiyoko.numKits 3 |[rand |"I am with Matron Komari from noon till evening every day, so while I am gone both Tatsumi and Aya are in charge and fully responsible for all events in the den until I return. It will teach them some measure of independence and responsibility when they cannot immediately turn to me as Big Sister to solve their problems for them." Just as she can't always turn to her mother to solve her problems for her. "Just so. After all, what is this but practice for my future? Even if I still hope to be close to Mother after I strike out on my own... I am merely doing for those two what Mother has done for me." |"Part of the challenge of scheduling is determining who does what. Everyone has personalities and traits of their own that make them more or less suited for certain tasks, but at the same time one cannot avoid the unpleasantness of life all the time and must learn to endure. After all, as the saying goes, nothing can be done about it. "Hence, there are two contradictory goals that must be fulfilled by the schedule: that of getting the tasks done in a speedy and correct manner without being overly draining on morale, and making people perform tasks that they dislike and will do poorly in order to move them beyond their comfort zones and learn from the experience. Now that I am grown... I have a much better understanding of and appreciation for the decisions that Mother must have made in my upbringing. It is the sort of perspective that, for all my precociousness, I could not have had because of my simple lack of experience." |Hey, you notice that she's scheduling herself as well. "Well, of course. I have to keep a hand in most tasks... something as simple as doing laundry or cooking breakfast for everyone else may seem a task too trivial for someone in my position, but I like being on the ground to be able to see if everything is going as intended. Not that I do not trust my siblings... but it is always better to be able to confirm the situation for oneself." Smart girl. "It is a small indulgence of life in the colonies that I am able to have a suitable excuse for performing tasks that would be considered beneath my station in polite society, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I am able to feel like I am of use." ] |[rand |"Since I cannot be here in the afternoons, there is a lot of trust involved here in allowing the hands Matron Komari has loaned us to work freely. So far, work has been proceeding in accordance to the scheduled arrangements... it is very nice to be able to ask someone to do something and be able to count on getting it done without the need for wasted resources in constant supervision." You can imagine. It's probably the same things that happens whenever Garth gets people involved for any kind of building project in Hawkethorne and gets it done in mere days — since no one has to look over each others' shoulders all the time to see if someone is skiving, all that extra energy goes toward actually completing the task. "Sometimes Nakano's cousin Hitoshi comes as an overseer of sorts, but he is just that in name. If anything, he works harder than anyone else. It is a sight to see." |"The day's schedule ends just about the time I return from Matron Komari's, so I am always happy to be able to serve the hands she has sent us tea and minor refreshments before they return through the gate — just as I sometimes do before I leave. You can tell from their faces that the refreshments themselves are always welcome, and having them served by a young princess of considerable refinement only makes it better, does it not?" That's rather forward of her. "It is important to show your appreciation for those who are taking the time to help you. Running the place and fixing it up would be quite impossible with the few hands we have here at the moment; I am all too aware of the importance these fine people have, even if they may not recognize it themselves." |Hey, you note that she's scheduling herself in the mornings, too. "Well, of course. I have to keep a hand in most tasks... something as simple as doing laundry or cooking breakfast for else may seem a task too trivial for someone in my position, but I like being on the ground to be able to see if everything is going as intended. Not that I do not trust the hired hands... but it is always good practice to be able to confirm the situation for oneself every now and again." Smart girl. "It is a small indulgence of life in the colonies that I am able to have a suitable excuse for performing tasks that would be considered beneath my station in polite society, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. I am able to feel like I am of use." ] ] At length, your fox-daughter fills up the grids on the chart, [party.has kiyoko |stopping every now and again to take instruction and advice from her mother |pausing every so often to think ]. You don't have much to say about her scheduling in and of itself, but can appreciate how your fox-daughter is going about it with a clear and methodical mind. So long as it looks all right and she seems to be knowing what she's doing, it should be fine, right? Eventually, though, Kinu sets down the charcoal stick and turns to you. "And that is it. I feel quite satisfied with the planning for next week." That's good. It has been nice spending time with her and understanding what she's up to about the place while you're gone. Even if you weren't about to help her out that much directly, being able to hear out your daughter and knowing her better with regards to how she works is always worth it. "Oh, you flatter. But thank you. I will put this back up, then, and send it out once the week turns over to the next. For now the task is done." All right, then, you'll be heading off first. Getting to your feet, you give your fox-daughter a final wave before stepping on out of her chambers and into the warm morning sun; you're back on the road again before long, safe in the knowledge that Kinu is a capable girl and will be fine while you're gone. '

rows.original: "There was not much that was pressing this morning, so I was just about to get to some needlework," your fox-daughter begins. "[pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]would you like to join me for a spell?" Needlework, eh? "There are always things that need to be mended on the frontier," Kinu replies sweetly. "It is but a simple fact of life that things get worn-down, worn-out, or simply torn for any number of reasons... [kiyoko.numKits 8 |especially when you have as many siblings as I do. Garments get passed down from one kit to the next in line and damage and wear accumulate. To be the littlest fox is a point of both pride and embarrassment, both for wearing the clothes passed down all the way to you, and yet being so threadbare and patched-over |such happenstances are inevitable where manual labor is involved in any fashion. But that is the struggle of civilization anywhere, a fight against entropy and the imposition of order on the natural state of things; it is merely more directly evident near the borders where the greatest changes are made visible ]." [party.has kiyoko |By your side, Kiyoko raises a hand to her lips and giggles, ears twitching. Wonder what your fox-wife finds so funny... ] Ah, well. You'd just... well, Kinu's looking fit to be a princess, even in her daily life like this. It feels a little strange for her to be doing sewing of any sort that isn't, you don't know, embroidery or fine stitching or something like that... "There is no shame in working with your hands or engaging in some simple, useful work. Would it be that I had a retinue of servants to attend to my every need and do all my menial labor for me, but such luxuries are not quite available to me, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], nor would I be well-advised to use them if they were. Certainly, if I were to be recognized as some kind of princess, those kinds of people would be far beneath me, that is for sure — but there is no reason to disrespect them or what they do, for that matter. I understand from Mother that this line of thinking is not always the case across the ocean. It must be my upbringing in this strange and foreign land, I suppose." [party.has kiyoko|Now it's your turn to|You] laugh. All right, all right, since she puts it so eloquently, you'll acquiesce. Come then, needlework it is. Kinu stands, gives you a small dip of her head, then heads off to a corner of the room. First, she returns with a large and ornately carved wooden box, then makes another trip for a bundle of clothes from a heavy trunk. Your fox-daughter creaks open the fox to reveal a simple sewing kit — needles, thread, a small selection of sharp edges, the works.[party.has kiyoko| Your fox-wife takes up position at your side, snuggling against you [kiyoko.pregStage 2|and wedging her big pregnant belly partway under the table|and making herself comfortable].] Well then, nothing for it. You pick up one of the nearest garments, examine it to get an idea of what you're up against, then select a needle from the kit and thread it. Sewing's and patching's the same no matter where you go, isn't it? After all, it's not supposed to look good at this point... [pc.bg noblescion courtesan |while you might have been raised amongst the upper crust of society, it's not as if you're completely unfamiliar with needlework, even if it tended to be more of the decorative and artistic sort rather than the practical. Even so, the basics are always the same no matter where you go, right? |like everyone else who didn't have people waiting on them hand and foot, you've had to do your own needlework in the past. Time to get to it, then! ] Kinu herself has already begun in earnest, wrapping her five tails about herself while she darns holes and patches rents. Even for something this simple, it's instructive to see the meditative, trance-like state your fox-daughter slips into without so much as a second thought, her eyes half-lidded and ears folded forward.[party.has kiyoko | By your side, Kiyoko has also done much the same thing, your fox-wife's soft breathing cleanly audible in the silence of the room. The white tips of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] wiggle back and forth as she works, delicate fingers moving with swift alacrity — ha, you note that while Kinu's bothered to use a thimble, Kiyoko doesn't. Brave, confident in her skills, or just simply foolhardy? Aha... ] It's a simple family moment, the [party.has kiyoko|three|two] of you engaged in useful work and just basking in each others' presence. Kinu hums to herself as she works, a lilting foreign melody that evokes a sense of quiet longing within you, her eyes never leaving needle and thread. [rand |"Ah, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]..." Yes? "Have you ever wondered?" Wondered what? "About garments like these. By and large they wear out — first they have to be darned, then patched, and finally sleeves and swathes have to be replaced wholesale. And just the other day, Nakano posed me an interesting question: if all of the cloth is replaced because of the ravages of time's fire, is it still the same garment? Of course, he says it is, because the spirit of the garment is what matters, and the material is but a secondary concern." Hmm... "Which is a little thought-provoking, because the nekomata of the Old Country believe that if a tool exists for a hundred years, it gains a spirit and mind of its own — which is why they break all their tools before they reach a hundred years of age. No doubt during that time, handles, blades and the like are completely replaced piecemeal... but does even complete destruction and renewal in another form prevent an object from still being itself? It's interesting to think about... but also comforting to know that these clothes are mine and will always be the same article, regardless of how many times I patch and darn them. Call it a girlish, clingy sentiment..." |"Hmm..." Hm? A hawk for her thoughts. "There is something satisfying about threading the eye of a needle, is there not?" You can't say you've given much thought to it. "It is a difficult enough task that not everyone can do it with ease, yet an easy enough task to be within the grasp of most, if one puts in a little time and effort. Eventually, with enough practice, most can do it easily and well. An endeavor that for most, is at that sweet spot of difficulty such that it poses something of a challenge for the uninitiated, yet is not so much that one eventually gets frustrated with it and gives up." Well, you can't say that she's obviously wrong... "Just so." With a single deft movement, Kinu threads the fine iron needle in her hands and starts once more. "Elegance and skill in deceptive simplicity." |"In some really backwater provinces in the Old Country, kitsune save up their fur from trimmings or sheddings," your fox-daughter begins. "Doubly so after winter when one needs to lose one's winter coat. They gather it all up, treat it and then spin the lot into yarn of sorts, then wool from which clothes are made. I suppose it is disconcerting, especially to other races, but is it then not our fault as leaders and administrators that such places are impoverished to the point where such practices are common?" Hmm... "That aside, it is hard to argue that garments made from kitsune fur are amongst the best anyone will ever wear." Kinu pauses in her needlework for a moment to take one of her five sleek tails in hand, lovingly stroking its length. "If Mother had not been strongly against it, I might have been tempted to wear my own skin, as it were..." [party.has kiyoko |Kiyoko's reply is crisp and curt. "However meaningful it may seem to you, that practice is highly unrefined and exceedingly unsanitary, regardless of how the fur is cleaned and treated beforehand. We have had this discussion before; do not think to change my ruling by bringing your [pc.mf|father|mother] into it." "Yes, Mother." ] While it's hard to argue that her mother's tails are amongst the best things in life that you've ever had the privilege of touching, you're of the opinion that kitsune fur is best when it's still on the fox. Without the fox in question, the fur loses a lot of its charm. "Perhaps that is the case, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]," Kinu replies, picking her needle back up. "Perhaps." |"It always makes me a little melancholy to do needlework," Kinu admits, her ears curling forward. "Clothes last long enough for one to be able to form fond memories of them, yet wear out quickly enough for you to remember how they were and see them fall apart. The knowledge that without you, they would be lost... and the reminder that you should not take what you have for granted, because it is always prone to crumbling to dust — an illusion for the moment, nothing more." ... ] Your fox-daughter bows her head again, and the room is silent once more save for gentle breathing, the crackle of the firepit and the soft rustle of fabric. There's a lot being said here, but of course, none of it is expressed in words, just the quiet homeliness of each others' presence. One by one, the pile of clothes to be mended disappears into the pile of patched garments, and eventually Kinu finishes up and sets her needles back into the box, arranged by size. "That should do it for now." How long as it been? Hours? Probably late afternoon, judging by how long it's felt — "Merely an hour. I do have to go over to Matron Komari's in the afternoon, do I not?" Kinu gathers the clothes in her arms and heads for the trunk to put them away. Well, it certainly felt like a lot longer... Your fox-daughter smiles. "It has been said that I have that effect on people when they are enjoying their time with me. I do enjoy being able to help others make the most of what moments we do have together." Which, unfortunately, has now come to an end. "There will be other times, I am sure. Departure is such a sad thing, yet an inevitable aspect of life." She looks at the clothes in her hands, then sets them into the trunk and shuts the lid with a heavy thud. "[pc.mf|Father|Mother], [party.has kiyoko|Mother, ]do keep yourselves safe out there. It was nice to be able to spend time with you." [party.has kiyoko |Kiyoko rises with a soft sigh. "Come now. Let us be going, or we will never have the heart to leave." Yes, she's right. |Yes, you'll do just that. Now, you've got to be going, or else you'll never be able to tear yourself away ]. Standing from your seat and turning tail, you thank Kinu one last time before heading out into the almost-noon sunshine.

[kiyoko.numKits 8 |尤其是当你像我一样有那么多兄弟姐妹的时候。衣物会一代代地传下来，使用过程中会逐渐破损和磨损。作为最小的那个，这既让人感到自豪，又会让人感到尴尬——既要穿着那些传下来的衣服，又得看到它们已经破旧不堪、补丁密布的样子 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]即使他们是那样的，我使用它们也不明智。当然，如果我被认作是某种公主的话，那些人肯定会在我之下——但并没有理由不尊重他们或他们的所作所为。从母亲那里我了解到，在大洋彼岸，人们的这种思维方式并不总是如此。我想，这肯定是因为我在这个陌生而异国他乡的成长环境吧。 [party.has kiyoko|现在轮到你了。|你]哈哈，好吧好吧，既然她说得这么有道理，你们应该会同意的。那么，就开始做针线活吧。” 小娟微微点头，然后走向房间的一个角落。她首先拿回来一个雕刻精美的木箱，接着又去那个重型的箱子那里取来一包衣物。你的狐妖女儿费了些力气才把那些衣物打开，里面是一个简单的缝纫工具包——针、线、还有一些锋利的工具，应有尽有。[party.has kiyoko| 这确实有点发人深省，因为古国的猫人相信，如果某种工具使用了百年，它就会拥有自己的灵魂和意识——正因如此，他们在工具使用满一百年之前就会将其毁掉。毫无疑问，在那段时间里，把手、刀刃之类的部件肯定是被逐一更换掉了……但是，即使某个物体被彻底破坏后又以另一种形式重新制造出来，它仍然能算是它自己吗？这个问题确实值得思考。…但想到这些衣服是属于我的，无论我修补多少次，它们始终会是那件衣服，这种感觉也让人感到很安心。或许这就是女孩子特有的、有点黏人的情感吧…… |嗯…… 嗯？用鹰来象征她的思维方式吧。 将线穿过针眼，这种感觉确实很令人满足，不是吗？ 你不能说你真的花了很多时间去思考这个问题。 这是一项难度适中的任务，并非每个人都能轻松完成它；但只要投入一些时间和精力，大多数人都能够掌握它。通过足够的练习，最终大多数人都能轻松而熟练地完成这项任务。对大多数人来说，它的难度正好处于一个恰到好处的水平——既能让初学者感到一些挑战，又不会让人因为过于困难而感到沮丧并放弃尝试。 嗯，也不能说她完全错了…… 只是这样而已。仅用一个熟练的动作，小娟就将手中那根细铁针穿了进去，然后再次开始操作。以简洁的形式展现出优雅与精湛的技巧。
